abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.heroSubtitle: For almost every Abu Dhabi family, IB November session exam preparation is a retake decision before it is a revision plan. UAE schools sit the May session, so a November entry is usually one subject being resat, and whether that is worth six months depends entirely on what the May results actually show. This page reads results as evidence, separates the retake from the remark, and sets out the record to keep in between. Lessons run one-to-one on live video, on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.tutorsIntro: The tutors below prepare Abu Dhabi students for November session retakes on live video. The first conversation is not about revision. It is about whether the component evidence supports a retake at all, and the answer is sometimes no.

intro.heading: A November entry is a decision first and a plan second
paragraphs: UAE schools sit the May session, which means a November entry from Abu Dhabi is almost always a retake. That changes the whole shape of the work. A May candidate is preparing for a first attempt at six subjects across a fixed two-year course. A November candidate is usually preparing for one subject they have already sat, with a results slip in hand that says, at component level, exactly where the marks went. That slip is the most useful document available in this situation and most families never read it properly.

Reading it properly is the first piece of work. A subject total tells you a grade was missed. The component breakdown tells you whether the loss sat in a paper, in the internally assessed component, or spread evenly, and those three point in different directions. A student who lost a grade on one paper while performing adequately on the others has a bounded, addressable problem. A student whose marks were flat and low across every component has a different question in front of them, and six months of revision may not be the answer to it.

So this plan starts with evidence rather than with a timetable, and the evidence produces one of three honest outcomes. A retake is worth it: the gap is narrow, it sits in a component that responds to work, and the grade matters for the next step. A remark is the better route: the grade is marginal and the loss looked like marking rather than capability. Or neither is worth it: the gap is wide, or the subject is not required for the intended destination, and the six months belong to something else entirely.

The third of those is the one nobody in this market will tell a family, and it is frequently the correct answer. A student retaking a subject their intended course does not require has spent six months improving a certificate. A student thirty marks below a boundary has a content problem that six months of part-time work alongside a university foundation year or a job is unlikely to close. Saying so is not discouragement; it is the difference between a plan and an expensive gesture. The provider who declines that sale is the one worth listening to on everything else.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a November candidate this matters more than usual, because many are no longer at school: they may be working, travelling, starting a foundation programme, or living somewhere else entirely by October. An online plan on Gulf Standard Time follows them, and the marked scripts accumulate in one place regardless of where they are sitting.

abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.programmesIntro: A November candidate from Abu Dhabi arrives by one of several routes, and the route determines what the six months should contain. These are the four that matter.

programmes.name: One subject, missed narrowly
programmes.description: The standard and most tractable case. A single subject, a grade missed by a small margin, and a component breakdown showing the loss concentrated rather than spread. Six months is generous for this, which means the plan should be modest and precise rather than a full re-teaching of the course.
programmes.countryNote: Confirm with the school or the examination centre what a retake entry involves administratively, including whether internally assessed component marks can be carried forward. That single question changes the amount of work substantially and the answer belongs to the coordinator rather than to a tutoring page.

programmes.name: A points total short of a university condition
programmes.description: Where an offer was conditional on a points total and the result fell short. The arithmetic is specific: which single subject, improved by how many grades, closes the gap, and is that the subject where the component evidence says the marks are actually available. Those are often not the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Universities differ in whether they will hold or defer an offer pending a November result, and the answer determines whether the retake has any value. Ask the institution directly and in writing before committing six months, because a retake into a closed offer is a certificate improvement.

programmes.name: A failing condition rather than a low grade
programmes.description: Where the Diploma was not awarded because of a failing condition rather than a points shortfall — for instance a grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay, or a grade 1 in a subject. This is a different problem from a low total and the remedy is specific to the condition that was triggered.
programmes.countryNote: Award rules and failing conditions are revised periodically. Confirm exactly which condition applied, and what satisfying it requires, with the school's IB coordinator. No tutoring page should be the source for that, including this one.

programmes.name: Deciding against a November entry
programmes.description: A legitimate and frequently correct outcome. Where the gap is wide, where the subject is not required for the intended destination, or where the university will not hold the offer, the six months are better spent elsewhere. The consultation that reaches this conclusion is worth paying for and is the smallest purchase on this page.
programmes.countryNote: No specific IB session or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date here has been confirmed from the IB directly. The school or centre holds the dates and the registration deadline, which sits well before the session.

abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.subjectsIntro: Retake requests from Abu Dhabi cluster in a small number of subjects, and what six months can achieve differs by subject because the components differ. These are the ones most often involved.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most common retake subject and one where six months is usually enough, because the loss is typically concentrated in algebraic fluency or in a single paper. Paper 1 performance without a calculator is the diagnostic that says whether the problem is technique or understanding.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Retaken less often and generally tractable, with losses concentrated in statistical inference or in the interpretation half of a question rather than in the calculation. Both respond well to a bounded six-month plan.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A frequent retake subject where the component breakdown is unusually informative: a loss concentrated in the data-based section points to graph and uncertainty work, while a loss spread across the extended-response paper points to the mathematics underneath the physics.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Retaken most often by students with medicine or pharmacy conditions attached. Six months is sufficient where mole fluency and one or two topics were the issue, and insufficient where the loss was flat across every component and every topic.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Often retaken alongside a conditional offer. The six months divide cleanly: retrieval practice for the content volume, which the candidate runs themselves, and marking-led work on command terms and data questions, which is where paid hours belong.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A tractable retake because diagram accuracy and evaluation structure are both mechanical gains. Where the internally assessed commentaries can be carried forward, the remaining work is narrow enough that six months is comfortable rather than tight.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Retaken where a language condition attached to an offer. Paper 1 guided analysis is the most improvable component in six months, because the technique is explicit and the gain shows up within weeks of marked practice.

subjects.name: History and the human sciences
subjects.description: Six months suits these subjects where the loss was in essay structure and timing rather than in content. Where the content itself was thin across a whole option, the honest assessment is that part-time work over six months may not close it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Where a failing condition was triggered by one of these, the remedy is specific to the component rather than to a subject. Establish with the coordinator exactly what satisfying the condition requires before any work is planned, because the requirements differ from an ordinary subject retake.

subjects.name: Scarce Higher Level options
subjects.levels: Further Mathematics, Global Politics, Music, Film, ab initio languages
subjects.description: Retaking a scarce subject raises an availability question before a planning question. The tutor pool that has taught the component is small, and for a November candidate who may no longer be in the UAE, an online plan is frequently the only one that exists.

abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.regionsIntro: A November candidate is often no longer in a school routine and sometimes no longer in the emirate. Delivery is online for that reason among others, but the local picture still shapes the first few weeks.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Villa communities where many retake candidates stay at home through the autumn. The constraint is structure rather than time: a day with no timetable produces less than a day with four fixed hours, and the plan's job is partly to supply the timetable.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Close to workplaces, and a meaningful number of retake candidates here take a job or an internship through the autumn. Evening sessions and weekend timed papers are the realistic shape, and the plan should be built around that rather than against it.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A small number of schools, so a retake candidate here is often the only one in their cohort and has no peer group working to the same session. That isolation is the under-discussed difficulty of a November entry and it is a scheduling problem more than a motivational one.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zeina
regions.note: Growing communities with substantial internal travel. Candidates who have left school no longer have a commute, which frees hours and removes the structure that used to organise them; both effects need building into the plan.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and the Corniche
regions.note: Established schools that handle retake registrations routinely and can usually say quickly what a retake entry involves. Families here often get a clear administrative answer faster, which matters because the registration deadline sits well before the session.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: A wide curricular mix and a population that moves. Candidates in this corridor are among the most likely to be in a different city or country by October, which is the clearest practical argument for an online plan that follows them.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Al Ain
regions.note: Greater distances and, in Al Ain, a separate school ecosystem under the same emirate regulator. For a scarce retake subject the local tutor pool is effectively nil, so the question is availability on a platform rather than proximity.

schoolClusters.note: Established Diploma programmes with administrative experience of November entries. These schools can usually answer quickly whether internally assessed marks carry forward and what the registration deadline is, which are the two facts a plan depends on.

schoolClusters.note: International schools whose leavers often move on quickly after results. A retake candidate from this cluster may be registering through their former school while living elsewhere, which makes the administrative questions more urgent rather than less.

schoolClusters.note: Where a student may have siblings on a different examination calendar, and where the school handles two sets of results and two retake routes. Worth confirming which process applies rather than assuming the Diploma one.

sections.heading: Reading the May results as evidence, not as a verdict
paragraphs: A results slip reports subject grades and, with them, information about where within each subject the marks were earned. That component-level view is what turns a disappointing total into a decision. Three patterns appear and they lead to different places. The loss sat in one paper while the others were adequate. The loss sat in the internally assessed component. Or the marks were flat and low across everything.

The first pattern is the best news available. A single weak paper in an otherwise adequate profile is a bounded problem: the content is largely known, the technique failed in one place, and six months of part-time work aimed at that component is a proportionate response. This is the case where a retake most reliably succeeds and where the plan should be modest rather than a re-teaching of the whole course.

The second pattern is more awkward because an internally assessed mark may be carryable rather than repeatable. Whether a retake candidate can carry forward internally assessed component marks is an administrative question with a real answer, and it changes the amount of work substantially: a candidate who must redo an Internal Assessment is facing a very different six months from one who is not. Ask the coordinator or the examination centre, in writing, before planning anything.

The third pattern is the one that argues against retaking. Flat low marks across every component usually indicate that the course was not learned rather than that an examination went wrong, and six months of part-time study alongside a job or a foundation programme is unlikely to close that. The honest version of this conversation names the size of the gap and lets the family decide, which is a very different service from assuming the retake and selling the hours.

sections.heading: Remark against retake: two routes, two deadlines
paragraphs: These are different things and families conflate them. A remark is a review of how an existing script was marked. A retake is a fresh attempt at the examination in a later session. The first is quick, cheap relative to a retake, and has a deadline close behind results. The second is six months of work with a registration deadline well ahead of the session. Both are administered through the school or the examination centre rather than by a family or a tutor.

A remark is worth considering where a grade sits narrowly below a boundary and the marked evidence suggests the script was better than the mark. It is not a second chance at the paper and it does not always move a grade: a review may confirm the original mark. What makes it attractive is the ratio — a short administrative process against six months of study — which is why it should be considered before a retake rather than after.

A retake is worth considering where the gap is real, the component evidence says it is addressable, and the grade matters for a destination that is still open. That last condition deserves emphasis. Universities differ in whether they will hold or defer an offer pending a November result, and the answer belongs to the institution. Ask them directly, in writing, before committing six months, because a retake into a closed offer improves a certificate rather than a destination.

Both routes have dates and the dates are not negotiable. Remark deadlines sit close behind results and are easy to miss in the week that follows them. Retake registration sits well before the November session and is handled by a school or centre. The whole argument for deciding the criteria in the spring, before results arrive, is that a family then spends results week making an arithmetic decision rather than discovering a process.

sections.heading: The six-month record: twelve data points on one instrument
paragraphs: Six months is a long time with no external measurement, and that is the characteristic risk of a November plan. A May candidate has mocks, school reports, teachers and a cohort. A retake candidate frequently has none of those: they have left school, their peers have moved on, and nothing in their week tells them whether the work is landing. Without a measurement they find out in November, which is too late to change anything.

The record fixes that cheaply. A baseline in September: one timed component sat under conditions and marked against the published criteria, with the mark and date recorded. Then fortnightly sessions, each opening with a timed component sat between sessions and marked beforehand. By November that is roughly twelve marks on comparable instruments, which is enough to see a trend rather than a mood.

The trend is what makes the plan honest. A mark moving steadily upward is confirmation. A mark flat across six data points by December is information: the method is not working and something has to change rather than continue. That conversation in December is possible and useful; the same conversation in November is a post-mortem. A plan without a record cannot have it at all, which is why the record is the product rather than an extra.

One further function. A retake candidate's family is usually anxious and has no information, which produces either excessive pressure or misplaced reassurance. A dated list of marks is neither: it is the thing both parties can look at. Reports go out after every session with the mark, the date and the component, and reading one takes a minute.

sections.heading: What carries forward and what does not
paragraphs: This is the administrative question that changes the size of a November plan more than any other, and it has a definite answer that a family has to obtain rather than assume. Whether a retake candidate can carry forward marks for internally assessed components, and under what conditions, determines whether they are resitting papers or reproducing an Internal Assessment as well. The difference between those two is several months of work.

Ask the question in writing, of the school or the examination centre that will register the entry, and ask it as part of the same conversation as the registration deadline and the entry arrangements. The coordinator deals with this routinely in schools that handle November entries, and the answer is specific to the candidate's circumstances and the rules applying to their cohort. It should not be taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

The second administrative item is where the examination will be sat. A candidate still connected to their school may sit at the school. A candidate who has left, or who has moved emirate or country, may need to arrange entry through a centre that accepts external candidates, and centre arrangements and charges vary. That is a question with a date attached, and the date sits well before the session.

The third is the core components. Where a failing condition was triggered by Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay rather than by a subject grade, the remedy is specific to that condition and is not an ordinary subject retake. Establish exactly which condition applied and what satisfying it requires before planning any work, because a plan aimed at the wrong thing is six months spent on a problem the candidate did not have.

sections.heading: Keeping a candidate working without a school around them
paragraphs: The under-discussed difficulty of a November entry is not academic. A retake candidate has usually left the structure that organised their work: no timetable, no cohort sitting the same papers, no teacher asking for anything on Tuesday. Many are also doing something else — a job, an internship, a foundation programme, a gap arrangement — and the retake becomes the thing that fits around it rather than the thing the week is built on.

Two practical responses work. The first is fortnightly rather than weekly contact with a timed component due each time, because a deadline every two weeks supplies the structure the school used to provide and a weekly one is easy to defer. The second is placing the work in a fixed slot the candidate controls rather than in whatever gap appears, because the gaps stop appearing by October.

For candidates who prefer compression, the autumn intensive is the alternative: two sessions a week for six to eight weeks on a single component, with timed practice throughout and a measurement against the September baseline at the end. It suits someone with a job or a programme who can commit a concentrated block better than a long thin one, and it produces its result early enough to leave the final weeks for full papers.

The scheduling realities of this emirate still apply. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, and where Ramadan falls in the plan — its position in the Gregorian calendar moves earlier each year, so it differs between cohorts — sessions move to post-Iftar times and weekly output drops. A candidate who has moved to another time zone is accommodated by scheduling rather than by changing the plan, which is one of the plainer advantages of delivering this work online.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi specifics: ADEK, registration and who may help
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages found in this research, which is a conspicuous gap on pages addressed to families here, and it is the authority whose framework the school's own policies sit inside.

For a retake candidate the school remains the administrative route in most cases even after leaving, which makes the relationship worth maintaining rather than closing. Registration deadlines, carry-forward questions, centre arrangements and any access arrangements all run through the school or the centre. A family who left on good terms in July has an easier September than one who did not, which is an unglamorous but real piece of advice.

One rule specific to this emirate shapes who may be paid to help. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than read from ADEK's current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication. A former student's position may differ from a current one, which is another question for the school rather than an assumption.

Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated generally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time. Because the permit is free, no provider can justify a charge on licensing grounds; tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

sections.heading: What a November plan costs, and what to refuse
paragraphs: Priced honestly this is a small plan. The evidence consultation is one or two sessions producing a written assessment. The six-month record is fortnightly sessions, which is roughly twelve to fourteen hours across the whole period. An autumn intensive is twelve to sixteen hours in a block. Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650.

Fortnightly contact across six months is deliberately lower frequency than a May plan, and that is not a cost-saving measure so much as an accurate reading of what the period needs. A single subject with six months in front of it does not require weekly teaching; it requires a measurement every two weeks and the work done between. A provider proposing weekly sessions for one subject over six months is proposing roughly twice the hours the task contains.

The in-home comparison is the same as elsewhere in this market and less relevant here, because many November candidates are not in Abu Dhabi by October. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and an online plan on Gulf Standard Time follows a candidate who has moved.

Four things to refuse. A promised grade, since boundaries are determined after a session from candidate performance and no provider controls that. Anything offering to alter or reproduce a submitted component. An unevidenced examiner claim at a premium rate, which gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content whatever is implied. And a plan that assumes the retake before reading the component breakdown, because the first honest question is whether to enter at all. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the International Baccalaureate, ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE, and operates no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: The conversation that ends with not retaking
paragraphs: This page would be dishonest without it. A meaningful share of families who arrive asking about November session preparation should not enter, and the reasons are checkable rather than matters of judgement. The university has closed the offer or will not defer it. The subject is not required for the intended destination. The gap is thirty marks and the candidate is working full time. The failing condition was in a core component and satisfying it requires something different from a subject retake.

In each of those cases six months of study produces a better certificate and not a better outcome, and the cost is not only the fees: it is six months of a young person's life spent on something that was decided before they started. The consultation that establishes this costs one or two hours. It is the smallest purchase described anywhere on this page and frequently the most valuable.

The alternative conversations are also worth having. A candidate with a wide gap in one subject may be better served by a different route into their intended field, by a foundation year that does not require the grade, or by an application cycle a year later with a stronger overall case. Those are not tutoring products, which is precisely why a tutoring provider rarely raises them.

Where the evidence does support a retake, the same honesty applies in the other direction: the plan is modest, the hour count is stated, and the record will say by December whether it is working. A November entry supported by component evidence, aimed at one component, measured fortnightly and pointed at a destination that is still open is a good use of six months. Everything in this page is addressed to distinguishing that case from the others.

process.title: Send the component breakdown, not the total
process.description: The results slip with its component-level detail is the document that matters, along with the subject and level and the reason the grade is wanted. A total tells us a grade was missed; the breakdown tells us whether six months can address it and which component it would be aimed at.

process.title: Ask the university, in writing, first
process.description: Before anything is booked, ask whether the institution will hold or defer the offer pending a November result. The answer determines whether the retake has any value, and it belongs to the university rather than to a school or a tutor. A retake into a closed offer improves a certificate.

process.title: Ask the school about carry-forward and deadlines
process.description: Whether internally assessed component marks can be carried forward, when the retake registration deadline falls, and where the examination will be sat if the candidate has left. Those three answers change the size of the plan and all three belong to the school or the centre.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. It is spent on the component breakdown and one question from the relevant paper, so the candidate sees the standard being applied and the family sees what the gap actually consists of.

process.title: The September baseline
process.description: One timed component sat under conditions and marked against the published criteria, with the mark and date recorded. This is the real starting point and it is sometimes different from what the May result suggested, in either direction. The plan is written from it.

process.title: Fortnightly record, reviewed in December
process.description: A timed component between sessions, marked before each one, with the mark and date recorded. In December the six data points are compared against the baseline. A flat trend at that point means the method changes rather than continues, which is a conversation only a record makes possible.

whyPoints.title: The decision comes before the plan
whyPoints.description: The first work is reading the component breakdown and establishing whether a retake is supported, whether a remark is the better route, or whether neither is worth six months. Selling revision hours before that question is answered is the common failure in this part of the market.

whyPoints.title: Three outcomes, including no
whyPoints.description: A meaningful share of families asking about November entry should not enter, for reasons that are checkable: a closed offer, a subject that is not required, a thirty-mark gap, or a core failing condition needing something else. The consultation that establishes it is the smallest purchase here.

whyPoints.title: Twelve data points instead of hope
whyPoints.description: Six months with no external measurement is the characteristic risk of a retake. A September baseline and a fortnightly timed component on comparable instruments produce a trend that is visible by December, when something can still be changed.

whyPoints.title: Fortnightly, because that is what the task needs
whyPoints.description: One subject with six months in front of it needs a measurement every two weeks and the work done between, not weekly teaching. A provider proposing weekly sessions for a single subject across six months is proposing about twice the hours the task contains.

whyPoints.title: The administrative questions asked first
whyPoints.description: Carry-forward of internally assessed marks, the registration deadline and the examination centre are three answers that change the plan's size, and all three belong to the school or centre. Asking them before writing a plan is cheaper than discovering them inside one.

whyPoints.title: A plan that follows the candidate
whyPoints.description: Many November candidates have left school and some have left the country. Online delivery on Gulf Standard Time follows them, and the marked record accumulates in one place regardless of where they are sitting, which a local in-home arrangement cannot do.

faqs.question: Who actually sits the IB November session from Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Almost entirely retake candidates. UAE schools sit the May session, so a November entry from this emirate is usually one subject being resat after a May result, rather than a first attempt at a full Diploma. That changes the nature of the work completely: the candidate already has a results slip with component-level detail showing where the marks went, which is far better evidence than anything a first-time candidate has. The November session is the Southern Hemisphere sitting; for an Abu Dhabi family it functions as the retake route.

faqs.question: How do I read a May results breakdown before deciding on a retake?
faqs.answer: Look for one of three patterns at component level rather than at the subject total. A loss concentrated in one paper while the others were adequate is the best case: the content is largely in place and six months aimed at that component is proportionate. A loss in the internally assessed component depends entirely on whether that mark can be carried forward, which is an administrative question with a real answer. Marks flat and low across every component usually indicate the course was not learned, and six months of part-time work is unlikely to close that.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a remark and a November retake?
faqs.answer: A remark is a review of how an existing script was marked; a retake is a fresh attempt at the examination in a later session. The remark has a deadline close behind results, requires almost nothing of the student, and may confirm the original mark rather than moving it. The retake has a registration deadline well before the session and requires six months of work. The ratio argues for considering the remark first where a grade sits narrowly below a boundary and the evidence suggests the script was better than the mark awarded.

faqs.question: Should I ask the university before committing to a November retake?
faqs.answer: Yes, in writing, and before anything is booked. Universities differ in whether they will hold or defer an offer pending a November result, and the answer determines whether the retake has any value at all. A retake into an offer that has closed improves a certificate rather than a destination, and it costs six months of a young person's time as well as the fees. The question belongs to the institution rather than to a school or a tutor, and it should be answered before any plan is written.

faqs.question: Do internally assessed marks carry forward to a November retake?
faqs.answer: It is the administrative question that changes the size of a November plan more than any other, and it has a definite answer specific to the candidate's circumstances and the rules applying to their cohort. Whether a retake candidate can carry forward internally assessed component marks determines whether they are resitting papers or reproducing an Internal Assessment as well, which is a difference of several months. Ask the school or the examination centre in writing, as part of the same conversation as the registration deadline. Do not take it from a tutoring page.

faqs.question: When should a family decide against a November entry?
faqs.answer: When any of four checkable conditions holds. The university has closed the offer or will not defer it. The subject is not actually required for the intended destination. The gap is wide — thirty marks rather than three — and the candidate is working or studying full time. Or the Diploma was withheld because of a core failing condition, in which case the remedy is specific to that condition rather than an ordinary subject retake. In each case six months produces a better certificate and not a better outcome, and the consultation that establishes it costs an hour or two.

faqs.question: How often should a November retake candidate have sessions?
faqs.answer: Fortnightly in most cases, which is deliberately lower than a May plan. One subject with six months in front of it does not need weekly teaching; it needs a measurement every two weeks and the work done between. Twelve to fourteen hours across the whole period is a realistic total. A provider proposing weekly sessions for a single subject across six months is proposing roughly twice the hours the task contains, and the surplus usually gets filled with content review the candidate did not need.

faqs.question: How do I know whether six months of retake work is going well?
faqs.answer: Only by measuring on the same instrument repeatedly. A September baseline — one timed component under conditions, marked against the published criteria, with the mark and date recorded — then a timed component every fortnight marked before each session. By December that is six comparable data points. An upward trend is confirmation; a flat trend is information that the method needs changing while there is still time to change it. Without the record a candidate finds out in November, which is too late to act on anything.

faqs.question: Where does a candidate who has left school sit the November exams?
faqs.answer: Usually still through their former school, which remains the administrative route in most cases, which is a practical reason to leave on good terms in July. Where that is not possible — the candidate has moved emirate or country, or the school does not handle November entries — entry has to be arranged through a centre that accepts external candidates, and centre arrangements and charges vary. That question has a deadline attached and the deadline sits well before the session, so it belongs in the first week of September rather than in October.

faqs.question: What is hardest about preparing for a retake outside a school?
faqs.answer: The absence of structure rather than the academic work. A retake candidate has usually lost the timetable, the cohort and the teacher who asked for something on Tuesday, and many are simultaneously doing a job, an internship or a foundation programme. The retake becomes the thing that fits around everything else. Two responses help: a timed component due every fortnight, which supplies the deadline the school used to provide, and a fixed slot the candidate controls rather than whatever gap appears, because by October the gaps stop appearing.

faqs.question: Is an autumn intensive better than six months of fortnightly work?
faqs.answer: For some candidates, yes. Two sessions a week for six to eight weeks on a single component, with timed practice throughout and a measurement against the September baseline at the end, suits someone with a job or a foundation programme who can commit a concentrated block better than a long thin one. It also produces its result early enough to leave the final weeks for full papers. The fortnightly version suits a candidate with more available time and less competing structure. Both have a stated hour count.

faqs.question: What does November session preparation cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Priced honestly it is small. The evidence consultation is one or two sessions producing a written assessment. The six-month fortnightly record is roughly twelve to fourteen hours in total. An autumn intensive is twelve to sixteen hours in a block. Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work, and the Bestimate survey putting IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan or a time-zone move affect a November plan?
faqs.answer: Both are scheduling questions rather than plan changes. Ramadan's position in the Gregorian calendar moves earlier each year, so whether it falls inside a particular autumn differs between cohorts; where it does, sessions move to post-Iftar times and weekly output drops, which should be built into the hour count rather than discovered. A candidate who has moved to another country or time zone is accommodated by scheduling, which is one of the plainer practical advantages of running this work online rather than as home visits.

faqs.question: Can anyone promise a better grade in the November session?
faqs.answer: No. Grade boundaries are determined after a session on the basis of candidate performance across the whole cohort, so the mark needed for a given grade is not knowable while the preparation is happening. Any provider offering a specific grade, a specific lift or money back on a result is describing a sales position rather than how awarding works. What can honestly be committed to is a September baseline, a marked component every fortnight with the mark and date recorded, and a December review that says whether the trend supports continuing.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is available for the subject we are retaking?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with the options named. Retake requests cluster in a small number of subjects, but the scarce ones stay scarce: Higher Level Further Mathematics, a specific third paper, a minority language at ab initio level. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. For a candidate who may themselves have left the country, the online pool is frequently the only one that exists. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit.

abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.closingHeading: Read the breakdown before booking anything
abu-dhabi/ib-november-session-exam-prepa.closingBody: A November entry from Abu Dhabi is a decision before it is a revision plan, and the decision is made from the component breakdown rather than from the subject total. One weak paper in an otherwise adequate profile is a good retake. Flat low marks across every component usually are not. Ask the university whether the offer will be held, ask the school about carry-forward and the registration deadline, then send the breakdown and take the free 30-minute trial lesson. If the honest answer is not to enter, that is what you will be told.

abu-dhabi/ib-online-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below works to the same record-keeping standard: marked work back before the next session, an error log the family can see, and a written view at the halfway point. They name the subject group and level they teach rather than claiming the whole Diploma.

intro.heading: Judge the tuition by what it leaves behind
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi who have paid for tutoring before usually arrive with the same complaint, and it is rarely about the tutor's knowledge. It is that after a term they could not say what had happened. The sessions were pleasant, the student said they were useful, the school report moved slightly or not at all, and there was nothing to read. That is a record-keeping failure rather than a teaching failure, and it is the thing this page is about.

The useful question to ask any provider is not how experienced the tutors are. It is: at the end of eight weeks, what will I have? A good answer is specific and physical. A marked diagnostic paper with every lost mark tagged. A log of those errors, carried forward, with the ones that have stopped recurring crossed off. Annotated feedback on your child's own written work, in the tutor's handwriting or comments rather than rewritten prose. A short note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. And a written mid-term review comparing the current position against the first paper.

Online delivery makes that record easier rather than harder, which is the opposite of what families expect. A screen-shared past paper can be annotated and saved. A worked solution can be kept rather than rubbed off a whiteboard. The error log is a shared document rather than a note in someone's folder. None of that is possible in the same way at a kitchen table, and it is why this page argues for online one-to-one on its merits rather than on convenience. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visiting is a service offered only in India.

Abu Dhabi adds its own structure to this. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings, and enrolment is spread between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities. That geography matters less for an online arrangement than it does for an in-home one, but the term dates, the school transport times and the inspection cycle all shape when a session can realistically run and when a school's own internal deadlines land.

What follows is organised around the record rather than around the sales case. It sets out the artefacts a term of tuition should produce, how to read a marked IB script, what the IB permits a tutor to do with a draft, what grade movement actually looks like over weeks rather than in a promise, who regulates what in this emirate, and who is legally permitted to teach your child privately at all. Market rates are published in AED with their sources, and nothing on this page claims an outcome that cannot be evidenced.

abu-dhabi/ib-online-tuition.programmesIntro: The record looks different at each stage of the IB, because the assessments are different. Below is what a term of online tuition should produce at each of the four programmes, with what Abu Dhabi schools in particular do with them.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There are no external papers, so the evidence is different in kind: reading fluency measured against the same passage every few weeks, written work with the same success criteria applied twice, and number facts timed. Progress here is visible in the artefacts rather than in a grade, which is why the baseline matters so much. Without a dated starting sample there is nothing to compare against.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP schools run inquiry units on their own cycle, and the exhibition in the final year is the one piece of work parents see in detail. A tutor's contribution should be visible as questions in the margin and conversations about the student's own line of inquiry, never as text. Mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education sit alongside the programme from early on and take real timetable space.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment runs on four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a letter. The evidence that matters is a task marked against the published criterion descriptors twice: once as submitted, once after revision. Parents who have only seen the summative level rarely know which criterion is dragging the subject down, and that single piece of information usually changes what the hours are spent on.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-Diploma transition is the point where Abu Dhabi families most often look for help, because the step in writing demand is steeper than the step in content. A term of recorded work across Criterion C and D in sciences or humanities is the most useful thing to bring into Diploma year one, and it is worth keeping rather than discarding at the end of Year 11.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject has an internally assessed component and external papers with published weightings. The evidence trail here is the richest: timed papers, markband judgements written against the student's own answer, and a dated sequence of draft feedback on the internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are relatively small per school, which means a student struggling in a Higher Level subject may be one of very few doing so and may have no peer to compare with. That isolation is a real argument for one-to-one hours. It also means the school's internal deadlines for the internal assessment and Extended Essay are firm, because the coordinator is managing a tight cohort.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, plus a core including a reflective project and personal and professional skills. The evidence here is a mix: the Diploma-course papers are marked exactly as they would be for a full Diploma student, while the reflective project needs the same kind of dated draft trail as an Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is thinner on the ground in Abu Dhabi than the Diploma, so a student on it often has fewer subject-specialist teachers available for the Diploma courses they do take. Online one-to-one is frequently the only way to reach a specialist in the specific course combination, which is exactly the constraint that geography imposes on an in-home arrangement.

abu-dhabi/ib-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, with the component where the marks sit and the artefact a term of sessions should produce in each. The point of naming the component is that it makes progress checkable.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks are lost on multi-step proof and on calculus questions where the method is right but unwritten. The artefact is a timed paper with every lost mark tagged as recall, method, command term or timing, repeated every third week so the categories can be compared rather than described.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Heavier on modelling, statistics and technology use, and the losses cluster on interpreting a result in context rather than on computation. The evidence worth keeping is a set of written interpretations of the same data, marked twice, because that is the skill that moves and the one schools report on least precisely.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The commonest loss is an explanation that describes rather than explains, and the second commonest is dropped units. Higher Level adds an extra paper and additional topics. A term should produce a folder of markband-judged long answers, each with the specific missing step identified rather than a general comment about detail.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation chains and equilibrium reasoning are where grades move; data analysis in the internally assessed work is where the criteria bite. The artefact is the student's own draft with annotations against the published criteria, kept in sequence so the improvement between drafts is visible to the school as well as to you.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume and command terms rather than conceptual difficulty. Students who can describe a process often cannot structure a six-mark answer into distinct scoring points. The useful record is a long answer rewritten once after markband feedback, with both versions kept so the difference is legible.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the marks, and both are coachable quickly. The evidence is a diagram bank built by the student with axes and shifts checked, plus evaluation paragraphs marked against the markbands. Higher Level adds quantitative questions that are reliable marks and frequently skipped.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper one analysis reward a thesis that answers the question asked rather than a well-written essay about the text. Sessions produce annotated extracts and recorded oral practice with timings, which is the one component where a saved recording is genuinely more useful than a live comment.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the specific organisation in the stem separates bands, and generic answers cap in the lowest one however fluent. The record is a set of answers marked for application specifically, with the generic sentences struck through so the student can see what was not being credited.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic A
subjects.description: Abu Dhabi students frequently carry Arabic alongside the Diploma, and the two routes are marked quite differently. The useful artefact is timed writing against the published criteria, because fluency in speech often masks a written structure that does not reach the higher bands.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are supervised by the school and both need a dated trail of the student's own drafts. A tutor's role is to ask questions, point at an argument that does not follow, and explain the assessment criteria. The record is a sequence of questions and the student's own revisions, which is also what the school's supervision expects to see.

abu-dhabi/ib-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Abu Dhabi is spread out, and the relevant variable for tuition is not distance but what time a child is actually home and free. Here is how the week usually falls by community, and what that does to session timing when no tutor has to travel.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise living with short commutes to island schools, so a 16:30 start is often possible. Study space is the constraint rather than time, which is why a quiet corner and a headset matter more here than they do in a villa community.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Villa and apartment mix feeding a small number of nearby schools. Sessions commonly run at 17:00 or 17:30, and families here are frequently balancing competitive sport, which makes two fixed weekly slots more durable than flexible booking.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The longest school bus runs in the emirate at both ends of the day. Students are often home only after 16:00, pushing sessions to 17:30 or later and making weekend morning slots popular during Diploma coursework season.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Older, central districts with established schools close together. Sibling bookings in different year groups are common, usually run back to back in one evening rather than shared, which keeps the record separate for each child.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A newer catchment with growing cohorts, so Diploma classes are small and a student may be the only one in a Higher Level subject. That is exactly where reaching a specialist online rather than locally changes the options available.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: A large mainland catchment with a mixed school profile and long inbound journeys for any visiting tutor. Evening video sessions remove that journey entirely, which is the practical reason online dominates here.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah and the Corniche
regions.note: Dense central area with short school runs and a wide range of curricula within a few kilometres. Families often want help with one component before an internal deadline rather than ongoing weekly support.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK rather than the federal Ministry, and far enough from the capital that the local specialist pool for a Higher Level subject is genuinely thin. Online delivery is not a convenience here so much as the only route to a subject specialist.

schoolClusters.city: The islands: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Where most of the emirate's IB provision sits, with small Diploma cohorts and firm internal deadlines for the internal assessment and Extended Essay. Students we support across this cluster are often the only one in their year taking a particular Higher Level subject, which is what drives the demand for one-to-one hours.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland corridor: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: A broader curriculum mix, with IB schools alongside British and American ones in the same catchment. Transport times are long, which pushes sessions late and makes a fixed slot more valuable than a flexible one. Internal deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several of these schools.

modes.description: One or two fixed slots a week across a term or a year. This is the arrangement where the evidence trail is most valuable, because it accumulates: the error log from October is still being crossed off in February, and the mid-term review has something real to compare against. It is also the cheapest per hour of the three.

sections.heading: What a term of IB online tuition in Abu Dhabi should leave you holding
paragraphs: At the end of eight weeks you should have five things, and you should be able to read all of them without interpretation. A marked diagnostic paper from week one with every lost mark categorised. A running error log showing which of those errors have stopped recurring. Annotated feedback on your child's own written work, in comments rather than rewritten prose. A short note after each session recording what was covered and what was set. And a written mid-term review that compares the current position with the week-one paper.

That list is deliberately mundane. It contains no percentages, no satisfaction scores and no claims about typical outcomes, because none of those can be evidenced for an individual student and this market is full of providers publishing them anyway. What it does contain is a set of documents that let you answer the only question that matters: is this working, and on what basis do I believe that?

The reason to insist on it at the start rather than the end is that a record cannot be reconstructed afterwards. If week one produced no marked baseline, there is nothing for week eight to be compared against, and the conversation defaults to impressions. Ask for the baseline before you agree the hours. Any provider who treats that as an unusual request is telling you something useful about how they work.

There is one honest limitation worth stating. A record shows what has changed in the student's work; it does not predict a grade, and nobody can. Grade boundaries move, papers vary, and a student who has fixed a method problem can still have a difficult morning. What the record does is remove the guesswork about whether the hours are being spent usefully, which is a narrower claim and a true one.

sections.heading: A term counted out week by week, and what each week produces
paragraphs: Plans sold by the hour tend to be vague about sequence. The table below sets out what a standard twelve-week term of one-to-one online sessions actually produces, week by week, so you can check progress against a schedule rather than against a feeling. It is the shape most Abu Dhabi Diploma and Middle Years students start with, and it assumes two sessions a week.

The two weeks that carry the most information are week one and week six. Week one establishes the baseline, and a term that skips it never recovers the ability to measure. Week six is where the error log gets compared against the baseline and hours are reallocated: whichever loss category has not moved either needs a different approach or needs more time, and deciding that halfway through is far cheaper than discovering it at the end.

Two things on this schedule depend on your child's school rather than on us. Internal assessment and Extended Essay draft deadlines are set by the school's coordinator and vary between Abu Dhabi schools even within the same cluster, so the supervision-support weeks move to fit them. And the school's own mock window usually displaces two weeks of ordinary work, which is normal and worth planning for rather than treating as lost time.

What the schedule does not include is homework supervision. That is a different service, and conflating the two is how a term of tuition disappears into whatever was due tomorrow. If homework help is what is needed, it is cheaper bought as such; if the goal is grade movement on a named component, the sessions have to be protected from the week's deadlines.

sections.heading: Reading a marked IB script: the grade is the least informative part
paragraphs: A score on a paper tells you almost nothing actionable. The same mark can come from a student who knows the content and runs out of time, one who answers a different question than the one asked, and one who has three blank topics. Those three need entirely different terms of work, and the single number does not distinguish them. This is why the first session produces a categorised script rather than a mark.

The four categories are worth learning to spot yourself, because you can do it on any paper your child brings home. Recall losses are blanks or wrong facts: the content was never secure. Method losses are answers that reach the right place without showing the steps, or reach the wrong place after a correct start. Command-term losses are answers in the wrong register, where a question asking the student to evaluate receives a description. Timing losses are at the end of the paper, where the answers get shorter and then stop.

The proportions tell you what to buy. A script dominated by method and command-term losses is a technique problem, and technique responds quickly to one-to-one correction because the student already knows the content. A script dominated by recall losses is a content problem, which needs more weeks at a lower intensity and will not be solved by a short pre-paper block however many hours it contains. Being told which of these you are looking at, in writing, in week one, is the most valuable thing the first session produces.

In Middle Years subjects the same logic applies through the criterion letters rather than through mark categories. A summative level of five tells you little; knowing that Criterion C is at three while Criterion A is at seven tells you exactly where the term goes. Most parents have never been shown the criterion breakdown, and most schools will provide it if asked.

sections.heading: Draft work, feedback and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Every IB subject has an internally assessed component, and the Diploma core adds the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. All of it has to be the student's own work, submitted through a school that is accountable for its authenticity. That makes the feedback trail on draft work both the most useful thing a tutor produces and the place where this market behaves worst. One provider found in the wider UAE search results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750, which is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than a shortcut.

The boundary is easy to describe and easy to check. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria in the student's own subject, model a technique on a different question or dataset, ask questions about a draft, point to a paragraph and say that the conclusion does not follow from the evidence, and mark the student's own practice against the markbands. A tutor may not supply sentences that end up in the submission, under any framing. If feedback arrives as replacement prose rather than as questions and criterion references, the line has been crossed regardless of how it is labelled.

This is also where the record does double duty. A dated sequence of questions and the student's own revisions is exactly what a school's supervision process wants to see, and it protects the student if authenticity is ever queried. Families sometimes treat the paper trail as an administrative chore; it is better understood as the student's own evidence that the work is theirs.

One related rule. A tutor should not be supplying IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the IB, and reproducing them is copyright infringement. Current material is available through the school and the IB's own channels, and that is where a tutor should point you rather than attaching a bundle to an email.
bullets: Questions, criterion references and modelling on other material: all legitimate

sections.heading: What movement actually looks like, and how long it takes to show
paragraphs: The most common disappointment in a first term of tuition is a timing mismatch. A family expects the school report to move within six weeks; some things do move in six weeks and others cannot. Knowing which is which before you start removes most of the frustration, and it also tells you which component to target if the window is short.

The pattern is consistent enough to publish. Command-term accuracy and answer structure change fastest, because they are habits rather than knowledge, and a student who has been corrected on the same thing four times usually stops doing it. Timing improves next, once the student has sat enough papers under real conditions to know what pace feels like. Method discipline follows. Content recall is slowest, because it requires repeated retrieval over weeks and cannot be compressed.

Internal assessment and Extended Essay marks sit outside this entirely, because they move in discrete steps at each draft rather than gradually. A piece of work can sit at the same level for a month and then move two bands after one substantial revision. That is normal and it is why draft-stage support is scheduled around the school's deadlines rather than spread evenly.

The table below is a planning tool rather than a promise. No tutor can promise a grade, and the figures are stated as what typically becomes visible rather than what will happen. What it is useful for is deciding what to target: if you have five weeks, aim at the things that move in five weeks, and do not spend the block on the slowest-moving category.

sections.heading: ADEK, the regulators and what an inspection rating actually means for you
paragraphs: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes, and it is named by almost nobody in the tutoring market despite being the authority that governs every school its customers attend. Knowing which body governs what is practically useful, because it tells you who sets the rules your child's school is following and where to check a claim about a school.

The map is complete and public. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK. Dubai falls under the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not only inspection sits with the emirate.

What an inspection rating does not tell you is how your child's particular subject is taught. A school rated well overall can still have a thin Higher Level cohort in one subject, a teacher change mid-year, or a timetable that puts a difficult subject last on a Thursday. Parents sometimes read a strong rating as a reason not to need support and a weak one as a reason to panic; neither follows. The subject-level reality is what matters, and the marked script is the evidence for it.

One thing to be clear about, because the market is not. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim one. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is not the same as being endorsed by it, and any provider implying otherwise in this market should be asked to produce the permit number.

sections.heading: What online delivery changes about the record itself
paragraphs: The usual case for online tuition is convenience, and that is the least interesting part of it. The more substantial argument is that a video session with a shared screen produces a better record than a session at a table, and the record is what this page has been arguing matters.

Three concrete differences. A past paper annotated on a shared screen can be saved and reopened in the next session; a page annotated in pencil at a table usually goes into a folder and is not looked at again. A worked solution survives as a document rather than being wiped off a whiteboard. And the error log can be a live shared file that the student, the tutor and you are all looking at the same version of, which is the mechanism by which an error actually gets crossed off rather than forgotten.

There is a fourth difference that matters more in Abu Dhabi than in a denser city. An in-home tutor has to be someone willing to drive to your community at the time your child is free, which in practice limits the pool to a radius rather than to a subject. For a widely taught subject that is a mild constraint. For a Higher Level subject with a small cohort, in Al Ain or on Yas Island, it is often the difference between a specialist and a generalist. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the comparison here is between models rather than a sales point against our own other service.

The honest counterweight: some students work better with someone physically present, particularly younger ones and those who need the social pressure of a person in the room. If that is your child, say so at the trial lesson. The useful version of this comparison is a model-level one, which is what the table sets out, rather than an argument that one format wins for everyone.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach your child privately in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated, and the regulation is specific. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, and figures circulating online could not be verified against an official source, so no amount appears here. What a parent can do is ask any individual tutor whether they hold the permit and to show it, which is a reasonable and checkable question.

Abu Dhabi adds a rule that matters more here than elsewhere. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This has been reported in the press rather than read from the current policy document, so verify it against ADEK's own publication before relying on the exact wording. The principle is sound either way: your child's own classroom teacher is the wrong person to pay privately, however convenient it seems.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal category from an individual tutor and needs its own permit from the relevant emirate authority. This is why the phrase describing tutors as holding regulator approval should always be challenged: the permits in question attach either to an individual through MoHRE or to an institute with premises, and no tutoring platform is accredited by an education regulator simply by operating.
