sections.heading: What this costs in Abu Dhabi, and what you should refuse to pay for
paragraphs: Published UAE market rates, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 an hour, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey putting IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180 to 350, independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and BartyED AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Those are the providers' own published figures, not ours.

What is worth paying for in paper practice is marking and diagnosis by someone who knows what the assessment language actually requires. That is a skilled hour and it is where the mark movement comes from. What is not worth paying for is supervision while a student sits a paper, which they can do alone for nothing, or a provider's library of papers, which should come from the school and which no third party should be distributing in the first place.

The efficient arrangement for most Abu Dhabi families is fortnightly rather than weekly: the student sits and self-marks a paper in the fortnight, and the session is spent on comparison, categorisation and rewriting. Weekly marking sessions outrun the student's ability to produce and digest scripts, which means paying for an hour in which there is nothing new to diagnose.

We quote after a free trial lesson, and the trial is spent marking an existing script rather than talking about method. If that script shows a content gap rather than a technique problem, we will say so and recommend subject teaching instead, which is a different and usually longer purchase.

faqs.question: Can you send us IB past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. IB past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade boundary tables are the IB's copyright material, made available to schools through licensed access. The correct route is your child's subject teacher or the school's own resources, and a tutoring provider offering a library of papers is distributing material it has no right to distribute. There is a practical reason to care as well: unofficial paper banks often contain mislabelled papers or material from a superseded syllabus, which is a real risk in recently revised subjects.

faqs.question: How do we get past papers for my child's subjects in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask the subject teacher, specifically and narrowly. A request for papers or questions on the two topics your child is currently revising is almost always granted; a request for everything available usually is not. Also ask the Diploma coordinator what the school's policy is on releasing full papers before mocks, since schools reserve some for timed practice. Teachers in this emirate are generally willing, and the papers they supply are matched to the syllabus your child is actually sitting.

faqs.question: When should a DP student start doing full past papers?
faqs.answer: From the middle of the second Diploma year, and immediately before each set of school mocks. Before that, question-level work on topics already taught does the same job without the discouragement of meeting untaught content in an exam format. One exception is worth making early: read one paper of each type with its mark scheme in DP1, simply to know what the document looks like. That is an hour, once, rather than a programme of full papers in the first year.

faqs.question: Why does my child do lots of papers and not improve?
faqs.answer: Because doing a paper and practising are different activities. The marks come from what happens afterwards: marking the script severely against the scheme, categorising each lost mark into a fault type, and rewriting the two highest-value answers under time to prove the fix. A student who completes twelve papers and marks none of them properly has spent twelve hours confirming what they already knew. The marking half is the half that moves marks and the half almost everyone skips.

faqs.question: How should a student mark their own script honestly?
faqs.answer: By awarding a mark only where the words on the page would earn it from a marker who has never met them and will infer nothing. If the scheme wants a comparison and the script implies one, no mark. If a unit is missing, no mark. If the working happened in the student's head, no method mark. Applying that rule is uncomfortable for about three papers and then becomes automatic, and it is the single most valuable habit in exam preparation because every subsequent decision depends on an accurate score.

faqs.question: What is an error log and how does my child keep one?
faqs.answer: A single running document with one line per lost mark and four columns: the paper and question, what the question asked for, what the student actually did, and the fault type. It takes about two minutes per paper. The fault types repeat across subjects: command term misread, mark allocation ignored, working not shown, units missing, data not used, question not answered, timing collapse, content gap. Only the last is a revision problem, and the log makes clear which fortnight's work should target which fault.

faqs.question: How much time should a six-mark question get?
faqs.answer: Divide the paper's total time by its total marks, which is printed on the front cover, then multiply by six. On a paper with 80 marks in 120 minutes that is one and a half minutes per mark, so nine minutes. The point of the arithmetic is not precision but allocation: students lose far more marks to spending twenty minutes on an interesting eight-mark question than to being slow. Have your child write their own figures on a card and use them in every timed practice.

faqs.question: What should my child do when a question stalls in an exam?
faqs.answer: Mark it, leave space, and move on, according to a rule agreed in advance. The marks at the end of a paper are usually easier than the marks being fought over in the middle, so a student who cannot abandon a question is trading cheap marks for expensive ones. The rule needs a trigger: when the question has consumed its mark allocation in minutes and the method is still not clear, it goes. Agreeing that takes one minute and is worth more than most revision.

faqs.question: Which command terms cause the most lost marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, outline, evaluate and discuss, in our experience of Diploma scripts. Explain answers written as descriptions lose the reasoning marks. Outline answers written as explanations waste time that the rest of the paper needed. Evaluate and discuss answers that list two sides without reaching a judgement lose the judgement marks. The corrective exercise is the same for all of them: before writing, underline the command term and the mark allocation, and let those two things alone decide the shape of the answer.

faqs.question: Are these sessions online, or do you come to the house?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Marking work is screen work: the student's script, their own marking, the scheme they used and the error log all need to be visible at once. A family in Al Ain or Al Shamkha also gets a tutor who teaches their child's actual subject at their actual level, rather than whoever is within an evening's drive.

faqs.question: What does past paper marking cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where travel is priced in, and AED 650 at one provider for a named tutor. Those are their figures, not ours. What is worth paying for is the marking and diagnosis hour. What is not is supervision while a student sits a paper, or access to a provider's paper library.

faqs.question: Is weekly paper marking better than fortnightly?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A student needs time to sit a paper properly, mark it themselves, and rewrite the answers the last session identified, and a week rarely contains that alongside school. Fortnightly sessions mean each hour has something new to diagnose, which is what you are paying for. Weekly becomes sensible in the final two months before the May session, when the student is producing papers at volume and the limiting factor is how fast scripts can be marked and categorised.

faqs.question: Should my child redo a paper they have already done?
faqs.answer: Only the answers that lost marks, and only under time. Redoing a whole paper tests memory of that paper rather than technique, and the familiar questions produce an inflated score that distorts the error log. The useful version is narrow: take the two answers with the most marks available, rewrite them to time without looking at the previous attempt or the scheme, and then mark them. That is twenty minutes and it is the step that proves a technique fix has actually taken hold.

faqs.question: How should practice work around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Full timed papers are better scheduled either side of the month rather than inside it, because school days shorten and the evening reorganises around iftar. Question-level work and marking sessions fit comfortably into a shorter post-iftar slot, so the diagnosis half of the work continues uninterrupted. We move our sessions later rather than pausing them, because the weeks around Ramadan sit close to the final mock period for many Abu Dhabi schools and a month's gap is expensive at that point.

faqs.question: My child's mock script came back. What should we do with it?
faqs.answer: Read it question by question with someone who can mark it, which is the single most valuable hour of tutoring available in the two years. The mock is usually the only full paper a student sits under real conditions before the May session, so the script carries information no practice paper can: how the timing actually went, what happened in the final section, and which marks were cheapest to recover. Most scripts get glanced at and filed, which wastes the one genuinely realistic data point a student has.

abu-dhabi/ib-past-papers-practice.closingHeading: Bring a script, not a request for papers
abu-dhabi/ib-past-papers-practice.closingBody: Ask your child's subject teacher for a paper on a topic already covered, have them sit it and mark it themselves without mercy, and bring both the script and their marking to the free trial lesson. We will mark it independently, show you the gap between the two scores, and start an error log with a fault type against every lost mark. By the end of the hour you will know whether the problem is technique, which moves in weeks, or content, which takes longer and needs a different kind of teaching.

intro.heading: A Physics IA is marked on evidence, so the support should leave evidence too
paragraphs: The IB Physics internal assessment is a single scientific investigation reported in no more than 3,000 words, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. It is 20% of the Physics grade at Standard and Higher Level alike, marked by the school and moderated externally by the IB. Schools allocate class time for it, and in Abu Dhabi that allocation almost never covers the part students find hardest, which is making their own data defensible.

Parents here usually arrive with a specific artefact in hand: a draft, a teacher's comment, or a mark in the middle of the range with no explanation of how to move it. That is the right place to start, and it is why this page is built around evidence rather than reassurance. A Physics IA is assessed on what is on the page, so the only useful account of tutoring is what changes on the page, week by week, with a mark attached to each version. If a tutor cannot name the criterion a session worked on and the mark the draft now earns, there is nothing for a parent to check.

The pattern in Abu Dhabi drafts is consistent enough to be predictable. Research design is competent: students pick a sensible relationship, identify variables and control what they can. Data analysis is where marks start to leak, because uncertainties are stated but not propagated, graphs carry no error bars, and gradients are read off without any account of what the uncertainty in that gradient actually is. Conclusion then cites a literature value without comparing it properly, and evaluation lists weaknesses without ranking them by effect on the result.

None of that is a physics knowledge problem. A student scoring a 6 in Physics can score fourteen out of twenty-four on the investigation, because the report never shows the quantitative reasoning the criteria ask for. That is good news for a family deciding whether tutoring is worth it, because the fixes are specific, visible and markable, and you can check them yourself against each returned draft rather than waiting for a report card.

All of it happens one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For investigation work that suits the task: the student shares their spreadsheet, the tutor recalculates an uncertainty live, and the graph is rebuilt on screen with error bars while the student watches the gradient uncertainty change. ADEK licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools, which set their own IA deadlines, and those deadlines cluster, so the earlier a draft exists the more a session can do with it.

abu-dhabi/ib-physics-ia-help.programmesIntro: The investigation is a DP task, but the practical skills behind it start much earlier in the IB continuum. Here is what each programme contributes for a family in this emirate.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics is taken at SL or HL from group four. The internal assessment is one scientific investigation, 24 marks, 20% of the grade, with the remaining 80% sat in written papers. HL students meet additional content and additional-higher-level material, but the investigation specification and its criteria are identical at both levels.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools generally run the investigation in the second half of DP1 or the first term of DP2, in the same window as the Mathematics exploration. Families here frequently need both tasks supported in the same two months, which is a scheduling problem more than a subject one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Sciences is assessed partly on inquiring and designing and on processing and evaluating, which are the direct ancestors of the DP criteria. A student who has written MYP lab reports arrives knowing what a controlled variable is, though usually not how to propagate an uncertainty.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools around Al Raha and Saadiyat produce DP1 physicists comfortable with lab writing. Students arriving from a British or Indian system in the emirate often meet uncertainty analysis for the first time in the DP, which is one or two extra sessions, predictably.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry in the PYP builds the habit of asking what would change the result, which is the question criterion D eventually asks formally. None of it is externally assessed, so nothing here affects a Diploma grade, but the reflex matters.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Abu Dhabi with children across several programmes often ask when science becomes graded by the IB. For Physics the answer is the DP: the investigation is the first science coursework that carries marks towards a Diploma.

abu-dhabi/ib-physics-ia-help.subjectsIntro: An investigation can sit anywhere in the syllabus, but some themes give cleaner data and easier uncertainty analysis than others. These are the areas we work in and what each means for a 24-mark report.

subjects.name: Space, time and motion
subjects.description: Kinematics, forces, momentum and energy. The most common investigation territory because the apparatus is accessible and the relationships are clean. The risk is a projectile or pendulum study so familiar that criterion A scores low for an unoriginal, under-justified design.

subjects.name: The particulate nature of matter
subjects.description: Thermal physics, gas laws and energy transfer. Excellent for linearisation, because several relationships become straight lines under the right substitution, which is exactly what criterion B rewards. Temperature control is the main experimental weakness to address in the design.

subjects.name: Wave behaviour
subjects.description: Standing waves, resonance, refraction and interference. Rich data and unforgiving measurement: a resonance tube investigation can produce beautiful results or an unusable data set depending on how the fundamental is identified and how the end correction is handled.

subjects.name: Fields
subjects.description: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields, circuits and electromagnetic induction. Circuit investigations are the safest route to a strong data set because instruments give repeatable readings with known instrumental uncertainties, which makes propagation straightforward to show.

subjects.name: Nuclear and quantum physics
subjects.description: Radioactivity, fission and quantum phenomena. Distinctive and difficult to do experimentally at school level in this emirate, so students here usually approach it through simulation or secondary data, which requires a much stronger justification under criterion A.

subjects.name: Additional higher level content
subjects.description: Rotational dynamics, thermodynamic cycles and further field theory. An HL student is not required to investigate HL content, but a design drawn from it often produces a more interesting relationship and a more defensible claim to originality.

subjects.name: Uncertainty and error analysis
subjects.description: Not a theme but the backbone of criterion B. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainties, propagation through products and powers, uncertainty in a gradient from maximum and minimum lines, and knowing when a result is consistent with a literature value.

subjects.name: Data logging and sensors
subjects.description: Where a school has the equipment, sensor data raises resolution and sample size at once. It also introduces systematic effects worth discussing in criterion D, such as calibration drift and sampling rate, which gives evaluation something quantitative to say.

subjects.name: Simulation and secondary data investigations
subjects.description: Permitted and sometimes the only option for a topic, but the design has to work harder: the model's assumptions, the source's reliability and the parameter ranges must all be justified. We treat these as higher-risk routes and say so before a student commits.

sections.heading: What IB physics IA help in Abu Dhabi actually involves
paragraphs: It involves four criteria and nothing else. Research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation are worth six marks each, and every hour of tutoring should be traceable to one of them. A session that improves a student's general physics is a good session and may not move the report at all, which is why we express every output as a criterion, a mark and a reason, and send it in writing afterwards.

The first substantive question in any first session is what evidence exists. Raw data in a spreadsheet is evidence. A teacher's comment is evidence. A full draft is the best evidence of all, because it can be marked cold, and a cold mark from someone who does not know the student is a closer approximation of moderation than a teacher's mark can be. Where there is nothing yet, the session goes on design, which is the stage with the highest return.

The second question is whether the data can support a claim. Physics investigations fail quietly at this point. A student has eight data points across a narrow range with no repeats, and no analysis will rescue it: the gradient uncertainty will swamp the result, and criterion C will have nothing to conclude. Saying this plainly in week one, when there is still time to collect more, is worth more than any amount of help with the writing in week four.

The third is the quantitative reasoning the criteria want shown. Absolute and percentage uncertainties on every measured quantity, propagation through the calculation, error bars on the graph, a gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines, and a conclusion that states whether the accepted value lies within the experimental range. That sequence is where most of the recoverable marks in an Abu Dhabi draft are sitting.

sections.heading: The twenty-four marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The four criteria are equally weighted at six marks each, which is unusual and strategically important. A student who pours effort into a beautiful method and neglects evaluation is leaving a quarter of the mark on the table. We have read drafts from this emirate with immaculate designs and two-paragraph evaluations, scoring five out of six on criterion A and two out of six on criterion D.

Research design covers the research question, the methodology and the justification of both. Data analysis covers processing, uncertainties and graphical treatment. Conclusion covers the interpretation of the result and its comparison with accepted scientific context. Evaluation covers strengths, weaknesses and realistic improvements, discussed in terms of their actual effect on the result rather than listed.

The table below is our reading diagnostic, not the official rubric: it is what we look for when marking a draft cold, expressed as the thing on the page that separates a four from a six. Read the real criterion descriptors in your child's own copy of the Physics guide, in the edition their school teaches. We reference the guide and work from the school's wording; we do not reproduce or supply IB documents or mark schemes.

One structural point about the 3,000-word ceiling. It is enough for a focused report and not enough for a narrative one. Reports that run out of words before evaluation have usually spent 600 of them restating theory that the examiner already knows. Theory earns marks only where it justifies a design decision or explains a discrepancy.

sections.heading: Uncertainties: where Physics investigations in this emirate lose criterion B
paragraphs: Criterion B is the one Abu Dhabi drafts most often under-score, and the reason is almost always the same. Uncertainties are recorded conscientiously in the raw data table and then abandoned. The processed column has no uncertainty attached, the graph has no error bars, the gradient is read as a single number, and the conclusion quotes a result to four significant figures with no range at all.

The repair is mechanical and teachable in one session. Each measured quantity carries an absolute uncertainty from the instrument's resolution or from the spread of repeats, whichever is larger. Fractional uncertainties add through products and quotients and multiply through powers. The processed value therefore carries a calculable uncertainty, which becomes the error bar. Maximum and minimum gradient lines through the error bars give the uncertainty in the gradient, and that uncertainty is what makes the conclusion defensible.

The table below is the practical reference we use on screen. The values in it are typical instrument resolutions a student in a school lab will encounter, offered so a student can sanity-check their own numbers rather than as a substitute for reading the instrument. A stopwatch's resolution is not the uncertainty in a human-timed measurement, and that distinction alone is worth a mark.

Significant figures are the small, cheap version of the same point. A processed value quoted to more figures than its uncertainty justifies is a visible signal that the uncertainty was never carried through, and markers read it that way. Round the uncertainty to one or two significant figures and match the value to it.

No allowance for the probe not having reached equilibrium

Around 1 degree, with parallax discussed if read by eye

sections.heading: Research design: one relationship, one range, one justification
paragraphs: Criterion A rewards a focused research question with a justified method, and the most common failure is breadth. A question asking how temperature affects resistance is three investigations in a sentence. A question asking how the resistance of a 30 cm length of a specified wire varies with temperature between 20 and 80 degrees Celsius, measured at ten-degree intervals with five repeats, is one investigation with a range and a plan.

The second half of criterion A is justification, and students routinely justify what they controlled while skipping why they chose this relationship, this range and this apparatus. A single sentence tying the expected relationship to theory, and another explaining why the chosen range will produce a measurable change, is worth more than a page of apparatus description.

Design is also where originality lives. The criteria do not demand a novel experiment, but a design that twenty classmates have submitted is harder to justify as the student's own thinking. A standard pendulum investigation can still score well if the student narrows it to something specific and defends the narrowing, which is the difference between following a practical sheet and designing an investigation.

We ask three questions before any data is collected. Can you measure the dependent variable to a precision that will show a change across your range? Will you get at least seven or eight distinct values of the independent variable with repeats at each? And what will you do if the relationship is not what you expect, because a null or unexpected result is a legitimate investigation and needs a plan rather than a panic.

Justify the range and the apparatus, not only the controlled variables
Seven or eight distinct values of the independent variable, with repeats at each
A plan for an unexpected result before the data is collected

sections.heading: What the evidence trail looks like across four sessions
paragraphs: Because this task is marked on what is on the page, progress is checkable. The table below is the trail we aim to produce for a student who comes to us with raw data already collected, which is the most common starting point in this emirate. Each row is an artefact a parent can look at, and the marks shown are the kind of movement that is realistic rather than promised.

Two things are worth saying plainly about those numbers. They are illustrative of the structure of the work, not a prediction for any individual student, and we publish no figures about average improvements because we cannot show you the data behind such a claim. What we can show you is the mark we gave each draft and the reason, which is the only honest evidence a tutor can offer.

The trail matters for a second reason. A student who can show a dated sequence from design to final report has strong evidence that the work is their own, which several Abu Dhabi schools now ask for explicitly. Building that record deliberately is better than reconstructing it if anyone asks.

Where the trail stalls, that is information too. A draft that gets the same criterion B mark twice means the propagation has not been understood rather than not been explained, and the session plan changes accordingly. Marking each version is what makes that visible instead of invisible, and it is also what tells a family when to stop buying sessions, because a draft whose weakest criterion is now the student's own rewriting job does not need another hour of tutoring.

sections.heading: Linearising, plotting and reading a gradient properly
paragraphs: A large share of criterion B sits in one decision: what to plot against what. A relationship that is a curve on the first attempt is usually a straight line under the right substitution, and plotting the straight-line version is both easier to analyse and far easier to defend. A period against length graph is a curve; a period squared against length graph is a line whose gradient has a physical meaning the student can state.

Once the plot is linear, three things follow. Error bars come from the propagated uncertainties, not from a guess. The best-fit line is drawn through the bars and not through the points alone. Maximum and minimum gradient lines, both passing through the bars, give an uncertainty in the gradient that the student can quote alongside it. That final number is the one criterion C needs, because a result without a range cannot be compared with an accepted value in any meaningful way.

Spreadsheet software will supply a trend line and a correlation coefficient at the click of a button, and students reach for both. The correlation coefficient is weak evidence here: a high value on a poorly designed data set proves little, and criterion B is not asking for it. What markers want is a gradient with its uncertainty and an explanation of what the gradient physically represents, including its units.

The intercept is often ignored and frequently the most interesting part of the graph. An intercept that should be at the origin and is not is evidence of a systematic effect, which gives criterion D something quantitative to discuss instead of a list of generic weaknesses. Pointing a student at their own intercept is one of the most productive five minutes in a marking session.
bullets: Choose the substitution that makes the relationship linear, and say why
Error bars from propagated uncertainties, best-fit line drawn through them
Gradient uncertainty from maximum and minimum lines, quoted with units
Discuss the intercept: an unexpected one is evidence of a systematic effect

sections.heading: What a Physics tutor may and may not do, and the safety line as well
paragraphs: The investigation must be the student's own work. The IB treats a breach as malpractice affecting the whole Diploma, and there are providers in this market selling completed internal assessments. A family buying one is buying a risk to the award rather than a mark, and no amount of deadline pressure makes that a reasonable trade.

A tutor may teach the physics; review a design before data collection; question whether a data set can support a claim; demonstrate uncertainty propagation on numbers the student is not using; mark a draft against the four criteria; point out that an evaluation lists rather than ranks; and check significant figures, units and the word count. A tutor may say honestly that a draft is already strong and needs no further sessions.

A tutor may not produce the work. No data is generated or adjusted on the student's behalf, which in a practical subject is worth stating explicitly: invented or tidied data is a fabrication, not a presentation choice, and markers notice data that is too good. No text is supplied for pasting. No graph is produced for the student from their numbers; they make it and we mark it.

There is also a safety and ethics line specific to the sciences. An investigation involving mains electricity, lasers, radioactive sources, significant heights or chemical hazards needs the school's supervision and risk assessment, and work involving other people as subjects needs informed consent handled as the school requires. We will not help design a home experiment that belongs in a supervised lab, and we say so at the design stage rather than after the fact.
bullets: A tutor teaches, questions, demonstrates on other numbers and marks against the criteria
A tutor never generates, adjusts or tidies the student's data
Hazardous work belongs in the school lab under the school's risk assessment
Keep dated drafts and raw data files as evidence of authorship

sections.heading: Timing, Ramadan, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges
paragraphs: Schools set their own internal assessment deadlines and work back from the May session, which puts the Physics investigation late in DP1 or early in DP2, usually within a fortnight of the Mathematics exploration. Counted backwards from the school's deadline, the design review belongs eight weeks out, data collection six weeks out, a full draft four weeks out so a teacher's mark is still actionable, and the final fortnight on evaluation and presentation only.

Ramadan shifts the evening. School days shorten, households reorganise around iftar, and the 5pm slot disappears across the emirate. We move sessions to post-iftar timing rather than pausing, because the Ramadan weeks often sit on the drafting window. Students also sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside the Diploma should note that UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and that the Cambridge February and March series is offered in India only.

On cost, the most useful angle for a Physics family is what the travel premium buys, because the in-home market is where Abu Dhabi rates climb. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 survey puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists. TutorChase publishes AED 270, EdFlik AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya AED 33 to 52, and BartyED AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Those are the providers' own published figures, read in October 2026.

What the premium buys, for this task specifically, is a person in the room and a tutor drawn from whoever is within driving distance on a weekday evening. What it does not buy is a better view of a spreadsheet. Uncertainty propagation and graph work happen on a shared screen either way, which is the honest reason we deliver this online rather than a claim that online is always better. We quote our own fee after the free trial lesson.

process.title: Send the data, the question and the deadline
process.description: Three things get a useful answer: the research question, whatever data exists, and the school's deadline. We will say how many sessions the report needs and whether a Physics specialist is free in that window before any money changes hands.

process.title: Free trial on a cold read
process.description: The first lesson is free and is spent marking what exists rather than on introductions. The student leaves with a criterion-level mark, a verdict on whether the data set can support a conclusion, and one specific task to complete before the next session.

process.title: One criterion per session, with a written mark
process.description: Each session targets the weakest criterion and ends with a written mark and reason sent to the family. The student rewrites between sessions. This is what makes progress visible rather than a matter of impressions.

process.title: Final pass on figures, units and word count
process.description: Significant figures matched to uncertainties, units on every axis and in every table header, graph captions numbered and referenced, sources cited, and the report inside its 3,000-word ceiling. Marks lost here are lost to inattention.

process.title: Decide about the papers
process.description: The investigation is twenty per cent of the grade. If the papers are the weaker side we will say so and scope weekly work instead. If they are not, the engagement ends with the report, which is a normal and expected outcome.

whyPoints.title: A written mark after every session
whyPoints.description: Each session ends with a criterion, a mark out of six and the reason, sent to the family. A parent can see what changed between draft two and draft three instead of taking a tutor's word for it.

whyPoints.title: Quantitative work, not encouragement
whyPoints.description: Most recoverable marks in an Abu Dhabi Physics draft sit in propagated uncertainties, error bars and gradient uncertainty. Sessions are spent on those calculations with the student's own numbers on screen, not on general revision advice.

whyPoints.title: An honest early verdict on the data
whyPoints.description: If eight points across a narrow range cannot support a conclusion, we say so in week one while there is still time to collect more. That verdict is uncomfortable and far more valuable than help with the writing in week four.

whyPoints.title: Design review before measurement
whyPoints.description: The cheapest intervention in the whole task is one session before any data is collected. Families who book it rarely need the expensive rescue session, and we would rather sell the first than the second.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty and lab safety stated
whyPoints.description: No data is generated or adjusted for a student, no text supplied, and no hazardous home experiment designed around a school's supervision. These are the lines that separate tutoring from the finished-IA trade operating in this market.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not proximity
whyPoints.description: Physics investigation marking is a specialism, and in Al Ain or the outer communities there may be nobody local who has done it. Online delivery means your child works with someone who has, on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel premium on the hour.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB Physics internal assessment worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four marks, split equally across four criteria worth six each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The report has a 3,000-word ceiling and counts for twenty per cent of the final Physics grade at both Standard and Higher Level, with the other eighty per cent sat in written papers. The school marks it and the IB moderates externally. The equal weighting matters strategically: a student who writes a superb method and a two-paragraph evaluation is leaving a quarter of the available mark untouched.

faqs.question: Why did my child's Physics investigation lose marks on data analysis?
faqs.answer: Almost always because uncertainties were recorded and then abandoned. The raw data table carries them, the processed column does not, the graph has no error bars, and the gradient is read as a single number with no range. Criterion B wants the uncertainties propagated through the calculation, plotted as error bars, and converted into a gradient uncertainty using maximum and minimum lines. That sequence is mechanical and teachable in about one session, and it is where most of the recoverable marks in a competent draft are sitting.

faqs.question: How do you work out the uncertainty in a gradient?
faqs.answer: Draw the steepest and shallowest lines that still pass through the error bars on your plotted points, find the gradient of each, and take half the difference between them as the uncertainty in your best-fit gradient. Quote the gradient with that uncertainty and with its units. This is what lets the conclusion say something defensible, because a result with a range can be compared with an accepted value, while a bare number cannot. A spreadsheet trend line will not give you this, which is why the manual construction still matters.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help design the experiment before my child collects data?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most useful session in the task. A design review narrows the research question to one measurable relationship with a stated range, checks that the dependent variable can be measured precisely enough to show a change, confirms there will be seven or eight distinct values with repeats, and identifies the instrumental uncertainties in advance. The student then takes the design to their own teacher for approval. A weak design cannot be rescued by analysis, so an hour here routinely saves three later.

faqs.question: Is a simulation or secondary data acceptable for the Physics IA?
faqs.answer: It is permitted, and sometimes it is the only route to a topic a school cannot support in its lab, but the design has to work considerably harder. The model's assumptions, the reliability of the source and the justification for the parameter ranges all have to be argued under criterion A, and criterion D has to evaluate the model rather than the apparatus. We treat these as higher-risk routes and tell students so before they commit, because a weak simulation investigation is harder to rescue than a weak practical one.

faqs.question: What should go in the evaluation to score well on criterion D?
faqs.answer: Weaknesses ranked by their actual effect on the result, with improvements that would change the number rather than tidy the method. A list saying the thermometer was imprecise, the room was draughty and more repeats would help scores poorly because nothing is quantified. An evaluation that identifies the dominant uncertainty, estimates how much of the discrepancy it explains, and proposes a specific change that would reduce it scores well. An unexpected intercept on the graph is often the best available evidence of a systematic effect worth discussing here.

faqs.question: My child has eight data points and no repeats. Is that enough?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and finding out now is worth a great deal more than finding out after the draft is written. Eight distinct values is around the minimum, and without repeats there is no way to estimate the spread of readings, which means the uncertainties will come only from instrument resolution and will understate reality. If there is still lab access, the right move is a second collection round with repeats at each value. If there is not, the report has to be honest about the limitation, and criterion D is where that honesty earns marks.

faqs.question: Are IB Physics IA sessions online or in person in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For this task the shared screen is genuinely the right tool: the student's spreadsheet, the graph being rebuilt with error bars, and the criteria are all visible at once, and the tutor can recalculate a propagated uncertainty live while the student watches the gradient uncertainty change. No part of that improves by adding a drive across the emirate.

faqs.question: What does Physics IA support cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE figures run AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, and AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where the travel premium applies. One provider publishes AED 650 for a named tutor. Those are the providers' own numbers, read in October 2026, not ours. Most investigation work is three to four sessions, so the total is closer to a month of tutoring than a term. We quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: Can a tutor check my child's data for errors?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question it, which is different from correcting it. We will ask whether a reading that breaks the pattern was recorded or transcribed wrongly, whether the instrument drifted during the run, and whether an outlier should be investigated or discussed. What we will not do is alter the numbers or suggest which ones to quietly drop. Data must be reported as collected, and anomalies belong in the analysis and evaluation where they earn marks. Invented or tidied data is a fabrication and markers do notice data that is too clean.

faqs.question: How long should the Physics investigation report be?
faqs.answer: Up to 3,000 words, and that is a ceiling rather than a target. The commonest structural fault we see is a report that spends six hundred words restating textbook theory and then runs out of space for evaluation, which is worth a quarter of the mark. Theory earns credit only where it justifies a design decision or explains a discrepancy. Data tables, graph captions and references are handled according to your school's guidance, so check how yours counts them before planning the final draft.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi DP Physics student start the investigation?
faqs.answer: Design review around eight weeks before the school's deadline, data collection six weeks out, and a full draft four weeks out so a teacher's mark still leaves time to act. Schools in the emirate set their own dates but work back from the May session, which usually puts the Physics investigation late in DP1 or early in DP2, often within a fortnight of the Mathematics exploration. That collision is the real reason the term feels overloaded, and it is manageable if the design work happens before it starts.

faqs.question: Does my child need to investigate higher level content at HL?
faqs.answer: No. The investigation specification and its four criteria are identical at Standard and Higher Level, and nothing requires HL students to draw their topic from additional higher level material. In practice an HL student choosing from that content often ends up with a more interesting relationship and a stronger claim to having designed something themselves, which helps under criterion A. But an SL-level topic investigated rigorously will out-score an HL-level topic investigated carelessly, every time.

faqs.question: How are Physics sessions scheduled around Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: They shift later rather than stopping. School hours shorten, households reorganise around iftar, and the usual 5pm slot stops working, so we schedule post-iftar sessions instead. Continuity matters in this task because the Ramadan weeks frequently overlap the drafting window, and a month's pause lands on the exact fortnight when a marked draft is most useful. For a student who is fasting, two shorter sessions a week with marked drafts in between usually works better than one long evening session.

faqs.question: What if no Physics specialist is free before our deadline?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of substituting a general science tutor. Investigation marking against the four criteria is a specific skill, and demand concentrates in the fortnights when Abu Dhabi schools' deadlines cluster. If nobody suitable is free in your window, the realistic options are a later slot with written draft feedback in the meantime, a tutor outside the emirate on a compatible evening schedule, or the school's own clinic hours with a specific list of what to ask. An honest no beats a poor match on a graded component.

abu-dhabi/ib-physics-ia-help.closingHeading: Bring the data and the teacher's comment
abu-dhabi/ib-physics-ia-help.closingBody: If your child has collected data, the first useful step is a cold mark on what exists. Send the research question, the spreadsheet and whatever the teacher has written, and the free trial lesson will produce a criterion-level mark, an honest verdict on whether the data can support a conclusion, and one specific task to do next. You will be able to see what changes between that draft and the next one, because every session ends with a mark and a reason in writing. If the draft is already strong, we will tell you that and you can stop there.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here work with Diploma candidates in Abu Dhabi in the months before predictions close, producing dated marked work a subject teacher can weigh and giving written feedback on the student's own internal assessment drafts against the published criteria.

intro.heading: You cannot buy a prediction. You can change the evidence behind it
paragraphs: A predicted grade in the Diploma Programme is a professional judgement made by the subject teacher, signed off by the school, about the grade a candidate is likely to achieve in the final session. It is not a mark, not an entitlement, and not negotiable in the way a parent might negotiate a price. It is also the single most consequential number in a Diploma candidate's second year, because it is what a university sees months before any real result exists. Those two facts together explain why this search exists and why most of what is written for it is dishonest.

The dishonest version promises movement. A tutor offers to raise a prediction, or implies that enrolling will. Nobody outside the school can do that, and a page claiming otherwise is describing a transaction that does not exist. The honest version is narrower and considerably more useful: a teacher's judgement rests on evidence, that evidence is specific and partly within a candidate's control, and there is a window of weeks in which adding to it is possible before the prediction is finalised.

So this page is about evidence. What a subject teacher in an Abu Dhabi Diploma school actually looks at when forming a prediction. Which of those inputs a candidate can still affect in October, in December, in February. What a marked timed paper produced in the right week is worth compared with a reported improvement in confidence. And how to have the conversation with a coordinator about what evidence would change a judgement, which is a legitimate question and one most schools will answer.

The timing is unforgiving and deserves stating plainly. The earliest UK application deadline falls in mid-October, and the main one in mid-January, with North American and UAE university timelines spread across the same window. Most Abu Dhabi schools therefore finalise predictions in the autumn or early winter of the second Diploma year, often immediately after the mock window. By the time a family sees a prediction they dislike, the evidence period behind it has usually closed. Acting in September is cheap; acting in February is mostly about the real session instead.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. On this particular job, the online format matters because turnaround does: a timed paper marked within two days of being sat, with a written component breakdown, is evidence a teacher can use. A session scheduled around an Abu Dhabi school run three weeks later is not. The format also widens the pool, which matters when the subject in question is HL Chemistry or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and the family lives in Al Ain or Al Shamkha rather than beside an island school. Choosing a specialist who can mark to the published criteria is a different decision from choosing whoever can reach an address before seven in the evening, and only one of those decisions produces a document a subject teacher will weigh.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.programmesIntro: Predictions are a Diploma phenomenon, but the habits that produce a defensible one start earlier. These are the IB programmes running in Abu Dhabi schools and what each contributes to the evidence a prediction eventually rests on.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No grades and no predictions, but the written-explanation habit that later separates a 5 from a 6 in Group 4 subjects is built here. Assessment is continuous and reported against the programme's framework, which parents arriving from examination-led systems often find hard to read as progress.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP schools vary in how much examination-style practice they introduce late in the programme. The useful question for a parent is how the school will evidence readiness for MYP, because that is the first point at which criterion-based judgement starts to look like a grade.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks are awarded against criteria A to D with published descriptors, and this is where a student first learns that a judgement can be evidenced rather than merely received. Students who learn to read a criterion descriptor in MYP 4 are considerably better placed to understand a Diploma prediction two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Some Abu Dhabi schools run MYP to Year 11 with eAssessment, others switch to IGCSE at Year 10. Either way, the final MYP or IGCSE profile is the first substantial piece of evidence a Diploma subject teacher inherits about a new student, which makes it part of the prediction story before the Diploma even begins.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme where predictions are made. Six subject predictions plus the core are sent to universities, and each one is a subject teacher's judgement about an outcome in the final session. The inputs are classwork, internal assessment progress, mock performance, and the teacher's reading of trajectory over two years rather than over a term.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP candidates normally sit the May session, and most schools in the emirate close predictions in the autumn or early winter of the second year to meet application deadlines. Two schools a few kilometres apart can close them a month apart, which is worth knowing before planning when to produce evidence.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP candidates take DP courses and receive predictions in those subjects, alongside a career-related study and a reflective project with its own internal deadlines. The prediction conversation is the same in substance, but the overall application profile is read differently by universities, which is worth clarifying with the school early.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of Abu Dhabi schools, and university recognition of the qualification varies by destination. A CP candidate should ask the school's counselling team directly how their chosen universities treat the course, rather than assuming it maps onto the full Diploma.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.subjectsIntro: Prediction evidence is subject specific. These notes name what a teacher in each subject is likely to be looking at, and what a candidate can produce that genuinely adds to it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Teachers weigh consistency across topic tests more heavily here than a single strong result, because the course is cumulative. The evidence that moves a judgement is a marked timed paper showing method marks recovered in the areas previously lost, particularly in proof and in HL Paper 3 reasoning.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical interpretation is where judgements get made, because it separates candidates who can run a test from those who can explain what it means. A marked piece showing conclusions written with reference to significance and context is directly legible as improvement.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Internal assessment progress carries unusual weight in this subject, because a well-designed investigation demonstrates skills the written papers only sample. Alongside that, a marked data-analysis question showing uncertainty propagated and discussed is the clearest single piece of evidence a candidate can produce.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Teachers look at long-answer reasoning rather than at numerical accuracy, because the marks live there. Evidence that lands is a marked extended-response question where the reasoning line is written out, which is precisely the habit most candidates lose under time pressure.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline dominates the judgement, since content knowledge is rarely the limiting factor. A candidate who produces two marked data-based questions answered to the right command term shows a change a teacher can see immediately and attribute to the student.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation is the band divider. A teacher forming a prediction looks for responses that reach a supported judgement rather than stopping at analysis, and for accurately labelled diagrams. Both are visible in a single marked extended response.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Judgements rest on control of argument across a response rather than on the quality of individual observations. The evidence that counts is a marked Paper 1 analysis sustaining a line of reading, and for HL the essay, which many candidates leave until the predictions have already closed.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source handling and argument maintained across an essay are what a teacher weighs. A marked response showing provenance used analytically rather than described, and an argument held past the first paragraph, is the most legible improvement in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus and a supported judgement in extended responses carry the band. Teachers notice when a candidate stops naming tools and starts pointing them at the case material, and a single marked response can demonstrate it.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE social studies alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: These subjects run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools and occupy timetable hours that a candidate producing prediction evidence has to work around. They are rarely part of the prediction itself, but they are part of the week, and plans that ignore them overstate available time.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.regionsIntro: Prediction season in Abu Dhabi collides with application deadlines and mock windows in the same weeks, and how much room a family has depends partly on where they live. These notes are about available hours.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island communities with manageable commutes and a high share of HL science candidates. Autumn here is crowded: mocks, prediction deadlines and university applications all land in the same six weeks, so evidence has to be produced early or not at all.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs and small Diploma cohorts. The practical advantage is that a timed paper can be sat on a weekday evening and discussed the next day. The disadvantage is less internal comparison when judging whether a prediction is reasonable.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A long term-time school run that pushes weekday sessions past 5pm, which in prediction season competes directly with application writing. Families here often produce evidence in weekend blocks and keep weekdays for coursework.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Bandar
regions.note: Adjacent to the main Diploma cluster, with heavy autumn demand for HL Chemistry and Mathematics support. Slot scarcity peaks exactly when prediction evidence is most useful, which argues for starting in September rather than November.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A growing second-year cohort and a slow afternoon commute. Candidates here commonly want one session for coursework feedback and one for timed practice in the same week, which is workable if the week is planned before October.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment living with the shortest travel in the emirate, so short frequent sessions are realistic. For producing dated marked evidence on a schedule, frequency matters more than session length.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: An hour inland with few HL specialists physically present. A candidate here wanting a marked HL Physics paper returned inside two days has no local route to it, which is the practical case for live video rather than a philosophical one.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Small second-year cohorts where a subject may run a single HL class, so a prediction is formed with limited comparative data. That raises the value of an individual candidate's dated marked work, because there is less cohort evidence surrounding it.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi
The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: The largest Diploma population in the emirate, with prediction deadlines set at different points across schools only a short drive apart. Families comparing timelines with friends are frequently comparing different institutional calendars.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Fewer Diploma schools across a wider geography, and the thinnest local specialist supply in the emirate. Candidates in this cluster are the most likely to need marked work turned around without a tutor being physically available.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.modesIntro: Three ways to work on prediction evidence, separated by when in the year a family starts. The earliest is the cheapest and the most effective, which is not a coincidence.

modes.title: Autumn evidence block
modes.description: Begun in September of the second year, before predictions close. One or two subjects, weekly, each session producing a dated marked artefact: a timed section, a question set, or feedback on an internal assessment draft. The aim is a short sequence of comparable marked pieces by the time the teacher forms a judgement.
bullets: Started before the school's prediction deadline rather than after it
Every session ends with something marked and dated
Component breakdowns kept so movement is comparable across pieces
Written summary the candidate can take to their subject teacher

modes.title: Post-prediction repair block
modes.description: Where the prediction has already closed and the family is unhappy with it. Here the honest target shifts from the prediction to the final session, with any conversation about revisiting the judgement handled by the family and the school. The teaching is the same; the claim being made about it is different.
bullets: Explicit that the prediction is closed and the target is the real session
Evidence produced in case the school is willing to review
Focus on the two or three repairs with the largest mark value
No implication that tutoring obliges a school to revisit a judgement

modes.title: Internal assessment feedback track
modes.description: Internal assessment progress is one of the inputs a teacher weighs, and it is the input most often behind schedule. Feedback is given on the student's own draft against the published criteria and recorded with dates. The tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of the work, and the student is told so in the first session.
bullets: Feedback mapped to criterion letters and their published descriptors
Comments returned on the student's own draft for them to act on
Dated log showing what was advised and when it was acted on
Deadline mapping so coursework and applications do not collide

sections.heading: Who issues a predicted grade, and who reads it
paragraphs: The subject teacher forms the prediction and the school submits it. In most Abu Dhabi Diploma schools the process involves a departmental discussion and sign-off by the coordinator, which is why a prediction is harder to shift than a single teacher's opinion would be. The school is accountable for the accuracy of its predictions over time, which gives it a structural reason to be conservative, and families reading a prediction as a personal judgement about their child usually miss that institutional pressure.

On the receiving side, a prediction does different work in different systems. UK universities use it to decide whether to make an offer at all, and then set a conditional offer in real grades. North American admissions treat it as one element in a holistic file alongside transcript, testing where required, essays and references. Universities in the UAE and the wider Gulf have their own policies and, separately, students heading into the UAE system meet Ministry of Education equivalency requirements, which are a different process entirely and not something a tutoring service performs.

That variation matters because it determines how much a shortfall costs. A candidate predicted 34 against a 36 requirement at a UK university may not receive an offer, which is an immediate consequence. The same candidate applying to a holistic admissions system may still receive one, with the real result mattering more. Knowing which situation applies tells a family how urgent the evidence question is, and that is a conversation for the school's counselling team rather than for a tutor.

The last reader is the candidate themselves, and the effect there is underrated. A prediction two bands below a target reads as a verdict to a seventeen-year-old, and a good deal of the autumn is spent managing what that does to effort. Converting the prediction from a verdict into a description of current evidence is, in practice, the first useful thing an outside tutor does.

sections.heading: The evidence a subject teacher actually weighs
paragraphs: Ask a Diploma teacher how they arrive at a prediction and the answer is rarely a formula. It is a weighted impression built from several sources, and the weights differ by subject and by teacher. What is consistent is which sources exist. Classwork and topic tests across two years give the base. Mock performance gives a single high-stakes data point. Internal assessment progress shows whether the candidate can sustain independent work. Trajectory, meaning the direction of travel across terms, often matters more than any single result.

A candidate can affect three of those four meaningfully in a short window. Topic test performance is immediate. Internal assessment progress is within their control if the draft timeline has not already collapsed. Trajectory is built by producing a short sequence of comparable marked pieces that each improve on the last, which is exactly what an evidence block is designed to generate. The mock is the one that cannot be redone.

What carries almost no weight, and should not, is a report that a student is working harder, attending tutoring, or feels more confident. Teachers hear this every autumn and have no way to act on it. The version that does carry weight is a marked timed paper with a component breakdown, produced under conditions the teacher recognises, handed over as a document. The difference is not effort; it is legibility.

There is an etiquette point worth making. Evidence is offered to a teacher, not used to pressure one. A candidate who brings three dated marked pieces and asks whether these change the picture is having a professional conversation. A parent who emails the coordinator with a tutor's assertion that a child is a 6 is having a different and less productive one. The first occasionally moves a judgement. The second rarely does.

sections.heading: The application calendar, counted backwards from the date predictions close
paragraphs: Families almost always discover this calendar too late, so it is worth laying out backwards. The fixed point at the end is the real session, which for Abu Dhabi candidates is normally in May. Before that sits the application cycle, with the earliest UK deadline in mid-October of the second year and the main deadline in mid-January. Before those sits the date the school closes predictions, which has to precede the application it supports. And before that sits the evidence window, which is the only part a candidate controls.

In practice, for a school submitting to the mid-October deadline, predictions are being formed in September and early October of the second year, on evidence largely generated in the first year and the first weeks of the second. That is a short and early window, and it is why families aiming at early UK deadlines who begin thinking about predictions in November have already missed the relevant period.

For the mid-January deadline the window is wider, running through the autumn and usually closing after the mock. That is the more common Abu Dhabi pattern and it is workable: a candidate starting in September has a full term to produce comparable marked work, and the mock sits inside the window rather than after it. The practical advice is simple and almost nobody gives it: ask the coordinator in the first week of the second year when predictions close.

One honest note about the last column of the table below. After predictions close, the correct target is the real session, and the correct framing of any tutoring is improving the outcome rather than the prediction. A school may be willing to revisit a judgement if substantial new evidence appears, and some do, but no tutor should imply that is owed. Selling post-deadline work as prediction improvement is the most common misrepresentation in this part of the market.
