sections.heading: Asking the school to look again: how that conversation actually works
paragraphs: There is a version of this conversation that works and a version that does not, and the difference is entirely in what is brought to it. The version that works starts with a question rather than a claim: what evidence is this prediction based on, and what would need to be true for it to change? Most coordinators in Abu Dhabi will answer that directly, because it is a reasonable professional question and because they would rather receive it than an accusation.

The answer is usually specific. A teacher may say the prediction reflects inconsistency across topic tests, or an internal assessment draft that has not arrived, or performance in one paper component that has not moved across two mock cycles. Each of those is actionable. A candidate who returns six weeks later with three dated marked pieces addressing the named issue is in a genuinely different position from one who returns with a statement that they are working hard.

What does not work, and is worth naming because families try it, is pressure. A prediction is a professional judgement the school stands behind, and schools are measured over time on how accurate their predictions are. A coordinator who adjusts a judgement without new evidence has made their own institution's data worse, and they know it. Pressure also costs goodwill that the candidate needs for references and for the rest of the year.

The other thing that does not work is a tutor's opinion offered as a credential. An outside tutor saying a candidate is a 6 carries no weight and should not; the tutor has seen a fraction of the course and none of the classwork. What carries weight is the artefact: a marked paper, with the mark scheme applied, with a component breakdown, dated. Hand over documents, not assertions, and let the teacher weigh them.
bullets: Open with a question about evidence, not a claim about the grade
Ask what specifically would need to change for the judgement to move
Return with dated marked documents addressing that specific point
Never present an outside tutor's opinion as a reason to revise a prediction

sections.heading: Where a grade band is genuinely won, subject by subject
paragraphs: Band boundaries in the Diploma are won in narrow places, and knowing where saves a term of effort. In the sciences, the recurring gap between a 5 and a 6 is rarely content. It is command-term precision and the data-handling questions, where uncertainty is calculated and never discussed, or where a conclusion is stated without reference to the data that supports it. Those are habit repairs, and they produce visible movement in a marked piece within weeks.

In Mathematics, both courses reward method presentation more than candidates believe. Method marks lost to unwritten steps account for a steady band in every marked script, and recovering them lifts a raw mark without any new content being learned. At HL, Analysis and Approaches candidates win marks in Paper 3 by learning the structure of an extended investigation, which is a teachable form rather than a body of knowledge.

In the language and humanities subjects, the band divider is argument. A Paper 1 response that identifies techniques and never connects them to effect sits below one that sustains a reading. A History essay that narrates sits below one that argues. An Economics response that analyses and stops sits below one that evaluates. Each of those is a structural change a candidate can make deliberately, and each is visible to a teacher in a single marked response.

The reason to name these specifically is that prediction evidence has to be produced quickly. A candidate with eight weeks does not have time to raise their performance across a whole subject, but they do have time to fix the one structural habit that is costing marks in every response, and to demonstrate it twice. That is a realistic target and it is what an evidence block aims at.

sections.heading: Internal assessment progress as prediction evidence
paragraphs: Internal assessment is the input families most often neglect and teachers most often weigh. A science investigation, a mathematics exploration, a history essay: each is a sustained piece of independent work with published criteria, and progress on it tells a teacher something the written papers cannot, which is whether the candidate can organise their own thinking over weeks. A strong draft arriving on schedule moves a judgement more than most things a candidate can do in the same period.

The boundary around help here is strict and worth stating in full. A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain the published criteria and their descriptors, discuss the student's own draft, identify where a method is unclear or a conclusion unsupported, and model the technique on a different example. A tutor must not write, complete or produce any part of the work, and must not edit it to a finished state. Sites in this market sell completed internal assessments at a fixed price; that is an academic-integrity breach and the consequence falls on the student.

In practice this means feedback given against criterion letters rather than as line edits. A candidate is told that the evaluation criterion expects specific limitations with their impact on the conclusion, and that their draft lists limitations without impact. They then make the change. It is slower than having it done for them and it is the only version that is theirs, which also means it is the only version that counts as evidence.

Keeping the feedback log dated serves a second purpose. If authorship of a piece of work is ever questioned, a dated sequence of the student's own drafts with external feedback on each is the strongest possible answer. That protection is worth more to a candidate than any marginal improvement a more intrusive kind of help might produce.

sections.heading: What no tutor should promise about a prediction
paragraphs: This page carries no figure for how much tutoring moves a grade, and that absence is deliberate. There is no dataset behind such a number for this market, and a statistic published without a sample size, a date and a method is a liability dressed as a credential. Competitor pages in this cluster publish satisfaction percentages and median tutor scores with no underlying data, and one shows contradictory figures on the same page. We would rather publish nothing than publish that.

Nor does this page offer a guarantee. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a prediction, or an admission outcome, and a guarantee attached to any of those is either unenforceable or conditional in ways the page does not state. Where a refund or guarantee appears in this market, read the conditions, and notice how often they are not on the same screen as the promise.

There is also a false-urgency claim to avoid. Tutoring is not required for a prediction, for university admission, or for Ministry of Education equivalency. Those are institutional processes with their own criteria, and implying that a family must buy teaching to pass through them misrepresents how they work. Equivalency in particular is run by the authority, described on its own pages, and is not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees.

What can honestly be offered is narrow and real. A tutor can read a script, name the repairs, teach them, produce dated marked evidence that the error frequency has fallen, and hand that evidence to the family to use as they see fit. Whether a school revises a judgement on the strength of it is the school's decision. Saying that plainly is less persuasive than a promise and considerably more useful.

sections.heading: How sessions run, and the record a family keeps
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and the candidate's own marked work open during the session. Gulf Standard Time lessons are scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school week: late afternoon where the school run is short, later for the Khalifa City and Al Raha catchments, and weekend blocks in the autumn when applications and coursework are already filling weekday evenings. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For prediction work the online format earns its place on turnaround: a timed paper sat on a Sunday and returned marked with a component breakdown by Tuesday is a usable document, and no travel has to be arranged to make that happen. The in-home market in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because the journey is priced in, and in this job the journey buys nothing.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. A practical caution applies here: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The teacher who sets the prediction is not the person to buy lessons from.

What a family keeps is the record: dated marked pieces with component breakdowns, a feedback log for internal assessment drafts, and a short written note after each marked item. Where no specialist is free for a subject at the hours needed, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral rather than filling the hour.

process.title: Ask when predictions close
process.description: The first question of the second Diploma year, put to the coordinator in writing. It determines whether there is an evidence window at all and how long it is. Families aiming at the earliest UK deadline in mid-October have a far shorter window than those aiming at the main mid-January one.

process.title: Establish what the current judgement rests on
process.description: Ask the subject teacher what evidence the prediction is based on and what would need to change. The answer is usually specific: inconsistency across topic tests, a missing internal assessment draft, one paper component that has not moved. That answer sets the target for everything afterwards.

process.title: Free trial lesson on the most recent marked work
process.description: One free trial lesson with the subject specialist, on the condition that it is a single lesson, spent reading the most recent marked script or test against the criteria. The output is a written list of the repairs with the largest mark value, which the family keeps either way.

process.title: Produce comparable marked pieces on a schedule
process.description: Weekly sessions, each ending in something marked and dated, with component breakdowns kept so that movement across pieces is comparable. Three pieces showing the same error class reducing is evidence; one good result is not, and teachers know the difference.

process.title: Hand documents to the school, not opinions
process.description: The candidate takes the marked work and the written summary to their subject teacher and asks whether it changes the picture. No assertion about the grade is made on our behalf. The judgement remains the school's and we do not represent it as influenceable by us.

process.title: The honest fallback
process.description: If predictions have already closed, we say that the target is now the real session and describe the work accordingly. If no specialist is free for your subject at the hours you need, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral elsewhere.

whyPoints.title: Honest about who owns the decision
whyPoints.description: The prediction belongs to the subject teacher and the school. We say so in the first paragraph rather than implying that enrolling will move it, which is the standard claim in this part of the market and is not a thing anyone outside the school can deliver.

whyPoints.title: Evidence as documents, not assertions
whyPoints.description: Dated marked pieces with component breakdowns, produced under conditions a teacher recognises. A tutor's opinion about a candidate's band carries no weight and should not. The artefact is what a teacher can weigh, so the artefact is what the work produces.

whyPoints.title: The calendar laid out backwards
whyPoints.description: Predictions close before the application they support, which closes months before the session. We publish that sequence and tell families to ask the coordinator in the first week of the second year. Almost no competing page in this market names a single date in it.

whyPoints.title: No invented statistics
whyPoints.description: There is no figure here for how much tutoring moves a grade, because no dataset supports one. Competitor pages in this cluster publish satisfaction percentages and median tutor scores with no method stated, and at least one contradicts itself on the same page.

whyPoints.title: Internal assessment help with a stated limit
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own draft against the published criteria, logged with dates. We do not write, complete or produce assessed work. The dated log is also the candidate's protection if authorship of their work is ever questioned, which is worth more than any shortcut.

whyPoints.title: No false urgency about institutions
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is not required for a prediction, for admission, or for Ministry of Education equivalency, and this page says so. Equivalency is run by the authority and described on its own pages; we neither perform it nor present ourselves as a route through it.

faqs.question: Who decides my child's IB predicted grade?
faqs.answer: The subject teacher forms it and the school signs it off, usually after a departmental discussion and with the coordinator's involvement. The IB does not issue predictions and no external tutor can change one. Schools are also accountable over time for how accurate their predictions turn out to be, which gives them a structural reason to be careful rather than generous. That institutional pressure is worth understanding before a family reads a prediction as a personal judgement about their child.

faqs.question: Can tutoring raise a predicted grade before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Tutoring cannot raise a prediction; it can change the evidence a teacher weighs when forming one. The useful output is a short sequence of dated marked pieces, each with a component breakdown, showing a specific error class reducing. A candidate who hands three such documents to their subject teacher and asks whether they change the picture is doing the only thing available. A parent asserting a tutor's opinion about the grade is not, and it rarely helps.

faqs.question: When do Abu Dhabi schools finalise IB predictions?
faqs.answer: It varies, and the variation matters more than the average. Schools submitting to the earliest UK deadline in mid-October form predictions in September and early October of the second year, on evidence largely generated in the first year. Schools working to the main mid-January deadline usually close predictions in the autumn or early winter, often just after mocks. Two schools a few kilometres apart in this emirate can differ by a month, so ask your coordinator directly in the first week of term.

faqs.question: What evidence does a subject teacher actually look at?
faqs.answer: Four things, weighted differently by subject. Topic tests across the whole course, which give the cumulative base. Mock performance, as a single high-stakes data point. Internal assessment progress, which shows whether a candidate can sustain independent work. And trajectory, meaning direction of travel across terms, which is often decisive at a band boundary. Reported effort or tutoring attendance carries almost no weight, because a teacher has no way to act on it. Marked documents are what change a picture.

faqs.question: Is it worth asking the school to review a prediction we think is low?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you ask the right question. Open with what evidence the prediction rests on and what would need to change for it to move, rather than with a claim that it is wrong. Most Abu Dhabi coordinators answer that directly and specifically, naming inconsistency across tests, a missing internal assessment draft, or one component that has not improved. Then act on the answer and return with dated marked work. Pressure without new evidence rarely moves a judgement and costs goodwill the candidate still needs.

faqs.question: Our prediction has already been submitted. Is there any point in tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the target has changed and the description should change with it. Once a prediction is submitted the work is about the final session, where the real grade is decided and where a conditional offer is actually met. Some schools will revisit a judgement if substantial new evidence appears and some will not, and no tutor should imply that a review is owed. Selling post-deadline teaching as prediction improvement is the commonest misrepresentation in this part of the market.

faqs.question: How many marked pieces make a convincing case to a teacher?
faqs.answer: Three comparable ones, addressing the same named weakness, with component breakdowns, spread over several weeks. One strong result reads as a good day; three showing the same error class reducing reads as a change. The pieces have to be comparable, which means similar question types marked the same way, otherwise there is nothing to compare. A single marked paper with no breakdown attached is the weakest version of this and the one most often offered.

faqs.question: Does internal assessment progress affect a prediction?
faqs.answer: In science and mathematics subjects it carries real weight, because a sustained independent investigation demonstrates skills the written papers only sample. A strong draft arriving on schedule often moves a judgement more than anything else a candidate can do in the same weeks. It is also the input most frequently behind schedule, so it is where an early intervention pays most. Feedback must be on the student's own draft; the work has to be demonstrably theirs for it to count as evidence at all.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do and not do with an IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills the task requires, explain the published criteria and descriptors, discuss the student's own draft, point out an unclear method or an unsupported conclusion, and model the technique on a different example. A tutor must not write, complete or produce any part of the work, or edit it to a finished state. Feedback here is given against criterion letters and logged with dates, which also gives the candidate a record that the work is their own if authorship is ever questioned.

faqs.question: How much does prediction-season support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialist tuition run AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, per Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Unitors IB from AED 200. Qualified subject tutors online sit between AED 150 and AED 300, and budget online options run AED 33 to AED 65 per Tutopiya and EdFlik. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list. Our route is a free trial lesson, on the condition that it is one lesson, then a consultation.

faqs.question: Do universities see the prediction or the real grade?
faqs.answer: Both, at different times. The prediction is what a UK university uses to decide whether to make a conditional offer, and the real result is what meets or misses that condition months later. North American admissions treat a prediction as one element in a holistic file alongside transcript, essays and references. Universities in the UAE and the region apply their own policies, so ask the admissions office directly rather than inferring. That answer tells you how decisive a shortfall actually is.

faqs.question: Can one more grade point realistically be found in eight weeks?
faqs.answer: In a narrow sense, often yes, and the honest version names where. Band boundaries are usually lost to a structural habit rather than to missing content: method marks not written out, command terms answered wrongly, analysis that stops short of evaluation, uncertainty calculated and not discussed. Fixing one such habit and demonstrating it twice is achievable in eight weeks. Raising performance across a whole subject in that time is not, and a plan that promises it is selling hours.

faqs.question: Should my child tell their teacher they have a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better handled as a matter of fact than as leverage. Teachers generally respond well to a candidate who says they are doing extra marked practice and asks whether a particular piece is useful to see. What they respond badly to is an outside opinion presented as a credential, or a parent email asserting a band. Hand over documents, ask questions, and leave the judgement where it belongs. The relationship also matters for the reference, which lasts beyond this term.

faqs.question: Which IB session do Abu Dhabi candidates sit, and when are results released?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session. This page publishes no IB exam or results dates deliberately: the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project, and a wrong date is the one error a family acts on. Confirm the session, internal upload deadlines and the results date with your school's IB coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages. Cambridge and Pearson dates elsewhere on our site are sourced and carry their reference.

abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.closingHeading: Ask when the window closes, then produce documents
abu-dhabi/ib-predicted-grades-improvemen.closingBody: The two useful actions on this page cost nothing. Ask the coordinator, in the first week of the second Diploma year, when predictions close. Then ask the subject teacher what the current judgement rests on and what would need to change. The answers turn a vague worry into a specific target with a deadline attached. After that the work is mechanical: produce three comparable marked pieces addressing that target, with component breakdowns and dates, and hand them over. Book a free trial lesson with the subject specialist to read the most recent marked work and name the repairs worth the most marks.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.tutorsIntro: These are tutors available for Diploma and Middle Years work with Abu Dhabi students. Read what each one teaches and at which level before you book a trial. A specialist in one group is not interchangeable with a specialist in another, and the trial is where you find out.

intro.heading: Tuition you can audit, not tuition you have to trust
paragraphs: Most parents in Abu Dhabi buy private tuition on a recommendation and judge it on atmosphere. The student says the sessions are fine. The tutor is pleasant and punctual. Three months pass, a mock lands two grades below the predicted grade, and nobody can say what the hours actually did. That outcome is not usually a bad tutor. It is an arrangement with no paper in it, which means there was never anything to check.

A private tuition hour is an unusual purchase. You are not in the room, the product is invisible, and the only person who can report on it is a fifteen-year-old with an interest in a quiet life. The way around that is not more supervision. It is insisting that each hour produces something physical: a script with marks on it, a note that names what was covered, a list of errors that is shorter this month than last. Documents are checkable. Impressions are not.

That is the whole organising idea of this page. Rather than describe tuition in the abstract, it sets out the six documents a term of IB private tuition in Abu Dhabi should leave behind, what each one proves, how to tell a real session note from a decorative one, and the point at which the evidence should persuade you to stop paying. It also publishes what the Abu Dhabi market charges in AED, with the providers named, because a rate card is part of the evidence too.

Delivery is stated plainly up front. Sessions for Abu Dhabi families run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For Diploma work that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the constraint on a Higher Level subject is almost never distance. It is whether anybody within reach actually teaches that course at that level, and a screen removes that question from the problem.

A word on why the documents are the argument rather than the biography of the tutor. Abu Dhabi families are shown credentials constantly: years taught, degrees held, cohorts examined, and sometimes examiner status that nobody can verify. Those claims may all be true and they still do not tell you whether this adult will help this child with this component. The folder does, within six weeks, and it does so in a form you can compare against the school's own reports. Buying on evidence rather than on biography also changes who you end up hiring, because the tutors who work this way are a self-selecting group.

Nothing here is a promise about a grade. No tutor can produce one, and any provider offering one is telling you something about themselves rather than about your child. What a well-run term of tuition can promise is that by week six you will know, from marked work rather than from a conversation, whether the arrangement is working. That is a smaller claim than most of this market makes, and it is the one worth paying for.
bullets: A paid diagnostic that names topics and command terms, not a feeling about ability
Marked work returned against the published criteria for that component
A running error log that shrinks, or an explanation of why it has not
A fortnightly note a parent can read in ninety seconds
A written coverage position before the first invoice, including the fallback
An agreed point at which the arrangement ends because it is no longer needed

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.programmesIntro: IB Gram arranges tuition across the three IB programmes an Abu Dhabi student is likely to be sitting, plus the Middle Years to Diploma crossing that causes most of the damage. Each one produces different evidence, so each one is audited differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three or four at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. Each subject is marked out of 7, giving 42, with up to three further points from the core, for a ceiling of 45. Roughly a fifth of most subject grades comes from work marked inside the school and moderated afterwards, which is the part a private tutor can most usefully strengthen without ever touching the writing.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are spread thinly across many schools rather than concentrated in a few large ones, so a school may run a single Higher Level set of eight students in a subject. That is pleasant for the student and difficult for the teacher, who may be the only person in the building who has taught that syllabus. Evidence from a second specialist is worth more here than in a city with deep subject departments.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, reported as 1 to 8 per criterion rather than as a percentage. There is no external paper until the optional eAssessment, so the usable evidence is criterion-level: which letter the marks sit lowest on, and whether that letter is about knowledge, investigating, communicating or applying. Parents often cannot read these reports, which is precisely why they are useful to a tutor.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the Middle Years years are where an incoming family discovers that the previous system taught a different sequence. A student arriving from an American or Indian school part-way through MYP 4 has no external benchmark to measure against, so the first month of tuition should be spent building one rather than teaching. A diagnostic that maps criterion by criterion is the only honest starting point.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, no external assessment, and reports written in language that rarely tells a parent whether there is a problem. Tuition at this stage should be short, specific and finite: number fluency, reading stamina, handwriting speed, the ability to work alone for twenty minutes. Evidence is a before-and-after on one narrow skill, timed and recorded, not a general sense that confidence has improved.
programmes.countryNote: Primary tuition is the easiest thing in Abu Dhabi to buy too much of. A Year 4 student who reads for pleasure and finishes homework in forty minutes does not need a weekly paid hour. We say so, and we say it before taking money, because a family that wastes a budget in Year 4 has less of it available in DP2, which is when the subject specialist actually costs something.

programmes.name: The MYP to DP crossing
programmes.ageRange: The eighteen months either side of DP1
programmes.description: The crossing is not a programme but it behaves like one. A student moves from criterion-referenced reporting with no timed papers to a system where Paper 1 is written under a clock and marked by somebody who has never met them. Students who scored 7s and 8s on MYP criteria frequently open DP1 with 3s and 4s, and the cause is almost always exam behaviour rather than missing content.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has several continuum schools running the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes in one building, and several that take students in at DP1 from British and American schools across the emirate. The second group arrives with stronger exam technique and weaker research habits. Knowing which of the two your child is decides what the first six paid hours should be spent on.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma courses Abu Dhabi families ask for most often, with the part of each one that produces the clearest written evidence. Always confirm weightings and criteria against the current subject guide your child's school is teaching, because guides change between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics carrying 6 of them and presentation 4. That split is the evidence: a student losing marks on use of mathematics has a content problem, one losing them on communication has a writing problem, and the two need different hours.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is assumed throughout, so marks leak where a student knows the mathematics but cannot make the calculator produce it under time pressure. The fix is observable: a timed set of calculator tasks, recorded, repeated a fortnight later, with the time taken written down each attempt.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Data-based questions reward a narrow set of behaviours around uncertainty, gradient and units. A marked paper shows immediately whether the loss is conceptual or procedural, because procedural losses cluster in the same two or three question types across every paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mechanisms and equilibrium carry the heaviest marks and the heaviest misconceptions. Organic questions in particular are where a student with good recall and no reasoning habit is exposed, and that pattern is visible on a script within the first marked set.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response marks depend on using the command term rather than on knowing more. A student who writes everything they know about a system and scores four out of seven is making a writing error, and a marked script with the mark scheme beside it makes that obvious in one session.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks are the fastest recoverable marks in the Diploma and the most frequently thrown away. Axes unlabelled, no shift arrow, no reference to the diagram in the prose: three fixes, each worth marks on every paper for the rest of the course.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the stimulus material is where grades separate. Students write a textbook answer and lose the application marks entirely, which a marked paper shows as a clean pattern of threes and fours on every eight-mark question.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is the most coachable component in the Diploma because it is rehearsed, timed and marked against four published criteria. Recording a practice attempt and marking it against those criteria produces evidence a parent can actually hear.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Paper 1 source work has a fixed structure and a fixed set of errors: describing a source rather than using it, missing the comparison, ignoring provenance. These are drillable, and the improvement shows on a marked paper inside a month.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies are remembered and then misapplied. The recoverable marks sit in linking a named study to the specific demand of the question, which is a writing habit rather than a knowledge gap, and it is visible in the margin of any marked essay.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay is written to a prescribed title and the exhibition to three objects. Both are marked against published criteria, so both can be reviewed without anybody drafting a sentence. Capable students struggle here because the subject rewards precision about claims, not fluency.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Graded A to E and combined with Theory of Knowledge for up to three points. The research question is where most of the final grade is decided, and that decision happens in a single conversation months before any writing, which is the cheapest useful hour in the whole Diploma.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Abu Dhabi does not change which tutor they can reach, because sessions run over video. It changes what time the hour can start and what the household can realistically sustain for a term. These are the patterns we plan around.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise households with short bridge commutes to the island schools and a quiet study problem rather than a travel problem. Sessions here commonly start at 16:30 and the constraint is finding a room where a sibling is not also doing homework.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The densest school cluster in the emirate, with several Diploma cohorts within a few minutes of each other. Bus runs are short, so a 16:00 start is realistic, which matters because an early slot survives a whole term better than a 19:30 one.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Low-density villa communities with school runs that cross the bridge twice a day. Families here often prefer a single 90-minute block at the weekend to two weekday hours, and for Extended Essay work that is usually the better structure.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Established central district feeding long-standing British and IB schools, with bilingual households common. Arabic as a first language and English Language and Literature frequently need to be planned together rather than treated as separate purchases.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Apartment and townhouse mix along the Al Zeina and Al Muneera stretch, with a strong pull towards the Khalifa City schools. Evening traffic back along the highway is why a weekday session rarely starts before 17:00 in this corridor.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Large villa plots and a wide spread of school choices across the mainland. Households here often run three or four children on different timetables, so the scheduling question is which child gets the hour, not which tutor is nearest.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Event weekends change the shape of the week several times a year. A study plan built on a fixed Friday evening slot will break here, so we usually anchor the week on a Saturday morning instead and treat weekday slots as secondary.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Central, close to several well-established schools, with short home runs. The practical advantage is a session that can begin before the household eats, which protects the hour from being quietly dropped once the evening fills up.

schoolClusters.city: The island and the central districts
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi island holds a long-established group of British and international schools, several of which run the Diploma alongside or instead of A Levels. Cohorts are modest in size, which means a single teacher often carries a whole Higher Level set, and a second specialist voice is correspondingly more useful.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the Saadiyat corridor
schoolClusters.note: This is where most of the emirate's newer Diploma capacity sits, within a short drive of each other. Families moving between these schools mid-year are common, and the subject sequencing between two of them is rarely identical, which is the single most frequent cause of a sudden drop in marks.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.modesIntro: Three ways an Abu Dhabi family buys private tuition from us, each producing a different volume of evidence for a different amount of money. The choice should follow the problem, not the budget.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A fixed hour each week with the same tutor for a named course at a named level, running over live video. This is the format that produces a continuous paper trail, because the error log and the marked set accumulate rather than resetting each time. It is also the format most likely to be quietly wasted if nobody reads the notes.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, same subject for a full term
Marked work returned between sessions, not during them
A fortnightly written note naming topics and the current error list
An agreed review point at week six with a stop option

modes.title: A diagnostic block, then a decision
modes.description: Two or three paid hours used purely to establish where the marks are going, ending in a written report rather than a plan to buy more. Families who have never used tuition before should start here. It costs less than a term, it tells you whether the problem is content, technique or workload, and quite often it tells you that no tuition is needed at all.
bullets: Two to three sessions with a defined output
A timed past paper marked against the published scheme
A written topic and command-term map of the losses
A recommendation that may be to buy nothing further

modes.title: Component support, time-boxed
modes.description: A finite block attached to one assessed component: the mathematics exploration, a scientific investigation, the Extended Essay research question, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition. The student does every piece of the work. The tutor teaches the method, reads drafts the student has written and gives feedback against the criteria, and the block ends when the component is submitted.
bullets: Scoped to one component with a known deadline
Feedback against the published criteria, in writing
A record of which draft received which comments
Ends on submission rather than rolling into a retainer

sections.heading: The six documents a term of IB private tuition should leave behind
paragraphs: A term of IB private tuition in Abu Dhabi, bought weekly, is somewhere between twelve and sixteen paid hours. At the end of it a parent should be able to open a folder and find six things. A diagnostic report from the start. A set of marked scripts. A running error log. A sequence of session notes. A mid-term review. And a clear statement of what remains to be fixed. If four of the six are missing, the hours may still have been pleasant and useful, but there is no way for anybody outside the room to know.

This is not an administrative preference. It is the only mechanism available to a parent who cannot sit in on the lesson and should not have to. Each document answers a different question. The diagnostic answers whether the problem was correctly identified. The marked scripts answer whether the work is being judged against the real criteria or against the tutor's taste. The error log answers whether anything is actually being retired. The notes answer whether the sessions follow a plan. The review answers whether to continue.

The documents also protect the tutor. A specialist who has spent eight weeks rebuilding a student's approach to data-based questions has something to point at when the mock comes back only one grade higher than before. Without that record the conversation becomes a referendum on likeability, and the tutor with better manners wins over the tutor with better teaching. We would rather be judged on the folder.

What follows is each document in turn, what a good one contains, and the version of it that looks like evidence while proving nothing. The distinction matters more than the format. A one-page note that names three topics and two command terms is worth more than a four-page report of adjectives.

table.caption: THE SIX DOCUMENTS, WHAT EACH PROVES, AND THE USELESS VERSION
rows: After the first one to three paid hours
That the problem was identified from evidence rather than assumed from the grade
A paragraph saying the student lacks confidence and needs to practise more
That work is judged against the published criteria for that component
A tick-and-cross script with a percentage and no criterion reference
That specific errors are being retired, not just revisited
A list that grows every week and is never pruned
Within a day of each session
That the hour followed a plan connected to the diagnostic
We covered functions and did some practice questions
That somebody has compared the current position with the starting one
A message asking whether to continue next term
What is fixed, what is not, and what the school should be told
Nothing, because the arrangement simply stops being mentioned

sections.heading: Reading a session note: four that say nothing and one that says something
paragraphs: Session notes are the document families receive most often and read least carefully. Almost every provider sends something. Very few send anything a parent could act on. The test is simple: could a different tutor pick up this note and run next week's hour from it? If not, it is a receipt, not a record.

The four common failures are worth naming because they are so familiar that they pass unnoticed. The first is the topic list: we covered integration, we did quadratics. True, uninformative, and compatible with having achieved nothing. The second is the sentiment report: good engagement, working hard, growing in confidence. This describes the student's manner rather than their marks. The third is the homework instruction: finish questions 4 to 11. That is a plan for the student, not a report to the parent. The fourth is the volume note, where four paragraphs of prose describe a single exercise in order to look thorough.

A note that says something names the component, the specific error, what was done about it, and what evidence will show whether it worked. Something closer to: worked on data-based questions from two past papers; the recurring loss is reading an uncertainty from a graph and then not propagating it; corrected four of six attempts unaided by the end of the hour; two further questions set, and this will be re-tested on the next timed paper. That is four lines, and a parent who reads only that line each fortnight knows where they stand.

Ask for the note in writing, at the start, before the first paid hour. The request is not aggressive and the answer is informative either way. A tutor who already works this way will say yes immediately, because they are describing their existing habit. A tutor who does not will negotiate, and that negotiation is the most useful thing you will learn in the first week.
bullets: Names the component, not just the topic
Names the specific error, in the student's own work
States what was attempted and how far the student got unaided
States what evidence will test whether it worked
Fits in ninety seconds of a parent's attention

sections.heading: Marking against published criteria rather than against a feeling
paragraphs: The single most common failure in paid tuition is marking by impression. A tutor reads a student's work, forms a view, and reports that view. It may even be accurate. It is still not usable, because it cannot be compared with the mark the school will give, and it cannot be tracked over time. The alternative is to mark against the criteria the component is actually assessed on, with the letters and the mark allocations in front of both of you.

The Diploma makes this unusually easy, because for internally assessed work the criteria are published and the mark allocations are fixed. A student can be told that they are losing marks on a specific criterion rather than that their work needs to be stronger. In the mathematics exploration, for example, the twenty marks are divided across five criteria, and the largest single block sits on use of mathematics. A student scoring well on presentation and badly on that criterion has a mathematics problem dressed as a writing problem, and a tutor who marks by impression will spend weeks on the wrong one.

The sciences investigation works the same way, with the available marks spread across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation is where whole cohorts lose marks, because it requires a student to criticise their own method specifically rather than list generic limitations. Once a student has seen their own work scored criterion by criterion, that conversation becomes concrete. Before that, it is advice.

Two cautions. First, criteria and mark allocations change between subject guides, and a school may be teaching a cohort under a guide that differs from the one a tutor last taught. Confirm the current allocation against the guide your child's school is using before relying on any number, including the ones in the table below. Second, a tutor's criterion mark is an estimate for teaching purposes, not a prediction. The mark that counts is awarded by the school and moderated afterwards.

table.caption: INTERNALLY ASSESSED WORK: WHERE THE MARKS SIT - CONFIRM AGAINST YOUR CHILD'S CURRENT SUBJECT GUIDE

Mathematics beyond the student's comfortable level, used incorrectly, in pursuit of a higher criterion score

Criterion-based, covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation

sections.heading: The error log, and why it is the only document that matters in February
paragraphs: An error log is a list of the specific mistakes a student has actually made in their own written work, with the date each one first appeared and the date it stopped appearing. It is unglamorous and it is the most valuable artefact in the folder, because it is the only one that shows movement rather than activity.

The discipline is in the specificity. Careless mistakes in algebra is not an entry. Sign error when expanding a bracket preceded by a minus, four times in two papers, is an entry. The first cannot be retired; the second can be drilled in ten minutes and tested a fortnight later. A log of twenty vague entries is a complaint. A log of twenty precise entries is a curriculum for the next five weeks, and it will be noticeably shorter by the end of them.

The log also settles the argument every family eventually has in February, when the mock results arrive and everybody disagrees about whether the tuition is working. A grade is a blunt instrument; it moves in whole steps and can stay still for a term while a great deal changes underneath. The log shows the underneath. If eleven of fifteen recurring errors have gone and the grade has not yet moved, the arrangement is working and needs more time. If nothing has been retired in six weeks, the grade is not the problem and something about the arrangement has to change.

Keep the log somewhere the parent can see it, and keep it short. The temptation is to let it become a complete record of every mistake ever made, at which point nobody opens it. A good log holds the live errors only. Retired entries move to a separate list, which is itself a useful thing to read in April, when a student has stopped believing that anything has improved.

table.caption: ERROR LOG ENTRIES: THE USELESS FORM AND THE USABLE FORM
rows: Sign error expanding a bracket after a minus; four instances across two papers
Ten targeted items, then re-tested on the next timed paper two weeks later
States the uncertainty but does not propagate it into the final answer; three of four data questions
One worked method, applied to five past data questions unaided, marked against the scheme
Writes description where the command term is explain; loses the final two marks on seven-mark items
Command-term rewrite drill on previously marked answers, then a fresh timed question
Axes unlabelled and no reference to the diagram in the written answer
Three diagrams redrawn to a checklist, then applied in a full past-paper answer
Identifies a device and names its effect without connecting it to the guiding question
Two paragraphs rewritten against the criterion wording, marked, repeated on a new extract

sections.heading: What IB private tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and what each band should leave on paper
paragraphs: Published rates in this market run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, and the gap is real rather than reputational. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52 for online sessions. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a named examiner-marketed tutor. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and specialist subject tutors at AED 200 to 450 and above. Every one of those figures is the provider's own published number, as read in October 2026, and none of them is IB Gram's price.

The useful way to read that spread is not cheap to expensive. It is how much documentation each band can sustain. Marking a Diploma script properly against a mark scheme takes between twenty and forty minutes. Writing a session note that names errors takes ten. Maintaining an error log takes five. That is roughly an extra hour of unpaid work for every two paid hours, and a tutor charging AED 50 cannot do it and still eat. So at the budget end you are buying contact time only, and you should plan the evidence yourself.

In the middle band, around AED 150 to 300, marked work and written notes are a reasonable expectation and worth asking for explicitly before booking. Above AED 400 the question changes again: at that price the tutor should be bringing judgement you cannot get elsewhere, which usually means genuine depth in a specific Higher Level course rather than general competence across many. Paying a premium rate for general competence is the most common way families in this emirate waste money on tuition.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on these pages. The reason is that a single number would be either misleading or useless across the range of courses, levels and components families ask about. What is published instead is the trial lesson, which costs nothing and is where a specific quote is given against a specific brief. Monthly packages in this market, for comparison, have been advertised at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what the evidence can honestly show, and what it cannot
paragraphs: Parents buy tuition to move a grade and then try to read the grade weekly, which is the one measurement that will not cooperate. A Diploma subject grade is a coarse scale applied to a wide mark range. A student can gain a substantial number of marks and stay on the same number, then gain two more and jump. Watching the grade alone produces a flat line for eight weeks followed by a surprise, and most arrangements are cancelled during the flat part.

What moves earlier and visibly is the mark on a specific component, under the same conditions, marked against the same scheme. That requires the conditions to be held constant: same paper length, same time allowance, same marker, same scheme. Two timed papers four weeks apart, both marked properly, will tell you more than a term of reported impressions. Three will show a trend.

Mock examinations are a weaker signal than families assume. Schools set mocks for different purposes, sometimes deliberately hard to provoke effort, sometimes on partial content, and the marking standard is not necessarily the same as the board's. A mock result is evidence about a particular paper on a particular day. It is not a prediction, and a single bad mock should change the plan only if the error pattern in it is new.

The honest limits are worth stating. Nobody can attribute a grade change to tuition alone, because the student is also being taught at school, maturing, and sitting different papers. Nobody can promise a particular grade, and a provider who does is describing their sales process. What a well-documented arrangement can show is a shrinking error list, rising marks on repeated timed components, and a student who can explain what they are doing differently. That is as close to proof as this purchase gets, and it is enough to make a decision with.
bullets: Hold the conditions constant or the comparison means nothing
Expect component marks to move before the subject grade does
Treat a mock as evidence about one paper, not a forecast
Judge a new error pattern as significant; judge a known one as unfinished work
Accept that attribution is impossible and measure the work instead

sections.heading: A minor's data: recordings, forms and the file you are entitled to ask about
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement generates a file about a child: marked work, notes about weaknesses, sometimes recordings of sessions. That is the point of it, and it also means a family should know what exists, where it sits and how to have it removed. Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data is the UAE framework here, and the practical questions it implies are ones every provider should be able to answer plainly.

There are four worth asking before the first paid session. What is collected at enquiry, and why. Whether sessions are recorded, who can see a recording and for how long it is kept. Who else inside the organisation can read the session notes about your child. And how to ask for the whole file to be deleted, including from the tutor's own devices. A provider who answers these in a sentence each has thought about it. A provider who has not will tell you so by the shape of the answer.

Recordings deserve a particular decision rather than a default. For a mathematics or science session they are genuinely useful, because a student can re-watch a worked method at the point of getting stuck in homework. For a session discussing a student's own writing or their difficulties, they can be inhibiting, and a student who knows they are being recorded performs rather than works. Our default is to record only where the family has asked for it and the student knows.

The adjacent point is what goes into an enquiry form. Caution is sensible about handing over a child's school, year group, grades and photograph to a provider you have not yet spoken to. A tutoring enquiry needs the course, the level, the examination session and the specific difficulty. It does not need the child's name to produce a useful first answer, and any form that demands more than it needs before giving you anything is telling you about its business model.

sections.heading: The honesty boundary around a coursework draft, stated precisely
paragraphs: Every family buying component support eventually arrives at the same question, usually at eleven at night with a deadline two days away. How much can the tutor touch? The answer is specific enough to put in a table, and getting it wrong is not a style error. Assessed work in the Diploma must be the student's own, and a breach is investigated as malpractice against the student, not against the person who helped.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may teach the method the component requires. They may discuss whether a research question can be answered in the word allowance. They may read something the student has produced and say where it does not meet a criterion. They may point at a paragraph and say this does not answer the question you set. They may teach referencing conventions, and they may teach a student how to evaluate their own method rather than list generic limitations.

What a tutor may not do is cross from feedback into authorship. They do not supply sentences for the student to use. They do not restructure a piece by rewriting it. They do not provide data for an investigation the student did not carry out. They do not correct language to a standard the student cannot produce unaided, because the finished piece then misrepresents the student's ability, which is the thing being assessed. The line is not whether help was given. It is whose work the examiner is reading.

The school's supervisor has a defined role in this, with recorded meetings and an authenticity declaration at the end. A private tutor sits outside that structure and should behave as though their contribution may be asked about, because it may. We tell families this before a component block starts, and we decline the requests that cross the line, including the urgent ones. Anybody offering a finished internal assessment for a fee is selling your child an expulsion risk.

sections.heading: Delivery, coverage and the sentence most providers leave out
paragraphs: Tuition for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a home anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is said here in plain words because the alternative is a parent discovering it after paying, which is a trust failure rather than a logistics one. Two providers ranking for these searches route UAE enquiries to Indian telephone numbers without ever stating where the tutor sits.

The second sentence most providers leave out is about coverage. There is no honest version of yes, we have a specialist for everything. Higher Level courses with small cohorts across the whole emirate are the hardest to staff, and a provider claiming instant availability in all of them is either guessing or about to put a generalist in front of your child. We state the coverage position, including the fallback, before an invoice is raised.

The fallback is simply stated. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a course at the level required, we offer a specialist elsewhere, most often one of our India-based IB teachers, working on Gulf Standard Time so the family's evening is unchanged. The session is identical in format and the documentation is identical. Families are told this in advance rather than discovering a different accent on the first call. Some decline, which is a reasonable decision made with the right information.

For an evidence-led arrangement, delivery over video turns out to help in one unglamorous way. Everything is already in digital form. A marked script is annotated on screen and saved to a shared folder in the same movement; nothing depends on a paper copy surviving a schoolbag. A family who wants to see what has been covered opens a folder rather than asking a teenager.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop paying
paragraphs: A tuition arrangement with no exit condition becomes a subscription. The student gets used to the hour, the household absorbs the cost, and nobody asks whether it is still doing anything. An evidence-led arrangement has the opposite problem built out of it, because a shrinking error log eventually runs out of entries, and that is a result rather than a loss of a customer.

There are three honest reasons to stop. The first is success: the errors that were costing marks have been retired, the student can produce the work unaided under time pressure, and the remaining gap is ordinary revision the student can do alone. The second is a changed diagnosis: six weeks in, the evidence shows that the problem was never the subject. It was sleep, or workload across six subjects, or a component that nobody had told the student was due. Tuition is the wrong purchase for all three and continuing to buy it is an expensive way to avoid the real conversation.

The third is honest failure. If after six weeks of marked work nothing has been retired, something about the arrangement is wrong: the wrong subject, the wrong level of specialism, the wrong time of day, or a student who is not willing. Changing the tutor is sometimes right. Stopping is sometimes right. Buying more of the same is almost never right, and the reason families do it anyway is that stopping feels like giving up on the child. It is not. It is reading the evidence you paid to collect.

We build a review point into every block at around week six, with a stop option that costs nothing. It is a strange thing to advertise, but it follows directly from the rest of this page. A provider who holds the evidence and never recommends stopping is not using the evidence. They are using the file as a sales document, which is a different product with a similar folder.
bullets: Stop on success: the log is empty and the work holds up under a clock
Stop on re-diagnosis: the problem turned out not to be the subject
Stop on failure: six weeks of marked work with nothing retired
Change the variable, not the volume, when something is not working
Put the review date in writing before the first paid hour

process.title: Say what the evidence already shows
process.description: Send the course, the level, the examination session and whatever marked work exists: a school report, a mock script, a returned draft. Three lines and one photographed script produce a better first conversation than a long description of how the student is finding things.

process.title: Take the trial lesson as a diagnostic
process.description: The free session is not a sample lesson. It is where a specialist finds out whether the loss is content, technique or workload, and whether the student will work with this particular adult. Ask for a short written view afterwards, even if you book nothing.

process.title: Agree the scope and the paperwork in writing
process.description: Subject, level, components, the number of hours, what arrives between sessions, what the fortnightly note will contain, and the week-six review date. This takes one message to settle and prevents most of the disagreements that end tuition arrangements badly.

process.title: Run the first marked set
process.description: A timed component under real conditions, marked against the published scheme, forms the baseline everything later is compared with. Keep the conditions written down, because a comparison against a differently timed paper is not a comparison.

process.title: Review at week six against the folder
process.description: Open the log, the notes and the marked set together. Decide one of three things: continue, change a variable, or stop. If the answer is stop, we say so, and the arrangement ends without a renewal conversation.

whyPoints.title: The folder, not the feeling
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic, marked criterion-level work, a running error log, fortnightly notes and a week-six review. Six documents that let somebody who was not in the room judge whether the hours worked. Everything else on this list follows from that one commitment.

whyPoints.title: Specialists by course and level
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level course is a different teaching job from its Standard Level version, and we match on the course a student is actually entered for. Where we cannot staff that honestly in the emirate, we say so and name the fallback before any invoice.

whyPoints.title: Online, one-to-one, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Sessions run over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to UAE homes, and we say that before payment rather than after. The advantage is a specialist chosen for the syllabus rather than for the drive.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line held, including at midnight
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, reviews what the student has produced and gives criterion-level feedback. They do not supply sentences, data or structure for assessed work. We decline the urgent requests too, because the risk falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, never invented
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a published competitor or market rate with the source named and the month stated. We publish no satisfaction percentages, no star ratings and no IB examination dates we have not confirmed with the IB.

whyPoints.title: A review that can end the arrangement
whyPoints.description: Week six, against the folder, with a stop option. Tuition should be a finite purchase with an exit condition, and a provider holding the evidence has an obligation to say when the evidence no longer supports buying more.

faqs.question: What should be in the folder after a term of IB private tuition in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Six things. A diagnostic report from the first one to three hours, naming topics and command terms rather than describing confidence. A set of marked scripts judged against the published criteria for that component. A running error log with dates. A sequence of fortnightly notes a parent can read in ninety seconds. A mid-term review comparing the current position with the starting one. And a closing note saying what is fixed and what is not. If four of the six are missing, the hours may have been useful, but nobody outside the room can tell.

faqs.question: How do I tell a real session note from a decorative one?
faqs.answer: Ask whether a different tutor could run next week's hour from it. A decorative note lists topics covered, reports good engagement, or sets homework. A real note names the component, the specific error in the student's own work, how far they got unaided, and what evidence will test whether the fix held. Four lines is enough. Request the format in writing before the first paid session: a tutor who already works this way agrees immediately, and one who negotiates has told you something useful in week one.

faqs.question: Why does marking against criterion letters matter more than a percentage?
faqs.answer: Because a percentage cannot be acted on. Internally assessed Diploma work is scored against published criteria with fixed mark allocations, so a student can be told exactly which criterion is costing them. In the mathematics exploration the largest single block of marks sits on use of mathematics, which means a student scoring well on presentation and poorly there has a mathematics problem, not a writing one. A tutor marking by impression will spend weeks on the wrong thing. Confirm current allocations against the subject guide your child's school is teaching.

faqs.question: What does a usable error log entry actually look like?
faqs.answer: Specific enough to drill and test. Careless in algebra is not an entry; it cannot be retired. Sign error when expanding a bracket preceded by a minus, four instances across two papers, is an entry: ten targeted items fix it and a timed paper a fortnight later proves it. A good log holds only live errors, with the date each appeared and the date it stopped. Retired entries move to a separate list, which is worth reading in April when a student has stopped believing anything has changed.

faqs.question: The mock came back the same grade after eight weeks. Has the tuition failed?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and the log answers it rather than the grade. A Diploma grade is a coarse scale over a wide mark range, so a student can gain real marks and stay on the same number for a term. Open the error log. If most recurring errors have been retired and component marks under timed conditions are rising, the arrangement is working and needs more time. If nothing has been retired in six weeks, the grade is not the problem and something about the arrangement has to change.

faqs.question: Are the AED figures on this page what IB Gram charges?
faqs.answer: No. Every figure is a published market or competitor rate with the source named, read in October 2026. Tutopiya advertises from around AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650. Bestimate's rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180 to 350. IB Gram gives a specific quote against a specific brief after the free trial lesson, because one hourly number across every course and component would mislead.

faqs.question: Why can a tutor at AED 50 an hour not produce the documentation?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than attitude. Marking a Diploma script properly against a mark scheme takes twenty to forty minutes. Writing a note that names errors takes ten. Maintaining an error log takes five. That is roughly an extra unpaid hour for every two paid hours. At the budget end of this market you are buying contact time, and the sensible response is to plan the diagnostic and keep the log yourself rather than to expect a tutor to work for nothing. Decide which you are buying before you book.

faqs.question: Should sessions be recorded, and who should be able to see them?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a decision, not a default. For mathematics and sciences a recording is genuinely useful, because a student can re-watch a worked method at the moment they get stuck. For sessions about a student's own writing or their difficulties it can be inhibiting, and a student who knows they are recorded performs rather than works. Our default is to record only where the family asks and the student knows. Ask any provider who can access a recording, where it is stored and when it is deleted.

faqs.question: What should I refuse to put on a tutoring enquiry form?
faqs.answer: More than the question needs. A useful first answer requires the course, the level, the examination session and the specific difficulty. It does not require a child's full name, school, grade history or photograph. UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 governs personal data here, and the practical test is simpler than the law: a form demanding a child's whole profile before giving you anything is describing its business model. Ask what is collected, why, who reads it and how to have it deleted.

faqs.question: Exactly how far can a tutor go on a draft my child has written?
faqs.answer: As far as feedback, and no further. A tutor may teach the method, question whether a research question fits the word allowance, mark a draft against the criteria, and say that a paragraph does not answer the question the student set. They may not supply sentences, restructure by rewriting, provide data the student did not collect, or polish language to a standard the student cannot reach unaided. The test is not whether help was given but whose work the examiner is reading. Breaches are investigated against the student.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Every session for a UAE family runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and we state that before any payment rather than after. For Higher Level Diploma work the trade is favourable: the binding constraint is almost never distance but whether anybody within driving range actually teaches that course at that level. A screen removes the drive from the problem and widens the pool of people who do.

faqs.question: What happens if no Abu Dhabi specialist covers my child's Higher Level course?
faqs.answer: We say so before raising an invoice and name the fallback. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for the course at the level required, we offer a specialist elsewhere, most often one of our India-based IB teachers, working on Gulf Standard Time so the family's evening is unchanged. Format and documentation are identical. Families are told in advance rather than discovering it on the first call, and some decline, which is a reasonable decision made with correct information rather than after the fact.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for private tuition altogether?
faqs.answer: On one of three readings of the evidence. On success, when the errors costing marks have been retired and the student produces the work unaided under a clock. On re-diagnosis, when six weeks shows the problem was sleep, workload or an unnoticed component deadline rather than the subject. Or on honest failure, when nothing has been retired in six weeks. In that last case change a variable or stop; buying more of the same is the most common and most expensive mistake families make here.

faqs.question: Does ADEK register or approve private tutors in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; it does not issue a certificate to individual tutors. The permit that does exist is federal: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no provider may claim approval, accreditation or registration from ADEK for its tutors.

faqs.question: Why will you not publish the IB examination and results dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to confirm them from the IB itself. The IB website returns an error to automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been verified at source, and a wrong date on a page like this one would be read as fact by a family planning around it. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published and sourced, so those appear. For IB dates, ask your child's Diploma coordinator or check ibo.org directly, and plan the work backwards from the school's own internal deadlines.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the evidence, not with a term's worth of hours
abu-dhabi/ib-private-tuition.closingBody: If you are considering IB private tuition in Abu Dhabi, buy the diagnostic before you buy the term. Send the course, the level, the session your child is entered for and one piece of marked work, take the free trial lesson, and ask for a short written view afterwards. You will either have a scoped plan with a review date in it, or you will have a clear reason not to spend anything, and both of those are worth more than twelve pleasant hours nobody can account for. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the coverage position is stated before the first invoice.
