abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches one or two named Diploma courses at a stated level rather than the IB in general, because a Higher Level Physics paper and a Standard Level one reward different work. Send the course title and level exactly as your child's school entered them, together with the component your child is struggling on, and a shortlist comes back with evening availability.

intro.heading: Why the course title matters more than the subject name
paragraphs: Half the wasted money in private tuition is spent on a competent tutor teaching slightly the wrong course. A family asks for a maths tutor; the student is on Applications and Interpretation Higher Level; the tutor is strongest on Analysis and Approaches and quietly teaches the proof-heavy version of the same topics. Everything in the session is correct. None of it is quite what Paper 3 will ask. The student works hard, feels better, and gains nothing measurable.

The Diploma is unusually prone to this, because the names overlap and the assessment does not. Two courses called Mathematics have different papers, different technology assumptions and different university consequences. Chemistry at Higher Level sets a longer Paper 1 and expects the additional higher-level content throughout Paper 2, so it is not Standard Level with extra homework. English A: Language and Literature at Higher Level carries a written essay that the Standard Level course does not set at all. A tutor matched to the subject rather than the course is a coin toss.

So this page is organised by what each course assesses. For each of the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for, it sets out the components, their weightings, what the examiner is paying for in each, and the specific places marks go missing. That last part is the most useful and the least written about. Diploma students rarely lose marks on content they have never met; they lose them on content they know, answered in a shape the mark scheme does not reward.

Two cautions about the figures that follow. Subject guides are revised between cohorts, and the sciences in particular changed shape for first examinations in 2025, so every weighting on this page should be confirmed against your own child's current subject guide with the school's Diploma coordinator. And no IB examination or results date appears anywhere here, because the organisation's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a tutoring page is worse than no date at all. Cambridge and Pearson dates, where they appear elsewhere on this site, come from those boards' published key dates.

On delivery, the position is simple and it is the same on every country page on this site. Tutoring for UAE families is one-to-one, over live video, at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates; visiting a student's address is a service we run only in India. For a subject-and-level match this is the whole argument: the set of people who teach Higher Level Further Mathematics and live within a drive of Al Shamkha is usually empty, while the set who teach it is not.
bullets: Higher and Standard Level are different courses, not two speeds of one
Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation assess different things
Science investigations are marked out of 24 and carry 20 per cent of the grade
Marks are usually lost on known content answered in the wrong shape
Confirm every weighting against your child's own current subject guide

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.programmesIntro: Private tuition by subject and level applies across three IB stages, but the unit of work changes. In the Diploma it is a course. In the Middle Years Programme it is a set of criteria. For a student moving between the two it is a mapped list of differences. Each needs a different kind of specialist.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six courses across the subject groups, three at Higher Level, plus the three core components. Each course has its own assessment architecture, and a tutor has to know that architecture rather than the subject generally. The unit of booking is a course at a level: Chemistry HL, Economics SL, Mathematics AI HL, and so on, confirmed from the school's own entry record.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi's Diploma cohort is spread across a comparatively small number of schools, so niche course-and-level combinations are genuinely scarce in the emirate. Higher Level Further Mathematics, Design Technology, Music and several Group 2 languages are the usual examples. The honest answer for those is a specialist elsewhere teaching over video, or a wait, rather than a nearby generalist.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each on a one-to-eight scale, converted to a grade out of seven. The useful work is translating criterion language into actions a student can take, since most read only the final grade. Specialism here matters less than in the Diploma, but criterion literacy matters more, because the instrument is unfamiliar to parents from most other systems.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then enter students for the Diploma, while others switch to IGCSE at 14. Which route a school takes changes what Year 10 support should look like entirely, and families moving between schools in the emirate occasionally discover the mismatch after the move rather than before.

programmes.name: Transition into the Diploma
programmes.description: A mapped audit rather than general revision. A student coming from IGCSE into Mathematics AA HL has specific named gaps: proof conventions, function notation, radian measure, the expectation that method is written out. A student from an American system into the sciences has different ones. The work is finite and should be quoted that way.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-year arrivals are common in Abu Dhabi because of posting cycles, and a student joining DP1 in January has missed a term of a two-year course with no realistic chance of the school repeating it. That is the clearest case on this page for a subject-and-level specialist available this week over video rather than a nearby generalist available tomorrow.

programmes.name: The Diploma core
programmes.description: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the service strand, worth up to three bonus points between the first two. The Extended Essay is marked out of 34 with critical thinking carrying 12 of those marks; the Theory of Knowledge essay has a 1,600-word ceiling and the exhibition a 950-word one. This is annotation and process work, not taught content.
programmes.countryNote: School-set internal deadlines for the core cluster in the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2 in most Abu Dhabi schools, which is also when mock examinations sit. Booking core support against the school's own internal calendar rather than a generic one is the difference between help and hindrance.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: What follows is course by course rather than subject by subject, with the components that carry the weight and the specific place marks are lost. Confirm each weighting against your child's current subject guide, because guides are revised between cohorts and the sciences changed shape for first examinations in 2025.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers plus the exploration: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one at 30 per cent each, Paper 3 at 20 per cent, exploration at 20 per cent. Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions and is where Higher Level candidates most often run out of time rather than ideas.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers at 40 per cent each, one without a calculator, plus the exploration at 20 per cent. The non-calculator paper is the discriminator: students who have leaned on technology through the Middle Years Programme lose marks on arithmetic and surd manipulation rather than on the topic being tested.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weighting structure as Analysis and Approaches at each level, including a Paper 3 at Higher Level, but the content is statistical, modelling-led and technology-dependent throughout. A graphing calculator from the school's permitted list is assumed in almost every question, and keystroke fluency is a real source of marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 36 per cent in two parts, multiple choice and data-based, Paper 2 at 44 per cent, and the scientific investigation at 20 per cent marked out of 24. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the spread, and the investigation loses most of its marks on evaluation rather than on method.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Same component structure as the other sciences after the 2023 guide. Marks go missing in extended responses where a correct physical principle is asserted without the derivation the mark scheme requires. Higher Level specialists are the scarcest science tutors in the emirate, which is why course-level matching matters here more than anywhere.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the three sciences and the lowest conceptual difficulty, which produces a specific failure pattern: knowledge present, command term misread. Data-based questions in Paper 1B are the most improvable component in the course and the least practised at home.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 at 30 per cent, Paper 2 at 40 per cent and the portfolio at 30 per cent. At Higher Level a third paper is added covering policy and quantitative work. Diagram accuracy earns marks prose cannot, and the top evaluation band requires a judgement that chooses rather than a list that balances.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 at 35 per cent each with the individual oral at 30 per cent. At Higher Level, Paper 1 at 35 per cent, Paper 2 at 25 per cent, the HL essay at 20 per cent and the oral at 20 per cent. The HL essay exists only at Higher Level and is frequently started far too late.

subjects.name: Group 2 languages: French, Spanish and Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive and receptive skills across two papers and an individual oral, with the oral assessed on a recorded performance. Rehearsal is the single most effective use of tutoring time in any Group 2 course, and recorded video sessions have an obvious advantage: the student can hear themselves.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Extended Essay marked out of 34 across five criteria, 4,000-word ceiling, with critical thinking worth 12. Theory of Knowledge essay capped at 1,600 words against a prescribed title, exhibition commentary at 950. Both are read-and-annotate work where the student writes every word themselves.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities and the course-level requests they generate
abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical everywhere because sessions run over live video. What varies by community is which courses the local school cluster offers and therefore which specialists are asked for. These seven generate most of the subject-specific enquiries in the emirate.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A small, high-attainment Diploma cohort with heavy Higher Level loads, so the requests skew to Mathematics AA HL, Chemistry HL and the Extended Essay. Core support here is usually annotation on an existing draft rather than teaching from the brief.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: A long-established mix of Diploma and American diploma provision, which produces the emirate's most frequent confusion about which instrument a piece of work is being assessed on. Confirming the course and level from the school's entry is the first job in this community.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Newer cohorts with many students who transferred curricula within two years, so transition audits are the most common request: an IGCSE-to-AA mapped gap list, or an American-system-to-sciences one, rather than general subject tuition.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Mixed curriculum catchment where some students take IB courses alongside an American diploma. Group 2 language requests are more common here than elsewhere, usually French or Spanish at Standard Level with an oral deadline approaching.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest source of Diploma enquiries in the emirate and the widest spread of courses. Applications and Interpretation requests outnumber Analysis and Approaches here, which changes the tutor specification entirely and is often not stated when a family first makes contact.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Established IB provision with internal coursework deadlines set early, so scientific investigation support is requested in DP1 rather than DP2. That is the right time for it and is unusual enough across the emirate to be worth noting.

regions.name: Masdar City and Khalifa University's surrounds
regions.note: A high concentration of engineering-track families, which produces more Analysis and Approaches Higher Level requests and more questions about which Mathematics course a physical-science degree expects. Those questions should be answered from the specific university's published entry requirements.

schoolClusters.city: The island Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Experienced Diploma departments with full Higher Level provision, which means a student struggling here is usually struggling with a specific component rather than the course as a whole. Requests from these schools are component-level: Paper 3, the HL essay, the investigation's evaluation criterion.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and Al Raha
schoolClusters.note: The widest spread of courses and levels in the emirate, and the cluster where Applications and Interpretation is most common. Students we support from these schools most often need the course identified precisely before anything else happens.

schoolClusters.city: Al Reem Island and Yas Island
schoolClusters.note: Growing cohorts with many mid-course arrivals, so transition work and Group 2 language orals dominate. A student who joined in DP1 from another system needs a mapped gap list rather than a general course review.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways to book a subject specialist, chosen by what the student is short of rather than by how many hours are available. A component problem and a course-wide problem need different shapes of help.

modes.title: Course-long weekly specialist
modes.description: One course at one level, one tutor, a fixed weekly slot across a term or longer. Suited to a student whose grade has drifted across the whole course rather than on one component. Includes a timed assessment every second session and a fortnightly written note, so the course is tracked rather than merely attended.

Finite, usually four to eight sessions, and quoted with an end date. The highest return per hour of anything on this page.

Two or three sessions produce a mapped list of named differences, then a short block closes them. The deliverable is the list, which the student keeps and the school can see.

sections.heading: The six subject groups, and which courses Abu Dhabi families actually book
paragraphs: A Diploma student chooses one course from each of six groups, with three taken at Higher Level, and the enquiry pattern in this emirate is heavily concentrated. Group 5 Mathematics generates more requests than all the other groups combined, which is unsurprising: it is compulsory, it has two distinct courses, and it is where a weak foundation becomes visible fastest. Group 4 sciences come next, led by Chemistry, then Group 3 Economics and Business Management, then Group 1 English A.

Groups 2 and 6 generate fewer requests and are much harder to fill. A Standard Level French or Spanish student with an oral four weeks away is a common and urgent enquiry; a Higher Level Arabic B student or a Visual Arts candidate is a rare one, and the specialist may not exist in a UAE time zone at all. That asymmetry is worth knowing before a family builds a plan around finding someone locally.

There is a second pattern worth naming. Requests cluster around the components that are assessed late and taught early. The scientific investigation, the Mathematics exploration, the Extended Essay and the Higher Level English essay are all introduced in DP1 and completed under pressure in DP2, which is precisely why they arrive as emergencies. A family that books a single-component block on one of them in DP1, when nobody feels any urgency at all, is buying the cheapest useful hours in the whole programme, and buying them at the only point when a tutor has room to teach the skill rather than rescue a draft.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the most consequential choice a Diploma student makes and the one most often made for the wrong reason. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented course. Applications and Interpretation is statistical, modelling-led and assumes a graphing calculator in nearly every question. They are not easier and harder versions of the same syllabus, and a student who dislikes algebra does not automatically belong on Applications, where regression, hypothesis testing and financial mathematics make their own demands.

The weighting structures are identical, which hides the difference. At Standard Level both courses set two papers at 40 per cent each plus the exploration at 20. At Higher Level both set three papers, at 30, 30 and 20 per cent, plus the exploration at 20. So a family comparing the two on paper sees the same architecture and concludes the courses are similar, which they are not. The difference is entirely in what the questions ask for.

Where it matters most is university entry, and this is where honest advice has to be specific rather than general. Engineering, physics, mathematics and several economics degrees typically expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while many other courses accept either. The only safe method is to read the published entry requirements for the specific programme at the specific university, including Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, Zayed University and NYU Abu Dhabi for students staying in the emirate. Nothing on this page should be treated as a substitute for that, and no tutor should present a course choice as a requirement when the university's own page is a click away.

sections.heading: The sciences after the 2023 guide, and where the 24 investigation marks sit
paragraphs: The Diploma sciences were reorganised for first examinations in 2025, and the change matters for anyone buying tuition. The internal assessment is now a single scientific investigation marked out of 24 across four criteria: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, each worth six. It carries 20 per cent of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 1 is in two parts, multiple choice and data-based, at 36 per cent; Paper 2 is at 44 per cent.

The practical consequence is that a quarter of the available marks sit in two criteria most students treat as an afterthought. Conclusion and evaluation together are worth 12 of the 24, and they are the parts written last, usually late at night, usually thinly. A draft that describes a limitation without saying what it does to the result has written an evaluation that scores in the bottom band while reading perfectly acceptably. That is a thirty-minute fix with an outside reader and almost never gets one.

On the written papers, the pattern is just as consistent. Data-based questions in Paper 1B are answered from memory rather than from the data supplied. Extended responses in Paper 2 assert a correct principle and skip the derivation the mark scheme pays for. Command terms are read as synonyms when they are not. None of these is a content gap, and all of them are visible in one marked paper. Confirm the current weightings with your school's Diploma coordinator, because the guides are revised and a stale figure is worse than none.

sections.heading: The orals: the most coachable component in the Diploma
paragraphs: Every Group 1 and Group 2 student sits an individual oral, and it is the single most improvable assessment in the Diploma for a reason nobody says out loud: it is rehearsable. A written paper is sat once under conditions nobody can simulate exactly. An oral is a performance of a known length on prepared material, and performances improve with rehearsal in a way that recall does not.

In English A: Language and Literature the individual oral is worth 30 per cent at Standard Level and 20 per cent at Higher Level, which makes it the largest single component at Standard Level. Students routinely prepare it for a fortnight. The components they prepare for months are worth less. In Group 2 languages the oral carries a comparable share and is where fluency, not vocabulary, decides the band, which is exactly what rehearsal addresses.

Rehearsing over video has a specific advantage: the session can be recorded and the student can hear themselves, which is uncomfortable and extremely effective. Most students have never heard their own oral. The first time they do, they notice the filler, the under-length answers and the three points they meant to make and did not, without any of it needing to be pointed out. Three rehearsals with playback, spread across a fortnight, change a band more reliably than any amount of additional reading. The one caution is timing. An oral rehearsed six weeks out and then left alone goes stale, and an oral rehearsed the night before is a recital rather than a performance. A fortnight of spaced rehearsal, finishing two or three days before the assessment, is the window that produces the best bands.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level: what the extra content actually is
paragraphs: Families often ask whether a student should drop a subject from Higher to Standard Level, and the answer depends on what the difference is in that specific course, because it varies. In some courses Higher Level adds an extra paper. In others it adds content threaded through the existing papers. In English A it adds a separate written essay. Treating Higher Level as a general intensity setting is how the decision gets made badly.

The level change also has consequences beyond workload. A Diploma requires three subjects at Higher Level, so dropping one means raising another. University entry requirements are frequently expressed at Higher Level for the subject most relevant to the degree, so a student intending to read engineering who drops Mathematics to Standard Level may have closed a door that is difficult to reopen. Those are the questions to settle before the timetable change, and they belong to the school's Diploma coordinator rather than to a tutor.

Where tutoring genuinely helps is in establishing whether the Higher Level course is beyond the student or merely behind. Those look identical from a report grade and completely different on a marked paper. A student who scores respectably on Higher Level questions from taught topics and badly on anything from the first term is behind, which is fixable. A student who finds the taught material itself out of reach under time is in a different position, and an honest tutor says so rather than selling two more terms of sessions.

sections.heading: Where Diploma marks are lost, group by group
paragraphs: After enough marked papers the pattern is monotonous, which is good news: monotonous problems are teachable. Across every group, the largest single category of lost marks is a correct idea expressed in a shape the mark scheme does not reward. The second largest is time. Content genuinely never met is a distant third, and it is the only one of the three that most families assume is the problem.

The table below is the diagnostic shortlist a first session works through. It is deliberately concrete, because a general instruction to read the question more carefully has never improved anybody's mark. Telling a Biology student that the word explain requires a because, and then marking four answers until the because appears without prompting, does.

One subject-group note worth adding. In Group 5 the losses are mechanical: method omitted, so partial credit is unavailable. In Group 4 they are evaluative: a limitation named with no consequence attached. In Group 3 they are judgemental: an evaluation that lists and never chooses. In Group 1 they are structural: an argument asserted and never sustained. Four different problems, four different remedies, and a tutor who treats them all as read the question more carefully is not going to move any of them. There is also an order worth respecting. Fixing the mechanical losses first produces visible mark movement inside a month and buys the student enough confidence to tackle the evaluative and structural problems, which take a term. Starting with the hardest category, which is what a keen tutor instinctively does, leaves a student working hard on the slowest-moving part of their own script while the easy marks continue to leak away in every paper they sit.

sections.heading: The honesty line across the investigation, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
paragraphs: A page organised around assessment components has to be clear about which of them a tutor may touch and how. The rule is the same across all of them: a tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains what the criteria reward and how many marks each carries, reads what the student has produced, and writes down what the criteria would credit and refuse. The student then revises it, in their own words, with their own judgements and their own data.

What is never acceptable is authoring, supplying or editing assessed work to completion. This is a live issue in this market rather than a theoretical one: at least one site ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student's own certification rather than on the vendor. A deadline is not a reason to buy one, and no tutor who values a student's diploma will come near it.

Two operational consequences follow. Feedback is written rather than spoken, so a supervisor, a coordinator or a parent can see exactly what was said and when. And board materials are referenced and linked rather than reproduced: subject guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the IB and are used on screen from the official source. Both of those make the support auditable, which is the point. If a Diploma coordinator asked how a student was helped, the answer should be a document rather than a memory.

sections.heading: How private tuition reaches an Abu Dhabi student
paragraphs: One-to-one, over live video, at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. The session uses a shared whiteboard, a document camera or phone stand so handwritten working is visible in both directions, and the real past paper annotated live rather than a retyped version. Sessions are recorded, which matters particularly for Group 2 orals and for Mathematics working a student will want to revisit.

IB Gram does not send tutors into homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates. Visiting a student's address is a service we run only in India. On a page about subject and level matching, that constraint is the argument rather than the apology: the number of people who can teach Higher Level Further Mathematics, hold a valid tutoring permit and reach a specific Abu Dhabi community by 18:00 is frequently zero, while the number who teach the course is not.

Coverage is stated before anything is paid. Mathematics at both levels and in both courses, the three sciences, English A and Economics start within a week in normal conditions. Business Management at Higher Level, French and Spanish are usually available with a little more notice. Arabic B at Higher Level, Further Mathematics, Design Technology, Music and Visual Arts are genuinely thin, and where nothing suitable is free you are told so and offered a later slot, a wait, or nothing rather than a generalist described as a specialist. Where a specialist sits in another time zone, the session times that implies are stated plainly before you decide, because a tutor three hours west means a 21:00 start in Abu Dhabi and that is a real constraint on a school night rather than a detail.

sections.heading: Choosing a private tutor: six questions worth asking
paragraphs: Most families assess a tutor on qualifications and rapport, both of which matter and neither of which predicts much on their own. The six questions below are more diagnostic, and a tutor who answers all of them well is almost always worth booking regardless of where they studied.

Which course and level do you teach, and can you name the components and their weightings? A specialist answers immediately. Where do students lose marks in this course? A good answer is specific to components, not general advice about revision. What will exist after four weeks that I can look at? The right answer is a marked script, an error log and a written note. How do you handle my child's internal assessment? The right answer draws the line at annotation. What happens if this is not working? The right answer involves a review against evidence. And do you hold a private tuition work permit?

That last one is worth asking of anybody. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. Asking the question also tells you something about how seriously the person on the other end takes the arrangement.

process.title: Send the course title and level exactly as the school entered them
process.description: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL is a different request from Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL, and a family that writes maths tutor will get a coin toss. The school's entry record or statement of entry is the only reliable source, and it takes a minute to check.

process.title: Name the component, if you know it
process.description: Paper 3, the HL essay, the investigation's evaluation criterion, an individual oral. A component-level request produces a far better tutor match and a far shorter diagnostic than a general description of the subject being difficult, and it is usually knowable from the last piece of marked work.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: A real lesson on real content with the person who would teach the course, booked without card details. It is also where the course and level get confirmed out loud, which catches the mismatches that a form does not. If the match is wrong, this is the cheap place to find out.

process.title: A timed component diagnostic
process.description: Session one is timed questions from the actual component, marked against the published mark scheme while the student watches. The output is an error log classified by topic and command term. Teaching that starts before this exists is aimed at a described problem rather than a measured one.

process.title: Fortnightly marked work and a term review
process.description: Timed questions every second session, marked and returned with a one-page note. At the end of a term the first diagnostic sits beside the latest comparable one. Where little has moved, the useful responses are a different tutor, a different approach, or stopping, and we will say which we think applies.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses, and the two Mathematics courses are not difficulty settings of one syllabus. Tutors are matched from the school's own entry record, and the first session confirms it out loud, because a competent tutor teaching slightly the wrong course is the most expensive failure in this market.

whyPoints.title: Weightings known before teaching starts
whyPoints.description: A tutor who cannot name the components and their shares is not yet a specialist in that course. Knowing that the investigation's conclusion and evaluation carry 12 of its 24 marks, or that the individual oral is 30 per cent at Standard Level, changes where a term's hours go.

whyPoints.title: Component blocks quoted as finite
whyPoints.description: Paper 3 technique, an HL essay, an oral rehearsal or an evaluation criterion are defined pieces of work with an end date. They are quoted that way rather than converted into an open-ended weekly commitment, and they are the highest return per hour available in the Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Honest about fit, including upwards
whyPoints.description: Sometimes the marked paper shows a student is behind on a Higher Level course, which is fixable. Sometimes it shows the course is out of reach under time, which is a different conversation and belongs with the Diploma coordinator. Selling two more terms instead of having it is the easy option and the wrong one.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work line stated in advance
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and annotates; the student writes. Nothing assessed is authored, supplied or edited to completion, and feedback is written so a coordinator could audit it. In a market where completed Internal Assessments are openly on sale, that is a substantive difference.

whyPoints.title: Scarce courses named as scarce
whyPoints.description: Arabic B at Higher Level, Further Mathematics, Design Technology, Music and Visual Arts are thin in UAE evening hours and you are told so before paying. A generalist presented as a specialist in those courses produces a cancelled arrangement in week three and a wasted month in between.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether we ask for a maths tutor or name the exact course?
faqs.answer: It matters more than almost anything else on this page. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a non-calculator paper; Applications and Interpretation is statistical, modelling-led and assumes a graphing calculator throughout. A tutor strong in one can teach the other's topics and quietly teach them the wrong way, which produces correct sessions and no mark movement. The weighting structures are identical at each level, which hides the difference. Send the course title and level exactly as your child's school entered them, from the statement of entry rather than from memory, and the match stops being a coin toss.

faqs.question: What share of a DP science grade does the investigation carry now?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Standard and Higher Level, marked out of 24 across four criteria worth six marks each: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The useful consequence is that conclusion and evaluation together carry 12 of those 24, and they are the parts students write last and thinnest. An evaluation that names a limitation without stating what it does to the result reads perfectly well and scores in the bottom band. Confirm the current structure with your school's Diploma coordinator, since the science guides changed for first examinations in 2025 and are revised between cohorts.

faqs.question: My son is on Chemistry HL and sinking. Should he drop to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Settle one question first: is he behind, or is the course beyond him? Those look identical on a report grade and completely different on a marked paper. A student who scores respectably on Paper 2 questions from topics taught in the first year, and badly on everything recent, is behind, which is fixable in a term. A student who finds the taught material itself out of reach under time is in a different position. One timed diagnostic distinguishes them. The decision itself belongs with the Diploma coordinator, because dropping a Higher Level subject means raising another and may affect university entry requirements.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics course do UAE universities expect for engineering?
faqs.answer: Engineering and physical-science degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, but the only safe answer is the one published by the specific programme. Read the entry requirements on the university's own page: Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, Zayed University and NYU Abu Dhabi all publish theirs, and they do not all say the same thing. No tutor should present a course choice as a hard requirement when the university's own page is one click away, and no page should imply that tutoring is needed to satisfy an admissions rule.

faqs.question: How much of the English A grade is the individual oral worth?
faqs.answer: In Language and Literature it is 30 per cent at Standard Level and 20 per cent at Higher Level, which makes it the largest single component at Standard Level. Most students prepare it for about a fortnight. It is also the most improvable assessment in the Diploma, because unlike a written paper it is a rehearsable performance on prepared material. Three rehearsals with playback across two weeks change a band more reliably than additional reading does, and recorded video sessions help here specifically: most students have never heard their own oral, and the first time they do they fix half of it unprompted.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 at Higher Level actually test?
faqs.answer: In both Mathematics courses Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions worth 20 per cent of the grade, and it is where Higher Level candidates most often run out of time rather than ideas. Each question builds across several parts, so an early error propagates, and students who have practised only short exam questions have never experienced a problem that develops over twenty minutes. It is the clearest case on this page for a single-component block: four to eight sessions on sustained problems, six to ten weeks before the examination, rather than general course revision.

faqs.question: Why do marks go missing on content my daughter clearly understands?
faqs.answer: Because the mark scheme pays for a shape rather than for the idea, and the shapes are not interchangeable. In Mathematics, method not written down means a slip in the last line costs every mark instead of one. In the sciences, a correct principle asserted without the derivation scores half. In Economics, an evaluation that balances considerations without choosing cannot reach the top band. In English, an argument asserted and never sustained reads fluently and scores descriptively. All four are visible in one marked paper and none of them is a knowledge problem, which is why the first session is a paper rather than a conversation.

faqs.question: Can a single tutor cover two Diploma subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about when. Mathematics and Physics is a genuine pairing: the overlap in algebraic technique is real and a strong tutor in both saves a slot. Chemistry and Biology is a weaker pairing than it looks, because the assessment demands differ more than the content suggests. Economics and Business Management is usually a false economy. The honest test is whether the tutor can name the components and weightings of both courses without checking. If they can, the pairing is real; if they hesitate on the second, you are buying one specialist and one generalist.

faqs.question: How scarce are tutors for less common Diploma courses in the emirate?
faqs.answer: Genuinely scarce, and this is disclosed before booking rather than discovered later. Mathematics in both courses and at both levels, the three sciences, English A and Economics are reliably available in UAE evening hours and usually start within a week. Business Management at Higher Level, French and Spanish need a little more notice. Arabic B at Higher Level, Further Mathematics, Design Technology, Music and Visual Arts are thin, and sometimes the honest answer is that nothing suitable is free. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is a choice rather than an oversight.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my daughter with her Mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary that is worth stating precisely. A tutor will explain what the five criteria reward and how the 20 marks are allocated, discuss whether a proposed question is developable, teach the mathematics the question needs, read a draft your daughter has written and write down what the criteria would credit and refuse. She then revises it herself, in her own words. What never happens is authoring, supplying or editing assessed work to completion. At least one site ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments, which is malpractice under IB rules and risks her own certification.

faqs.question: Is it better to start in DP1 or wait until the components get closer?
faqs.answer: DP1, and the reason is cost rather than virtue. The components that arrive as emergencies in DP2, including the scientific investigation, the Mathematics exploration, the Extended Essay and the Higher Level English essay, are all introduced in DP1 when nobody feels any urgency. A four-session block on one of them in DP1 does the work of three times as many hours bought in a panic in November of DP2, because there is room to teach the skill rather than to triage a draft. The hours bought early are the cheapest useful hours in the whole programme.

faqs.question: What should I ask a prospective tutor before booking anything?
faqs.answer: Six things. Which course and level do you teach, and what are its components and weightings? Where do students lose marks in this specific course? What will exist after four weeks that I can look at? How do you handle an internal assessment draft? What happens if this is not working? And do you hold a private tuition work permit? A specialist answers the first two immediately and specifically. A generalist offers advice about revision technique. The permit question is worth asking of anybody, since private tutoring in the UAE requires one under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

faqs.question: Does my child's tutor need a UAE work permit for private lessons?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, whose service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing and lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be cautious of any amount quoted to you.

faqs.question: How is a video session supposed to work for handwritten mathematics?
faqs.answer: Through a second camera pointed at the page, which sounds improvised and works better than sitting beside someone. A phone on a cheap stand, or a tablet with a stylus, lets the tutor watch the working as it is produced rather than inspect a finished answer. That is the whole point for Group 5 and for Physics, where the marks sit in the method. The real past paper is annotated live on a shared screen, and the session is recorded, so a worked solution from October is still available in April. Nothing on that equipment list costs more than one in-home session at market rate.

faqs.question: Are the weightings on this page definitely current for my child's cohort?
faqs.answer: Treat them as a working guide and confirm them with your school's Diploma coordinator. IB subject guides are revised between cohorts, and the sciences changed shape for first examinations in 2025, so a figure that was right for one year group can be wrong for the next. No IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the organisation's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date published across a site is worse than no date at all. Where this site quotes Cambridge or Pearson dates elsewhere, they come from those boards' own published key dates.

abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.closingHeading: Name the course, then the component
abu-dhabi/ib-private-tutor.closingBody: The single most useful thing you can send is the course title and level exactly as the school entered them, plus the component the last piece of marked work went wrong on. With those two facts a shortlist comes back the same day, and the free trial lesson is a real lesson with the specialist rather than a call with a coordinator. Session one is timed questions from that component, marked against the published mark scheme while your child watches. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, recorded, and the coverage position for your course is stated before anything is paid for.

intro.heading: The Psychology IA is a replication, and most lost marks are decided before data collection
paragraphs: The IB Psychology internal assessment is a report on a simple experimental study that replicates published research. It runs to between 1,800 and 2,200 words and is marked out of 22 across four criteria: introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation. It carries a quarter of the Psychology grade at Standard Level and a fifth at Higher Level under the guide most UAE schools are currently teaching, and the school's marks are moderated by the IB. Confirm the edition of the guide with your child's teacher, because schools move between guide editions at different times.

The word replication carries most of the weight in that description, and it is where families are most often surprised. The student is not designing an original experiment. They are taking a published study, usually a well-known one, and testing a narrow hypothesis derived from its theory with a manageable sample. A student who arrives with an exciting original idea about social media and attention has to be redirected, because an original study has no theoretical anchor to introduce and nothing to compare its result against.

The second thing decided before data collection is the statistics. The design determines which inferential test is available, and the test determines what the analysis section can say. A student who collects ordinal data from an independent samples design and then wants to run a t-test has a problem that cannot be fixed by writing. We work through the design, the level of data and the test together, in one session, before anybody recruits a participant.

The third pre-data decision is ethics, and in the Psychology IA it is a gate rather than a section. The IB's guidelines require informed consent, the right to withdraw, debriefing, anonymity and the absence of stress or deception beyond the trivial, and they set limits on participant age that your child's teacher will confirm. A study that breaches them is not marked down; it cannot be submitted. Students in Abu Dhabi most often trip on recruiting younger siblings or classmates below the permitted age without the right consent.

Everything we do runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The work after data collection is spreadsheet and document work: the raw data table, the descriptive statistics, the test output and the report. ADEK licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools, which set their own internal deadlines, and those deadlines cluster, so an early design session is worth more than a late rescue. A typical engagement is one session before data collection and two afterwards, which is fewer hours than families expect and placed differently from where they would have put them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology sits in group three at SL or HL, covering the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches plus options and research methods. programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools typically run the experimental study late in DP1 or early in DP2, when research methods teaching has caught up with the task. Families here often ask for help at the statistics stage, which is later than ideal but still workable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Individuals and Societies and MYP Sciences both build parts of this task: source-based argument from one, controlled variables and data processing from the other. Students who have done both arrive with the right instincts about measurement.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools around Al Raha and Saadiyat produce students used to structured investigation. Those arriving from systems where psychology was never taught meet hypothesis writing and inferential testing together, which is one additional session rather than a crisis.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students taking DP Psychology complete the same experimental study against the same criteria. The career-related study sometimes supplies a sensible participant pool, provided the ethical requirements around consent and anonymity are met in the same way.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No psychology is assessed in the PYP. The relevant point for families is the reverse one: primary-age children in the household are generally not eligible participants for a DP student's study, because of the age and consent requirements the IB sets.
programmes.countryNote: This comes up constantly in Abu Dhabi, where households are often large and a younger sibling looks like a convenient participant. Check the age rule with the teacher before planning a sample around family members.

abu-dhabi/ib-psychology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: The experimental study has to sit on a theory the student can introduce properly. These are the territories that work, and the practical consequence of each for a replication.

subjects.name: Cognitive approach: memory models
subjects.description: The most replicated territory in the IB. Serial position, levels of processing, schema effects on recall. Materials are easy to standardise, the data is numerical, and the theory is well documented, which makes the introduction straightforward to write.

subjects.name: Cognitive approach: reconstructive memory
subjects.description: Leading question and misinformation studies are popular and ethically manageable if the deception stays trivial and the debrief is thorough. The design risk is a dependent variable that produces too little variation to test.

subjects.name: Cognitive approach: thinking and decision making
subjects.description: Framing effects and anchoring replicate well with short written materials and give clean nominal or ordinal data. A good route for a student whose school limits the time available for data collection.

subjects.name: Sociocultural approach: social identity and conformity
subjects.description: Rich theory and heavier ethical constraints, because anything resembling social pressure needs careful handling. Replications here usually have to be scaled right down to stay inside the guidelines.

subjects.name: Sociocultural approach: stereotypes
subjects.description: Stereotype-related replications need particular care in a multicultural setting, and we steer students away from designs that could categorise participants by nationality or ethnicity. Where the design avoids that, the theory is strong.

subjects.name: Biological approach: effects of arousal and attention
subjects.description: Simple manipulations such as background noise or brief physical activity produce measurable effects on a cognitive task. Attractive because the independent variable is easy to operationalise, with the caution that physical activity needs the school's approval.

subjects.name: Research methods: experimental design
subjects.description: Not a content area but the backbone of the task. Independent samples against repeated measures, counterbalancing, standardised instructions, allocation of participants, and the operationalisation of both variables in measurable terms.

subjects.name: Research methods: descriptive statistics
subjects.description: Measures of central tendency and dispersion, chosen to suit the data rather than by habit, and a graph that shows the comparison the hypothesis makes. A mean with no measure of spread alongside it is a routine mark loss.

subjects.name: Research methods: inferential statistics
subjects.description: Choosing a test from the design and the level of data, stating the significance level and whether the test is one or two tailed, reporting the statistic properly and interpreting it against the null hypothesis rather than announcing proof.

sections.heading: What IB psychology IA help in Abu Dhabi actually does
paragraphs: It front-loads. Almost every decision that sets the ceiling on a Psychology IA mark is made before data collection: which study is being replicated, how the variables are operationalised, which design is used, who the participants are, and which inferential test the resulting data will permit. Help that arrives after data collection can improve the write-up considerably and cannot change any of those five things.

So the first session establishes where the student is. If no data exists, we spend the hour on design and statistics, which is the cheapest and most consequential work available. If data exists, we establish what the data actually is, in the statistical sense, before touching the report: how many participants, which design, what level of measurement the dependent variable produced, and whether the groups are independent or related. Those four answers determine everything the analysis section can legitimately say.

The second thing we do is check the ethics trail, because it is not optional and not retrospective. Consent documentation, the right to withdraw, a debrief, anonymised data, no stress or deception beyond the trivial, and participant eligibility as your child's school applies the IB guidelines. A study with missing consent documentation is a problem no amount of writing solves, and finding that out at the draft stage is the worst possible moment.

The third is the report itself, marked criterion by criterion. Introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation carry 22 marks between them, and the pattern in Abu Dhabi drafts is a strong introduction, a thin exploration section and an evaluation that discusses the wrong things. We mark cold, which approximates moderation better than a teacher's read, and send the mark with reasons in writing.

sections.heading: Choosing a study to replicate that will survive a school setting
paragraphs: The best replications are old, simple, well documented and built on written or spoken materials. That is not a lack of ambition; it is what makes the introduction writable and the procedure standardisable. A student replicating a classic memory or decision-making effect has a theory to introduce, a published method to adapt, a predicted direction for the result and something concrete to compare their own finding against.

The worst choices share a shape: a modern phenomenon with no single published study behind it, a design requiring equipment a school does not have, a procedure needing more than one session per participant, or anything whose manipulation could distress a participant. Each of those fails for a practical reason rather than an intellectual one, which is why the screening conversation is short and worth having early.

The table below sets out the territories that replicate reliably in an Abu Dhabi school, what a manageable version looks like, and the specific risk each carries. It is offered as a screening tool rather than a list to pick from blindly: the student still has to find the published study, read it, and derive their own narrowed hypothesis from its theory.

One scaling rule is worth stating. A school replication should be a simplified version of the original with one independent variable at two levels, and nothing else. Students who add a second variable to make the study more interesting halve their sample per condition and lose the ability to run a simple test. Interest comes from the theory in the introduction, not from the complexity of the design.

sections.heading: Ethics is a gate, and these are its bars
paragraphs: The IB's ethical guidelines for the experimental study are not advisory. A study conducted outside them cannot be submitted, and the student has no route back except running a different study. In Abu Dhabi the two most common breaches are both recruitment problems: participants below the eligible age without the consent the guidelines require, and classmates recruited casually with no documented consent at all.

The requirements have a practical shape. Participants give informed consent before taking part, knowing in general terms what they will be asked to do. They are told they may withdraw at any point, including withdrawing their data afterwards. They are debriefed properly at the end, which means being told what the study was testing and why any minor withholding was necessary. Their data is anonymised, so names do not appear in the report or the raw data table. And nothing in the procedure causes stress, embarrassment or harm.

Deception is permitted only where it is trivial and unavoidable, and the debrief has to repair it. A study that withholds the true purpose of a word list is fine. A study that tells participants they performed badly is not. Students sometimes propose the second kind because the original research did something similar decades ago, and the answer is that ethical standards have moved and the IB's apply now.

Your child's teacher is the authority on how their school implements these guidelines, including participant age limits and whether the school requires its own approval form before data collection. Ask for that form at the design stage. We check that the student has it and that the trail is complete, but the school's own process is the one that governs.

sections.heading: The twenty-two marks and what each criterion rewards
paragraphs: Four criteria carry the 22 marks: introduction, exploration, analysis and evaluation. The distribution is uneven and shapes where effort pays. Introduction and analysis each carry six marks; evaluation carries six; exploration carries four. A report with a well-researched introduction and a thin treatment of design and sampling is leaving the exploration marks on the table, and that is the single most common pattern in drafts we read from this emirate.

Introduction marks come from the theory, not from background. The strongest introductions state the theory, explain the specific published study being replicated, derive the hypothesis from the theory rather than announcing it, and state the null hypothesis as well. Students lose marks here by writing a history of psychology or by stating a hypothesis that does not follow from the theory they just described.

Analysis marks come from doing the statistics correctly and reporting them properly, which includes stating the descriptive statistics chosen and why, presenting a graph that shows the comparison the hypothesis makes, naming the inferential test and justifying it from the design and data level, and interpreting the result against the null hypothesis without claiming proof. Evaluation marks come from evaluating the student's own study: the design, the sample and the procedure, each with a specific effect on the result.

The table below is our reading diagnostic rather than the official rubric. Read the criterion descriptors in your child's own copy of the Psychology guide, in the edition their school teaches, and treat your child's teacher as the authority on how their school applies them. We do not reproduce or supply IB documents, past reports or mark schemes.

sections.heading: Choosing and reporting the inferential test
paragraphs: This is the section students most want and most schools have least time for. The test is not a matter of preference. It follows from two facts: whether the two sets of scores come from the same participants or different ones, and what level of measurement the dependent variable produced. Get those two facts straight and the test chooses itself.

Reporting then has a fixed shape. State the test used and why, in terms of the design and the data level. State the significance level, conventionally 0.05, and whether the test is one tailed or two tailed, with a reason drawn from whether the hypothesis predicted a direction. Give the calculated value of the test statistic and the critical value or probability, and then state the decision about the null hypothesis. A result that does not reach significance is a perfectly good result, reported in exactly the same way.

The language matters at the end. A significant result means the null hypothesis is rejected at the stated level, which is not the same as having proved the research hypothesis, and markers notice the difference. Students who write that their study proves an effect lose marks they would keep by writing that the result supports the hypothesis at the 0.05 level.

One practical warning about sample size. A school study with ten participants per condition may not produce a significant result even if the effect is real, and that is worth anticipating in the design rather than discovering in the analysis. A non-significant result with a clearly reasoned evaluation of sample size and power scores considerably better than a significant result nobody can explain.

sections.heading: Evaluating your own study, not the original research
paragraphs: Evaluation is worth six marks and is the criterion most often misdirected. Students evaluate the published study they replicated, discussing its historical limitations and its ecological validity, when the criterion asks them to evaluate the study they themselves ran. That misdirection is understandable, because the original research is what they read about, and it is the most expensive single error in this task.

The structure that works has three parts: design, sample and procedure. Design evaluation asks whether the chosen design introduced order effects or participant variables, and what that did to the result. Sample evaluation asks who the participants actually were, how they were recruited, and what that means for generalising, which in a school study is usually a great deal. Procedure evaluation asks what in the running of the study could have produced the result independently of the manipulation.

Each point needs a direction and a consequence. A sample of sixth form students from one Abu Dhabi school is not simply a limitation; it is a limitation with a specific effect on what the result can be generalised to, and a student who says so is scoring. A procedure run in a classroom during a lunch break has a specific noise and distraction problem, and naming it concretely is worth more than a sentence about environmental factors.

The strongest evaluations also propose modifications that would change the outcome rather than tidy the method. More participants is a weak improvement unless the student says what difference the extra participants would make to the test. Counterbalancing the order of conditions, matching materials for difficulty, or running all participants at the same time of day are improvements with stated effects, which is exactly what the criterion rewards.

sections.heading: What a Psychology tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: The report must be the student's own work, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice affecting the whole Diploma. In Psychology the line has a second dimension, because the data itself is at stake: a student who invents participants or adjusts scores has fabricated research, which is a more serious matter than a borrowed sentence and is usually visible in data that behaves too well.

A tutor may teach the research methods content; help identify a published study suitable for replication; question whether a hypothesis follows from the theory; check that the operationalisation of both variables is measurable; explain which inferential test the design permits and why; demonstrate a test on a data set the student is not using; mark a draft criterion by criterion; and say that a report needs no further sessions.

A tutor may not write the report, run the student's statistics and hand over the output, supply an introduction, select the replication on the student's behalf or recruit participants. The student runs their own test, which in practice means we talk them through it while they do it, and that is slower and the only acceptable version.

Keep the ethics paperwork, the raw anonymised data and the dated drafts together. That package is both what the school may ask for and the student's own evidence of authorship, and assembling it as the study proceeds costs nothing while reconstructing it later is unpleasant. Several schools in the emirate now ask to see that package alongside the final report, so a student who has kept it has nothing to explain.

sections.heading: Timing, Ramadan, and what the market charges in AED
paragraphs: The scheduling constraint in a Psychology IA is participant availability, not lab access. Data collection needs a time when enough eligible participants are free in one place, which in practice means a school day rather than a weekend. Counting backwards from the school's deadline: design and statistics settled six weeks out, ethics paperwork and school approval five weeks out, data collected four weeks out, analysis and a full draft two weeks out, final fortnight on evaluation and presentation.

Ramadan compresses the school day across the emirate and removes the late-afternoon slot, so sessions move to post-iftar timing rather than pausing. For this task there is a specific consideration: a cognitive performance study run during Ramadan has a participant state issue that a careful student should discuss rather than ignore, and some will prefer to collect data outside that month. Students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside should note that UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the Cambridge February and March series is offered in India only.

On cost, the useful framing for this task is the value of the earliest hour. Published UAE rates, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, Unitors IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, TutorChase AED 270, Bestimate's 2026 survey putting IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, and BartyED AED 650 for a named tutor. Those are the providers' own published figures.

At any of those rates, a single design-and-statistics session before data collection is a better purchase than three sessions afterwards, because it is the only point at which the mark ceiling can still be raised. We quote after the free trial lesson and will tell you honestly when one session is all the study needs.
