process.title: Send the grade breakdown
process.description: Share the subject grade breakdown, the subjects and levels under consideration, and the deadline the grade is needed for. Without the breakdown the first session is spent diagnosing what a document would have told us in five minutes, and you pay for that session.

process.title: Confirm the administration with your school
process.description: Before any teaching is planned, confirm with your IB coordinator that your child can re-register through the school or an accepting centre, which subjects are in scope, and whether the existing internal assessment mark carries forward. That answer shapes the plan and the cost.

process.title: Scope the plan to a component
process.description: We propose a named number of hours against the specific component that lost the marks, with the week-by-week shape and the lost weeks already built in. You get the hour count and the structure before you commit to anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson with the proposed tutor, on the actual component, at no charge. You see the teaching rather than a profile. If the match is wrong we offer a different tutor rather than asking you to persist with one that is not working.

process.title: Teach, then test
process.description: Content repair first, component technique second, full timed papers last. Written feedback after each marked piece. A progress review every fourth session that either confirms the hour count or tells you honestly that it needs to change.

process.title: Hand back to the exam centre
process.description: In the final fortnight the work is timed papers and logistics: the correct timetable confirmed with your centre, the zone checked, the materials ready. We stop adding content, because at that point adding content costs marks rather than earning them.

whyPoints.title: The money is on the page
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all, and the two that do quote USD. This page gives AED bands with the provider who published each one and the month they were read, so you can check the figures rather than take them on faith.

whyPoints.title: Component-level planning, not course repetition
whyPoints.description: A resit plan built around the paper that lost the marks costs a fraction of a plan built around the whole subject, and usually moves the grade further. That requires reading the breakdown first, which is why we ask for it before quoting hours.

whyPoints.title: The calendar, counted backwards
whyPoints.description: The November session is a sequence of subtractions from the papers, and the entry deadline sits months ahead of them. No competitor page researched names a session or a deadline at all. Missing the entry is the one failure no amount of teaching fixes.

whyPoints.title: A specialist, not a neighbour
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Economics Higher Level Paper 3 teacher rather than whoever is within a drive of Al Raha. For a resit, where the whole problem is usually one specialised component, that is the difference between hours that work and hours that pass.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the boundary
whyPoints.description: We teach criteria, review drafts the student wrote, and mark practice work. We do not write assessed work, and we say so because a competitor in this market sells completed Internal Assessments and that is an expulsion risk for your child, not a shortcut.

whyPoints.title: Sourced, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every regulatory statement here points to u.ae, KHDA, MoHRE or a dated news source. We publish no self-assigned star rating, no unsourced statistic, and no IB exam date we could not confirm, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking.

faqs.question: How much should an IB retake tutor in Abu Dhabi cost in total, not per hour?
faqs.answer: Think in hours, then multiply. One Higher Level subject rebuilt across a full resit cycle is typically thirty to thirty-six teaching hours. At the published UAE qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour that is roughly AED 4,500 to AED 10,800; at specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above it runs higher. Those are market figures from Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate as read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Exam entry is charged separately by your school or centre. A short component clinic of four to six sessions can cost a fraction of that and sometimes moves the grade just as far.

faqs.question: Is retaking one Higher Level subject cheaper than retaking two Standard Level ones?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and not by a small margin. A single Higher Level subject concentrates every hour on one set of papers and one failing component, so thirty hours all point the same way. Two Standard Level subjects split the hours, duplicate the diagnostic work and double the practice the student has to complete between sessions, while the week stays the same length. Paper technique does transfer between subjects, which is why two subjects is not quite double the cost, but it is close. The better question is which grade the university condition actually names, because retaking a subject nobody asked about is the most expensive mistake available here.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home retake tutor in Abu Dhabi cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Almost all of the gap is travel. Published UAE in-home rates run roughly AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 online, and a tutor crossing from Abu Dhabi Island to Khalifa City in evening traffic is being paid for that journey whether the invoice itemises it or not. The second cost is hidden: insisting on in-home shrinks your shortlist to specialists who live within a drive, which for a minority Higher Level subject often means nobody suitable. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Lessons to Abu Dhabi families are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is an India-only service for us.

faqs.question: When does registration for a November IB resit actually close?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, which is the detail that catches families out. Re-registration closes while results are still being discussed and while university appeals are still live, so the decision has to be made faster than it feels reasonable to make it. We do not publish a specific date on this page because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unconfirmed date is worse than no date. Ask your school's IB coordinator in the first fortnight after results, in writing, and ask them for the centre's internal cut-off too, which is usually earlier than the IB's own.

faqs.question: Can my child keep the Internal Assessment mark from the first attempt?
faqs.answer: In many subjects yes, and in some the option exists to submit new work instead, but the answer is subject-specific and your IB coordinator is the authority on your child's case. It matters financially as well as academically: if the papers were the problem and the internal assessment mark was sound, carrying it forward means every tutoring hour goes into paper technique. If the internal assessment was the weak component, the plan and the cost are different, and you need the coordinator's written answer before booking any hours. We plan the teaching around their decision rather than guessing at it.

faqs.question: Would an enquiry upon results be cheaper than paying for a retake?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking before you spend anything. Where the component breakdown looks inconsistent with everything the student produced across two years, a remark is faster and cheaper than a resit, and it has a short window immediately after results. Your school administers it. We will say so when the breakdown points that way, because a tutoring plan sold over the top of an unexplored remark route is a tutoring plan optimising for our hours rather than your outcome. If the remark changes nothing, the resit route is still open and you have lost only a few weeks.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do Abu Dhabi students retake most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level leads clearly, usually because of Paper 3, the extended investigative paper. Chemistry Higher Level and Physics Higher Level follow, with the losses concentrated in topics taught late in the second year when coursework pressure peaks. Economics Higher Level appears regularly because of Paper 3, the quantitative paper. Computer Science Higher Level is less common but often the most improvable, because the recurring loss is pseudocode convention under timing rather than any real gap in understanding. Each of those is a different plan with a different hour count.

faqs.question: Is there any local IB specialist in Al Ain for a Higher Level resit?
faqs.answer: Rarely at Higher Level, and this is the honest answer rather than a sales line. Al Ain sits under ADEK like Abu Dhabi city but has a much smaller set of international schools and correspondingly few resident subject specialists at Diploma Higher Level. Families there who insist on an in-person tutor usually end up with someone teaching a level below the one being resat. Online delivery is not a second-best option in Al Ain; it is how a student there gets a Chemistry Higher Level or Computer Science Higher Level teacher at all. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time either way.

faqs.question: Does ADEK approve or license private tutors in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, as u.ae sets out, and publishes its own school inspection ratings. It does not approve individual tutors and it does not set tutoring rates. The permit that applies to an individual tutor is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Any tutoring page describing itself as ADEK-approved or KHDA-approved without holding the specific permit involved is making a claim it cannot support. IB Gram holds no such approval and does not claim one.

faqs.question: Can we hire my child's own school teacher privately for the resit?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct making the same point about students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, but treat the direction as settled. Beyond the rules, there is a practical reason: the teacher who taught the course the first time is the least likely person to spot why the delivery did not land.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start a November resit plan?
faqs.answer: The registration deadline is the real cut-off, not the teaching one. Once entry is secured, a six to eight week intensive of two sessions a week built entirely around timed papers can still move a grade, particularly where the problem is execution rather than content. What it cannot do is rebuild a topic that was never learned, and it costs more per grade point than starting in the summer because you are buying intensity to replace time. If you are inside eight weeks, the first conversation should be about scope reduction: one component, not one subject.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child redo the Internal Assessment if that is the weak part?
faqs.answer: Within the IB's academic-honesty boundary, and the boundary is firm. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each rewards, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and evidence, teach referencing and data presentation, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text to insert, rewrite a paragraph to its final form, choose the question outright or generate the data. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student. There is a provider in this market selling completed Internal Assessments; that is an expulsion risk with a price tag.

faqs.question: Do resit grades get averaged with the first attempt?
faqs.answer: No. The two attempts do not average. The Diploma is reissued using the subject results that stand after the resit, which is why a retake is worth considering at all. Your IB coordinator can confirm exactly how this works for your child's registration and which results appear on the reissued documents. The practical consequence is that a resit carries upside without arithmetic downside to the subject grade, so the decision turns entirely on cost, time and whether the grade is actually needed for something specific rather than on any risk of making the result worse.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan or while the family travels in summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. During Ramadan the productive study window for many students moves to after Iftar, and a plan insisting on a 17:00 session through the month will simply lose sessions. Summer travel is the bigger practical problem, because it usually collides with the content-repair block a November plan depends on. Online delivery survives a family moving between Abu Dhabi and abroad; an in-home arrangement does not. Write the weeks you already know will be lost into the plan before it starts, then protect the rest, because continuity is what a resit cycle is actually built on.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram guarantee the grade goes up after a retake?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. A resit plan changes what a student knows, how quickly they work, and how accurately they read a command term. It cannot promise a 7 or any specific grade movement, and a page offering that guarantee is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you will not check. What we will commit to is a named hour count against a named component, written feedback on every marked piece, a progress review every fourth session, and an honest statement if the plan needs changing. We also publish no self-assigned star rating and no statistic without its source.

faqs.question: What does the resit grade actually need to be for before we pay for it?
faqs.answer: Find out first, because the answer changes whether the spend makes sense. A UK or UAE university offer naming a specific subject grade is a clear case for a resit. A general wish for a higher total is weaker, especially once the hour cost is on the table. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency has published requirements for the British and American tracks, but no IB points threshold appears in the source used here, so check moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority directly. No part of equivalency, admission or progression requires tutoring, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

abu-dhabi/ib-retake-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the breakdown, not the booking
abu-dhabi/ib-retake-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB retake tutor in Abu Dhabi, the cheapest useful hour you will spend is the one before you book anything: get the component grade breakdown from your school, ask the IB coordinator in writing whether your child can re-register and whether the internal assessment mark carries forward, and find out exactly which grade the university condition names. Send us those three answers and we will propose a named hour count against the specific component that lost the marks, with the lost weeks already built in. A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor comes first, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so you watch the teaching before you commit to the plan.

abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.tutorsIntro: These tutors run revision rather than teaching courses. They work from past-paper performance, build a week-by-week sequence backwards from the papers, and mark timed work between sessions so the next session starts from evidence instead of a conversation.

intro.heading: Revision is sold by the block, so price the block
paragraphs: The reason two Abu Dhabi families get quotes of AED 3,000 and AED 18,000 for the same thing is that neither quote is for the same thing. Revision is not an hourly product. It is a block with a length, a frequency, a group size and a marking load, and changing any one of those moves the total more than the headline hourly rate does. So this page starts with the block and works back to the hour, which is the opposite of how the rest of this market presents it.

The published market figures give you the anchors. Bestimate's UAE estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Advertised packages in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Per hour, UAE rates run roughly AED 33-65 budget, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200-450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists, with one premium provider at AED 650. Those are other people's prices, read in October 2026, published here because almost nobody in this search results page publishes any.

Now the arithmetic that matters. A full Diploma revision run is about sixteen weeks before the May papers. At one ninety-minute session a week on one subject, that is twenty-four hours. At the qualified-tutor band that is roughly AED 3,600-7,200 for the subject. Two subjects across the same sixteen weeks is forty-eight hours, and the total doubles while the calendar does not get longer, which is why most families revise two subjects properly rather than four badly. A compressed six-week run at two sessions a week is eighteen hours, costs less in total and more per week, and buys intensity in place of time.

What changes the number specifically in Abu Dhabi is staffing depth rather than any emirate-level price difference. The emirate has fewer IB World Schools than Dubai and therefore a thinner resident pool in the Higher Level subjects families most want revised: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Chemistry, Physics, Economics. Thin supply is priced. A Biology Standard Level revision block is cheap to staff from Al Reef to Al Ain; a Computer Science Higher Level block in February is not, anywhere.

IB Gram delivers revision to Abu Dhabi families as one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For a revision block that is a structural advantage, because the whole value of revision is the specialist who knows where marks go in that exact paper, and geography has nothing to do with who that person is.

abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.programmesIntro: Revision means something different in each IB programme, and the cost follows that difference. Below is what is actually being revised at each stage, and what the emirate's provision looks like.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject grade comes from externally marked papers plus an internally assessed component, and the bonus points come from a TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Revision here is paper-specific: the question is not whether the student knows the topic but whether they can produce the marks the paper allocates within the time the paper allows.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts are concentrated in a modest number of schools on the island and along the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. Cohort sizes mean school-run revision sessions are often generalist rather than paper-specific, which is precisely the gap a paid revision block is being asked to fill, and it is worth asking the school what it already provides before paying for anything.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, with the Personal Project in the final year. Most MYP schools run no external examination, so revision here is about criterion literacy rather than paper technique: knowing what criterion C actually rewards and what it never rewards, and writing to it on purpose.
programmes.countryNote: Because MYP revision is criterion-led, a block here is shorter and cheaper than a Diploma block, usually four to six sessions ahead of a summative assessment window. Abu Dhabi families often buy their first revision block at this stage, which is also the cheapest point at which the algebraic fluency gap that later ruins a Mathematics Paper 1 can be closed.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry across six themes, with the exhibition in the final year. There is no revision in the examination sense at all. What a tutor can usefully do is build number fluency and reading stamina, which are the two things that decide how hard the MYP years feel later.
programmes.countryNote: Buying revision classes at PYP level is usually the wrong purchase and we will say so. Where an Abu Dhabi family does want support at this stage, a short weekly maths or reading block is the honest version, priced at the lower end of the market because it does not require a Diploma subject specialist.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: The TOK exhibition and essay plus the 4,000-word Extended Essay together feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix. These are the components most often left out of a revision budget and the ones most likely to cost a Diploma total its last point, because they are assessed against criteria most students never read closely.
programmes.countryNote: Revision support here is criterion teaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, never writing or editing to completion. Abu Dhabi families often discover in the final term that the bonus-point matrix is where the missing point lives, and a short block on it costs far less than a subject block.

abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: Revision costs are driven by which subject you are revising, because the staffing market for each is different. These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families most often book a revision block in, with the paper that justifies the spend.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most revised subject and the dearest to staff at Higher Level. Revision concentrates on Paper 1, where algebraic accuracy without a calculator decides the grade, and on Paper 3 at Higher Level, which asks the student to follow an unfamiliar extended argument under time.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-permitted throughout, which makes the revision load verbal rather than computational. Blocks focus on interpreting a model and commenting on its limitations, because students lose marks describing a correct statistical result in language that earns nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms dominate the revision list. A block here is heavy on multi-step calculation accuracy and on navigating the data booklet quickly, which is a drilled skill and not a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, induction and quantum arrive late in the second year and are consistently the weakest topics at revision time. Extended-response reasoning steps, not final answers, are where the marks sit, so revision is as much writing practice as physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content volume in the Diploma sciences, so revision is retrieval under timing rather than re-teaching. Command-term discipline carries the grade: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each pay differently.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3, the quantitative paper, is the single most common reason a revision block gets booked in this subject. Diagram labelling is the cheapest mark recovery available anywhere in the Diploma.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis of an unseen text is the revisable part, because it rewards a repeatable method. Revision installs that method and then runs it against unseen extracts until the structure is automatic.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Students name a framework and then fail to apply it to the stimulus, which caps the grade in the description bands. A revision block is a sequence of timed case responses with structural feedback.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Productive skills decide the grade while most private revision is receptive, which is the wrong way round. Blocks weight timed writing in the required text types and oral rehearsal with sentence-level correction.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Study recall is usually sound and evaluation is thin, which holds answers in the middle bands. Revision targets methodological critique and the Higher Level extensions, which are routinely under-revised.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study precision separates the top bands: named places, dated events, figures. Revision converts a bank of vague examples into a small number of exact ones the student can deploy under time.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions under timing and the Higher Level abstract data structures topic. The hardest subject in this list to staff in Abu Dhabi and often the most improvable per hour spent.

abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes when a revision session can start and therefore how many sessions a week is realistic, which is the real constraint on a block. These are the parts of the emirate the bookings come from.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island
regions.note: Dense apartment living and short school runs. Sessions start early in the evening, but a quiet room for ninety minutes is the limiting factor, and families often shift to 19:30 once younger siblings are settled.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with a 20-40 minute school run to the island. A 16:30 start is realistic here only on days without an activity, which is why most Khalifa City blocks settle on two fixed evenings rather than flexible slots.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Close enough to the island schools that students are home by 15:45, which makes this the one part of the emirate where a twice-weekly block genuinely fits without eating into sleep.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Small DP cohorts mean few classmates revising the same Higher Level subject, so there is no study group to lean on and the block carries more weight than it would in a larger cohort.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with younger DP cohorts, so school-side revision provision is still maturing. Families here more often buy a block to cover something the school has not yet built.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Long commutes from mainland communities push sessions later, and during Ramadan the practical window moves to post-Iftar entirely. Arabic B and Mathematics blocks cluster here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Ninety minutes inland, under the same regulator, with almost no resident Higher Level Diploma specialists. Online delivery is the only route to a paper-specific revision tutor in this catchment.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established central districts with a high share of students holding conditional UK and UAE offers, which is the circumstance that justifies a sixteen-week block rather than a six-week one.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi Island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's longest-established international provision, where school-run revision is usually structured and worth checking before buying anything. Named here as context for the local education landscape only.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland
schoolClusters.note: Larger cohorts and broader Higher Level choice, but revision provision is spread thinner across more subjects, which is where the gaps a paid block fills tend to appear. Listed as ecosystem context.

sections.heading: What an IB revision block costs in Abu Dhabi, by length
paragraphs: An IB revision block in Abu Dhabi costs between roughly AED 600 and roughly AED 11,000 for one subject, and the spread is almost entirely about how many hours you buy rather than what an hour costs. The table below prices the common block shapes using published UAE market bands as read in October 2026, so you can see the total before you discuss a rate.

Read the table by row rather than by column. The cheapest row is a four-session component block, which is also the row most families never consider, because the market sells subjects rather than papers. If mock evidence shows Economics Higher Level at a 5 with Paper 3 the only weak component, four sessions on Paper 3 is a better purchase than twenty-four hours on Economics, and it costs a sixth as much. The most expensive row is two Higher Level subjects across sixteen weeks, which is a genuine commitment and should only be entered with a reason more specific than wanting better grades.

Two figures are not in the table because they are not tutoring costs. Exam entry is handled and charged by your school or exam centre. And school-run revision, where it exists, is often included in fees you are already paying, which makes it the first thing to check rather than the last. A parent who buys a sixteen-week block for a subject the school is already revising intensively has bought the same thing twice.

For context on where tutoring sits in a family's education spend: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi fee regulation sits with ADEK and operates separately, but the shape of the household budget is the same across the Gulf. School fees are the fixed cost. Revision is the variable one, which is exactly why it should be scoped to a named component and a named number of weeks rather than booked open-ended.

sections.heading: Why group size changes the price more than the tutor does
paragraphs: The biggest single lever on a revision quote is not the tutor's seniority. It is how many students are in the room and how much marking the tutor does between sessions. A group of six at a tuition centre and a one-to-one block with the same teacher are different products at different prices because the marking load per student differs by a factor of six, and marking is where revision feedback actually lives.

So price the marking, not just the contact time. A ninety-minute one-to-one session with a full marked paper returned before the next session involves perhaps forty minutes of the tutor's time outside the lesson. That is real work and it is in the rate whether anyone itemises it or not. A group session where the paper is marked collectively, or self-marked against a scheme, costs less and tells the student less about their own specific error pattern. Both are legitimate; they are not interchangeable.

Paired revision is the useful middle, and the condition on it is strict. Two students genuinely at the same level in the same subject, with similar error patterns, can share a session productively and halve the cost each. Two students at different levels cannot, and the session degrades into the tutor teaching one and parking the other. We will say no to a pairing that will not work rather than take the booking, because an eight-week block that is wasted costs the family more than a quoted rate difference ever saves.

One caution about the market generally. Several providers in this space advertise a low group rate and a high one-to-one rate on the same page without saying what the group size is. Ask the number. Ask what happens if two of the group drop out, and whether the rate then changes. Ask who marks the timed work and when it comes back. Those three questions separate a revision product from a room with a teacher in it.

Ask who marks the timed work and how quickly it returns

sections.heading: The sixteen weeks before the May papers, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE IB schools sit the May session, so a Diploma revision block is a subtraction from May rather than an addition to today. Nobody in this search results page publishes a revision calendar, which is odd, because sequencing is most of what a parent is buying. The table below gives the order of the weeks and what each block of weeks should actually contain.

Note what the table does not contain: specific dates. The IB's own website blocks automated checking, so no IB exam or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB directly, and an unconfirmed date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date. Confirm the window with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. For Cambridge and Pearson qualifications the dated equivalents are available and sourced: Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with the November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

The sequencing mistake we see most often in this emirate is running content revision too late. A block still teaching new topics in the final fortnight has been mis-scoped, because at that point every hour spent on content is an hour not spent on timed execution, and timed execution is what the mark scheme rewards. The reverse mistake also exists: starting full papers in week one, before there is enough content in place for a paper to produce useful diagnostic information rather than just a low score.

Build the known losses into the plan at the start. Abu Dhabi families travel in the school holidays, and the holidays sit inside the revision window. Where Ramadan falls in the block, sessions move to post-Iftar rather than stopping, and the family rhythm reorganises for a month. A sixteen-week plan with four weeks of travel in it is a twelve-week plan, and discovering that in January is free while discovering it in April is not.

sections.heading: Online revision against the in-home version, priced
paragraphs: Families searching for revision classes in Abu Dhabi often picture a tutor at the dining table. That is a real market and it has real prices: Bestimate puts UAE in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350 an hour, independent home tutors ask AED 200-500, and advertised in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions run around AED 1,599-1,799. Online qualified tutoring sits at roughly AED 150-300. The gap is mostly travel, paid for whether the invoice says so or not.

For revision specifically there is a second cost that does not appear on any invoice. Insisting the tutor arrives in person narrows your shortlist to people who teach the exact subject at the exact level and live within a sensible drive of your community. In Khalifa City for Biology Standard Level, that constraint is survivable. For Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3, or Computer Science Higher Level, it usually produces either nobody or a generalist teaching a level below the one being revised, and a generalist running a revision block is an expensive way to feel organised.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Revision for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. We state it plainly because the opposite wastes your time. For a sixteen-week block the online route also protects continuity in ways the in-home one cannot: no session lost to Mussafah traffic or a sandstorm, every worked solution captured on a shared screen and reopenable in week fourteen, and sessions that keep running while the family travels.

There is one in-home advantage worth naming honestly, because pretending otherwise is not useful. A student who will not sit down without someone physically present sometimes does better with a person in the room, regardless of that person's subject depth. If that is your child, say so early. The right answer may be a local generalist for accountability plus a short online component block with a specialist, which is cheaper than either option bought at full length.

sections.heading: What the mock evidence has to show before a block is worth buying
paragraphs: A revision block bought without component-level mock evidence is a block priced on a guess. The useful document is not the mock grade; it is the breakdown showing how each paper and the internally assessed component contributed. Most Abu Dhabi schools will provide it if asked, and it takes five minutes to read.

Three patterns recur, and each points at a differently priced block. A flat profile, every component a little under target, usually means timing and execution rather than knowledge, and responds to the six-week intensive built on full papers. A single collapsed component against sound performance elsewhere points at the four-session component block, which is the cheapest useful purchase in this market. A weak internally assessed mark with strong papers is the awkward case, because the remedy depends on the subject and on the school's internal deadlines, and it needs the subject teacher's input first.

The fourth possibility is that no block is needed yet. Where a mock was sat early, before a third of the syllabus had been taught, the score is not evidence of anything except the calendar. Buying sixteen weeks of revision on the back of a mock in October is often buying re-teaching of content the school has not finished teaching. We will say so, and the honest recommendation is sometimes to wait six weeks and rebook on better information.

Practically: put the mock breakdown next to the student's internally assessed marks and ask one question. Were the mocks consistently stronger than the timed work, or consistently weaker? Stronger mocks than timed work points at execution. Weaker points at content. Those are different blocks at different prices, and knowing which you have is worth more than the first five hours of anyone's time.

sections.heading: Who is legally allowed to run paid revision in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, and a parent can verify it. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

Two things follow from that, and neither is in most providers' marketing. The permit is free, so anyone describing a permit fee as a cost driver in their rate is inventing one. And no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify fine amounts or detail the penalties; a figure circulating as a specific maximum could not be verified and is left out of this page deliberately.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. A training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which u.ae describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK regulates schools, not tutoring rates, and approves no individual tutor.

One boundary to apply before you book. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct makes the same point. So the apparently convenient move, paying your child's own subject teacher to run the revision block, is the one to avoid. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, MoE, IB or Cambridge approval, accreditation or partnership and does not claim any.

sections.heading: Revision for TOK, the Extended Essay and the internal assessments
paragraphs: The components most often left out of a revision budget are the ones most likely to cost a Diploma total its last point. The TOK exhibition and essay plus the Extended Essay feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix, and the internally assessed component in each subject carries real weight within that subject's grade. None of this is examined in May in the way a paper is, which is exactly why it drops out of a revision plan built around papers.

What revision means here is criterion teaching. Each of these components is marked against named criteria with published mark allocations, and most students have never read them closely enough to write to them on purpose. A short block that walks the criteria, shows what each one rewards and what it never rewards, and then gives feedback on the student's own draft against those criteria is among the cheapest grade movements available in the Diploma.

The boundary is firm and worth stating before anyone asks. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and evidence, teach referencing conventions, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of the work, supply text to insert, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, choose the research question outright or generate data. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student, not the tutor.

That line is not boilerplate in this market. There is a provider selling completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is not a cheaper revision block; it is an expulsion risk with a price attached, and it is the reason to be sceptical of any revision offer phrased around a guaranteed outcome. We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source, which is both lawful and keeps the student on the current version.

Criterion literacy is the cheapest grade movement in the Diploma
A tutor reviews the student's own draft; it never writes any part of it
No grade guarantee appears anywhere on IB Gram's pages
Official papers and mark schemes are linked, never redistributed

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the weeks you will actually lose
paragraphs: A sixteen-week block running into May crosses the whole shape of the UAE spring, and the calendar realities are not decoration. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, and the usable weekday window for an Abu Dhabi student after the commute home is roughly 16:00 to 21:00, narrower in Khalifa City and Al Reef than on the island or in Al Raha because of the school run.

Where Ramadan falls inside the block, the sessions move rather than stop. School days shorten, the household reorganises around Iftar, and for many students the productive study window shifts to after the evening meal. A plan that keeps insisting on a 17:00 slot through the month will quietly lose four to six sessions, which is a quarter of a sixteen-week block. Moving to post-Iftar for the month preserves the continuity, and continuity is the whole mechanism by which revision works.

Travel is the larger practical risk because it is predictable and families plan it before they plan revision. Spring holidays sit inside the revision window, and Abu Dhabi households travel in them. Online delivery survives that: a session runs from a hotel room in Kerala or Kent as well as it runs from Al Bateen, allowing for the time difference. An in-home arrangement does not survive it at all, because the tutor is in Khalifa City and the student is not.

So agree the week-by-week shape at the start and write down the weeks you already know will be lost, before the first session rather than after the tenth. A sixteen-week plan with four known lost weeks is a twelve-week plan and should be scoped as one. Building the losses in costs nothing in January. Discovering them in April costs the thing you were buying.

process.title: Send the mock breakdown
process.description: Share the component-level mock marks, the subjects and levels, and the date of the papers. With that in hand we can quote a block length and an hour count. Without it, the first session is spent discovering what a document would have shown in five minutes.

process.title: Check what the school already provides
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator what revision the school runs, in which subjects, and how intensively. Where provision is already strong, the honest recommendation is a short component block rather than a full one, and we would rather tell you that than sell sixteen weeks twice.

process.title: Scope the block in weeks, not hours
process.description: We propose a named number of weeks and sessions against named components, with the travel weeks and Ramadan already built in. You see the total hours and the total structure before any money is discussed.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson with the proposed tutor, on the actual weakest component, at no charge. You watch the teaching rather than read a profile. If the match is wrong we offer a different tutor instead of asking you to persist.

process.title: Teach, mark, review
process.description: Topic repair first, component technique second, full timed papers last. One marked timed piece between sessions with written feedback. A review at weeks four, eight and twelve that either confirms the plan or says plainly that it needs changing.

process.title: Stop adding content
process.description: In the final fortnight the work is retrieval, logistics and sleep. We confirm the timetable with the family, stop introducing anything new, and reduce session length rather than increase it. Adding content in the last two weeks costs marks rather than earning them.

whyPoints.title: The block is priced, not just the hour
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and the two that do quote USD. This page prices the actual purchase, a block of a named length, in AED, with the provider who published each band and the month it was read.

whyPoints.title: Group size is disclosed as a number
whyPoints.description: The largest lever on a revision quote is how many students share the session and how much marking happens per student. We state the trade rather than advertising a low group rate without saying how many people are in the group.

whyPoints.title: Sequenced backwards from the papers
whyPoints.description: Topic repair, then component technique, then full timed papers, then stop. No researched competitor publishes a revision sequence at all, and the most common failure we see in this emirate is content teaching still running in the final fortnight.

whyPoints.title: A paper specialist, not a neighbour
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Mathematics Higher Level Paper 3 teacher rather than whoever lives near Al Raha. Revision is paper-specific work, so the specialist matters more here than in any other kind of tutoring.

whyPoints.title: The cheap option offered first
whyPoints.description: Where mock evidence shows one failing component, we quote a four-session component block rather than sixteen weeks, because it costs a sixth as much and often moves the grade just as far. We also tell you when the school's own provision makes a block unnecessary.

faqs.question: How much do IB revision classes in Abu Dhabi cost for a full term?
faqs.answer: A sixteen-week block of one weekly ninety-minute session is about twenty-four teaching hours. At the published UAE qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour that is roughly AED 3,600-7,200 for one subject; at specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above it runs to about AED 10,800. Those bands come from Unitors, TutorChase and Bestimate as read in October 2026 and are market figures, not an IB Gram price list. Exam entry is charged separately by your school. A four-session component block on a single weak paper costs a fraction of this and is often the better purchase.

faqs.question: Is a six-week intensive cheaper than a sixteen-week revision block?
faqs.answer: Cheaper in total and more expensive per week. Eighteen hours against twenty-four means a lower bill, but you are buying intensity in place of time, and intensity moves a grade less efficiently than spacing does. The intensive works well where the mock evidence points at execution rather than knowledge, because full timed papers with feedback are what fixes execution. It works badly where whole topics are missing, because six weeks is not long enough to teach content and then practise it. If you are inside eight weeks of the papers, reduce the scope to one component rather than compressing a whole subject.

faqs.question: Does a group revision class work as well as one-to-one for IB?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on the marking. A group session where timed work is marked collectively or self-marked tells a student far less about their own error pattern than a one-to-one session with a full paper marked and returned. For content coverage a group is adequate and cheaper. For component technique, which is what Diploma revision mostly is, individual marking is the mechanism. Ask any provider three questions: how many students exactly, who marks the timed work, and how quickly it comes back. Those answers separate a revision product from a room with a teacher in it.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May papers should a revision block start?
faqs.answer: Sixteen weeks is the usual full run and it has a clear internal shape: topic repair in the first four weeks, component technique in the next four, full timed papers in the following four, and error-pattern drilling before stopping entirely in the last fortnight. Starting earlier than sixteen weeks usually means revising content the school has not finished teaching. Starting later is workable but narrows what is realistic. Confirm the actual examination window with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than relying on any tutoring site, including this one, for an IB date.

faqs.question: Can two of my children share one IB revision session to cut the cost?
faqs.answer: Only if they are genuinely at the same level in the same subject with similar error patterns. Paired revision halves the per-student cost and also halves the marking per student, which is an honest trade when the match is real. When it is not, the session degrades into teaching one child while the other waits, and eight weeks of that costs more than any rate saving. We will decline a pairing we think will not work rather than take the booking. Siblings two years apart in different subjects cannot share a block, however convenient the timing would be.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are the most expensive to find a revision tutor for in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Computer Science at Higher Level is the hardest to staff locally, followed by Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Economics Higher Level, where the demand is concentrated on Paper 3 in each case. Abu Dhabi has fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, so the resident pool in minority Higher Level subjects is thin, and thin supply prices upward. Biology and Business Management at Standard Level are the easiest and cheapest to staff. Delivering online removes the geography constraint entirely, which is the main reason specialist subjects are findable at all from Al Ain or Al Shamkha.

faqs.question: What should the mock results show before we pay for a revision block?
faqs.answer: Component-level marks rather than an overall grade. Ask the school for the breakdown showing how each paper and the internally assessed component contributed. A flat profile across components points at timing and execution, and the six-week intensive on full papers suits it. One collapsed component against sound performance elsewhere points at a four-session component block, which is the cheapest useful intervention available. A mock sat before a third of the syllabus had been taught is not evidence of anything except the calendar, and buying sixteen weeks on the back of it usually means paying for re-teaching the school is about to do anyway.

faqs.question: Do revision sessions keep running during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing moved rather than the sessions cancelled. School days shorten through the month, the household reorganises around Iftar, and for most students the productive window shifts to after the evening meal. A block that insists on a 17:00 slot through Ramadan will quietly lose four to six sessions, which in a sixteen-week plan is a quarter of what you bought. Agree the post-Iftar timing before the month starts rather than improvising in week two. Continuity is the mechanism by which revision works, so protecting the sequence matters more than protecting the hour it happens at.

faqs.question: Will the block continue if we travel out of the UAE during the spring holidays?
faqs.answer: Online sessions continue, allowing for the time difference, which is one of the practical reasons we deliver this way. An in-home arrangement does not continue, because the tutor is in Abu Dhabi and the student is not. The more useful habit is to write the travel weeks into the plan before the first session. A sixteen-week block with four known travel weeks is a twelve-week block and should be scoped, sequenced and priced as one. Discovering the gap in April rather than January is how a revision plan loses its final-stage timed papers, which are the stage that matters most.

faqs.question: Is the school's own revision programme enough on its own?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is the first thing to check rather than the last. Many Abu Dhabi schools run structured revision in the final term, and it is already inside fees you are paying. Where that provision is strong in a subject, buying a sixteen-week private block in the same subject is paying twice for the same thing. Ask the IB coordinator which subjects are covered, how intensively, and whether timed work is individually marked. Where the answer is thin in one subject or one component, that is exactly where a short private block earns its money.

faqs.question: Can a revision tutor help with the Extended Essay and TOK as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a firm boundary, and it is often the best value in the whole plan. These components feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix and are marked against named criteria most students have never read closely. A tutor may teach those criteria, discuss whether a research question is answerable in the word count, read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on structure, argument and evidence, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph to its final form, choose the question or generate data. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student.

faqs.question: Does the price of a revision class in Abu Dhabi include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask any provider directly and get the answer in writing before booking, because the quoted figure and the invoiced figure are not always the same thing. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees as fact on this page without a Federal Tax Authority citation, which is the honest position rather than a dodge. What matters practically is whether the number you were quoted is the number you pay, and whether a block price is per session, per hour or inclusive of marking time. The AED bands on this page are published market rates from other providers, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Are revision tutors in Abu Dhabi required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published so no amount should be quoted to you. ADEK licenses and inspects private schools in Abu Dhabi; it does not approve individual tutors.

faqs.question: Can we book my child's own subject teacher to run the revision block privately?
faqs.answer: Avoid it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct makes the same point about students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it. There is also a practical reason beyond the rules: the teacher who delivered the course the first time is the least likely person to spot why the delivery did not land for your child.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest revision purchase that can still move an IB grade?
faqs.answer: A four-session component block on one named paper, priced at roughly AED 900-2,700 at published UAE market rates for six hours of teaching. It only works where mock evidence shows the rest of the subject performing and one component dragging the grade down, which is more common than parents expect. Economics Higher Level Paper 3 and Mathematics Higher Level Paper 3 are the two components where this happens most often in Abu Dhabi. Where two or more components are weak, the component block is not enough and you are back to a full block, honestly priced.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram promise the grade will improve after a revision block?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody honestly can. A revision block changes what a student can retrieve under time, how accurately they read a command term and how they allocate minutes across a paper. It cannot promise a 7 or any specific movement, and a page offering that is either misunderstanding the assessment or hoping you will not check. What we commit to is a named number of weeks against named components, one marked timed piece between sessions with written feedback, and reviews at weeks four, eight and twelve that say plainly whether the plan is working.

abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.closingHeading: Price the block before you price the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-revision-classes.closingBody: If you are costing IB revision classes in Abu Dhabi, work out the purchase before you negotiate the rate. Ask the school for component-level mock marks, ask the IB coordinator what revision the school already runs, and count the weeks you will genuinely have once travel and Ramadan are deducted. Send us those three things and we will quote a named block length against named components, with the lost weeks built in and the cheaper component-block option offered first where the evidence supports it. A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor comes before any commitment, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here work with high-attaining Diploma candidates in Abu Dhabi at the top of the grade range, where the work is criterion-level precision rather than content coverage: marked timed papers, internal assessment feedback against the descriptors, and the specific habits that separate a 7 from a 6.

intro.heading: Six sevens and the core: breaking a single number into seven jobs
paragraphs: A perfect Diploma score is built from six subject grades of 7, giving 42, plus the points available from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay taken together, which brings the maximum to 45. That is the entire structure, and writing it out matters because the framing changes what a candidate does with their year. A student chasing a single number works harder at everything. A student who understands they are chasing seven separate judgements, each assessed against its own published criteria, works on the two that are furthest from target and protects the rest.

That redistribution is the whole value of coaching at this level. A candidate at 41 or 42 predicted is almost never uniformly short. They are typically a 7 in three subjects, a secure 6 in two with a specific identifiable gap, and carrying an Extended Essay that has not been looked at properly since the first draft. Those three problems have nothing in common and each responds to a different kind of work. Treating them as one problem called revision is how a strong candidate finishes where they started.

The second thing worth saying early is that a 45 is not primarily a knowledge target. Candidates at this level know the content. What separates the top band from the one below is precision: command terms answered exactly, method lines written out, evaluation reached rather than implied, uncertainty discussed rather than calculated, an internal assessment that addresses every criterion rather than most of them. These are narrow, nameable behaviours, and that is good news, because narrow things can be fixed inside a term.

There is also a structural point about the Diploma that top candidates learn late. The award of the diploma carries conditions beyond a points total, including minimum totals at higher and standard level, limits on how many low grades a candidate may hold, and a grade E in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay as a failing condition. A candidate chasing 45 is nowhere near those limits, but the existence of the core as a failing condition is the reason the Extended Essay deserves attention in the autumn rather than in the week before submission. Confirm the current conditions with your school's IB coordinator, because they are set by the IB and not by us.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. At the top of the grade range the practical consequence is the pool: a candidate needing someone who can mark HL Chemistry to the published criteria and then discuss an Extended Essay in the same subject is choosing a specialist, not a neighbour. In Abu Dhabi that pool is small on the ground and considerably larger online.

At this level the gap is precision against the criteria rather than missing content

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.programmesIntro: A 45 is a Diploma outcome, but the habits behind it are built across the IB continuum. These are the programmes running in Abu Dhabi schools and what each contributes to a candidate who ends up at the top of the range.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Nothing here is graded on the Diploma scale, but the inquiry habit and the expectation of written justification are where top Diploma candidates usually began. Students who learn early to explain why rather than state what arrive in the Diploma with the one skill that distinguishes the top band in every subject group.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP schools report against the programme's framework rather than against marks, which makes it hard for parents to spot early strength. The useful proxy is whether a child can explain their reasoning aloud, which is a better predictor of Diploma performance than any primary score.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP criteria A to D with their published descriptors are the first place a student meets criterion-referenced assessment, which is exactly how Diploma internal assessment works. A student who learns in MYP 4 to read a descriptor and write to it has a genuine head start on the component that most often costs a Diploma candidate their seventh point.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school runs MYP to Year 11, the eAssessment route gives useful practice in writing to criteria under conditions. Where the school switches to IGCSE at Year 10, the Extended tier provides examination practice instead but less criterion-referenced work, which is worth compensating for in the first Diploma year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme where the number is decided. Three subjects at higher level, three at standard level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. The points come from the six subjects and the core, and a candidate at the top of the range is managing seven assessments rather than six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and for internal assessment are set by each school rather than by the IB, and they vary widely across the emirate, which means a 45 campaign has to be planned against your own school's calendar.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP candidates take DP courses and are graded on them, but the CP is not scored out of 45 and does not carry the diploma points structure. A family arriving at this page while their child is on the CP should be clear on that distinction before setting a target, and should ask the school how their destination universities read the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Abu Dhabi schools offer the CP, and recognition varies by destination. The reflective project has its own internal deadlines, which in practice compete with DP subject assessment in the same weeks.

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.subjectsIntro: At the top of the range, the difference between a 6 and a 7 is specific in every subject. These notes name the behaviour rather than the topic, because content is rarely the limiting factor for a candidate at this level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The seventh point at HL is usually found in Paper 3, where the extended investigation rewards a structured approach that can be learned as a form. Proof questions divide the band: candidates who assert a result where a derivation was required lose marks they had the mathematics to earn.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Top marks turn on interpretation rather than computation. A statistical test run correctly and concluded without reference to the significance level and the context scores below a response that does both, and that difference recurs across every paper in the course.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The 7 is lost in two places: data questions where uncertainty is calculated but neither propagated nor discussed, and extended answers where a correct mechanism is given without the reasoning the mark scheme credits. The internal assessment is the other half, and it is where a careful candidate gains most.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: At the top of the range marks go on long-answer reasoning in fields and circular motion, and on graph questions where a gradient is found and not interpreted. A candidate who writes the physical reasoning line before the algebra rarely loses these marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most command-term sensitive subject in the Diploma. A 7 requires answering evaluate as evaluate and suggest as suggest, every time, under time pressure. Candidates at this level lose the seventh point to precision rather than to knowledge, which makes it among the most recoverable.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Evaluation marks are the band divider, and they are lost by stopping after analysis. Diagram accuracy with fully labelled axes carries marks that strong candidates give away casually. HL quantitative questions reward interpretation of the number rather than the number itself.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The top band requires an argument sustained across a whole response rather than a sequence of accurate observations. Paper 2 rewards genuine comparison rather than two readings in sequence, and the HL essay is frequently the component where a 6 becomes a 7 because it is written under less pressure.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source questions reward provenance used analytically, and essays reward an argument held past the first paragraph. At the top of the range the losses are structural: a strong thesis followed by narrative, or a comparison written as two separate descriptions.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The core carries the points that take 42 to 45 and also carries a failing condition, since a grade E in either prevents the award of the diploma. Both are assessed against published criteria, both are written over months, and both are the components a strong candidate is most likely to leave until they are urgent.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE social studies alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: These subjects are taught alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools and occupy real timetable hours. For a candidate planning a 45 campaign they are fixed load, and a plan that quietly assumes they can be deprioritised has overstated the available week.

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.regionsIntro: A 45 campaign is a time-budget problem as much as an academic one, and in Abu Dhabi the time budget depends on the commute. These notes are about how many usable study and session hours a week actually contains.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: The shortest school runs in the capital and small Diploma cohorts, which means a candidate can finish school, sit a timed paper and still have the evening. For a top-band candidate managing seven assessments, recovered commuting time is the cheapest resource available.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island communities with a high concentration of HL science candidates and manageable travel. Competition for the same tutors peaks here in the autumn, when internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines land together.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with minimal travel, suiting the frequent short sessions that criterion-level work benefits from. The practical constraint is a quiet space for a two-hour timed paper rather than the clock.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A long term-time school run that removes an hour or more from each weekday. Candidates here typically protect two weekday evenings for coursework and put timed papers in a weekend block, which is a workable shape if it is planned in September.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Bandar
regions.note: Close to the main Diploma cluster and generating heavy autumn demand for HL Chemistry, Physics and Mathematics AA. A candidate aiming at the top of the range should book the slot before the Extended Essay deadline rather than after it.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A growing second-year cohort with a slow afternoon commute. Top-band candidates here often split the week between one subject session and one core session, which is the right instinct and only works if both are scheduled.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: An hour inland, with very few HL specialists physically present. A candidate here wanting an HL Chemistry specialist who can also read an Extended Essay in the subject has no local route to it, which is the practical case for live video.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Small second-year cohorts where a candidate at the top of the range may have no local peer group at the same level, and where a single HL class means limited internal comparison. That makes externally marked work more informative rather than less.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi
The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: The largest Diploma population in the emirate and the densest concentration of high-attaining candidates. Internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and internal assessment differ by several weeks across schools in this corridor.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Fewer Diploma schools across a wider geography and the thinnest specialist supply. Candidates here are the most likely to be the strongest in their subject in their school, which is isolating and makes external marked comparison genuinely useful.
schools: Nord Anglia International School Abu Dhabi

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.modesIntro: Three shapes of work for a candidate near the top of the range, distinguished by which of the seven targets is furthest from where it needs to be.

modes.title: Two-subject precision block
modes.description: The commonest shape. Two subjects where a secure 6 needs to become a 7, taught through marked timed work against the published criteria rather than through content coverage. Sessions are short and frequent because the work is habit correction, and each one produces something marked and dated.
bullets: Diagnostic marked paper per subject before anything is planned
Each session targets one named behaviour, not a topic list
Marked timed section every second session to test whether it held
Content teaching only where a marked paper proves a genuine gap

modes.title: Core points block
modes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay taken seriously in the autumn rather than the week before submission. Feedback is given on the student's own draft against the published criteria; the tutor does not write, complete or produce any part of the work. For a candidate at 42 or 43 this is frequently where the remaining points are.
bullets: Feedback mapped to criterion letters and their descriptors
Comments returned on the student's own draft for them to act on
Research question and scope interrogated early, not after the first draft
Dated feedback log kept so authorship of the work is demonstrable

modes.title: Full-profile review, single session
modes.description: One session spent on the whole picture rather than on one subject: current predicted grades, the most recent marked work in each subject, internal assessment and Extended Essay status, and the school's internal deadlines. The output is a written ranking of where the remaining points realistically sit.
bullets: All seven targets reviewed, not just the weakest subject
Written ranking of where points are recoverable and where they are not
Honest statement when a target is out of reach in the time available
No programme attached; families often act on this alone

sections.heading: The arithmetic of 45, written out
paragraphs: Six subjects, each graded 1 to 7, give a maximum of 42. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute the remaining points through the published diploma points matrix, bringing the maximum to 45. A standard Diploma has at least three subjects at higher level and the rest at standard level, and the core also includes creativity, activity and service, which is a requirement rather than a source of points.

Setting it out this way does two useful things. It converts a single intimidating number into a list, and it shows immediately that the core is not a formality: it is the difference between 42 and 45, and it is assessed against its own published criteria, written over months, and entirely within the candidate's control in a way that an examination is not. Candidates who treat the Extended Essay as an obligation to be discharged are leaving points on the table that a subject grade cannot replace.

It also exposes where coaching can and cannot help. A candidate predicted 7 in a subject does not need teaching in it; they need to not lose it. A candidate predicted 6 in two subjects needs precision work in exactly those two. A candidate whose Extended Essay research question is too broad in September has a fixable problem and one that becomes unfixable by February. Reading the profile tells you which of these you have, and almost nobody does that reading before buying hours.

The figures in the table below are the structure of the qualification rather than our interpretation of it. Every one of them should be confirmed against your school's IB coordinator or the IB's own published materials, which is also where the current failing conditions and the points matrix live. This page deliberately does not reproduce IB documents or dates; it points at them.

sections.heading: The core: where the last points sit, and the condition nobody mentions
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are assessed independently, each against published criteria, and their grades are combined to produce the core points that take a 42 to a 45. They are also the two components where a strong candidate is most likely to underperform, for a simple structural reason: both are long-range tasks with internal deadlines set by the school, and both compete for attention with subjects that give feedback weekly.

The Extended Essay is the more recoverable of the two and the more commonly mishandled. Its quality is largely decided by the research question, and a research question that is too broad, not answerable within the word limit, or not genuinely located in the subject will cap the grade regardless of how well the essay is written. That is a September problem with a September solution, and a February problem with no solution. A single session interrogating the question before the first draft is one of the highest-value hours available to a candidate at this level.

Theory of Knowledge rewards a different skill, which is the ability to make a knowledge claim, examine it against perspectives, and do so with reference to specific examples rather than general ones. Strong candidates often write fluently and score below their ability because the essay describes a debate rather than taking a position within it. This is a structural habit and it is correctable with marked practice against the criteria.

There is a condition attached that every 45 candidate should know and many do not: a grade E in either Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the award of the diploma. A candidate on course for straight sevens is nowhere near an E, but the existence of the condition is the strongest available argument for taking both components seriously early. Confirm the current failing conditions with your coordinator, since they are set by the IB.
