sections.heading: What a 7 requires that a 6 does not, by subject group
paragraphs: The jump from 6 to 7 is not more content. In every subject group it is a specific increase in precision, and because it is specific it can be targeted. In Group 4 it is command-term exactness and data discussion: uncertainty propagated and its effect on the conclusion discussed, limitations named with their impact, relationships explained rather than described. In Group 5 it is method presentation and, at HL in Analysis and Approaches, the structure of an extended investigation.

In Groups 1 and 2, the language subjects, the 7 lives in sustained argument. A response that makes a series of accurate points about a text sits below one that holds a single line of reading across the whole answer and uses the points as evidence for it. The difference is planning in the first two minutes, which sounds trivial and is worth a band.

In Group 3 it is judgement. Economics responses that analyse and stop sit below those that evaluate with support. History essays that narrate sit below those that argue and sustain it. Business Management responses that name tools sit below those that apply them to the stimulus and reach a conclusion. Each of these is a structural change rather than a knowledge acquisition, and each is demonstrable in a single marked response.

The practical consequence for a candidate with a term available is that the target should be one named behaviour per subject, demonstrated twice in marked work. That is achievable. Raising general performance across six subjects in a term is not, and any plan that proposes it has not read the profile.

sections.heading: Where a 7 slips to a 6 in the final weeks
paragraphs: Candidates who lose a seventh point in May usually lose it to something they already knew how to avoid. The largest category is time. A paper where the last extended question is attempted in four minutes loses marks that were fully available, and the cause is almost always over-investment earlier in the paper: a strong candidate writing a six-mark answer to a three-mark question because they can. This is a pacing discipline, it is taught with timed practice rather than with content, and it regresses under pressure unless maintained.

The second category is reversion. A habit corrected in February returns in May, because exam conditions strip away deliberation and leave only what is automatic. Method lines stop being written. Command terms stop being read carefully. Graphs get gradients without interpretation. The defence is repetition under timed conditions close to the session rather than a single correction months earlier, which is why a 45 plan should include timed work in the final weeks even when nothing is wrong.

The third is the internal assessment left at good-enough. A candidate with a strong profile often has an internal assessment that would score well and could score full marks, and the gap is usually one criterion handled thinly: an evaluation that lists limitations without impact, or a conclusion that does not connect back to the research question. Those are an hour's work each and they are worth the same as a mark gained in an examination.

The fourth is the Extended Essay submitted without a final read against the criteria. Candidates proofread for expression and not for criteria coverage, which are different activities. Reading a finished essay with the descriptors beside it, criterion by criterion, routinely finds marks in the conclusion and in the engagement with the research question. It takes one session and it happens after the writing is done.

sections.heading: The evidence a candidate at the top of the range should keep
paragraphs: For a 45 campaign the record serves a different purpose than it does for a struggling candidate. It is not there to prove improvement to a teacher; it is there to show the candidate where their own marks are leaking. At this level the leaks are small, consistent and invisible without data, which means the record has to be granular: not a grade per paper, but a count of which error class cost how many marks in each marked piece.

A workable log has four columns: the date, the piece, the error class, and the marks lost to it. Over six weeks the pattern is unambiguous. A candidate who finds that command-term errors cost three marks in one paper, four in the next and three in the one after has a problem worth a session; one who finds a single three-mark loss and nothing since has a one-off. Without the log both look the same, and the second gets treated as the first, which wastes a term.

The internal assessment and Extended Essay feedback belong in the same record, with dates. That serves the diagnostic purpose and a second one: a dated sequence of the student's own drafts with external feedback on each is the clearest demonstration available that the work is theirs. For a high-profile candidate whose work may be scrutinised, that record is worth keeping for its own sake.

What should not be in the record is any projected score. Nobody can convert a set of marked pieces into a predicted total with any reliability, and a tutor who offers a number is offering a guess with a decimal point on it. The log says what has been fixed and what has not. The total is decided in May by examiners, and this page publishes no estimate of it.

sections.heading: What nobody can honestly promise about a 45
paragraphs: No tutor can guarantee a score, a grade, or a points total, and nothing on this page should be read as doing so. Where a guarantee appears in this market it is either unenforceable or hedged by conditions that are not displayed alongside it, and the honest position is to state the limit rather than to hide behind the hedge. What can be offered is specific work on specific weaknesses, with marked evidence of whether the weakness reduced.

This page also carries no statistics, which in a market full of them is a deliberate choice. Competitor pages publish satisfaction percentages, median tutor scores and cohort attainment figures with no sample size, date or method stated, and at least one publishes two contradictory figures on the same page. A number without a method is a liability for whoever publishes it and useless to whoever reads it, so there are none here.

Nor should a page in this market claim examiner access. Describing a tutor as an IB examiner without being able to evidence their current status is a misrepresentation, and implying that examiner status gives access to marking decisions, grade boundaries or paper content is worse. If examiner experience is relevant to a candidate, ask for the evidence and ask what specifically it is supposed to deliver.

The last limit is the one families least want to hear. Some candidates are not going to reach 45, and a reasonable adviser says so. A student predicted 38 in October with two subjects at 5 is not two months from a perfect score, and the useful conversation is about where the achievable points are rather than about the headline number. Selling a 45 campaign to that candidate is selling hours, and it costs them the chance to secure the points actually in reach.

sections.heading: How sessions run, and the week a 45 campaign actually has
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and the candidate's own marked work on screen. Gulf Standard Time lessons are scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school week: earlier on Saadiyat and the island where the school run is short, later in Khalifa City and Al Raha, and weekend blocks where weekday evenings are already committed to coursework. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing without changing the plan.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. At this level the online format is not a compromise but the only way to reach the right specialist: a candidate needs someone who marks HL Chemistry to the published criteria and can also interrogate an Extended Essay research question in the subject, and the chance that such a person lives within a short drive of a particular Abu Dhabi address is low. In-home rates in the emirate are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour because the journey is priced in, and the journey contributes nothing here.

On time budgeting: a Diploma candidate in the UAE also carries Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies lessons alongside the programme, because private schools teach these alongside their licensed international curriculum. Any plan built on the assumption that the week contains more discretionary hours than it does will fail in the fourth week, usually by sacrificing the core components first, which are exactly the ones carrying the last three points.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. One practical caution: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Where no specialist is free for a subject at the hours needed, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral rather than filling the hour.

process.title: Review the whole profile first
process.description: Current predicted grades in all six subjects, the most recent marked work in each, and the status of the internal assessments, Theory of Knowledge essay and Extended Essay. A 45 campaign that starts with the weakest subject rather than with the profile usually targets the wrong thing.

process.title: Rank where the points actually are
process.description: A written ranking of which of the seven targets has recoverable points and which does not, with the reasoning stated. A subject already predicted 7 needs protecting rather than teaching. An Extended Essay with a flawed research question in September is the highest-value item on most lists.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a marked piece
process.description: One free trial lesson with the subject specialist, on the condition that it is a single lesson, spent on the most recent marked paper read against the criteria. The output is a named behaviour to fix and a stated test for whether it has been fixed.

process.title: Short, frequent sessions with marked checks
process.description: Precision work responds to frequency rather than duration. Each session targets one named behaviour, each produces something marked and dated, and a timed section every second session tests whether the correction held under pressure. Content teaching happens only where a marked paper proves a genuine gap.

process.title: Protect the core components
process.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are scheduled in the autumn rather than squeezed in before submission, with feedback given on the student's own draft against the published criteria and logged with dates. We do not write, complete or produce any part of the work.

process.title: Say when the target is not reachable
process.description: If the profile does not support 45 in the time available, we say so and rank the points that are genuinely in reach instead. That conversation is less enjoyable than agreeing with the target and it is the one that leaves a candidate better off in May.

whyPoints.title: The number broken into its parts
whyPoints.description: A 45 is six subject grades of 7 plus the core points, which makes it seven separate judgements rather than one target. Setting that out changes where a candidate spends their term, and it is the single most useful thing this page does. Competitor pages in this market treat the number as a slogan.

whyPoints.title: The core taken seriously in the autumn
whyPoints.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry the points that separate 42 from 45 and a grade E in either is a failing condition. Most candidates leave both until they are urgent. We schedule them early and interrogate the research question before the first draft.

whyPoints.title: Precision, not coverage
whyPoints.description: At the top of the range the gap is command-term exactness, method presentation, evaluation reached rather than implied, and uncertainty discussed with its impact. Those are narrow behaviours, which is why they are fixable in a term. Content revision at this level is mostly wasted effort.

whyPoints.title: No guarantee and no statistics
whyPoints.description: Nobody can guarantee a score and this page does not. There is also no satisfaction percentage, no cohort attainment figure and no median tutor score here, because no dataset supports one and a number without a method is a liability for the publisher.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty as a working limit
whyPoints.description: Feedback is given on the student's own draft against the published criteria and logged with dates. We do not write, complete or produce assessed work, and IB materials are linked to their official sources rather than hosted. One site in this market sells completed internal assessments outright.

whyPoints.title: Honest about who will not reach it
whyPoints.description: A candidate predicted 38 in October with two subjects at 5 is not a 45 candidate, and saying so is more useful than agreeing. The productive version of that conversation ranks the points genuinely in reach, which is usually more than the family expects and in different places.

faqs.question: How is a 45 actually made up in the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Six subject grades of 7 give 42, and the remaining points come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay combined through the published diploma points matrix, for a maximum of 45. A standard Diploma has at least three subjects at higher level, and creativity, activity and service is a completion requirement rather than a source of points. The practical consequence is that a 45 is seven separate judgements, not one, which is why a candidate short of it is usually short in two specific places.

faqs.question: Can coaching realistically take a predicted 42 to a 45?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where the three points sit, and that is a reading exercise before it is a teaching one. If they sit in two subjects at a secure 6 with an identifiable precision gap, and in a core component with an addressable weakness, the work is narrow and plausible. If they sit in three subjects where content is genuinely missing, the time usually is not there. Nobody can guarantee an outcome, and this page does not. The honest first step is a profile review.

faqs.question: How much do Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay contribute?
faqs.answer: Together they provide the points that take 42 to the maximum of 45, awarded on a combination of the two grades through the published diploma points matrix. They also carry a failing condition: a grade E in either prevents the award of the diploma. Confirm the current matrix and the current failing conditions with your school's IB coordinator, since both are set by the IB. The practical point is that the core is not a formality and no subject grade can replace the points it carries.

faqs.question: When should my child start work on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Before the first draft, and ideally while the research question is still being chosen. Essay quality is largely determined by that question: one that is too broad, not answerable within the word limit, or not genuinely located in the subject caps the grade regardless of the writing. That is a problem with a September solution and no February solution. A single session interrogating the question is among the highest-value hours available to a candidate at this level.

faqs.question: What separates a 7 from a 6 in the IB sciences?
faqs.answer: Precision rather than content. At the top of the range, marks go to command-term exactness, to data questions where uncertainty is propagated and its effect on the conclusion discussed, and to extended answers where the reasoning line is written out rather than implied. Limitations named without their impact score below limitations named with it. These are narrow behaviours, which is why they can be corrected inside a term and demonstrated in two marked pieces.

faqs.question: Why do strong candidates lose marks on pacing?
faqs.answer: Because capability itself causes it. A strong candidate writes a six-mark answer to a three-mark question because they can, and then has four minutes for the final extended question where real marks were available. The loss is invisible in a grade and obvious in a script: look at where the writing thins out. The repair is timed full papers rather than content work, and it has to be maintained close to the session because pacing discipline regresses under pressure.

faqs.question: Is it worth reviewing a finished internal assessment that already scores well?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is among the cheapest marks available. A strong internal assessment often has one criterion handled thinly, most often an evaluation that lists limitations without impact or a conclusion that does not reconnect to the research question. Reading the piece criterion by criterion with the descriptors beside it takes about an hour and routinely finds marks. The work must remain the student's own; feedback identifies the gap and the student makes the change.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skills it requires, explain the published criteria, discuss the student's own draft, interrogate the research question, point out an unsupported conclusion, and model technique on a different example. A tutor must not write, complete or produce any part of it, or edit it to a finished state. Feedback here is given against criterion letters and logged with dates, which gives the candidate a record that the work is their own if authorship is questioned. Sites selling finished essays are an integrity breach.

faqs.question: Should a candidate aiming at 45 take tutoring in all six subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and doing so is the commonest way to spend a lot and gain little. A subject already predicted 7 needs protecting with timed practice, not teaching. Effort spent revising a subject where no points are available is effort removed from the two where they are. The useful first purchase is a profile review that ranks where the remaining points realistically sit, and most families find the ranking surprising in both directions.

faqs.question: What does top-band IB coaching cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates for IB specialist tuition run AED 200 to AED 450 an hour and above, per Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, Unitors IB from AED 200 and BartyED AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Qualified subject tutors online sit between AED 150 and AED 300. Those are market figures rather than an IB Gram price list. At this level the hours needed are usually few and specific, so the total matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: How do we know the coaching is working before results arrive?
faqs.answer: By keeping a granular log rather than a general impression. Four columns are enough: the date, the piece, the error class, and the marks lost to it. Over six weeks a real pattern separates itself from a one-off. A candidate losing three or four marks to command terms in every marked piece has something worth a session; one with a single three-mark loss and nothing since does not. No projected total should appear in the log, because nobody can calculate one reliably.

faqs.question: Do you describe your IB tutors as examiners?
faqs.answer: We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners unless current examiner status can be evidenced, and we do not use examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Several sites in this market do both. If examiner experience matters to you, ask for evidence of current status and ask what specifically it is supposed to deliver for your child. What a candidate at this level actually needs is someone who marks accurately against the published criteria and explains the marks.

faqs.question: My child is predicted 38. Is a 45 campaign the right plan?
faqs.answer: Probably not, and the honest conversation is more useful than the encouraging one. A candidate at 38 with two subjects at 5 has points available, but they are in different places from a candidate at 42, and chasing a headline number can cost the points genuinely in reach. The productive version ranks every target by how recoverable it is and spends the term on the top of that list. Families usually find there is more available than they thought, in places they had not considered.

faqs.question: Which session do Abu Dhabi candidates sit, and when do internal deadlines fall?
faqs.answer: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session. Internal deadlines for internal assessment, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay are set by each school rather than by the IB, and they differ by several weeks across the emirate. Ask your coordinator for the full list in the first weeks of the second year. This page publishes no IB exam or results dates, because the IB's own site could not be verified by automated checking for this project.

abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.closingHeading: Read the profile before buying hours
abu-dhabi/ib-score-45-coaching.closingBody: A 45 is six sevens plus the core, which means the first useful hour is spent reading a profile rather than teaching a subject. Look at all six predicted grades, the most recent marked work in each, and the state of the internal assessments, Theory of Knowledge essay and Extended Essay. Rank where the remaining points are genuinely recoverable and where they are not. Then spend the term on the top two or three items on that list, with marked evidence after each session. Book a free trial lesson with a subject specialist to start that reading, and expect an honest answer about what the time available will support.

abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach the subjects rather than sell the choice, which is why they are useful at this stage. A subject teacher can tell you what the Higher Level course actually demands in week thirty, which is a different question from what the option booklet says it covers.

intro.heading: The real price of a wrong Higher Level choice
paragraphs: Subject selection advice is almost always priced as a consultation and almost never priced as what it prevents. That is the wrong way round. A single ninety-minute conversation costs whatever the market charges for ninety minutes. A Higher Level subject that was the wrong choice costs two years of weekly tutoring to keep afloat, and in Abu Dhabi, at published market rates, that number runs from roughly AED 4,800 to well over AED 20,000 before anybody has decided whether it worked.

Here is the arithmetic, because nobody in this market publishes it. A Higher Level subject a student is struggling with typically absorbs a weekly ninety-minute session across both Diploma years, with a heavier block before the final papers. Call it thirty hours in the first year and forty in the second, so seventy hours. Published UAE rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and IB specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450 for specialist exam-year work. Seventy hours at those bands is roughly AED 10,500-21,000 for one subject. At the budget band, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65, it is far less, and for a Higher Level subject the student is already failing at, far less is usually not enough.

Now compare that with the cost of getting the choice examined properly before it is made. Two or three sessions with subject teachers who actually teach those Higher Level courses, looking at the student's own MYP criterion marks or IGCSE component scores against what the course demands, costs a tiny fraction of the figure above. It is the highest-leverage spend available anywhere in the Diploma, and it is also the spend most families skip, because the option booklet arrives in February and the decision feels administrative rather than financial.

What makes this specifically an Abu Dhabi problem is the depth of provision. The emirate has fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, so a given school may offer one option in a subject group rather than three, and the choice a student makes is constrained by the timetable blocks that school runs. A student who wants Physics Higher Level and Economics Higher Level may find they sit in the same block. That is not a mistake anybody made; it is a supply reality, and the useful advice is about which compromise is cheapest to live with rather than which combination is theoretically ideal.

IB Gram delivers subject-selection guidance and the tutoring that follows as one-to-one online sessions on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For this particular decision that is almost irrelevant to the cost and quite relevant to the quality, because the person best placed to tell you what Chemistry Higher Level feels like in week thirty is the person who teaches it, not the person who lives nearest to Khalifa City.

abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.programmesIntro: Subject selection happens at a specific moment in a longer sequence, and the decisions before and after it matter to the cost. Here is where each stage sits.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the subject groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Higher Level courses carry more content, more papers or longer ones, and a higher workload across both years. The Diploma total runs to 45, with up to three bonus points from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. The structure means the selection decision is really six decisions plus a decision about which three are Higher.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools run the Diploma within their own timetable blocks, and a smaller cohort means fewer parallel options in each subject group. Ask which combinations the school can actually timetable before building a plan around a theoretical ideal, because the answer narrows the real choice set considerably and it is better to know in February than in September.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria on an eight-point scale, with the Personal Project in the final year. The criterion marks are the best single predictor available of whether a student will cope at Higher Level, and they are more informative than a report comment because they separate out what the student can actually do from how hard they tried.
programmes.countryNote: For an Abu Dhabi family choosing Diploma subjects out of MYP, the criterion profile is the document to bring. A student at 6 or 7 on the analytical criteria in a subject is a different proposition from one at 4, and the gap between those two in a Higher Level course is where most of the later tutoring spend goes.

programmes.name: IGCSE entry route
programmes.description: Many Abu Dhabi students arrive at the Diploma from IGCSE rather than MYP, which gives a cleaner signal: component-level marks on external papers. An Extended-tier grade in Mathematics or a strong Physics 0625 performance tells you something specific about readiness for the corresponding Higher Level course.
programmes.countryNote: Where a student has IGCSE component marks, use them rather than the overall grade. A student with a strong grade built on a strong multiple-choice paper and a weak extended-response paper is a risk at Higher Level in that subject, and it is cheap to spot now and expensive to discover in Year 13.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A narrower framework combining at least two DP courses with a career-related study, Personal and Professional Skills, service learning and a reflective project. The DP courses are taken as individual certificates and graded 1 to 7 in the same way as Diploma subjects.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision is thinner in Abu Dhabi than full Diploma provision, but it belongs in a selection conversation, because for some students two or three strong DP certificates plus a career study is a better outcome than six subjects half-carried. Raising it is not a downgrade; forcing a full Diploma that needs propping up for two years is the more expensive path.

abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.subjectsIntro: What follows is what each Higher Level course actually demands, not what the option booklet says it covers. This is the information that makes a selection decision cheaper later.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest-stakes choice in the list. Higher Level demands algebraic fluency without a calculator on Paper 1 and the ability to follow an unfamiliar extended argument on Paper 3. A student who needed support for IGCSE Extended algebra will need support for two years here, and that is the single largest tutoring cost in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-permitted throughout, modelling-led, and genuinely different rather than easier. The demand is verbal: interpreting a model and commenting on limitations in language the mark scheme rewards. It suits strong writers who find abstract algebra punishing, and it is accepted by many but not all university courses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level adds substantial content in organic chemistry and energetics, and the calculation load is multi-step, so one early error propagates. Commonly chosen for medicine and engineering pathways and commonly the subject propped up for two years when the choice was made on ambition rather than on prior performance.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mathematical demand is the hidden cost: Physics Higher Level alongside Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level is a combination that works for some students and strains badly for others. Fields and quantum arrive late and are consistently where the marks go.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Lower mathematical demand and the largest content volume in the Diploma sciences. The cost here is time rather than difficulty, which makes it a poor partner for two other content-heavy Higher Levels and a reasonable one alongside a mathematical subject.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds Paper 3, the quantitative paper, which surprises students who chose Economics to avoid mathematics. A strong essay writer with weak numeracy will need support for that paper specifically, which is a narrow and therefore cheap intervention if anticipated.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Framework application against stimulus material is the skill. Students who can describe and not apply cap out in the middle bands. Lighter in content than Economics Higher Level and a common alternative where the quantitative paper is the concern.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Higher Level adds an essay component and more demanding analysis of unseen texts. For a student who arrived in English-medium education recently, this is the subject where the Higher Level decision has the largest effect on the whole week's workload.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.levels: HL and SL, plus ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic A is for students working in Arabic as a language of instruction and literature; Arabic B is language acquisition. Placing a student in the wrong one is a common and costly selection error in this emirate, and the bilingual Diploma possibility makes the choice worth examining properly.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth study and an additional paper, with a heavy reading and writing load. It pairs badly with two other essay-based Higher Levels for most students, because the weekly writing volume becomes the constraint rather than the content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Popular, accessible at Standard Level, and more demanding at Higher Level than its reputation suggests because of the extension content and the evaluative writing. Rarely a university prerequisite, so worth checking against the intended course before choosing it at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The workload is continuous rather than concentrated before exams, which changes the shape of the whole two years. Choosing it at Higher Level alongside two content-heavy sciences is a timetable decision as much as an academic one, and it is routinely underestimated.

abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.regionsIntro: School provision differs across the emirate, and so does the set of combinations actually available. These are the catchments families choose from.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island
regions.note: The widest range of established Diploma provision in the emirate, so the broadest set of timetable blocks and the fewest forced compromises between Higher Level subjects in different groups.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities feeding schools with mid-sized Diploma cohorts. Option blocks here are real constraints, and families regularly discover a desired Higher Level pairing cannot be timetabled.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Short commutes to island schools, so students here often have a genuine choice between two or three Diploma providers, which is itself a selection variable worth using.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Small cohorts and high fees, with subject groups sometimes offering a single option. A minority Higher Level subject may simply not run in a given year, which has to be checked before planning around it.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools still building out their Diploma offer. Ask which Higher Level courses have actually run for two consecutive years, because a course listed in a booklet is not the same as a course with a track record.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Mainland communities with a strong Indian and Arab resident mix, so Arabic A against Arabic B placement and Hindi or other language options come up more often here than elsewhere.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Ninety minutes inland with a small set of international schools, the narrowest option set in the emirate, and almost no local Higher Level specialists to prop up a difficult choice afterwards.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established central districts where a high share of students hold UK or UAE university ambitions, which makes prerequisite checking the dominant part of the selection conversation.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi Island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Longest-established international provision in the emirate, with the most mature option blocks and the most predictable Higher Level availability year to year. Named only as context for the local education landscape.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland
schoolClusters.note: Larger cohorts spread across more schools, with broader subject-group coverage overall but tighter blocking within each school. Listed as ecosystem context only.

schoolClusters.city: Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A separate catchment under the same regulator with the narrowest Diploma option set in the emirate, where the available combination usually decides the choice. Context only.

sections.heading: What a wrong Higher Level choice costs, in AED
paragraphs: A wrong Higher Level subject is paid for in tutoring hours over two years, and nobody in this market publishes that number, so here it is. A Higher Level course a student cannot carry unaided absorbs roughly seventy hours of support across the Diploma: a weekly session through the first year, a weekly session through most of the second, and a heavier block before the papers. At the published UAE qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour that is roughly AED 10,500-21,000. At specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above it runs higher again.

Compare that with the alternative cost structure, which is where the argument lands. Three sessions before the decision is made, one on the criterion or component evidence and two as subject-teacher tasters in the courses actually in question, is four and a half hours. At the same bands that is roughly AED 675-2,025. The ratio is not marginal. It is the difference between a four-figure precaution and a five-figure consequence, and the precaution also produces a better decision rather than merely a cheaper one.

The table below sets out the common selection errors with the hours each typically generates. It is built from what families in this emirate actually come to us with, and it is ordered by cost rather than by frequency. Note the cheapest row: choosing a subject the school can only timetable against another required subject is a scheduling error that costs nothing to detect and a whole option to fix once term has started.

One honest qualification. Some stretch choices are worth making. A student who wants Chemistry Higher Level for a medical pathway and sits a little below the comfortable threshold may be better served by making the choice and funding the support than by taking the safe option and closing the pathway. That is a legitimate decision and we will help cost it. What is not legitimate is making it without knowing the number, which is what happens when selection advice is delivered as encouragement.

sections.heading: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the one selection decision with consequences beyond the Diploma, because university courses state which route they require and the two courses are not interchangeable. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic, proof-oriented route with a no-calculator Paper 1. Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led with technology permitted throughout and a heavier interpretive and statistical emphasis. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, so there are four possible answers rather than two.

What students get wrong is treating Applications and Interpretation as the easier option. It is not easier; it is differently hard. The marks there are lost in words rather than in algebra: choosing a model and failing to justify it, running a statistical test correctly and then describing the result in language that earns nothing. A strong writer with weak algebraic instinct often does better on that route, and a strong algebraist who writes reluctantly often does worse. That is a question about the student, not about the subject's difficulty.

The prerequisite side has to be checked institution by institution and course by course, against what each one publishes. Engineering, mathematics, physics, economics at some institutions, and several medical pathways commonly specify the analysis route or a particular level. Other courses accept either. Requirements change between admissions cycles, so anything read today needs rechecking before an application goes in, and no tutoring page, including this one, should be the source of record for a university's requirements.

A practical sequence that works. Get the student's actual algebraic performance on paper, from IGCSE component marks or MYP criterion scores rather than from a teacher's impression. Book one taster session on genuine Analysis and Approaches Higher Level material, not an introductory sample. Check the published requirements for the two or three most likely degree directions. Then decide, knowing that a borderline case can be made defensible with a short summer bridging block rather than two years of weekly support.

sections.heading: The evidence to bring to a selection conversation
paragraphs: A selection conversation held without documents is a conversation about hopes. The documents that make it useful are specific, and all of them exist already, which is why this stage is cheap. From an MYP student: the criterion-level marks for each subject, separated rather than averaged, with the analytical criteria read especially closely. From an IGCSE student: component-level marks, not overall grades, plus the tier each subject was taken at.

Why component level rather than grade. A student can reach a strong IGCSE Mathematics grade on the strength of the questions they always get right while the extended, multi-step questions at the end of the paper remain unattempted. That grade and a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches course are a poor fit, and the overall grade conceals exactly the information that would have told you. The same applies in the sciences, where a strong multiple-choice performance and a weak extended-response performance average into a reassuring number.

The third document is the school's option block structure, which decides what is actually possible. Ask for it in February, in writing, and ask which Higher Level courses have run for two consecutive years, because a course in the booklet is not a course with a teacher and a cohort. In a smaller Abu Dhabi school a Higher Level option may run only if enough students choose it, which means the final answer depends on other families' decisions and is not knowable in advance.

The fourth is a short written list of likely degree directions, even if vague. Three plausible directions is enough to run a prerequisite check that catches the one error with permanent consequences, which is the Mathematics route. Everything else in a Diploma selection can be mitigated with support; a closed prerequisite usually cannot, and discovering it in Year 13 is the one outcome that no amount of tutoring buys back.

sections.heading: Switch windows, and what changing a subject actually costs
paragraphs: Every Diploma school allows some movement early in Year 12 and then stops allowing it, and the date it stops is set by the school and the registration calendar rather than by anything a tutoring site can tell you. Ask your IB coordinator two questions in writing: until when can a subject be changed, and until when can a level be changed between Higher and Standard. Those are different deadlines in most schools, and the second is usually later than the first.

A level change from Higher to Standard in the same subject is the cheapest correction available. The content overlaps heavily, the student keeps the teacher and the class in many schools, and the catch-up is small. A subject change in the first weeks of Year 12 is more expensive, because the student joins a class several weeks in and has to close that gap, usually with eight to fifteen hours of support. A subject change after the first term is rarely permitted and, where it is, generates a genuine content debt.

What makes this an Abu Dhabi-specific conversation is the timetable again. In a school with a single option in a subject group, dropping a Higher Level subject may not leave a viable alternative in the same block, so the change cascades into a second change. That is worth modelling before a switch request goes in, and the person who can model it is the coordinator, not a tutor. We can tell you what the catch-up will cost in hours once the change is defined.

The honest framing for parents weighing this. A switch made in week three costs a dozen hours and some discomfort. A wrong choice carried to the end costs seventy hours and a grade. Families delay the decision because switching feels like an admission of error, and the delay is the expensive part. If a Higher Level subject is clearly not working by the fourth week, the evidence will already be visible in the marked work, and acting on it then is the cheapest version of every option available.

sections.heading: The hidden workload: TOK, the Extended Essay and CAS
paragraphs: Selection conversations concentrate on the six subjects and then the week turns out to contain more than six subjects. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS all run alongside, and together the first two feed up to three bonus points through a published matrix. A combination that looks balanced across six subjects can be unmanageable once the Extended Essay drafting period collides with two Higher Level internal assessments in the same term.

So count the writing. Three essay-based Higher Level subjects plus an Extended Essay in a written discipline produces a term in the second year where four substantial pieces of extended writing are live simultaneously, and that is where students who chose well on paper come apart. The fix at selection time is not to avoid essay subjects; it is to notice the pile-up and to place the Extended Essay in a subject that is not already one of the three heaviest.

The internal assessments deserve their own count. Each subject has an internally assessed component with its own deadlines, and in most schools those deadlines cluster, because the school is working backwards from the same submission dates for everybody. Six internal assessments with overlapping school deadlines is the real workload of the second year, and a selection decision that creates six high-effort internal assessments rather than a mix is a decision that will be paid for in the spring.

One boundary to state while on this subject, because families ask at selection stage. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, discuss whether a research question is answerable within the word limit, read a draft the student has written and give feedback on structure, argument and evidence, teach referencing, and mark practice work. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text, rewrite a paragraph to its final form, choose the research question outright or generate data. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student, and there are providers in this market selling completed Internal Assessments, which is an expulsion risk sold at a price.
bullets: Up to three bonus points come from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix
Count the extended-writing pieces live in the same term, not just the subjects
Place the Extended Essay outside the three heaviest subjects where possible

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and what the regulator requires alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma selection conversation in the UAE is not only about the six subjects, because some subjects are not optional. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's published mandatory-subject requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. ADEK applies the equivalent requirement in Abu Dhabi.

For selection purposes this means the real week contains more than the Diploma. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. Those are hours in the timetable that compete directly with the three Higher Level subjects a family is deliberating over, and leaving them out of the workload calculation is how a balanced-looking choice becomes an overloaded one.

The language placement question is distinct and specifically expensive to get wrong. Arabic A is for students working with Arabic as a language of instruction and literature; Arabic B is language acquisition, with an ab initio route for beginners. Placing a student too high produces two years of struggle in a subject that should have been a strength; placing them too low can affect the bilingual Diploma possibility. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

One constraint on tutoring in these subjects that parents should know before buying any. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support here works from the school's own materials and the official programme rather than from an alternative course a tutor prefers. KHDA also requires schools to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE or IB approval or accreditation of any kind and claims none.

sections.heading: Checking university requirements without promising an outcome
paragraphs: The one irreversible part of a selection decision is a prerequisite. Support can mitigate a hard subject; it cannot create a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches grade for a student who was never entered for the course. So a prerequisite audit is worth one session, and the method matters more than the conclusions, because the conclusions expire.

The method is to work only from what each institution publishes about each specific course, and to record where and when it was read. Requirements differ between courses at the same institution, change between admissions cycles, and are sometimes stated as preferences rather than conditions, which is a distinction worth reading carefully. Anything a tutoring site tells you about a university's requirements, including anything on this page, should be treated as a prompt to check the source rather than as the source.

For UAE universities and for Ministry of Education equivalency there is an additional layer, and the honest position includes an admission of ignorance. The published equivalency requirements for the British track are specific: five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. For the American track, English is met by IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61, or 450 in SAT reading and writing, with at least 450 in SAT Math. For the IB, the source that documents those tracks states no points threshold, so no IB equivalency figure appears on this page. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly.

Two things we will not do. We will not present equivalency or attestation as processes IB Gram performs or guarantees, because they are completed with the authority and we are not an intermediary in them. And we will not imply that tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or school progression, because that is a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process. What a selection audit does is make sure the combination chosen does not close a door; it does not open one.

sections.heading: What a selection session should actually produce
paragraphs: The output of useful selection guidance is a short document, not a feeling. It should name the proposed six subjects and levels, the option block each sits in, the risk attached to each Higher Level choice stated in plain terms, the prerequisite position for the two or three likely degree directions, and the switch deadlines the school has confirmed. One page. If a provider's output is encouragement rather than that, you have bought a conversation.

The risk statement is the part worth paying for and the part most often missing. A risk statement reads like this: Chemistry Higher Level is a stretch on the current evidence, because the extended-calculation components at IGCSE were the weakest part of a good overall grade; it is defensible with a six-session summer bridging block on multi-step calculation, and if it is still not working by week four of Year 12 the level change to Standard should be taken rather than deferred. That is actionable. A statement that the student has strong potential in the sciences is not.

The second thing it should contain is a cost line for each stretch choice. If the family is choosing one subject above the comfortable threshold, the plan should say roughly how many support hours a year that implies and what that costs at market rates, so the decision is made with the number visible. Most families, shown the number, either commit properly or choose differently, and both of those are better than discovering it in instalments.

Finally it should say what is not knowable. Whether a Higher Level option will run depends on other families' choices. Whether a university's requirements hold depends on the admissions cycle. Whether a student's maturity closes a gap in six months is a genuine unknown. A selection document that admits those three things is more useful than one that does not, and it is also the only honest version, because nobody in this business can promise a grade, a score or an admission, and we do not.

process.title: Gather four documents
process.description: MYP criterion marks or IGCSE component marks with tiers, the school's option blocks in writing, a list of which Higher Level courses have run for two consecutive years, and three plausible degree directions. All four already exist, which is why this stage is cheap.

process.title: One evidence session
process.description: Ninety minutes reading that evidence against the specific courses under consideration. The output is a ranked shortlist with the risk on each Higher Level choice named in plain terms, not a recommendation delivered as certainty.

process.title: Taster the risky choice
process.description: One session with a teacher of the actual Higher Level course, on genuine Higher Level material rather than an introductory sample. This is the cheapest insurance available in the Diploma and the only way to learn what the course feels like.

process.title: Audit the prerequisites
process.description: A session checking the published entry requirements for the likely degree directions, with the Mathematics route checked first because it is the one error that cannot be mitigated later. Everything read is dated and attributed to the institution's own page.

process.title: Bridge, or change
process.description: Where a stretch choice is worth making, a four to eight session summer block closes the named gap so Year 12 starts level. Where it is not, the change happens before term rather than in week six, which is the difference between a dozen hours and seventy.

process.title: Review at week four
process.description: Four weeks into Year 12 the marked work already shows whether a Higher Level choice is working. We look at it with you and say plainly whether to continue, bridge, or take the level change while the school's window is still open.

whyPoints.title: The mistake is priced, not just described
whyPoints.description: A wrong Higher Level choice costs roughly seventy support hours over two years, which at published UAE rates is a five-figure AED sum. No competitor page researched for this project publishes that arithmetic, and it is the only number that makes the decision feel like what it is.

whyPoints.title: Subject teachers, not advisers
whyPoints.description: The person who can tell you what Chemistry Higher Level feels like in week thirty is someone who teaches it. A taster session on genuine Higher Level material is worth more than any amount of discussion about a student's potential.

whyPoints.title: Component evidence over grades
whyPoints.description: A strong overall IGCSE grade can hide exactly the weakness that makes a Higher Level course unaffordable. We work from component marks and MYP criterion profiles, separated rather than averaged, because that is where the signal is.

whyPoints.title: Switch deadlines surfaced early
whyPoints.description: Subject-change and level-change deadlines are different dates and both are set by your school. Getting them in writing in February is what turns a week-four problem into a twelve-hour fix rather than a seventy-hour one.

whyPoints.title: Prerequisites checked at source
whyPoints.description: We work only from what each institution publishes about each specific course, with the date recorded, and we say plainly that requirements change. Nothing about admissions is promised, because nothing about admissions can be.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what is unknowable
whyPoints.description: Whether an option runs depends on other families. Whether a gap closes depends on the student. We put those unknowns in writing rather than smoothing them over, and we publish no guarantee of any grade, score or admission anywhere.

faqs.question: How much should IB subject selection guidance in Abu Dhabi cost?
faqs.answer: Price it as a small number of sessions, not as a package. One evidence session plus one or two subject-teacher tasters is three to four and a half hours, which at the published UAE qualified-tutor band of AED 150-300 an hour is roughly AED 450-1,350, and more at specialist rates. Set that against the cost of a wrong Higher Level choice, which absorbs around seventy support hours across two years and runs into five figures in AED at the same bands. Any provider quoting a long programme for a selection decision is selling the wrong shape of thing.

faqs.question: What actually happens if we choose the wrong Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: The subject becomes a standing cost. A Higher Level course a student cannot carry unaided typically absorbs a weekly session across both Diploma years plus a heavier block before the papers, roughly seventy hours. At published UAE rates of AED 150-450 an hour that is a five-figure AED commitment for one subject, and the grade is still uncertain at the end. The alternative is a level change to Standard, which is cheap if taken in the first weeks of Year 12 and progressively less available after that, which is why the switch deadlines matter so much.

faqs.question: Which maths route should my child take for engineering or medicine?
faqs.answer: Check each specific course at each specific institution, because requirements differ between courses at the same university and change between admissions cycles. Many engineering, mathematics and physics courses specify Analysis and Approaches or a particular level; some medical pathways specify particular sciences at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is accepted for many quantitative courses and not for all. Read the institution's own published requirement, record the date you read it, and recheck before applying. No tutoring site should be your source of record for a university requirement, including this one.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation easier than Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: No, it is differently hard, and treating it as the soft option is the commonest error in this decision. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented with a no-calculator paper, so the marks go on algebraic slips. Applications and Interpretation permits technology throughout, so the marks go on modelling choices and on interpretation written without precision. A strong writer with weak algebraic instinct is usually better on the applications route; a strong algebraist who writes reluctantly is usually worse. The right question is about your child, not about which course is harder.

faqs.question: What documents should we bring to a subject selection session?
faqs.answer: Four, and all of them already exist. MYP criterion marks separated by criterion rather than averaged, or IGCSE component marks with the tier each subject was taken at. The school's option block structure in writing. A list of which Higher Level courses have actually run for two consecutive years at that school. And three plausible degree directions, however loosely held. With those four, a single session produces a usable shortlist. Without them, the conversation is about hopes, which is pleasant and changes nothing about what the next two years cost.

faqs.question: Why do you want component marks rather than my child's IGCSE grades?
faqs.answer: Because a grade averages away the thing you need to see. A student can reach a strong Mathematics grade on the questions they always get right while the extended multi-step questions at the end of the paper go unattempted, and that profile predicts trouble at Higher Level that the grade conceals entirely. The same applies in the sciences, where a strong multiple-choice performance and a weak extended-response performance average into a reassuring figure. Component marks show which kind of question the student can actually do, which is what a Higher Level course will ask for repeatedly.

faqs.question: Can my child change a Diploma subject after Year 12 has started?
faqs.answer: Usually yes in the first weeks, and the window is set by your school and the registration calendar rather than by anything a tutoring site can tell you. Ask your IB coordinator in writing for two dates: the last date a subject can be changed, and the last date a level can be changed between Higher and Standard. Those are normally different, with the level change available later. A change in weeks one to four typically needs eight to fifteen hours of catch-up support. A change after the first term is rarely permitted and generates a real content debt.

faqs.question: Is dropping from Higher Level to Standard Level a failure?
faqs.answer: It is a correction, and taken early it is the cheapest one available. The content overlaps substantially, the student often keeps the same teacher and class, and the catch-up is small. The expensive version is deferring the decision because the change feels like an admission, carrying the subject for eighteen months and paying for weekly support throughout. If the marked work in week four already shows the course is not landing, the evidence is there to act on, and acting then costs a fraction of acting in Year 13.

faqs.question: Can a Higher Level subject we want simply not be available at our school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common constraint in this emirate rather than an unusual one. Abu Dhabi has fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, so a school may run one option in a subject group rather than three, and two desired Higher Level subjects can sit in the same timetable block. Whether a minority option runs at all sometimes depends on how many students choose it, which means the answer depends on other families and is not knowable in February. Ask for the option blocks and for which courses have run two years running.

faqs.question: How do we balance three Higher Level subjects without overloading the week?
faqs.answer: Count the extended writing rather than the subjects. Three essay-based Higher Levels plus an Extended Essay in a written discipline creates a term in the second year with four substantial pieces live at once, and that is where well-chosen combinations come apart. Count the internal assessments too: six subjects means six internally assessed components with school deadlines that tend to cluster, because the school works backwards from the same submission dates for everyone. A mix of effort shapes is more manageable than six high-effort components, however balanced the subjects look.

faqs.question: Where does Arabic fit into a Diploma subject choice in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: In two places, and they are different. Arabic can be a Diploma subject, as Arabic A for students working in Arabic as a language of instruction and literature or Arabic B for language acquisition with an ab initio route for beginners, and placement in the wrong one is a costly error in this emirate. Separately, Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools alongside the licensed curriculum, so they occupy timetable hours that compete with the Diploma. Both belong in a workload calculation, and most selection conversations include neither.

faqs.question: Does the school's option booklet tell us everything we need?
faqs.answer: It tells you what is offered, not what is deliverable or what each course demands. Three things it usually omits: which Higher Level courses have actually run for two consecutive years, which combinations are impossible because of timetable blocking, and what the Higher Level course asks for in week thirty rather than in week one. The first two come from the coordinator if you ask in writing in February. The third comes from a session with someone who teaches the course, on genuine Higher Level material rather than an introductory sample.

faqs.question: Should we consider the Career-related Programme instead of the full Diploma?
faqs.answer: It belongs in the conversation, and raising it is not a downgrade. The Career-related Programme combines at least two DP courses, taken as individual certificates and graded 1 to 7 exactly as Diploma subjects are, with a career-related study, Personal and Professional Skills, service learning and a reflective project. For some students, two or three strong certificates plus a career study is a better outcome than six subjects carried with weekly support for two years. Provision is thinner in Abu Dhabi than full Diploma provision, so check availability before planning around it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the Extended Essay topic at selection stage?
faqs.answer: A tutor can discuss whether a proposed research question is answerable within the word limit and teach what the assessment criteria reward, which is genuinely useful at this stage because it influences which subject the essay should sit in. A tutor may not choose the question outright, write any part of the essay, supply text to insert or rewrite a paragraph into its final form. A breach is a malpractice finding against the student. The practical selection-stage advice is to place the Extended Essay in a subject that is not already one of the three heaviest.

faqs.question: Can you tell us which combination will get my child into a particular university?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody can. What is possible is to check the published entry requirements for specific courses at specific institutions, record where and when they were read, and make sure the chosen combination does not close a door. That is a real service with a real limit. Requirements change between admissions cycles, institutions distinguish between conditions and preferences, and admissions decisions involve far more than subject choice. No part of IB Gram's offer includes a guarantee of any grade, score, admission or equivalency outcome, and nobody honest in this market offers one.

faqs.question: Is a summer bridging block worth paying for before Year 12?
faqs.answer: It is, where a specific gap has been identified and the stretch choice is worth making anyway. Four to eight sessions on a named weakness, usually algebraic fluency or extended writing, lets a borderline Higher Level choice start level rather than behind. At published UAE rates that is a modest cost against the roughly seventy hours a struggling Higher Level subject absorbs over two years. What makes it worth it is the diagnosis: a bridging block aimed at a vague sense of weakness is just early tutoring, and the taster session is what turns it into something targeted.

abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.closingHeading: Cost the choice before you make it
abu-dhabi/ib-subject-selection-guidance.closingBody: If you are weighing IB subject selection guidance in Abu Dhabi, the useful sequence is cheap and takes a fortnight. Collect the component or criterion marks, ask the coordinator in writing for the option blocks and both switch deadlines, and write down three plausible degree directions. Then book one evidence session and one taster on the Higher Level course you are least sure about, on real Higher Level material. We will give you a one-page output naming each risk, the prerequisite position and the hours a stretch choice implies at market rates. A free trial lesson comes first, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-tok-essay-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below support Theory of Knowledge for Abu Dhabi Diploma students on live video. They work from the prescribed titles themselves, name the area of knowledge every claim depends on, and comment in the margin of the student's own document rather than producing argument for them.

intro.heading: A TOK essay is an argument about knowledge, not an opinion about a topic
paragraphs: The characteristic weak TOK essay from an Abu Dhabi school is fluent, sincere, full of interesting examples and almost entirely about the wrong thing. It discusses the topic the prescribed title mentions — certainty, evidence, bias, technology — rather than discussing how knowledge in a named area of knowledge is actually produced and justified. That distinction is the whole subject, and a student who has not grasped it can write 1,600 competent words and score in the lower bands while believing the essay was good.

The component is specific. The IB releases six prescribed titles for each session, a student selects one, and the essay is a 1,600-word response assessed externally against a single instrument. The titles are knowledge questions: they ask something about the nature, production or limits of knowledge, usually framed with a reference to areas of knowledge. A response that treats the title as a prompt for a general discussion has not answered it, however much it has to say.

What a strong essay does is narrow and specific. It takes a claim, anchors it in a named area of knowledge — history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics or the arts — and tests it against a real example from that area. Then it does the same with a counterclaim, in the same area or a contrasting one, and reaches a position. Two areas of knowledge handled properly beat five mentioned, and one well-chosen real example beats three invented hypotheticals. That hierarchy is counter-intuitive to a student who has been told the course rewards range, and it is the first thing a marked essay demonstrates. Depth inside an area is what the assessment requirements ask for, and breadth of reference across areas is what weak essays substitute for it.

The second thing students misjudge is scale. At 1,600 words there is room for an introduction, two developed arguments with counterclaims, and a conclusion that actually concludes. There is no room for a paragraph defining knowledge, a history of epistemology, or a survey of five areas of knowledge. Students who write those paragraphs are not padding; they genuinely believe the essay requires them, and they lose the space the argument needed.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For Theory of Knowledge the format is well suited: the prescribed title sits on screen beside the student's own paragraph, comments go in the margin as questions, and every version is saved and dated. A family in Khalifa City or on Al Reem Island works with someone who has read the titles rather than with whoever teaches essay writing nearby.
