sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a TOK tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The exhibition commentary must be the student's own work, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice with consequences that reach the whole Diploma. This is not a disclaimer at the bottom of a page. It is the operating rule of the sessions, and it is also the reason some of what parents see advertised in this market should be avoided outright: there are providers in the Gulf selling completed internal assessments, and a student who buys one is risking their Diploma, not improving it.

What a tutor may do is substantial. A tutor may teach the rubric, interrogate a prompt choice, question whether an object has a real context, read a draft and say which sentences justify inclusion and which merely describe, point out that a paragraph is 280 words of description, model the justification move on an object the student is not using, and check images, citations and word count. A tutor may mark a draft against the rubric and explain the band.

What a tutor may not do is produce the work. No sentence of the commentary is written for the student. No paragraph is rewritten into a better version for them to paste. No object is chosen on their behalf. The distinction holds even when a deadline is two days away and the draft is weak, which is precisely when families are most tempted and when we are most explicit about it. If the honest answer is that the draft needs the student to spend four hours rewriting, that is the answer we give.

A practical safeguard: your child's school will ask them to confirm the work is their own, and many Abu Dhabi schools now require drafts to be retained. Keep the dated drafts. A student who can show the progression from a shortlist to a marked draft to a final commentary has the best possible evidence of authorship, and that record is worth building deliberately rather than reconstructing under pressure.
bullets: A tutor teaches the rubric, questions the argument and marks the draft
A tutor does not produce, rewrite or complete any part of the assessed commentary
Keep dated drafts as your own evidence of authorship
Avoid any provider offering finished internal assessments at any price

sections.heading: The DP1 calendar counted backwards, including Ramadan
paragraphs: Exhibition deadlines are set by the school, not by the IB, so there is no published date to work back from. What is predictable is the shape of the Abu Dhabi DP1 year, and that shape is what we plan against. The exhibition usually lands in the second or third term, in the same window as the first subject internal assessment drafts, which is why a student who starts in the deadline fortnight is competing with their own Chemistry IA for attention.

The sensible order of operations is to work backwards from the school's internal deadline in four steps: objects collected three to four weeks out, prompt fixed three weeks out, full draft two weeks out, revision and administrative checks in the final week. Four sessions map onto those four points. Anything compressed tighter than that produces a commentary written once and submitted, which is the version that sits in the middle bands.

Ramadan shifts the whole evening timetable in Abu Dhabi. School days shorten, and families reorganise around iftar, which in practice means a 5pm session becomes impossible and a post-iftar slot becomes the only workable one. We plan for that explicitly, moving sessions later rather than pausing them, because a DP1 student who stops work for a month during a term that contains both the exhibition and IA drafting pays for it in April. Students sitting Cambridge or Pearson qualifications alongside should note that UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and that the Cambridge February and March series is offered in India only.

For families arriving mid-year, which happens constantly in this emirate, the first session covers one extra question: what did your previous school teach as its optional theme? A student who covered knowledge and technology for a term and lands in a class doing knowledge and politics has a prompt-choice problem that is solvable in a session and expensive if it is discovered in the draft.
bullets: Objects collected three to four weeks before the school's internal deadline
Prompt fixed before the first paragraph is written, not after
Full draft two weeks out, leaving a week for revision and the submission checklist
Ramadan sessions moved to post-iftar timing rather than paused

process.title: Tell us the deadline and the prompt shortlist
process.description: One message with three things: your child's school, the date their TOK teacher wants the commentary, and whether a prompt has been chosen. That is enough for us to say how many sessions the task needs and whether a specialist is free in that window.

process.title: Take the free trial with the object list open
process.description: The first lesson is free and we use it on real work rather than introductions. The student brings eight candidate objects and whatever draft exists. By the end they have a tested prompt choice and a specific next task to do before session two.

process.title: Write between sessions, in 300-word blocks
process.description: The student drafts one object paragraph between each session. The tutor marks it against the rubric before the next slot, so the session is spent on the argument rather than on reading. This rhythm is why four sessions is usually enough.

process.title: Final pass on the submission checklist
process.description: Word count under 950, three images, the prompt reproduced exactly as published, citations in the school's style, and the school's own declaration completed. These are marks available for administration rather than thinking, and they are routinely lost.

process.title: Decide whether to continue into the essay
process.description: Some families stop here, which is a reasonable outcome. Others continue into DP2 for prescribed-title work once the six titles are released. We say plainly which we think applies, including when the honest answer is that no further sessions are needed.

whyPoints.title: The rubric, not a general essay method
whyPoints.description: TOK exhibition marking is holistic and specific. A tutor who coaches general essay writing will improve the prose and leave the band unchanged. Our sessions work from the rubric wording your child's school uses and from the justification move the rubric actually rewards.

whyPoints.title: A specialist rather than whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: There are few TOK specialists in Abu Dhabi and fewer still in Al Ain. Online delivery means your child works with someone who has taken students through this task repeatedly, rather than with the nearest available tutor whose main subject is something else.

whyPoints.title: Short blocks, honestly scoped
whyPoints.description: The exhibition is a 950-word task. We scope it at three to five sessions and say so, rather than selling a term of weekly lessons for a component that does not need one. If the draft is already in the upper bands we will tell you that too.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated and practised
whyPoints.description: The commentary is the student's own work. We teach, question and mark; we do not draft. That line holds in the final week before a deadline, which is the only time it is ever tested.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the Abu Dhabi evening
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the school day and the school run, with post-iftar slots during Ramadan and recorded feedback for students who travel for sport or family. No session depends on anyone crossing the emirate in traffic.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, no invented ones
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or survey that published it, with the month it was read. We publish no pass rates, no satisfaction percentages and no score promises, because we cannot show you the data behind them.

faqs.question: How many objects does the TOK exhibition need, and can my child use four?
faqs.answer: Three, and no, four is not an option. The task specifies exactly three objects, each placed in a specific real-world context and each linked to the same IA prompt. A fourth object cannot gain credit and the words it consumes come out of a 950-word ceiling that is already tight. If your child has four strong candidates, the useful exercise is deciding which three make three genuinely different claims about the prompt. Two objects that make the same point are a more common problem than too few objects, and dropping one of them usually raises the mark rather than lowering it.

faqs.question: What is the word limit for the TOK exhibition commentary?
faqs.answer: 950 words for the commentary covering all three objects, which works out at roughly 300 words per object once a short framing sentence is allowed for. The limit is a ceiling, not a target, and markers do not reward reaching it. What costs marks is spending 450 words on the first object and 150 on the third, because the rubric is holistic and judges the consistency of the justification across all three. Citations and image captions are handled according to your school's own guidance, so check whether yours counts them before planning the final draft.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my child's exhibition objects for them?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to your child's Diploma rather than a help. The objects and the commentary must be the student's own work under IB academic honesty rules. What a tutor can do is question a shortlist the student brings: does this object have a date and a place, can you describe its context first-hand, does it make a different claim from your second object. That questioning routinely changes which three objects get used, but the student makes the choice and can account for it if asked.

faqs.question: Why did my child's TOK exhibition draft come back in the middle band?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the commentary describes the objects rather than justifying their inclusion. A middle-band draft typically explains what each object is, asserts that it relates to the prompt, and moves on. The upper bands need an explicit argument for each object: this object, in this context, shows this about the prompt, and here is why. The fastest diagnostic is to ask your child to highlight the words in each paragraph that connect the object to the prompt. If there is nothing to highlight in one of the three, that is the paragraph to rewrite first.

faqs.question: Does the TOK exhibition count towards the IB points total?
faqs.answer: Indirectly, and more than its size suggests. The exhibition is one third of the TOK grade and the prescribed-title essay is the other two thirds. TOK is graded A to E, then combined with the Extended Essay grade in a published matrix worth up to three points on the 45-point scale. Separately, a grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma, whatever the six subject grades look like. So a ten-mark commentary in the first Diploma year feeds a core grade that can decide both points and the award itself.

faqs.question: Can my child change the wording of an IA prompt to fit their objects better?
faqs.answer: No. The thirty-five IA prompts are published and used exactly as written. Rewording one is a structural error that a moderator will notice immediately, and it usually signals that the objects were chosen before the prompt. If the published prompts do not suit a student's objects, the correct move is to change the objects or change the prompt, not to edit the question. In a first session we test two or three prompts against the student's object pool before any writing begins, which is cheaper than discovering the mismatch in a marked draft.

faqs.question: When in DP1 should an Abu Dhabi student start the exhibition?
faqs.answer: Three to four weeks before the school's internal deadline, with objects collected before the prompt is fixed. Schools in the emirate set their own exhibition deadlines, and they tend to fall in the second or third term, in the same weeks as the first subject internal assessment drafts. A student who starts in the deadline fortnight is competing with their own Chemistry or Maths IA for attention, which is how a solvable 950-word task turns into a crisis. Collecting candidate objects over one evening early in the term costs almost nothing and removes the worst of that collision.

faqs.question: Are TOK sessions online or does a tutor come to our villa in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For this task the online format is genuinely the stronger one, because the work is screen work: the commentary document is shared, the tutor marks the link sentences in real time, and the three object images sit open alongside. A family in Khalifa City also gets a TOK specialist rather than whichever tutor happens to be within a reasonable drive on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: What does TOK exhibition support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The market rather than our price list: published UAE rates run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 200 to 450 or more for IB specialists, with one provider publishing AED 650 for a named tutor. Those are the providers' own figures, read in October 2026. Because the exhibition is a short block of three to five sessions rather than a standing weekly commitment, the total is closer to a single month's tutoring than a term's. We quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: My child is strong in their subjects but weak at TOK. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Common enough to be unremarkable. TOK asks for a different move from almost every other DP component: not what is true, but how a claim comes to count as knowledge. A student who is excellent at applying a method can find that genuinely disorienting, especially in a single weekly period taught alongside six subjects. The exhibition is usually the easier of the two TOK tasks for that student, because objects are concrete and the student chooses them. It is a good place to build the habit before the essay, where the same move has to be sustained abstractly.

faqs.question: How is the exhibition marked, and who has the final say?
faqs.answer: The school marks it out of ten against a single holistic rubric, and the IB moderates externally. That means the teacher's mark is a proposal rather than a final result: if the moderator judges the school's standard across the sampled work to be out of line, marks for the cohort can move. The practical consequence for your child is to write for a reader who does not already know what they meant. A commentary that makes the rubric's demands visible on the page survives moderation better than one that relies on a teacher filling in the gaps.

faqs.question: Does the exhibition need to include anything from the UAE or Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Nothing requires it, but local objects usually score better, and the reason is provenance rather than patriotism. The rubric wants each object in a specific real-world context, and a student can describe a context they have stood in with a precision no summary matches: a dated museum label on Saadiyat, a bilingual sign where the two languages diverge, a regulator document their own school is assessed against. The alternative is an object found through a search, which almost always arrives with a generic context and a paragraph that reads like it was written from a summary.

faqs.question: Can we get help in the last week before the exhibition deadline?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with one honest caveat about what a final week can achieve. A single diagnostic session on an existing draft can identify which sentences are doing rubric work, which paragraph is weakest, and what one change would move the band, and the student then has several hours of their own rewriting to do. What we will not do is write or rewrite any part of the commentary, however close the deadline, because the work must be the student's own. Specialist availability also tightens in deadline fortnights, so tell us the date early even if you book late.

faqs.question: How do TOK sessions work during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. School days shorten and households reorganise around iftar, so the usual 5pm slot becomes unworkable and a post-iftar session becomes the practical one. We schedule accordingly and keep the cadence, because DP1 students who pause for a month during a term containing both the exhibition and their first IA drafts pay for it later in the year. If your child is fasting and prefers shorter sessions, two 40-minute slots a week often work better than one long one.

faqs.question: What happens if no TOK specialist is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a general essay tutor and hoping. TOK is a small specialism, the deadlines in Abu Dhabi schools cluster in the same fortnights, and demand concentrates there. If nobody suitable is free in your window, the options are a later slot with written draft feedback in between, a tutor outside the emirate on a compatible evening schedule, or a recommendation to use your child's own TOK teacher's clinic hours. An honest no is worth more to you than a poorly matched yes on a graded core component.

abu-dhabi/ib-tok-exhibition-help.closingHeading: Start with the object list, not the deadline
abu-dhabi/ib-tok-exhibition-help.closingBody: If your child has an exhibition deadline in Abu Dhabi, the useful first step costs nothing: have them photograph eight candidate objects this week, note where and when each came from, and book the free trial lesson with that list open. One session is usually enough to fix a prompt choice, kill the two objects that make the same point, and leave a specific writing task to do before the next slot. Tell us the school, the deadline and whether a prompt has been chosen, and we will say how many sessions the task actually needs, including when the answer is fewer than you expected.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are priced on subject depth and level rather than on a single platform rate. Each names the IB subject group and level they teach, which is the variable that moves a quote more than anything else in this emirate.

intro.heading: The price is knowable, and most of this market hides it
paragraphs: Of the six strongest pages ranking for IB tutoring queries in this market, three publish no price at all. One of the three asks the price in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. The two that do publish quote in US dollars, a currency Abu Dhabi families neither earn nor spend. That is the state of pricing transparency you are shopping in, and it is why most parents arrive at a first call with no idea whether AED 200 an hour is cheap or extortionate.

It is neither; it is the middle of the market. Published rates across the UAE run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those figures are read from provider pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table in October 2026, and they are the market rather than an IB Gram price list.

The headline band is the least interesting part, though. What a parent actually needs is the list of things that move a quote, because that is what you can negotiate, plan around or decide to pay for deliberately. Subject scarcity moves it. Level moves it: a Higher Level Diploma subject is not priced like a Middle Years one. Session length moves the per-hour figure. The month you book in moves availability and therefore the effective rate. Whether the hours include marking between sessions moves it substantially, and is the single most common omission from a cheap quote.

Abu Dhabi has its own pressures on all of this. The emirate's Diploma cohorts are small per school, so a Higher Level subject with few local teachers has a genuinely thin specialist pool, and scarcity pricing follows. Enrolment is spread between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities, which makes any in-home rate carry a meaningful travel component. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its inspection and fee processes shape school budgets, which in turn shape what families have left for tutoring.

This page is organised around the money. It publishes the bands with sources, names the variables that move them, places tutoring cost next to school fees and exam entry so the figure has context, compares provider models on what is actually inside the price, and sets out what a quote should itemise before you agree to it. It also says what the money cannot buy, because the two most expensive mistakes in this market are paying for a guarantee nobody can give and paying for work that must be the student's own. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visiting is a service offered only in India.
bullets: Half this market publishes no price; the rest quote in a currency you do not use

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.programmesIntro: Price varies by programme more than by city, because the assessments differ and so does the preparation a tutor has to do between sessions. Here is what each stage of the IB typically costs to support, and what drives the figure in Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to support, because there are no external papers and the content does not require a subject specialist. Market rates sit at the lower end of the published bands. The cost driver is frequency rather than rate: early literacy and number work needs short, regular sessions, so a monthly figure matters more than an hourly one.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the competing cost at this stage is usually Arabic support, which many families buy separately because it is mandated alongside the licensed curriculum. Budgeting for both at once is the realistic version, and two short sessions a week on different subjects is a very different monthly figure from one longer session.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Mid-band pricing, because the tutor needs to know the four-criterion assessment model rather than only the subject. The hidden cost here is marking: criterion-referenced feedback on a task takes real time between sessions, and a quote that excludes it is cheaper on paper and worth less in practice.
programmes.countryNote: The Middle Years to Diploma transition drives most of the spend in this emirate, and it is the point where families often buy more hours than they need. A clearer and cheaper approach is to find out which criterion is dragging a subject down before buying a term, because the answer usually narrows the work to one skill rather than a whole subject.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most expensive stage and the one where the spread between providers is widest. Higher Level subjects sit at the top of the specialist band because the pool of tutors who genuinely teach them is small. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are small per school, which thins the local specialist supply in any one Higher Level subject. That is the clearest scarcity premium in the emirate, and it is also the strongest argument for online delivery: a figure driven up by geography rather than expertise is a figure worth removing.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Usually bought as a short block rather than as weekly hours, timed to the school's draft deadlines. Priced in the specialist band because the work is feedback-heavy rather than teaching-heavy. A block of six to eight sessions across a term is the typical shape, and it should be quoted as a block with the deadlines named.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the worst value in the UAE market sits. One provider found in the wider search results sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is not expensive tutoring, it is a malpractice risk for the student, and it is the one line item a parent should refuse outright regardless of what it is called.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subject is the second biggest variable in a quote after level, because supply differs sharply. Below are the subjects Abu Dhabi families ask for most, with a note on what drives the price in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested and best supplied Diploma subject, which keeps it near the middle of the specialist band rather than the top. Higher Level carries a premium because proof and calculus depth narrow the pool. Hours are also the heaviest here, which makes the monthly figure larger even at an ordinary rate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Priced similarly to Analysis and Approaches but with thinner supply at Higher Level, because fewer tutors have taught the modelling and statistics content in depth. A tutor quoting the same rate for both routes without asking which one your child takes is quoting a subject name rather than a course.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Reliable scarcity premium at Higher Level across the UAE. The extra paper and the additional topics mean more preparation between sessions, which shows in the rate. Families often get better value buying fewer hours on the specific topics that are failing than a standing weekly slot across the syllabus.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Similar band to Physics, with an additional cost pressure around the internally assessed work, where data analysis feedback is time-consuming. Expect a block quote for that rather than an hourly one, and expect it to be more expensive per hour than ordinary teaching time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Better supplied than Physics and Chemistry, so usually slightly cheaper at the same level. The cost here hides in volume: the content load means more hours rather than a higher rate, and a family budgeting on an hourly figure alone often underestimates the term.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Mid-band and well supplied. Diagram and evaluation technique responds quickly to correction, which means fewer hours are often genuinely enough, and that is worth knowing before buying a year. Higher Level quantitative questions are reliable marks and cheap to fix.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marking-heavy, so the honest rate includes written feedback time and a quote that excludes it is misleading. Supply is reasonable but quality varies widely, because the subject looks teachable by any strong English graduate and is not without knowledge of the markbands.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Mid-band. The cost-effective version of support here is short and specific: application to the organisation in the stem is the band separator, and that can be corrected in a handful of sessions once a marked script has shown that generic answers are what is capping the grade.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Often bought alongside the Diploma because Arabic is mandated in UAE schools, and frequently priced separately. Supply of tutors who know the IB Arabic criteria, as opposed to teaching the language well, is thin, and that gap shows in the rate rather than in availability.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Almost always sold as a block rather than hourly, and the price reflects reading and feedback time rather than teaching. A sensible quote names the number of sessions, the school's deadlines they sit against, and the fact that feedback arrives as questions rather than as text.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.regionsIntro: Location changes the price of in-home tuition and almost nothing about the price of online tuition, which is a useful thing to know before comparing quotes. Here is how the travel component actually falls across the emirate.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Central and quick to reach, so the travel loading on an in-home rate is at its lowest here. The constraint families report is quiet study space rather than cost, which is why online sessions and a decent headset are the common answer.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short runs to nearby schools but a limited local tutor pool, so in-home quotes here tend to reflect scarcity rather than distance. Online removes the scarcity rather than the distance, which is the more valuable of the two.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The longest school transport runs in the emirate, which pushes sessions past 17:30 and puts any visiting tutor into evening traffic in both directions. That travel time is inside the in-home rate whether it is itemised or not.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established central districts with the densest local tutor supply, and therefore the most competitive in-home pricing in Abu Dhabi. Also where sibling bookings are most common, which is the one arrangement that genuinely lowers the per-child cost.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer catchment, growing cohorts, thin local specialist supply in any single Higher Level subject. Quotes here can look high for reasons that have nothing to do with teaching quality, which is exactly the premium online delivery removes.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mainland catchment with long inbound journeys. In-home rates carry the heaviest travel loading in the emirate, and families here are the most likely to find that an online quote is simply a different number rather than a compromise.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, and far enough out that the local specialist pool for a Higher Level subject is genuinely thin. Scarcity, not distance, is what prices tuition here, and it is the clearest case in the emirate for buying a specialist remotely.

regions.name: Al Dhafra and the Western Region
regions.note: Very limited local provision at Diploma level. Any in-home arrangement involves a long journey priced into the hour, and for most Higher Level subjects there is no local option at any price. Online is the market rather than an alternative to it.

schoolClusters.city: Island schools: Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Where most of the emirate's IB provision sits. Fees at this end of the market are high, which compresses what families have left for tutoring and makes the number of hours more negotiable than the rate. Students we support here are frequently buying a short block before an internal deadline rather than a standing weekly slot.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland corridor: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: A wider fee range and a wider curriculum mix, so tutoring budgets vary more here than anywhere in the emirate. Internal deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several of these schools, which is also when local specialist availability is tightest and effective rates are highest.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition.modesIntro: The same hourly rate buys quite different things depending on how it is packaged. Three arrangements, with what each actually costs over a term and what is usually inside and outside the price.

modes.description: The cheapest per hour of the three and the easiest to budget, because the monthly figure is stable. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Ask explicitly whether marking between sessions is inside that.

The total is larger and the planning window is shorter, which makes it the arrangement where buying the wrong subject is most expensive. A marked diagnostic before the block is the cheapest insurance available.

It should be the most clearly itemised thing you buy: number of sessions, which deadlines they sit against, and an explicit statement that feedback arrives as questions rather than as text.

sections.heading: What IB tuition in Abu Dhabi costs, with every figure sourced
paragraphs: A qualified subject tutor working online in this market publishes rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 or more. Those are the two bands most Abu Dhabi Diploma families are choosing between. Below that, AED 45 to 150 buys a budget or university-student tutor, which is useful for homework supervision and rarely enough for Higher Level exam technique. Above it, one provider publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Packages seen in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are worth converting to a per-hour figure before comparing, because the session length and the tutor's level differ between them. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are roughly AED 240 to 600 for budget support, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

Every one of those figures comes from a named provider page or from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. None of them is an IB Gram price. We do not publish a rate card on this page because our quote follows a free trial lesson and a marked diagnostic paper, and quoting a term before anyone has read your child's work is guesswork dressed as a price. What we will say is which band we sit in once we know the subject and level.

One number is genuinely fixed and worth knowing: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Any tutor or agency charging you for a permit, or citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate, is charging for something that costs nothing.

sections.heading: The seven variables that actually move the number here
paragraphs: A single headline rate is close to useless because seven things change it, and six of them are within your control or at least within your knowledge. Understanding them is the difference between negotiating and guessing. They are, roughly in order of how much they move a quote: level, subject supply, whether marking is included, session length, the month you book, how many children are involved, and location, which matters only for in-home arrangements.

Level is the biggest. A Higher Level Diploma subject and a Middle Years subject are not the same product, and the gap between them is usually larger than the gap between two providers at the same level. Subject supply is second and is specific to this emirate: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts are small per school, so the pool of tutors who have genuinely taught a given Higher Level subject is thin, and scarcity prices accordingly.

The variable that most often explains a suspiciously cheap quote is marking. Criterion-referenced feedback on a written task, or a marked timed paper with the losses categorised, takes real time between sessions. A rate that covers only contact time is cheaper and buys less, and the difference does not show until the end of the term when there is nothing to read. Ask explicitly, and ask for the quote itemised.

The month matters more than families expect. Demand concentrates around internal assessment deadlines and the external paper season, and specialist tutors fill up first. Booking in those weeks means choosing from a smaller pool at the top of the band, which is a real cost rather than a sales tactic. Location, finally, is a travel loading on in-home rates only, heaviest in Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Ain and the Western Region, and absent entirely from an online arrangement.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entry and the full Diploma
paragraphs: An hourly rate in isolation is hard to judge. Put next to the other numbers a family in this emirate is already paying, it becomes a decision rather than a shock. The table below sets tutoring against the costs that surround it, using only figures that can be sourced or that you can obtain directly from your own school and exam centre.

A deliberate omission: this page does not publish Abu Dhabi school fee figures. Fees vary enormously by school and year group and are set through the emirate's own regulatory process, so quoting a band would be inventing a number. Your school publishes its own, ADEK is the authority that governs private schools in the emirate, and that is where to read it. What can be said as context is from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package.

Exam entry is the cost families most often forget, and it only applies if your child is sitting outside a school as a private candidate. It is paid to the registered exam centre, varies by subject count, and has its own deadline that sits months before the papers. If the Diploma is being taken through a school, entry is inside the fees and the question does not arise.

The number that deserves the most thought is the two-year total. A standing weekly session in one Higher Level subject across both Diploma years is a large commitment, and many families would be better served by a smaller, sharper pattern: a diagnostic each term, a short block where the diagnostic shows a problem, and a core block around the internal assessment and Extended Essay deadlines. That is usually both cheaper and better targeted than continuous hours, and it is the arrangement a good tutor will suggest if asked what they would do with your budget.

sections.heading: Provider models compared on what is inside the price
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself to an unnamed alternative that is worse. A more useful comparison is between models, because the model determines what is inside the hour. There are five you will realistically encounter in Abu Dhabi, and the differences are structural rather than a matter of quality.

A specialist agency assigns a tutor and takes a margin for vetting and replacement. An international marketplace lists tutors who set their own rates, which gives you range and puts the verification burden on you. An independent freelance tutor is usually the cheapest per hour and carries no replacement arrangement if it does not work. A tuition centre with premises sells group hours at a low per-head rate and is regulated as an institute rather than as an individual. A platform like this one matches a tutor and runs the record-keeping.

The questions that separate them are the same five whatever the model: what is the hourly rate, is marking between sessions inside it, is the tutor's MoHRE permit verified, what happens if the match is wrong, and is there a free trial with the actual tutor rather than a sales call. A provider that cannot answer all five quickly is not necessarily bad, but you are buying something less defined than you think.

One caution about pricing claims across models. Do not take any provider's published rate, including those on this page, as current without checking the date it was read. One competitor's structured pricing data contradicts the figures printed on the same page, and another's discount table contradicts itself. Every figure here is dated to October 2026 and attributed, which is the standard worth holding any provider to, including us.

sections.heading: Hidden extras, and what a quote should itemise before you pay
paragraphs: The gap between two quotes for the same subject at the same level is usually not the rate. It is what is bundled. A quote that itemises is easier to compare and harder to pad, and asking for one is a reasonable request that takes a provider five minutes.

Six lines are worth insisting on. The hourly rate and the session length, stated separately, so the per-hour figure is yours rather than theirs. Whether marking and preparation between sessions is included. Whether materials are included, and what they are, because a provider should not be sending you past papers and mark schemes at all. Whether there is a rescheduling arrangement and what notice it needs. Whether anything is payable up front and what happens if you stop after one session. And whether the quoted figure includes VAT.

On that last point, this page states only the obvious: ask whether a quoted AED figure includes VAT, and ask the provider for their tax registration number if they claim to charge it. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a general matter, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and this page does not have one. Any provider asserting the treatment confidently without a citation is telling you something about how they handle facts.

Two things should never appear as a line item. A charge for the tutor's permit, which is free. And anything described as producing, completing or supplying assessed work, at any price, under any label. One provider in the wider UAE results prices finished internal assessments at AED 3,750; the correct response to that line on a quote is to leave, because the risk it creates sits with your child rather than with the seller.

sections.heading: Why the exam and deadline season reprices this market
paragraphs: Published rate cards in this market do not move much across the year. The effective price does, and it moves for a reason worth understanding: supply of genuine subject specialists is finite, and demand is extremely seasonal. The result is that the same AED 250 an hour buys a different quality of tutor in October than it does eight weeks before the papers.

The seasonality is driven by school calendars rather than by providers. Internal assessment and Extended Essay draft deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several Abu Dhabi schools, because they all have to feed the same external submission points. Mock windows cluster similarly. Then the external paper season arrives and every family who had been thinking about it starts calling at once. A specialist with eight weekly slots fills them in that first fortnight.

Cambridge and Pearson dates show the same shape in the IGCSE market and are publishable because they are sourced. In the UAE a Cambridge candidate sits the June series or the November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so it never appears in an Abu Dhabi school's calendar. That gives the local market two demand peaks rather than one. The larger peak builds towards the June papers, with entries closing in the spring well ahead of them and the exact date on the centre's statement of entry. The second, smaller peak sits over the summer, when families who want the November resit route decide before that entry closes. Pearson's published figures mark the same two windows: the International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, no session or results date is published on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date would be unverified, and your child's Diploma coordinator is the authority on it.

The practical consequence is simple and slightly unwelcome. If you already suspect you will want support in the spring, the cheapest and best-matched version of it is booked in the autumn. That is not an argument about outcomes, which nobody can promise. It is an argument about who is still available.

sections.heading: What the money cannot buy, at any rate
paragraphs: Three things are for sale in this market that should not be, and all three are expensive precisely because they are unverifiable. Knowing what they are protects a budget better than any negotiation.

The first is a promised outcome. No tutor can promise a score, a specific improvement or a university place, and a provider offering one is selling a claim rather than a service. Several competitors publish satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and student counts with no stated sample, date or method; one shows two different review figures on the same page. Treat an unevidenced number as a reason for caution rather than confidence, and apply the same standard to us.

The second is regulatory approval. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE as an institution, the IB or any examination board, and does not claim one. A tutoring business with premises and staff needs a permit from the relevant emirate authority, and an individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition permit. Neither of those makes a platform accredited, and the phrase describing tutors as regulator-approved is the single most misleading thing available in this market.

The third is completed assessed work. The IB requires internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay to be the student's own, submitted through a school accountable for authenticity. A tutor may explain criteria, model technique on other material, ask questions about a draft and mark practice. No tutor text goes into a submission. Also, no provider should be supplying IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads: those belong to the IB, and redistributing them is copyright infringement regardless of how common it is.

sections.heading: Who you are legally paying, and how to check
paragraphs: Before the price matters, the permit does. Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

MoHRE's service page is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. It shows no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and amounts circulating online could not be verified, so none appears here.

Abu Dhabi carries one additional rule that bears directly on who you should be paying. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This has been reported in the press rather than read from the current policy document, so check the exact wording against ADEK's own publication. The principle is sound regardless: the person who marks your child's school assessments should not also be paid to prepare them for it.

What to do with this is a two-minute conversation. Ask any individual tutor, including ours, whether they hold the MoHRE permit and to show it. Ask a centre which authority licenses it and for the permit reference. Both answers are checkable, both questions are routine, and the willingness to answer tells you a great deal about where your money is going.

process.title: Tell us subject, level and the real deadline
process.description: Three pieces of information set a quote: which subject, Higher or Standard Level or which Middle Years year group, and what is actually coming up. A Higher Level Physics block before an internal deadline and a Standard Level Economics weekly slot are different products at different prices, and guessing at either produces a useless number.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the tutor who would teach
process.description: The trial is with the specific tutor rather than a sales call, on a real past-paper question, and nothing is committed afterwards. It is also the point at which you can ask the tutor directly about their MoHRE permit and what they would do with your budget if it were smaller than you had hoped.

process.title: Marked diagnostic before any quote for hours
process.description: One timed paper or criterion-marked task, with every lost mark categorised. This is what decides how many hours are genuinely needed, and it is why we do not publish a rate card: a term quoted before anyone has read your child's work is a guess. Occasionally the honest answer is fewer hours than you expected.

process.title: An itemised quote you can compare
process.description: Rate and session length stated separately, marking and preparation shown as a line, rescheduling notice named, and anything payable up front spelled out. Comparable with any other provider's quote if they will itemise theirs. If a figure is a market band rather than our price, it is labelled as one with its source.

process.title: Review the spend at the halfway point
process.description: At the midpoint of a block or term we compare the running error log against the first diagnostic and say in writing whether the hours are earning their cost. Categories that have closed release their hours; categories that have not moved get a different approach rather than a bigger invoice.

whyPoints.title: Prices published with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider or research source that printed it and the month it was read. Half this market publishes no price, and two ranking providers contradict their own figures on the same page. A dated, attributed band is a lower bar than it sounds and almost nobody clears it.

whyPoints.title: The quote follows the diagnostic
whyPoints.description: We do not price a term before reading a marked script, which is slower to buy and occasionally produces a smaller invoice than expected. It also means the hours are aimed at the category of error that is actually costing marks rather than at the subject that feels worst in the house.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the price and shown as a line
whyPoints.description: Criterion and markband feedback between sessions is the slow part of this work and the most common thing missing from a cheap quote. Ours is included and itemised so the comparison with another provider is like for like. A rate covering only contact time buys less than it appears to.

whyPoints.title: No cost that does not exist
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years. No quote from us includes a permit charge, a registration fee or a materials bundle of past papers and mark schemes, because that material belongs to the boards and should be referenced rather than resold.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one online, so you are not paying for a car
whyPoints.description: Sessions run live over video, one student and one tutor, at Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home rates in this emirate carry a travel loading that is heaviest exactly where specialist supply is thinnest, and removing it is the clearest saving available.

whyPoints.title: No unevidenced number anywhere on this page
whyPoints.description: No satisfaction percentage, no average score, no student count, no star rating. Not because they would not help the page rank, but because none of them could be produced with a sample size, a date and a method if a parent asked. Apply that test to every provider you speak to.

faqs.question: What is a realistic hourly figure for IB tuition in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Below that, AED 45 to 150 buys budget or university-student support, which suits homework supervision rather than Higher Level exam technique. One premium provider publishes AED 650. Those figures come from provider pages and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read October 2026, and are the market rather than our price list. For a Higher Level Diploma subject, expect to be choosing within the specialist band rather than below it.

faqs.question: Why do two quotes for the same subject differ by half?
faqs.answer: Usually because one includes marking and preparation between sessions and the other covers contact time only. Criterion-referenced feedback on a written task, or a timed paper marked with the losses categorised, takes real time, and a rate that excludes it is genuinely cheaper and genuinely buys less. The difference does not show until the end of the term when there is nothing to read. The other common cause is level: a Higher Level Diploma subject and a Middle Years one are different products. Ask both providers to itemise rate, session length and marking separately.

faqs.question: Does a longer session work out cheaper per hour?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in this emirate it also fits the week better. A ninety-minute slot usually carries a lower per-hour figure than sixty minutes because the preparation overhead is spread further. It also suits the Khalifa City and Al Raha school runs, where students are frequently home only after 16:00 and a single later session is easier to protect than two short ones. The caveat is attention: ninety focused minutes beat two unfocused hours, and for younger students shorter and more frequent genuinely works better even at a higher per-hour rate.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to book a whole term up front?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth weighing against what you give up. A term booked up front may carry a lower rate and will certainly secure a slot before the deadline season fills the specialist pool. What it costs you is the ability to stop cheaply if the match is wrong. The compromise most families find useful is a short committed block with a written review at the midpoint, so there is a natural decision point. Ask what happens if you stop after one session, and get the answer before paying anything.

faqs.question: Does where we live in the emirate change what we pay?
faqs.answer: For in-home tuition, substantially. The travel component sits inside the hourly rate whether it is itemised or not, and it is heaviest in Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Mussafah, Al Ain and the Western Region. It is lowest in the central districts around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif, where local tutor supply is densest. For online tuition it changes nothing at all, which is why comparing an in-home quote from a distant community against an online one is comparing two different cost structures rather than two prices for the same thing.

faqs.question: Why would a Higher Level subject cost more than a Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Because the supply of tutors who have genuinely taught it is smaller, and in Abu Dhabi that is sharper than in a denser market. Diploma cohorts here are small per school, so fewer local teachers have carried a given Higher Level course through to the papers. Higher Level also means an additional paper, more content and more preparation time between sessions. The useful consequence is that the scarcity part of that premium is geographic rather than about expertise, and buying remotely removes it while keeping the specialist.

faqs.question: Should we be paying anything towards the tutor's permit?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge and is valid for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee alongside a two-working-day completion time. Any tutor or agency charging you for it, or citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate, is charging for something that costs nothing. It is also a reasonable question to ask directly: does the tutor hold the permit, and will they show it? Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Does the quoted AED figure include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for a tax registration number if VAT is being charged. This page deliberately does not state the general VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE, because doing so properly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation and we do not have one to hand. What we will say is that a quoted figure should be unambiguous about whether it is inclusive, and a provider asserting the tax treatment confidently with no citation is telling you something about how carefully they handle facts generally.

faqs.question: Are the monthly packages advertised online good value?
faqs.answer: Convert them before deciding. A package of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and one of AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions are both real market offers, but the per-hour figures and the tutor levels behind them differ considerably. Divide by the actual hours, then ask whether marking is included and whether the tutor is a subject specialist or a generalist. A package that looks cheap per month and expensive per useful hour is the commonest trap in this market, and the arithmetic takes a minute.

faqs.question: Do rates rise as the papers get closer?
faqs.answer: Published rate cards mostly do not move. The effective price does, because specialist supply is finite and demand is seasonal. Internal assessment and Extended Essay draft deadlines cluster in the same weeks across several Abu Dhabi schools, mock windows cluster similarly, and then the external paper season arrives and everyone calls at once. The same AED 250 buys a different quality of match in October than it does eight weeks before the papers. Booking early is an argument about who is still available rather than a claim about results.

faqs.question: Can we lower the cost by having two children share a tutor?
faqs.answer: Siblings are the one arrangement that genuinely reduces cost per child, and the better version is usually back-to-back individual slots rather than a shared session. Two children in different year groups or on different criteria have almost nothing in common to work on, so a shared hour halves the attention without halving the need. Back-to-back slots keep each child's error log separate while saving on scheduling and often on rate. If both children are in the same subject and year, a genuinely shared session can work.

faqs.question: How many hours does a Diploma subject actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families buy, if the hours are aimed correctly. A marked diagnostic that categorises lost marks as recall, method, command term or timing usually narrows the work to one or two skills rather than a whole subject, and technique losses respond quickly to one-to-one correction. Content gaps are the expensive case and need weeks rather than intensity. The pattern that tends to give the best value across two Diploma years is a diagnostic each term, a short block where it shows a problem, and a core block around the coursework deadlines.

faqs.question: What should I refuse to pay for outright?
faqs.answer: Two things. Any charge connected to the tutor's permit, which is free. And anything described as producing, completing or supplying work that has to be the student's own, whatever it is labelled. One provider in the wider UAE results prices finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. The IB requires that work to be the student's own, submitted through a school accountable for its authenticity, so the risk created by that purchase sits with your child rather than with the seller. A tutor explains criteria, models technique and asks questions about a draft.

faqs.question: Can anyone guarantee an improvement for the money?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is the clearest warning sign available. No tutor can promise a score, a specific grade movement or a university place. Several providers in this market publish satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and student counts with no stated sample, date or method, and one shows two different review figures on the same page. The standard worth applying, to us as much as to anyone, is whether a number could be produced with its sample size, date and method on request. If not, it should not be influencing a purchase.

faqs.question: Are school fees in Abu Dhabi relevant to what we should spend on tuition?
faqs.answer: Practically, yes, because they set what is left. This page does not publish Abu Dhabi fee figures: they vary enormously by school and year group and are set through the emirate's own regulatory process, so a band would be invented. ADEK is the authority that supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and your school publishes its own figures. As context from elsewhere in the country, Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees there would not rise for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: Tutor profiles below name a subject, a level and the components the tutor marks. That combination is what the price is actually for: a Higher Level specialist who marks a named paper costs more than a generalist, and on a narrow component problem they also cost less in total hours.

intro.heading: Why nobody near you will quote a price
paragraphs: The hardest part of buying IB tuition in Abu Dhabi is that the market will not tell you what anything costs. Of the competitor pages examined for this cluster, three publish no price at all, and one of them has a frequently-asked-questions block that asks about the price and then declines to answer it. The two that do publish quote in US dollars, which is not the currency an Abu Dhabi family transacts in, and one of those contradicts its own figure between the visible page and its structured data. So the first thing a parent needs is simply the numbers.

Here they are, as published by the market in 2026. Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, runs from about AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit at AED 150-300, where Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, with travel inside the fee, runs AED 180-500, with Bestimate showing 180-350 and independent home tutors advertising 200-500. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists sit at AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+. Premium named tutors reach AED 500-650 and more; BartyED publishes AED 650.

The spread is roughly fourteen-fold between the bottom and the top, which is why a single headline number would be dishonest rather than helpful. What closes the gap is understanding which variables move the price and by how much. Eight of them matter in this emirate: the level, the component, the session length, the group size, whether anyone is travelling, the time of year, the tutor's tier, and the shape of the commitment. Each one has a direction and a rough magnitude, and this page gives both.

Abu Dhabi adds its own cost logic. Private schools here are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and enrolment stretches from the island through the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor out to Al Shamkha, Al Reef and Al Samha. That geography is the single largest driver of the in-home premium: a tutor driving from the island to Al Reef at the afternoon peak spends forty minutes or more each way, which is why in-home work is sold in two-hour blocks and priced above the online bands. Removing the travel removes the surcharge.

IB Gram delivers to Abu Dhabi as one-to-one tuition over live video. We do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Our own fee depends on subject, level and session length and is quoted after a consultation rather than advertised as one number, and a free trial lesson happens before any payment is taken. Everything else on this page is the market's, with its sources named, so you can price a decision rather than guess at one.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Price varies by programme as much as by subject, because what is being bought changes. Primary work is fluency, Middle Years work is criteria literacy, and Diploma work is component-specific technique with an internal assessment calendar attached. Those are three different products at three different costs.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. MYP tuition is usually the cheapest useful IB tuition a family will buy, because the specialism required is narrower: a tutor who can read the school's criteria descriptors and teach against them does not need Higher Level examination experience.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi, MYP 4 and MYP 5 are where spending starts, and they are also the stage where spending is most efficient. Fixing criteria literacy and command terms before DP1 costs a fraction of fixing the same problem in DP2, when the internal assessment calendar leaves no room. Families in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor often make this move a year earlier than families further out, simply because the shorter school run makes a weekly session easy to hold.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each with an internal assessment worth a fifth to a third of the grade, plus the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. This is where tuition is most expensive per hour and most variable in total cost, because the number of hours needed depends almost entirely on when the work starts and how narrow the problem is.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi cohorts sit the May session and schools generally run mocks between December and February of DP2. Specialist availability tightens through that window across the whole Gulf, and prices at the top of the market firm up with it. A Higher Level science block bought in October is cheaper and easier to staff than the same block bought in January. Confirm examination and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based learning with no external assessment, so there is no paper to prepare for. Pricing here should reflect shorter sessions: thirty to forty-five minutes twice a week does more for reading accuracy and number fluency than a single hour, and a provider charging an exam-preparation rate for primary work has mispriced the product.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries cluster in the newer mainland communities, where families are least willing to add a second car journey to the afternoon. Two short online sessions a week are affordable in both money and time; the same pattern delivered in-home would require two journeys and is priced accordingly, which is why in-home primary work is almost always sold as one longer visit instead.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: Cost per subject follows scarcity and component difficulty rather than a published tariff. Below is what each subject actually requires of a tutor, which is the thing you are paying more or less for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits in the widest-supplied part of the market, so it is at the lower end of specialist pricing. Higher Level Paper 3 work is a narrower skill, which moves it into the AED 200-450+ band because the pool of people who have marked two extended problems well is small.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology assumed. Supply is reasonable at both levels, and the work most often needed - interpretation sentences next to correct calculations - is quick to teach, so the total hours tend to be low even at a specialist rate.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most price-sensitive Higher Level subject in this market, because demand across the Gulf peaks in the same December-to-February window every year. Booking the block in the autumn is the single largest saving available on this subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level organic and energetics carry a concentrated set of lost marks, which is good news for cost: a narrow problem needs few hours. The pool tightens before mocks in the same way Physics does.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Reasonable supply at both levels. Most requests are for criterion-based feedback on the scientific investigation rather than content teaching, which is a short block rather than a weekly commitment and prices accordingly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level is widely supplied; Higher Level Paper 3 is not. The internal assessment is three commentaries, which is three short pieces of work rather than one long one, and that shape suits a small number of scheduled sessions.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 support is widely available at mid-market rates. The Higher Level essay is a narrower specialism and is usually bought as a short block at the specialist rate rather than as a weekly session across a year.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: The one subject where a UAE-based tutor is worth paying for specifically, because the Diploma course and the Ministry-mandated Arabic requirement run in the same week and interact. Supply is good inside the UAE and thin outside it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers and a research-based internal assessment. Supply is good, and the common fault - a tool applied without a judgement about the business in the stimulus - is cheap to correct once named.

subjects.name: Visual Arts and Music
subjects.description: The thinnest supply in every market, which shows up as waiting time as well as price. These need planning a term ahead, and we would rather decline than place a generalist on a comparative study or a process portfolio.

abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: What your community does to the price
abu-dhabi/ib-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Online delivery removes travel from the fee entirely, but it is worth seeing what the travel would have been, because that is the part of an in-home quote that is not teaching. These are the Abu Dhabi communities we work with and the cost logic in each.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: The shortest real school run in the emirate and the densest local tutor pool, so in-home pricing here is at the lower end of the AED 180-500 band. Even so, the Higher Level specialist shortlist within twenty minutes stays small.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Ten minutes from Khalifa City. Families here often compare a weekly in-home visit against a short online specialist block and find the block cheaper in total because the hours needed are fewer.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: One causeway run. In-home work here is routinely sold as a two-hour minimum, so the real comparison is AED 360-1,000 per visit against a single focused online hour.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Short runs and an early workable slot. The cost advantage here is time rather than money: a session can finish before dinner, which means fewer cancelled and rebooked hours across a term.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Thirty to forty minutes each way at the peak. This is where the in-home premium stops describing teaching, and where the price gap between the two delivery models is at its widest.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Samha
regions.note: The longest afternoon runs. The subjects most needed here - Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Economics - are the scarcest locally, so a radius search raises the price and lowers the match quality at the same time.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: A longer run back from island schools and a steady flow of mid-year arrivals. Transition work is usually a fixed eight to twelve hours rather than an open commitment, which makes it easy to budget.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mixed communities with wide curriculum variety. Group classes are more available here than elsewhere in the emirate, which makes the group-versus-one-to-one cost comparison a live question rather than a theoretical one.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern corridor
schoolClusters.note: The heaviest concentration of international provision in Abu Dhabi, with IB continuum schools and British schools offering the Diploma alongside A-Levels. Internal assessment deadlines cluster here, which is why specialist blocks in this corridor are booked earliest and why late booking costs more.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: The island, Saadiyat and Al Reem
schoolClusters.note: Established island schools and newer provision nearby. Several cohorts here offer the Diploma as one route among others at post-16, so families are often pricing two different two-year plans against each other rather than one.

modes.title: Pay by the session
modes.description: The most expensive per hour and the cheapest to leave. This is the right shape at the start, while the match is unproven, and the right shape for a problem that may turn out to be narrow. Families who commit to a term before the first lesson routinely overbuy, because the marked paper has not yet told anybody how big the problem is.

sections.heading: The eight variables that move an IB tuition quote
paragraphs: A fourteen-fold spread between the cheapest and most expensive published hour in this market is not irrationality; it is eight separate variables compounding. Knowing which ones apply to your situation turns an unanswerable question into an estimate you can check. Three of the eight are under your control, three are under the provider's, and two belong to the calendar.

The variables you control are group size, session length and commitment shape. Group size has the largest effect of anything on this page: group rates in Abu Dhabi start around AED 45 per student against AED 200-450 and above for one-to-one specialist work, which is a factor of four to ten. Session length matters less than it looks, because ninety minutes is commonly priced below one and a half times the hourly rate. Commitment shape moves the effective rate down and the risk up, which is why it belongs after a proven six weeks rather than before a first lesson.

The variables the provider controls are tier, specialism and whether anyone travels. Tier is the steepest: the move from a qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 to a premium named tutor at AED 500-650 is a tripling, and the question worth asking is what the premium is evidenced by. Examiner status is the most common justification in this market and the least often documented. Travel is the clearest: the in-home band of AED 180-500 against the online band of AED 150-300 is largely a car.

The calendar variables are the ones families notice last. Specialist supply across the Gulf tightens between December and February of DP2 because every school runs mocks off the same session, and prices at the top firm up with it. And the total hours needed shrink the earlier the work starts, which is a far bigger lever on total cost than any hourly rate.

sections.heading: The full AED rate card for this market
paragraphs: This is the table the cluster is missing. Every figure is a published market rate attributed to the provider that published it in 2026, and none of them is IB Gram's price. Ours depends on subject, level and session length and is given after a consultation, because quoting one number for Higher Level Mathematics in DP2 and for MYP 3 science would make the number meaningless.

Read it with two cautions. The first is that a rate describes a seat, not a result: a permit to tutor, which is free and valid for two years from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, tells you somebody may legally teach, and the eligible categories include university students and school students aged 15 to 18. A low rate is often a young tutor, which is entirely appropriate for homework support and entirely wrong for Higher Level Chemistry.

The second is that monthly packages and hourly rates are not comparable until you divide. A package at AED 799 for eight sessions is AED 99 a session, but only if all eight are used, and school holidays in Abu Dhabi eat sessions. Ask what happens to an unused session before taking a monthly plan, and ask whether a pause for mocks or travel is permitted.

Nothing here states a position on the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees, which belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to a tutoring page. What a parent should do is ask any provider whether the number quoted is inclusive, and get the answer in writing.
