abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.programmesIntro: Which programme a child lands in determines how forgiving the first term is. These are the IB programmes running in Abu Dhabi schools, read from the point of view of a family arriving mid-cycle.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The most forgiving entry point. Assessment is continuous and reported against the programme's framework rather than against marks, so a new arrival is not immediately measured against a cohort. The adjustment is to inquiry-led learning, which children from examination-led systems find disorienting for a term and then usually prefer.
programmes.countryNote: Parents arriving in Abu Dhabi from systems that test annually often read a PYP report as containing no information. Ask the school to translate it: which skills are secure, which are emerging, and what would change the picture. That conversation costs nothing and usually removes the impulse to buy tutoring in month one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria A to D in each subject, each with published descriptors. This is where a new arrival meets criterion-referenced marking for the first time, and where early marks drop for reasons of format rather than knowledge. Learning to read a descriptor and write to it is a short, high-value intervention worth a handful of sessions.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools differ in whether they run MYP through Year 11 or switch to IGCSE at Year 10, and a mid-cycle arrival may be joining either route. Ask which applies before enrolling, because it changes what the next two years look like and what a transition plan has to prepare for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The least forgiving entry point, particularly in the second year. A candidate joining mid-Diploma inherits internal assessment deadlines already in motion, a prediction window approaching, six subjects at two levels, and the core components. Schools vary considerably in whether they will admit a student mid-Diploma at all, and some will only take a candidate into the first year.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session, and internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and internal assessments are set by each school. A family relocating with a child in the second Diploma year should ask prospective schools for those deadlines before accepting a place, because they determine whether the year is salvageable.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Offered by a small number of Abu Dhabi schools and occasionally a better fit for a late arrival than the full Diploma, because the course load is structured differently. Recognition varies by destination, so a family considering it should ask the school how universities they care about have treated the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: For a relocating family, the CP is worth raising explicitly as an option rather than waiting to be offered it. Some schools present only the Diploma to incoming students and mention the CP only when a Diploma place is declined.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.subjectsIntro: Where a new arrival's marks actually go, described by the shape of the gap rather than by topic. Format and language account for far more early losses than missing content.

subjects.name: Mathematics across the IB programmes
subjects.levels: MYP and DP, HL and SL
subjects.description: Usually the most transferable subject and the one where an arrival is most often ahead on procedure. The gap sits in investigating patterns at MYP and in the exploration and unstructured problems at Diploma level, both of which ask for sustained reasoning rather than correct answers.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content overlap with most national curricula is high, and the gap is the internal assessment: an independent investigation assessed against published criteria. A candidate arriving mid-Diploma has usually never produced one, and it is the single largest piece of unfamiliar work they face.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The adjustment is to extended written reasoning. A new arrival who can produce correct numerical answers will still lose marks until they write the physical reasoning line the mark scheme credits, which is a format habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most command-term sensitive subject in the Diploma, and the one where a student from a recall-heavy system loses most. Describe, explain, suggest and evaluate each have a specific meaning, and accurate answers written to the wrong one collect the knowledge mark only.

subjects.name: English A and English B
subjects.description: Which course a new arrival is placed in is one of the most consequential decisions of the first fortnight, and it is often made quickly on limited evidence. English A assumes a different relationship with literature from English B, and a misplacement costs a year rather than a term.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: History and Economics reward argument and source handling, which a student from a content-recall system may never have been asked for. The gap is structural: a strong first paragraph followed by narrative is the recurring pattern in early work.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: New to almost every arriving child and taught alongside the licensed curriculum. For a student arriving in the upper years with no Arabic, the school's placement decision and expectations should be established in writing early, because this is a genuinely new subject rather than a continuation.

subjects.name: Islamic education
subjects.description: Taught in UAE private schools alongside any licensed international curriculum, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. The content and language of instruction follow published requirements, and a new family should ask the school which stream their child joins and what is expected.

subjects.name: Social and moral studies
subjects.description: Covers UAE social studies and moral education and is new to every arriving child. It is usually the least academically demanding of the three mandatory subjects and the one most often overlooked when a family is planning a catch-up term, which then collides with it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Unfamiliar to almost every mid-Diploma arrival and carrying both points and a failing condition. A candidate joining in the second year may have a school deadline weeks away for work that has not been started, which should be established before the place is accepted rather than afterwards.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.regionsIntro: Where a relocating family ends up living in Abu Dhabi is usually decided by housing and commute rather than by schooling, and it then determines what the school week looks like. These notes are about that.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Shamkha
regions.note: The common landing zone for families relocating on a villa budget, and where mid-year school places appear most often. The school run can add forty minutes each way in term time, which pushes any weekday session to 5pm or later.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with short commutes, frequently chosen for a first year because leases are shorter and the city is easier to learn. Short travel makes frequent short sessions realistic during a settling-in term.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A short list of schools with the shortest school runs in the capital and the longest waiting lists. A family arriving mid-year here is often choosing between a place that is available and the school they wanted.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Bandar
regions.note: Close to the main school cluster and popular with families relocating on a package that includes housing. Demand for mid-year places in this corridor is high, which affects how much choice an arriving family actually has.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A newer catchment with capacity in some year groups and a slow afternoon commute. For a new arrival, available capacity can matter more than reputation in the first year, with a move considered later.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A large mainland catchment with the widest fee spread in the emirate and long travel to the island. This is where the in-home travel premium is least worth paying during a month when a family has not yet learned the roads.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: An hour inland under the same emirate authority, with fewer international-curriculum schools and a much thinner pool of IB specialists on the ground. A relocating family here will find live video is the only route to a Diploma subject specialist.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where most mid-year arrivals land, and the cluster with the most variable policies on admitting students part-way through a two-year course. Ask each school directly whether it will take a mid-Diploma entry and what it expects of one.

schoolClusters.city: Island, Saadiyat and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: Smaller cohorts, longer waiting lists and shorter commutes. A new arrival here may be the only mid-year entrant in a year group, which is isolating socially and means the school forms its view on very little evidence.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Mainland Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A broad fee range with more mid-year capacity and fewer IB programmes. Families relocating at short notice often start here and move later, which is a reasonable strategy if the first school is chosen with that in mind.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.modesIntro: Three ways to buy support during a relocation, and the right one depends on how far through a programme the child has arrived rather than on how worried the family is.

modes.title: Orientation block, three to five sessions
modes.description: Short and deliberately bounded. The work is learning how the new assessment system marks: criterion descriptors in MYP, command terms and internal assessment format in the Diploma. For most arrivals below the second Diploma year this is the whole of what is needed, and buying more in month one is usually waste.
bullets: Explicitly time-limited, with a stated end after a few sessions
Focused on assessment format rather than on content coverage
One marked piece per subject to establish whether a real gap exists
Written summary the family can take to the new school

modes.title: Settling-in term, one or two subjects
modes.description: Weekly work in the one or two subjects where a marked piece showed a genuine content gap rather than a format gap. Costed monthly because a transition term runs for months, and reviewed monthly rather than committed for the year.
bullets: Subjects chosen from marked evidence, not from the report comment
Monthly cost stated at the start and reviewed at week four
Mandatory UAE subject hours counted as fixed load in the plan
Stopping point agreed rather than left open

modes.title: Mid-Diploma triage
modes.description: For a candidate who arrived in the second Diploma year. The honest version starts with what is still possible: which internal assessments can be completed to the school's deadlines, what the prediction window allows, and whether a reduced or deferred route is better. Sometimes the right answer is to raise the Career-related Programme or a repeated year with the school.
bullets: School internal deadlines established in writing before planning
Internal assessment and core components prioritised over revision
Clear statement when a target is not reachable in the time left
Alternatives raised with the school rather than hours sold regardless

sections.heading: The first ninety days, and where the money actually goes
paragraphs: A relocation has a predictable rhythm and tutoring gets bought at the wrong point in it almost every time. Weeks one and two are logistics: enrolment, uniform, transport, documents. Weeks three and four are the first assessments, which produce marks a new arrival cannot yet interpret. Weeks five and six are the first report or parent meeting, which is when the decision to hire a tutor usually gets made. By then the family has paid a deposit on a diagnosis nobody has made.

The cheaper sequence inverts that. In weeks three and four, ask the school a single question per subject: is this mark about content my child has not covered, or about the way the answer was written? Teachers answer this readily and the answer is free. Then, if content genuinely is missing, buy one marked piece per affected subject to confirm it. Only after that does a programme make sense, and by then it is a programme with a target instead of a subscription with a hope.

The expensive scenario is the mid-Diploma arrival, and it is worth separating out because the usual advice does not apply. A candidate who joins the second Diploma year in October has internal assessment deadlines in motion, a prediction window closing, and no runway. Here the first spend should go on the core and internal assessment components rather than on examination revision, because those are the deadlines that cannot be deferred and the marks that are still fully in play.

Across all of these the structural point is the same: the first term's spend should buy information before it buys teaching. Information is cheap, teaching is not, and a family that reverses the order pays for both.

sections.heading: The transition map: what your previous curriculum did and did not prepare for
paragraphs: Different origins produce different gaps, and naming them in advance makes the first marked piece much more informative. A student arriving from an Indian board usually brings strong procedural mathematics and limited experience of extended written explanation. A student from an American system brings continuous assessment habits and may be unused to terminal examinations and to the depth a higher level Diploma subject assumes. A student from a British system arrives closest in assessment culture and furthest in internal assessment experience, since the IB's independent investigations have no precise GCSE equivalent.

Those patterns are tendencies rather than rules, and the point of knowing them is to shorten the diagnosis. If a child from a recall-heavy system produces accurate but uncredited Biology answers, that is the expected pattern and it is a short fix. If a child from a British system struggles with a Chemistry internal assessment, that is also expected and it is a specific piece of teaching. In both cases the family can skip a month of general worry.

The one origin that deserves separate mention is a mid-cycle move within the IB itself, from one IB school to another in a different country. These students look like the easiest cases and frequently are not, because course options differ between schools: a subject taken at higher level in the previous school may only run at standard level in the new one, or not at all. That is a timetable problem with academic consequences and it needs establishing before the place is accepted.

The table below gives typical durations. They are indicative rather than promises, and the only way to know which applies to one child is a marked piece in the subject. Anybody quoting a duration without having seen marked work is estimating from a category, which is useful for planning and worthless as a commitment.

sections.heading: What a settling-in term costs in Abu Dhabi, as a term total
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market advertises; a relocating family needs a term total, because relocation budgets are set in lumps. So this section works from the month and the term rather than from the hour. Bestimate's Dubai rate table converts weekly one-hour sessions into monthly estimates of AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Multiply by three or four for a term, and by the number of subjects.

The hourly figures behind those bands are published. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270; Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above; BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Observed monthly packages are AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Two things inflate a relocation budget unnecessarily. The first is buying three subjects when a marked piece would have shown one. The second is buying in-home delivery during the month when a family has not yet learned the roads and the tutor's travel time is being priced into every hour. In-home one-to-one in the emirate is quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors, and across a settling-in term that premium is a significant line for something that reaches nothing on a mark scheme.

There is also a cost-in-context point relocating families appreciate. School fees are the dominant education line in any relocation budget, and in Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Fee regulation differs by emirate, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authorities approve tuition fees, curricula and assessment methods directly. Ask any prospective school for its approved fee schedule in writing rather than relying on a website figure.

sections.heading: The three UAE subjects nobody warns a relocating family about
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In practice that means a child arriving from abroad into any licensed international curriculum picks up three subjects they have never studied, on top of everything else changing in their life. Relocating families consistently discover this in the second week of term, from the timetable.

KHDA has published the clearest public detail of how this works, for Dubai, and it is worth reading even for an Abu Dhabi family because the structure is instructive. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction.

The language rules are specific too. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for social studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have the appropriate approval from the regulator to teach these subjects, which is a concrete thing a parent can ask about.

Two further details matter for planning. Instructional time for these subjects is calculated based on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means a tutor cannot offer an alternative syllabus for them. Support here is support with the school's own material, or it is nothing.
bullets: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies run alongside any licensed international curriculum
Separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are required in several of these subjects, and combined classes are prohibited
Language of instruction is specified per subject and per group
Mandatory-subject content cannot be varied without prior Ministry permission

sections.heading: Arriving mid-Diploma: what is and is not possible
paragraphs: This is the hardest relocation case in schooling and it deserves a straight answer. A student joining the second year of the Diploma Programme inherits a two-year course with one year gone, internal assessments in progress or already due, a Theory of Knowledge essay and an Extended Essay with school deadlines, and a prediction window that may close within weeks. Schools in Abu Dhabi differ considerably in whether they will accept such a student at all, and the ones that will often set conditions.

The first task is therefore administrative rather than academic. Ask every prospective school, in writing: will you admit a mid-Diploma entry, which subjects at which levels can you actually timetable, what are your internal deadlines for internal assessment and the core, and when do you close predicted grades. Those four answers determine whether the year is salvageable, and they should be obtained before a place is accepted, not after.

Where the answers are workable, the spending priority is clear and counter-intuitive: internal assessment and the core first, examination revision later. Internal assessments carry a fixed share of each subject grade and have hard deadlines; examination content can be built across the remaining months. A family that spends the first two months on revision and then meets an internal assessment deadline with nothing written has spent in the wrong order.

Where the answers are not workable, the honest alternatives are to enter the first Diploma year instead, losing time but gaining a complete course; to consider the Career-related Programme if the school offers it; or to continue the previous qualification where an approved centre in the UAE offers it. All three are legitimate. Selling a mid-Diploma family an intensive programme that cannot meet the deadlines is not, and it is what this part of the market does.

sections.heading: Choosing a school in a city you arrived in last week
paragraphs: Relocating families usually choose a school on availability, commute and fee, in that order, because those are the constraints that bind. That is reasonable. What is worth adding is two pieces of free information most arrivals do not use. The first is the regulator's own published inspection outcome for each school under consideration: in Abu Dhabi the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection results. Read them on the regulator's site rather than on a school's marketing page.

The second is the fee schedule, approved rather than advertised. Fee regulation differs across the country: Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, while Dubai's KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in that emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. Ask each school for its approved schedule in writing, including the extras, because the gap between headline tuition and the total a family actually pays is where relocation budgets break.

For capacity context, Dubai's private sector is expanding: the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Abu Dhabi's market moves on its own schedule, but the regional direction means mid-year availability is better in some communities than a family assumes from a single rejection.

One practical note on sequence: the school choice and the tutoring question are related and should be decided in that order. A family that signs for a school whose timetable cannot deliver the higher level subjects their child needs has created a problem no tutoring resolves. Establish the available courses first, then the support.

sections.heading: Documents, attestation and the paperwork clock
paragraphs: Every relocating family meets the documents process, and the only reliable advice about it is to start earlier than feels necessary. School transfer certificates, previous reports and, for school-leaving qualifications, equivalency and attestation all have their own requirements and their own queues. These are administered by the Ministry of Education and the relevant attestation authority, and no school, university or tutoring service performs or expedites them.

For a child mid-way through school, the immediate documents are the transfer certificate and previous records, which the new school will specify. For a student approaching the end of school, the equivalency route matters. On the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published here, because none has been read on an official source for this project and figures circulating online cannot be verified. Check your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority.

Nothing in this section should be read as implying tutoring is required for equivalency, admission or school progression. These are regulatory processes with published criteria, and presenting academic support as a route through one would be a false-urgency claim about something that does not work that way.

sections.heading: How lessons run during and after a move
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. For a relocating family the practical benefit is continuity: sessions can start while the family is still in the previous country, continue from temporary accommodation, and carry on unchanged when the household finally settles. Nothing in the arrangement depends on an address, which during a move is the point.

Scheduling is deliberately flexible in the first weeks and then fixed. Gulf Standard Time lessons settle around the Abu Dhabi school week once the school run is known: earlier for island and Saadiyat families, 5pm or later for Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City, weekend blocks where weekday evenings are gone. Where a family is still split across time zones, sessions are set against the student's local time rather than ours. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For an arriving family the honest argument is choice rather than price: in the first month you do not know the city, you do not know which tutors are near you, and you have no way to judge who is good. Choosing online means choosing a subject specialist on the strength of their subject rather than on the strength of their postcode, and the in-home market prices the journey at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour anyway.

Two limits stated plainly. Supply for Diploma higher level sciences and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches in this emirate is thin in the autumn term, and where no specialist is free at the hours you need we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral. And where a marked piece shows that no tutoring is needed, which happens more often than this market admits, we say that too.

process.title: Wait two weeks, then ask one question
process.description: Per subject, to the teacher: is this mark about content my child has not covered, or about how the answer was written. The answer is free, immediate and determines everything else. Families who buy a programme before asking it are paying for a diagnosis nobody has made.

process.title: Buy one marked piece per affected subject
process.description: A single session per subject in which a piece of work is marked against the published criteria and read back. That separates a format gap, which takes a few sessions, from a content gap, which takes weeks per topic. The difference across three subjects is substantial money.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: One free trial lesson, on the condition that it is a single lesson, with the person who would actually teach the subject rather than a coordinator. For a new arrival this is also the moment to confirm the tutor knows the programme, the level and the school's internal deadlines.

process.title: Establish the school's internal deadlines
process.description: Internal assessment dates, core component deadlines and the prediction date, in writing. For a mid-Diploma arrival these determine whether the year is salvageable and in what order to spend. For younger arrivals they determine when the pressure actually lands.

process.title: Agree a term total and review it monthly
process.description: A settling-in plan is costed as a monthly figure with a term total stated, and reviewed at week four against marked evidence. Most families should be spending less by month four, not more, and a plan that does not anticipate reducing is a subscription rather than a plan.

process.title: Say when nothing should be bought
process.description: If the marked work shows a transition effect rather than a content gap, the right advice is to do very little and let the term do its work. We say that. If no specialist is free at the hours you need, we offer a different slot, a later start or a referral elsewhere.

whyPoints.title: Transition and content priced separately
whyPoints.description: Weak early marks after a move are usually a format and orientation effect, which costs a few sessions, not a content gap, which costs weeks per topic. Nothing in this market makes that distinction, because the expensive diagnosis is also the more profitable one.

whyPoints.title: Costed as a term, because relocations are
whyPoints.description: Monthly and term totals from Bestimate's rate table with the hourly sources named, rather than a single hourly figure. A relocation budget is set in lumps, and a page that quotes only an hourly rate is answering a question nobody asked.

whyPoints.title: The mandatory UAE subjects named up front
whyPoints.description: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies arrive with the timetable and surprise almost every relocating family. The rules on class organisation, language of instruction and content are quoted from the regulator's published guidance, and content for these subjects cannot be varied without Ministry permission.

whyPoints.title: Straight about arriving mid-Diploma
whyPoints.description: It is the hardest point in the school system to arrive at, and the useful response is four written questions to the school before accepting a place. Where the answers do not work, we name the alternatives rather than selling an intensive programme that cannot meet the deadlines.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through the move itself
whyPoints.description: Lessons run over live video against the student's local time, so they can begin before the family arrives, continue from temporary accommodation and carry on unchanged afterwards. Nothing in the arrangement depends on an address, which during a relocation is the whole point.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims, no outcome statistics
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry, the IB or any board, and says so. There are no satisfaction or attainment figures on this page, because no dataset supports one and an unsourced number is a liability.

faqs.question: My child's first Abu Dhabi report was poor. Should we hire a tutor immediately?
faqs.answer: Ask one free question first, per subject: is this mark about content my child has not covered, or about how the answer was written. A student who has changed country, school system and assessment culture within two months produces weak early marks for reasons that have little to do with ability. A format and orientation gap costs a handful of sessions; a content gap costs weeks per topic. Buying a programme before anyone has made that distinction is how a first term gets expensive without getting better.

faqs.question: What are the three extra subjects on my child's new timetable?
faqs.answer: Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those three, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations, so they run alongside any licensed international curriculum. KHDA's published guidance for Dubai requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and prohibits combined classes for both groups. Ask your school which stream your child joins, what language the lessons are in, and what is expected.

faqs.question: Can a tutor teach my child the Arabic and Islamic studies syllabus?
faqs.answer: Only using the school's own material, and that is a real constraint rather than a preference. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. Schools must also ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from the regulator for those subjects. The practical approach is support with comprehension, vocabulary and study habits around the school's material, and a conversation with the school about expectations for a new arrival.

faqs.question: What does a settling-in term of tutoring cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Work from the term rather than the hour. Bestimate's Dubai rate table gives monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions of AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work; multiply by three or four for a term and by the number of subjects. Observed packages include AED 799 per month for eight online sessions. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and most families should be spending less by month four.

faqs.question: We are relocating with a child in the second year of the IB Diploma. Is that workable?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is the hardest point in the school system to arrive at. Before accepting a place, ask each prospective school in writing whether it admits a mid-Diploma entry, which subjects at which levels it can actually timetable, what its internal deadlines are for internal assessment and the core, and when it closes predicted grades. Those four answers decide whether the year is salvageable. Where they do not work, entering the first Diploma year, the Career-related Programme, or continuing the previous qualification are all legitimate alternatives.

faqs.question: Can lessons start before we physically arrive in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a staged move it is often the best use of the gap. Because lessons run over live video they can begin from your previous country, continue from temporary accommodation, and carry on unchanged once the household settles, with sessions set against the student's local time rather than ours. For a child about to meet a new assessment system, a few orientation sessions before term starts are worth more than the same sessions bought in a panic in week five.

faqs.question: How do IB criteria work compared with the marks my child is used to?
faqs.answer: MYP subjects are assessed against criteria A to D, each with published descriptors, and Diploma internal assessments work the same way. The shift for a new arrival is that a mark is awarded against a described standard rather than against a total of correct answers, so an accurate piece of work can score modestly if it does not address what the descriptor asks for. Learning to read a descriptor and write to it is a short, high-value intervention and usually the first thing worth buying.

faqs.question: Which schools in Abu Dhabi take students mid-year?
faqs.answer: Availability varies by year group, by community and by month, and policies differ between schools a short drive apart. Mid-year capacity tends to be better in the Khalifa City, Al Shamkha, Yas and mainland catchments than on Saadiyat or the island, where waiting lists are longest. Read each school's published inspection outcome on the regulator's own site rather than on its marketing pages, and ask for the approved fee schedule in writing including extras. One rejection is not a reading of the whole market.

faqs.question: Is English language support the same as subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and conflating them wastes a term. A student arriving with strong subject knowledge in another language needs subject-specific academic vocabulary, which is a different job from general English support and a different job again from subject teaching. The sequence that works is school-provided language support alongside targeted work on the vocabulary of one or two subjects, with marked pieces to show which is actually limiting the marks. Ask the school what language provision it offers before buying anything privately.

faqs.question: Should we delay the school choice until we know the city?
faqs.answer: Where you can, decide the school on what it can timetable rather than on where you have found a villa. A school whose timetable cannot deliver the higher level subjects your child needs creates a problem no tutoring resolves, and that is a worse outcome than a longer commute for a year. Establish the available courses and levels first, then the fees in writing, then the commute. Many relocating families start in a school with capacity and move later, which is a reasonable plan if chosen deliberately.

faqs.question: Do we need to do anything about equivalency now?
faqs.answer: For a child mid-way through school, the immediate documents are the transfer certificate and previous records, which the new school specifies. Equivalency matters at the end of school, when a leaving certificate needs recognition inside the UAE, and it is run by the Ministry and the attestation authority rather than by a school or a tutoring service. Start collecting documents earlier than feels necessary, because the process has its own queue, and verify your own requirements on the official pages.

faqs.question: How long does it take for a new arrival to settle academically?
faqs.answer: A term for most, two for a mid-cycle arrival into a demanding year, and that is the shape to plan spending around rather than the shape to fight. The marks in weeks three to six are not a reading of a child; they are a reading of a transition. What helps measurably is a small number of sessions on assessment format, consistency at home, and the school's own support. What usually does not help is three subjects of weekly teaching bought in month one and still running in month six.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two of my children?
faqs.answer: Separately, yes, and the same tutor across two children in the same subject often works well because the material is shared. In the same session, no: a Year 7 arrival and a Diploma candidate are doing unrelated work, and a shared hour short-changes both. Families sometimes ask for this to manage a relocation budget, which is understandable, and the honest answer is that the saving is not real. Two shorter individual sessions are better value than one combined hour.

faqs.question: What should we send you before the first conversation?
faqs.answer: Four things, and the conversation becomes useful immediately. The programme and year group your child has joined, the subjects and levels, the last report or marked piece from the previous school, and the new school's internal deadlines if you have them. If any are unknown, finding them out is the first task. We would rather spend the first conversation establishing whether anything needs buying than quoting hours against a problem nobody has diagnosed.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.closingHeading: Buy information before you buy teaching
abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-for-new-expat-student.closingBody: The cheapest and most useful thing a newly arrived family can do is ask each teacher whether a weak mark is about missing content or about how an answer was written, then buy one marked piece in the subjects where the answer was content. That sequence costs a fraction of a term's programme and tells you whether a programme is needed at all. For a child arriving mid-Diploma, add four written questions to the school about timetabling, internal deadlines and the prediction date before accepting a place. Book a free trial lesson with the subject specialist, and expect an honest answer about whether to spend.

Read them as a shortlist by component rather than by distance: the question that decides a match is whether this tutor marks the paper your child is losing marks on, not how far away they happen to live.

intro.heading: The problem with searching by radius
paragraphs: A search for an IB tutor near me in Abu Dhabi is usually driven by logistics rather than pedagogy. School finishes somewhere between half past two and half past three. There is a drive home. There is homework, and in most households there is a younger sibling with a different timetable. Inside that window a parent is looking for something that will not collapse the evening, and "near" feels like the variable that protects it. For in-home tutoring it genuinely is: a tutor who lives twenty minutes away can hold a half past four slot, and one who lives forty minutes away cannot.

The difficulty is that proximity and specialism are close to independent of each other. The Diploma Programme is six subjects at two levels with eight or nine pieces of assessed coursework, and the help a student needs is almost always narrower than a subject. A Chemistry HL candidate losing twelve marks on organic mechanisms needs a tutor who marks organic mechanisms. The chance that such a person lives within twenty minutes of Al Reef, is free at half past six, and is not already booked by three other families in the same compound is not high. Searching by radius quietly converts a subject requirement into whoever is available.

Abu Dhabi makes this sharper than most cities because the emirate is spread across three belts that do not behave like one city. The island holds long-established schools and short internal distances, but pickup queues and parking eat the time that distance saves. The Khalifa City, Shakhbout City, Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach corridor is the densest concentration of international provision in the emirate and has a genuinely short internal commute. The newer mainland communities - Al Shamkha, Al Falah, Al Reef, Al Samha, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Baniyas - are where the drives get long and where the local tutor pool thins out at exactly the same time.

Private schools across all three belts are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Families moving in from Dubai sometimes assume the Knowledge and Human Development Authority covers them; it does not. One practical consequence is that school listings, inspection reports and fee rules all sit with a different authority, and so does the school calendar your tutoring plan has to fit around.

IB Gram's answer is to remove distance from the equation entirely. Tutoring for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, and we do not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. What that buys is a different shortlist. Instead of the three tutors willing to drive to Al Samha at seven, you are choosing from the tutors who teach that subject at that level, and the slot is set by your child's school run rather than by somebody else's traffic. The rest of this page is the arithmetic behind that claim: drive times by community, availability by subject, the permit position, and what the local market charges for the travel you would otherwise be funding.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: A request for a tutor near you can come from any stage of the IB, and the stages behave differently when you remove travel from the plan. Younger students benefit from shorter, more frequent sessions, which only works if nobody is driving. Diploma students need a specialist for a specific component, which is where the radius hurts most.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-based learning with no external assessment, so the useful work is fluency: reading accuracy, number facts, written structure and the habit of explaining a method. Younger children concentrate better in thirty to forty-five minutes than in an hour, and two short sessions a week beat one long one. That pattern is only affordable in time terms when nobody has to travel to deliver it.
programmes.countryNote: Primary enquiries in Abu Dhabi cluster in the newer mainland communities, where families are furthest from the island schools and least willing to add a second car journey to the evening. Two thirty-minute sessions on a shared screen, immediately after the school run, is the shape that survives a term in Al Reef or Al Shamkha.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject on an eight-point scale, converted to a 1-7 grade by the school. The marking is the thing families cannot interpret, and a tutor who has read the school's criteria descriptors is worth more than one who merely knows the content. MYP 4 and 5 also carry the personal project and the Diploma subject decision in the same eighteen months.
programmes.countryNote: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor produces most of our Abu Dhabi MYP work, partly because the IB continuum schools sit there and partly because criteria-based marking first becomes decisive in MYP 4. Sessions here can genuinely start at half past four, which makes a weekly rhythm easy to hold.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. This is where the radius problem is most acute: the help needed is component-specific, the specialist pool for Higher Level sciences and Paper 3 papers is thin in every market, and the student has the least spare time in the week to absorb a long commute.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma cohorts sit the May session and the school builds its internal deadlines backwards from it. Confirm the examination window and results dates with the school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from a tutoring site. What a tutor can plan around confidently is the school's own mock window, usually between December and February of DP2.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Availability is the honest subject of this page, so the grid below is organised by how findable a specialist actually is rather than by syllabus order. Each entry names the level, what the component load looks like, and whether the pool for it is deep or thin in this time zone.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Two papers at SL, three at HL, plus a 20-mark exploration. The SL pool is the deepest of any DP subject; the HL Paper 3 pool is noticeably thinner, because marking two long multi-part problems well is a narrower skill than teaching calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with a calculator or software assumed throughout. Marks are lost in interpretation rather than method: a correct regression with no sentence about what the gradient means in context scores half of what it could.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two papers plus a 20% scientific investigation. Higher Level Physics specialists are in demand across the whole Gulf at the same points in the year, so this is the subject where a match most often takes a few days rather than a day.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Structure and reactivity across two papers plus the investigation. Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the heaviest concentration of lost marks at Higher Level, and the pool tightens sharply in the weeks before school mocks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content with heavy command-term weighting. The pool is reasonable at both levels, and the most requested work is criterion-based feedback on the scientific investigation rather than content teaching.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries as the internal assessment, diagrams expected throughout, and at Higher Level a Paper 3 that rewards calculation plus evaluation. Finding someone who marks Paper 3 specifically is harder than finding an economics teacher.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, comparative essay, individual oral, and at Higher Level a 1,200-1,500 word essay. Paper 1 support is widely available; the Higher Level essay is a narrower specialism and often best handled as a short block.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Literature at A level and language acquisition at B level, with oral components to prepare. This is the one subject group where a UAE-based tutor has a real advantage, because the school context and the parallel Ministry requirement both matter.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study papers and a research-based internal assessment. Marks go missing where a tool is applied mechanically without a judgement about the business in the stimulus material.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: System fundamentals and computational thinking, with a developed solution as the internal assessment. Students build something that works and then under-document the design decisions the criteria reward.

abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi community by community, and the slot each one supports
abu-dhabi/ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: Online delivery means your community does not limit who can teach your child, but it does decide what time the session can start. These are the drive-time realities our Abu Dhabi families describe, and the slots that actually survive a full term in each.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with school runs often under fifteen minutes. A half past three start is genuinely workable here, which makes it one of the few communities where a session can finish before dinner.

regions.name: Al Maryah Island and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Short central runs and a dense cluster of working parents. Sessions tend to be booked in the earliest slots so that the evening is left intact for homework.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Island distances are short, but pickup queues and parking take the time the distance saves. Five o'clock is the slot most families here settle on.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: The tightest school cluster in the emirate with a ten to fifteen minute internal run. Half past four works, and this is where weekly rhythms hold most reliably through a term.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Ten minutes from Khalifa City and next to long-established IB continuum provision. Many students here come to us mid-MYP, when criteria-based marking first starts to decide grades.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: One causeway run of twenty to twenty-five minutes to most schools. Five or half past five is typical, and families with two children in different schools usually need the later end of that.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer housing and a longer run back from island schools, so six o'clock is the common starting point. A noticeable share of students here arrive mid-year from other curricula.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Thirty to forty minutes each way at the afternoon peak. Half past six is realistic; anything earlier gets cancelled by traffic within a month of booking it.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Samha and Baniyas
regions.note: The longest afternoon runs to island schools, commonly forty minutes or more. These are the communities where the local tutor pool is thinnest and the case for removing travel from the plan is strongest.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: Large mixed communities with a wide spread of curricula. Diploma enquiries here often come from students who entered the DP from a national or Indian curriculum and need the assessment format taught from scratch.

schoolClusters.city: The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of international provision in the emirate, with IB continuum schools alongside British schools offering the Diploma next to A-Levels. Short internal distances here are why this corridor supports earlier session slots than anywhere else in Abu Dhabi.

sections.heading: What "near me" actually buys, and what it costs
paragraphs: Proximity buys three real things. It buys a tutor who can physically be present, which matters for very young children and for students who genuinely will not engage with a screen. It buys local knowledge: a tutor teaching in Abu Dhabi knows which schools set which internal deadlines and how the emirate's term dates fall. And it buys a kind of accountability that some families value, where the person teaching your child is someone you have met in your own living room.

It costs three things in return, and they are rarely itemised. The first is choice. A twenty-minute radius around Al Samha contains a small number of IB tutors and a smaller number who teach the subject and level you need. The second is money: the in-home band in this market runs AED 180-500 an hour, against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and a share of that gap is the driving. The third is reliability. A session that depends on a car arriving at half past six in Abu Dhabi afternoon traffic will be cancelled several times a term, and the cancellations cluster in the weeks when they hurt most.

The trade only looks obvious once you decide what the tutoring is for. If the job is homework supervision and company while a Year 7 student works, proximity is worth a lot and specialism is worth little. If the job is finding the eleven marks disappearing from Physics Paper 2 extended response, specialism is worth almost everything and proximity is worth nothing at all, because the diagnosis happens on a shared screen with the student's own script open.

IB Gram only does the second job, which is why we deliver online and say so before anything else. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address, and in-home visits in Abu Dhabi are not something we sell at any price; that service exists only in India. The comparison below is the one we give parents who ask us to justify it.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi school run, and what it does to a half past four session
paragraphs: Most private schools in the emirate release students between about half past two and half past three. Everything after that is geography. The island is compact, but the delay there is not distance: it is the pickup queue and the parking, which routinely add twenty minutes to a five-minute journey. The Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor has the shortest real-world school run in Abu Dhabi, because the schools and the housing are in the same place. The mainland communities have the longest, and they get longer at the afternoon peak.

The practical effect is that the same nominal slot means different things in different communities. A half past four session is comfortable in Khalifa City, tight on Saadiyat, and unrealistic in Al Reef. Families who book the slot that sounds convenient rather than the slot that matches the drive lose the first month to late starts, and then conclude that tutoring does not work for them. It is worth being pessimistic about the drive when choosing the time, because the slot you can keep is worth more than the slot you would prefer.

The second thing the calendar does is seasonal. Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier each year and now falls inside the spring term, which is also the window in which most Abu Dhabi schools run Diploma mocks. School days shorten during Ramadan, which frees the afternoon, but concentration moves to after Iftar for many families. Sessions can shift to a post-Iftar slot for the month and move back afterwards; what does not work is pretending the month is the same as any other and then cancelling half of it.

Because our delivery is online, the latest workable slot is set by the student's stamina rather than by a tutor's drive home. That is the one scheduling advantage worth naming plainly: a nine o'clock session in Al Samha is a reasonable request to us and an unreasonable one to anybody who would have to get there.

sections.heading: Why the subject you need is the one nobody local teaches
paragraphs: Scarcity in IB tutoring is not random. It follows the assessment. Standard Level Mathematics is taught by a large number of people because the content is widely held and the papers are conventional. Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, which is two extended multi-part problems, is taught well by far fewer, because it requires someone who has marked that paper type and knows how partial credit falls across the sub-parts. The same pattern repeats in every subject group: the general version is abundant and the component-specific version is thin.

Then the calendar concentrates it. Diploma mocks in Abu Dhabi usually fall between December and February, and the same few weeks see Higher Level science and Paper 3 specialists booked out across the Gulf simultaneously. A family searching in November has a wide choice. The same family searching in January has a narrow one, at a higher price, with a longer wait. Nothing about this is specific to one provider; it is the shape of demand in a market where every school's internal calendar runs off the same session.

The group where scarcity is structural rather than seasonal is the arts. Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film are thin in every market we operate in, and a tutoring site that implies otherwise is telling you something about its marketing rather than its roster. Our position on those subjects is to say no when we cannot cover them properly and to tell a family when that changes, because placing a generalist on a Visual Arts comparative study wastes a term that the student does not have.

Where a UAE-based tutor does carry a genuine advantage is Arabic. Arabic A and Arabic B students in Abu Dhabi are usually also meeting the Ministry requirement for Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, and a tutor inside the system understands how those two bodies of work interact in one week. For that subject we prioritise UAE-based tutors deliberately. For Physics HL we do not, because the component skill matters more than the postcode.

sections.heading: Checking that a tutor near you is permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of pages in this market either skip the subject or imply it is optional. It is not. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. The official service is named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days.

The eligible categories are broader than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. That last pair is worth noticing when a very low hourly rate is quoted to you, because a permit says a person may tutor legally; it says nothing about whether they can teach Higher Level Chemistry. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted as unverified.

There is a separate regime for anything with premises and staff. In Dubai, an institute needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. This is why a claim that tutors carry the approval of a Dubai education authority should stop a conversation: that permit is issued to institutions with a physical site, not as a badge an individual or an online platform can carry.

IB Gram is independent. We hold no approval, accreditation, licence or registration from ADEK, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any examination board, and we would not claim one. What we can tell you is what to ask for and where to verify it, which is the table below.

sections.heading: The one option to rule out: a tutor at your child's own school
paragraphs: Among tutors near you, the most tempting is the one who already teaches your child. They know the student, the cohort, the internal deadlines and the marking. Parents ask for this constantly and it is the single arrangement we will not help with, for reasons that are both regulatory and practical.

On the regulatory side, Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Both of these should be verified against the current policy documents directly rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one. Treat them as the reason to ask the question rather than as the final word on it.

On the practical side, the conflict is obvious once stated. The person marking your child's internal assessment should not be paid by you to improve it. If the grade goes up, nobody can tell whether the teaching or the marking moved, and the student cannot tell either. If a dispute arises about a predicted grade, the family has no independent voice to appeal to. An outside tutor with no stake in the grade can be blunt about a draft in a way an invested teacher cannot.

What a school teacher is genuinely useful for is free. Ask the subject teacher which component is costing marks and what the internal deadline calendar looks like for the next term. That conversation costs nothing, takes ten minutes, and makes any tutoring you then arrange substantially more accurate.

sections.heading: What a match actually involves, and how long it takes
paragraphs: Matching is the step most providers describe in a sentence and most families judge a provider on. The input that makes it fast is a document rather than a conversation: the most recent marked paper, or the returned internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments on it. From a marked script a specialist can usually name the failure pattern before the first session, which means the trial lesson is spent testing a hypothesis instead of gathering history.

Times vary by subject and by season, and the table earlier on this page gives the honest spread. Standard Level Mathematics is usually a two-day match. Higher Level Physics in January is not. Where the wait is real, we would rather give a date than fill the slot, because the cost of a mismatched tutor is not the money; it is the six weeks a family spends hoping it improves before admitting it has not.

Occasionally the only suitable specialist for a narrow component sits outside the Gulf time zone, most often in India, which is an hour and a half ahead of Gulf Standard Time. That moves a session earlier in the Abu Dhabi evening rather than later. We say so at the point of matching rather than after, because a family who agreed to half past eight and then discovers it has to be seven has been told something late that should have been said first.

The trial lesson is the real test and it is free, with no payment taken before it happens. It is a working session, not a sales call: the tutor teaches the component the script identified and finishes by saying what they would do over the next six weeks and in what order. If the match is wrong after it, we change the tutor rather than defend the first choice.

sections.heading: Comparing two quotes without comparing two different things
paragraphs: Hourly rates in this market are not comparable as printed, because they describe different products. AED 60 an hour from a university student, AED 200 from a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 270 from an IB specialist and AED 450 from a named tutor are four different transactions. The published bands for 2026 run roughly: budget online AED 45-150, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; qualified subject tutor online AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; specialists AED 200-450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate 200-450+; and premium named tutors AED 500-650, BartyED publishing AED 650.

Before comparing the numbers, make them describe the same thing. Ask how many students are in the session, because a group rate and a one-to-one rate differ by a factor of three or four. Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, since ninety-minute sessions are common. Ask who marks the work between sessions and whether that time is included. Ask whether the quoted figure is inclusive of any applicable tax, and get the answer in writing; we do not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees on this page because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to us.

Then ask the questions that are not about money. Which subject and level does the tutor actually teach, and which components have they marked? Will the same tutor take every session, or is the booking with an agency that allocates whoever is free? What happens if the first match is wrong - a replacement, or a refund argument? Is there a written note after each session? Does the provider hold a MoHRE permit for the individual teaching, and will they show it?

One final warning about the top of the market. Examiner status is used heavily in tutoring marketing and is rarely evidenced. We do not describe tutors as examiners for the boards unless current status can be shown, and we would not use examiner status to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists. If a page is charging a premium for that claim, ask what the claim is based on.

sections.heading: Where the regulator fits, and what it does not cover
paragraphs: Parents sometimes hope that a regulator vets tutors the way it vets schools. It does not, and understanding the split saves money. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and publishes inspection outcomes. Dubai's schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate. Sharjah's sit with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, as does Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

All of those bodies regulate schools. None of them accredits a tutoring platform. The individual tutor sits under the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime instead, and a physical institute in Dubai sits under a separate educational services permit. So when a tutoring page tells you its tutors are approved by an education authority, the claim is either describing a school permit it does not hold or inventing a status that does not exist for its category.

What the regulator is genuinely useful for is checking a school. If a tutoring provider names schools it works with, those schools should appear on the authority's own listing, and the current inspection report should be read there. We deliberately do not publish inspection ratings on these pages, because a rating copied second-hand ages badly and the authority's own site is one click away. The same applies to the federal position on curriculum: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The honest summary is short. Use the regulator to verify schools. Use the ministry permit to verify an individual tutor. Use a marked paper and a trial lesson to verify teaching. Nothing else in this market verifies anything.
