In a market where completed internal assessments are openly advertised, that boundary protects the student from a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: Does it matter where my child's IB tutor is based if the lessons are online?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma work it matters much less than the subject match. What the tutor needs is the component skill: someone who has marked Paper 3, or who knows what criterion D of a scientific investigation is asking for. Where location does matter is the clock and the context. A tutor in the Gulf shares your evening, so the slot is simple. A tutor an hour and a half ahead shifts the session earlier. And for Arabic A and Arabic B, a UAE-based tutor genuinely understands how the Diploma course and the Ministry requirement interact in the same week, which is why we prioritise one there.

faqs.question: How do I check whether an IB tutor advertising near me holds a UAE tutoring permit?
faqs.answer: Ask them to show it. The private tutor work permit is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free of charge and valid for two years, through the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing on the ministry's app, website and e-services system. A tutor holding one can produce it. If the answer is that the agency handles it, ask which named individual the permit covers. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so ignore any specific figure quoted at you.

faqs.question: I live in Al Reef. Can I find a Physics Higher Level tutor nearby?
faqs.answer: Probably not quickly, and that is the clearest argument on this page. Al Reef sits forty minutes or more from the island schools at the afternoon peak, which shrinks the set of tutors willing to travel there, and Higher Level Physics is one of the thinner specialisms in the whole Gulf. The combination means a local search usually ends with a general science tutor rather than a Physics specialist. Online, the shortlist is everyone who teaches Physics at Higher Level, and the session can start at seven without anybody driving. Expect two to four working days for the match, and longer in the weeks before school mocks.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after school in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on your community. Most private schools release between about half past two and half past three. On Al Reem Island a half past three start is workable. Inside the island, pickup and parking push it to a quarter to four or later, and five o'clock is the common choice. In Khalifa City and Shakhbout City, half past four works. From Saadiyat or Al Raha Beach, five o'clock. From Al Shamkha or Mohammed Bin Zayed City, half past six. From Al Reef, Al Samha or Baniyas, seven. Pick the time that survives a bad traffic day rather than the one you would prefer.

faqs.question: How long does it usually take to be matched with a tutor in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Two to five working days for most Diploma subjects, with the spread driven by subject, level and the time of year. Standard Level Mathematics is usually two days. Higher Level Physics, Higher Level Chemistry and Paper 3 Economics take longer, and in the weeks before school mocks they take longer still, because every school in the Gulf runs mocks off the same May session. The arts are the exception at a week or more. Sending a marked paper with the enquiry shortens all of these, because the match is then made against a component rather than against a subject label.

faqs.question: Which Diploma components are the hardest to staff with a real specialist?
faqs.answer: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Film are the thinnest group in every market we work in, and we would rather decline than place a generalist on a comparative study or a process portfolio. After the arts, the difficulty is component-specific rather than subject-specific: Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Economics Paper 3 and the Higher Level English essay are each narrower specialisms than the subjects they sit inside. Sciences at Higher Level are available but squeeze hard around mocks. Standard Level Mathematics, Biology and Business Management are the easiest to cover at short notice.

faqs.question: If the tutor is in another time zone, what does that do to our lesson slot?
faqs.answer: Usually it moves the session earlier in the Abu Dhabi evening rather than later. The specialists we most often draw on outside the Gulf sit in India, which is an hour and a half ahead of Gulf Standard Time, so a session that is eight in the evening for you is half past nine for them. That is workable once or twice a week and unworkable as a nine o'clock slot. We tell you at the point of matching that the tutor sits outside the Gulf, so you can decide before agreeing a time rather than discovering the constraint in week three.

faqs.question: Do you add a travel charge if the tutor is further away?
faqs.answer: No, because nobody travels. Every session for an Abu Dhabi family runs one-to-one over live video, so there is no mileage, no waiting time and no minimum session length imposed to make a journey worthwhile. That last point is worth noticing: in-home tutoring in this market is often sold in two-hour blocks because an hour does not justify the drive, which is why the monthly in-home packages advertised here run AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. Online, a single focused hour is a sensible purchase, and a thirty-minute follow-up is too.

faqs.question: How does a shortened Ramadan school day change the tutoring timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and now falls inside the spring term, which overlaps the window when many Abu Dhabi schools run Diploma mocks. School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, but for a lot of households concentration genuinely sits after Iftar. We move the slot for the month and move it back afterwards. The thing that does not work is leaving the timetable unchanged and then losing half the month to cancellations, which costs more continuity than the shift ever would.

faqs.question: We travel between Abu Dhabi and abroad often. Can the same tutor continue?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because delivery is online, the only thing that changes when the family moves is the clock. The same tutor keeps the plan, the error log and the marked work, which is the part that would be lost in a new search. Families who spend summers in another country commonly keep a reduced schedule running through it, and families relocating mid-year avoid the gap that normally opens between leaving one tutor and finding another. For a permanent move out of the UAE, the plan continues with a recalculated slot rather than starting again.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who teaches at a school near us a better choice?
faqs.answer: Not if it is your child's own school. Abu Dhabi professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the ministry permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same arrangement; both are worth verifying against the current policy documents. The practical objection stands on its own: the person marking the work should not be paid by you to improve it, because then nobody can tell whether the teaching or the marking moved. A teacher at a different school carries no such conflict.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for a tutor, to get a useful answer fastest?
faqs.answer: Four things. The subject and the level, written as the school writes it, since Higher and Standard Level are different assessments. A photograph of the most recent marked paper or returned internal assessment draft, with the teacher's comments visible. The school's next deadline that matters, whether that is an internal assessment date or the mock window. And your community, so the slot is set against a realistic drive. With those four, a specialist can usually name the failure pattern before the trial lesson, which is the difference between a diagnostic first session and an introductory one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two IB subjects for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and Physics is the most common genuine pairing, because the overlap in algebraic technique is real. Chemistry and Biology is plausible at Standard Level and rarely sensible at Higher Level, where the component skills diverge. Pairing a science with a humanities subject almost never works well. Where a single tutor can cover both, the continuity is a real advantage: one error log, one plan, one person who notices that a Maths problem is actually a reading problem. Where it cannot, two shorter sessions with specialists beat one generalist hour.

faqs.question: What happens if the match turns out to be wrong after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: We change the tutor. The honest reason this matters is that families do not act on a bad match quickly; they wait, hoping the next session is better, and the cost of that patience is measured in weeks of a two-year programme. So the review point is set in advance at six weeks, against fresh marked work rather than against impressions. If the component that was leaking marks is still leaking them, the plan changes or the tutor does. No payment is taken before the first trial lesson, and a replacement is not treated as a complaint to be defended.

faqs.question: Does ADEK approve or register tutoring companies in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; it does not accredit tutoring providers. Individual tutors sit under the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit regime instead. In Dubai, an institute with physical premises needs a separate educational services permit from the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. So any tutoring page claiming to be approved by an education authority is either describing a school or institute permit it does not hold, or inventing a status that does not exist for its category. IB Gram holds no regulator approval and does not claim one.

abu-dhabi/ib-university-admissions-guida.tutorsIntro: The tutors here work on the academic half of an application: the subject grades a conditional offer will be written against, the higher level courses a degree programme requires, and the written components a candidate produces themselves with feedback rather than assistance.

intro.heading: Three separate processes that families treat as one
paragraphs: An Abu Dhabi Diploma candidate heading to university is moving through three processes at once, and almost all the confusion in this area comes from treating them as a single thing. The first is the application itself, which is read by universities and decided on predicted grades, written work and references. The second is the Diploma, which produces the real grades months later and determines whether a conditional offer is met. The third applies only to recognition inside the UAE: the Ministry of Education equivalency and attestation route, which is an administrative process run by the authority and entirely separate from any university's admissions decision.

Each has a different owner, a different timetable and a different failure mode. The application is owned by the candidate and the school's counselling team. The grades are owned by the examiners. Equivalency is owned by the Ministry. A tutor owns none of them, and the honest description of academic support here is narrow: it addresses the subject grades the offer will be written against, and nothing else. Any page implying a tutoring service can influence an admissions decision is describing something that does not exist.

The sequencing is the part that catches families. Predicted grades have to be finalised before the application that carries them, so the evidence period behind a prediction closes earlier than most households expect. The earliest UK deadline sits in mid-October of the second Diploma year and the main one in mid-January, which means many Abu Dhabi schools form predictions in the autumn. By the time a family is thinking seriously about applications, the academic evidence behind them is often already fixed.

Subject choice runs even earlier. Degree programmes in engineering, medicine, physical sciences and economics commonly specify higher level subjects and, in mathematics, a particular course. Those requirements are published by each institution on its own admissions pages and they are revised. A candidate who chooses standard level Chemistry in Year 11 has narrowed their options for a year before anyone notices, and no amount of later guidance reopens that door for the same application cycle.

Academic support is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we do not do at all is write applications: no personal statement, no supplemental essay, no reference. Those must be the candidate's own work, and the reasons are both ethical and practical, since admissions offices increasingly read for voice and inconsistency between a written piece and the rest of a file is noticed. What academic support does reach is the one column an offer is written against: the higher level subject grade. A candidate holding a conditional offer at a particular grade in Chemistry needs that grade, and marked work against the published criteria is how it is pursued. Everything else on this page is reading rather than advising, and it is framed that way on purpose, because a tutoring service that drifts into speaking for a university or for the Ministry has started inventing authority it does not hold.

abu-dhabi/ib-university-admissions-guida.programmesIntro: Admissions outcomes are shaped at each stage of the IB continuum, not only in the final year. These are the stages in Abu Dhabi schools and what each contributes to an application file.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The final MYP or IGCSE profile is the evidence a Diploma teacher inherits and, on the British equivalency track, the IGCSE certificate itself carries administrative weight later. Students and families treat these years as preliminary; the recognition process does not, since the five counted subject passes come from this stage.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Abu Dhabi school runs MYP to Year 11 rather than IGCSE, families intending to use the British equivalency track should ask the school early what certificates their child will actually hold, because the counted subjects on that track are GCSE or IGCSE passes.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with at least three at higher level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity and service. Universities read the higher level choices as the academic signal and write conditions against the subject grades. The core components appear on the file and are read, particularly the Extended Essay subject where it aligns with the intended degree.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates normally sit the May session, and schools close predictions at different points in the autumn or early winter. Ask the coordinator for the prediction date in the first week of the second year, since it is the hinge on which the academic half of an application turns.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP candidates hold DP course grades plus a career-related study and a reflective project, and the qualification is read differently from the full Diploma by different institutions. That is a question to put to each destination university rather than to infer, and it should be asked before the application rather than after an offer is refused.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of Abu Dhabi schools offer the CP. Recognition for UAE equivalency and for overseas admission both need checking directly, and the school's counselling team is better placed than any tutoring service to describe how a particular university has treated the qualification in the past.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, the alternative route
programmes.description: Worth understanding because it is the comparison most Abu Dhabi families are implicitly making and because it is the track the published UAE equivalency rules describe most precisely. On that track the requirement includes one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five GCSE or IGCSE passes.
programmes.countryNote: Families weighing a Diploma against A Levels for UAE recognition should read the Ministry's own published requirements for each track rather than relying on comparison tables found on tutoring sites, several of which publish the wrong subject count.

abu-dhabi/ib-university-admissions-guida.subjectsIntro: Admissions requirements are usually written in terms of specific higher level subjects, so subject choice is an admissions decision disguised as a timetable decision. These notes describe what each subject signals and what it closes off.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematics course most commonly specified for engineering, physical sciences, mathematics and quantitative economics, and sometimes required at higher level. Candidates who take the alternative course and later apply to those programmes find the requirement is published and non-negotiable, so check each course page before choosing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Accepted widely for social sciences, business, design and many life-science routes, and genuinely the better fit for some candidates. The risk is only in assuming it is interchangeable with the other course for quantitative degrees, which the published requirements frequently say it is not.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Commonly required at higher level for medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and chemical engineering. It is the single most consequential subject choice in the Diploma for admissions purposes, because the number of programmes that require it at higher level is large and the substitution options are few.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Specified at higher level by many engineering and physics programmes, often alongside mathematics. Candidates aiming at engineering who take Physics at standard level should read the requirements of their target courses carefully, because the pairing requirement is where applications are quietly ruled out.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Required or strongly expected for life sciences and several health routes, and accepted at standard level by some programmes that require Chemistry at higher level. The combination rules vary by institution, which is why the course page rather than a general guide is the document to read.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Rarely a formal requirement and frequently a useful signal, particularly where the Extended Essay is written in the subject. Candidates should not assume it substitutes for a mathematics requirement on a quantitative programme, which is a common and costly misreading.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Carries weight for English-language proficiency purposes at many institutions, though each sets its own policy and some require a separate test regardless. Ask the specific university what it accepts, since this is one of the most variable requirements in the field.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Read by admissions offices more often than candidates expect, particularly where it is written in the subject of the intended degree. A well-chosen research question aligned with the application is a genuine asset; one written in an unrelated subject is neutral rather than harmful.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Part of the core points and occasionally referenced in interviews for discussion-based courses. Its admissions value is indirect, through the points it contributes and through the habits of argument it builds, both of which show up elsewhere in a file.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE social studies alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools. They are not usually part of an overseas application, but they occupy timetable hours during application season, and on the British equivalency track Arabic and Islamic education are explicitly not counted among the five required subject passes.

sections.heading: What a university application is actually assessed on
paragraphs: An application file has a small number of elements and each is assessed on something different, which is worth separating because families tend to over-invest in the element they can most easily buy help with. Predicted grades are assessed as a professional judgement from the school about likely attainment. Subject and level choices are assessed against published requirements, mechanically, and either satisfy them or do not. Written work is assessed for argument, specificity and voice. The reference is assessed as corroboration.

The mechanical elements are the ones where applications quietly fail, and they fail early. A candidate who does not hold the required higher level subject is ruled out regardless of how strong everything else is, and no amount of guidance in the final year reopens that. This is the single most important thing for a Year 11 family in Abu Dhabi to understand: the most consequential admissions decision your child will make is their Diploma subject selection, made two years before any application exists.

The judgement elements behave differently. A prediction can be short of a requirement and the application still proceeds, with the offer either not made or made at a level the candidate must then reach. In holistic systems a weaker element can be offset by a stronger one. That is where the written work earns its place, and it is also where the temptation to buy help is strongest and the integrity line sharpest.

The honest summary is that academic support affects one column of the table below and reads the rest with you. Nothing we do influences an admissions committee, and no tutoring service should imply otherwise. The university decides, the examiners decide the grade, and the Ministry decides recognition inside the UAE.

sections.heading: UAE recognition: the Ministry of Education equivalency route
paragraphs: For study or employment recognition inside the UAE, a school-leaving certificate goes through the Ministry of Education's equivalency process, which is separate from and additional to any university's own admissions decision. It is an administrative process run by the authority. IB Gram does not perform it, does not guarantee any outcome from it, and nothing on this page should be read as a route through it. What this page can do is set out what has been published, name what has not, and point you at the official channel.

On the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The published article covering these requirements does not mention EmSAT and states no IB points threshold.

That last point is the one to be careful about. No IB points figure for equivalency appears on this page, because none has been read on the Ministry's own pages or on an emirate attestation authority's own page for this project. Figures circulate online; publishing one without an official source would be exactly the error one competitor has already made with the subject count. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority, and ask your school's counselling team what it has seen in practice.

sections.heading: The application calendar, counted backwards
paragraphs: The sequence matters more than any individual date, so it is worth laying out in reverse. At the end sits the real Diploma result, which for Abu Dhabi candidates normally follows the May session and determines whether a conditional offer is met. Before that sit the offers themselves, made across the winter and spring. Before those sit the application deadlines: the earliest UK deadline in mid-October of the second year and the main one in mid-January, with North American deadlines spread across the same window and UAE institutions setting their own.

Before the deadlines sits the date the school closes predicted grades, because a prediction has to exist before the application that carries it. That is the hinge, and it is the date families most often fail to ask about. A school supporting applications to the mid-October deadline is forming predictions in September on evidence largely generated in the first Diploma year. A school working to mid-January usually closes predictions after the mock window.

Before that sits the evidence window, which is the only part a candidate controls, and before that sits subject selection in Year 11, which is the part that determines whether the application is possible at all. Reading the sequence this way makes the priorities obvious: subject choice first, evidence second, written work third, and the deadline itself is merely the point by which the earlier work has to be done.

One practical instruction for every Abu Dhabi Diploma family: in the first week of the second year, ask the coordinator in writing for the prediction date, the internal deadlines for the Extended Essay and internal assessments, and the counselling team's own application milestones. Those four dates, on one page, prevent most of the avoidable problems in this area.

sections.heading: Subject choice as an admissions constraint
paragraphs: The most consequential admissions decision in the Diploma is made before the Diploma starts, and it is made with very little information. A Year 11 student picks three higher level subjects, and that choice either satisfies the published requirements of the degrees they will apply to or quietly rules several of them out. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy routes commonly require Chemistry at higher level. Engineering and physics programmes commonly require Physics and mathematics, often at higher level. Quantitative economics and mathematics degrees frequently specify Analysis and Approaches.

The mathematics course question is the sharpest version of this, because the two IB mathematics courses are genuinely different subjects and many programmes name one of them. A candidate in Applications and Interpretation applying to a degree that requires Analysis and Approaches at higher level has met a published requirement they cannot satisfy, and the application does not survive it. That is not a matter of persuasion or of a strong personal statement.

The correct action is unglamorous and takes an evening. Open the admissions page for each specific course under consideration, read the subject requirements as published, and write them down. Do this before the subject selection form is signed, not afterwards. Requirements are revised and vary between institutions offering apparently identical degrees, so a general guide is not a substitute for the course page, and neither is a tutoring site's comparison table.

Where a choice has already been made and is restrictive, the realistic options are to widen the target list, to consider a foundation or pathway route where the institution offers one, or to look at systems with more flexible entry. All three are legitimate and all three are better than discovering the constraint in January. The school's counselling team is the right partner for that conversation; a tutor's role stops at the subject grade.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi applicants most often lose ground
paragraphs: The first and largest failure is the missed requirement, described above. The second is a late start on predicted-grade evidence, where a family engages in November with a prediction formed in September. Both are timing failures rather than ability failures, and both are preventable with two questions asked at the start of the year.

The third is generic written work. Admissions offices read a very large number of essays and the ones that do nothing are the ones that could have been written by anybody about anything: a stated passion, a list of activities, a conclusion about wanting to make a difference. Specificity is the entire currency here. One concrete piece of work the candidate actually did, described precisely, outperforms three paragraphs of enthusiasm, and that is a writing lesson rather than an admissions secret.

The fourth is a damaged school relationship. A family that has spent the autumn pressing the coordinator about a prediction has also been building the context in which the reference is written. Predictions are professional judgements the school stands behind and schools are accountable for their accuracy over time. Asking what evidence a judgement rests on is reasonable; pressing for a revision without new evidence is not, and it costs something the candidate needs.

The fifth is the English proficiency assumption. Institutions set their own policies, and some require a separate test regardless of a strong Diploma English grade. This is among the most variable requirements in the field and one of the easiest to check, and it is regularly discovered late, when a test has to be booked and sat in the weeks before a deadline.

sections.heading: Written work: the boundary, stated plainly
paragraphs: IB Gram does not write personal statements, supplemental essays, references or any part of an application. That is not a positioning statement; it is the only defensible position. Written work is assessed partly for voice, and an essay that does not sound like the rest of a candidate's file is a liability rather than an asset. Admissions offices read for inconsistency and institutions have their own procedures where authorship is in doubt.

What legitimate support looks like is narrower and genuinely useful. A candidate can be asked better questions: what did you actually do, what went wrong, what did you change, what would you do differently. They can be shown where a paragraph asserts rather than evidences. They can be told that a sentence is doing no work. They then rewrite it themselves. The output is their own writing, improved by their own thinking, which is also the only version that survives an interview.

The same boundary applies with more force to IB coursework, where the rules are explicit. A tutor may teach the skills a task requires, explain the published criteria, discuss the student's own draft, identify an unsupported conclusion, and model technique on a different example. A tutor must not write, complete or produce any part of an Extended Essay, internal assessment or Theory of Knowledge essay. Sites in this market sell completed internal assessments at a fixed price; that is an integrity breach and the consequence falls on the candidate.

We keep feedback logs with dates for this reason as much as any other. A dated sequence of a student's own drafts with external feedback on each is the strongest available demonstration that the work is theirs, and for a candidate whose file will be read closely that record is worth more than any marginal improvement a more intrusive kind of help might produce.

sections.heading: Documents, attestation and studying inside the UAE
paragraphs: A candidate intending to study or work in the UAE on the strength of an overseas or international qualification will meet the attestation and equivalency process, and the useful thing to know early is that it is a documents process with its own requirements and its own queue. It is run by the Ministry and the relevant attestation authority. It is not performed by a school, a university or a tutoring service, and no page should present it as something a provider can expedite.

The practical advice is therefore administrative. Find out from the Ministry's own pages, or from the emirate's attestation authority, exactly which documents are required for your child's curriculum and destination, and start collecting them before results arrive rather than after. Families who begin the process in August, with a university start date in September, discover the timeline the hard way.

It is also worth separating this from admissions. A UAE university's admission decision and the Ministry's equivalency decision are different things with different criteria, and a candidate can satisfy one and still have work to do on the other. Ask the university's admissions office directly what it requires and in what order, because the sequence differs between institutions.

Finally, a caution that applies across this whole page: nothing here should be read as implying that tutoring is required for equivalency, for admission, or for school progression. Those are institutional and regulatory processes with published criteria. Academic support affects a grade. Presenting it as a route through a regulatory process would be a false-urgency claim about a process that does not work that way.

sections.heading: How academic sessions run, and what guidance cannot do
paragraphs: Academic sessions are one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing, a shared whiteboard and the candidate's own marked work open. Gulf Standard Time lessons are scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school week: earlier where the school run is short, later for the Khalifa City and Al Raha catchments, weekend blocks during the autumn when applications and coursework fill the weekdays, and post-Iftar timing during Ramadan.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. In application season the online format matters mostly for turnaround and for reach: a timed paper marked within two days is a document a teacher can weigh before a prediction closes, and a candidate needing a higher level Chemistry specialist is choosing from a national pool rather than from whoever can reach an address in Al Shamkha on a Tuesday evening.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any regulator, board or university, and no page of ours should imply one. Individual private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years.

The limits worth repeating: we do not influence admissions decisions, we do not write applications, we do not perform or guarantee equivalency, and we publish no statistic about admissions outcomes because no dataset supports one. What we do is teach the subjects an offer will be written against, give feedback on the student's own written work against published criteria, and read published requirements with you. Where no specialist is free for a subject at the hours you need, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral.

The output is a written list of where the marks are going and what that means for the prediction.

process.title: Produce academic evidence while the window is open
process.description: Dated marked pieces with component breakdowns, produced before the school closes predictions, handed to the subject teacher as documents rather than as claims. Once predictions close, the honest target is the real session and we describe the work that way.

process.title: Written work stays the candidate's own
process.description: We ask better questions, point out where a paragraph asserts rather than evidences, and explain the published criteria for coursework. We do not write personal statements, supplemental essays or any part of an Extended Essay or internal assessment, and we keep dated feedback logs.

process.title: Refer what belongs elsewhere
process.description: Equivalency and attestation go to the Ministry and the attestation authority. Admissions policy questions go to the institution. Reference and application strategy go to the school's counselling team. We say so rather than answering questions that are not ours to answer.

whyPoints.title: Three processes kept separate
whyPoints.description: The application, the Diploma result and UAE equivalency have different owners, timetables and failure modes, and most of the confusion in this area comes from treating them as one. This page separates them and says which one academic support actually touches.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency quoted from the source, with the gap named
whyPoints.description: The British-track rule is five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels. One ranking competitor publishes six. We also publish no IB points figure, because none has been read on an official page.

whyPoints.title: Subject choice named as the real decision
whyPoints.description: The most consequential admissions decision a Diploma candidate makes is their higher level selection in Year 11, two years before any application exists. Almost no page in this market says so, because it is advice that cannot be sold to the family who most needs it.

whyPoints.title: We do not write applications
whyPoints.description: No personal statements, no supplemental essays, no references, and no part of an Extended Essay or internal assessment. Written work is read partly for voice, and an essay that does not match the rest of a file is a liability. Support means better questions and the candidate's own rewrite.

whyPoints.title: No admissions statistics
whyPoints.description: There is no acceptance rate, placement figure or outcome percentage on this page, because no dataset supports one and a number without a sample, date and method is a liability. Competitor pages in this market publish exactly those figures with nothing behind them.

whyPoints.title: No false urgency about institutions
whyPoints.description: Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for admission or for school progression, and this page says so. Equivalency is run by the authority and described on its own pages. We neither perform it nor present ourselves as a route through it.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education require for British curriculum students?
faqs.answer: The published requirement is proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, together with passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five subjects. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required, which is wrong. Verify your own case on the Ministry's pages or with the emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: How many IB points does UAE equivalency need?
faqs.answer: This page does not publish a figure, and the reason is worth stating. No IB points threshold for UAE equivalency has been read on the Ministry's own pages or on an emirate attestation authority's own page for this project, and figures circulating online cannot be verified. Publishing an unsourced number would repeat exactly the error one ranking competitor has already made with the IGCSE subject count. Ask the Ministry or the attestation authority directly, and ask your school's counselling team what it has seen in practice.

faqs.question: Does my child's Diploma subject choice limit which degrees they can apply to?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and the choice is made in Year 11 before most families are thinking about applications. Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy routes commonly require Chemistry at higher level; engineering and physics programmes commonly require Physics and mathematics at higher level; quantitative economics and mathematics degrees frequently specify Analysis and Approaches rather than either maths course. Requirements are published per course and revised, so read the admissions page for each specific course before the selection form is signed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write my child's personal statement?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. Written work is assessed partly for voice, and an essay that does not sound like the rest of a candidate's file is a liability rather than an asset. Institutions read for inconsistency and have their own procedures where authorship is in doubt. Legitimate support looks like better questions about what the candidate actually did, pointing out where a paragraph asserts rather than evidences, and then the candidate rewriting it themselves. That version also survives an interview.

faqs.question: When do Abu Dhabi schools finalise predicted grades for applications?
faqs.answer: It varies and the variation is the point. A school supporting applications to the earliest UK deadline in mid-October forms predictions in September of the second year, largely on first-year evidence. A school working to the main mid-January deadline usually closes them in the autumn or early winter, often just after mocks. Two schools a short drive apart in this emirate can differ by a month, so ask your coordinator in writing in the first week of the second year rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Our prediction is below the requirement for a course. What now?
faqs.answer: It depends on the system. In the UK a prediction below a requirement often means no offer is made at all, which makes it decisive. In holistic admissions a weaker element can be offset elsewhere and the real result matters more. The practical options are to widen the target list, to ask the school what evidence the prediction rests on and whether new evidence would be considered, and to consider pathway or foundation routes where the institution offers one. The counselling team is the right partner for that.

faqs.question: Is the Extended Essay read by universities?
faqs.answer: More often than candidates expect, particularly where it is written in the subject of the intended degree, and it is sometimes referenced in interviews. A well-chosen research question aligned with the application is a genuine asset; one in an unrelated subject is neutral rather than harmful. The value comes from the candidate having done real work on a real question, which is why the help that counts is feedback on their own draft against the published criteria rather than anything more intrusive.

faqs.question: Does a strong IB English grade satisfy university English requirements?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is one of the most variable requirements in the field. Each institution sets its own policy and some require a separate test regardless of a strong Diploma English grade, while others accept the Diploma result subject to conditions. It is also one of the easiest requirements to check and one of the most frequently discovered late, when a test has to be booked and sat in the weeks before a deadline. Read the institution's own page and ask its admissions office if anything is unclear.

faqs.question: Can you help with applications to universities inside the UAE?
faqs.answer: We can read published requirements with you and teach the subjects a condition will be written against. We cannot and do not perform the Ministry equivalency or attestation process, and no provider should present itself as able to expedite it. UAE institutions also set their own admission criteria separately from equivalency, so a candidate can satisfy one and still have work on the other. Ask the admissions office what it requires and in what order, because the sequence differs between institutions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between equivalency and a university offer?
faqs.answer: They are separate decisions made by different bodies against different criteria. A university's admissions office decides whether to offer a place, on its own published requirements. The Ministry of Education's equivalency process decides whether a school-leaving certificate is recognised for use inside the UAE. A candidate can hold an offer and still have equivalency work outstanding, or the reverse. Neither process requires tutoring, and treating them as one is the commonest misunderstanding in this area.

faqs.question: How early should subject requirements be checked?
faqs.answer: Before the Year 11 subject selection form is signed, and again at the start of the second Diploma year to catch revisions. It takes an evening: open the admissions page for each specific course under consideration, read the subject and level requirements as published, and write them down. Requirements vary between institutions offering apparently identical degrees, so a general comparison guide is not a substitute for the course page, and neither is a tutoring site's table.

faqs.question: Will pressing the school about a prediction help my child's application?
faqs.answer: It usually costs more than it gains. A prediction is a professional judgement the school stands behind, and schools are accountable over time for how accurate their predictions prove. Asking what evidence the judgement rests on, and what would need to change, is a reasonable question most coordinators answer directly. Pressing for a revision without new evidence rarely moves it and does affect the context in which the reference is written, which the candidate still needs.

faqs.question: Do you publish university placement results for your students?
faqs.answer: No, and the absence is deliberate. Any acceptance rate, placement figure or outcome percentage would need a stated sample size, date and method to mean anything, and we do not have a dataset that supports one. Competitor pages in this market publish exactly those numbers with nothing behind them, including figures that contradict each other on the same page. A statistic without a method is a liability for whoever publishes it and useless to whoever reads it.

faqs.question: What should we bring to a first conversation about admissions support?
faqs.answer: Four things. The list of courses and institutions under consideration, with their published requirements if you have already read them. Your child's current predicted grades and subject levels. The school's prediction date and internal coursework deadlines. And the most recent marked work in the subject an offer is most likely to name. With those, the first conversation is about the academic gap that matters rather than a general discussion about ambition.

abu-dhabi/ib-university-admissions-guida.closingHeading: Read the requirements, get the dates, then work on the grade
abu-dhabi/ib-university-admissions-guida.closingBody: The two highest-value hours in this whole area cost nothing. Spend one opening the admissions page of every course under consideration and writing down what it actually requires in subjects, levels, points and English. Spend the second asking your coordinator in writing for the prediction date and the internal coursework deadlines. Those two hours prevent the failures that no later guidance can repair. After that, academic support has a narrow and real job: the higher level subject grade a conditional offer will be written against. Book a free trial lesson with that subject's specialist to see where the marks are currently going.

abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.tutorsIntro: These tutors mark and date every piece of timed work and open the next session with the script rather than with a conversation. For a transferring student that record is the only way to tell an adjustment period from a real problem, and the two need opposite responses.

intro.heading: Judge the transition on scripts, not on how the term feels
paragraphs: A student moving from ICSE into IGCSE in Abu Dhabi will have a wobbly first half-term. That is normal, it is not evidence of anything, and the mistake families make is reacting to it. The reverse mistake is equally common: assuming the wobble is normal when the scripts are actually showing a structural problem with tier placement or specification mismatch. Both mistakes are avoided by the same thing, which is a written record of marked work with enough detail to read a trend.

The record is five columns and takes two minutes to keep. Date, paper and component, raw mark against the available mark, and an error category. The error category is the column almost nobody keeps and the one that does the work: knowledge gap, where content was never covered; method error, where the approach was wrong or the working was not shown; command-word misread, where the student answered a different question; arithmetic or transcription slip; and timing, where questions were not reached. Four weeks of that column tells you more than a term of reports.

For an ICSE student specifically, the first scripts tend to show method error and command-word misread rather than knowledge gap, and that pattern is good news. ICSE is a broad, content-rich board with a strong English tradition and substantial internal project work, so the transferring student usually arrives with the content, the writing fluency and the working habits. What they do not arrive with is the habit of writing to IGCSE mark schemes, which allocate method marks and follow command words closely.

That distinction is worth money. A knowledge gap needs teaching, which is hours. A method error and a command-word misread need marked practice, which is fewer hours and faster results, because the student already agrees with the principle and the fault lives in the hand rather than the head. A provider who cannot tell you which of the two your child's scripts show is quoting hours against a diagnosis nobody made.

There is one structural thing the record cannot fix and it has to be checked before any of this matters. Confirm, in writing, the tier each subject is entered at, the board and specification code, the series the entry is for, and which route each science uses for the experimental-skills component. A student practising Extended-tier papers while entered at Core is producing a record of a paper they will never sit, and four weeks of beautifully kept data about the wrong exam is worse than no data.

IB Gram delivers this support as one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run in India only. For an evidence-led approach the online format helps directly: scripts are annotated on a shared screen, stored and timestamped, so week two sits beside week nine without anybody keeping a folder, and a specialist in the exact specification is findable rather than limited to whoever lives nearby.
bullets: Keep five columns per script: date, paper, component, mark, error category
ICSE students usually show method error, not knowledge gap, in the first scripts
Method error and command-word misread respond to marked practice, not teaching hours
A real movement repeats across two attempts at the same paper format

abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.programmesIntro: Two systems with different assessment traditions, and a transfer point between them. Here is what each side is and where the evidence comes from.

programmes.name: ICSE, the starting point
programmes.description: An Indian board examination at Class 10 with a notably broad subject spread, a strong emphasis on English language and literature, and substantial internal assessment and project work contributing to several subjects. Assessment rewards thorough, well-written, accurately detailed work, and the English demand is higher at the same age than in most comparable systems.
programmes.countryNote: Indian-curriculum provision is a major part of UAE private education, 26 per cent of Dubai private-school students in 2024-25 across a sector of 227 schools teaching 17 curricula, and Abu Dhabi has a comparable concentration. An ICSE student transferring here is usually joining a British-curriculum school that has handled the move before, which is worth using when asking what evidence they will collect.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Individually certificated subjects assessed by externally marked papers, with many subjects tiered into Core and Extended. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Mark schemes allocate method marks and follow defined command words closely.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Confirm the zone with the exams officer; for a family new to the system this is the cheapest risk in the whole transition to remove.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other board widely used in the emirate, with its own specification codes such as 4MA1 for International GCSE Mathematics A and its own paper structures. Exams are available in May and June and again in November each year, and some specifications are arranged differently from the Cambridge equivalent of the same named subject.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes dated calendars, which makes planning checkable: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables appear ahead of each series, so work only from the live official PDF.

programmes.name: Core and Extended tier placement
programmes.description: The decision that determines whether any record you keep is meaningful. Core covers less content and caps the attainable grade; Extended covers more and opens the top grades, and in Mathematics and several sciences the papers differ entirely between tiers. A record built on the wrong tier's papers describes an exam the student will not sit.
programmes.countryNote: An ICSE student is frequently placed cautiously on arrival because the school has no internal data yet, and caution can cap a grade unnecessarily. Ask for the tier in writing, ask when it becomes final, and ask what evidence would cause a review, because the first marked internal assessment is precisely the evidence that should trigger one.

abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.subjectsIntro: This is where an ICSE-trained student typically stands in each IGCSE subject and what the first marked scripts usually show. Several entries recommend recording the evidence and spending nothing.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Normally the strongest transfer in the combination, because ICSE's English demand at the same age is high. The first scripts tend to show strong writing fluency losing marks to paper conventions: summary where analysis was asked, or a response that ignores the question's specific focus. A short block fixes it.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: ICSE literature study builds textual knowledge well. What the record shows is quotation precision and the number of distinct points made under time, both countable, and both improvable within four weeks of marked practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Content is usually secure. The dominant error category in the first scripts is method error, because IGCSE awards marks for visible working and ICSE answers were scored on correctness and presentation. Two or three marked sessions typically clears it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Coverage transfers reasonably. The record generally shows marks lost in extended responses where reasoning steps are missing, and in the experimental-skills component, which is assessed either by a practical examination or by an alternative written paper depending on the route the school uses.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation and nomenclature are usually sound. The error log fills with explanation questions answered by description, and with multi-step calculations where an early slip propagates further than it did before.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is familiar territory for an ICSE student. Command-word precision is the recurring entry in the record: describe, explain, state, suggest and compare each pay differently and the trained default is thorough description.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: ICSE builds detailed factual knowledge; IGCSE rewards argument and sourcework. The countable evidence is how much usable argument appears in a timed answer rather than how much accurate detail, which is a different measurement than the student is used to.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and data are pattern-based and the fastest marks available to a transferring student. Case-study precision, with named places and figures, takes longer and shows in the record as a slow climb rather than a jump.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Often new at this stage. Diagram conventions are the cheapest marks in the paper and the most commonly lost, through unlabelled axes or a missing new equilibrium, which makes them an easy early win in the record.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: The demand is applying a concept to the case rather than defining it accurately. The first scripts typically show knowledge-band marks with analysis marks unawarded, which reads as method error rather than a gap.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Programming background often transfers strongly, and the specific loss is pseudocode convention, which is marked as convention. The record shows it immediately because the logic is right and the notation is not.

subjects.name: Hindi
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes where offered
subjects.description: Frequently a reliable grade and frequently overlooked at transfer. Availability differs between Abu Dhabi schools, so ask which language options have actually run for two consecutive years rather than which appear in a prospectus.

abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.regionsIntro: Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum schools sit in different parts of the emirate, which changes how many marked papers a week a family can realistically produce. These are the catchments.

regions.name: Mussafah and Shabiya
regions.note: Dense Indian-curriculum provision and long journeys to British-curriculum schools, so timed papers get sat at weekends rather than on weekday evenings. That is fine, provided they are genuinely timed.

regions.name: Al Reef and Al Shamkha
regions.note: Strong Indian resident population in mainland communities with the longest commutes in the emirate. One marked script a week is realistic here; two is not, and a plan should say so rather than pretend otherwise.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Both Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum options within reach, so some transfers involve no commute change at all, which makes weekday evening timed work genuinely possible.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi Island
regions.note: The oldest British-curriculum provision alongside established Indian-curriculum schools, with short school runs, so a weekday timed paper and a separate session both fit in the same week.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Students are typically home by 15:45, the earliest in the emirate, which is why transferring families here can collect evidence twice a week without the student losing sleep over it.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer British-curriculum provision where some subjects have shorter track records and the board has occasionally changed between cohorts, so confirm the specification code rather than assuming last year's applies.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Bateen
regions.note: Established central districts with a long-settled professional Indian population, where students often take nine or ten subjects, so the evidence has to be prioritised across subjects rather than collected for all of them.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Limited British-curriculum options under the same regulator and few resident specialists in a specific IGCSE specification, so online marking is often the only route to a script read by someone who knows the paper.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi Island and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Long-established British-curriculum provision where internal mocks are generally real past papers marked to the scheme, which makes school evidence usable alongside tutor evidence. Named only as context for the local education landscape.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland
schoolClusters.note: A broader British-curriculum population across more schools, with both Cambridge and Pearson specifications in use, so the code question is answered school by school. Listed as ecosystem context only.

schoolClusters.city: Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: A separate catchment under the same regulator with limited British-curriculum options and the thinnest specialist pool in the emirate. Context only.

sections.heading: The record a transferring family should keep
paragraphs: A first term after a board change produces more opinion than information, which is why a written record is worth more here than in almost any other tutoring situation. Five columns: date, paper and component, raw mark against the available mark, and a dominant error category. Keep it from the first marked script, keep the components separate, and never average them into a percentage, because the average is exactly what hides the information you need.

The error category does the diagnostic work. Knowledge gap means content was never covered and needs teaching, which is hours. Method error means the approach was wrong or the working was not shown, which needs marked practice. Command-word misread means the student answered a different question, which needs a short targeted block. Arithmetic slip needs a checking routine. Timing means questions were not reached, which needs full timed papers. Five categories, five different responses, five different costs.

Read the record for a change in the dominant category rather than a rise in the mark. For a transferring student the healthy sequence runs from command-word misread and method error towards slips and timing, which is progress even if the total moves modestly, because the later faults are cheaper to fix than the earlier ones. The unhealthy pattern is the same dominant category at weeks one, three, five and seven, which means the sessions are not addressing the fault and adding more of them only makes the fault more expensive.

The table below shows the format with an illustrative sequence. It is an example of what a record should look like, not a published result: we do not publish student outcome statistics on these pages, because any figure without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is a marketing claim rather than evidence, and this market has a great deal of exactly that.

sections.heading: What transfers intact from ICSE, and should cost nothing
paragraphs: This market has no incentive to tell a transferring family what their child is already good at, so it is worth stating. ICSE is a broad board with a high English demand at Class 10, substantial internal project work in several subjects, and a tradition of thorough, well-presented written answers. An ICSE student arriving in IGCSE usually brings three things that classmates do not: written fluency, breadth of content, and experience of producing extended coursework to a deadline.

English is the clearest case. Where a CBSE transfer frequently needs real English support, an ICSE transfer frequently does not, because the writing demand the student has been meeting is already substantial. What the first scripts show is strong writing losing marks to paper conventions: summary where analysis was asked, or a well-written response that does not address the question's specific focus. That is four to six sessions of marked practice, not a term of language work.

The project experience matters too and gets overlooked. A student used to producing internal assessment work to a brief has the habit of planning, drafting and submitting, which is precisely what some British-curriculum classmates lack. Where a science specification uses a practical route or a subject carries coursework, that habit is an asset and should not be treated as something to be built from scratch.

Breadth has one practical consequence worth planning around. ICSE students often arrive having studied more subjects than their IGCSE cohort will sit, which sounds like an advantage and occasionally produces a mismatch instead: content covered in less depth across more ground. Where that shows in the record it appears as a knowledge gap in the later, harder topics of a subject rather than across the subject, which is a narrow and cheap thing to fix once identified.
bullets: Written fluency from a high ICSE English demand usually transfers intact
Experience of producing coursework to a deadline is a real asset
First English scripts lose marks to paper conventions, not to language
Breadth can mean depth gaps in the harder topics, which is narrow and cheap to fix
Do not pay for what the record shows is already there

sections.heading: Tier placement, and the evidence that should trigger a review
paragraphs: A transferring student is often placed cautiously because the school has no internal data on them yet. That is a reasonable default and it should not be a permanent one. Tier placement determines the content taught, the papers sat and the attainable grade ceiling, and in Mathematics and several sciences the papers differ entirely between Core and Extended, so a cautious placement is not a safe version of a good placement; it is a different qualification with a lower ceiling.

The evidence to bring on arrival is ICSE subject marks with whatever internal detail the school holds, read for performance on multi-step and extended work rather than for the overall figure. An ICSE student with solid mathematics marks is often a straightforward Extended candidate. An ICSE student whose strength was presentation and thoroughness rather than multi-step problem solving may genuinely be better placed at Core initially, with a review once internal evidence exists.

Then ask three questions in writing and keep the answers: which tier is my child entered at in each subject, when does the entry become final, and what evidence would cause you to review it. The third is the one nobody asks. Abu Dhabi schools differ, and some will review a tier decision on the strength of internal results during Year 11, which means a cautiously placed student can move up if the evidence appears. The record described above is exactly the evidence, which is one more reason to keep it from week one.

Two cautions. Extended is not automatically better: a student placed above their evidence sits papers designed for stronger candidates and can finish with a lower grade than Core would have produced. And whatever the tier, every past paper, worksheet and marked script must match it. Four weeks of carefully recorded data on the wrong tier's paper is worse than no data, because it produces confident conclusions about an exam the student will not sit.

sections.heading: Method marks and command words: the two faults that dominate the first term
paragraphs: Across transferring students from Indian boards, two error categories account for most of the lost marks in the first half-term, and neither is a knowledge problem. The first is method error, specifically working not shown. IGCSE mark schemes allocate method marks, so a correct final answer written without the intervening steps forfeits marks that were sitting there for free. The second is command-word misread, where a thorough and accurate description is given to a question that asked the student to explain, suggest or compare.

Both are behavioural, and that is good news because behaviour shifts faster than knowledge. The mechanism is seeing the mark scheme applied to their own script. A student who watches two method marks awarded to the lines of working they almost omitted stops omitting them, usually within three scripts. Explaining the principle in the abstract changes very little, because the student already accepts the principle and the habit is in the hand.

Command words are worth a dedicated session or two because the list is short and the payoff appears immediately in the record. State, describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate and show each carry defined expectations and different mark structures. List the ones that actually appear in the student's specifications, write what each pays for, and practise them separately with marked feedback until the shape of each answer is automatic. Three sessions usually covers a whole subject combination, because the terms repeat across subjects far more than students expect.

The third fault worth naming is graph and table convention. Axes, scales, units and labelling carry marks in the sciences and in geography, and a transferring student frequently produces a correct graph that scores below its quality because a convention was missed. It is the cheapest recovery in the whole transition and it appears in the record as a step change rather than a climb, usually within two scripts of being named.
bullets: Method error, usually working not shown, is the commonest first-term fault
Command-word misread is the second, and both are behavioural
Marked practice shifts them in three scripts; explanation does not
Three sessions on command words usually covers a whole subject combination
Graph and table conventions are the cheapest recovery available

sections.heading: English after ICSE: a different conversation entirely
paragraphs: Families transferring from ICSE often arrive expecting the English conversation that transferring families from other Indian boards need, and usually they do not need it. ICSE's English demand at Class 10 is substantial, and the students who have met it tend to write fluently, at length, and with control. What the first IGCSE English scripts show is almost never a language problem.

What they do show is paper convention. IGCSE reading papers reward precise selection and analysis of how a text works rather than summary of what it says, and a student who writes an excellent summary has produced a strong answer to a question that was not asked. Writing papers reward register control, structure and audience awareness against a specified task, and the marks follow the task specification rather than the general quality of the prose. Both are learnable in four to six marked sessions.

Placement should still be confirmed rather than assumed. English as a First Language and English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different demands, and for most ICSE transfers First Language is the right one, but the decision belongs to the school's English department and should be informed by a real piece of the student's extended written work rather than by a conversation. One session reading that piece gives the school something to work from.

One further point specific to this transfer. ICSE literature study builds genuine textual knowledge, and the recoverable marks in IGCSE Literature are in quotation precision and in the number of distinct points made within the time available. Both are countable, which makes them ideal for the record: a student making four developed points in forty minutes in week one and six in week five has improved measurably, and that is a better conversation with a teenager than a general comment about depth.
bullets: ICSE English fluency usually transfers; the gap is paper convention
Reading papers want analysis of how a text works, not summary
Writing papers follow the task specification rather than general quality
Confirm First Language or Second Language placement with the school anyway
In Literature, count quotations and developed points; both are measurable

sections.heading: The science experimental component, and what the record should show
paragraphs: Experimental skills are assessed either through a practical examination or through an alternative written paper, depending on the route the school enters candidates for, and the first thing to establish is which applies to each science. Both assess design and evaluation rather than execution: apparatus choice, variable control, tables and graphs, uncertainty, and the reasoning the mark scheme wants to see. A transferring student who has done plenty of laboratory work may still have done none of that.

ICSE project and practical experience helps with the habits and not necessarily with the assessed skills, because the assessed skills are about justifying a method rather than following one. So the record for this component should track something specific: in each marked script, whether the variables were correctly identified and controlled, whether the table and graph met convention, and whether the evaluation named a real limitation rather than a general one. Three dimensions, tracked across three or four scripts, is enough to see movement.

This is also the component most often left out of a transfer plan entirely, because it is not obviously a subject and it has no textbook chapter. That omission is expensive: it is a defined part of the grade in every science and it rewards a trainable skill. Three to four written sessions per science usually covers the gap, and the gain shows quickly in the record because the marks are formulaic once the conventions are in place.

A boundary worth stating. A tutor teaches the criteria and the conventions, reviews work the student has produced and marks practice questions. A tutor does not design the student's investigation, write any part of a submitted report, supply text or complete a draft. Where a specification carries assessed coursework, a breach is a malpractice matter for the student. We also do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents; we cite and link them, which keeps the student on the current version.
bullets: Confirm whether each science uses a practical exam or an alternative written paper
The assessed skill is justifying a method, not following one
Track three things per script: variables, conventions, a real limitation named
Three to four written sessions per science usually closes the gap
A tutor reviews the student's own work and never designs or writes it

sections.heading: The series, the deadlines and the zone check
paragraphs: UAE IGCSE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in June and November, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, which is directly relevant to a family arriving from an Indian board, because material and advice written for that audience about a spring sitting does not apply to a candidate entered here.

The Cambridge zone requirement is the cheapest risk in this transition to remove and the most expensive to ignore. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and it says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exams officer which zone the centre sits in, work only from that version, discard the rest.

Pearson's dated publications show why entries close so far ahead of the papers. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results landed with students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official PDF rather than any restatement, this page included.

For a mid-year transfer, the series choice can be the whole decision and the record is what should drive it. A student who joined in January and is entered for the June series has not been taught the course, and four weeks of marked evidence will make that obvious quickly. The honest options are a November entry, a reduced subject list, or both, and that conversation belongs with the school in the first fortnight, because entries close months before the papers.
