sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and the hours the record does not see
paragraphs: A record of marked scripts measures subject progress and says nothing about the hours available to produce it, and in UAE schools those hours include provision that is not optional. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's published mandatory-subject requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. ADEK applies the equivalent requirement in Abu Dhabi.

KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. For a transferring student taking nine or ten IGCSE subjects alongside that provision, the week is genuinely full, and a plan promising two marked scripts a week has to be measured against it rather than against enthusiasm.

The organisational rules are specific where Arabic is involved. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies. Schools must ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects.

One constraint on buying support in these subjects: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support works from the school's own materials and the official programme rather than from an alternative course a tutor prefers. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership, and claims none.

sections.heading: Permits, rates and when the record says stop
paragraphs: For a family new to the UAE tutoring market, two practical facts. Individuals providing private tuition need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, according to u.ae, granted free of charge for two years; eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, no amount should be quoted to you.

On rates, published UAE market figures as read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at roughly AED 33-65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65; qualified subject tutors online at roughly AED 150-300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150; and specialists at roughly AED 200-450 and above. In-home one-to-one runs roughly AED 180-500 including travel. Those are other providers' published figures rather than an IB Gram price list, and the question that separates the bands is who marks the timed work: at the budget end it is usually the student, against a downloaded scheme, which gives a score and no error diagnosis.

Which brings the record back to the centre of the argument. The reason to insist on marked, dated, component-separated scripts is that it is the only way to know whether the money is working. If the dominant error category has been identical across four marked attempts at the same format, the sessions are not addressing the fault, and adding a second weekly session doubles the cost of not addressing it. Ask what specifically will be different next week, phrased as a question about the error category.

We will raise that ourselves rather than wait, including when the answer is a different tutor or stopping altogether. A transferring student's first-term wobble is usually adjustment, and most of these plans should be four to ten sessions rather than a standing arrangement. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which regulates schools and approves no individual tutor; ADEK's reported professional-ethics rules and the MoHRE code of conduct both point away from paying your child's own teacher. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home tutoring is a service we provide only in India.

process.title: Confirm the structural facts
process.description: Tier per subject, board and specification code per subject, the series, the science experimental route and the Cambridge zone, all in writing from the school. Without these, any record you keep may describe papers your child will never sit.

process.title: Send ICSE marks and one piece of writing
process.description: Subject marks with whatever internal detail the school holds, read for multi-step and extended performance, plus a real piece of extended written work. The first informs the tier argument; the second settles the English placement question quickly.

process.title: Three-script diagnostic
process.description: Three sessions, three marked papers across different components, and a written error analysis naming the dominant category. No obligation to continue. For most transferring ICSE students this shows the wobble is adjustment rather than structure.

process.title: Free trial lesson
process.description: One session with the proposed tutor on the first named fault, using the student's own specification, with marked work rather than discussion. If the match is wrong we offer a different tutor instead of asking you to persist with it.

process.title: Weekly script, format held constant
process.description: One session and one timed piece a week, the same paper format repeated three or four times so attempts are comparable, components recorded separately, and the error log reviewed openly every fourth session.

process.title: Act on the trend, including stopping
process.description: A changing dominant error category means it is working. The same category four times means the sessions need changing or a different tutor. Near-ceiling Core scripts before the entry deadline means a tier review conversation, with the dated scripts as the argument.

whyPoints.title: A record you can read without us
whyPoints.description: Dated scripts, components separated, an error category on every piece. No researched competitor page publishes anything resembling a progress record, which is how a term after a board change can pass with nobody able to say whether it worked.

whyPoints.title: Adjustment separated from structure
whyPoints.description: A transferring student's first half-term is bumpy for ordinary reasons. The record is what distinguishes that from a tier mismatch or a specification error, and the two need opposite responses at opposite costs.

whyPoints.title: ICSE strengths left alone
whyPoints.description: Written fluency, breadth and coursework habits usually transfer intact, and English in particular rarely needs the work a transferring family expects. We say so in writing rather than quoting hours against strengths the record already shows.

whyPoints.title: The tier review nobody asks for
whyPoints.description: Cautious placement on arrival is reasonable and should not be permanent. Four weeks of near-ceiling Core scripts is an argument, and some Abu Dhabi schools will review on internal evidence if a family brings it before the entry closes.

whyPoints.title: Codes and zones checked first
whyPoints.description: 0580, 0620, 0625 and 4MA1 are different papers. UAE candidates sit June and November, not the India-only February and March series. Cambridge will not take responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone timetable.

whyPoints.title: No figures we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No guaranteed grade, no self-assigned rating, no outcome statistic without its sample size, date and method, and no reproduction of Cambridge, Pearson or ICSE materials. Official sources are cited and linked instead.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a bumpy first IGCSE term is normal after ICSE?
faqs.answer: By keeping a record rather than reading the atmosphere. Five columns per marked script: date, paper and component, raw mark against the available mark, and a dominant error category. For a transferring student, scripts showing method error and command-word misread are ordinary adjustment and respond quickly to marked practice. Scripts showing a knowledge gap across a whole subject, or inexplicable results, point at something structural such as a tier mismatch or practice on the wrong specification. Those need opposite responses at very different costs, and only the record distinguishes them.

faqs.question: Which ICSE strengths carry into IGCSE without any extra help?
faqs.answer: Written fluency, because the ICSE English demand at Class 10 is substantial. Breadth of content, which usually covers the IGCSE syllabus comfortably at the standard end. And the habit of producing coursework to a deadline, which matters where a specification carries assessed practical or project work. None of those should appear as a line item in a quote. A provider recommending a year-long programme including English language work to an ICSE transfer has not looked at a piece of the student's actual writing.

faqs.question: What error categories should a tutor record on my child's scripts?
faqs.answer: Five cover almost everything. Knowledge gap, where content was never covered and teaching is needed. Method error, where the approach was wrong or working was not shown. Command-word misread, where a different question was answered. Arithmetic or transcription slip. And timing, where questions were not reached. Each implies a different intervention and a different number of hours, and only the first is fixed by teaching more content. The useful signal over four weeks is which category dominates and whether it changes, not the raw mark.

faqs.question: Why does my child's correct answer still lose marks in IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: Because IGCSE mark schemes allocate method marks, and a correct final answer written without the intervening steps forfeits them. For a student trained in a system that scored correctness and presentation, that is an unfamiliar rule rather than a weakness, and it is the commonest single entry in a transferring student's error log. It shifts within about three scripts once the student watches method marks being awarded to the working they nearly omitted. Explaining the rule in the abstract achieves much less, because the habit lives in the hand.

faqs.question: Can a cautious Core tier placement be changed after my child arrives?
faqs.answer: Often, and the record is the argument. Schools place a transferring student cautiously because they have no internal data yet, which is reasonable and should not be permanent. Ask three things in writing: the tier for each subject, when the entry becomes final, and what evidence would cause a review. Then bring four weeks of dated scripts showing Core papers performing near the ceiling. Abu Dhabi schools differ, and some will review on internal evidence before entries close. Nobody offers a review if nobody asks for one.

faqs.question: Does my child need English support coming from ICSE?
faqs.answer: Usually less than families expect. ICSE's English demand is high, so the first IGCSE English scripts rarely show a language problem. What they show is paper convention: a summary offered where analysis was asked, or a well-written response that does not address the question's specific focus. Reading papers reward analysis of how a text works; writing papers follow the task specification rather than general prose quality. That is four to six marked sessions. Confirm the First Language or Second Language placement with the school anyway, using a real piece of extended writing.

faqs.question: How many marked scripts a week are realistic for a family in Al Shamkha?
faqs.answer: One, honestly, and a plan should say so rather than promise two. Mainland communities have the longest commutes in the emirate to island schools, which means a timed paper usually happens at a weekend rather than on a weekday evening. That is perfectly workable provided it is genuinely timed, because an untimed script tells you nothing about the fault category that matters most at the end of a paper. Families in Al Raha or on the island can realistically produce two, because students are home earlier.

faqs.question: Why does the tutor keep setting the same paper format each week?
faqs.answer: Because a second attempt at the same format is what makes the first one interpretable. A mark on a Paper 2 and a mark on a Paper 4 are not comparable, and a Cambridge mark is not comparable to a Pearson one, so changing format weekly produces data that cannot show a trend. Holding it constant for three or four attempts lets you see whether a component genuinely moved. After that the format changes deliberately, to check whether the improvement transfers rather than being specific to one paper.

faqs.question: What should the record show after four weeks for it to be working?
faqs.answer: A change in the dominant error category, which is a better signal than a rise in the raw mark. The healthy sequence for a transferring student runs from command-word misread and method error towards slips and timing, because the later faults are cheaper to fix than the earlier ones. The unhealthy pattern is the same dominant category at weeks one, three, five and seven, which means the sessions are not addressing the fault. Adding a second session to that plan doubles the cost of not addressing it.

faqs.question: How is the science practical component assessed and what should we track?
faqs.answer: Either through a practical examination or through an alternative written paper, depending on the route the school enters candidates for, so confirm which applies to each science first. Both assess design and evaluation rather than execution. Track three things in each marked script: whether the variables were identified and controlled correctly, whether the table and graph met convention, and whether the evaluation named a real limitation rather than a general one. Three or four written sessions per science usually closes the gap, and the gain appears quickly because the marks are formulaic.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will my child sit, and does the Indian spring sitting apply?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May and June and again in November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so advice or material written for an Indian audience about a spring sitting does not apply to a candidate entered in this emirate, which is worth knowing for exactly this transfer.

faqs.question: My child joined in January. Is the June series realistic?
faqs.answer: Four weeks of marked scripts will answer that faster than any discussion. Where the taught course cannot be completed before the papers, no plan of sessions changes the arithmetic, and the honest options are a November entry, a reduced subject list, or both. That conversation belongs with the school in the first fortnight, because entries close months ahead of the papers and the window for choosing differently is shorter than it feels. The record is what makes the case concretely rather than as an opinion about readiness.

faqs.question: The error log has not changed in a month. Is more tuition the answer?
faqs.answer: Not until you know why. If the dominant error category has been identical across four marked attempts at the same format, a second session doubles the cost of not addressing the fault. The right question is what specifically will be different next week, asked about the error category rather than about effort. Sometimes the answer is a different tutor, and we would rather say so than take the booking. A second session genuinely helps where the record shows timing as the main fault, because that responds to volume of full timed practice.

faqs.question: Can we see the error log, or is it just for the tutor?
faqs.answer: You should be able to read it without the tutor present, which is the whole point of keeping it in that shape. Date, paper and component, raw mark against the available mark, and the dominant error category, with the components never averaged into a single percentage. If a provider will not commit to a record you can read, you have no way to judge the term except by how the sessions feel, which after a board change is the least reliable measure available. Ask for it as a condition of the arrangement.

faqs.question: Are tutors in Abu Dhabi required to hold a permit, and does it affect the price?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and, per u.ae, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Because the permit is free, any provider citing permit costs as a rate driver is inventing one. No fine schedule is published for tutoring without a permit, so no amount should be quoted to you either.

faqs.question: Can IB Gram promise my child settles into IGCSE within a term?
faqs.answer: No. What we commit to is the record: dated scripts with components separated, a named error category on each, the same format held constant so attempts are comparable, and an honest reading of the trend including when it says stop. That is checkable and it is more than this market usually offers. We publish no outcome statistics, because a figure without its sample size, date and method is a marketing claim rather than evidence, and we publish no self-assigned star rating and no guaranteed grade.

abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.closingHeading: Keep the record, read the trend
abu-dhabi/icse-to-igcse-transition.closingBody: If you are managing an ICSE to IGCSE transition in Abu Dhabi, make the record the condition of whatever you buy. Get the tier, board, specification code, series, science experimental route and Cambridge zone in writing from the school first, because a record built on the wrong paper is worse than none. Then ask for dated scripts with components separated and a named error category on each, and start with a three-script diagnostic rather than a term. We will read the trend with you, argue a tier review where the scripts support one, and say plainly when the sessions should stop. A free trial lesson comes first, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.heroSubtitle: IGCSE A star coaching in Abu Dhabi has a question to settle before any teaching happens: whether an A* even exists on your child's certificate. Cambridge International reports most subjects on an A* to G scale while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1, so a family in Abu Dhabi can be chasing a grade their board does not issue. This page sorts that out, then names where the last marks in each paper are lost. Lessons run one-to-one over live video.

abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at Extended tier, and the work for a top grade is narrow: marking to the published mark scheme, closing the last two or three mark-losing habits, and rehearsing the components that candidates meet least often.

intro.heading: First establish which grade your child can actually be awarded
paragraphs: An A* is a specific grade issued on a specific scale, and in Abu Dhabi a family can spend a term chasing one their board does not award. Cambridge International reports most international GCSE subjects on an A* to G scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale, where the top grade is a 9 and there is no A* at all. Schools in this emirate use both boards, sometimes different boards for different subjects in the same year group, so the first action is to ask the centre which scale each of your child's subjects is reported on.

This is not pedantry. It changes the target, the way progress is read, and the way a sixth form or university reads the result. A candidate aiming for a 9 on a 9 to 1 scale is aiming at a band that was deliberately set above the old top grade, and comparisons between the two scales are made by the boards and the receiving institutions rather than by a tutor. Where an equivalence matters to your family, read it on the board's own page or ask the sixth form what it treats as equivalent, in writing.

Once that is settled, the second precondition is the tier. In tiered subjects, the top grades are only available at Extended tier, and tier is fixed in the entry made by the centre before its internal cut-off. A candidate entered at Core has a capped ceiling no amount of teaching can lift in that series. So a top-grade campaign begins with two administrative facts, both obtainable in a single email: the grade scale per subject, and the tier on the entry.

After that the work becomes genuinely narrow, which is the good news. Candidates in reach of the top band know the content. What separates them from it is a small set of repeated behaviours visible in any marked script: method lines left unwritten, command words answered loosely, conclusions stated without the evidence that earns the mark, answers rounded before the final step, and the last long question met with four minutes left. Those are nameable and each one has a fixed cost in sessions.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. At the top of the range the practical consequence is who you can choose: a candidate needs someone who marks Extended-tier Chemistry or Additional Mathematics to the published mark scheme, and in Abu Dhabi that person is unlikely to live within a short drive of any particular address. The in-home market prices the journey at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, and the journey contributes nothing to a mark scheme.
bullets: Cambridge International reports most international GCSE subjects on an A* to G scale
Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale, with 9 as the top grade
In tiered subjects the top grades are available only at Extended tier
Tier is set by the centre in the entry, before its own internal cut-off date
Grade thresholds are set per series and published by the boards after the papers are sat
UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only

abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.programmesIntro: A top grade is built across two or three years and decided in the last two terms. These are the stages Abu Dhabi families pass through, and what each contributes to the final letter or number.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: Checkpoint tests in March, May and October are diagnostic and carry no certificate, which makes them the cheapest reliable signal a family will get about whether a top grade is realistic. The habits that later separate the top band, particularly writing a reasoned explanation rather than an answer, are established here or not at all.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools on the Cambridge pathway usually stream for IGCSE tier using Year 9 internal data. A family with a top-grade ambition should ask how that decision is made and on what evidence, because an Extended-tier place is the precondition for everything on this page.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Reported on an A* to G scale in most subjects, with Core and Extended tiers in subjects such as Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610. Grade thresholds are set per series after the papers are sat, so the raw mark needed for an A* is not a fixed number and varies between series and between subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a top-grade candidate that administrative detail is worth five minutes of a parent's time.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Reported on a 9 to 1 scale with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. There is no A* on this scale; the top grade is a 9. Some qualifications are modular, which changes how a top-grade campaign is sequenced because a candidate may bank a strong paper rather than carrying everything into one series.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any top-grade plan should be built against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The reason the top grade matters to most families. Abu Dhabi sixth forms publish their own entry requirements and several specify both grade and tier for AS sciences and mathematics. A top IGCSE grade also predicts comfort rather than merely entry: the algebraic fluency that earns an A* is what the first term of AS Mathematics assumes.
programmes.countryNote: Where a sixth-form place depends on a grade, ask the receiving school in writing which grades on which scale it requires, since it may be reading both an A* to G and a 9 to 1 profile in the same admissions round and will have its own view of equivalence.

abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.subjectsIntro: Where the last marks sit, subject by subject. At the top of the range these are component-level and behavioural rather than topical, which is why they are findable in a single marked script.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The final marks live in the unstructured questions at the end of the paper, in upper and lower bounds, and in algebraic fractions. Beneath those sits a steady band of method marks lost to unwritten steps, which strong candidates give away because they can do the step in their head.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics / Further Pure
subjects.description: Calculus notation, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities carry the marks, and the paper assumes an algebraic speed that Mathematics alone does not build. Candidates lose top marks on presentation conventions rather than on understanding, which is a fast repair.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism hold the largest share of lost marks, with practical-skills questions close behind. At the top of the range the losses are in naming a relationship as proportional rather than describing it as increasing, and in justifying which plotted point is anomalous.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry under time pressure, exact organic reaction conditions, and the qualitative-analysis tables. A top-band candidate rarely misunderstands these; they lose marks to imprecision, such as stating a reagent without its conditions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The most command-word sensitive subject at this level. Answers that describe where an explanation was required score the knowledge mark only, and answer length mismatched to mark allocation costs time needed for the data questions later in the paper.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Marked on reading as much as on writing. The directed-response task rewards evidence used in service of an argument rather than retelling, and the composition is assessed on controlled structure. Top-band candidates lose marks to length without shape.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The summary task divides the top band: compression in the candidate's own words rather than selective copying. The directed-writing task is marked on audience and register, both specified in the prompt and both routinely ignored by otherwise strong writers.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Extended-answer questions carry the top marks and they require a judgement with support, not a balanced summary. Candidates who analyse thoroughly and stop short of evaluating sit a band below where their knowledge places them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Top marks go on written conventions rather than coding ability: trace tables completed exactly, pseudocode in the expected style, and precise vocabulary for data representation and the fetch-execute cycle. Capable programmers lose a band here routinely.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE social studies alongside IGCSE
subjects.description: Taught alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, and running through the whole examination year. For a top-grade campaign these are fixed timetable hours, and any plan that treats them as optional has overstated the week it is working with.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: The shortest school runs in the capital, which lets a candidate sit a timed section on a weekday evening and still have time to review it. For top-band work, where the gains come from frequency, that is a material advantage.

regions.note: Established island communities with manageable travel and a strong concentration of Extended-tier science candidates. Competition for the same specialists peaks here between the mock window and the June series.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment living and minimal travel, which suits the short frequent sessions that command-word and method-line habits respond to. The practical constraint is a quiet room for a timed paper rather than the clock.

sections.heading: A* or 9: which scale is your child actually on?
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools use both major international GCSE boards, and some use different boards for different subjects within the same year group. Cambridge International reports most international GCSE subjects on an A* to G scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale, where 9 is the top grade and no A* is issued. A family can therefore set a target that their child's certificate will never show, and in practice this happens most often where a household moved from a Cambridge school to a Pearson one or where the school mixes boards.

The consequence is practical rather than cosmetic. Progress gets read against the wrong landmark, and a sixth-form conversation gets conducted in the wrong currency. Where equivalence between the two scales matters, it is set by the boards and interpreted by receiving institutions, not by a tutoring service, so the only reliable route is to read the board's own published explanation and to ask the sixth form in writing what it requires on which scale.

The second half of this question is the tier, and it is the one that actually caps a grade. In tiered subjects the top grades are available only at Extended tier, and the tier is fixed in the entry submitted by the centre. A candidate entered at Core cannot be awarded a top grade in that series however well they perform, and no teaching changes that after the entry closes. Confirm the tier on the entry, in writing, before buying a top-grade campaign.

Both facts come from the same email to the school's exams officer: which board and option code is each subject entered under, on which grade scale is it reported, and at which tier. Five minutes of administration prevents the single most common wasted term in this part of the market.

sections.heading: Why no honest page can tell you the marks an A* needs
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask what percentage an A* requires, and the honest answer is that there is no standing figure. Grade thresholds are set per series by the board after the papers have been sat and the cohort's performance is known, and they are then published. They differ between subjects, between components and between series. A page that quotes a single percentage for a top grade is either reporting one historical series without saying so or inventing a number.

What a family can do, and should, is read the board's published thresholds for recent series in their child's specific subject. That gives a realistic band rather than a promise, and it converts a vague target into an arithmetic one: if the threshold has sat in a particular range across several series, a candidate currently scoring below it knows roughly how many marks are in play. That is a far more useful piece of information than a tutor's estimate.

It also reframes a mock result usefully. A school marking a mock has to borrow thresholds from somewhere, usually a previous series, and the choice shifts a candidate's apparent grade. Asking which thresholds were applied, and what the raw mark was, often turns an alarming mock grade into a gap of a few marks. Several marks is a narrow, cheap problem. A whole band may not be.

One thing to avoid entirely: reproducing or sharing board threshold documents, past papers or mark schemes. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and the correct behaviour is to cite and link them. A tutor who offers a folder of mark schemes is offering something they are not entitled to distribute, which is a reasonable signal about the rest of their practice.

sections.heading: Where the last marks are lost, component by component
paragraphs: At the top of the range, lost marks are not spread across the syllabus. They cluster in a small number of components and in a small number of behaviours within them. In Mathematics the clustering is in the final unstructured questions and in bounds, with a steady tax of method marks on every page. In Physics it is electricity, electromagnetism and the practical-skills questions. In Chemistry it is moles under time pressure and the precision of stated conditions.

In the written subjects the clustering is different but equally predictable. The English summary task rewards compression and punishes selective copying. The directed-writing task rewards register and audience, which the prompt specifies and which strong writers override with their own voice. Economics and Business extended answers reward a supported judgement and give nothing extra for a thorough balanced summary. Biology punishes a described answer where an explanation was required, in every paper, every series.

The reason to tabulate this is efficiency. A candidate three or four marks below a top threshold does not need a syllabus review; they need the two components where those marks are going, rehearsed under the real duration and marked strictly. A single diagnostic paper identifies which ones, and the plan after that is short. Buying a term of general revision for a four-mark gap is the most common overspend in this part of the market.

There is a scheduling implication too. The components where top-band marks hide are frequently the ones a school practises least, because they are awkward to run: alternative-to-practical papers, long data-analysis questions, and timed composition. Those are exactly where an outside session adds something the classroom has not already provided.

sections.heading: The five habits that separate the top band
paragraphs: The first is writing the method. Both boards award method marks, and a correct final answer with nothing shown collects fewer of them than a wrong answer reached visibly. Top-band candidates give these away constantly because the step is obvious to them. Installing the habit takes two or three sessions and maintaining it takes timed practice, because it is the first thing to disappear when a paper is tight.

The second is reading the command word and answering it exactly. Describe, explain, suggest, evaluate, justify, compare: each has a mark-scheme meaning and an answer written to the wrong one collects the knowledge mark and stops. This is the single largest source of lost marks in Biology and a significant one everywhere else, and it is a reading habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The third is finishing. Marks lost to unattempted questions at the end of a paper are invisible in a grade and obvious in a script: look for where the writing thins out. The cause is usually over-investment earlier, a strong candidate writing a six-mark answer to a three-mark question. The repair is a question-order strategy and timed full papers, not more content.

The fourth is precision in the final step: not rounding before the end, carrying units, labelling axes, stating conditions. The fifth is checking: a ten-second sanity check that a probability does not exceed one or a length is not negative. Neither is intellectually demanding and both are worth marks in every series, and candidates at the top of the range skip them because they trust themselves, which is exactly when they cost most.

sections.heading: Alternative-to-practical, coursework and the option codes behind them
paragraphs: A top-grade campaign has to be built against the components the candidate is actually entered for, and in the sciences that is not automatic. In several subjects the practical assessment is examined through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory session, and which applies depends on the option code the centre has entered. A candidate rehearsing for one and sitting the other has lost marks before the series begins.

That paper is also where top-band marks hide, because it is the component schools practise least. It asks candidates to identify variables, criticise an experimental method, read a scale precisely, draw a graph to the examiner's conventions and identify anomalies with reasons. Each of those is a learnable technique and none of them is taught by revising the theory. Three or four past alternative-to-practical papers marked strictly is among the highest-yield blocks available in Physics, Chemistry and Biology.

Where a coursework component exists, the position differs between school candidates and private candidates, and a private candidate generally cannot submit coursework externally, so the centre enters an option code without it and the written papers carry more of the grade. That changes what a top-grade plan should rehearse. Establishing the exact option codes on the entry is therefore a prerequisite, and the exams officer can supply them.

One further Pearson-specific point: where a qualification is modular, a candidate may be able to bank a strong paper and re-sit a weaker one rather than carrying everything into a single series. For a top-grade candidate that is a strategic question worth raising with the centre early, because the rules are set by the board and the sequencing decision belongs to the entry.

sections.heading: The calendar for a top-grade campaign, counted backwards
paragraphs: A top-band plan fails most often on timing rather than on content, because the useful work has to happen before the components stop being teachable. Counting backwards from the series makes the sequence obvious. The last fortnight before papers is for timed rehearsal and nothing new. The month before that is for the components with the lowest practice frequency, which means the alternative-to-practical papers and the long data questions. The term before that is where habits are installed, because habits need maintaining.

Before any of it sits the administration. The centre's internal entry cut-off fixes the tier and the option codes, and once it passes the ceiling is set. For a top-grade candidate the cut-off is therefore the most important date in the year, and it falls months before the papers. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, and each board's deadline precedes its series by months.

There is one administrative trap specific to Cambridge. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A revision calendar built from the wrong zone's timetable can put a candidate in the wrong room on the wrong day.

Finally, results. For Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates matter for a top-grade candidate whose sixth-form place or scholarship depends on the grade, because the timing determines whether a condition clears in August or in January.

sections.heading: How sessions run, and the limits worth stating
paragraphs: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, screen sharing and the candidate's own marked script open during the session. Gulf Standard Time lessons are scheduled around the Abu Dhabi school week: earlier where the school run is short, 5pm or later for the Khalifa City and Al Shamkha catchments, weekend blocks for timed papers, and post-Iftar timing during Ramadan.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run only in India. For top-band work the argument for online is specialist reach rather than price, although the price argument exists too: in-home rates in the emirate are quoted at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to AED 500 by independent home tutors, against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an exam-year specialist. A family in Al Ain and a family on Saadiyat Island choose from the same pool online, and from very different pools otherwise.

Private schools in Abu Dhabi are overseen by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from any regulator or examination board, and no page of ours should suggest otherwise. Individual private tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years.

Two further limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and a top-grade target in particular depends on thresholds nobody knows in advance. And where no specialist is free for your subject at the hours you need, we say so and offer a different slot, a later start or a referral rather than filling the hour with someone who cannot mark the paper to the published scheme.

process.title: Send one email to the exams officer
process.description: Ask which board and option code each subject is entered under, on which grade scale it is reported, at which tier, and when the internal entry cut-off falls. Those four answers determine whether a top grade is even available in that series, and they cost nothing to obtain.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a recent marked paper
process.description: One free trial lesson with the subject specialist, on the condition that it is a single lesson, spent reading a marked paper against the published mark scheme. The output is a written list of where the last marks went, grouped into the five top-band habits.

process.title: Read the published thresholds for the subject
process.description: Look up the board's published grade thresholds for recent series in that specific subject. That converts a vague target into a number of marks in play, which is the difference between a cheap narrow plan and an expensive broad one.

process.title: Install one habit at a time, with a stated test
process.description: Short frequent sessions, one named habit each, with a marked timed section every second session to show whether the correction held. Naming the test in advance makes the plan checkable, and if the habit has not moved we change the approach rather than repeating it.

process.title: Rehearse the components the school practises least
process.description: Alternative-to-practical papers, long data-analysis questions and timed composition, under the real duration and marked strictly. These hold a disproportionate share of top-band marks precisely because they are awkward for a classroom to run regularly.

process.title: The honest fallback
process.description: If the entry is at Core tier, a top grade is not available in that series and we say so rather than selling a campaign for it. If no specialist is free at the hours you need, we offer a different slot, a later start or a referral elsewhere.

whyPoints.description: Cambridge reports most international GCSE subjects A* to G and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1, and Abu Dhabi schools use both, sometimes within one year group. faqs.question: Does my child's IGCSE board even award an A*?
faqs.answer: Check per subject, because Abu Dhabi schools use both boards and sometimes mix them within a year group. Cambridge International reports most international GCSE subjects on an A* to G scale, so an A* exists there. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 scale, where the top grade is a 9 and no A* is issued. One email to the exams officer asking which board and option code each subject is entered under settles it, and it changes the target you should be working towards.

faqs.question: Is a grade 9 the same as an A*?
faqs.answer: They are top grades on two different scales, and how they compare is determined by the boards and interpreted by the institutions reading them, not by a tutoring service. The 9 to 1 scale was designed with the top band set above the previous top grade, so the two are not a straight swap. Where the comparison matters to your family, read the board's own published explanation and ask the receiving sixth form or university in writing what it requires on which scale.

faqs.question: Can a candidate entered at Core tier still get a top grade?
faqs.answer: No. In tiered subjects the top grades are available only at Extended tier, and the tier is fixed in the entry submitted by the centre before its internal cut-off. A Core entry caps the ceiling for that series regardless of performance, and no teaching changes it afterwards. This is why the first action in a top-grade plan is confirming the tier in writing. If the entry is already at Core, the honest options are a later series or a different target.

faqs.question: What percentage does an A* need in IGCSE?
faqs.answer: There is no standing figure, and any page quoting one is reporting a single historical series or inventing it. Grade thresholds are set per series by the board after the papers have been sat and the cohort's performance is known, and they differ by subject, by component and by series. What you can do is read the board's published thresholds for recent series in your child's specific subject, which gives a realistic band and turns a vague target into a number of marks in play.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE component holds the most recoverable top-band marks?
faqs.answer: In the sciences, the alternative-to-practical paper, and it is also the component schools practise least because it is awkward to run. It asks candidates to identify variables, criticise a method, read a scale precisely, draw a graph to the expected conventions and justify anomalies. None of that is covered by revising theory. Three or four past papers of that component, marked strictly, usually produces more marks per hour than any other block available in Physics, Chemistry or Biology.

faqs.question: My child understands everything but still misses the top grade. Why?
faqs.answer: Five habits account for most of it, and all five are visible in a marked script. Method lines left unwritten, because the step was obvious. Command words answered loosely, so a described answer meets an explain question. Papers not finished, because a six-mark answer was given to a three-mark question earlier. Rounding before the final step, or units and labels omitted. And no sanity check on a result any sketch would have flagged. Each is a habit with a fixed cost in sessions, not a knowledge gap.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a top-band repair usually take?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, which is why the diagnostic comes first. Installing a method-line or command-word habit is typically two or three sessions plus short marked sets to maintain it, because habits regress under exam pressure. Rehearsing a low-frequency component such as alternative-to-practical is three or four papers. A genuine content gap is the expensive case and the only one that justifies a term. A marked paper tells you which of these you are buying.

faqs.question: What does Extended-tier coaching cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the emirate run AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150, and AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an exam-year specialist, per Bestimate's Dubai rate table, with TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online options run AED 33 to AED 65, per Tutopiya and EdFlik. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list, and for a top-band candidate the number of hours matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: Should we rehearse with past papers or with the textbook?
faqs.answer: Past papers, marked against the published mark scheme, every time. At the top of the range the content is known and the marks are going to how answers are presented, which a textbook cannot show. The important discipline is marking strictly rather than generously, because a generous mark conceals exactly the small losses the campaign is meant to remove. Use the official sources for papers and schemes; we link them rather than redistributing material that belongs to the boards.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge zone timetable matter for a June entry?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it takes five minutes to check. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the centre which zone it sits in and build the revision calendar from that timetable. A plan built from the wrong version can place a candidate in the wrong room on the wrong day.

faqs.question: Can my child bank a strong paper and re-sit a weaker one?
faqs.answer: On some Pearson qualifications the modular structure allows a candidate to carry forward a result and re-sit a component rather than the whole qualification, which is a genuinely useful option for a top-grade candidate. Cambridge's structure differs and the carry-forward rules are set by the board. Either way the sequencing decision sits with the entry, so raise it with the exams officer early rather than assuming. The answer changes how a campaign is planned and what it costs.

faqs.question: Is a top IGCSE grade necessary for an Abu Dhabi sixth form?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by each school and published on its own admissions pages, and several specify both grade and tier for AS sciences and mathematics. Ask the receiving school in writing which grades on which scale it requires, since it may be reading both grade scales in the same admissions round. Nothing on this page implies that tutoring is required to meet an admissions requirement; the requirement belongs to the institution and the route through it is the institution's to describe.

faqs.question: How late can a top-grade plan still start?
faqs.answer: Habits need a term to install and maintain, so a plan beginning after the mock window is working with less than it should. Even so, the two highest-yield blocks are both short: rehearsing the low-frequency components, and timed full papers in the final weeks. A candidate starting eight weeks out can still realistically do both. What cannot be done late is building algebraic fluency or closing a genuine content gap, and an honest adviser says which case applies.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series does an Abu Dhabi centre enter candidates for?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series; the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Build any plan against the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date, because provisional timetables are revised. Your centre confirms which series it has entered your child for.

abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.closingHeading: Settle the scale and the tier, then find the last marks
abu-dhabi/igcse-a-star-coaching.closingBody: Two emails and one session do most of the work on this page. Ask the exams officer which board, option code, grade scale and tier each subject is entered under, and when the internal cut-off falls. Then look up the board's published thresholds for recent series in that subject, so the target becomes a number of marks rather than a letter. Finally, have one recent marked paper read against the mark scheme to find which of the five top-band habits is costing them. Book a free trial lesson with a subject specialist for that reading and keep the written list either way.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.tutorsIntro: The teachers below run one-to-one IGCSE classes over live video for Abu Dhabi students. Each teaches to a named specification rather than to a general subject, and will tell you which paper codes a student is entered for before the first class is scheduled.

intro.heading: A class is only useful if it matches the specification
paragraphs: Parents searching for IGCSE classes in Abu Dhabi usually mean one of four different things: a group class at a centre, a small online class with a handful of students, one-to-one teaching sold by the hour, or a holiday revision course. These are not variations of one product. They differ in how much individual attention an hour contains, in whether a student can ask a question mid-explanation, and above all in whether the material matches the specification that child is entered for.

The specification question is the one almost nobody asks first, and it decides everything else. Mathematics is Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1, and those are different papers with different tiering language and a different balance of question types. Physics is 0625 or 4PH1. Chemistry is 0620 or 4CH1. A class advertised as IGCSE Physics with no code attached is a class that will match some of its students and quietly mismatch the rest, and the mismatch shows up in April rather than in October.

Science is where this bites hardest. A student on a combined or co-ordinated award is not studying a shortened version of three separate sciences; the content map is different, and the papers are different. Every term, families discover that their child has spent months revising from separate-science notes for material that will never be examined, while leaving gaps in the parts the award does assess. Establishing the route before booking a class is a ten-minute conversation with the school that saves a term.

There is a second timetable running alongside the international one. Under the federal position, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge. Those subjects compete for the same evenings as IGCSE revision, and a class plan that ignores them is a plan that falls over in November.

All classes described here are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run a centre, a campus or a visiting service anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is something we offer only in India. That is relevant to the comparison this page makes, because the honest case for a one-to-one online class is the individual attention per hour and the match to the specification, not convenience. The sections below give you the code map, the attention arithmetic, the science routes, the Arabic and Islamic Education position and the equivalency rules that outlast all of it. Read the tables as reference material you can take to a parents' evening. The code map, the attention arithmetic and the science routes are all questions a school will answer in one email, and the answers decide which class is worth paying for long before any provider is compared on price.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.programmesIntro: An IGCSE class plan has to fit four things: the board, the tier, the year group and the mandatory subjects running in parallel. The blocks below set out what each of those changes about the class a student should actually be sitting in.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE specifications
programmes.description: Cambridge codes are four digits and they are not interchangeable with anything else: 0580 Mathematics, 0607 International Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0653 Combined Science, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, 0500 First Language English, 0510 English as a Second Language, 0455 Economics, 0460 Geography, 0470 History, 0478 Computer Science. The tiering language is Core and Extended.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your Abu Dhabi school's exams officer which zone the centre sits in.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications
programmes.description: Pearson codes begin with a 4: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A, 4EB1 English Language B, 4ET1 English Literature. The tiering language is Foundation and Higher. Question style, mark distribution across papers and the balance of short to extended responses all differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and provisional timetables are published ahead of each series. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Build a class schedule against the live official timetable rather than a remembered date, because provisional dates can be revised.

programmes.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
programmes.description: These subjects run alongside the international curriculum rather than instead of it, and the first-language and additional-language Arabic routes assess very different things. For students who later seek UAE equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required IGCSE subjects, which surprises many families and changes how they allocate revision time.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's regulator KHDA publishes detailed mandatory-subject guidelines, including that instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and that classes for Arabs and non-Arabs must be organised separately. Abu Dhabi families should confirm the current requirements with their school and with ADEK, since the emirate publishes its own regulatory framework.

programmes.name: After Year 11: A Level, IB Diploma and equivalency
programmes.description: IGCSE results act as the entry gate to A Level and the IB Diploma Programme, and as part of the Ministry of Education equivalency file for students applying to UAE universities. That makes subject and tier choices in Year 9 consequential for Year 13, particularly where a sixth-form course names a specific IGCSE grade as a prerequisite.
programmes.countryNote: On the British track, Gulf Today reported the requirement as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One competing site publishes a six-subject figure; verify on the Ministry's own channel.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask for classes in, each with the code that decides which papers are sat. If a provider cannot tell you which code their class teaches, that is the question to settle before any other.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most commonly taught IGCSE class and the most commonly mismatched, because Cambridge Extended and Pearson Higher cover overlapping but non-identical content. A class built on one board's past papers leaves a student from the other rehearsing the wrong distribution of question types for a year.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0580, with its own assessment structure including an investigation component at the Extended tier. Students entered for 0607 who join a 0580 class are sitting in the wrong room, and the mismatch is usually noticed late because the topic names look familiar.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The practical assessment route is the decision that changes a class plan: an alternative-to-practical paper rewards method description, scale reading and control-variable identification, which are teachable skills and rarely taught at home. Confirm which route the school enters before booking.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Classes here live or die on calculation fluency and extended-response structure. Moles work splits into a mass-to-moles step and a ratio step, and the second is where most marks go; organic chemistry rewards pattern recognition rather than memorised lists.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The widest content map of the three sciences, which makes class pace the critical variable. A group class moving at the mean leaves the quickest students bored and the slowest unable to ask, and Biology is the subject where that gap compounds fastest across a year.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, single or double award
subjects.description: A distinct content map rather than a reduced one. Students on these awards sit their own papers, and revising from separate-science material wastes hours on content that will not be examined while leaving the assessed parts thin. Establish the route before anything else.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading marks go to selection and inference rather than retelling, and the directed writing task is marked on audience and register. Classes work best when every session includes writing produced under time, because the skill is performative rather than informational.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The choice between First and Second Language English sets a ceiling that can affect later applications, so it deserves a deliberate conversation with the school. Within the paper, summary and note-making tasks respond quickly to structured class work.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both reward a definition or a diagram before the explanation, and both award evaluation marks only for a judgement with a stated condition. These are class-friendly skills, because a modelled answer discussed aloud teaches several students at once.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study recall decides Geography and source handling decides History, and both need specific named detail rather than general understanding. A class that produces one case-study card per topic per week leaves a student with a usable revision set by March.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are examined and rarely practised, which makes them reliable class material. The practical components reward methodical evidence in the format the mark scheme expects rather than the shorthand a student invents for themselves.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Foreign Language (Cambridge 0508 / 0544)
subjects.levels: First Language and Foreign Language routes
subjects.description: Two genuinely different qualifications sharing a language. Treating the foreign-language route as an easier version of the first-language one is the most frequent planning error in this emirate, and the routes need separate class material from the start.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.regionsIntro: Class format and class timing are decided more by geography than parents expect. Where a household sits in Abu Dhabi determines whether a centre-based group class is realistic at all, and what time a live class can start on a school night.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Rawdah
regions.note: Close to several of the emirate's long-established British-curriculum schools, so centre-based group classes are a genuine option here. The trade-off is pace: a group moving at the mean rarely matches a student who is strong in two topics and weak in one.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Villa communities with several children per household, where the practical constraint is the family calendar rather than the drive. Staggered one-to-one slots usually work better than a shared group class booked around one child's timetable.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: A corridor where a centre class means a real round trip on a school night. Families here commonly compare the drive plus the class against a live class starting at the same hour with no travel attached at either end.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Smaller catchments with high rates of mid-course transfer between curricula. New arrivals need a specification audit before a class is booked, because the subject names transfer across systems and the papers do not.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-rise addresses where study space is often shared. A one-to-one class with headphones and a fixed sixty minutes is more workable than a group session that assumes a quiet desk and a printer in the room.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zahiyah
regions.note: Newer residential pockets with a mixed school map, so siblings are frequently on different boards. A household here can need a Cambridge class for one child and a Pearson class for the other in the same subject.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Mussafah
regions.note: The longest drives to the island school cluster. A centre-based class on a weekday evening usually cannot start before seven here once traffic is counted, which is why live classes and weekend slots dominate.

regions.name: Al Shamkha, Al Falah and Al Reef
regions.note: Outer communities with large school cohorts and busy mandatory-subject timetables. Class plans here have to account for Arabic and Islamic Education commitments as well as nine IGCSE subjects.

schoolClusters.city: The island cluster: Al Bateen, Al Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and Al Rawdah
schoolClusters.note: Established British-curriculum cohorts entering large IGCSE cohorts each year, with both boards represented across the cluster. Students we support here most often need Mathematics and the separate sciences, and most often arrive knowing their syllabus codes.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, Al Reem and the Khalifa City to Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: Academies serving the newer residential bands, with a high proportion of students joining mid-course. Specification audits are the most common first request from this cluster, because transferring students often do not know which award they have been entered for.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland: Mussafah, Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Al Shamkha and Al Reef
schoolClusters.note: Large entries across a wide fee range, with several schools running combined and co-ordinated science awards alongside separate sciences in the same year group. Confirming which award applies is the first step for almost every class here.

abu-dhabi/igcse-classes.modesIntro: Three ways to take a class, all delivered one-to-one over live video. The differences are in pace, in what the hour produces, and in how a student's own questions get answered, which is the thing group formats cannot guarantee.

modes.title: Specification class, weekly through the course
modes.description: A weekly class following the entered specification in order, with the syllabus code written on the plan. The pace is set by one student's understanding rather than a cohort mean, so a topic already secure is covered in ten minutes and a topic that is not gets a full session. The record shows which specification points have been covered and when.
bullets: Specification points ticked off against the board's own order
Pace set by the student, not by a group average
Questions answered inside the explanation, not afterwards
A coverage record you can compare against the school's scheme of work

modes.title: Topic class, booked where the gap is
modes.description: Single classes aimed at one topic that has not landed, bought as needed rather than on a subscription. Families use this where the school is covering the course competently and one or two topics have gone past without sticking. Each class ends with a short piece of written work that tests whether the gap has actually closed.
bullets: One named topic per class, agreed in advance
No ongoing commitment or minimum block
A short written check at the end of each class
Useful where the school's teaching is otherwise sound

modes.title: Holiday intensive, between terms
modes.description: Concentrated classes in the school holidays, when there is time for several sessions a week. The usual purpose is a catch-up across a whole unit, or a head start on a Year 11 topic known to be difficult. Sessions are shorter and more frequent than during term, which suits content consolidation better than long single blocks.

sections.heading: What an Abu Dhabi parent means by IGCSE classes
paragraphs: The search phrase covers four products with very different economics. A group class at a centre, typically six to fifteen students working through a specification at a shared pace. A small online class, often four to eight. One-to-one teaching sold by the hour. And a holiday revision course, compressed into a week or two. Families usually compare them on price per hour, which is the least informative comparison available.

The comparison that matters is individual attention per hour and match to the specification. In a class of twelve, a student gets perhaps four or five minutes of attention directed at their own understanding across an hour, even with an excellent teacher. That is not a criticism of group teaching; it is arithmetic. Group teaching earns its place when the material is new to everybody and the cohort is genuinely at a similar point, which is exactly the condition a school already provides for six hours a day.

The second question is whether the class teaches the specification your child is entered for. A centre running a mixed class of Cambridge and Pearson candidates has to teach the intersection of two specifications, and the intersection is smaller than either. A class advertised as IGCSE Chemistry without a code is a warning sign rather than a convenience, because somebody in that room is being taught to the wrong paper.

The third is pace. A student who is secure in half a specification and lost in the other half is poorly served by any class moving linearly through all of it, group or otherwise. That is the single strongest argument for one-to-one at this stage of a course: not more attention in the abstract, but the ability to spend forty minutes on electrolysis and four on the states of matter, because that is what this particular student needs this particular week.

sections.heading: The code map: the same subject, two different specifications
paragraphs: Every IGCSE subject exists in more than one version, and the version decides the papers. The table below maps the codes Abu Dhabi families meet most often. Read it with your child's option sheet beside you, because a single nine-subject timetable in this emirate frequently spans both boards, and the mismatch between what a class teaches and what a student sits is almost always invisible until a mock paper arrives.

The differences are not cosmetic. Cambridge tiers are Core and Extended; Pearson tiers are Foundation and Higher, and the content included in each differs. The number of papers sat, how marks are distributed across them, and the balance of short-answer to extended-response questions all vary. In the sciences, the practical assessment route differs again, with alternative-to-practical papers assessing a specific set of method and data skills.

There is also a within-board trap. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are separate syllabuses with different assessment structures, and the topic names look similar enough that a student entered for 0607 can sit happily in a 0580 class for months. Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 are likewise distinct from each other and from the separate sciences.

Getting this right costs one email. Ask the school for each subject's syllabus code, the tier entered, and the series the entry is for. Write the answers on a single sheet and give a copy to any provider before a class is booked. A provider who does not want that sheet is telling you how specific their teaching is going to be.

sections.heading: Individual attention per hour: the arithmetic of class size
paragraphs: Dividing an hour by the number of students in the room gives a number that explains most of what families observe about classes. In a group of twelve, even distribution gives each student five minutes of teacher attention directed at their own work. In practice distribution is never even: confident students ask and receive, quiet students watch. A student who needs to interrupt an explanation three times to follow it cannot do that in a group without stopping eleven other people.

That arithmetic is why group classes are good value for some purposes and poor value for others. New content delivered to a cohort at a similar level works well in a group, and the school is already doing it. Diagnosis of one student's specific errors, or re-teaching a topic a student has already failed to absorb once, does not work in a group at any price per hour.

Published rates in this market help place the comparison. Providers quote roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200 to 450 and above for a subject specialist, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase publishing AED 270. Group formats are cheaper per student per hour, as they must be. The useful question is cost per minute of attention your child actually receives, which often inverts the ranking.

One practical test before booking any group class: ask how the provider handles a student who is behind the group on one topic and ahead on another. The answers divide neatly. Some will say the student should book an additional one-to-one session, which is honest and tells you what the group class is actually for. Others will say the class is paced to suit everybody, which is not a thing a class can do.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: This is the most consequential thing on the page and the thing families most often get wrong. IGCSE science comes in separate subjects, a co-ordinated award and a combined award, and they are not versions of each other. The papers differ, the content differs, and the number of IGCSE grades the student walks away with differs, which matters for the five-subject equivalency count later.

The practical damage is always the same shape. A student on Cambridge Combined Science 0653 revises from a friend's separate Chemistry 0620 notes, spends weeks on content their paper will not assess, and arrives in the exam thin on the material it does. Nobody notices because the topic headings overlap. The reverse happens too: a separate-science student using combined-award material finds the depth insufficient and does not know why.

Then there is the practical assessment question, which sits alongside the route. Where a centre enters students for an alternative-to-practical paper, that paper assesses specific skills: reading a scale accurately, identifying independent and control variables, describing a method precisely enough to be repeated, and handling data from an experiment the student never performed. These are teachable in a class and are rarely taught at home.

Ask the school three things in one email. Which award each science is entered for and its code. Which papers that award sits. And which practical route the centre uses. The answers take five minutes to obtain and they determine every past paper your child should be practising for the next two years. Any provider should want them before scheduling a first class.
