sections.heading: The review point, and the right to conclude stop
paragraphs: Every tuition arrangement should have a date at which it is formally evaluated, agreed before the first payment, with a named check that will be repeated. Without that, the default is continuation, and continuation is where budgets quietly go. Four weeks is the right interval for the first review: long enough for a technique change to show, short enough that an unproductive match has not consumed a term.

The evaluation needs an artefact rather than a conversation. The same diagnostic repeated - a timed section, a marked past-paper question set, a fixed set of problems - placed beside the original with both dates visible. Alongside it, one piece of work the student completed unaided that they could not complete four weeks earlier. Those two things answer the question. A tutor's confidence, a student's improved mood and a parent's sense that things feel calmer are all pleasant and none of them is evidence.

Three outcomes are legitimate at that review. Continue, because the check moved. Change target, because the check did not move and the diagnosis was wrong - which happens, and which is a tutor's responsibility to say first. Or stop, because tuition is not the constraint. We would rather make that third recommendation and keep the relationship for the subject where we can help than carry a booking that is not working. A provider who has never recommended stopping to anybody is not a provider whose continuation advice is worth much.
bullets: Agree the review date and the repeated check before the first payment
Evaluate on an artefact, not on how the sessions felt
Ask for one task the student now completes unaided and could not before
Continue, change target, or stop - all three are legitimate outcomes

process.title: Send a marked paper and the entry details
process.description: One marked mock or past paper, plus the board, syllabus code and tier for the subject. The paper lets a tutor form a hypothesis before the trial; the entry details stop you funding a target the tier has already capped. Both are free to obtain.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: One real topic, with the marked work on screen. No charge, no card details, one trial per student, and no obligation to book. The tutor who teaches it is the tutor you would continue with unless you ask to change.

process.title: Get the loss and the session count in writing
process.description: You should finish the trial with the named loss, a statement of whether it is technique or content, and an estimate of how many sessions each would take. Sometimes the right estimate is zero, because the school's own clinic covers it. We say so when that is the case.

process.title: Choose the shape, not just the rate
process.description: Monthly weekly sessions for an open-ended gap, a fixed block with an end date for a diagnosed narrow one, or nothing beyond the diagnostic hour. We quote the shape with the notice period, the marking position and the expiry position stated.

process.title: Written task every session, checked in the next
process.description: Each session sets one short written task with a hand-in, and the next session begins by checking it. That loop is what converts teaching into retention. It also makes the four-week review meaningful, because there is a record of independent work to look at.

process.title: Four-week review with a repeated check
process.description: The same diagnostic is repeated at four sessions and placed beside the original. Continue, change target or stop - and if the honest reading is stop, you hear it from us rather than deciding it three months later after the money has gone.

whyPoints.title: We publish AED figures and say whose they are
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page carries the provider that published it and the date. Three of the six competitor pages we researched publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. A market figure with a source attached is worth more to you than a confident range with none.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: IB Gram runs no home visits in the UAE; home tuition is an India-only service. In Abu Dhabi that removes between a quarter and a half of a visiting quote in the longer-drive communities, and that money converts into contact hours rather than into fuel.

whyPoints.title: Marking is inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Written work set between sessions is marked within the session rather than billed separately. Marking charged hourly can add a third to a monthly total, and a provider who separates it has an incentive to set work rather than to teach.

whyPoints.title: A diagnostic you can buy on its own
whyPoints.description: A single hour that names the loss, prices the fix and checks the tier, with no obligation to book anything after it. For a meaningful share of families that hour is the entire purchase, and we would rather sell it honestly than pad it into a term.

whyPoints.title: Short commitments and a cheap exit
whyPoints.description: Monthly invoicing with a stated notice period, no expiry on sessions inside an agreed window, and a tutor change offered on request in the first fortnight with a second trial at no charge. The cheapest thing about a wrong match should be leaving it.

whyPoints.title: A review that is allowed to say stop
whyPoints.description: The four-week review repeats the original check and compares artefacts rather than impressions. Where tuition is not the constraint - a reading-rate issue, a tier ceiling, an options choice - we say so, which costs us the booking and is the reason to trust the other advice.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE home tuition cost per hour in Abu Dhabi right now?
faqs.answer: Published figures as at October 2026, each from the provider that published it: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65; Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; Unitors IGCSE from AED 150; TutorChase AED 270; BartyED AED 650. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors advertising up to AED 500, and specialist exam-year tuition at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly packages advertised in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those are IB Gram's prices; they are the market you should hold any quote against, including ours.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition in Abu Dhabi more expensive than online for the same tutor quality?
faqs.answer: Mostly travel. A visiting quote has to pay for the drive, and in this emirate that is a real cost: a journey from the island to Al Shamkha, Al Falah or Al Reef at 17:00 is neither short nor predictable, and a tutor can fit fewer sessions into an afternoon. The published gap is roughly AED 180 to 500 in-home against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one. There is a second, hidden premium: a 60-minute visiting slot commonly delivers teaching in the low forties of minutes once arrival and settling are counted, so the effective cost per teaching hour is higher than the quoted rate suggests.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Abu Dhabi if we pay the in-home rate?
faqs.answer: No, at any price. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE - home tuition is a service we provide only in India - so there is no in-home rate to quote. Abu Dhabi lessons are one-to-one over live video, with your child's marked papers shared on screen and annotated during the session. The cost effect is that the travel premium does not exist, and the coverage effect is larger: a household in Al Falah selects from everyone who teaches their syllabus and tier, rather than from the adults willing to drive out there on a weekday afternoon.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do we actually need to see a grade move?
faqs.answer: One to two per subject, with written work in between. Below one a week, the interval exceeds the period over which a newly taught method stays available, so each session starts with recovery rather than progress - which is why a budget spread across five subjects at fortnightly contact moves nothing. Above two a week in one subject, the limiting factor stops being teaching and becomes the independent work the student does alone, so additional sessions mostly displace the practice that makes them useful. The sweet band is one or two sessions and one short written task, checked at the start of the next lesson.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper overall to start IGCSE tuition in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and not because of the rate. In Year 10 an hour can teach: there is room to rebuild algebraic manipulation across six to eight sessions, which improves Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry simultaneously - the only real multiplier in this market. In February of Year 11 the same weakness is patched topic by topic at full cost without the multiplier, and the subject count has usually grown because more things have slipped. Households that start in Year 10 generally spend less across the two years than those that start in Year 11, and demand peaks in the spring, which firms up rates exactly when late starters are looking.

faqs.question: Should I buy a monthly package or pay per session?
faqs.answer: Either, provided you know four things before you pay: the notice period for cancelling, whether unused sessions expire and when, whether marking of written work sits inside the rate or is billed separately, and what happens if the match is wrong in week two. Packages are fine where those answers are reasonable and dangerous where they are not - term-end expiry can forfeit sessions already paid for, and separately billed marking can add a third to a monthly total. Monthly invoicing with a stated notice period is the lowest-risk shape while you still do not know whether the tutor suits your child.

faqs.question: Does the quoted tuition price include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, and get the answer on the invoice rather than in a message. We will not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees generally on this page, because doing so responsibly requires a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an opinion, and several pages in this search result state it as settled fact. What you are entitled to is clarity about the specific figure you are being quoted: whether it is inclusive, what the invoice will show, and whether any package price changes that position. A provider who cannot answer that about their own price is worth a second look.

faqs.question: Is group tuition at an Abu Dhabi centre better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: On cost per booked hour, clearly. On cost per minute of individual attention, no - a group of four divides the hour four ways. Groups work reasonably where the content is new to everybody and the pace suits the whole group, which is why they suit general revision better than a diagnosed individual gap. If a marked paper shows your child losing marks specifically on quantitative chemistry while the rest scores normally, a group covering the whole syllabus will spend most of its time on material your child already has. Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City have more group availability than the island communities do.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest way families here waste money on tuition?
faqs.answer: Continuing past the point where it stopped working, because no review date was ever set. The default in an informal arrangement is continuation, so a plan with no stop condition becomes an annuity. The fix costs nothing: agree before the first payment that at four sessions the original diagnostic will be repeated and placed beside the first result, with one piece of unaided work the student could not have produced earlier. Then the decision is made on artefacts rather than on how the sessions felt. Continue, change target or stop are all legitimate, and a tutor should be willing to recommend the third.

faqs.question: Can we just pay a tutor to help with the homework the school sets?
faqs.answer: You can, and it is one of the least productive purchases available. A session driven by the week's homework follows the school's timetable rather than your child's actual losses, so the content is whatever happens to be due rather than what is costing marks. It feels reassuring because something gets finished, and it rarely moves a grade. The more useful version takes the same hour and spends it on the repeated loss a marked paper identified, with a short written task set and checked next week. If homework completion is the real problem, that is a self-management issue and worth naming as one.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for the November resit if the June grade disappoints?
faqs.answer: Two separate costs, and the second is the one families forget. Entry runs through an examination centre registered with the board, and the centre sets its own fee and its own deadline on top of the board's - so the figure depends on the centre rather than on any national rate, and it is worth asking two centres. The tuition cost is small if the decision is quick: a single-subject resit with a diagnosed narrow gap is often a six to eight session block. It becomes expensive if the decision drifts into September, because by then entry deadlines and useful preparation time have both narrowed.

faqs.question: Our child is entered at Core tier - does that change what we should spend?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and in a way most quotes ignore. Tiered Cambridge and Pearson subjects award a restricted grade range at the lower tier, so money spent chasing a top grade in a Core or Foundation entry buys something the papers cannot deliver. Before funding anything, ask the school's examinations officer in writing for the tier, the maximum awardable grade at that tier, and whether a change deadline is still open. If it is open, the sensible spend is a short block aimed at producing the evidence for a move up. If it has closed, the sensible spend is maximising the grade available at the current tier, which is cheaper and different work.

faqs.question: What should a free trial include, and what should make me suspicious?
faqs.answer: It should include a stated length, no payment details, no obligation, and - the part that matters - a named diagnosis at the end. Ours is 45 minutes, one per student, with no card details taken, and it works best when you send a marked paper first so the session tests a hypothesis rather than forming one. Be suspicious of a trial that requires card details to begin, since that is a subscription with a delayed first payment. Be equally suspicious of one that ends in enthusiasm without a named loss, a technique-or-content judgement and a session estimate, because none of those are available from rapport alone.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put both of my children in one session?
faqs.answer: Only if they are in the same year, on the same syllabus and at the same tier. Otherwise a shared hour means one child taught while the other waits, and you have paid full price for half the attention each. The arrangement that genuinely saves is one tutor across consecutive slots - say 35 minutes for a Year 9 and 50 for a Year 11 - which keeps the household to a single evening block, gives each child their own target and record, and lets one tutor fix a shared household gap, usually algebra, once instead of twice. A provider who suggests sharing without asking each child's year is managing their calendar.

faqs.question: Is there anything we should try before paying for tuition at all?
faqs.answer: Two things, both free. Ask the head of year what subject support the school already runs - most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools hold clinics and catch-up sessions delivered by the staff who wrote and marked the mocks, and they are frequently under-used because nobody told the student to attend. And get the entry details in writing: board, syllabus code and tier for each subject. Those two actions cost nothing, and between them they resolve a meaningful share of the enquiries we receive - either because free provision covers the gap, or because the real problem was a tier or route decision rather than teaching.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tuition.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis first, then decide how much to spend
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tuition.closingBody: If you are pricing IGCSE home tuition in Abu Dhabi, start with the two free actions: ask your school what support it already runs, and get the board, syllabus code and tier for each subject in writing. Then book the free 45-minute trial lesson, with a marked paper sent in advance. You finish with the named loss, a technique-or-content judgement and an estimate of sessions needed - sometimes zero. No charge and no card details. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, invoiced monthly, with marking included and a four-week review that is allowed to conclude stop.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one school week, and the hours that actually exist
paragraphs: An Abu Dhabi Year 11 student sits eight to ten IGCSE subjects. The school day ends somewhere between 14:30 and 15:15. The bus from an island school to Khalifa City or Al Reef eats another forty to sixty minutes. Two afternoons a week there is a club or a squad that finishes at 16:30. There is Arabic homework, there is a coursework deadline somebody forgot to write down, and by 20:00 the student is finished regardless of what the revision timetable says. The question behind an IGCSE home tutor search is rarely which subject. It is where does the hour come from.

This page answers that first, because the answer constrains everything else. In an Abu Dhabi week there are usually three genuinely usable focused windows, not seven, and they are not where parents assume. Two short sessions placed in those windows do more than one long session wedged into a Thursday evening, and a Saturday morning is worth roughly double a weekday evening for anything requiring sustained thought. A tutoring plan that ignores this gets abandoned in week five and the family concludes tutoring does not work.

The second thing this page does is state what a tutor can and cannot change, component by component. IGCSE grades are not a single thing. A written theory paper is highly responsive to teaching. A speaking endorsement in a language, an assessed practical, an art portfolio or a controlled assessment administered by the school are not responsive to an outside tutor in the same way, and some of them are not responsive at all. Any provider willing to sell you tuition for all of them without distinguishing between them is selling hours rather than outcomes.

On the home-tutoring question itself, the honest position. Visiting IGCSE tutors are a real market in Abu Dhabi and published rates run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel folded in, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. Home tuition is a service we provide only in India. In Abu Dhabi the lesson is one-to-one over live video, with your child's own marked papers shared on screen and annotated as the tutor talks.

That is a real constraint and it comes with a real compensation: the tutor is chosen for the syllabus rather than for the postcode. A household in Al Shamkha or Al Falah choosing a visiting tutor is choosing among the adults prepared to make that drive at 17:30. The same household choosing online is choosing among everyone who teaches Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier. For mainstream Mathematics the difference may be small. For second-language English routes, for Arabic as a first language, or for a minority syllabus, the pool is the entire decision - and where we cannot cover something, this page says so rather than offering an approximate match.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The stage matters more than the subject. What is worth buying in the Year 9 options year, in Year 10, in the autumn of Year 11 and in the final six weeks are four different purchases, and families routinely buy the wrong one for the stage they are in.

programmes.name: Year 9: the options year
programmes.description: Nothing is entered yet, so everything is still cheap to fix. The work that pays off here is algebraic fluency, scientific vocabulary and writing a paragraph that answers a question. A student who leaves Year 9 secure in those three is a candidate for the higher tier in several subjects rather than one.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools run options evenings in this year, and the decisions taken there - Computer Science against ICT, three separate sciences against a coordinated award, First Language against Second Language English - shape the next four years more than any tutoring will. One hour spent understanding the options sheet is worth more than ten spent on content.

programmes.name: Year 10: the teaching year
programmes.description: The only year in which an outside tutor can genuinely teach rather than triage, because there is room to stop and rebuild a foundation. Six to eight sessions on algebraic manipulation in Year 10 makes the back half of three subjects teachable. The same intervention is impossible in February of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Abu Dhabi families buy tuition in Year 10, and the ones who do spend less in total across the two years than the ones who start in Year 11. That is not a sales line; it is what happens when teaching replaces damage control.

programmes.name: Year 11, autumn term
programmes.description: Mocks, forecast grades and coursework deadlines land together. This is the term in which a marked mock paper becomes available, and that paper should drive every tutoring decision that follows - topic order set by marks dropped rather than by the textbook.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools collect forecast grades for the board well before the examinations, so performance improvements that arrive late in Year 11 may not be reflected in what the centre submitted. Families who care about forecast grades need the work done in the autumn, not the spring.

programmes.name: Year 11, the final stretch
programmes.description: Two subjects, not five. Timed sections, command-word reading, time allocation by marks, and the specific topics a marked paper has identified. The content phase is over; what moves now is technique and the handful of topics carrying the most marks.
programmes.countryNote: This is the period families in Al Raha and Khalifa City most often ask for daily sessions. Daily sessions in May usually produce a tired student. Three focused sessions a week with real work in between beats five sessions with none.

programmes.name: After the series: results, resits and the next course
programmes.description: Results, enquiries about results, November resit decisions and the gap into Year 12. Each has its own deadline, and the deadlines sit much earlier than families expect. A single-subject November resit is a normal arrangement, handled through an examination centre.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families deciding between a British sixth form and an IB Diploma place are often doing so in the weeks around results, which is also when resit deadlines bite. Both decisions deserve an hour of planning before any tuition is bought.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Below are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi households most often ask about, with the specific loss a tutor is being hired to stop and what four weeks of focused work realistically changes in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Four weeks of work on algebraic manipulation changes performance across the whole paper, because almost every later topic routes through it. Four weeks spent on individual topics while manipulation stays weak changes one topic. Diagnose which situation you are in before booking.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism carry a large share of the dropped marks, and circuit reasoning is teachable in about three sessions once the student stops treating every circuit as a new puzzle. The practical-skills component needs separate, deliberate attention and almost never gets it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry decide the grade and are typically taught once, early, and never revisited. Four sessions on quantitative chemistry moves more marks than a term of general revision. Equation precision is the other reliable gain at Extended tier.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The loss is language rather than knowledge: describing where the paper asked for an explanation, naming a process without its location, missing the comparative word. Data and graph questions are the fastest-moving component and respond within two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: The recurring problem is coverage rather than ability - students assume content is out of scope because the school has not reached it. A syllabus audit against the board's published document is session one, and it usually finds two topics nobody has taught.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with different components and a different reading by sixth forms. Summary and directed writing are the two most teachable parts of the whole IGCSE set, and both are technique rather than vocabulary.

subjects.name: English Language, First Language
subjects.description: Marks are decided by control of register and by answering the task set rather than the task imagined. Directed writing improves quickly with taught structures; reading responses improve more slowly, because they depend on inference built over years.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation selection and integration carry the marks, not quantity of reading. Unseen poetry is where unprepared candidates lose most and is also the most drillable component, because the approach is a repeatable procedure rather than a body of knowledge.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study command words decide the band: identify, explain, analyse and evaluate each require a different answer shape and length. Students who write everything they know land in the lower bands. Taught as structure, this subject moves faster than any other.

subjects.name: ICT and Computer Science
subjects.description: Two different qualifications routinely confused at options time. ICT is practical application work with a substantial coursework-style load; Computer Science examines algorithms, pseudocode and data representation under timed conditions. The wrong choice is not fixable by tuition.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Nearly all avoidable loss is failure to use named examples and failure to read the resource provided. Both are habits rather than knowledge gaps, which is why a well-targeted four-week block can move this subject more than a term of reading.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0508 First Language; 0544 Arabic Foreign Language
subjects.description: Two separate syllabuses at different paces, and placement in the wrong one wastes two years. Federal regulation requires private schools to teach Arabic language, so this is timetabled rather than optional, and support needs to match the route the school has entered.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: What changes between Abu Dhabi communities is the shape of the evening: when the bus drops, how far the club run is, and whether there is a desk in a quiet room. These are the households we are asked about most and what we plan around in each.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and Al Karamah
regions.note: Short journeys from several long-established schools, so a 16:00 session is realistic and the student is still alert. Households here more often have a dedicated study room, which makes a longer single session workable.

regions.name: Al Nahyan and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central island districts with mixed apartment and villa housing. Shared study space is the common constraint rather than travel, so sessions are scheduled for when a quiet room is actually available rather than at a fixed weekly time.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with schools nearby and a high proportion of mid-cycle arrivals. Syllabus-code mismatches surface here constantly, and the first session is usually an audit of what the student has actually been taught.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Long bus runs to island schools, so 17:00 is the practical floor for focused work. Two 50-minute sessions placed on separate days survive this corridor far better than one long block on a Thursday.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Bandar
regions.note: Apartment and marina housing with clubs running late twice a week. Saturday mornings are the most requested slot here, and for anything requiring sustained thought they are worth roughly double a weekday evening.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Mainland communities where a visiting tutor's drive is longest and the travel premium highest. Evening slots from 17:30 are normal, and online delivery changes the arithmetic here more than anywhere else in the emirate.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Large mixed districts with students travelling across the emirate to school. Household timetables vary widely, so the weekly slot is set after the first week rather than assumed at booking.

regions.name: Yas Island and Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Newer schools with a younger year-group profile, so Year 9 and Year 10 enquiries dominate. That is the better-value end of the arc, and families here tend to arrive before the Year 11 crunch.

schoolClusters.city: Island schools: Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
schoolClusters.note: Settled British-curriculum provision with well-established examination practice, and short journeys home for students living on the island. Boards and tiers still differ between schools and sometimes within a year group, so the examinations officer is the right first source rather than a parents' group chat.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and island corridor: Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas and Saadiyat
schoolClusters.note: Where most newer capacity sits and where the longest bus journeys are. A higher share of these households changed curriculum within the last two years, which is why coverage audits and tier checks matter more in this cluster than revision does.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE components a tutor can actually move
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is assembled from components, and they are not equally responsive to outside teaching. Written theory papers are the most responsive thing in school education: the content is published, the question types repeat, the mark schemes reward identifiable behaviours, and a student can practise under conditions that resemble the real thing. That is where tutoring earns its money. Several other components behave completely differently, and a provider who quotes one hourly rate across all of them is not telling you what you are buying.

Assessed practical work sits at the other end. Where a syllabus examines practical skills through work administered by the school, an outside tutor cannot influence the administration, the equipment or the supervision. What a tutor can do is teach the thinking the component assesses - variables, fair testing, measurement, uncertainty, drawing a conclusion the data supports - and rehearse the written alternative-to-practical paper where the syllabus uses one. That is genuinely useful and it is a narrower claim than families usually hear.

The same logic applies to speaking endorsements in languages, to art and design portfolios and to controlled assessments run under school supervision. Each has a boundary a tutor must not cross: the work submitted has to be the student's own, and boards treat breaches as malpractice with consequences falling on the student. A tutor teaches the skill, questions the plan, challenges a weak source and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not supply content for submission or rewrite a draft into adult prose. Ask any provider where their line is before you book; the answer is diagnostic.

sections.heading: Where the usable hours sit in an Abu Dhabi school week
paragraphs: A revision timetable that assumes seven evenings is a work of fiction, and students know it, which is why they stop looking at it in week two. The realistic count in an Abu Dhabi household is three usable focused windows per week, and the useful exercise is identifying which three rather than pretending there are more. School finishes between roughly 14:30 and 15:15. A bus run to Khalifa City, Al Shamkha or Al Reef consumes forty to sixty minutes. Two afternoons carry a club or a squad. Friday ends early but the day has a different rhythm, and Saturday morning is the single most valuable block in the week.

The placement rules are simple and they matter more than the total. Nothing demanding goes after 20:00, because what happens there is attendance rather than learning. The session that sets a written task and the session that checks it must sit on different days, or the task does not get done and the checking becomes a conversation about why. And the heaviest cognitive work - a full timed section, a coursework plan, a topic that cannot be split - goes in the weekend morning rather than the weekday evening.

This is also where online delivery stops being a compromise. A video lesson can start at 16:15 for a student who is home early and at 17:45 for one who is not, in the same week, without recalculating anybody's drive. During Ramadan it can move to a late-morning weekend slot or a post-Iftar evening without a rebooking negotiation. And if the family travels between Abu Dhabi and abroad over a half term, the sessions travel too. A visiting tutor's timetable is a fixed asset; a video slot is not.

sections.heading: Where marks are actually lost, and what four weeks changes
paragraphs: Parents arrive with a grade and a worry. What a tutor needs is the loss - the specific, repeated behaviour that is costing marks on paper. These are diagnosable, they are consistent across students, and they are mostly not what the student thinks is wrong. A Year 11 student will say they find Chemistry hard. The marked paper says they drop almost everything on quantitative questions and score normally on the rest. Those lead to completely different four weeks.

The pattern across subjects is that technique losses move fast and content losses move slowly. A student who writes everything they know in response to an evaluate command is losing marks to a habit, and habits can be replaced in three or four sessions with worked structures and immediate feedback. A student who has never understood moles is losing marks to absent knowledge, which takes longer and cannot be bluffed. Knowing which of the two you are paying to fix tells you how long to buy for, and a tutor who cannot tell you after one marked paper has not looked properly.

The table below is the version of this we use in a first session. It is deliberately specific, because generic advice about revision techniques is the thing this market is already saturated with. Note how often the fix is a procedure rather than a body of knowledge: read the resource before the question, name the example, write the comparative word, state the step the marker needs. Those are habits, and habits are what an outside tutor is unusually well placed to change, because they are visible in the first ten minutes of a session.

sections.heading: The study space, and the three things that break it
paragraphs: Tutoring fails in households more often for environmental reasons than academic ones, and the reasons are boringly consistent. The first is the phone. A student with a phone face-up beside them is not studying for fifty minutes; they are studying in ninety-second segments, and the cost is not the time lost but the restart each time. The fix is physical distance rather than willpower - the phone in another room, which students accept far more readily when it is framed as a condition of the session rather than a punishment.

The second is the absence of a working surface. A teenager revising on a bed is signalling to their own body that this is rest time, and performance follows the signal. This matters particularly in apartment households on Al Reem Island or Al Raha Beach where a bedroom is also the only quiet room. A kitchen table at a fixed hour works better than a desk that exists in theory. The third is noise, usually a younger sibling, usually at exactly the hour a Year 11 student has energy. Scheduling around it beats arguing with it, which is one reason we set the weekly slot after the first week rather than at booking.

For an online session the technical requirements are small and worth stating: a laptop rather than a phone, on a table; the student's own exercise book, past papers and a pen within reach; and a way to show written work, either a document camera, a phone propped over the page, or a photograph sent at the start of the session. Audio matters more than video - a session where the tutor cannot hear a muttered half-answer loses the most useful signal in the room. Headphones solve that for roughly the price of nothing.
bullets: Phone in another room, framed as a condition of the session
A table rather than a bed, even if it is the kitchen table at a fixed hour

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAE academic calendar
paragraphs: Revision plans written in October rarely survive the UAE calendar, and the collisions are predictable enough to plan for. Ramadan brings shortened school days and a completely different domestic rhythm, and it falls within the spring term, which is also the term carrying mocks, coursework deadlines and the run-up to the June series. A plan that assumes a stable weekday evening through that period is a plan that will be abandoned.

What works is moving rather than pausing. Many Abu Dhabi families shift a weekday evening session to a late-morning weekend slot during Ramadan, and others move to a post-Iftar evening session that is shorter and more focused than the one it replaces. Both are scheduling conversations rather than rebookings, and neither involves anybody recalculating a drive - which is the practical reason online delivery survives this period and a visiting arrangement often does not. Around Eid, the honest advice is to stop for the days themselves and resume rather than to schedule sessions nobody will attend.

The other calendar features worth planning around: the long summer, which is where the highest-value blocks sit for both Year 9 to 10 and Year 11 to 12 transitions; the half terms, which are long enough for a four-session block on one named gap; and the November series, which means a resit decision has to be made in the weeks around August results rather than in September. Build the plan around these rather than against them, and write the pause dates in at the start so a gap looks like a plan instead of a drop-out.
bullets: Shift sessions during Ramadan rather than pausing - weekend mornings or post-Iftar
Stop for Eid itself and resume; do not schedule sessions nobody attends

sections.heading: Coverage, and what happens when nobody suitable is free
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is a strange silence given that every provider has one. Ours is straightforward. For mainstream IGCSE subjects on either board a match is usually available within a few days. For minority syllabuses, for some language routes and for particular tier and board combinations, it can take longer, and sometimes nobody suitable is available at all. When that is the case we say so, because the alternative - a near-match who does not know the syllabus - costs a family more than a wait does.

This is also where the honest comparison with in-home tutoring sits. A visiting arrangement in Al Shamkha or Al Falah is constrained twice: by who teaches the subject and by who will drive there on a weekday afternoon. The intersection of those two sets can be empty for a specialist subject, and when it is, families end up with a generalist who is physically present. Online removes the second constraint entirely, which does not guarantee coverage but materially improves it, particularly for second-language English routes and for Arabic as a first language.

Where a UAE-based specialist is not available, the tutor may be based elsewhere and teaching into Gulf Standard Time. We state that before booking rather than after, with where the tutor is and what hours they can offer. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, and one shows a Dubai address on an Abu Dhabi page. Disclosure costs nothing and is the difference between a trade-off a family accepted and one they discovered.

sections.heading: Two children, one tutor, one evening
paragraphs: A substantial share of Abu Dhabi enquiries involve two children rather than one, often a Year 11 and a Year 8 or Year 9. The instinct is to put them in a shared session to halve the cost. That rarely works. Two years of age difference is two years of content difference, and a shared session means one student working while the other waits, at full price, learning that tutoring is boring.

What does work is one tutor, consecutive slots. Thirty to forty minutes for the younger child, fifty for the Year 11, back to back. The household commits a single evening block instead of two, each child keeps their own target and their own record, and the tutor gains something genuinely useful: visibility across the household. A shared algebra weakness in two siblings is a pattern a single tutor spots in week two and two separate tutors each see half of. The same applies to a shared habit, such as starting to write before reading the resource.

There is one case where a shared session is right: two students in the same year group, on the same syllabus and tier, with a similar profile - typically twins or close-in-age siblings in the same class. Then the shared element is an advantage, because explanation to another student is one of the better ways to consolidate anything. Outside that narrow case, consecutive slots give you more for the same evening, and a tutor who recommends the shared session regardless of year gap is optimising for their own calendar.
bullets: Consecutive slots, not a shared screen, where years differ
One evening block committed rather than two

sections.heading: When a tutor is the wrong purchase
paragraphs: Some of the enquiries we receive should not end in a booking, and saying so is cheaper for everyone than finding out in week six. The clearest case is the school's own provision. Most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools run subject clinics, catch-up sessions and departmental support, and they are free, run by the people who set the mocks and marked the work, and frequently unused because nobody told the student to go. Ask what exists before buying anything; it is a genuinely better first purchase at a price of zero.

The second case is a reading-level or processing issue presenting as a subject problem. A Year 10 student losing marks across every written subject simultaneously, including the ones they enjoy, is not having nine subject problems. Reading speed, comprehension or a specific learning difficulty is a reasonable hypothesis, and the right next step is a conversation with the school's learning-support team and in some cases a formal assessment - not a Chemistry tutor. Buying subject tuition in that situation treats the symptom in the most expensive available way.

The third case is a wrong subject choice that is still reversible, and the fourth is motivation. If a student has genuinely disengaged, a weekly one-to-one session with a stranger is a difficult place to start, and a shorter commitment with an explicit exit point is the honest arrangement rather than a term's block. We would rather lose the booking and keep the credibility. Where tuition is the right purchase, it is usually narrower and shorter than families expect: two subjects, a named loss, a block with an end date, and a review that is allowed to conclude stop.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the timetable
process.description: Board, syllabus code and tier for each subject, plus the school day's finish time and the club nights. The first three come from your school's examinations officer in one email; the last two come from you and determine where the sessions can actually go.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A marked mock, a marked past paper or a photographed exercise book page is worth more than a description of the problem. It lets the tutor name the repeated loss before the trial lesson rather than spending the trial lesson discovering it.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial lesson
process.description: One real topic from the actual syllabus, with the marked work on screen. No charge and no card details taken. You end with a written note naming the loss, whether it is a technique gap or a content gap, and how many sessions each would take.

process.title: Slot set after the first week
process.description: We place the weekly session once the bus time, the club nights and the quiet-room availability are known, rather than committing to a time at booking that collapses in week three. Two short sessions on separate days is the default shape.

process.title: Written task between sessions, checked in the next
process.description: Every session ends with one short written task with a stated hand-in. The following session starts by checking it. That loop is the mechanism by which teaching becomes retention, and a plan without it is a sequence of pleasant conversations.

process.title: Four-week review that can say stop
process.description: At four sessions you get the same diagnostic repeated and a plain statement of whether it moved. If it has not, we change target or change tutor. If the honest answer is that tuition is not the right purchase, we will say that too.

whyPoints.title: We tell you which components we cannot move
whyPoints.description: Written theory papers and alternative-to-practical papers respond strongly to teaching. Supervised practicals, speaking endorsements and portfolio subjects do not respond in the same way, and some we decline outright. That distinction is made before you book rather than discovered afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Sessions are placed in the hours that exist
whyPoints.description: An Abu Dhabi week contains about three usable focused windows. We find yours in week one and build around them, which is why the slot is set after the first week. A plan that fights the bus timetable gets abandoned in week five.

whyPoints.title: The loss is named, not the subject
whyPoints.description: After one marked paper a tutor should be able to say what is being dropped and why - quantitative chemistry, command-word discrimination, missing named examples. That determines whether you are buying four weeks or a term, and you are told which.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated up front, including refusals
whyPoints.description: Where we cannot cover a syllabus we say so with a reason, and where a tutor is based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time we say that before booking. A near-match who does not know the syllabus costs a family more than a wait.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool not limited by a drive
whyPoints.description: A household in Al Shamkha or Al Falah choosing a visiting tutor is choosing from those willing to make that journey at 17:30. Online removes that constraint, which matters most for second-language English routes and minority syllabuses.

whyPoints.title: Limits on assessed work stated plainly
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, questions the student's plan and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. Nothing is produced for submission, and board syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes come from the board's own site rather than from us.

faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our villa in Khalifa City or Al Shamkha?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We run no home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we provide only in India. For Abu Dhabi households the lesson is one-to-one over live video, with your child's marked papers on screen. Published market rates put a visiting tutor at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel folded in, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, so most of the premium is the drive. In Al Shamkha and Al Falah the practical gain is larger than the saving: you choose from everyone who teaches the syllabus rather than from those prepared to make the journey.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE practical science work?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the distinction matters. Where practical skills are assessed through work administered by the school, an outside tutor has no influence over the administration, the equipment or the supervision, and should not claim otherwise. What a tutor can teach is the thinking the component assesses: variables and controls, measurement and uncertainty, recording data, and drawing a conclusion the data actually supports. Where the syllabus uses a written alternative-to-practical paper, that paper is highly teachable and is usually the least rehearsed component in the whole set, which makes it one of the better-value things to work on.

faqs.question: How many hours a week can a Year 11 student in Abu Dhabi realistically study?
faqs.answer: Fewer than any revision timetable suggests. School ends between roughly 14:30 and 15:15, a bus run to the mainland communities takes forty to sixty minutes, two afternoons carry a club, and nothing demanding survives past 20:00. In practice there are about three usable focused windows in the week: two weekday evenings and a weekend morning. The weekend morning is worth roughly double a weekday evening for anything requiring sustained thought, so that is where a timed paper section or a coursework plan belongs. Planning around three real windows beats planning around seven imaginary ones.

faqs.question: My child says they find Chemistry hard - how do I find out what is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Send one marked paper rather than a description. Students self-diagnose by feeling and the paper diagnoses by behaviour, and the two usually disagree. A typical finding is that the student scores normally on everything except quantitative questions, where they score close to zero - which is a moles and stoichiometry problem, not a Chemistry problem, and it has a specific four-week fix. A tutor who cannot name the repeated loss after one marked paper has not looked properly. The distinction also tells you how long to buy for: technique losses move in three or four sessions, absent content takes a term.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for tuition in all five subjects my child is struggling with?
faqs.answer: Spread across five subjects, most household budgets buy roughly fortnightly contact in each, which is below the frequency at which anything consolidates - so five subjects feel attended to and none moves. Two subjects at weekly contact with written work in between is a better purchase. Choose them by what gates the next stage, which usually means Mathematics and the separate sciences, and then by where the gap is technique rather than content, because technique moves fastest. Drop the subject your child already passes comfortably; the marginal grade there buys nothing you need.

faqs.question: Ramadan lands in the same term as the mocks - what happens to our IGCSE sessions?
faqs.answer: They move rather than stop. Most Abu Dhabi families shift a weekday evening session to a late-morning weekend slot, or to a shorter post-Iftar evening session that is often more focused than the one it replaces. Because there is no drive to recalculate, this is a scheduling message rather than a rebooking. Around Eid itself the honest advice is to pause for the days and resume, instead of scheduling sessions nobody will attend. Ramadan falls in the spring term alongside mocks and the run-up to the June series, so writing the shifts into the plan in advance is worth doing in October.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both of my children in the same session to save money?
faqs.answer: Where the years differ, consecutive slots work better than a shared screen. Two years of age difference is two years of content difference, so a shared session means one child works while the other waits at full price. Thirty to forty minutes for the younger child followed by fifty for the Year 11 keeps the household to one evening block, gives each child their own target and record, and lets a single tutor spot patterns across the household - a shared algebra weakness, or a shared habit of writing before reading the resource. A genuinely shared session makes sense only for the same year, same syllabus and same tier.

faqs.question: Does my child need a laptop, or will a phone do for an online lesson?
faqs.answer: A laptop on a table, not a phone and not a bed. The requirements are otherwise small: the student's own exercise book and past papers within reach, a pen, and a way to show written work - a document camera, a phone propped over the page, or a photograph sent at the start. Headphones matter more than people expect, because the most useful signal in a session is a muttered half-answer and a tutor who cannot hear it loses the diagnosis. Put the phone in another room as a condition of the session; students accept that framing far more readily than they accept it as a punishment.

faqs.question: Should I ask the school for help before hiring a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the better first purchase because it costs nothing. Most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum schools run subject clinics, catch-up sessions and departmental support, delivered by the people who wrote the mocks and marked the work. These are frequently under-used simply because no one told the student to attend. Ask the head of year what exists, when it runs and whether attendance is tracked. If your child is already going and the gap persists, you have both a stronger case for tuition and a much clearer brief for the tutor - which makes the paid hours more productive when you do buy them.

faqs.question: My child is losing marks in every written subject at once - is that nine problems?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. Simultaneous losses across every written subject, including the ones the student enjoys, point to something upstream: reading speed, reading comprehension, processing, or a specific learning difficulty that has not been identified. Nine subject tutors would be the most expensive possible response to a single cause. The right next step is the school's learning-support team, and in some cases a formal assessment, before any subject tuition is bought. We say this to families regularly and it loses us bookings, but a Chemistry tutor cannot fix a reading-rate problem and should not be sold as if they could.

faqs.question: How do you handle coursework and controlled assessment honestly?
faqs.answer: By teaching and questioning, and by not touching the submission. A tutor may explain what the criteria reward, teach the underlying skill, discuss a plan the student has made, challenge a weak source, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves. A tutor may not supply content for submission, redraft the student's text into their own prose, or hand over finished sections. The work is the student's own and boards treat breaches as malpractice, with consequences falling on the student rather than the tutor. We also do not supply board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; those come from the board's own site.

faqs.question: What if you do not have a tutor for my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a reason, so you can look elsewhere quickly. Mainstream subjects on either board are usually matched within a few days. English as a second language routes can take up to a fortnight. Arabic as a first language is limited. Art, design and portfolio subjects we decline outright, because the assessed component needs supervised production at school. Where no UAE-based specialist is free, the tutor may be based outside the UAE and teaching into Gulf Standard Time, and we state that before booking rather than after. A near-match who does not know your syllabus costs more than a wait.

faqs.question: Is a long weekend session better than two short weekday ones?
faqs.answer: One of each, ideally. Two 50-minute weekday sessions on separate days create the loop that makes teaching stick: the first sets a short written task, the second checks it. Place them on the same day and the task never gets done. A 90-minute weekend morning session is the right place for work that cannot be split - a full timed paper section marked against the real criteria, or a planning conversation about the student's own coursework draft. What does not work is a single long weekday evening block, because the last third of it is spent managing a tired student.

faqs.question: My child has six weeks until the exams - is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but it changes what you should buy. With six weeks the content phase is over. What moves a grade now is technique and a small number of high-mark topics identified from a marked paper: reading the command word, allocating time by marks, showing the step the marker needs, and the two or three topics where the most marks are available. Pick two subjects at most. Three focused sessions a week with real work in between beats five sessions with none, and a tutor who promises to cover the whole syllabus in six weeks is describing an impossibility.

faqs.question: Which schools in Abu Dhabi do your IGCSE students come from?
faqs.answer: Across the island and the mainland corridor: long-established British-curriculum schools in Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah, and newer provision in Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas Island and Saadiyat Island. We name schools on this page as context for the emirate's IGCSE landscape, not as partners or clients - IB Gram has no affiliation with any school or group and claims no endorsement from any of them. What matters more than the school name is the entry detail: which board, which syllabus code and which tier, since those differ between schools and sometimes within a single year group.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper and a look at your week
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Abu Dhabi, send two things: one marked paper, and the time your child's school day and club nights actually end. Then book the free 45-minute trial lesson. The tutor works on one real topic with the marked work on screen, and you finish with a written note naming the repeated loss, whether it is technique or content, and how many sessions each would take. No charge, no card details. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, placed in the hours your week actually has.

intro.heading: A fee quote is six decisions wearing one number
paragraphs: Parents in Abu Dhabi usually start the search for IGCSE tuition by asking the price, and they are usually given a single figure. That figure is almost meaningless on its own. An hour of Cambridge IGCSE Biology for a Year 10 student in October, booked at four in the afternoon, is a different commercial product from an hour of Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics for a Year 11 student in April, booked at seven in the evening, with a visiting tutor driving from the island out to Al Reef. Both get described as an hour of IGCSE tuition. They are priced differently because they cost differently to supply.

There are six factors that move the number, and they move it in predictable directions. Subject scarcity is the largest single multiplier: a tutor who can teach Arabic as a first language to syllabus 0508 standard, or who can handle the Additional Mathematics 0606 content properly, is competing for far fewer hours of their own time than a tutor offering general science. Tier matters next, because Extended-tier content covers ground that Core does not, and the person teaching it needs to know the harder material cold. Year group matters because a Year 11 hour in the second half of the year is a scarce, deadline-bound hour. Clock time matters because the window between the end of the school day and bedtime is narrow. Board matters because a tutor who knows both the Cambridge and Pearson versions of a subject is rarer than one who knows either. And travel matters, because somebody has to pay for the forty minutes in the car.

The published market data for this emirate makes the ranges visible. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one work at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour at the budget end and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to AED 52; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150; TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist work; BartyED sits at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Monthly packages circulate at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. None of those are IB Gram prices. They are the market you are shopping in, and knowing the shape of it is what stops a quote being either an insult or a trap.

Abu Dhabi has its own cost geography on top of that. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, and enrolment sits in three loose bands: the island itself, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and the newer mainland communities out towards Al Shamkha and Al Samha. A tutor living on the island who takes a seven o'clock booking in Al Ghadeer is not selling an hour; they are selling an hour plus most of an evening. That is why the visiting band in the published data is so wide, and it is also why the online band sits below it. The driving does not get cheaper by being hidden inside a round number.

The honest position on delivery, stated before any of the pricing detail: IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address. Home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with the student's work marked between sessions. We have kept the phrase home tutor fees on this page because it is what parents type, and because the honest answer to the question includes what the visiting market charges and why. The rest of this page prices both and lets you decide which you are actually buying.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The cheapest hour on any Abu Dhabi rate card, and often the most useful one. Nothing here is externally examined, so an hour spent fixing fraction work, algebraic manipulation or scientific writing is an hour that buys back three later. Tutors at this stage do not need subject-specialist depth, which is exactly why the market band sits low.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi families tend to buy at this stage only when a school report flags something, which is a pity: the Checkpoint years are when a rate of AED 120 to AED 180 an hour can still change a trajectory. Demand is lightest in Years 7 and 8, so the slot choice is wide and evening premiums barely apply.

programmes.name: IGCSE Core tier
programmes.description: Core-tier entries examine a narrower body of content and cap the grade available, so the teaching job is consolidation rather than extension. The market prices Core below Extended, usually by AED 30 to AED 60 an hour for the same tutor. The real question on a Core entry is whether the ceiling is right, because a tier decision made in Year 10 is hard to reverse late.
programmes.countryNote: Core entries are more common in Abu Dhabi than parents assume, particularly where a student joined a British-curriculum school mid-Key Stage 4 from another system. Any quote for Core work should be paired with an honest view on whether a move to Extended is realistic in the time left.

programmes.name: IGCSE Extended tier
programmes.description: The volume hour in this market. Extended covers the full content and carries the grades a sixth-form or Diploma place usually needs, and almost every tuition enquiry in Abu Dhabi for Years 10 and 11 is about an Extended entry. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with specialists quoted higher.
programmes.countryNote: The Extended rate in Abu Dhabi rises through the academic year rather than staying flat. September bookings are negotiable; March bookings for a May or June series are not, because the people who can do the work are already timetabled. Families who plan in autumn pay the autumn price.

programmes.name: AS, A Level and IB Diploma entry
programmes.description: Included here because the IGCSE budget decision is usually really a post-16 decision. The grades a student leaves Year 11 with determine which Higher Level or A Level options open, and post-16 tuition is the most expensive band on the card. Spending at IGCSE to protect an option is cheaper than buying remedial hours in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi sixth forms and Diploma programmes commonly set subject-specific entry grades at IGCSE. A family weighing AED 200 an hour for Extended Mathematics in Year 11 against the cost of a Year 12 catch-up block is looking at the same decision from two ends.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Scarcity, not difficulty, sets the premium. These are the Cambridge and Pearson subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to price, with a note on what makes each one cheap or expensive to supply here.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most supplied subject in the emirate and therefore the most competitively priced. Plenty of tutors can teach it, so a quote above the AED 300 mark needs justifying by something concrete: examiner experience, a track record with the harder Extended topics, or availability in a slot nobody else has.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A genuine scarcity premium. The content moves into calculus and advanced trigonometry, far fewer Abu Dhabi tutors teach it confidently, and the quotes reflect that. Expect to pay at the specialist end of the market band rather than the general maths rate, and expect fewer slots to choose from.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Priced above general science because the mathematical content filters the supply. The marks that move are usually in the longer structured questions and the practical paper, where candidates lose marks on method and precision rather than recall, so sessions need a tutor who can mark as well as explain.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mid-band pricing with a sharp seasonal spike. Organic chemistry and mole calculations generate most of the enquiries, and they generate them in the same six weeks every year, which is when the rate hardens. Booked in September the same tutor is routinely quoted lower.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The best supplied science in Abu Dhabi and usually the cheapest of the three. The teaching job is less about concepts than about writing: candidates who know the material lose marks by answering a command term loosely, and that is fixable in a small number of sessions.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510)
subjects.description: High volume, moderate pricing, and the subject where the entry route matters most. A student capable of first-language work entered for the second-language syllabus has had a ceiling set for them, so a first session should look at the entry decision before it looks at the writing.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: The clearest scarcity premium in the emirate. Tutors who can teach first-language Arabic to IGCSE standard are in short supply relative to demand, and the federal requirement that private schools teach Arabic keeps that demand steady. Quotes here sit well above the general-subject band.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 and 0455)
subjects.description: Reasonably supplied and reasonably priced, with the marks concentrated in application and evaluation rather than definition. Students who revise by memorising terms plateau in the low grades, so sessions that are worth paying for are built around past-paper answers, not notes.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Thin supply, firm pricing. The theory paper and the practical problem-solving paper reward different things, and tutors who are strong on both are scarce in Abu Dhabi. Families often pay a premium here simply for availability in a usable evening slot.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 and 0653)
subjects.description: Cheaper per subject than three separate sciences and a common Abu Dhabi entry. The pricing trap is that one tutor rarely covers all three disciplines to the same depth, so a single low rate can mean two of the three disciplines are being taught thinly.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: Where you live in Abu Dhabi changes a visiting quote and does nothing at all to an online one. These are the areas families ask us about most, with the travel reality that sits behind a visiting rate in each.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Dense in British-curriculum families and a common base for tutors, which keeps visiting quotes nearer the middle of the band. The constraint is the school-run window: a four o'clock start is rarely realistic in term time.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Close enough to the island for a visiting tutor to accept a single booking, far enough that two bookings in one evening need an hour of slack. Quotes here often assume a 90-minute session to make the trip worth it.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Far enough out that travel becomes the dominant cost in a visiting rate. Families here are routinely quoted at the top of the in-home band, and are the most likely to find the online rate materially cheaper for the same tutor quality.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Island addresses with the shortest travel times and the widest tutor choice, so visiting quotes sit lower. Parking and building access still eat ten minutes a session, which is why hourly rates here still carry a visit premium.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short hop from the island proper but with a villa-and-tower mix that makes access times unpredictable. Quotes tend to assume evening traffic across the bridge rather than the distance itself.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Large, spread out, and well served by schools, so there is local tutor supply but it clears early. Late-evening slots here attract the firmest premiums of any mainland community.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Bridge-dependent in both directions and busy with weekend traffic, which pushes visiting quotes up on Fridays and Saturdays. Online removes that variable entirely for families who travel at weekends.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Samha
regions.note: The outer edge of what a visiting tutor will accept at any price, and the clearest case for live video delivery. Market quotes that do reach out here are usually package-only rather than hourly.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Al Bateen schools
schoolClusters.note: The oldest cluster of British-curriculum provision in the emirate, with established IGCSE cohorts and well-documented subject offers. Families here usually know which board their child sits before they call, which makes a quote easier to give accurately.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas corridor
schoolClusters.note: Where most of the emirate's newer British and international capacity sits, and where the largest share of IGCSE tuition enquiries originate. Subject offers vary noticeably between schools in this corridor, which is why a scarcity premium on one subject can differ street to street.

schoolClusters.city: Mainland and mixed-curriculum communities
schoolClusters.note: Schools serving Mohammed Bin Zayed City, Mussafah, Baniyas and the newer southern communities, with a broader spread of curricula and a higher proportion of Core-tier entries. Travel distances here are what make the visiting market expensive.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-fees.modesIntro: Three ways of buying the same teaching, with different cost structures. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video, which is why none of them carries a travel line.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, single subject
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with the same subject specialist, with work set and marked between sessions. This is the cheapest effective way to buy sustained progress because the rate is stable and the tutor's knowledge of the student compounds. It is also the format where a scarcity premium hurts least, since one slot a week is easier to find than three.
bullets: Same tutor, same slot, booked for a term rather than a session at a time
Marked work between sessions, so the paid hour is spent on diagnosis
No travel component, because nobody travels
Easiest format to pause for exam weeks and restart afterwards

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A short, dense run of sessions in the weeks before a Cambridge or Pearson series, built around timed papers rather than content delivery. The hourly rate for this work is higher everywhere in the market because availability is scarce at exactly that point in the calendar, which is the argument for booking it in autumn rather than in spring.
bullets: Built around full timed papers, marked and returned with a diagnosis
Priced at the specialist end of the market band because of when it falls
Booked months ahead or not available at all in peak weeks
Suited to a student whose content knowledge is sound and whose technique is not

modes.title: Two-subject pairing for one student
modes.description: Two related subjects taught by one tutor across the week, most often Mathematics with Physics or Biology with Chemistry. Pairing reduces the administrative overhead and gives the tutor a fuller picture of workload, and it is the one arrangement where a sensible rate reduction is reasonable to ask for because the tutor is filling two slots from one relationship.
bullets: One tutor, two subjects, one shared view of the student's week
Reasonable basis for asking about a combined rate
Only sensible where the tutor genuinely teaches both to the same depth
Not available on every pairing; Additional Mathematics is often standalone

sections.heading: Six factors move an Abu Dhabi IGCSE quote, and they move it predictably
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor fee in Abu Dhabi is built from six inputs. Ask a provider to price each of them separately and the number stops looking arbitrary. Subject scarcity is the first and largest: the smaller the pool of people in or available to this market who can teach the specification properly, the higher the rate, and the less room there is to negotiate on slot times. Tier is second, because Extended content is wider than Core and the teaching has to go further.

Year group is third. A Year 9 hour is bought to prevent a problem; a Year 11 hour in the second half of the year is bought to fix one, with a fixed deadline attached. Scarcity rises as the deadline approaches, and so does the price. Clock time is fourth: in a city where the school day ends in the early afternoon and most families want a slot between four and nine in the evening, that five-hour window is where almost all demand sits, and demand pricing applies to it. Board is fifth, because a tutor fluent in both the Cambridge and the Pearson version of a subject is scarcer than one fluent in either, and families whose children sit both boards across subjects value that fluency.

Travel is sixth, and it is the one factor that disappears entirely under live video delivery. The published Abu Dhabi and Dubai figures show the effect clearly: Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour against a qualified online band that Unitors starts at AED 150, and independent home tutors quote as high as AED 500. The difference is not teaching quality. It is a car, a bridge and an evening. The table below gives each factor a direction and a rough swing, so a quote can be read rather than simply accepted or refused.

sections.heading: Scarcity pricing by subject: which IGCSE hours cost more in this emirate
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent can know before asking for a price is whether the subject is abundant or scarce in Abu Dhabi. Abundance is why Mathematics and Biology quotes cluster so tightly: dozens of credible people can teach them, so nobody can hold out for a premium. Scarcity is why Arabic as a first language, Additional Mathematics and Computer Science quotes sit noticeably higher, and why the slot offered is often the one the tutor has left rather than the one you wanted.

Scarcity in this market has three sources. Some subjects are taught in relatively few Abu Dhabi schools, so the local teaching population is small to begin with. Some require a skill set that is in demand elsewhere: a competent Computer Science teacher has options outside tutoring. And some, Arabic first language in particular, sit against a standing requirement rather than an optional choice, because private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum regardless of which international programme they run. Demand for that subject does not soften.

The practical consequence is that a budget should be allocated by scarcity, not evenly. If a student needs help in Biology and in Additional Mathematics, the Biology hour is the one to shop around on and the Additional Mathematics hour is the one to book early and pay the going rate for. Families who do the reverse end up overpaying for an abundant subject and then finding nothing available in the scarce one in March. The table sets out where each common subject sits.

table.caption: IGCSE SUBJECT SUPPLY IN ABU DHABI AND WHAT IT DOES TO THE RATE
columns: What a parent should do about it
rows: Lowest end of the qualified band
Compare three quotes; there is genuine competition for your booking

Book the organic chemistry block in autumn before the rate hardens
Check the tutor marks longer structured questions, not only explains them
Book early and expect to take the slot that is offered

Secure continuity for the whole year rather than buying in blocks
