sections.heading: The four-to-nine squeeze: why the same hour costs more at six o'clock
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi school days finish early by international standards, and the hours parents want for tuition are the hours between the end of the school run and a reasonable bedtime. That is a five-hour window, five or six days a week, and it is where almost every enquiry lands. A tutor can sell perhaps three of those hours well on a weekday. Everything outside the window is easy to book and everything inside it is contested, and the rate follows.

The squeeze is sharper in Abu Dhabi than the raw hours suggest, for two local reasons. First, the geography: a visiting tutor who accepts a five o'clock booking in Khalifa City cannot realistically take a seven o'clock in Al Reef, so the opportunity cost of a mid-evening slot is an entire evening. Second, the school-run pattern: families with two or three children in different year groups are frequently not home and settled until well after four, which compresses demand into the later part of the window where the premium is highest.

There is money in knowing this. The two cheapest usable slots in this market are early morning before school, which works for a disciplined Year 11 student revising rather than learning new content, and weekend mornings, which are wide open and attract no premium at all. Both are only available at sensible prices because the lesson happens over live video and no travel is involved. A Saturday morning session costs a tutor nothing in driving and competes with nothing, which is why it prices the way it does.

sections.heading: Two quote shapes, one decision: per hour against per package
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi providers quote in two shapes and the shapes are not comparable without arithmetic. An hourly quote is simple and flexible and carries no commitment. A package quote attaches a lower effective rate to a block of sessions, and the published examples in this market are around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. On the face of it the package wins. It wins only if every session is used.

The arithmetic that matters is the effective rate after attrition. Eight sessions at AED 799 is just under AED 100 a session if all eight happen. Miss two to illness, travel and an exam week, which is an ordinary month in Years 10 and 11, and the effective rate rises by a third. Packages with a strict expiry and no rollover quietly transfer the risk of a disrupted month from the provider to the family. Packages with rollover, or with a cancellation window measured in hours rather than days, do not.

There is a second difference that rarely appears in the headline. Hourly bookings are usually cancellable close to the session; package sessions often are not, because the provider has committed the tutor's slot for the block. For a family whose child plays sport, travels to see relatives in the holidays, or has mock weeks that move, flexibility has a cash value. The right question to a provider is not what the package costs but what happens to session six if nobody can attend it.

table.caption: READING TWO ABU DHABI QUOTE SHAPES AGAINST EACH OTHER
rows: Cancellation window in hours, and whether the rate is held for the term
Whether unused sessions roll over, and what expiry applies
Whether travel is inside the price and what a cancelled visit costs
That the block is built around marked timed papers, not revision talks
That one tutor genuinely teaches both subjects to the same depth

bullets: Divide the package price by the sessions you will realistically attend, not by the sessions sold
A short cancellation window is worth real money in Years 10 and 11
Ask what happens to an unused session before asking what the discount is

sections.heading: One budget, nine subjects: buying the hour that is worth most
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi families arrive at this decision from the wrong end. A Year 11 student is taking eight or nine IGCSE subjects, three or four of them are shaky, and the budget covers one or two hours a week. The instinct is to buy help in the weakest subject. That is often the wrong purchase, because the weakest subject is sometimes weak for reasons an hour a week will not change, while a subject sitting just below a grade boundary can move with very little.

A better triage runs on three questions. First, what does this subject gate? A Mathematics or Science grade that gates a post-16 option is worth more than a grade in a subject the student will drop. Second, how far is the gap? A student two grades below target in a content-heavy subject needs a term; a student half a grade below in a technique-heavy subject may need four sessions. Third, what kind of gap is it? Missing content is slow to fix. Misread command terms, poor working, bad time allocation across a paper, and consistently abandoning the last question are quick to fix, and they are extremely common.

Run that triage honestly and the ordering usually changes. The Ministry of Education's equivalency rule gives a useful floor to protect: for the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. That is a floor, not a target, but it tells you which five subjects must not be allowed to fall over while you are busy optimising a sixth.
bullets: Buy the hour that protects a post-16 option before the hour that fixes a favourite subject
Technique gaps move faster per dirham than content gaps; diagnose before booking a term
Protect the five subjects that carry Ministry equivalency before optimising anything else
Verify equivalency requirements on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on a tutoring page

sections.heading: The ethics rule that removes the cheapest option in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: A recurring assumption among families new to the emirate is that the cheapest and most effective tutor is the child's own class teacher, privately, after hours. In Abu Dhabi that option is closed. Press reporting on the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the federal private tuition work permit also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation from the policy document, and check the current ADEK publication before relying on the detail.

The permit itself is worth understanding before any money changes hands. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated through a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. The official route is the Ministry's own service page for private tutor licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing, and this one will not. The practical point for a parent comparing quotes is that a tutor charging well below the market band and unwilling to discuss their permit status is not offering a bargain; they are offering a different risk profile. Asking the question is free and takes one message.
bullets: Your child's own school teacher is not an available route in this emirate
The private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years
Apply or verify through mohre.gov.ae, not through a tutoring intermediary
No fine amounts are published; treat any quoted figure with scepticism

sections.heading: What the fee does not include, and the questions that find out
paragraphs: The gap between two Abu Dhabi quotes is often not the rate at all. It is what sits inside the hour and what sits outside it. Marking is the big one: a tutor who marks a set of past-paper answers between sessions is doing an hour of unpaid work that makes the paid hour far more valuable, and a tutor who does not is spending the first twenty minutes of your session finding out what went wrong. Both can quote the same number.

Resources are the second. Nobody should be sending you scanned syllabus documents, mark schemes or past papers as downloads. Those are Cambridge and Pearson copyright, and reproducing them is not something a legitimate provider does. What a good tutor does instead is point you at the official pages on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, tell you precisely which document matters for your child's entry, and work from the material the school has already issued. A provider offering a private library of papers is telling you something about how they operate.

The third gap is reporting. Some rates include a written note after each session and a longer review each term; some include nothing you can show a school. For a family spending AED 800 a month, a record of what was covered and what moved is not an administrative extra, it is the only way to tell whether the spending is working. Ask for a sample before the first invoice rather than after the third.
bullets: Is work marked between sessions, and by the same person who teaches it?
Who confirms which specification and tier my child is actually entered for?
What written record do I get after each session, and may I see a sample?
Is the rate fixed for the term, or does it change closer to the series?
What is the cancellation window in hours, and does it apply both ways?
Does the tutor hold a current private tuition work permit?

sections.heading: When to taper: the exit test for an IGCSE tuition budget
paragraphs: A tuition budget should have an end condition written into it from the beginning, and almost none do. Families start in October with two hours a week and are still paying for two hours a week in April without ever having asked whether one would now do. The absence of an exit test is the single largest avoidable cost in this market, and it is entirely within a parent's control.

Three signals say it is time to reduce. The student is now starting work before the session rather than during it, which means the bottleneck has moved from understanding to practice and practice is cheaper than teaching. Timed paper scores have been stable at or above target across three consecutive attempts, which means the remaining gap is consistency rather than capability. And the questions in the session have changed character, from what does this mean to is this the best way to answer it, which is a sign the student is now self-diagnosing.

Tapering is not stopping. The usual sensible shape is to move from weekly to fortnightly while keeping a standing slot in the weeks before the series, so continuity survives and the rate stays at the autumn level rather than the spring one. Families who cancel outright in February and then try to rebook in April discover the second half of this page's pricing logic the hard way: the hour they let go is the hour that is now scarce. Booking a reduced commitment is cheaper than buying a new one late.
bullets: Write the exit condition into the plan before the first invoice
Three stable timed-paper scores at target is a reduction signal, not a stopping signal
Keep a standing slot through the series rather than cancelling and rebooking
Fortnightly continuity holds the autumn rate; a spring restart does not

process.title: Tell us the entry, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message names the board, the syllabus code if you have it, the tier and the year group: Cambridge 0580 Extended, Year 11, sitting in the June series. That is enough to price the request accurately and to say honestly whether the scarce subjects on your list have availability in the slot you want.

process.title: A free 45-minute trial lesson, no card details
process.description: One trial lesson with the proposed tutor, 45 minutes, at no charge and with no payment details collected. The trial is a working session on your child's actual material, not a sales call, and it ends with a written note on what the tutor thinks the gap is and roughly how many sessions it represents.

process.title: A written plan with a price and an end point
process.description: Before any money changes hands you get the slot, the rate, the cancellation window and a view on how long this should take. The plan names what will be marked between sessions and what written record you will receive, so the invoice and the deliverable match from the first week.

process.title: Weekly sessions with work marked in between
process.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. Work is set and marked between sessions so the paid hour is spent on what went wrong rather than on finding out. Nobody travels to an Abu Dhabi address, so no travel is priced into the rate.

process.title: A review at six sessions against the exit test
process.description: At the six-session mark we look at timed-paper scores, the marked work and the student's own account of the sessions, and give a direct view: continue, change tutor, change subject priority, or reduce. Recommending fewer hours is a normal outcome of that review and not a failure of it.

whyPoints.title: Every figure here belongs to the market, with its source named
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from published competitor pricing and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and they are presented as the market you are shopping in rather than as our price list. Three of the six best-ranking pages in this search publish no price at all; two quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: Travel is not hidden inside the rate
whyPoints.description: A visiting hour in Abu Dhabi contains a car journey whether or not the invoice itemises it, and for Al Reef, Al Shamkha or Al Samha addresses that journey can be the largest single cost in the quote. Live video delivery removes it rather than disguising it, which is why the online band sits below the visiting band everywhere in the published data.

whyPoints.title: Subject scarcity is priced openly rather than averaged away
whyPoints.description: Providers who quote one flat rate for all subjects are either overcharging for Mathematics or underpaying whoever teaches Arabic first language and Additional Mathematics. We say which subjects are scarce in this emirate and what that does to availability, so a family can book the hard subject early and shop around on the easy one.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, reviews a draft the student has written themselves and gives feedback that the student then acts on. No part of an assessed folder is supplied by the tutor, and no finished work changes hands in either direction. That line is an IB and Cambridge academic-honesty requirement and it is also the difference between tuition and an essay service.

whyPoints.title: The permit question is answered rather than avoided
whyPoints.description: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, free for two years through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. We point parents at the official service page and say plainly that no fine schedule has been published, rather than repeating an unverified figure.

whyPoints.title: An exit test, written down at the start
whyPoints.description: Every plan carries the conditions under which we would recommend reducing or stopping. A provider whose commercial interest runs one way should put the opposite case in writing at the beginning, and a family that knows what success looks like can stop paying for it when it arrives.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Abu Dhabi charge per hour?
faqs.answer: The published market for this region spans roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour. Budget and university-student tutors advertise from around AED 33 to AED 65; qualified subject tutors working online start near AED 150 and run to about AED 300; visiting one-to-one work sits at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoting up to AED 500; premium named tutors reach AED 650. Those are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices. Where your own quote lands inside that range depends on the subject, the tier, the year group, the slot and whether anyone drives.

faqs.question: Why is the quote for Additional Maths higher than the quote for Biology?
faqs.answer: Supply. Cambridge IGCSE Biology is taught by a large number of credible tutors in and available to this market, so no one of them can hold out for a premium. Additional Mathematics 0606 moves into calculus and advanced trigonometry, far fewer people teach it confidently to IGCSE standard, and those who do have limited hours to sell. The rate difference reflects scarcity rather than a judgement about which subject is harder for your child. The practical consequence is worth acting on: shop around on Biology, and book the Additional Mathematics slot early at the going rate rather than hunting for a discount that does not exist.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package cheaper than paying for single IGCSE sessions?
faqs.answer: Only if every session is used. Packages circulating in this market run at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is just under AED 100 a session if all eight happen. Lose two to illness, travel or a mock week, which is an ordinary month in Year 11, and the effective rate rises by roughly a third. The questions that decide it are whether unused sessions roll over, what expiry applies, and what the cancellation window is in hours. A package with rollover and a short notice period is usually good value; one with strict expiry transfers the risk of a disrupted month to you.

faqs.question: Does an Abu Dhabi tutoring fee include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider directly and get the answer in writing, because the treatment of tuition fees under UAE tax rules is not something a tutoring page should assert as fact. What a parent can reasonably require is clarity about the quote in front of them: whether the AED figure stated is the amount that will be charged, whether any tax is added at invoice, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. The Federal Tax Authority is the authority on the underlying treatment. Any provider who cannot say plainly whether the number they quoted is the number you pay has told you something useful about their billing.

faqs.question: How much of a home tutor's fee is actually travel?
faqs.answer: For an Abu Dhabi address it is frequently the largest single component. Compare the two published bands: visiting one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 an hour against qualified online work from about AED 150. The gap is not teaching quality, since it is often the same calibre of tutor; it is a car, a bridge and an evening that can hold only one booking instead of two. For families in Al Reef, Al Ghadeer, Al Shamkha or Al Samha the effect is at its strongest, because a tutor accepting a single booking that far out loses the rest of the evening to driving.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor him privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Press reporting on the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the federal private tuition work permit also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording against the ADEK policy document before relying on the detail. The practical answer for a parent is that this apparently cheap and convenient route is not available in this emirate, and a teacher who offers it is accepting a professional risk on your child's behalf.

faqs.question: How many tutoring hours a week should I budget for Year 11?
faqs.answer: One hour a week per subject, in at most two subjects, is where most Abu Dhabi families should start, with work marked between sessions. Three or four hours a week across four subjects sounds more serious and usually produces less, because the student has no time left to do the practice the sessions set. The exception is a short pre-series block in the weeks before the exams, where two or three sessions a week on timed papers is justified for a student whose content knowledge is sound but whose technique is not. Budget for the block in autumn, when the rate is still negotiable.

faqs.question: Do tutoring fees rise in the weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Effectively, yes. The headline rate on a provider's page may not change, but the availability behind it does, and what a family is quoted in March for work in May reflects that. Tutors who can teach scarce subjects are already timetabled by then, so what remains is either a less experienced tutor at the same price or a specialist at the top of the band. Families who book in September and keep a standing slot pay the autumn rate all year. Families who cancel in February and rebook in April discover the difference. Continuity is a pricing strategy as much as an academic one.

faqs.question: What should I ask before agreeing a tutoring rate?
faqs.answer: Six questions settle almost everything. Is work marked between sessions, and by the person who teaches it? Who confirms which specification and tier my child is entered for? What written record do I get after each session, and may I see a sample? Is the rate fixed for the term? What is the cancellation window in hours, and does it apply to the tutor as well as to us? Does the tutor hold a current private tuition work permit? A provider who answers all six in writing is quoting a service. One who answers none is quoting a number.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper university-student tutor a false economy for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and it depends on the job. A capable university student is a reasonable buy for drilling practice, checking method on routine questions and keeping a Year 10 student working steadily, and the published band for that work starts near AED 45 an hour. What they generally cannot do is read a marked script diagnostically, explain why a technically correct answer scored two out of four against a specific mark scheme, or judge whether a tier entry is right. If the gap is technique and examiner expectation rather than practice volume, the cheaper hour buys activity rather than movement.

faqs.question: Can two siblings share one paid hour?
faqs.answer: It can work, with conditions, and it is usually a worse buy than it looks. Two students in the same subject and the same year group with similar gaps can share a session productively. Two students a year apart, or in different subjects, cannot: the hour becomes thirty minutes each with a handover, and both pay attention for half of it. A better use of the same budget is often one shared 90-minute session where the tutor sets independent work for one student while teaching the other in turn. Ask for that structure explicitly rather than assuming it.

faqs.question: What happens to the fee if we cancel a session on the same day?
faqs.answer: That depends entirely on the written cancellation window, which is why it belongs in the plan before the first invoice. A reasonable arrangement states a notice period in hours, applies it to both sides, and says what happens to the slot: rescheduled within the week, credited, or charged. Package sessions are usually less flexible than hourly bookings because the provider has committed the tutor's time for the block. For a family with sport, travel or moving mock weeks, a short notice window has a real cash value and is worth more than a small discount on the rate.

faqs.question: Does a free trial lesson commit me to anything?
faqs.answer: Ours does not. The trial is one 45-minute session with the proposed tutor, at no charge, with no card or payment details collected and no obligation to continue. It runs on your child's actual material rather than a generic assessment, and it ends with a written note on what the tutor thinks the gap is and roughly how many sessions it represents. If the answer is that tuition is not the right purchase, that is a legitimate outcome of a trial. Ask any provider offering a trial to state the length, the eligibility and the payment requirement before you book it.

faqs.question: At what point should we stop paying for IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: When three things are true at once: the student starts the work before the session rather than during it, timed paper scores have been at or above target across three consecutive attempts, and the questions in the session have shifted from what does this mean to is this the best way to answer it. At that point the bottleneck is practice, and practice is cheaper than teaching. The sensible move is tapering rather than stopping: fortnightly sessions with a standing slot through the series keeps continuity and holds the rate you agreed in autumn.

faqs.question: Why does an online IGCSE hour cost less than a visiting hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Because nobody drives. A visiting tutor who accepts a six o'clock booking in Al Raha cannot take an eight o'clock in Al Bateen, so the price of that single hour has to cover an evening. The published bands show the effect: in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to AED 350 against qualified online work from about AED 150. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an Abu Dhabi address at all, since home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE session runs one-to-one over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. The saving is structural, not a discount.

intro.heading: Plenty of options, almost no way to tell them apart
paragraphs: Al Bandar sits in the Al Raha Beach development, a short drive from several of the emirate's best-known international schools and inside the deepest concentration of teaching staff on the Abu Dhabi mainland. A parent here searching for an IGCSE home tutor does not run out of names. They run out of ways to distinguish between them, because every profile says much the same thing: experienced, qualified, results-focused, friendly, flexible. Those words describe a manner, not a capability.

The capability that matters is narrow and specific. Abu Dhabi schools enter IGCSE mathematics candidates on at least four different syllabuses: Cambridge Mathematics 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 and, for stronger candidates, Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1. Each has its own components, its own calculator rules and its own characteristic mark losses. A tutor who has prepared candidates on 0580 Extended and a tutor who has prepared candidates on 4MA1 Higher are not interchangeable, and neither is interchangeable with a graduate who is simply good at mathematics.

That matters here more than in a thin market, because abundance hides mismatch. In a community with two available tutors a parent knows they are compromising. In a community with thirty, the natural assumption is that at least one of them must be right, so selection becomes a matter of availability and manner rather than of syllabus. The result is a competent generalist teaching a Year 11 candidate the mathematics they already know, politely, for a term.

So this page is a selection guide. It sets out the four syllabuses and what distinguishes them, the three genuinely different kinds of tutor this market contains and what each is for, and a twelve-minute test a parent can run during a trial session that requires no subject knowledge. It also covers the things proximity does not solve, including the tier trap, which caps a grade administratively and is invisible in any profile.

A statement of model first. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Al Bandar is one of the few places in the emirate where an in-home arrangement is genuinely easy to organise, and it is still priced above an online session in every published rate table, which is worth knowing before you choose. Our lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and the argument for them here is selection rather than logistics: you choose the person who has taught the code, not the person who can park. That is a narrower claim than the one most pages in this search make, and it is the one that survives contact with a market as crowded as this one.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.programmesIntro: Al Bandar families approach IGCSE from three positions, and the selection question differs in each. Here is what to screen for at each stage.

programmes.name: The first IGCSE year
programmes.description: Screen for a tutor who asks about the tier before anything else. Year 10 is the only year in which a tier decision can still be changed, and a tutor who begins teaching content without establishing whether the entry can award the grade the family wants has skipped the most consequential question in the course.
programmes.countryNote: Schools across the Al Raha Beach and Khalifa City belt enter candidates with both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, occasionally using different boards for different subjects in the same school. The entry statement carries the code and the exams officer will confirm it in one email, so a tutor who shrugs at the question in September is telling you something.

programmes.name: The examination year
programmes.description: Screen for mark-scheme fluency. Ask where candidates lose marks on the specific paper your child sits. The answer you want is specific and unglamorous: invisible method, early rounding carried forward, bearings, similar-shape scale factors, histograms with unequal class widths. The answer that signals a generalist is about confidence and motivation.
programmes.countryNote: Al Bandar students usually sit their papers at the centre their school runs, within the same belt. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong version. Ask the exams officer for the centre and its zone in writing.

programmes.name: What the grades are for
programmes.description: Screen for someone who can discuss the next step, because the IGCSE choices feed it. A student aiming at the IB Diploma faces a route decision between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation; one aiming at A-Levels faces subject prerequisites. A tutor who knows what Year 12 expects teaches Year 11 differently.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE university route, the Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education from those five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-bandar.subjectsIntro: Every entry here names the code, because the code is the screening tool. A tutor who can discuss these distinctions has taught the courses; one who cannot has taught the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers of equal weight, one of them sat without a calculator. Screen by asking which paper that is and how the tutor drills for it; non-calculator fluency is a separate strand of work and a generalist will not have planned for it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607
subjects.description: Assumes a graphics calculator throughout and adds an investigation component. Screen by asking what the investigation rewards: a written argument rather than a bare answer. Tutors who conflate 0607 with 0580 give this away immediately.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight with a calculator permitted in both, graded 9 to 1. Screen by asking how preparation differs from Cambridge: the honest answer is reading discipline on the long back-of-paper questions, not non-calculator drilling.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
subjects.description: Taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates and a genuinely narrow specialism. Screen by asking what content it adds beyond 4MA1 Higher; an answer that cannot name calculus, series and coordinate geometry has not taught it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Screen on the practical paper's command terms, where candidates describe when the question says explain. A tutor who talks only about content has not marked the paper, which is where this subject's avoidable losses sit.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Screen on mole arithmetic and titration calculations, which are where numerate students gain fastest and where weaker candidates lose most. Organic naming and electrolysis products are the reliable marks worth securing early.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Screen on the long extended responses, where structure rather than knowledge decides the mark, and on the data and statistics questions. A tutor whose plan is to re-read the syllabus has misdiagnosed the subject.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Screen on the directed writing task and on planning under time. Strong writers still lose marks for answering a different question than the one set, and that is a technique problem with a teachable fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Screen on the summary task and the writing registers, which reward structure over vocabulary. Fluent speakers often lose marks precisely there, so a tutor who proposes vocabulary work has read the student rather than the paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Screen on the explain-versus-evaluate distinction and on diagram accuracy. Calculation marks are easy for numerate students; evaluation is where almost every candidate in this belt loses marks, and it is coachable.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Screen on pseudocode conventions and trace tables. Students who can program and cannot write pseudocode to the syllabus conventions lose marks for correct work, which is a precise and checkable area of expertise.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE Social Studies alongside the IGCSE course
subjects.description: Mandatory in UAE private schools beside the licensed curriculum, with published rules on class organisation and language of instruction. Treat any sweeping tutoring claim about these subjects with care, and plan the timetable space they occupy.

sections.heading: Why a deep local market makes selection harder, not easier
paragraphs: In most of Abu Dhabi the tutoring problem is scarcity. Around Al Bandar it is the opposite, and the opposite problem is less obvious. A family here can assemble a shortlist of plausible in-home tutors in an afternoon, mostly resident in or near Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt, all available, all presentable, all describing themselves in the same vocabulary. Nothing in that process tests the only thing that matters, which is whether the person has prepared candidates on your child's specific syllabus and tier.

Abundance also produces a particular failure mode: the street recommendation. One generalist gets a good report from a neighbour and ends up teaching several households in the same precinct, across different boards and year groups. The recommendation was honest, and it was about manner and reliability rather than about 0580 Paper 2. The parent who follows it has outsourced the selection decision to someone whose child sits a different paper.

The fix is not scepticism about people. It is a screening question that bites. Ask which syllabus code and tier they have prepared candidates on, and when. Then ask what each component is worth and which paper permits a calculator. Then ask where candidates lose marks on that specific paper. Those three answers separate the three kinds of tutor this market actually contains, which are set out in the table below, and they do it in minutes rather than in a term. None of the three types is dishonest, and all three are priced differently in the published market bands, so the aim is to buy the one your child's situation calls for.

sections.heading: Four IGCSE maths syllabuses, and how to tell which one a tutor knows
paragraphs: This is the table a parent in this belt most needs, because the school's name reveals nothing about the board. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 runs a Core route graded C to G and an Extended route graded A* to E, assessed by two written papers of equal weight, one of them without a calculator. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 assumes a graphics calculator throughout and adds an investigation component, which is why it is favoured by schools continuing into the IB Diploma.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 has two papers of equal weight with a calculator permitted in both, grades on the 9 to 1 scale, and tiers at Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4. Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 is a separate qualification taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates, running into calculus, series and coordinate geometry, and functioning as a bridge towards AS work.

Use the table as a script. A tutor who has prepared candidates on the syllabus will tell you which paper bans the calculator, what the grade range is, and which topics generate the most avoidable losses, without hesitating. One who has not will speak about mathematics in general, which is a perfectly respectable thing to be able to do and is not what a Year 11 candidate eight weeks from the papers is paying for. Confirm your child's code with the exams officer first, so you are testing against the right answer.

sections.heading: The twelve-minute test for any IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: Run this during a trial session. It needs no subject knowledge on your part and it works on any tutor in this market, including ours. Start with the code: which syllabus and tier have you prepared candidates on, and when? Then the components: what is each paper worth and which one permits a calculator? Then the losses: where do candidates lose marks on this paper, and what do you do about each?

Then four shorter questions. What will you refuse to do with coursework, which matters for a 0607 investigation and for any later IB Internal Assessment? How will progress be reported and in what units, where an answer about confidence is not a measurement? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, so a quoted permit fee is a signal in itself? And who bears the cost if the match turns out to be wrong?

The answers sort candidates quickly. A syllabus specialist is specific, slightly dull and quick to name unglamorous losses such as invisible method and early rounding. A general subject teacher gives good answers on content and vague ones on components. A capable graduate gives warm answers about building confidence. None of those three is dishonest, and all three are sold in the same words on the same directories, which is why the test is worth twelve minutes of a free session rather than a term of fees.

sections.heading: What proximity does not solve: the tier trap
paragraphs: No amount of local choice addresses an administrative ceiling. The route or tier a student is entered for limits the grade that can be awarded regardless of performance. Cambridge grades 0580 Core from C to G, so an A is not available on that entry. Pearson Edexcel caps 4MA1 Foundation at grade 5. A candidate on the lower option who answers every question correctly still cannot be awarded above the cap, and a tutor sitting in your living room cannot change that.

Families in this belt are not immune to it, and in some ways are more exposed. Schools here are strong and well regarded, reports are detailed, and the word IGCSE appears without a code or a tier in most of them. A parent reading a report that says their child is working at a secure level has no way of knowing that the entry caps at a 5. The question that surfaces it is one line in an email to the exams officer, and the window for a change closes when final entries are submitted, months before the papers.

If the tier looks wrong for the student's ambitions, the conversation with the school is about evidence rather than opinion. A full past paper at the higher tier, sat under time at home and marked against the published mark scheme, is a stronger case than a parental view, and it costs a weekend. Ask also for the exam centre and its Cambridge administrative zone in writing, because Cambridge states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one.

sections.heading: In-home is easy here, and still priced above online
paragraphs: Al Bandar is one of the few communities in the emirate where an in-home arrangement is straightforward. Tutors resident in Khalifa City and across the Al Raha belt can be with you in twenty minutes, so the logistics argument for online is weaker here than almost anywhere else in Abu Dhabi. It is worth saying that plainly rather than pretending the geography is against you.

The pricing argument survives anyway. Published figures put in-home one-to-one across Abu Dhabi at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Short journeys put Al Bandar at the lower end of the in-home range rather than outside it; the premium shrinks and does not disappear. Monthly packages in the market sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

The selection argument is the stronger one here. An in-home shortlist in this belt is deep but still local, and it will not reliably contain a Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 specialist or someone who has prepared 0607 investigation candidates. Online widens the set to every specialist on the roster, at a lower published band, and the trade-offs deserve naming: a younger or distractible student is harder to supervise on screen, and the tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India. If presence in the room is what your child needs, this belt is a good place to buy it, with the premium understood.

sections.heading: Exam logistics from the Al Raha Beach precincts
paragraphs: Two practical items catch families in this belt, and neither is about teaching. The first is the timetable version. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version. The zone follows the centre rather than your address, so a student at an Al Raha Gardens school sitting at that school's centre needs that centre's zone, in writing, from the exams officer.

The second is the series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only and should never appear in an Abu Dhabi revision plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. As a guide to the rhythm rather than a date to plan on, Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always open the live official timetable on the board's own site, since provisional timetables are revised.

A third item is worth a sentence because this belt is dense with schools and short on parking. Exam mornings in the Al Raha and Khalifa City clusters put every family on the road at the same time, and the drive that takes twelve minutes in term time can take twice that on the first day of a series. The useful preparation is unglamorous: know the centre, know the zone, know the room, and leave earlier than feels necessary on the first morning.

sections.heading: How progress is measured, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: In a market full of plausible options, how a provider measures itself is part of the selection decision. The measure here is timed questions. A cold paper at the start, every lost mark classified as a method error, an arithmetic slip, a misread question or genuine unknown content, and the same question types repeated after the repair work. At six sessions you receive a statement naming what has moved and the three topics still costing the most marks. That is checkable, which is the only property that makes a measurement worth anything.

If the match is wrong, the tutor changes at our cost. This matters more in a crowded market than a thin one, because the social cost of switching a well-liked local tutor is high and families often persist for a term rather than have the conversation. A scheduled review at six sessions removes that problem by making the question routine.

What we will not publish is anything we cannot evidence. No satisfaction percentage, no score-improvement figure, no student count, no star rating, because none of them could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method; in the pages researched for this project one provider displayed two contradictory review totals on a single page. We also claim no accreditation: IB Gram holds no licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no premises in the UAE. And on coursework the boundary is fixed. A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on your child's own work, including on a 0607 investigation, and never produces it or supplies submittable text. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments, and the malpractice consequences of that fall on the candidate.

faqs.question: There are plenty of IGCSE tutors near Al Bandar. How do I choose between them?
faqs.answer: Test for syllabus knowledge rather than manner. Ask which syllabus code and tier they have prepared candidates on and when, what each paper is worth and which permits a calculator, and where candidates lose marks on that specific paper. A specialist answers all three immediately and names unglamorous losses such as invisible method and early rounding. A capable generalist answers warmly about confidence. Both are sold in the same words on the same directories, and twelve minutes of a free trial separates them.

faqs.question: Does a neighbour's recommendation in Al Raha Beach tell me anything useful?
faqs.answer: It tells you about reliability and manner, which matter, and nothing about whether the tutor has prepared candidates on your child's paper. Abundance in this belt produces a particular pattern: one well-liked generalist teaching several households across different boards and year groups. The recommendation was honest and it was about the wrong variable. Take the name, then run the syllabus questions yourself, because your child may sit Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 while the neighbour's sits Cambridge 0580 Extended.

faqs.question: How many different IGCSE maths syllabuses might an Abu Dhabi school use?
faqs.answer: At least four. Cambridge Mathematics 0580, with Core graded C to G and Extended A* to E and one paper sat without a calculator. Cambridge International Mathematics 0607, which assumes a graphics calculator and adds an investigation component. Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1, two calculator papers on the 9 to 1 scale with Foundation capped at grade 5. And Pearson Edexcel Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1, taken alongside 4MA1 by stronger candidates. The code sits on the exam entry statement, not in the school's name.

faqs.question: My child's school is well regarded. Could the tier still be capping the grade?
faqs.answer: Yes, and strong schools are no protection because the issue is administrative. Cambridge grades the 0580 Core route C to G and Pearson Edexcel caps the 4MA1 Foundation tier at grade 5, so a candidate on the lower option cannot be awarded above the cap however well they perform. Detailed reports rarely state the tier; they say IGCSE. One line in an email to the exams officer surfaces it, and the window for a change closes when final entries are submitted, months before the papers.

faqs.question: Is in-home tutoring a reasonable choice from Al Bandar?
faqs.answer: It is more reasonable here than almost anywhere else in the emirate, because tutors based in Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt can arrive in twenty minutes. The honest trade-offs are price and breadth: published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and a local shortlist will not reliably contain a 4PM1 specialist or someone who has prepared 0607 investigation candidates. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge 0607 investigation component actually reward?
faqs.answer: A written mathematical argument rather than a correct final answer. Students who treat 0607 as 0580 with a graphics calculator lose most of their marks exactly here, because they present results without the reasoning, the exploration or the commentary the task is built to assess. Ask any tutor what the investigation rewards; it is the single fastest way to find out whether they have prepared 0607 candidates or are assuming it is a Cambridge maths paper with different buttons.

faqs.question: How is preparing for Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 different from Cambridge 0580?
faqs.answer: The calculator rules change the work. Cambridge 0580 sits one of its two equally weighted papers without a calculator, so non-calculator fluency is a separate strand requiring short, frequent drilling. Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 permits a calculator in both papers, which moves the risk to the long multi-step questions at the back of each paper, where candidates stop reading after the first clause and lose a correct method. A tutor who proposes identical preparation for both has prepared candidates for neither.

faqs.question: What should a tutor say when I ask where candidates lose marks?
faqs.answer: Something specific and slightly boring. Invisible method, where a correct approach earns nothing because only one line was written. Early rounding carried through a multi-step answer. Bearings, similar-shape area and volume scale factors, compound percentage change, histograms with unequal class widths, vectors, all of which arrive late in most schemes of work and are commonly left unconsolidated. Reading errors, where a reason is requested and a calculation supplied. An answer about confidence and motivation is a different kind of answer.

faqs.question: Do tutors in this part of Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it. A quoted permit fee is a warning sign, and working without a permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Al Bandar candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only and must not appear in an Abu Dhabi plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, since it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses a paper after reading the wrong version.

faqs.question: How do I avoid an awkward conversation if the tutor turns out to be wrong for my child?
faqs.answer: Schedule the conversation in advance so it stops being awkward. We review at six sessions, report progress on timed questions rather than impressions, and change the tutor at our cost if the match is poor. That matters more in a community where tutors arrive through neighbour recommendations, because the social cost of switching is what keeps families in a mismatch for a full term. Nothing renews automatically either, so stopping requires no conversation at all.

faqs.question: Will an Al Bandar tutor mark a full paper against the published mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most useful single thing a tutor does. The practice is to sit a full paper to the published duration, then go through it against the mark scheme so the student sees what each mark is awarded for. What we will not do is publish or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

faqs.question: Are the ratings on tutoring directories in this market worth anything?
faqs.answer: Not without a sample size, a date and a method. In the pages researched for this project, one provider displayed two different review totals on the same page and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a far larger claim about students taught. Self-asserted rating markup is against Google's structured-data policy and, as a commercial representation in the UAE, a consumer-protection exposure. We publish no rating, student count or satisfaction figure, which is also why this page offers you a test instead.

faqs.question: What if we only want to know what is wrong, not buy a course?
faqs.answer: Then take the free screening trial and stop there. Your child works on real questions at their tier, the tutor watches the method rather than the answers, and you leave with the largest error category named, a view on whether the entry tier can award your target grade, and the six answers from the twelve-minute test. No card is required and nothing renews. Taking the diagnosis to the school is a legitimate use of it, and sometimes the honest conclusion is that no tutoring is needed.

intro.heading: Al Bateen, Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif, the Corniche: four addresses, one answer
paragraphs: Al Bateen is among the better-served parts of Abu Dhabi for tutoring. It is central, it sits close to several long-established schools, and a tutor living in Khalidiyah or Al Mushrif can reach it without a bridge crossing. A family here searching for somebody local will get results, which is not true of Al Reef or the outer mainland communities. That is the honest starting point, and this page does not pretend otherwise.

The interesting question is what that convenience actually buys. Compare Al Bateen with Khalidiyah, with Al Mushrif and with the Corniche, and the four areas draw on substantially the same pool of tutors, send children to overlapping sets of schools, and face the same scarcity in the same subjects. The differences between them are measured in minutes of driving. The things that determine whether tutoring works, which are the syllabus code, the tier, the quality of the diagnosis and the consistency of the slot, do not vary by postcode at all.

That matters because proximity is the filter families instinctively apply first, and in a central area it feels like a filter that costs nothing. It does cost something. A tutor who can reach Al Bateen in fifteen minutes is still selected from the set of people willing to travel at that hour, and for Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654, for Pearson 4CH1 rather than Cambridge 0620, or for Arabic as a first language, that set can be empty on the island exactly as it is on the mainland. The convenience hides the scarcity rather than solving it.

What the comparison does reveal is where a short commute is genuinely valuable. Fifteen minutes saved each way, twice a week, is an hour of a student's time per week returned, and for a Year 11 candidate in the final term that hour is worth having. The useful move is to notice that online delivery returns the same hour without the premium, and then to spend it on the thing the marked script says is costing the grade.

What follows is the comparison in detail, with the supply picture, the cost picture, and the things that are identical across all four districts. It also covers what an ADEK inspection band actually means, since Al Bateen families compare schools as often as they compare tutors, and both comparisons are frequently made on the wrong evidence. IB Gram does not sell home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, and that has been the position on every country page we publish. The practical consequence for a central household is that the best hour of the day stays available, because nobody has to be anywhere by then.

paragraphs: Families in Al Bateen compare their options with Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and the Corniche regularly, usually when choosing a school and occasionally when choosing a tutor. For tutoring the comparison turns out to be undramatic. All four draw on the same tutor pool, because the drive between them is short enough that a tutor serving one serves all of them. All four send children to overlapping sets of schools, so the boards and codes in play are the same. All four face identical scarcity in the same handful of subjects.

What does differ is small and worth knowing. The Corniche and Al Markaziyah are apartment districts with shorter school runs and later parental commutes, which shifts the typical request towards evening slots. Al Mushrif sits slightly inland, so a tutor coming from Khalidiyah loses a few minutes. Al Bateen's villa plots mean an in-home visit involves a gate and a parking decision that an apartment visit does not. None of those changes who is qualified to teach Cambridge 0620 Extended.

The practical conclusion is that a recommendation from a neighbour two streets away is worth exactly as much as one from Al Mushrif, and both are worth less than knowing whether the tutor has taught your child's syllabus code. sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same
paragraphs: Three things determine whether IGCSE tutoring works, and none of them is geographic. The first is whether the tutor knows the syllabus your child is entered for, meaning the code, the tier, the papers and what the mark scheme credits. A tutor who knows chemistry but not 0620 Extended will teach correct chemistry against the wrong question style, and that is equally true whether they live fifteen minutes away or fifty.

The second is the quality of the diagnosis. A plan built from a marked mock script targets the clusters where marks are actually being lost; a plan built from a conversation works forward through the syllabus and reaches those clusters in week six, by which time the budget is spent. Reading the script is free and takes fifteen minutes, and it is the single highest-return action available to a parent in any of these four districts.

The third is consistency. A slot that holds every week for a term beats a better tutor seen irregularly, because each gap costs the first part of the next session in recovery. Central districts have an advantage here, since short commutes make afternoon slots viable, but the advantage is realised by choosing a time that survives a bad week rather than by living closer to somebody. All three factors are available to a family in Al Bateen, Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif or the Corniche on identical terms, which is why the recommendation does not change by address.

sections.heading: What a short commute is genuinely worth
paragraphs: There is a real benefit to living centrally and it is worth naming precisely, because precision is what lets a family decide whether to pay for it. A fifteen-minute journey each way, rather than forty, returns roughly fifty minutes of a student's own time per visit. Twice a week across a term that is a meaningful quantity, and in the final term of Year 11 it is the difference between a student who has time to attempt a timed paper and one who does not.

That is the benefit. It is a benefit of the student's commute, not of the tutor's, and it is already available to an Al Bateen household regardless of delivery. What a short tutor commute buys is slightly different: the possibility of an afternoon slot rather than only an evening one, which matters because the afternoon hour is better for new content while the student is still alert and the school lesson is recent.

Online delivery supplies that same benefit without the premium, which is the only reason this page argues against the local option at all. Nobody travels, so the afternoon slot is available and so is the late evening one, at the same rate, and a session can move when the week collapses. The market cost of the alternative is documented: in-home one-to-one tuition in Abu Dhabi is quoted at AED 180 to 350 an hour in Bestimate's 2026 survey, with independents reaching AED 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The difference is the journey, not the teaching.

sections.heading: Triage: the part that is identical in every district
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in these districts is typically entered for eight to ten subjects, and no family can or should buy support for all of them. The triage method is the same in Al Bateen as in Al Reef, which is itself the clearest evidence that the address is not the variable. It is done from the marked mock scripts, read side by side, rather than from which department sent the most worrying email.

Rank each subject on three questions. How far is the current mark from the target, in grade boundaries rather than percentages, since a subject two marks below a boundary is a better investment than one twenty marks below. Are the losses concentrated in two or three topics, or spread evenly across the paper, because concentrated losses respond to tutoring and even losses mean content was never learned. And does the subject reward technique, as mathematics and English as a Second Language strongly do and biology does much less.

The output is a short written ranking: one or two subjects with a weekly slot, one or two with a short block that then stops, and the rest left alone with a revision plan the student runs themselves. That last category is the uncomfortable one, because it means accepting that a subject will land where it lands. It is also the difference between a budget that moves three grades and one that moves none, and the conversation is far better had in October than in April.

sections.heading: Inspection bands: what a rating means and what it does not
paragraphs: Families in these districts compare schools as often as they compare tutors, and the comparison is frequently made on half-remembered ratings. The UAE school inspection framework uses a six-band scale, from Outstanding at the top through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. For a school in Al Bateen, Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif or anywhere else in the emirate, the body that publishes that judgement is ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain.

Two cautions follow from that. The first is that a rating quoted from a Dubai report describes a school inspected by KHDA, which oversees private education in that emirate, and is not comparable to an Abu Dhabi judgement in the way parents assume. The second is that a band is a whole-school judgement across many areas, and a school rated Good may be strong in the sciences and weak in a specific subject your child happens to take. Read the published report rather than the headline band, and verify both on the regulator's own site rather than on an aggregator.

The relevance to tutoring is narrow but real. An inspection band tells you nothing about whether your child's particular IGCSE class is covering the syllabus at the pace the entry requires, which is the question a tutoring decision actually turns on. The marked mock script answers that; the inspection report does not. Where the report is genuinely useful is in confirming which curricula and programmes a school offers, which is worth checking before relying on anything a tutoring provider tells you about a school's board.

sections.heading: The scarce subjects are scarce here too
paragraphs: Central location does not solve the supply problem that families in outer communities complain about. It hides it, which is in some ways worse, because an Al Bateen household expects to find somebody and is therefore more likely to accept the nearest person who says yes rather than asking what they have actually taught. The scarcity is in specific codes rather than in subjects, and it looks the same across the island as across the mainland.

Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 is scarce because the double award removes specific sub-topics and most tutors have only taught the single sciences. Pearson science codes are scarce relative to Cambridge, because most tutors in this market learned Cambridge first and a family that assumed Cambridge will not know to ask. Arabic as a first language is scarce because it is treated as a specialism by the regulators themselves. Extended-tier chemistry becomes scarce whenever several schools' internal deadlines land together.

The remedy is the same wherever you live. Confirm the code and tier in writing from the school before anything else. Ask any prospective tutor to name one topic in that syllabus that is not assessed at your child's tier, because somebody working from a specification can exclude things and somebody working from a general idea of the subject cannot. And accept a short wait for the right person rather than a fast match that has to be re-diagnosed later, which is the choice that actually costs money.

sections.heading: Materials, marking and the line that applies everywhere
paragraphs: IGCSE carries little independent coursework, so the honesty question here is mostly about materials rather than about writing. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. Reproducing or distributing them as downloads is copyright infringement, and for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. A tutor should reference and link the official source rather than handing over a folder, and a provider advertising a bundle of mark schemes as a selling point has told you how they treat rules generally.

What a tutor should do with a mark scheme is teach from it. Working through why a method mark is awarded, and what wording earns nothing, is durable learning and is where a large share of recoverable marks sit. Handing a student a set of worked answers teaches them to recognise familiar questions, which fails as soon as the question changes. The distinction is easy to check: ask what the tutor does with a mark scheme in a session.

Marking is the related question that changes what a quoted rate means. A full Extended paper marked properly against the published scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes, so whether it sits inside the fee materially affects the comparison between two providers. Written feedback naming which mark was lost and why gives a family something to act on. A verbal walkthrough in the session leaves no record by the following week. Ask before booking, in all four districts, because this is another variable that has nothing to do with where anybody lives.

sections.heading: Deciding on evidence rather than on an address
paragraphs: The decision procedure that follows from all of this is short and does not mention where anybody lives. Email the school for the board, the syllabus code, the tier, and whether any paper is sat without a calculator, for each subject under consideration. Read the marked mock scripts side by side and rank the subjects. Then approach two or three providers with the same brief rather than with a vague request, which is what makes their replies comparable.

Ask each of them the same four things. Which code and tier, and what are the papers. Name one topic in that syllabus not assessed at my child's tier. From this script, which lost marks are content, which are method, which are timing. And what happens if the match is wrong. The answers arrive in minutes from somebody who teaches the course and get assembled in front of you by somebody who does not, and the difference is audible without any technical knowledge on your part.

Then test the one that answers best with a free hour over live video, no card details and no commitment, worked on your child's own script. Afterwards ask your child whether they followed it, which is the judgement that predicts whether the arrangement will hold. Done in that order, the question of whether a tutor could have driven from Khalidiyah to Al Bateen in fifteen minutes turns out never to have come up, which is the point this page has been making throughout.
