faqs.question: Is it easier to find an IGCSE tutor in Al Bateen than elsewhere in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: For mainstream subjects, yes. Al Bateen is central, close to several long-established schools, and reachable from Khalidiyah or Al Mushrif without a bridge crossing, so a family searching locally will get results in a way that Al Reef households will not. For specific codes the picture is identical to the rest of the emirate: Coordinated Sciences 0654, Pearson science codes and Arabic as a first language are scarce here too. Central location hides that scarcity rather than solving it, which makes it easier to accept the wrong match.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Bateen rather than Khalidiyah change anything for tutoring?
faqs.answer: No. The two districts are adjacent, share schools and draw on the same tutor pool, so a tutor serving one almost certainly serves the other and quotes them nearly identically. What differs is housing type and commute by a few minutes, and whether an in-home visit involves a villa gate or an apartment lobby. None of that affects whether somebody has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended to an examination, which is the variable that determines whether the hour is worth paying for.

faqs.question: What is a short school commute actually worth?
faqs.answer: Roughly fifty minutes of your child's own time per journey, compared with a forty-minute run from the outer communities. Across a term that is a real quantity, and in the final months of Year 11 it is the difference between having time to attempt a timed paper and not. That benefit belongs to the student's commute and is already yours. A short tutor commute is a separate and smaller benefit: it makes an afternoon slot possible, which online delivery supplies anyway without the travel premium.

faqs.question: How much does an in-home IGCSE tutor cost on the island?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 UAE survey puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour across Abu Dhabi, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. Budget platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65, which buys accountability rather than grade movement. The gap between in-home and online is largely the journey, which from a central district is shorter but still priced in. IB Gram quotes after the free trial.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects should we actually pay for?
faqs.answer: One or two, chosen from the marked mocks rather than from which teacher is most concerned. Rank on three things: how close the mark is to a grade boundary, whether the losses cluster in a few topics or spread evenly across the paper, and whether the subject rewards technique. Mathematics and English as a Second Language reward technique strongly; biology much less, because its content is learnable alone. Subjects with evenly spread losses need content recovery rather than tutoring, which is slower and different work.

faqs.question: What does an ADEK inspection band actually tell me?
faqs.answer: A whole-school judgement across many areas, on a six-band scale running from Outstanding through Very Good, Good and Acceptable to Weak and Very Weak. For an Abu Dhabi school the publisher is ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; a rating quoted from a Dubai report describes a KHDA inspection of a different system. A band tells you nothing about whether your child's particular class is covering the syllabus at the pace the entry requires, which is what a tutoring decision turns on.

faqs.question: Can I rely on a neighbour's tutor recommendation?
faqs.answer: Only after one check. Ask which board and syllabus code the neighbour's child sits, because a tutor who is excellent on Cambridge 0580 Extended may be an awkward fit for Pearson 4MA1 Higher even though both are IGCSE mathematics. Question phrasing, paper structure and formula provision all differ. If the code matches, a recommendation from two streets away is genuinely useful. If it does not, you are being recommended somebody for a different examination, which is how diligent revision produces a confusing mock result.

faqs.question: Why is Coordinated Sciences hard to find a tutor for even centrally?
faqs.answer: Because a double award is not a simplified version of three separate sciences. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 removes specific sub-topics while keeping others at full depth, so a tutor who has only taught 0620, 0625 and 0610 will cover material that is not assessed and may under-weight material that is. Most tutors in this market have taught the single sciences, which makes the double award a genuine specialism. Confirm the code with the school and ask a prospective tutor which sub-topics the syllabus cuts.

faqs.question: Should past-paper marking be included in the rate?
faqs.answer: Ask, because it is the variable that makes two quotes incomparable. Marking a full Extended paper properly against the published scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and written feedback naming which mark was lost and why is where most of the visible improvement comes from. Some tutors include it, some charge for it, and some go through answers verbally in the session, which leaves no record by the following week. A higher rate that includes written marking is often the cheaper arrangement overall.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give my child a folder of mark schemes?
faqs.answer: They should not. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them as downloads is copyright infringement, with unreleased material carrying a malpractice exposure as well. The proper use of a mark scheme is in the session: working through why a method mark is awarded and what wording earns nothing. Handing over worked answers teaches a student to recognise familiar questions, which fails the moment the question changes.

faqs.question: Is an afternoon or an evening slot better in these districts?
faqs.answer: Afternoon, where the commute allows it, because the student is alert and the school lesson is recent enough for the day's worksheet to be the material. Central districts make that genuinely available rather than theoretical. Apartment households on the Corniche with later parental commutes often prefer the evening, which is fine provided the content suits a tired hour: past-paper sections, circle theorems, technique drills rather than new teaching. Both windows cost the same when nobody is travelling to the house.

faqs.question: Do tutors visit homes in Al Bateen?
faqs.answer: Local independent tutors do, and the central location means the travel premium is smaller than from the mainland, which is part of why the in-home option looks attractive here. IB Gram is not among them: there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from us, and visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Al Bateen lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which keeps both the afternoon and the evening window available at the same rate.

faqs.question: My child transferred from an MYP school nearby. What changes?
faqs.answer: The evidence base. MYP assesses against four criteria graded 1 to 8, with investigation and communication credited heavily and no terminal written papers in most schools. IGCSE produces the grade from written papers in a single series. Students arrive able to reason about unfamiliar problems and unfamiliar with structured paper technique, timing and showing working in a form that earns method marks. Because these districts contain both kinds of school within a short drive, this transfer is common here and the gap is predictable and short.

faqs.question: How do I make two Al Bateen tutoring quotes comparable?
faqs.answer: Give both providers the same written brief: board, syllabus code, tier, calculator rules, the ranking from the mocks and the scripts themselves. Then ask each the same four questions, and note whether full-paper marking is inside the rate and what happens if the match is wrong. Quotes in this market are not comparable because the requests are not, and five minutes writing the brief does more for the comparison than an hour of reading profiles. Keep the written replies rather than relying on a phone conversation.

faqs.question: Is there any case for choosing a tutor by location?
faqs.answer: Yes, in specific situations. A young child who needs an adult physically in the room, a student for whom in-person support has been recommended by a professional, and a household with unreliable connectivity are all cases where a local tutor is the right answer and the travel premium is money well spent. For an academic IGCSE subject at Extended or Higher tier, syllabus depth beats distance, and in a central district the convenience of being close makes it easier to settle for the wrong match.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingHeading: Same answer in four districts: ask about the code
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingBody: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Bateen is easier to find than in most of Abu Dhabi, and that convenience changes less than it appears to. Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and the Corniche share the same tutor pool, the same schools and the same scarcity in the same codes. Email the school for the board, code, tier and calculator rules, rank the subjects from the marked mocks, ask any provider the four questions on this page, and test the best answer with a free hour over live video.

intro.heading: The Al Falah day: mostly travel, with one usable block at the end of it
paragraphs: Al Falah is a planned villa community out towards the airport road, and almost none of its secondary provision is on the doorstep. Children travel: to Khalifa City, to Al Raha, to Yas Island, sometimes all the way to the island centre. That means an early departure, a long return, and an evening whose shape is set by a bus timetable rather than by anything a parent decides. Any tutoring arrangement that does not start from those facts is being planned for a household that does not exist.

Work out the actual numbers for your own route and the picture becomes clear. A 7:00 departure and a return somewhere between 15:30 and 16:45 leaves a tired child, a meal, prayer, and school homework that is due tomorrow and therefore has to win. What remains is one block, typically between 17:30 and 20:00, and it is the only slot a weekly session can occupy with any chance of surviving a full term. Families who book two weekday sessions in that single block almost always drop to one by half term, having paid for both.

So this page treats scheduling as the first subject rather than an afterthought. It maps the journey from Al Falah to each school cluster in minutes, because the journey is the constraint. It sets out the Year 10 option-sheet decisions, which quietly determine what grade is even available two years later. It maps revision across a UAE academic year including Ramadan, since the position of Ramadan relative to the exam term moves each year and reshapes the final run-up. And it names what happens when a session has to move, because in a household built around travel, sessions move.

The second half of the page does the IGCSE work properly: Core against Extended and Foundation against Higher, how many subjects a UAE student should carry, the five-subject count the Ministry of Education uses for British-track equivalency, and the exam-week logistics that trip up families whose exam centre is not the school nearest home. None of that is local colour. It is the specific set of decisions an Al Falah parent has to make, in the order they arrive.

One statement first. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any UAE address. Home visits are a service offered only in India. The phrase people type is home tutor, so that is the phrase this page uses, and the delivery is one-to-one live video in Gulf Standard Time. From Al Falah that is not a compromise so much as the only arrangement that does not add a second journey to a day that is already made of journeys. It also means the choice of tutor is made on subject knowledge rather than on who is willing to drive out towards the airport road at six in the evening, which is the trade most families in this community are quietly asked to accept.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE course begins
programmes.description: The cheapest and most effective place to intervene, and the least used. A student who arrives in Year 10 with secure arithmetic, the habit of writing method and some experience of timed work needs far less support later. Sessions here are short, early in the evening, and often fortnightly rather than weekly.
programmes.countryNote: For Al Falah families this is also the stage where the evening is easiest to protect, because homework volume is lower and bedtimes are earlier. A 17:30 slot works. By Year 11 the same household will be fighting for 18:30, so building the habit of a fixed weekly slot at this stage pays off twice.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years ending in external papers. Year 10 is the year of decisions: subject count, tier, and whether the entry can deliver the grade the family is aiming at. Year 11 is execution: content repair, then timed papers with mark schemes read afterwards. The scheduling problem is sharpest in Year 11, when homework load peaks at the same time as revision demand.
programmes.countryNote: Al Falah students sit their papers at the centre their school runs, which may be a long drive from home. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, since it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong version. Confirm the zone with the exams officer, then plan the journey for exam week.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades are being used for
programmes.description: A-Levels, the IB Diploma, or a UAE university route, and each has different entry expectations. The practical consequence in Year 10 is the option sheet: a student who drops a subject that a later route requires has made a decision that is hard to reverse, and one that no amount of tutoring addresses.
programmes.countryNote: For the UAE route, the Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at not less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Checking the option sheet against that count in Year 10 takes minutes. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae, because a tutoring page is not the authority.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-falah.subjectsIntro: Al Falah requests spread across the sciences and maths, with a humanity or two attached. Each entry names the specific work rather than the subject in general.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The most requested subject. Work targets the non-calculator paper, algebraic manipulation, and the back-of-paper multi-step questions where visible method decides whether partial credit is earned at all.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two calculator papers of equal weight on the 9 to 1 scale. Higher-tier work concentrates on surds, algebraic proof, vectors and the long problems candidates abandon after the first clause.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Equation rearrangement under time pressure, graph interpretation, and the practical paper's command terms, where describing instead of explaining costs marks on questions the student can do.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, titration calculations, electrolysis products and organic naming rules. Students who understand the chemistry and fail the arithmetic need a maths intervention rather than more chemistry.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Data handling, rate graphs and the long extended responses where structure rather than knowledge decides the mark. Revision by reading is the most common reason a capable student under-performs here.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Reading comprehension technique, the summary task and the writing registers. Students who speak fluently often lose marks on exactly the tasks that reward structure over vocabulary.

sections.heading: What the Al Falah school run costs in minutes, and what that leaves
paragraphs: Scheduling arguments in this community are really arithmetic arguments, so here is the arithmetic. Secondary provision near Al Falah is limited, so most children travel, and the bus route matters as much as the destination: a route that loops through several communities can add half an hour to the return for the children at the end of it. Two students from the same classroom can therefore be home forty minutes apart, and a parent who books a session on the strength of the bell time will spend the term apologising.

Add the fixed claims. A meal, prayer, and school homework set for tomorrow, which has to be done because a child who skips it to attend tutoring arrives at school behind and the tutoring takes the blame. In most Al Falah households that leaves a single block between roughly 17:30 and 20:00. One session fits there comfortably. Two do not, and families who try end up paying for a second session that is cancelled more often than it runs.

The table below gives indicative one-way journey ranges from Al Falah to the clusters children here actually attend, so you can estimate your own evening rather than guess at it. Treat them as a planning aid and check your own route, because the spread between off-peak and peak is large and the bus adds to both. The practical conclusion is simple: find the real return time first, then choose the slot, and hold that slot for the whole term. Because lessons run over live video, moving a slot later is a message rather than a logistics problem, which is the one scheduling advantage online delivery has over a car.

sections.heading: The Year 10 option sheet, which decides more than any tutor can
paragraphs: Three decisions are made in Year 10 that set the limits of what Year 11 can achieve, and all three are reversible only for a short window. The first is the tier. Cambridge grades the 0580 Core route C to G and the Extended route A* to E; Pearson Edexcel caps the 4MA1 Foundation tier at grade 5 while Higher runs 9 to 4. A capped entry cannot award the grade a family may be assuming, and no amount of tutoring in the spring changes that. This applies across tiered subjects, not only mathematics.

The second is subject count. A student carrying too many subjects spreads thin and under-performs across the set; a student carrying too few can find a route closed later. For the UAE university path, the Ministry of Education's published British-track requirement counts five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A family that assumed those two counted can arrive at application with four qualifying subjects. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae; one competitor page ranking for these searches publishes the wrong subject count, which is exactly the kind of error a family acts on.

The third is which subjects a later route requires. Dropping a science or a second language in Year 10 can close an A-Level or Diploma combination two years later, and the student making the choice is fifteen. The table below sets out the decisions, when the window closes and what to ask for in writing. All of this costs an email to the exams officer and a conversation at home, and it is worth more than a term of tutoring fees.

sections.heading: When revision actually happens in a UAE academic year
paragraphs: A revision plan drawn as twelve identical weeks does not survive a UAE school year, because the year is not twelve identical weeks. It has a long hot start, a winter break that interrupts momentum at exactly the wrong moment for Year 11, school assessment weeks that consume all available attention, a spring break, and Ramadan, whose position relative to the exam term shifts by roughly eleven days each year in the Gregorian calendar and therefore cannot be planned once and reused.

The sensible design works with that shape. Autumn term is for content repair and habit building, when the pressure is lowest and the gains compound. The weeks after the winter break are the most productive revision weeks of the entire year, and families who start tutoring in February have usually missed them. School assessment weeks are for whatever the school is testing, because a student cannot run two revision programmes at once, and insisting otherwise is how plans get abandoned rather than adjusted. Ramadan calls for shorter sessions at post-Iftar timing, with the load reduced rather than the plan cancelled.

Then the final stretch, which should be timed papers rather than content. By then the question is not what the student knows but what they can produce in the time allowed, under the specific conditions of their board. The table below maps the year with what each phase is for, and it is deliberately the opposite of a flat weekly schedule. Al Falah families with long commutes benefit more than most from this shape, because it concentrates demand in the periods when the household has capacity and backs off when it does not.

sections.heading: Where a session fits once homework and prayer are in
paragraphs: The single usable block has to accommodate one session and nothing else, which means the rest of the week carries the practice. That inverts how most families imagine tutoring works. The hour with a tutor is not the study; it is the diagnosis, the teaching and the correction. The study is the twenty minutes on the other nights, and if those twenty minutes do not happen, the hour is spent re-teaching rather than advancing.

In practice that means the tasks set between sessions have to be small enough to survive a long school day. One question type. One set of corrections from the last marked attempt. Fifteen minutes of arithmetic for a student sitting the Cambridge non-calculator paper. A task that takes an hour will not be done, and a tutor who sets one is misreading the household rather than being rigorous. Over a term, short and completed beats ambitious and skipped by a wide margin.

The other half of this is protecting the block itself. Three things reliably destroy it: scheduling the session on the night the school sets its heaviest homework, scheduling it before the bus reliably arrives, and adding a second weekly session the household cannot support. Ask your child which night is worst and avoid it. Build the slot on the observed return time rather than the published one. And add the second session only in the final stretch, after a diagnosis has said what it is for.

sections.heading: Exam week from Al Falah: the centre, the zone and the journey
paragraphs: Two logistics problems catch Al Falah families, and both are avoidable. The first is the timetable version. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The zone follows the centre, not your home address, so the question goes to the school's exams officer and the answer should be in writing.

The second is the journey itself. If the exam centre is in the Al Raha belt, on Yas Island or on the island, exam week means a morning drive at peak hour with no bus to fall back on, often starting earlier than the normal school run because the centre wants candidates seated well before the start. A dry run the week before costs an hour and removes the one variable that can end a paper before it begins. Build in a margin that assumes something goes wrong on the road, because occasionally it does.

On sessions and series, the position for UAE candidates is straightforward. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in June and November, and those are the two series UAE candidates sit; the February and March series is offered to India only and must not appear in an Abu Dhabi plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. As a guide to the rhythm rather than a date to rely on, Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Open the live official timetable on the board's own site, since provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: The second journey is the thing that fails
paragraphs: An in-home arrangement from Al Falah adds a journey to a day already built from journeys, and it is usually the tutor's journey that breaks first. A specialist coming from Khalifa City, Al Raha or the island at the evening peak is committing forty minutes or more each way, and that cost is paid either as a travel premium or as a shorter session, with cancellations as the eventual outcome. Published Abu Dhabi figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The difference is the road.

Counted in minutes rather than dirhams, the comparison is starker. A sixty-minute online session costs the household sixty minutes. A sixty-minute in-home session costs the household sixty minutes plus the risk that the tutor arrives late and the slot overruns into bedtime, in a community where the slot had no slack in it to begin with. Over a term of twelve sessions, a pattern that loses one session a month to travel has delivered nine lessons for the price of twelve.

There are real losses on the other side and they should be said plainly. A younger or distractible student is harder to supervise through a screen, and a tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper. Both are worth testing in the free trial rather than assuming. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India. If a physical presence in the room is what your child actually needs, buy it from the local market with the travel premium understood, and schedule it for a weekend rather than into the weekday block.

sections.heading: What we measure, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: A household giving up its only usable evening block deserves evidence that the hour is working. The measure used here is timed questions rather than impressions: a cold paper at the start, every lost mark classified as a method error, an arithmetic slip, a misread question or genuine unknown content, and the same question types repeated after the repair. That produces a sentence a parent can check, naming the three topics still costing the most marks, rather than a report that the student seems more confident.

At six sessions the tutor reports what has moved and what has not, and the plan changes accordingly. If the match is wrong, the tutor changes. The most common way tutoring quietly fails is a family persisting politely with someone competent who is not right for their child, and a scheduled review removes the social cost of saying so. Nothing renews automatically, and a family that wants only the diagnosis can take it and stop.

What we will not do is publish numbers we cannot evidence. No satisfaction percentage, no score-improvement figure, no self-asserted rating, because we could not show you the sample size, the date and the method. No promise of a grade, because IGCSE is externally assessed and the grade belongs to the student on the day. And no claim of accreditation: IB Gram holds no licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no premises in the UAE. On coursework the boundary is equally fixed. A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on your child's own work; a tutor does not produce it, supply submittable text, or edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being theirs.

faqs.question: What time should an IGCSE session start for a child commuting from Al Falah?
faqs.answer: Usually between 17:30 and 18:30, and the right answer depends on your bus route rather than on the school bell. Children travelling to Al Shamkha or the airport corridor can often manage 17:00 or 17:30; those on the Al Raha, Yas Island or island runs are generally home too late for anything before 18:00. Observe the actual door time across a normal week before booking. Because lessons run over live video, shifting a slot later is a message rather than a logistics problem.

faqs.question: Do you send an IGCSE tutor to a villa in Al Falah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Al Falah lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The in-home market here is real and quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against about AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. In a community this far from the school clusters, the in-home premium is mostly the evening-peak journey, which is also what makes those arrangements slip.

faqs.question: Can my child manage two weekday tutoring sessions alongside an Al Falah school run?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually better not to try. After travel, food, prayer and school homework, most households here have one usable block between roughly 17:30 and 20:00. One session fits it; a second gets cancelled, and the cancellation habit then spreads to the first. The better structure is one protected weekday session plus a longer weekend session when a full timed paper and its mark-scheme review are needed, since that review is a two-hour job no school night can hold.

faqs.question: How much homework should my child do between sessions?
faqs.answer: Fifteen to twenty minutes on two or three nights, not an hour. The tutor's hour is for diagnosis, teaching and correction; the practice happens on the other nights, and if it does not happen the next session is spent re-teaching rather than advancing. Realistic tasks are one question type, one set of corrections from the last marked attempt, or a short arithmetic drill for a student sitting the Cambridge non-calculator paper. A task that will not be completed is worse than no task.

faqs.question: Which Year 10 decisions matter most for an Al Falah student's IGCSE grades?
faqs.answer: Three. The tier, because Cambridge 0580 Core is graded C to G and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation caps at grade 5, so a capped entry cannot award a top grade however well the student performs. The number of subjects carried, since too many spreads a student thin and too few can close a route. And which subjects a later A-Level, Diploma or UAE university path requires. All three are set on the option sheet and all three are hard to reverse once entries are submitted.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a UAE route actually require?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry of Education's published requirement counts five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or 3, plus either one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A competitor page ranking for these searches states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on moe.gov.ae, and check the option sheet against the count during Year 10.

faqs.question: When in the school year should we start tutoring if exams are in June?
faqs.answer: Autumn term if you can, and no later than immediately after the winter break. The weeks following that break are the most productive revision weeks of the entire year, and families who begin in February have already lost them. Autumn is cheap in every sense: the pressure is low, the gains compound, and habits like writing visible method have time to become automatic. The final six to eight weeks should be timed papers rather than content, which only works if content was repaired earlier.

faqs.question: Should an Al Falah family keep IGCSE sessions running through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Shorter, later and fewer, rather than cancelled. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing on request, and the load drops while the rhythm is kept. Because Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, its position relative to the exam term shifts, so the plan has to be drawn fresh each year rather than reused. A household that pauses entirely tends to lose three or four weeks of momentum; one that reduces intensity usually resumes without a restart.

faqs.question: Does the exam centre change which timetable we should be using?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge, yes. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after reading the wrong one. The zone follows the centre, not your home address, so ask the school's exams officer for the centre name and its zone in writing. Then build the revision calendar on that version and open the live timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: What should we plan for exam-week mornings if the centre is a long drive away?
faqs.answer: A dry run the week before, and a margin that assumes something goes wrong on the road. If the centre is in the Al Raha belt, on Yas Island or on the island, exam week means a peak-hour drive with no school bus to fall back on, often starting earlier than the usual run because candidates are seated well before the start. One rehearsal removes the variable that can end a paper before it begins, and it costs an hour of a weekend.

faqs.question: Which series do Al Falah candidates sit, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only and should never appear in an Abu Dhabi revision plan. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November. As a guide to the rhythm, Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Confirm every date against the board's own live timetable.

faqs.question: Is an online session really as useful as a tutor sitting at the kitchen table?
faqs.answer: For most IGCSE subjects it is equivalent, and the trade-offs are worth naming. A younger or distractible student is harder to supervise through a screen, and a tutor needs to see written working, which means a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper. Watching method as it forms is often more diagnostic than seeing a finished page. What online definitely buys from Al Falah is choice of specialist and sessions that are not lost to the evening peak, and the free trial is where you test whether the format suits your child.

faqs.question: What happens if we need to pause for a fortnight mid-term?
faqs.answer: You pause. Nothing renews automatically, and we would rather a household stopped for two weeks and resumed than paid for sessions a tired student attends. Pauses are common here around school assessment weeks, family travel and Ramadan. The practical advice is to take a short diagnostic session at the end of a long pause rather than resuming the plan blind, because a fortnight off changes what the next session should be spent on and it is cheaper to find that out deliberately.

faqs.question: How will I know the sessions are moving marks rather than confidence?
faqs.answer: By timed questions. A cold paper is sat at the start and every lost mark is classified as method, arithmetic, reading or unknown content. The same question types are repeated after the repair work, and at six sessions you receive a statement naming what has moved and the three topics still costing the most marks. If the match is wrong the tutor changes. We publish no satisfaction percentages or score-improvement figures, because we could not show you the sample size, date and method behind them.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach named Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE syllabuses rather than a general subject. Tell us the code on your child's exam entry and the tier, and the match is made against that rather than against a postcode.

intro.heading: Does anybody near Al Ghadeer teach your child's actual syllabus?
paragraphs: Al Ghadeer is on the far northern edge of the Abu Dhabi emirate, off the E11 near Al Samha, which means the pool of tutors willing to drive to the community is small and the pool who happen to teach a specific IGCSE syllabus within that group is smaller again. Most parents here discover this in the same order. They search for a home tutor, find two or three who answer, and only later realise that the person teaching their daughter Chemistry has taught the Pearson 4CH1 course and she is entered for Cambridge 0620. The content overlaps. The papers, the tiering and the practical assessment do not.

So the honest answer to the question in the search bar is: probably not, and that is the wrong thing to optimise for anyway. A tutor chosen because they live twenty minutes away is a tutor chosen on a criterion that has no relationship to your child's grade. The criterion that does matter is whether they can tell you, without looking it up, how many papers your child sits, what each is worth, which topics appear only on the Extended tier, and where candidates routinely throw marks away on the paper they are weakest at.

IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge International runs its own suite with four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0500 for First Language English. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4EA1, assessed differently and available in a modular pattern Cambridge does not offer. Several Abu Dhabi schools run a mixture, so siblings in the same household can sit different boards in the same subject. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE and nothing more specific has told you very little.

What IB Gram does about the scarcity problem is remove geography from the match. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with papers screen-shared and annotated during the session. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. That is a limitation stated plainly, and it is also the thing that lets a Al Ghadeer family book the person who actually teaches 0580 Extended rather than the person who lives closest to the E11 junction.

The sections below are built around verification rather than persuasion. There is a table of what coverage genuinely looks like by subject and level, including where it is thin. There is a board comparison so you can work out which course your child is on. There is the Core and Extended tier question, which quietly decides a grade ceiling. There is the Ministry of Education equivalency rule, where one ranking competitor publishes the wrong subject count. And there is a short list of questions that will tell you in five minutes whether a tutor knows the syllabus or the subject's reputation.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes touch a Al Ghadeer household running the British curriculum. The notes say what each one demands and where a tutor match goes wrong if the route is not identified first.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years of linear courses examined at the end, with four-digit syllabus codes and, in several subjects, a Core and an Extended tier. Candidates typically take between five and nine subjects. Assessment is by written paper, with practical or alternative-to-practical components in the sciences and an optional coursework route in some subjects.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in Al Ghadeer sit the June series, with November available as a resit route. The February/March series is offered to India only and should be ignored on any UAE page. Every centre belongs to one of six administrative zones and Cambridge warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so take dates from your child's exams officer rather than from a tutor.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international suite, with codes in the 4XX1 pattern. Maths is offered at Foundation and Higher tier, and several subjects can be sat in a modular pattern across sittings rather than entirely at the end. Grading uses the 9 to 1 scale in the international specifications a UAE school is most likely to have adopted.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live PDF is the only version to plan around.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage before IGCSE, assessed through Checkpoint tests that schools use for setting and for tier decisions. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Weak algebra or weak scientific writing at this stage becomes a tiering decision in Year 10 that a parent rarely gets to revisit.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest and most effective place for a Al Ghadeer family to intervene, and the stage most often skipped. A Year 9 student whose Checkpoint maths is weak will be put forward for the Core tier, and the Core tier has a grade ceiling. Fixing the algebra in Year 9 is a term of work; arguing about the tier in Year 11 fixes nothing.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Where most IGCSE students in this corridor go next, unless the school runs the IB Diploma. Subject choices at this stage depend on IGCSE grades and on whether Extended tier maths was taken, since the Core tier does not prepare a student for A Level Mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside the five IGCSE passes. That is the published rule, and it is why the IGCSE tier decision in Year 9 reaches further than most families realise.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask us to cover, named by syllabus code where the code changes what a tutor needs to know. Coverage is genuinely uneven across them and the following section says where.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The single most requested subject here. Extended tier adds functions, harder trigonometry, vectors and more demanding algebra, and Cambridge assesses it across two papers rather than one. Marks are lost on method not shown, on premature rounding, and on failing to read what the question asked for in the units given.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger candidates, often as preparation for A Level Mathematics. The calculus and the harder trigonometric identities are new content rather than extensions, so a tutor who teaches 0580 well is not automatically equipped for 0606. It is a scarce subject to staff in this emirate.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits are where most of the lost marks sit, followed by the practical paper or the alternative-to-practical. Students who can rearrange the formula but cannot explain which quantity is conserved stall in the longer questions. The two boards assess practical skills by different routes.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles calculations, electrolysis and organic reaction pathways account for most of the damage. Candidates memorise the series of steps and then cannot apply it to a compound they have not seen. The qualitative analysis section of the practical component needs separate, deliberate preparation.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The volume of content is the problem rather than its difficulty. Candidates who revise by rereading score well below those answering past questions against the command terms. Genetics and transport in plants are the two topics most often reported as unfinished when a student arrives for tuition.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 and 0990)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing cannot be revised by memorising content, which is why late starts hurt here more than anywhere. Students need timed practice at summary writing and at writing in a specified form and register. The 0990 variant is the 9 to 1 graded version of the same course.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0993)
subjects.description: A different course from First Language English and a different grade ceiling for university purposes. Many Al Ghadeer students are placed in it by default and would be better served by First Language. That placement decision is worth a conversation with the school in Year 9, not Year 11.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Both are won on command terms and diagram accuracy. A question asking a candidate to analyse and answered with a description is capped whatever the content knowledge. Business Studies rewards applying theory to the stimulus material in the paper rather than reciting the theory alone.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478) and ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Two very different subjects that parents routinely conflate. Computer Science requires algorithm design, trace tables and pseudocode precision; ICT is practical application work assessed at a keyboard. A tutor comfortable with one is often no use at all for the other.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508) and Arabic as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Abu Dhabi schools run Arabic for every pupil regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the stream a child is in determines the course. Federal rules require Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies in private schools, so this sits alongside the IGCSE programme rather than instead of part of it.

sections.heading: What coverage honestly looks like for a Al Ghadeer IGCSE student
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a coverage limit. Every provider implies that any subject at any level is available on request, and families find out otherwise in week three when the tutor who was going to teach Additional Mathematics turns out to be teaching from the 0580 scheme of work. We would rather state the position at enquiry, because a parent who has already spent an hour a day on the E11 deserves a straight answer about what exists.

The pattern is consistent. Mainstream subjects at mainstream tiers are easy to match quickly. Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English and Economics at Cambridge or Pearson are all well staffed, and a free trial can usually be arranged within days. The difficulty concentrates in three places: subjects that look mainstream but are not, such as Additional Mathematics 0606 and Computer Science 0478; first-language subjects other than English and Arabic; and any request that pairs a specific board with a specific practical component.

There is a second axis parents rarely think about, which is the tutor's experience of the right tier. A teacher who has taught Core-tier maths for five years can explain every topic a Core candidate needs and will be noticeably weaker on the Extended-only material, because they have not taught it recently. Asking for a specialist in a subject is not the same as asking for a specialist in the paper.

When we cannot cover something, the fallback is stated rather than hidden. For a genuinely niche combination, the match may come from our wider pool of IB and IGCSE specialists outside the UAE, taught in your child's own time zone over the same video platform. The table sets out where coverage is strong, where it is thin, and what the realistic wait is.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: establish which one before hiring anybody
paragraphs: This is the first thing to settle and the thing most often skipped. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award an international GCSE in the same subjects, with overlapping content and genuinely different assessment. A tutor prepared for one will teach a reasonable lesson on the other and will not know where that board's candidates lose marks, which is the part you are paying for.

The differences that matter are structural. Cambridge Mathematics runs a Core and an Extended tier with different papers and a different grade ceiling; Pearson runs Foundation and Higher. Pearson offers modular entry in several subjects, so a student can bank a unit in one series and complete in another; Cambridge assessment is linear. The sciences differ in how practical skills are assessed. Even the grading scale can differ between specifications a school has adopted.

Finding out takes one message to the school office or one look at the exam entry statement, which lists the syllabus code against each subject. Those codes are the most useful four characters in this whole process. Once you have them, a tutor conversation becomes short and decisive, because you can ask about Paper 4 of 0580 and hear immediately whether the answer is specific or general.

A UAE-specific wrinkle worth knowing: some Abu Dhabi schools enter different subjects with different boards in the same cohort. It is entirely normal for a student to sit Cambridge sciences and a Pearson maths, and for a sibling two years above to have sat the opposite. Do not assume the school has one board.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that sets a grade ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge Mathematics and several Cambridge sciences are tiered. The Core tier covers less content and its papers cannot award the top grades; the Extended tier covers more and can. Schools decide entries, usually in Year 10, on the basis of Year 9 attainment and classroom evidence. Parents are informed rather than consulted, and by the time a report makes the consequence clear the decision is often months old.

The practical effect is that a Year 11 student on the Core tier has a ceiling they cannot exceed no matter how well they are tutored, and that ceiling may close off A Level Mathematics and some university routes. Nobody is served by discovering this in the spring of Year 11. A family that asks in Year 9 which tier their child is heading for, and what would have to improve to change it, has a real decision in front of them.

Tuition pitched at the wrong tier is the other half of the problem. A tutor working through Extended-only topics with a Core candidate is spending your money on material that cannot appear on the paper. A tutor working Core material with an Extended candidate is leaving the hardest third of the course untouched. This is why we insist on confirming the tier from the school's own paperwork before the first paid session.

If the tier is right and the grade is still short, the gap is almost always in the same places: algebraic manipulation that is slow rather than wrong, method marks lost because working is not shown, and a failure to check that the answer answers the question in the units asked for. Those three are trainable within a term.

sections.heading: Five minutes of questions that tell you whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials are easy to assert and hard to check, so the fastest filter is subject-specific detail. A tutor who genuinely teaches a syllabus answers these without hesitating, because the answers are part of their working week. A tutor who teaches the subject's reputation will give you warm, general replies and will change the topic to experience and results.

Ask how many papers your child sits for this subject on this board, and what each is worth. Ask which topics appear only on the higher tier. Ask which question on the paper their students most often lose marks on, and why. Ask what the command terms are and how a describe question differs from an explain question in the mark scheme. Ask what the practical component requires and how they prepare a student for it.

Then ask three questions that are not about the subject at all. Can you show your MoHRE private tuition work permit? What will you do with my child's coursework draft, in your own words? And what happens if the match does not work after three sessions? The answers to those tell you about risk rather than knowledge, and risk is the part a parent has least visibility of.

Finally, notice what a good answer sounds like. It is specific, it includes a number, and it sometimes includes an admission. A tutor who says they are strong on the written papers and would want to check the practical requirements before promising anything is being more useful than one who says they cover everything.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what that tells you
paragraphs: Al Ghadeer sits in the Abu Dhabi emirate, so the schools a family here chooses on the Abu Dhabi side are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. That is the authority whose school listing a parent should check for curriculum, programmes and ratings, and it is named by essentially none of the tutoring pages competing for this search.

The distinction matters more here than in most communities, because Al Ghadeer families regularly consider schools across the border. A school a short drive north is regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. Two regulators, two inspection frameworks, two published rating systems. A parent comparing a Dubai rating with an Abu Dhabi rating is comparing two different measurements.

The wider map is worth knowing because families move. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

One thing a regulator does not do is endorse tutors. There is no such thing as an ADEK-approved or KHDA-approved private tutor, and any provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist. A business running a training institute with premises in Dubai needs a specific KHDA Educational Services Permit; IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or partnership of any kind.

sections.heading: The five IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education counts
paragraphs: Certificate equivalency is the step that converts a British-curriculum school leaving record into something a UAE institution recognises, and it has a published rule that is widely misreported. On the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student taking five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic Education does not have five that count. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five, and getting this wrong changes a subject-choice decision in Year 9.

For the American track the requirements are different: English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB there is no points threshold we can verify, so no figure appears on this page. Anybody publishing one without a Ministry source is guessing.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring company performs or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for it. The honest role of a tutor here is to make sure the subject choices made in Year 9 and Year 11 leave the five countable passes achievable, which is a planning conversation rather than a service.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE programme
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. That is a federal requirement: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For a Al Ghadeer family running a Cambridge or Pearson programme, these subjects sit alongside the IGCSE timetable and carry their own homework, assessment and reporting.

The organisational rules are more specific than most parents realise. In Dubai, KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

There is also a constraint on material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That shapes what tutoring in these subjects can honestly consist of: working with the school's own material and the Ministry curriculum rather than introducing an alternative scheme.

The reason it belongs on an IGCSE page is timetable arithmetic. A student carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies has a genuinely full week, and a parent adding three hours of private tuition on top needs to know what is being displaced. Almost no competing page in this market mentions these subjects at all, which makes their load invisible in every tutoring plan published for UAE families.

sections.heading: Coursework, feedback and the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a controlled assessment, and every one of them requires the work to be the student's own. A tutor can teach the skills the task assesses, explain the assessment criteria, read a draft the student has produced and say clearly where it falls short of the criteria. A tutor cannot supply text for submission, rewrite a draft into its final state, or produce the work for the student to hand in.

It is worth being blunt about why this appears on a page about finding a tutor. One provider visible in these search results sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. Boards treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, not on the seller. A family paying for help should be able to tell the difference between teaching and substitution, and the test is simple: at the end of the session, who did the writing?

The same boundary covers material. We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables. Those are the boards' copyright, your child's school has legitimate access to what they need, and a tutor working from the official specification and citing it is doing the job properly.

Ask any prospective tutor the coursework question directly and listen for a specific answer. A tutor who describes reading a draft and giving criterion-referenced feedback is describing the job. A tutor who offers to tidy it up or get it finished is describing something that can end a qualification.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes, not the subject names
process.description: Take the codes from your child's exam entry statement or ask the school office. Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1, Cambridge 0620: those four characters determine who can usefully teach the course. Add the tier where the subject is tiered. This single step removes most of the mismatch that happens in this market.

process.title: A diagnostic trial, free, before anything is agreed
process.description: A full session online at no cost with the tutor we think fits. Your child works a real question from the right board and tier while the tutor watches how they handle being stuck. You get a written note afterwards naming the error pattern and the first six weeks of work, whether or not you continue.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE home tutor near Al Ghadeer who teaches my child's exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: Honestly, the odds are poor. Al Ghadeer sits on the emirate border with no IGCSE school inside the community, so the pool of tutors willing to drive here is small, and the subset who teach a specific code such as Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher is smaller again. Choosing by driving distance means choosing on a criterion unrelated to your child's grade. We match by syllabus code over live video instead, which makes the specialist available regardless of where either of you lives.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to a villa in Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. Al Ghadeer students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with past papers screen-shared and annotated during the session. We state this before any payment because the pattern families complain about in this market is a home-tutor promise followed, quietly, by a video link.

faqs.question: How do I check whether my Al Ghadeer child sits Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Look at the exam entry statement from the school, which lists a syllabus code against each subject, or send one message to the school office. Cambridge codes are four digits such as 0580, 0625 and 0500. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes follow a 4XX1 pattern such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. Do not assume the school uses one board throughout: it is common in Abu Dhabi for a student to sit Cambridge sciences and a Pearson maths in the same year.

faqs.question: Does it really matter if a tutor knows the other board instead?
faqs.answer: It matters more than the content overlap suggests. The two boards differ in tiering, in whether modular entry is possible, in how practical science skills are assessed and sometimes in the grading scale a school's chosen specification uses. A tutor prepared for the other board will teach a competent lesson on the topic and will not know which question on this paper candidates consistently throw marks away on. That knowledge is most of what you are paying for.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Core and Extended tiers in Cambridge maths?
faqs.answer: Core covers the shared core of the syllabus and its papers cannot award the top grades. Extended covers the core plus the extended topics and the full grade range is available. The school decides entries, usually in Year 10, on Year 9 attainment and classroom evidence. The practical consequence is that a Core entry can close off A Level Mathematics, so a Year 9 conversation about what would change the tier is worth far more than a Year 11 appeal.

faqs.question: Can tutoring move my child from the Core tier to the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Tuition can change the evidence the school is looking at, which is what changes a tier decision, but only if it happens early enough. Once an entry has been made for a series, the tier is fixed for that sitting. The honest window is Year 9 into early Year 10, when a term of focused work on algebraic fluency and on showing method can shift a borderline judgement. By the spring of Year 11 the useful question is how to secure the best available grade within the tier entered.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this part of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606 is the most common disappointment, because its calculus content is new rather than an extension of 0580 and tutors who teach 0580 well are often not equipped for it. Computer Science 0478 is the next, since pseudocode and trace-table precision is a narrow skill that ICT experience does not provide. First languages other than English and Arabic are the hardest of all, and there we say plainly that we cannot cover it rather than offering an approximate match.

faqs.question: What if no UAE specialist is free for a Al Ghadeer IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: We tell you at enquiry rather than after payment. For a niche combination the fallback is a specialist from our wider IB and IGCSE pool outside the UAE, teaching over the same video platform in your child's own time zone, and we say so explicitly so you can decide. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit at all, which is why families keep discovering one in week three. A stated limit is more useful than an implied promise.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE candidates in Al Ghadeer actually sit their papers?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series is offered to India only, so disregard any page quoting it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For the exact timetable, take it from your child's exams officer: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the correct zone version must be used, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does a Al Ghadeer student need for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The exclusion is the part families miss: Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One page ranking for these searches tells UAE parents six subjects are needed. The published rule is five, and the difference changes a Year 9 subject choice.

faqs.question: Does my child's Al Ghadeer school report tell me which regulator inspects it?
faqs.answer: Not usually, but the emirate does. A school on the Abu Dhabi side is licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. A school across the border is overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead. The two publish different frameworks, so an Abu Dhabi rating and a Dubai rating are not directly comparable, and ADEK's own school listing is the place to check.

faqs.question: Are there such things as ADEK-approved or KHDA-approved private tutors?
faqs.answer: No. Regulators license and inspect schools, and in Dubai they permit training institutes with premises through a specific KHDA Educational Services Permit. There is no regulator approval scheme for individual private tutors, so a provider describing its tutors as regulator-approved is describing something that does not exist. What a tutor can and should hold is the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is free of charge for two years.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit a Al Ghadeer IGCSE week?
faqs.answer: They run alongside it. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of the international curriculum they are licensed for, so an IGCSE student carries those subjects as well. KHDA calculates mandatory subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes per lesson, and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in several of them. Count that load before adding three hours of private tuition to the week.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help finish my child's IGCSE coursework if we are short of time?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense the question usually means. A tutor teaches the skills the task assesses, explains the assessment criteria and gives feedback on a draft your child has written. Supplying text, rewriting a draft to completion or producing the work is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate rather than on whoever supplied it. The test of whether help is legitimate is simple: at the end of the session, who did the writing? It should always be the student.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IGCSE tutor in the first five minutes?
faqs.answer: Ask how many papers your child sits for this subject on this board and what each is worth. Ask which topics are higher-tier only. Ask which question their students most often lose marks on, and why. Ask what the practical component requires. Then ask to see the MoHRE private tuition permit and what they will do with a coursework draft. Specific answers with numbers in them are the signal; warm general answers that pivot to results are the warning.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.closingHeading: Send the syllabus code and we will tell you honestly what we can cover

Send us the syllabus codes from your child's exam entry, the tier where the subject is tiered, and what the last marked paper looked like. We will tell you plainly whether a specialist in that exact course is available, how quickly, and what the fallback is if not. If the match exists, the first lesson is free and runs online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time, with a written note afterwards naming the error pattern and the first six weeks of work. If it does not, you will hear that instead of a booking.

intro.heading: The content is the point, so start with the specification
paragraphs: Al Jubail Island households send their children across a bridge to school, most often to campuses on Saadiyat Island, Yas Island or along the Al Raha corridor, and those schools use different specifications for the same subject. A physics student at one campus sits Cambridge 0625; at another, Pearson Edexcel 4PH1. The content overlaps substantially and the assessment does not, and the difference is large enough to make a term of well-intentioned tutoring partly misdirected.

So this page spends its words on content rather than on logistics. Which code your child sits, what each paper asks, how many marks sit where, and the specific places a mark scheme refuses to pay for an answer a student believes is correct. These are not abstract details. The gap between a grade 6 and a grade 7 in an Abu Dhabi IGCSE cohort is usually ten or twelve marks spread across a dozen small, repeatable, diagnosable errors, and almost all of them have names. Naming them is the first useful thing a tutor can do, and it takes one marked script rather than a term of acquaintance.

A short example of what that means in practice. In Cambridge IGCSE maths, area scales with the square of a linear scale factor and volume with the cube. A student who applies the linear factor to an area question loses the whole question, not part of it. In physics, a question asking a student to describe how they would measure something is marked against a list of method points, and a student who explains the physics instead of describing the method earns almost nothing. In biology, describe and explain are different instructions with different mark schemes. None of these is difficult. All of them are invisible until somebody who knows the specification reads the student's own script.

On delivery, so it is clear before anything else: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From an address with a bridge in front of every school, that also solves a practical problem, because a tutor willing to cross twice on a weekday evening for one hour is a small group and rarely the group that contains your child's specification specialist.

The rest of the page goes subject by subject through the content and the traps, then sets out how eight weeks of past-paper work should actually be run. The last section deals with coursework honesty, which matters less in IGCSE than in the Diploma but still matters in the subjects that carry it. None of it requires a tutor to be within driving distance of a mangrove channel.

sections.heading: The specification codes an Abu Dhabi IGCSE student actually sits
paragraphs: Before any content work, establish which specification. The code is printed on the front of every past paper a school issues and held by the exams officer, and the number of families who have never looked at it is remarkable. Getting it wrong does not produce obviously bad tutoring; it produces plausible tutoring aimed slightly off target, which is much harder to detect and just as expensive.

Cambridge codes each subject individually. Mathematics is 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, with Additional Mathematics at 0606 where a school offers it alongside. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses its own system: Mathematics Specification A is 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1. Schools around Al Raha, Saadiyat and Yas use both systems, and a single school sometimes uses different boards for different subjects.

The table below sets the main subject pairs side by side. The practical use of it is to check your child's papers against it and then tell any prospective tutor the code rather than the subject. One more detail worth collecting at the same time: the tier. Cambridge Core caps the grade at C and Extended reaches A star; Pearson Foundation caps at 5 and Higher reaches 9. A tutor working from the wrong tier's content list wastes a Core or Foundation student's hours on material they will never be assessed on. Collect all of it in one email and keep the reply. Codes, tiers and the centre's zone are the three administrative facts that shape a two-year plan, and families who hold them in writing stop having the same conversation every term.

sections.heading: Where maths marks go, paper by paper
paragraphs: IGCSE maths mark loss is the most predictable in the whole subject set, which is why a tutor who knows the specification can produce a prioritised list from one marked script in about fifteen minutes. The errors are not evenly distributed; a handful of them account for most of the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 7.

Unshown working leads. On a multi-step question most of the marks are method marks, so a correct final answer with no visible route scores less than a wrong answer with a clear one. Students praised for mental arithmetic are hit hardest, and the habit takes about three sessions and one dissected paper to break. Scale factors come next: area scales with the square of a linear factor, volume with the cube, and a student applying the linear factor loses the entire question rather than part of it.

Then premature rounding, which turns a correct method into a wrong answer and is invisible to the student. Then rule selection in trigonometry, where the error is choosing between the sine and cosine rules rather than applying either badly. Then probability trees, drawn correctly and then multiplied along the wrong branch. Then non-calculator number work, which on the Cambridge route carries half the grade and is barely rehearsed in most school practice. The table sets each against where it appears and how long it takes to fix. What makes this list useful rather than depressing is that none of the six is a knowledge problem. Every one of them is a habit, and habits respond to short repeated correction far faster than content does.

sections.heading: Physics: the two topics that cost most, and the question nobody answers
paragraphs: In IGCSE physics, electricity and waves account for a disproportionate share of mark loss in Abu Dhabi cohorts, and the reasons are different for each. Electricity fails on circuit reasoning rather than on formulae: students can state that current is the same throughout a series circuit and then cannot predict what happens to the reading on an ammeter when a resistor changes. Waves fails on diagrams and on the precision of definitions, particularly refraction and the difference between the terms students use loosely.

The larger issue sits across the whole subject, in the practical-skills questions. A question that asks a student to describe how they would measure a quantity is marked against a list of method points: what you change, what you measure, what you keep constant, how you reduce uncertainty, how you repeat. A student who instead explains the underlying physics beautifully earns almost nothing, because they answered a different question. This is the single most trainable thing in IGCSE physics and most students have never had it explained.

The fix is specific rather than general. Take six past-paper method questions, mark them against the published scheme, and have the student rewrite each as a numbered list of method points. Three sessions of that changes a student's performance on a recurring question type worth several marks every paper. It also matters that practical experience cannot be fully replaced by a textbook, which is why a session should work from the school's own practical sheets where they exist rather than from generic descriptions.
