sections.heading: Chemistry: moles, equations and the tables students never learn
paragraphs: IGCSE chemistry divides neatly into content that is learned and content that is practised, and most students treat all of it as the first kind. The learned part is reactions, trends and definitions. The practised part is moles calculations, ionic and half equations, and the qualitative analysis tables, and it is the practised part that separates grades.

Moles work is the clearest case. A student who understands the concept can still lose marks consistently on units, on significant figures, on state symbols in equations, and on multi-step calculations where a mass has to become moles, then a ratio, then a volume. Each of those is a drill rather than an insight. Six short exercises across three sessions usually secures the ground, and the improvement shows on every calculation question for the rest of the course.

The qualitative analysis tables are the other neglected area. Tests for cations, anions and gases, with the expected observations, appear in the specification and in the papers, and students regularly arrive at the exam having never systematically learned them because they feel like memorisation rather than chemistry. They are worth marks every series. Learning them properly is a week of self-study with a tutor checking recall, which is an unglamorous and very efficient use of an hour. There is a simple test for whether the practised content has been practised. Ask the student to write the ionic equation for a precipitation reaction, with state symbols, from memory. If the symbols are missing, the drilling has not happened, whatever the last report said about understanding.

sections.heading: Biology and the humanities: command terms decide the grade
paragraphs: In biology, geography, history, business studies and economics, the single largest cause of mark loss in Abu Dhabi cohorts is not knowledge. It is answering a different question from the one asked, because the command term was read as a general invitation to write about the topic.

The terms are precise and the mark schemes are built on them. Describe asks what happens, in sequence, without reasons. Explain asks why, and a description earns nothing in an explain question however accurate it is. Compare requires both sides in the same sentence, not two paragraphs side by side. Evaluate requires a judgement with support, and a balanced list without a conclusion is marked down. Suggest invites an application of principle to an unfamiliar case. State wants a short answer and no elaboration, and students lose time writing paragraphs for one mark.

In the humanities a second habit compounds it: generality. Mark schemes in geography and history explicitly reward specificity, so an answer that correctly describes a process with no named place, figure, date or case study scores poorly against one that names three. Business and economics reward application to the given case rather than textbook definition. Five minutes of command-term work in every session, sustained for a term, moves these subjects more reliably than content revision does, because the content is usually already there. Build the drill into the session rather than setting it as homework. A student marking their own command-term answers tends to award themselves the mark for having known the content, which is precisely the error the exercise exists to correct.
bullets: Explain questions earn nothing for an accurate description
Compare needs both sides in the same sentence
Evaluate needs a judgement, not a balanced list
Geography and history mark schemes pay for named specifics
Business and economics pay for application to the given case

sections.heading: Eight weeks of past-paper work, done so it is worth something
paragraphs: Most past-paper work is wasted, and the waste is structural rather than a matter of effort. A student is given papers, does them in a tired hour, marks them generously or not at all, notes a score and moves on. Nothing is learned because nothing was diagnosed. Done properly, eight weeks of past-paper work from February of Year 11 is the single most effective block in the two-year course.

Four rules make the difference. The paper is sat under real timing, in one sitting, from the student's own specification, which means weekend mornings rather than a 7pm weeknight after a bridge crossing. It is marked against the published mark scheme rather than by impression, which usually produces a lower score and a far more useful one. The session is spent on dissection rather than on sitting, so the paper happens before the hour begins. And every error goes into a single running log, categorised as content, technique or timing, which is reviewed each week rather than simply written.

The log is what turns eight scattered papers into a programme. After three papers, patterns are visible: this student loses four to six marks a paper to unshown method, two to premature rounding, and has never finished the last question. Those are three fixable things, and fixing them is worth more than attempting five further papers. The table lays out how the eight weeks are usually structured. Keep the log in one document rather than in margins. Errors written on six separate papers are six pieces of paper; errors written in one place are a diagnosis, and that difference is most of the value of the whole programme.

sections.heading: Entries, the two series and what a resit involves
paragraphs: Content work needs a date to aim at, and the dates in this market are more often misunderstood than unknown. Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February exam window does not apply to a student sitting in Abu Dhabi, however often that advice circulates.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results from that series reach students in January, with the November 2025 results having reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on dates restated elsewhere.

Two administrative facts affect content planning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise; that is a question for the school's exams officer. And final entries, including the tier, are submitted by the school months before the papers, after which the tier is fixed. A content plan written in April for a tier that was settled in November is working inside constraints nobody explained.
bullets: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November; February and March is India-only
Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November

sections.heading: Coursework honesty in IGCSE, and why it still matters
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but the subjects that do carry it, and the schools that set substantial assignments, raise the same question about what help is legitimate. It is worth settling once rather than negotiating it under deadline pressure.

The principle is simple and it does not change by board. Work submitted for assessment has to be the student's own. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the task is asking for, discuss an approach, question an argument, point at a weak step, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may teach the writing skills the task requires and may help a student plan their own structure.

No tutor may write any part of the submission, supply text to be copied, restructure the student's work into their own prose, or produce results for the student to transcribe. There is an active market in this region selling completed assessed work, advertised at four-figure dirham prices for IB Internal Assessments, and the same operators sell at IGCSE level. Buying it risks the qualification, and the risk falls on the student rather than on the seller. Any provider should state its position on this in writing before a first session, and the ones who will not are answering the question. The conversation is also easier to have early than late. A student under deadline pressure at eleven at night is in a poor position to judge where a line sits, which is exactly why the line should have been drawn in September.
bullets: Submitted work must be the student's own, on every board
A tutor teaches content, explains the task and feeds back on the student's draft
Nothing is written, supplied, restructured or produced for the student
Ask any provider to state its honesty position in writing before paying

process.title: Find the code and the tier
process.description: Read the front of a past paper the school issued, or email the exams officer for the specification code and the tier for each subject. This takes one message and determines what every subsequent session should be aimed at. A tutor without it is working from an educated guess.

process.title: Send a marked script, not a report
process.description: One recent assessment or mock per subject, with the marking intact. Most IGCSE mark loss is visible on the page and invisible in a grade, and a specialist reading the script can produce a prioritised error list in about fifteen minutes.

process.title: Take the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: The trial is a working session with a named tutor whose taught specifications you know in advance. It opens with the script, tests a hypothesis about the error pattern, and ends with a written gap list in syllabus language naming papers and topics.

process.title: Work topic by topic against the specification
process.description: Each weekly session names the syllabus point it is covering and follows the school's teaching order rather than a generic one, with practice chosen against the named point. Worked solutions are saved so that spring revision reopens them.

process.title: Switch to the eight-week paper programme in February
process.description: Whole papers under timing on weekend mornings, marked against the published scheme, dissected in the session, with every error logged and categorised. Three papers in, the pattern is visible; fixing the pattern beats attempting more papers.

whyPoints.title: Taught by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: The request we take is Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 Higher, not chemistry. Codes carry different paper structures, calculator rules and mark schemes, and a tutor on the wrong one gives plausible teaching aimed slightly off target.

whyPoints.title: Named errors rather than general advice
whyPoints.description: Scale factors applied as linear ones, method questions answered with physics, moles calculations losing state symbols, explain questions answered with descriptions. Each has a name, a cost and a number of sessions attached.

whyPoints.title: Past papers run as a programme
whyPoints.description: Sat under timing, from the student's own board, marked against the published scheme, dissected in the session and logged by error category. Papers handed out as homework and marked by impression teach almost nothing.

whyPoints.title: No crossing in either direction
whyPoints.description: From an island with no school on it, a tutor matched by specification rather than by willingness to drive twice on a weekday evening is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

whyPoints.title: Content work tied to the right series
whyPoints.description: UAE candidates sit Cambridge June and November, not the India-only February and March series, and Pearson runs May/June and November. A content plan aimed at the wrong window is a plan aimed at the wrong month.

whyPoints.title: A written honesty position
whyPoints.description: Teaching, explanation, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing written, supplied or restructured. Completed assessed work is sold in this region and the risk of buying it falls entirely on the student.

faqs.question: How do I find which IGCSE specification codes my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Two routes, both quick. The code is printed on the front of every past paper the school issues, so a glance at a recent one answers it. Or email the exams officer and ask for the specification code and the tier for each subject, which is administrative information the school already holds. Collect the tier at the same time, because Cambridge Core caps the grade at C and Extended reaches A star, while Pearson Foundation caps at 5 and Higher reaches 9, and a tutor working from the wrong tier's content list wastes hours.

faqs.question: What are the Cambridge codes for the main IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, with Mathematics at 0580 and Additional Mathematics at 0606 where a school offers it. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents are 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, with Mathematics Specification A at 4MA1. Schools around Saadiyat, Yas and Al Raha use both systems and a single school sometimes uses different boards for different subjects, so check each subject rather than assuming one answer covers the whole timetable.

faqs.question: Will a tutor cross the bridge to Al Jubail Island for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Some Abu Dhabi providers will, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because that figure absorbs a round trip across the water. From this address the practical problem is also who will agree to it: the group of tutors prepared to cross twice on a weekday evening rarely contains your child's specification specialist.

faqs.question: Which maths errors cost Abu Dhabi IGCSE students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Unshown method leads by a distance, because most marks on a multi-step question are method marks and a correct answer with no visible route scores less than a wrong answer with a clear one. Then linear scale factors applied to area or volume questions, which loses a whole question rather than part of one. Then premature rounding, which turns correct method into a wrong answer. Then trigonometric rule selection, probability trees read along the wrong branch, and non-calculator arithmetic that is secure with a calculator and absent without.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on physics questions about measuring something?
faqs.answer: Because those questions are marked against method points rather than against understanding. The scheme pays for what you change, what you measure, what you keep constant, how uncertainty is reduced and how the measurement is repeated. A student who instead explains the underlying physics, however accurately, answers a different question and earns very little. It is the most trainable recurring question type in IGCSE physics. Taking six past method questions, marking them against the scheme and rewriting each as a numbered list of method points changes the pattern in about three sessions.

faqs.question: What should chemistry tutoring concentrate on at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: The practised content rather than the learned content. Moles calculations fail on units, significant figures, state symbols and multi-step conversions from mass to moles to volume, all of which are drills rather than insights and respond to six short exercises across three sessions. Ionic and half equations are the same kind of skill. And the qualitative analysis tables, tests for cations, anions and gases with their expected observations, appear in the papers every series and are very often never systematically learned, because they feel like memorisation rather than chemistry.

faqs.question: How much difference does command-term work actually make?
faqs.answer: In biology and the humanities it is frequently the largest single factor, because the content is usually already there. Describe asks what happens without reasons; explain asks why and earns nothing for an accurate description; compare needs both sides in the same sentence rather than two paragraphs; evaluate needs a judgement and marks down a balanced list with no conclusion; state wants a short answer. Five minutes of this in every session, sustained across a term, moves these subjects more reliably than further content revision does.

faqs.question: Why do geography and history answers score badly when they are not wrong?
faqs.answer: Because the mark schemes explicitly reward specificity and the answers are general. A response that correctly describes a process with no named place, figure, date or case study in it scores poorly against one that names three, even where the understanding behind both is identical. It is a habit rather than a knowledge problem, which is why it responds quickly: practise answering the same question twice, once as the student naturally would and once with three named specifics inserted, and the difference in the mark is usually self-evident.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used so they are actually worth doing?
faqs.answer: Four rules. Sit the paper under real timing, in one sitting, from your child's own specification, which in practice means a weekend morning rather than a tired weeknight hour. Mark it against the published mark scheme rather than by impression, which usually produces a lower and far more useful score. Spend the session on dissection, so the paper is done before the hour starts. And log every error as content, technique or timing in one running document that gets reviewed weekly rather than simply written and forgotten.

faqs.question: When should an eight-week paper programme start?
faqs.answer: February of Year 11, or immediately after mocks if those sit later. Before that point, topic repair and technique work give the better return because there is still time to change what the student knows. After it, the limiting factor is usually technique, pacing and question-type recognition rather than content. Three papers into a properly run programme the error pattern is visible, and fixing two or three named error types is worth more than attempting five further papers without a log.

faqs.question: Which exam series does an Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidate sit, and when do results arrive?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series with November as the alternate or resit route. The February and March series is offered to India only, so plans built around a February window do not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows how long the gap between paper and result can be on that route.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a school assignment that will be assessed?
faqs.answer: Within a clear boundary, yes. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the task is asking for, discuss an approach, question an argument, point at a weak step, teach the writing skills involved, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. What no tutor may do is write any part of the submission, supply text to be copied, restructure the student's work into their own prose, or produce results for the student to transcribe. Ask any provider to state that position in writing before you pay for anything.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics worth taking alongside 0580?
faqs.answer: It depends on the destination and on the teaching time available. Cambridge 0606 Additional Mathematics covers further calculus and trigonometry and is a genuine bridge towards A-Level Mathematics or IB Analysis and Approaches, which makes it valuable for a student heading that way. The common problem in Abu Dhabi is that schools fit it into very little curriculum time, so students sit a demanding paper with less teaching than it warrants. If your child is taking it, find out how many lessons a week it gets before deciding how much support it needs.

faqs.question: Which campuses do your IGCSE students around Al Jubail Island attend?
faqs.answer: Families on and around the island travel to campuses on Saadiyat Island and Yas Island and across to Al Raha and Khalifa City. The names that come up include Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, West Yas Academy, Al Yasmina Academy, Reach British School and Amity International School Abu Dhabi, which between them use both Cambridge and Pearson specifications. Those names describe the local education map only. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school listed, and none of them is a client.

faqs.question: How many marks separate a grade 6 from a grade 7 in practice?
faqs.answer: Typically ten or twelve marks across a whole paper, which is why the small repeatable errors matter so much more than families expect. Four to six marks a paper lost to unshown method, two to premature rounding, two or three to a command term answered as a description rather than an explanation, and a final question left unattempted because of pacing: that is the gap, and none of it is about understanding. Grade boundaries vary by series and are published by the boards, so treat any specific figure as indicative rather than fixed.

From there the work is specific: the syllabus point, the error pattern on the page, the technique behind each repeated mistake, and from February an eight-week paper programme run on weekend mornings with every error logged. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor and their taught specifications named before the trial.

intro.heading: The syllabus is the plan, and almost nobody reads it
paragraphs: Al Karamah is an inland district on the Abu Dhabi island, next to Al Mushrif, and its families use the schools a few minutes away in either direction. Most of its Year 10 and Year 11 students sit Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs across eight to ten subjects. When a parent here searches for a tutor, the trigger is nearly always a single report comment or a mock grade, and the request that follows is usually too general to act on: he needs help with science, she is struggling in maths.

The syllabus turns that into something workable. Every IGCSE subject publishes exactly what it assesses, how each paper is weighted, which command terms it uses and what each one demands. Read it and a vague worry becomes a list. A student is not bad at physics; they are losing marks on explain questions and on graph gradients, and they have never been taught the difference between describe and explain in an examination context. The same is true of calculate against show that, which signal different amounts of written working. That is three sessions of work, not a term of general science support.

The second thing the syllabus settles is which course your child is actually on. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 are different papers with different calculator rules and different tier names. Cambridge Physics 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 differ in how practical skills are assessed. Revision advice written for the wrong board is worse than none, and it is freely available on the internet, which is why so much of it ends up in a student's notes.

This page is therefore built around content rather than around claims. It sets out the codes, the command terms, the traps each subject reliably sets, how past papers should be used so that they diagnose rather than just occupy an evening, and how practical skills are examined for students who are taught online. The AED market rates and the regulatory position are here too, because a parent deciding where money goes should see both.

On delivery, the position is plain. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in Al Karamah; home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video, with the student's own papers and mark schemes on screen and working written live on a shared whiteboard. The in-home market here is real and well priced, and the comparison in this page is made with its published figures rather than against a straw man. If you read one section, read the one on command terms, because it is the cheapest set of marks available to any student in this district and almost nobody is taught it deliberately.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.programmesIntro: Three stages matter for an IGCSE household in this district, because what happens before and after the examined years shapes how they go.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which algebraic fluency and scientific vocabulary are either built or not. There is no external examination, so weaknesses are invisible until Year 10, when the pace doubles. Support at this stage is cheap and unglamorous: fractions, negative numbers, rearranging formulae and writing a full sentence in an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools near Al Karamah run Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests, which are sat in March, May and October and give a genuine external reference point before the IGCSE years begin. A weak Checkpoint result is useful information rather than a verdict, and it arrives early enough to act on without any pressure.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of taught content ending in terminal papers, tiered as Core and Extended with Cambridge or Foundation and Higher with Edexcel. Grades gate sixth-form options, so a weak Year 10 narrows Year 12 before anyone discusses it. The work that moves a grade is timed papers marked against the published scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Entries are made by the school as an exam centre, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, or the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where IGCSE grades are spent. Three or four linear subjects, or six Diploma subjects with the core. Students arriving from comfortable Extended grades are frequently surprised by the algebraic and analytical step up in the first term, and that gap is the usual reason a Year 12 asks for help in October.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Verify the current wording with the Ministry.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by its paper structure and the specific place marks go, because that is the level of detail at which a tutor is either useful or decorative.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended, Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge bars the calculator in one paper by design; Edexcel allows it in both. Marks go on method lines, rounding instructions and three-dimensional trigonometry sketches far more often than on misunderstood topics.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity produces the widest mark spread at this level. Graph gradients, unit conversions and explain questions that want a mechanism rather than a restatement are the other three reliable losses, and all four are teachable routines.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tests students memorise in the wrong direction. Many marks are lost by answering a describe question with an explanation and running out of time later in the paper.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three sciences and the strictest command-term discipline. Rereading notes produces an early plateau. Answering past questions and checking which verb the scheme rewarded is what moves the grade.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages, where marks depend on selecting evidence rather than summarising it. Students who write fluently and generally still lose heavily on the targeted-response questions that demand precision.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different course with different expectations, and Al Karamah households sometimes discover mid-year that their child is on it. Exercise-level accuracy and listening technique matter more than vocabulary breadth here.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams plus structured evaluation. The four-mark explain questions are where grades are made, and students lose them by writing a definition and stopping. Data-response discipline is a short, learnable skill.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Applying a concept to the case study in front of you rather than reciting it. Marks are allocated for application and judgement, and generic answers score about half. Past-paper case practice is the entire method.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Early calculus, functions and trigonometric identities for students heading to a linear maths course or Higher Level. Usually timetabled as a twilight option, which makes it the subject most likely to need outside support.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Theory papers that reward precise technical vocabulary, plus practical components where marks go on following the task specification exactly. Students who code confidently often write poor theory answers, which is a separate skill.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-karamah.regionsIntro: The districts around Al Karamah share its schools and its traffic, and the differences that matter are about when a session can start.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: Adjacent, same catchment, same mock timetables. A tutor working across both districts is planning against one school calendar rather than two, which makes revision timing easier to coordinate.

regions.name: Al Nahyan
regions.note: North-east, denser housing and a wider spread of curricula. Subject requests here are less concentrated, and a student may be the only one in their street sitting a particular board.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: West along the shore, a short run away. Several island cohorts sit here, so Extended science and maths requests from Al Bateen look much like those from Al Karamah.

regions.name: Al Zahiyah
regions.note: The older downtown grid near Abu Dhabi Mall. Apartments rather than villas, so a quiet, fixed online hour matters more than the length of the session.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Across the Khaleej Al Arabi towards the airport, with a term-time round trip of well over an hour. This is where an in-home travel premium stops making sense for a weekly arrangement.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Long bus routes along the Dubai road corridor. Students arrive home tired, so shorter, more frequent sessions work better than one long block.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: A mainland community with a wide curriculum mix and the longest journeys in the sample. Families here are the most sensitive to a travel premium that buys no additional teaching.

schoolClusters.note: The nearest schools cover both main boards between them, which is why two neighbouring students can be sitting different papers for the same subject. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; no affiliation is implied.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor in this district is usually being asked to fix
paragraphs: Across first sessions with students from the central island schools, the same five losses appear, and only one of them is a knowledge gap. The largest is the command term: answering an explain question with a description, or a suggest question with a definition. The second is working not shown, which forfeits method marks even when the final answer is right. The third is the instruction inside the question, meaning units, significant figures and exact form. The fourth is timing, with the last two questions rushed or blank. The fifth is a genuinely missing topic.

This ordering matters because it decides what to buy. Four of the five are technique, and technique responds quickly: a student who is taught to read the verb and show the working can gain marks within a fortnight without learning anything new. The fifth takes longer and is the only one that needs sustained subject teaching. A tutor who starts by teaching content rather than by reading a marked paper is likely to be working on the one in five rather than the four.

The table sets out the traps by subject, because they are not the same everywhere. Physics punishes gradients and unit handling; chemistry punishes the direction of a qualitative test; biology punishes the verb; business punishes generic answers that never touch the case study. A single session spent identifying which of these a particular student owns is worth more than a month of general support, and it is the first thing any match conversation here should establish.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: find the codes before you book anybody
paragraphs: Both boards are widely entered in Abu Dhabi, sometimes within one school and occasionally within one student's subject set. The codes are on the statement of entry the school issues and on the front cover of every past paper the department distributes. If neither is to hand the exams officer will confirm them in one email. This is a five-minute job that changes which tutor is right and which past papers are worth sitting.

The practical differences are specific rather than philosophical. In maths, Cambridge 0580 examines one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper, while Edexcel 4MA1 allows a calculator in both and splits the marks equally between two papers. Tier names differ: Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher. In the sciences, the arrangements for practical assessment differ, which matters a great deal for a student taught partly online. In English, Cambridge's first-language and second-language routes are different qualifications with different expectations.

Mixing boards across a subject set is allowed and reasonably common, and it creates one hazard worth naming: a student revising from a sibling's or a friend's resources may be sitting a different paper. We ask for the codes before matching a tutor, not as bureaucracy but because a specialist on the wrong board will teach the content well and miss the examination behaviour, which is where the marks are. The codes also decide which past papers are worth sitting, and sitting the wrong ones is a quiet way to lose a term of revision.

sections.heading: Command terms, and why they are the cheapest marks available
paragraphs: Every IGCSE paper is written in a controlled vocabulary, and each verb has a defined expectation. State wants a short fact with no reasoning. Describe wants what happens, in sequence, without why. Explain wants the mechanism and the because. Suggest wants a plausible application of principle to an unfamiliar situation, which means there is rarely one right answer. Compare wants both sides addressed in the same sentence structure. Calculate wants the working on the page.

Students lose marks on this constantly, and it is not a reading problem. Nobody has taught them the vocabulary as a vocabulary. A Year 11 can usually be shown the difference between describe and explain in twenty minutes, then needs four or five marked attempts before the habit holds. That is one and a half sessions to recover marks across every science paper and most of the humanities, which is the best return available anywhere in IGCSE tutoring.

The method is simple enough that a parent can support it at home. Take a past question, cover the answer, write a response, then read the published mark scheme and count where the marks actually sat. Students are surprised by how often the scheme awards a mark for something they thought was obvious and withholds one for the part they laboured over. Doing that ten times across a subject changes how a student reads every question afterwards, and it costs nothing beyond the papers the department already hands out every week.
bullets: State: a fact, no reasoning, no padding
Describe: what happens, in order, without the because
Explain: the mechanism, with the because made explicit
Suggest: principle applied to something unfamiliar, so several answers may score
Calculate: the working shown line by line, units carried through

sections.heading: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher: a Year 10 decision
paragraphs: Tiering is the highest-stakes administrative decision of the IGCSE years and it is often taken without the family in the room. Core and Foundation cap the top grade available; Extended and Higher reach the full range but include harder content and less generous mark schemes. The school decides, usually late in Year 10, based on assessment evidence. Changing it afterwards is possible until final entries close and awkward after that.

The useful test is not confidence, it is headroom. A student scoring near the top of Core assessments is limited by the route rather than by ability, and that cap may close a sixth-form door nobody has mentioned yet. A student who is reaching the bottom of the Extended range under exam conditions may be better served by a strong Core grade than a weak Extended one, particularly if the subject is not continuing. Both arguments are legitimate and they point in opposite directions.

Bring the last two assessment papers to the subject teacher and ask directly what the tier is costing or protecting. If a short block of tutoring is worth buying in Year 10, it is the one that answers this question rather than the one that follows the decision. We would rather sell three diagnostic sessions in October of Year 10 than twenty remedial ones in April of Year 11, and the sequencing matters more than the total. Ask the school when its entry deadline falls, because the answer sets how long the decision stays open.

sections.heading: Past papers done properly, not just done
paragraphs: Most students who say they have done past papers have read them. The difference between reading a paper and sitting one is most of the value. A paper sat under time, without notes, then marked against the published scheme by someone who applies it strictly, produces a list of specific losses. A paper worked through with the answers alongside produces a feeling of familiarity and no information at all.

The sequence that works is this. Sit the paper to time. Mark it hard, against the real scheme, giving nothing for intention. Record each loss by type, not by topic: method not shown, verb misread, unit wrong, timing, content missing. After three papers the pattern is obvious, and the pattern is what gets taught. A student who discovers that half their losses are timing will spend the next fortnight on pace rather than on content, which is the correct response and not the instinctive one. The instinctive response to a bad paper is to read more notes, and reading more notes is what produced the bad paper.

There is a copyright point worth stating. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to the boards, and we do not reproduce or distribute them. They are referenced and linked from their official sources, and your school's department supplies them routinely. Any provider offering a download library of board materials or unreleased content is doing something it should not, and that is worth noticing before you trust the rest of its advice.

sections.heading: Science practicals when teaching happens online
paragraphs: This is the honest question for any online science arrangement and it deserves a direct answer. Practical skills in IGCSE science are assessed through the school's own arrangements, which vary by board and route, and the school owns that entirely. An online tutor does not and cannot deliver the practical component. What an online tutor can do is prepare a student for how practical skills are examined on paper, which is where most of the marks for those skills actually sit.

That preparation is specific: reading a method and identifying the variable that was controlled, spotting why a result is anomalous, recognising which apparatus gives the stated precision, drawing a table with units in the headings, plotting a graph with sensible scales and a line of best fit, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data rather than to expectation. Those are paper skills, they are heavily weighted, and students practise them far less than they practise content.

The work is done with the student's own laboratory records and real past questions on screen. Where the school's scheme of work has left a technique untaught, we say so and suggest the parent raise it with the department rather than attempting to substitute for a laboratory. A tutoring platform that implies it can replace practical work is overselling, and a parent is better served by knowing exactly which part of the job sits with the school, and by hearing it before the first invoice rather than after it.
bullets: Practical assessment arrangements belong to the school and the board, not to a tutor
Most practical marks on paper go to method reading, data handling and graphs

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi market charges, and what a visit adds
paragraphs: Cheapest first, because that is the order a parent actually shops in. Budget online tuition, typically a university student, runs about AED 45 to 150 an hour: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That tier is honest homework supervision and it is useful for a Year 8. It is not a mark-scheme specialist, and buying it for a Year 11 four weeks before a paper is the most common waste of money in this market.

Above that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-branded tuition reaches AED 500 to 650, where BartyED quotes AED 650. An in-home one-to-one visit including travel is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

Set the two bands side by side and the in-home premium is the journey. It is small in Al Karamah, where the drive from most of the island is short, and large anywhere across the bridge. What it does not buy is a wider choice of teacher, which is the opposite of what a family needs when the subject is Additional Mathematics or second-language English. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; the lesson runs online, and the arithmetic above is the argument.

sections.heading: The series, the permit and the lines a tutor may not cross
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in June and November and offers the February/March series to India only, which is why Indian revision timetables found online are useless here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Provisional timetables are published well ahead and then revised, so take dates from the board's live timetable and confirm your school's Cambridge administrative zone with the exams officer, because each zone has its own version.

On who may teach, the UAE regulates private tutoring by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you.

On what a tutor may do, the boundary is the same in every subject. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody here writes a coursework piece, a controlled assessment or an investigation, and a provider offering to is not a cheaper alternative but a malpractice risk carried by the student. Abu Dhabi adds one more rule: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not privately tutor students enrolled at their own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK.

All four are teachable in two or three sessions, and they recover marks across every paper rather than in one topic.

Record each loss by type rather than by topic: method not shown, verb misread, unit wrong, timing, content missing. faqs.question: When are the IGCSE examinations for a candidate in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in those two windows and offers the February/March series to India only, so an Indian timetable found online does not apply. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. faqs.question: Can one child in Al Karamah sit Cambridge for maths and Edexcel for science?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is reasonably common in Abu Dhabi, sometimes within one school. The hazard is revision material: a student working from a sibling's or a friend's resources may be practising for a different paper in the same subject. Keep a written list of the code for every subject and check revision resources against it. It also means a single tutor for all sciences is less likely to be the right answer than one specialist per board and subject.

faqs.question: What does an online IGCSE tutor cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: The market sorts into bands. Budget online tuition runs about AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists reach AED 200 to 450 and above, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those are the providers' own published figures. IB Gram begins with a free trial lesson and confirms its rate in the match conversation.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutoring tier ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. A university student at the budget end is good value for a Year 8 who needs a homework habit, supervision and someone to explain fractions patiently. The mistake is buying that tier for a Year 11 six weeks from a paper, because the job then is strict marking against a published scheme and a ranked diagnosis, which is a different skill. Match the tier to the task and the cheap option is sometimes exactly right.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers and mark schemes to students?
faqs.answer: No. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright material, and we reference and link them from their official sources rather than hosting or distributing them. Your child's department supplies them routinely, and the official sites carry the current syllabus. A provider offering a download library of board materials, or anything unreleased, is doing something it should not, which is worth weighing before trusting its advice on anything else.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Tutoring privately without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat specific amounts quoted to you with caution.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry count for British-track equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. At least one page ranking for these searches states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify the current requirement with the Ministry of Education directly. IB Gram describes the process and does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a coursework or controlled assessment task?
faqs.answer: Only within the rules, and the rules are clear. A tutor can teach the technique, explain the published criteria, question the student's reasoning and give feedback on what the student has already written. A tutor cannot write, rewrite, restructure in their own words or edit a piece to completion. The school authenticates submitted work, so the consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate. Any provider offering to produce the work should end your search rather than win it.

faqs.question: How quickly can an Extended science tutor be arranged for Al Karamah?
faqs.answer: Mainstream Extended maths and sciences are usually matched within a few days in term time. Smaller options such as Additional Mathematics, second-language English and computer science are thinner, and demand across everything concentrates in the weeks before a series. Where the right specialist is not free, we say so and offer a later weekday hour, a single diagnostic session the student can act on alone, or a waiting list with a date, rather than filling the slot with a mismatch.

intro.heading: Which board is your child entered for? Start there
paragraphs: The single most common mistake in an IGCSE tutoring search from Abu Dhabi island is treating IGCSE as one qualification. It is not. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award international GCSEs, both are widely taught across the emirate, and their papers differ in structure, tiering and even in what the grades are called. A Cambridge 0580 Mathematics candidate at Extended tier sits Paper 2 and Paper 4, weighted 35 and 65 per cent. An Edexcel 4MA1 candidate at Higher tier sits two papers of two hours, weighted equally. A tutor who prepares one and assumes the other will teach competent mathematics and still leave your child unready for the paper in front of them.

So the first question to answer in Al Khalidiyah is not who is nearby. It is which board, which subjects and which tier. That information sits on your child's entry confirmation or can be had from the school office in one email. Bring it to the first conversation and the whole search becomes answerable: a tutor either prepares Cambridge 0620 Chemistry or they do not, and nobody has to guess. Schools in the emirate also mix boards across subjects more often than parents expect, so the answer is worth getting subject by subject rather than once.

The second question is what the tutoring is for. An IGCSE year is two years of content assessed in a short window, and students fail to convert knowledge into marks for reasons that are diagnosable rather than mysterious. They answer the wrong command term. They skip the working the mark scheme awards separately from the answer. They spend eleven minutes on a four-mark question. They revise by rereading notes, which produces familiarity and not recall. All four are fixable, and none of them requires a tutor to be physically present.

On that point, we are direct. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session is delivered one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which for past-paper work means both people see the same question at the same size and the annotated script survives the session. Published in-home rates across Abu Dhabi run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors, and the difference buys a journey rather than a lesson.

What follows is the information an Al Khalidiyah parent usually has to assemble from four different websites: the two boards compared by code and paper, what Core and Extended actually change, where marks go missing subject by subject, the MoE equivalency rule that decides whether these certificates count for a UAE university application, who is legally permitted to tutor in the emirate, and what the whole thing costs set against school fees and examination entry.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khalidi.programmesIntro: Al Khalidiyah students reach the IGCSE years by several routes, and the route changes what the tutoring has to do. A child who came up through Cambridge Lower Secondary arrives with the right habits; one who transferred in Year 9 from a different system usually has content gaps that only show up in the first Year 10 assessment.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The feeder stage, with optional Checkpoint tests in English, mathematics and science. Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, and they are diagnostic rather than certificating. Support at this stage targets the algebra, scientific method and extended writing that the IGCSE years will assume without re-teaching.
programmes.countryNote: A weak Checkpoint result from a Year 9 student in Al Khalidiyah is the cheapest warning a family will ever get. Acting on it in Year 9 costs a term of light support; ignoring it until the Year 11 mock costs a tier decision.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Examined on a 9 to 1 grade scale with Core and Extended tiers available in many subjects. Core caps the achievable grade, usually at a 5 or a C equivalent; Extended opens the full range. Candidates typically take between six and ten subjects, and the tier decision is made by the school, often in Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge's own guidance states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered as Foundation and Higher in mathematics and the sciences, graded 9 to 1, with some subjects available in a modular structure. Mathematics A, code 4MA1, is examined through two papers of two hours each, weighted equally, which changes revision planning compared with a 35-65 split.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel International GCSE series run in May/June and November. As a worked example of the tail between sitting and results: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual continuation for an Abu Dhabi IGCSE student who is not moving into the IB Diploma. Subject choices here are constrained by IGCSE tier and grade, which is why the Year 10 tier conversation has consequences two years later rather than only at the end of Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade of no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-khalidi.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Khalidiyah families ask about most, written with the syllabus code where it matters. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole researched Abu Dhabi competitor cluster, which is why asking a tutor for a code is such an effective filter.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: 0580 Extended is Paper 2 at 35 per cent and Paper 4 at 65; 4MA1 Higher is two equally weighted two-hour papers. Marks are lost on unsimplified surds, on bearings and loci, and on multi-step problems where method marks are available but no working is shown.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
subjects.description: A graphics-calculator course with an investigation paper, often taught where a school feeds into the IB Diploma. Students coming from 0580 find the calculator work easy and the investigation unfamiliar, because it rewards exploration and clear reasoning rather than a single final answer.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the most lost marks, usually through confusion between series and parallel reasoning and through formula recall without unit discipline. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards knowing how an experiment is set up, which cannot be learned from theory notes alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tests are the predictable weak points. Students who can recite a definition still drop marks because they do not state the observation and the inference separately when a question asks for both.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The content volume disguises the real demand, which is applying a named process to an unfamiliar context. Transport in plants, genetics crosses and enzyme graph interpretation are where marks concentrate, and command-term precision decides whether a described answer scores.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing and, for 0511, an assessed speaking component. Marks are lost on summary tasks that lift whole sentences from the passage instead of condensing, and on writing tasks that ignore the stated audience and purpose.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Two papers covering reading comprehension, directed writing and composition. The reading paper rewards analysis of how a writer achieves an effect; weaker answers narrate what happens. The composition paper is lost on structure far more often than on vocabulary.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a heavy application demand. A defined term earns one mark; applying it to the business in the stem earns the rest. Evaluation questions are where grades separate, and most candidates write a conclusion that restates rather than one that weighs.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Maths
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 candidates, often as preparation for A Level or the IB Diploma. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive earlier than most students expect, and the gap between an IGCSE Extended grade 8 and comfort in this course is real rather than a formality.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: 0478 demands pseudocode and trace tables under timed conditions, which is where candidates who can code lose marks for not following the required notation. 0417 is practical and assessed on documents produced to a specification, so accuracy against the brief matters more than flair.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel? The comparison nobody hands Al Khalidiyah parents
paragraphs: Both boards are legitimate, both are accepted by universities, and neither is harder in any general sense. What differs is the architecture of the examination, and that is what a tutor has to know. In Cambridge Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier, Paper 2 is a short-answer paper carrying 35 per cent and Paper 4 is a longer structured paper carrying 65. In Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A, code 4MA1, the Higher tier is two papers of two hours weighted equally. Those two structures demand different revision shapes. A 65 per cent paper rewards stamina across multi-step questions; two equal papers reward even coverage.

Tier naming differs too, and the difference is not cosmetic. Cambridge uses Core and Extended; Edexcel uses Foundation and Higher. In both cases the lower tier caps the grade a candidate can achieve. A student entered for Core who needs a grade 7 cannot get there from that paper, no matter how well they perform, and the entry decision is made months before the examination. This is the single most consequential thing a parent can check early, and it is on the entry confirmation.

Science is where the board question bites hardest. Cambridge 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology each have an alternative-to-practical option, and the questions there assume familiarity with how apparatus is actually arranged. Edexcel 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 distribute practical understanding differently across their papers. A tutor preparing a student for the wrong one will cover the science and miss the assessment, and the gap shows up on the day.

Ask the school which board, which syllabus code and which tier, for every subject. Schools sometimes mix boards across subjects, so the answer is not necessarily uniform. Then ask any prospective tutor to name the papers and weightings for that code without looking them up. The response tells you more than any list of qualifications.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: Tiering is the part of IGCSE that most surprises families who arrived from a system without it. In many Cambridge subjects a candidate is entered for either Core or Extended, and the Core paper simply does not contain the questions that generate the top grades. The ceiling is structural. A student can answer every question correctly on a Core paper and still not reach the grades that an Extended entry makes available. The equivalent decision at Edexcel is Foundation against Higher.

Schools make this call for defensible reasons. Entering a struggling student for Extended can produce a worse outcome than a secure result at Core, because the Extended paper's harder questions can consume time and confidence. The decision is usually taken in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments. The problem arises when the evidence is thin, when a student was ill during the assessment that decided it, or when a content gap from Year 9 was mistaken for a capability limit.

That is a diagnosable situation rather than an argument to have. Set the student questions from both tiers, mark them against the published scheme, and look at what the scripts actually show. A student who handles Extended-style algebra but falls apart on the longer structured questions has a stamina and technique problem, which is fixable in a term. A student who cannot access the Extended material at all is correctly placed, and pushing them is unkind rather than ambitious.

The decision matters beyond Year 11. A Core or Foundation grade constrains which A Level or IB Diploma subjects are realistically open, and that constraint is invisible when the entry is made. For families in Al Khalidiyah planning towards a UAE or overseas university, the honest sequence is to settle the tier question with evidence in Year 10 rather than discover its consequences in Year 12.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: Parents usually describe the problem as a grade. Tutors need it as a location. An IGCSE grade is the sum of specific marks lost in specific places, and almost all of those places are recurrent across cohorts. Naming them is the difference between useful tutoring and general revision.

In mathematics, the losses cluster in four areas: working not shown on multi-step problems where method marks exist independently of the answer, premature rounding that destroys accuracy marks later in a chain, bearings and loci questions that require construction rather than calculation, and the algebraic manipulation of fractions and surds that was introduced in Year 9 and never consolidated. None of these is about ability. All four are fixable in a defined number of sessions.

In the sciences, the pattern is command-term failure and observation-versus-inference confusion. A question asking for an observation wants what you see; a question asking for an explanation wants the reason. Candidates routinely supply one when asked for the other and score nothing for an answer that contains correct science. In chemistry, moles calculations and ionic equations carry disproportionate mark weight. In physics, electricity circuits and the waves topic do the same. In biology, it is genetics crosses and graph interpretation.

In English and the humanities, the recurring loss is answering a different question from the one asked. A Paper 1 reading question asking how a writer creates an effect is not asking what happened. A business or economics evaluation question is not asking for a summary. Students who narrate instead of analysing can be strong writers and still sit in the middle of the grade range for two years, which is why the first useful tutoring session is usually spent on a marked script rather than on new content.
bullets: Maths: method not shown where method marks are awarded separately

sections.heading: Who is legally permitted to tutor your child in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a surprising number of tutoring websites either ignore this or imply the opposite. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent in Al Khalidiyah. First, a tutor who has never heard of the permit is worth a careful second look, because it suggests they are working outside a framework that exists specifically to protect families. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so be sceptical of any figure quoted to you, including figures that circulate in parent groups.

Second, the permit is free. If anyone asks you to cover the cost of their licensing, the request has no basis. What the permit does not do is certify teaching quality or subject knowledge: it is a right-to-work instrument, not an accreditation. A permitted tutor can still be the wrong tutor for Cambridge 0580 Extended, which is why the syllabus-code question remains the more useful filter.

A separate point applies specifically to Abu Dhabi. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, but do not go looking for your child's own class teacher as a private tutor. Also distinguish an individual tutor from an operation with premises: a training institute in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to a physical centre and which IB Gram does not hold or claim.

sections.heading: What IGCSE certificates must show for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: This is the question that eventually matters to every Al Khalidiyah family considering a UAE university, and it is absent from almost every tutoring page in the Abu Dhabi search results. Equivalency is the Ministry of Education's recognition of a foreign secondary certificate, and the British-track requirements have been publicly clarified. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student who takes five subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, has three that count. One competitor page ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not the published rule. Publishing the correct five-subject rule is a small thing that beats a ranking page on accuracy.

For the American track, the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published in that source, and no figure should be taken from a tutoring website. Verify any IB equivalency requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates. And tutoring is not a requirement for it. Any page implying that private lessons are needed to secure equivalency is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.

sections.heading: The Al Khalidiyah school run and when a session realistically fits
paragraphs: A tutoring slot that ignores the shape of the day gets cancelled. Abu Dhabi island school days generally end in the early to middle afternoon, and the gap between the final bell and a workable study hour is filled by the journey, a meal and whatever homework the school has set. For an Al Khalidiyah family whose child attends a school on the island, the realistic window opens around five. For a family whose child travels out to Khalifa City, Saadiyat or the mainland corridor, it opens later, because the bus or the car takes a substantial bite out of the afternoon.

This is where an online slot has an unglamorous but decisive advantage. A fixed video session at seven in the evening does not depend on anyone crossing the island, so it does not move when Corniche Road is slow or when a tutor's earlier visit overran. Families who have tried both formats describe the same pattern: the in-home arrangement worked until the third or fourth cancellation, at which point the week lost its rhythm and the tutoring stopped being useful before it stopped being paid for.

The second consideration is which hour the student is actually able to think in. A Year 11 student who gets home at four thirty and starts at five is often still in school mode and tired; the same student at seven, after a break and a meal, is noticeably sharper. Parents sometimes choose the earlier slot because it feels more disciplined. The script quality after each session is the better guide, and it usually argues for later.

Weekends deserve a deliberate choice rather than a default. A Saturday morning session suits a student carrying a heavy weekday timetable, and it is the only slot that reliably survives an examination term. The trade is that it occupies family time, so it works when the family decides it works, not when a tutor's diary prefers it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs, set against school fees and exam entry
paragraphs: Tutoring is usually discussed in isolation, which makes the number feel arbitrary. Placed next to the other costs of an IGCSE year, it becomes a decision rather than a shock. Private school fees across the UAE are the dominant line; for context on the direction of travel, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Abu Dhabi fee regulation sits with ADEK and operates separately.

Against that, the market figures for tutoring are modest per hour and significant per year. Published rates put budget online tutoring from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, including travel, are quoted at AED 180 to 500.

Monthly, the shape is clearer. Online packages have been advertised at around AED 799 a month for eight sessions; in-home monthly packages of four two-hour sessions at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. All of those are other providers' published figures, cited as the market. They are not an IB Gram price list, and the honest route to our own numbers is the free trial and a conversation.

The useful comparison for an Al Khalidiyah parent is not tutoring against zero. It is one well-matched session a week for a defined block against two badly matched sessions a week for a year, which is the pattern that quietly costs families the most. A diagnosed eight-week block that fixes a named gap is cheaper and more effective than open-ended support nobody reviews.

sections.heading: Vetting an IGCSE tutor in five questions you can ask by message
paragraphs: Most Al Khalidiyah families meet a prospective tutor through a neighbour, a parent group or a listing, and have to form a judgement from a short exchange. Qualifications are easy to state and hard to verify from a message. Assessment knowledge is close to impossible to fake, because a tutor who has prepared candidates for a specific syllabus carries its structure the way a driver carries a familiar route.

Ask for the syllabus code they prepare, and then for the papers and weightings under it. A genuine Cambridge 0580 Extended tutor will say Paper 2 at 35 per cent and Paper 4 at 65 without pausing. A 4MA1 tutor will say two papers of two hours, equally weighted. Someone who answers "IGCSE maths, all boards" is telling you they treat them as interchangeable, which is the mistake this whole page exists to prevent.

Ask what they will do in the first session. The right answer involves a diagnostic: a past-paper question set or a marked script, so the teaching starts from evidence rather than from an assumption about where the gap is. An answer that begins with a curriculum plan for the term is a tutor who has decided what your child needs before meeting them.

Ask how progress will be visible to you, and ask about the permit. The private tuition work permit is free and valid for two years, and a tutor should be able to answer plainly. Finally, ask what they will not do. For an IGCSE candidate there is no Internal Assessment to ghostwrite, but there is coursework in some subjects and there are practical write-ups, and the correct answer names the boundary without being prompted.

What will the first session consist of, and what will it diagnose?
