process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Not "IGCSE maths" but "Cambridge 0580, Extended, Year 11, needs Monday or Wednesday evening". That information is on the entry confirmation or available from the school office in one email, and it is what makes the request answerable rather than approximate.

process.title: We confirm the match or say no
process.description: If a tutor who prepares that code is free at that hour, we say so. If one will be free shortly, we give a date. If we cannot staff it properly, we say that instead of offering someone adjacent. Declining costs you nothing; a wrong match costs a term of Year 11.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a diagnostic
process.description: One session at no cost, with no card required, built around a past-paper question set rather than a chat. You get a short written read on where the marks are going, and a basis for deciding whether to continue. If the fit is wrong, we rematch rather than persuade.

process.title: Fix the slot, agree the measure
process.description: A standing weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, plus one thing we will both look at in eight weeks, usually a timed paper marked to the published scheme. The measure is agreed before teaching starts, so neither side has to rely on an impression later.

process.title: Review at eight weeks and decide
process.description: Continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. Finishing is a real option and we will say when the work is done. An IGCSE year has a natural end point, and tutoring that outlives the problem is a habit rather than a plan.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code
whyPoints.description: An Al Khalidiyah request is matched to a tutor who prepares that exact board, code and tier. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are different examinations, and treating them as one is the most common quality failure in this market.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice that is not a sales pitch
whyPoints.description: If the evidence says Core is the right entry, we say so, even though an Extended plan would mean more sessions. The entry decision belongs to the school, and our contribution is marked scripts from both tiers rather than an opinion.

whyPoints.title: The regulatory position stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit, its two-year validity and its zero cost are set out on this page with the source named. IB Gram claims no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds none.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, said before you pay
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India. That is on the page rather than in a conversation after a deposit, because a family should know what they are buying.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is another provider's published rate, named and framed as the market. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and two quote in a currency UAE families do not transact in.

whyPoints.title: Equivalency explained, never promised
whyPoints.description: The five-subject MoE rule and the Arabic and Islamic education exclusion are set out with the source. Equivalency is a Ministry process; we describe it and point you to the official channel rather than implying tutoring is needed to secure it.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: It is on the examination entry confirmation the school issues, and the school office can confirm it by email in a sentence. Ask for the syllabus code as well as the board, because the code is what identifies the paper: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580 or 0607, Edexcel Mathematics A is 4MA1. Schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects, so ask subject by subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything. Any tutor worth hiring will want this before the first session anyway.

faqs.question: Does a tutor who knows Cambridge 0580 automatically handle Edexcel 4MA1?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the honest ones say so. The mathematics overlaps heavily, but the examinations do not. Cambridge 0580 Extended is a 35 per cent short-answer paper plus a 65 per cent structured paper; Edexcel 4MA1 Higher is two two-hour papers weighted equally. Question styles, mark-scheme conventions and the balance of topics differ. Many experienced tutors prepare both and can say exactly how they differ. A tutor who treats them as the same qualification will teach good maths and still leave gaps in examination readiness.

faqs.question: My son is entered for Core and wants a grade 7. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: Not from a Core paper. The Core tier caps the achievable grade, usually around the middle of the scale, and that is a structural feature of the examination rather than a reflection of how well he performs on the day. If a grade 7 is genuinely needed, the entry tier has to change, and that decision belongs to the school and has a deadline. The useful first step is evidence: questions from both tiers, marked against the published scheme, so the conversation with the school rests on scripts rather than hope.

faqs.question: Can anyone visit us in Al Khalidiyah for the lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session for an Al Khalidiyah family runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. The reason is not cost-cutting on our side, it is match quality on yours: dropping the travel requirement means your child works with a tutor who prepares their exact syllabus code rather than whoever is free and within driving range on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does a UAE student need for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. A ranking competitor page states that six subjects are required, which does not match the published clarification. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process; verify your own case through the official channel rather than through any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE sitting in February or March that we could use as a resit?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A resit after a summer sitting therefore points at November rather than at the following spring. Several tutoring pages aimed at UAE parents get this wrong, which matters because an entry deadline is something a family acts on. Check the live official timetable on the board's own site before planning anything around a date.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge zone timetable warning actually mean for us?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge's own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. In practice your school manages this, but if you are planning revision from a timetable you downloaded yourself, confirm with the examinations officer that it is the right zone. It is a five-minute check against a real risk.

faqs.question: My daughter revises for hours and her grades do not move. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually the revision method rather than the hours. Rereading notes produces a strong feeling of familiarity and very little recall, which is why students who work hard can plateau for a year. The alternative is retrieval under conditions: a past-paper question answered from memory, marked against the published scheme, with the specific lost marks logged and re-tested a fortnight later. It feels worse and works better. The first session with a new tutor should produce a marked script, not a plan.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE tutoring permit mean a tutor is any good?
faqs.answer: No, and it is important not to confuse the two. The private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is a right-to-work instrument granted free of charge for two years. It says the person may lawfully offer private lessons in the UAE. It says nothing about whether they can prepare a candidate for Cambridge 0620 Chemistry. Treat the permit as a floor, not a recommendation, and keep the syllabus-code question as your real filter on competence.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject gives Abu Dhabi students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Across enquiries from the island, mathematics and the sciences dominate, with chemistry producing the sharpest drop between classwork and examination performance. The usual cause is that moles calculations and ionic equations carry mark weight out of proportion to the teaching time they receive, so a gap there costs more than it looks. In physics it is electricity and waves. In English it is answering a different question from the one asked, which is a technique problem disguised as a writing problem.

faqs.question: What time of day actually works for a Year 11 student living on the island?
faqs.answer: Later than most parents expect. A student who gets home at half past four and starts at five is often still in school mode and tired, and the session quality shows it. The same student at seven, after a break and food, produces noticeably better scripts. Families whose children travel out to Khalifa City or the mainland corridor usually find half past seven is the earliest realistic slot. A weekend morning is the one time that reliably survives an examination term.

faqs.question: Can we book a short block rather than commit to the whole year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a well-defined problem it is the better buy. Eight weeks of one session a week is eight to twelve hours of teaching, which is enough to close a named content gap and rebuild examination technique in a subject the student broadly knows. It is not enough to cover two years of untaught content. We would sit a timed paper at the start so the block targets what the script shows, agree a finish date, and review at the end rather than letting it drift onward.

faqs.question: Is online teaching workable for a practical subject like physics or chemistry?
faqs.answer: For the written papers, yes, including the alternative-to-practical questions, which test understanding of apparatus and method rather than manual skill. A shared screen is well suited to working through a circuit diagram or a titration calculation line by line. What online tuition cannot replace is time in the school laboratory, and it should not try. The school runs the practical programme; a tutor's job is to make sure your child can describe, explain and evaluate what happened there in the terms the mark scheme rewards.

faqs.question: Should we switch tutors if nothing has changed after two months?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but diagnose before you switch. If the eight-week measure has not moved, either the plan was aimed at the wrong gap or the match is wrong, and those have different fixes. A tutor who can show you a marked script from week one and week eight, plus an error log, makes the diagnosis straightforward. A tutor who cannot produce either has given you no way to tell. We treat a stalled plan as our problem to solve, including by rematching, rather than as something to explain away.

intro.heading: The Al Manaseer week, and where an IGCSE session actually fits in it
paragraphs: Al Manaseer occupies the western half of Abu Dhabi island, tucked between Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen with the Corniche a few streets north and Al Bateen Executive Airport to the south-west. It is apartment territory: tall blocks, families who have lived here a long time, and a road network that behaves very differently at eight in the morning than at half past three in the afternoon. That second fact is the one that decides whether a tutoring arrangement lasts.

The school map from here spreads in three directions. A short run west and south into Al Bateen and Al Ras Al Akhdar. A medium run east into Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan. And for a sizeable minority, a long run across the island or off it entirely, to Bloom Gardens, Al Reem Island or the Al Raha corridor. The same household often does two of these in one afternoon, because siblings rarely attend the same campus in this part of the city. Working out which of those three runs your household actually does, and how often, is the first useful piece of planning available to you.

Put numbers on it. British-curriculum secondary schools in Abu Dhabi finish between roughly 2.50pm and 3.30pm. Pick-up queues add fifteen to twenty-five minutes before a car moves. From Al Bateen the drive back is eight to fifteen minutes; from Al Mushrif, fifteen to twenty-five; from Bloom Gardens or Al Reem Island, twenty-five to thirty-five at that hour. A Year 11 student is through the door somewhere between 3.45pm and 4.45pm, needs food, and is not usefully thinking about a mark scheme before half past five. None of these figures is surprising to anyone who drives them. They are simply rarely written down before a weekly slot is agreed with a tutor.

So the 4pm slot is fictional and the 5pm one is fragile. The first dependable weekday window for an Al Manaseer IGCSE student is 6pm, and the long-run households should plan for 6.30pm or 7pm. An in-home arrangement has to cross the same city at the same hour, which is why market rates for in-home one-to-one visits in the UAE sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel folded in, against AED 150 to 300 for comparable teaching delivered online.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Visits to a family's address are something we offer only in India. For an Al Manaseer family every IGCSE lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is why a 6.30pm Wednesday slot can be held in September and still be running in April. Nothing cascades when a pick-up is late, nothing is cancelled because a tutor is stuck on Khalifa Bin Zayed Street, and the slot can be late enough to be real.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which subject sets and, with them, IGCSE tiers are effectively decided. School days are slightly shorter and the homework load is lighter, so this is the one stage at which a 5pm session is comfortable from most of Al Manaseer. It is also the cheapest point at which a maths or science gap can be closed.
programmes.countryNote: Families arriving in Abu Dhabi often move a child into the Al Bateen or Al Mushrif clusters part way through this stage, and a transfer between curricula here routinely produces a notation and method gap that looks like weakness. Three or four sessions usually settles what two years of quiet struggle otherwise would not.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Eight or nine subjects, a tier per subject, and terminal papers in June or November. Cambridge codes each subject individually, 0580 in maths and 0625 in physics among them, while Pearson uses its own, such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. The homework load jumps sharply in Year 10, which is exactly when a weekday session gets harder to place.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres sit the June and November Cambridge series, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam when the wrong zone timetable was used. Worth confirming with the school's exams officer rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Sixth form, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Three or four A-Levels, chosen on IGCSE grades. Entry requirements commonly sit at grade 6 or B in the subject, and at grade 7 or A for maths and the sciences. School days often end later and independent study replaces some lessons, which changes the shape of the week again.
programmes.countryNote: Al Manaseer students staying on the western island have sixth-form options close to home, while those moving to IB campuses typically travel to Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island or Al Raha. Either way the IGCSE grades achieved in Year 11 are the constraint, which is what makes Year 10 the right year to intervene.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-manasee.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Manaseer families ask about most, with a note on whether each realistically suits a weekday evening slot or belongs on a weekend morning.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1
subjects.description: Cambridge sets a non-calculator and a calculator paper per tier; Edexcel permits a calculator on both. Topic teaching sits well in a weeknight hour; whole papers do not. Non-calculator fluency is the most recoverable thing in the subject and the least practised in school.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1
subjects.description: Electricity and waves account for most mark loss, and the practical-skills questions assume laboratory experience. Describing a method precisely enough to earn the mark is a trainable skill and suits a focused weeknight session.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are where grades are made. Students who can recite reactions still lose marks on units and significant figures, which is an hour's work rather than a term's.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610 and Edexcel 4BI1
subjects.description: The highest-content science and the one most vulnerable to vague answers. Command-term discipline, describe against explain, decides more marks than recall does. Good value in short, frequent sessions rather than long ones.

subjects.name: English Language and English as a Second Language
subjects.levels: First language and second language routes
subjects.description: Two genuinely different qualifications, and Abu Dhabi families are sometimes unsure which their child sits. Both reward structural discipline in writing over vocabulary display. Benefits from a weekend slot when extended writing is involved.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Set texts, quotation accuracy and the ability to build an argument rather than retell a plot. The limiting factor is usually essay structure under timing, which means a longer weekend session once a term beats a short weeknight one.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study application and the command terms that separate an analyse from an evaluate. Students lose marks writing textbook definitions where the question asked for a judgement applied to the given business.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source skills, case-study specificity and the mark-scheme structures that reward naming a real example. The commonest loss is a generally correct answer with nothing specific in it, which is fixable with a handful of targeted sessions.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the written theory paper, where precision of terminology carries more weight than programming flair. Suits a weeknight hour well because the work breaks into small, checkable pieces.

subjects.name: Whole-paper technique across subjects
subjects.description: Papers sat under exam timing, then dissected against what the mark scheme actually rewards. This is weekend work. A tired student at 7pm on a Thursday cannot sit a two-hour paper honestly, and a dishonestly sat paper teaches nothing.

sections.heading: The Al Manaseer afternoon, measured honestly
paragraphs: An IGCSE session for a student living in Al Manaseer should start at 6pm or later, and that conclusion comes out of the school run rather than out of any theory about attention. Secondary schools serving the western island finish between roughly 2.50pm and 3.30pm. Pick-up adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes before a car moves at all. The drive back then ranges from eight minutes within Al Bateen to thirty-five from the eastern island at the worst hour.

The table sets out the main directions and what each does to the evening. The drive figures are typical rather than measured and they move with the day, but the ordering does not. Households whose children attend Al Bateen campuses have genuine options before six. Households crossing the island or a bridge do not, and a plan that pretends otherwise produces a missed session in week three and an abandoned arrangement by half term, with the tuition money spent and nothing to show for it.

What makes the later slot possible is removing the second journey. A tutor who has to physically arrive at a block in Al Manaseer at 6.30pm makes the same crossing the family just made, in the same traffic, and that journey reaches you as a higher rate or a two-hour minimum. Without it the slot can be as late as the household actually needs, long enough to be useful and short enough to be sustainable, and it holds for the whole year rather than being renegotiated every few weeks.

sections.heading: Which subjects belong on a weeknight and which belong on a weekend
paragraphs: Almost nobody asks this question and it changes outcomes more than the choice of tutor does. IGCSE work divides into tasks that fit a tired student in a sixty-minute slot and tasks that do not, and putting the second kind into the first kind of hour is the commonest way a well-funded tuition plan produces nothing.

Short, checkable work suits a weeknight. A maths topic, a set of chemistry calculations, pseudocode and trace tables, command-term drilling in biology, a geography case study learned properly. These break into pieces, each piece can be checked in the session, and a student who arrived home at a quarter to five can still do them well at six.

Extended writing and whole papers do not suit a weeknight. An English Literature essay under timing, a two-hour maths paper, a full history source paper: these need a fresh brain and an uninterrupted stretch, and a paper sat badly at 7.30pm on a Thursday is worse than no paper at all because it teaches the student that they cannot do it. Those belong on a Saturday or Sunday morning, which for Al Manaseer families is also the only time of week when the car is not part of the equation. The table sorts the common subjects accordingly. The test is easy to apply. Ask whether the task can be stopped halfway and resumed next week without losing anything. If it can, a weeknight hour is fine. If stopping halfway destroys the point of the exercise, as it does with a timed paper, it needs a weekend morning and it needs to be booked as one.

sections.heading: What an hour should contain when the student arrived home at 4.45pm
paragraphs: A session at the end of a long Abu Dhabi school day has to be designed differently from one at the start of a free afternoon, and a tutor who ignores that is wasting a slot the family worked hard to protect. The student in front of them has been awake since six, has sat six lessons, has spent half an hour in a car and has eaten something at speed. The hour needs to be built for that.

In practice it means starting with something the student can already do, for three or four minutes, to get the mathematics or the terminology moving before anything new arrives. It means one objective rather than three, named out loud at the start so the student knows what the hour is for. It means the tutor writing while talking, on a shared screen the student can reopen later, because a tired student retains far less of what they hear than of what they can go back to.

It also means stopping. Sixty minutes at six in the evening produces more than ninety does, and two hours after a long day is largely theatre. If a household has bought a two-hour block for convenience, the honest advice is to split it into two sixties on different evenings, or to move the second hour to a weekend morning. Any tutor who tells you a tired Year 11 can work productively for two hours straight on a weeknight has not watched one try.

sections.heading: Mock season and the fortnight that decides predicted grades
paragraphs: The most consequential two weeks of an IGCSE year are not in the exam series. They are the mock window in the winter term, because the grades that come out of it become the predicted grades a sixth form or a university sees, and because the scripts produced are the only honest diagnostic a family will get before the real thing.

Most households treat mocks as practice and then treat the results as a verdict, which is the wrong way round. The useful approach is to take the preparation seriously, because the predicted grades matter, and then to take the scripts even more seriously, because they show exactly where marks were lost. A script read carefully by somebody who knows the mark scheme produces a list of specific, fixable errors: method not shown, premature rounding, a command term misread, a case study with nothing specific in it, a paper that ran out of time at question nineteen.

The window for that reading is short. Within a fortnight of the mock, the student still remembers what they were thinking and can recognise the error. Six weeks later the paper is cold and the conversation becomes abstract. So the single highest-value booking in an Al Manaseer IGCSE year is one session per weak subject in the two weeks after mocks, with the marked script in front of the tutor. It is also the booking almost nobody makes, because the holidays usually fall in exactly that gap.
bullets: Mock grades become the predicted grades a sixth form reads

sections.heading: Entries, zones and the two series a UAE candidate sits
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests at other points in the year. UAE candidates sit June and November. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so advice built around a February exam window does not apply to a child sitting in Abu Dhabi, and it circulates widely enough to be worth stating plainly.

Two administrative details matter more than families expect. First, Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and says it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for the zone is used, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was consulted. That is a question for the school's exams officer, not for a tutoring website. Second, final entries are submitted by the school months before the papers, and once submitted the tier is fixed for that series.

The Pearson Edexcel route runs on its own calendar: International GCSE exams are available in May/June and in November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any table like the one below should point you at the live official timetable rather than restate dates that get revised. Ask the exams officer for three things in one email: the specification codes your child is entered for, the tier per subject, and the centre's zone. All three are administrative facts the school already holds, and all three change what a tutor should be preparing your child for.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened day and the schedule that survives it
paragraphs: Every weekly arrangement in the UAE meets Ramadan, and the ones that survive it are the ones that planned for it in September rather than renegotiating in the first week. The school day shortens across the country, the household's rhythm moves towards the evening, and a 6.30pm session that worked perfectly in November is suddenly sitting in the wrong part of the day.

The adjustment is straightforward if it is deliberate. Sessions after iftar work well for most families, and shorter, more frequent sessions suit a shortened school day better than the usual single block. For a Year 11 preparing for the June series this is not a month to drop out of, because the gap between Ramadan and the papers is short and cumulative subjects do not forgive a four-week pause. Deciding the replacement slot in advance, in writing, is what prevents a month of week-by-week cancellations.

The other predictable interruptions deserve the same treatment. The winter break lands shortly after mocks, which makes it either the most valuable fortnight in Year 11 or a complete loss depending on whether anything was arranged. Spring break sits uncomfortably close to the June series. And Al Manaseer households travel in the long summer, after which a Year 10 who stopped maths entirely for ten weeks returns measurably weaker in precisely the non-calculator fluency the tier decision rests on. Two sessions a month over the summer, online wherever the family happens to be, prevents that.

sections.heading: ADEK, school reports and what an inspection actually tells you
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. Reading an inspection report alongside your child's school report is one of the more useful hours an Al Manaseer parent can spend, because the two documents are written for different readers and say different things.

A school report tells you how your child is doing relative to that school's expectations. An inspection report comments on the quality of teaching, often by subject and phase, relative to a published framework. If a report describes attainment in science as below expectations while your child's own report describes them as meeting them, that mismatch is worth a conversation. It is also the kind of information that redirects tuition money sensibly: a child may be doing fine against a weak departmental standard.

What an inspection report does not do is endorse anybody's tutoring. No UAE regulator approves individual private tutors on teaching merit, and the phrase approved tutors in any form should be read as marketing. For completeness: IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry of Education, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and none of the schools named on this page is a client or a partner. A provider that implies otherwise is making a claim worth checking before you buy anything from them. Read the most recent report rather than the one a school quotes in its marketing, and check the date on it. An inspection outcome from several years ago describes a department that may have changed staff twice since, which makes it weak evidence either way.

sections.heading: Who may give private lessons in Abu Dhabi, and what you can ask
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated, and the rules are specific enough to be worth knowing before money changes hands. Giving private lessons as an individual requires a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

The terms are unusually clear. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page for the permit is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount circulating online is unverified.

One condition deserves emphasis in Abu Dhabi specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. So an offer of private lessons from your child's own classroom teacher is an offer that should not be made. That has been reported in the press rather than quoted here from the policy itself, so verify the current wording against ADEK's own document before acting on it either way.

process.description: A recent assessment or a mock script, marked, with the teacher's comments left on it. Mark loss in IGCSE subjects is visible on the page and invisible in a report, and this is what turns the first session into diagnosis rather than conversation.

process.title: Book the free trial at the real time
process.description: Not a convenient one-off hour but the time you intend to keep every week. A trial that works at 5pm and a weekly slot that never works again at 5pm is the single commonest reason an arrangement fails in October. You know the tutor's name before the lesson.

process.description: Topic teaching goes in the fixed weeknight hour and tracks the school's sequence. Extended writing and whole papers go to a weekend morning. Separating the two is what stops a Year 11 plan collapsing into unfinished past papers.

process.title: Review after mocks, with the scripts
process.description: The fortnight after mocks is the highest-value booking of the year: one session per weak subject with the marked script in front of the tutor, while the student still remembers what they were thinking. The plan for the spring is set from that, not from a guess.

whyPoints.title: A slot that survives the school run
whyPoints.description: Sessions start from 6pm Gulf Standard Time because that is when an Al Manaseer household is genuinely home, whether the drive came from Al Bateen or from Al Reem Island. The point of a realistic time is that it is still running in April.

whyPoints.title: The right work in the right part of the week
whyPoints.description: Topic teaching on a weeknight, whole papers and extended writing on a weekend morning. A two-hour paper attempted at 7.30pm on a Thursday teaches a student that they cannot do it, which is the opposite of the intention.

whyPoints.title: Both boards, by paper and tier

whyPoints.title: No journey folded into the fee

whyPoints.title: Mock scripts read properly, while they are warm

faqs.question: What is the earliest an IGCSE session can start for a family living in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: Six in the evening for most households, and 6.30pm or 7pm where the school run crosses the island. Secondary schools here finish between roughly 2.50pm and 3.30pm, pick-up adds fifteen to twenty-five minutes before the car moves, and the drive back runs from eight minutes within Al Bateen to thirty-five from Bloom Gardens or Al Reem Island at that hour. A student home at a quarter to five needs food and a pause. Booking the trial at the time you actually intend to hold weekly, rather than a convenient one-off, is the best protection against an arrangement that dies in October.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to apartments in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Other providers in Abu Dhabi do offer it, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because that figure absorbs the tutor's journey across the island. Al Manaseer lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the slot can be late enough to be realistic after a long run and the hour you pay for contains no commute.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE work should go on a weeknight and which on a weekend?
faqs.answer: Weeknights suit work that breaks into small checkable pieces: a maths topic, chemistry calculations, physics formulae, command-term drilling in biology, pseudocode and trace tables. Weekends suit anything needing a fresh brain and an uninterrupted stretch: extended writing in English or history, and whole papers under timing. A two-hour paper attempted at half past seven on a school night after a thirty-minute drive teaches a student that they cannot do it, which is worse than not attempting it. Most Al Manaseer Year 11 families end up using both parts of the week by February.

faqs.question: Is a one-hour session really enough, or should we book ninety minutes?
faqs.answer: After a long Abu Dhabi school day, sixty minutes usually produces more than ninety. The student has been awake since six, sat six lessons, spent half an hour in a car and eaten at speed. Concentration on technical material degrades noticeably after about seventy-five minutes, and the last stretch of a long weeknight session is frequently the least productive hour a family pays for all week. If a household wants more time, the better structure is two separate sixties, or one weeknight hour plus a longer weekend morning for papers.

faqs.question: What should a tutor do differently with a student who is already tired?
faqs.answer: Design the hour for the state the student is actually in. Open with three or four minutes of something already secure, to get the subject moving before anything new arrives. Set one objective rather than three, and say it out loud at the start so the student knows what the hour is for. Write while talking, on a shared screen the student can reopen later, because a tired student retains far more from something they can revisit than from something they heard once. And finish on time rather than pushing into a second hour that will not land.

faqs.question: When in the year is tutoring money best spent for an Abu Dhabi Year 11?
faqs.answer: Two windows matter more than the rest. The first is the two weeks after mocks, when the marked scripts still mean something to the student and a specialist can turn them into a list of fixable errors: method not shown, premature rounding, a command term misread, a paper that ran out of time. The second is February onwards, when whole papers under timing replace topic work. Spending in April is the most expensive and least effective option, and it is also when every available specialist has already been booked by somebody else.

faqs.question: Why do mock results matter if they are only practice?
faqs.answer: Because the grades that come out of them usually become the predicted grades a sixth form or a university sees, and because the scripts are the only honest diagnostic available before the real series. Most households treat the preparation casually and the results as a verdict, which is the wrong way round. Take the preparation seriously for the predicted grade, then take the scripts more seriously still: read by someone who knows the mark scheme, a mock paper produces a specific, fixable list rather than a general impression of how things are going.

faqs.question: June or November: which Cambridge window does an Abu Dhabi centre use?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November as the alternate or resit route. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so any guidance built around a February exam window does not apply here, however widely it circulates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so confirm the zone with the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Can the entry tier still be changed once Year 11 has started?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the window closes earlier than most families expect. Final entries are submitted by the school months before the papers and once submitted the tier is fixed for that series. Before that point a department will usually consider evidence, which is why a written diagnostic report carries more weight than a parent's impression. The practical consequence is that the tier conversation belongs in the autumn of Year 10 or very early in Year 11, and the question to ask is what the current tier caps the grade at and what that closes after Year 11.

faqs.question: Should tutoring stop during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It should move rather than stop. The school day shortens across the UAE and household energy shifts to the evening, so a session that worked at 6.30pm often works better after iftar, and shorter more frequent sessions suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 11 heading into the June series, a four-week pause in a cumulative subject is expensive, because the gap between Ramadan and the papers is short. Agreeing the replacement slot in advance and in writing is what stops a month turning into weekly cancellations.

faqs.question: How do I read my child's ADEK inspection report alongside their school report?
faqs.answer: Read them as answers to different questions. The school report says how your child is doing against that school's expectations. The ADEK inspection report comments on the quality of teaching, often by subject and phase, against a published framework. If the inspection describes attainment in a department as below expectations while your child's report says they are meeting them, that gap is worth raising. It also redirects tuition money sensibly, because a child can be comfortable against a weak departmental standard and still be underprepared for a terminal paper.

faqs.question: What does the MoHRE private tuition permit actually cover?
faqs.answer: It is the legal clearance an individual needs to give private lessons in the UAE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. What it is not is a judgement on anyone's teaching, and no UAE regulator approves individual tutors on merit, so treat the permit as a floor rather than a recommendation.

faqs.question: Can my child's class teacher at their Abu Dhabi school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: They should not. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction on serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This has been reported in the press rather than quoted here from the policy document, so verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. Either way, an offer of that kind is one a family is better off declining.

faqs.question: Which schools do your IGCSE students on the western island attend?
faqs.answer: Families around Al Manaseer come from campuses in Al Bateen and on the western island and from the larger British-curriculum schools further east, including the American Community School of Abu Dhabi, Al Bateen Academy, Cambridge International School Abu Dhabi, The British School Al Khubairat, International Community School Abu Dhabi and Brighton College Abu Dhabi. Those names describe the local school map and nothing further. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school listed, and none of them is a client.

faqs.question: Is it sensible to run three IGCSE subjects with a tutor in the same term?
faqs.answer: One well, two with effort, three rarely. A Year 11 in Abu Dhabi is carrying eight or nine IGCSE subjects plus the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and there is very little slack in that week. Running three tutoring subjects usually means three sessions receiving a third of the student's remaining attention each. The better approach is to pick the subject where the gap is widest, fix it properly over a term, then move the hour. Short diagnostic blocks across the candidate subjects first will tell you which one that is.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-manasee.closingHeading: Protect the slot, then fill it properly
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-manasee.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE home tutor in Al Manaseer, start by working out when your child is genuinely home and fed after the run from Al Bateen, Al Mushrif or the eastern island, and treat that time as the fixed point. Book the free trial at exactly that hour, send one piece of marked work for each subject you are worried about, and keep the weekend mornings free for whole papers once Year 11 arrives. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the tutor is named before the trial, and if the match is wrong we change it.

intro.heading: Start with the money, because nobody else in this market will
paragraphs: Of the competitor pages researched for IGCSE tutoring in the UAE, three publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars — a currency no family on Al Maryah Island pays a tutor in. One agency's own frequently-asked-questions block asks how much tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. That is the state of the market you are shopping in, and it is why this page opens with AED figures rather than with adjectives about dedication.

Here is the shape of it. Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, put a budget online tutor at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, and a named IGCSE or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Convert that into an annual decision and the numbers get real. One session a week for a school year, at the qualified-online band, is a four-figure commitment per subject. Two subjects doubles it. A family on Al Maryah Island funding three subjects in-home across Year 10 and Year 11 is spending on tutoring what some schools charge in fees for a term. That is not an argument against tutoring. It is an argument for buying the right thing.

The right thing, in IGCSE terms, is narrow and identifiable. It is the four topics in a syllabus where a student loses the same marks each paper. It is the difference between a Core and an Extended entry decision made in Year 10 rather than regretted in Year 11. It is a board-specific paper technique, because Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 do not reward the same answers. And it is almost never a general weekly hour of homework supervision, which is what most of the spend in this market buys.

The other half of the money question is delivery format. An in-home rate carries the journey inside it, and on Al Maryah Island that journey is a bridge crossing from the mainland at the worst hour of the day. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so the comparison on this page is honest rather than rhetorical. We teach over live video, one to one, with the fee paying for a subject specialist rather than for their car.

What follows is the detail: a monthly cost table, the places families waste money, the board question, the exam calendar read backwards from results day, what the Ministry of Education actually requires, and what a tutor may and may not do with coursework. Read it and you will be able to price any quote you are given, including ours.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maryah-.programmesIntro: An Al Maryah Island family shopping for IGCSE help needs to know which qualification their child is actually entered for, because the board changes the papers, the codes and the revision. These are the routes in play in Abu Dhabi schools.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International's IGCSE suite, identified by four-digit syllabus codes — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology. Most subjects offer a Core tier graded G to C and an Extended tier graded E to A*, and the entry tier is a decision the school makes with you. Grading is published on either the 9 to 1 or the A* to G scale depending on the subject and region.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so an Al Maryah Island candidate sits June, with November as the resit route. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE suite, identified by codes such as 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics and 4CH1 Chemistry. Mathematics A is tiered as Foundation and Higher. Several subjects are available in a modular structure in which units can be sat across series, which changes revision planning substantially compared with a single terminal entry.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so check the live official timetable rather than any restated date.

programmes.name: Cambridge O Level
programmes.description: Cambridge's O Level qualifications sit alongside IGCSE in the same June and November series and are still offered for some subjects in some schools. Content overlaps heavily with the equivalent IGCSE but the assessment pattern differs, particularly in the treatment of coursework and practical components.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Abu Dhabi schools enter O Level than IGCSE, but it appears in the emirate and it matters when a family moves school mid-key-stage. If a Year 10 student transfers between an O Level entry and an IGCSE entry in the same subject, the content gap is usually small and the paper-technique gap is not. That is a short, cheap piece of tutoring that families often skip and then pay for in Year 11.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into
programmes.description: An IGCSE grade set is the entry ticket to A Level, to the IB Diploma or to a career-related route, and schools set their own thresholds for each. Mathematics in particular gates the sixth-form choice: an Extended or Higher tier grade is usually required for an A Level or Higher Level maths course, and a Core or Foundation entry can close that door before anyone discusses it.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools Al Maryah Island families use run both A Level and IB Diploma pathways, which makes the Year 11 grade set a genuine fork rather than a formality. Spending on Year 10 maths to protect an Extended entry is usually better value than spending on Year 11 maths to rescue one, and that sequencing is the single largest avoidable cost in this market.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-maryah-.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Al Maryah Island families most often fund, with the specific place marks go. Price per subject is similar across the market, so the only thing that varies is whether the hour is spent on the right topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended; Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics. The repeating losses are method marks in multi-step algebra, bearings and compound-shape questions, and arithmetic slips in non-calculator work. Extended and Higher tier add harder algebraic manipulation and functions, which is where a tiering decision shows.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics, magnetism and radioactivity. Electricity circuits are the standard breaking point, and the practical-skills paper rewards precise description of a method and of control variables rather than recall of a result.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Mole calculations and ionic equations are where marks concentrate, and qualitative-analysis questions reward learned observations that most students never systematically revise.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The content is large and the losses are in command terms: an answer describing a process when the question asked for an explanation of a cause earns partial credit at best.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing and composition. Marks are lost on failing to adapt register to the audience named in the task and on summary questions that reproduce the passage rather than condense it. A defined, repeatable writing structure moves this grade faster than reading more.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking for students working in English as an additional language. The gain comes from exam technique and accuracy drilling rather than general conversation, and the listening paper is improved by targeted practice at speed rather than exposure.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Demand and supply, markets, the macroeconomy, business functions and finance. Diagram accuracy carries marks and is routinely sloppy, and extended-response answers lose marks for listing points without evaluating them against the context in the question.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Data representation, hardware, networks, algorithms, programming and the practical components. Pseudocode and trace-table questions are reliable marks that students treat as optional, and the written paper rewards precise terminology over general description.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: These sit alongside the international curriculum under federal and emirate requirements. Worth noting for cost planning: for Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so they are an obligation rather than part of the equivalency count.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and further options
subjects.description: Some Abu Dhabi schools enter stronger cohorts for Additional Mathematics or an early AS unit. It is a bridge into A Level or Higher Level work and tutoring on it is usually short and targeted, because the student is already secure in the IGCSE content underneath.

regions.name: the Corniche

sections.heading: What IGCSE tutoring costs per month on Al Maryah Island
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because the monthly figure is what a family actually decides about. Published market data gives usable bands. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions come out at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the mid range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those bands assume one subject. The moment a family funds two subjects weekly the monthly commitment roughly doubles, and three subjects at the specialist band crosses into a number that competes with other household education spending. Year 11 families on Al Maryah Island often arrive at that point by accident, having added subjects one at a time without recalculating the total.

The useful discipline is to set the monthly budget first and then decide what it buys. A fixed AED 800 a month buys one weekly session with a qualified subject tutor, or two sessions a week for half the year, or three targeted topic blocks spread across the year with gaps in between. Those are genuinely different products, and the third one is usually the best value because it has defined endpoints.

Every figure below is a market figure published by someone else and read in October 2026. IB Gram does not publish an hourly price on this page; the figure comes out of a free trial lesson and a consultation once the subject, board and frequency are known.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE families on this island waste the money
paragraphs: The first and largest waste is paying for general hours instead of a named weakness. An open-ended weekly hour with no defined target drifts into whatever homework is due, which is supervision at a specialist's rate. The fix costs nothing: before the first session, write down the four topics the last two marked papers show the student losing marks on, and insist the first month is spent on those.

The second is funding too many subjects at once. Three subjects at one hour a week is three hours of tutoring and almost no depth in any of them, and it triples the bill while splitting the student's attention in the term when they can least afford it. One subject taken properly to a changed grade is worth more than three nudged.

The third is the travel premium paid without noticing. On Al Maryah Island an in-home rate carries a mainland journey inside it, and the market gap between the online and in-home bands is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour. Over a school year of weekly sessions that difference is a substantial sum paid for driving, not teaching, and it is the one line a family can remove without losing a single minute of instruction.

The fourth is starting late. A Year 11 student six weeks from a June series can be helped, but the work is triage: pick the two highest-yield topics and drill them. The same money spent in Year 10 buys content security and a tiering decision, which is a better product. The fifth is a rolling commitment with no review point, which converts a teaching decision into a subscription.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: find out before you pay for anything
paragraphs: A surprising number of Abu Dhabi parents do not know which board their child is entered with, and it changes what tutoring should look like. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subjects with different papers, different codes and different structures. A tutor drilling Cambridge 0580 past papers at a student entered for Edexcel 4MA1 is doing useful general maths and wasting the specificity you are paying for.

The practical differences matter. Cambridge tiers many subjects as Core and Extended; Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher. Several Pearson subjects can be taken modularly, with units sat across series, which changes the revision calendar completely compared with a single terminal entry. Practical assessment in the sciences is handled differently between the boards, and the mark schemes reward differently phrased answers even where the physics is identical.

Find out by asking the school for the syllabus code, not the subject name. The code is unambiguous: 0580 is Cambridge Mathematics, 4MA1 is Edexcel Mathematics A, 0625 is Cambridge Physics, 4PH1 is Edexcel Physics. Give that code to any tutor you speak to and their answer tells you quickly whether they know the qualification or the subject.

One more board-specific trap, this one with real consequences. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable. If your child is a private candidate rather than a school entry, that is your responsibility to get right.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and what each decision costs later
paragraphs: The tiering decision is the cheapest high-value piece of advice in IGCSE and almost nobody charges for it, because it is made by schools in Year 10 and absorbed by families as a fact. It should be interrogated. A Core or Foundation entry caps the attainable grade. An Extended or Higher entry does not, but it puts harder material in front of a student who may not be ready for it, with a real risk of a worse outcome than a secure Core entry would have produced.

Where the cost shows up is post-16. Sixth-form courses set their own entry thresholds, and a maths A Level or an IB Higher Level maths course usually requires an Extended or Higher tier grade. A student capped at Core in Year 10 can find a sixth-form door closed in Year 11 by a decision taken eighteen months earlier, and reopening it means a resit series and another year's planning.

This is where tutoring spend is best placed. Four to six sessions in Year 10, aimed squarely at the content that separates Core from Extended, is a small, defined cost that protects a large, expensive decision. The same money spent in Year 11 on general revision buys far less, because the entry is already made and the ceiling is already set.

Ask the school two questions. Which tier is my child provisionally entered for, and what would have to change for the other tier to be viable? Any department will answer both, and the second answer is a precise tutoring brief.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, exams and the rest of the bill
paragraphs: Tutoring is one line in a larger education budget, and it reads differently once the others are on the page. School fees dominate, and in Dubai KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is a Dubai measure rather than an Abu Dhabi one, and it is a useful reminder that fee policy is set by the emirate regulator rather than nationally.

The scale of the sector is worth knowing too. Dubai's private school market in 2024-25 held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of students, Indian at 26, US at 14 and the International Baccalaureate at 7. Abu Dhabi's market is smaller and regulated by ADEK, but the curriculum mix is comparable, and the UK-curriculum share is why IGCSE tutoring demand in this emirate is as deep as it is.

Against those numbers, a tutoring decision is a marginal spend with a specific job. It is not an insurance policy against the school, and it is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency or for university admission — no tutoring provider should imply otherwise. It is the purchase of a defined number of hours of specialist attention on a defined weakness, and it should be budgeted and reviewed like any other defined purchase.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from results day
paragraphs: Families plan forwards from today and then run out of weeks. Boards work backwards from results day, and so should a tutoring budget. The two fixed facts for a UAE candidate are these: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi.

Pearson's published history gives usable anchors for how long each stage takes. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking dates and they tell you the shape of the wait: roughly eight to nine weeks from a summer paper to a result, and about two months from a November paper to a January result.

The entry deadline is the stage families miss, because it sits months before the exam and is handled by the school without much noise. For a private candidate it is not handled by anyone else. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so the correct action is always to open the live official timetable rather than to trust a date restated on a tutoring page, including this one.

Read backwards, the tutoring implication is simple. Topic-level work belongs six to nine months before the series. Paper technique belongs in the final three months. The last four weeks are for timed papers and error patterns only. A family that starts in the last four weeks is buying the third stage without the first two, which is why late spend feels expensive.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and what it does not require
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts an international school certificate into something UAE authorities recognise, and it is the subject on which this market is least accurate. For the British track, the published requirement is that students submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that matters most for an IGCSE family is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published five-subject rule. Check your own situation against the Ministry rather than against any tutoring site.

For the American track the same guidance sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that guidance, so no page should publish one, and this one does not.

Two things follow. First, equivalency is not a service IB Gram performs, guarantees or influences; we describe it and point you to the official channel. Second, tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying that it is has turned a regulatory process into a sales argument.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but where it exists the boundary is the same and the consequences are as serious. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question a student's method until they find its weakness, read work the student produced and say which criterion it is underselling, and teach referencing and the honest description of a method.

A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit assessed work to completion. May not produce a model answer to the actual task for the student to adapt. May not supply data the student did not collect. May not generate the student's research question or hypothesis and hand it over. There is an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price; that is an integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student, and it is not something we do at any fee.

There is also a copyright boundary that parents should be aware of when comparing providers. We do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source. A provider handing you a folder of scanned mark schemes is not giving you a bonus; they are redistributing somebody else's copyrighted material.

Stated plainly, since this page targets a home-tutor search: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to an Al Maryah Island address. Home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Everything described above happens on live video, one tutor to one student.

sections.heading: One-to-one, group class or centre: price per useful minute
paragraphs: Hourly rate is the wrong comparison between formats, because the formats deliver different quantities of attention. A group class at a quarter of the one-to-one rate may give a student five minutes of individual correction in an hour, which is not a quarter of the product at a quarter of the price. The honest metric is price per minute of attention directed at your child's specific error.

On that measure one-to-one is usually the better value for a diagnosable weakness and poor value for general content coverage, where a group class or the school's own revision provision does the job adequately and far more cheaply. The error families make is to buy one-to-one for coverage and groups for diagnosis, which is the arrangement exactly inverted.

A tuition centre adds a travel cost that nobody itemises: your own driving, twice, at the hour Abu Dhabi traffic is worst. For an Al Maryah Island family that means leaving the island and returning, which is a parent's hour as well as a student's. Online removes that line entirely, and it is a real saving even though it never appears on an invoice.

There is one more line worth counting. A centre or group class runs to a fixed timetable, so a clash with a school activity means a missed session that is paid for and not recovered. A one-to-one slot can move inside the week. Across a school year that difference is several hours of teaching either kept or lost, and it belongs in the comparison alongside the headline rate.

process.description: Not the subject name — the code. 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1. It tells any tutor which board, which papers and which mark scheme, and it tells you quickly whether the tutor you are speaking to knows the qualification or only the subject.

process.title: Name the weakness from marked papers
process.description: Put the last two marked assessments side by side and list the topics where the same marks are lost. That list is your tutoring brief and your budget control. Hours bought without it drift into homework supervision at a specialist's rate.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson on real work
process.description: Send the marked paper beforehand so the hour starts on evidence. At the end, ask the tutor to name the specific thing costing marks and the specific fix. A tutor who answers in generalities after an hour on a real script has told you something useful.

process.title: Agree the block, the slot and the review point
process.description: A defined number of sessions, a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, and a named assessment to review against. Sessions can shift post-Iftar during Ramadan and pause across school exam weeks. No open-ended commitment is needed to start.

process.title: Review against the next marked assessment, then decide
process.description: If the lost-mark pattern has moved, continue or close the block. If it has not, we change the approach or the tutor rather than selling you more hours. That review point is how a tutoring budget stays a decision rather than becoming a subscription.
