faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE tutor cost per month for a family on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: Using published market bands read in October 2026: roughly AED 240 to 600 a month for a budget tutor at one hour a week, AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support, per Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates. Package rates seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are one-subject figures. Two subjects roughly doubles them, which is where Year 11 budgets quietly escape.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home IGCSE rate on Al Maryah Island cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the journey is inside the rate. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Al Maryah Island has no school on it and few resident tutors, so an in-home match is almost always travelling from the mainland across a bridge at the busiest hour. You are paying a specialist's rate for seventy to a hundred minutes of their driving. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so for us the question does not arise.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE board is my child sitting, and why does it change the tutoring?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Cambridge codes look like 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry. Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1 and 4CH1. The boards examine the same subjects with different papers, different tiering and different mark-scheme phrasing, and Pearson offers modular unit entry in several subjects, which changes the revision calendar entirely. A tutor drilling the wrong board's past papers is teaching useful maths and wasting the specificity you are paying a specialist rate for.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidate actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only — it is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and in November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Always open the board's live official timetable rather than trusting a restated date.

faqs.question: How long is the wait between an IGCSE paper and a result?
faqs.answer: Pearson's published history gives the shape of it. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, which is roughly eight to nine weeks after the summer window. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so about two months after a November series. The November 2026 final timetable itself ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those are backward-looking dates, quoted so you can plan the wait. Future series dates move, so check the live official timetable before acting on any of them.

faqs.question: What is the single biggest way IGCSE families waste tutoring money?
faqs.answer: Buying general weekly hours instead of named topics. An open-ended hour drifts into whatever homework is due that night, which is supervision bought at a specialist's rate. The fix costs nothing: before the first paid session, put the last two marked papers side by side and list the topics where the same marks are lost. Hand that list to the tutor and insist the first month is spent on it. Families who do this spend materially less per grade point moved than families who book an hour a week and hope.

faqs.question: Should we fund one IGCSE subject properly or three subjects lightly?
faqs.answer: One, almost always. Three subjects at an hour a week each triples the bill, splits the student's attention in the term they can least afford it, and usually produces three small nudges rather than one changed grade. The exception is a genuine timetable emergency where two subjects are both at risk of a grade that closes a sixth-form door. Pick the subject that gates the post-16 choice, usually mathematics, take it properly to a changed outcome, and reassess with the next marked assessment in hand.

faqs.question: Is the Core or Extended decision worth paying a tutor to influence?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value tutoring spend in IGCSE and almost nobody sells it. A Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade, and sixth-form courses set their own thresholds — an A Level or Higher Level maths course normally needs an Extended or Higher tier grade. Four to six sessions in Year 10, aimed at the content separating the tiers, is a small defined cost protecting a large expensive decision. Ask the school which tier your child is provisionally entered for and what would have to change for the other tier to be viable. The second answer is your tutoring brief.

faqs.question: Does Arabic count towards the IGCSE subjects the Ministry asks for?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the detail families get wrong. The published requirement for the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are expressly not included among those five. A page currently ranking in this market states six subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Verify your own case with the Ministry of Education, not with a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Does tutoring help with equivalency or attestation in any way?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should imply it does. Equivalency and attestation are regulatory processes run by the Ministry of Education and the relevant attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform them, influence them or guarantee an outcome in them, and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. What tutoring can do is help a student reach the subject grades the process asks for. Treat any provider that presents equivalency as a reason to buy tutoring hours as having turned a government process into a sales argument.

faqs.question: Does a group class or a tuition centre work out cheaper in real terms?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, often not cheaper per useful minute. A group class at a quarter of the one-to-one rate may give your child five to fifteen minutes of individual correction in an hour. A centre adds two car journeys off and back onto Al Maryah Island at the worst hour, which is a parent's time nobody invoices. Groups are good value for content coverage and shared revision; one-to-one is good value for a diagnosed weakness and paper technique. The common mistake is buying them the other way round. Use the school's own revision provision first — it is already paid for.

faqs.question: Can a tutor produce any part of my child's IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question the student's method until they find the weakness themselves, read work the student wrote and name which criterion it is underselling, and teach referencing and honest method description. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete any assessed work, produce a model answer to the live task for adaptation, or supply data the student did not collect. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is a malpractice trigger for the student and something we do not do at any fee.

faqs.question: Do you hand out past papers and mark schemes as part of the fee?
faqs.answer: We reference them and link the official source rather than redistributing them. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyrighted material belonging to Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and bundling scanned copies into a tutoring package is redistribution of somebody else's property rather than a bonus for you. Papers are available through the boards and through your school's exams officer. What a tutor adds is not the paper; it is the marking of your child's attempt at it against the real rubric, which is the part a downloaded folder cannot do.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a licence, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: Yes to the first and no to the second. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust any quoted figure.

faqs.question: Is six weeks before the June series too late to be worth the money?
faqs.answer: It is worth money, but a different product. At six weeks the work is triage: sit a full paper under timing, find the two highest-yield repeating errors, and drill those only. Attempting to re-teach a syllabus in six weeks spends a lot and moves little. Two or three sessions a week in that window, built from the student's own scripts, is the format that earns its cost. The same budget spent nine months earlier buys content security and a tiering decision, which is why late spend feels expensive — you are buying stage three without stages one and two.

faqs.question: What do we need to send before a free trial lesson on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: Three things. The syllabus code for the subject, so the tutor is board-correct from the first minute. The last two marked assessments including the teacher or examiner comments, so the hour starts on evidence rather than introductions. And the time your child actually gets home, because a commute from Al Reem is twenty minutes and one from Yas or the mainland can be fifty, which changes which slots are real. With those in hand the tutor can tell you at the end of the hour what is costing marks and what the fix is.

intro.heading: Start at the bottom of the market and work upwards
paragraphs: Published rates for IGCSE tuition in the UAE span more than a factor of ten, and most families begin at the cheap end because that is the rational place to begin. The useful question is therefore not what the best tuition costs but what is actually missing from the cheapest option, and whether what is missing matters for your particular child. Sometimes it does not, and a page that cannot say so is advertising.

Al Muroor is a residential district on Abu Dhabi island, strung along Muroor Road between the Airport Road corridor and the central districts. Its position matters for cost in one specific way: it is central, so the travel loading on a visiting tutor is smaller here than from the mainland communities. Published in-home rates in the emirate still run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026, but the journey component of that is shorter from a central island address than from Al Shamkha or Baniyas.

The structure of this page is the price ladder. At the bottom, budget online tutoring and university-student tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. In the middle, a qualified subject tutor teaching online is published at AED 150 to 300. Above that, IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and more, and a premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650. Each step up adds something specific, and knowing what it adds is the whole of the purchasing decision.

The second question this page answers is how many subjects a household can genuinely support, which is where most of the waste in this market occurs. The arithmetic is unforgiving: tuition works through the marked written practice done between lessons, and a student's free evenings do not multiply when subjects are added. By the third or fourth subject the lessons are the only work happening, nothing consolidates, and the household is paying four times as much for less than one properly funded subject would deliver.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. From a central island district the cost argument for that is weaker than from the mainland and the choice argument is just as strong: requiring a specialist in a specific specification to also drive here at five in the afternoon reduces an already small pool.

Every AED figure on this page belongs to the market, is attributed to a named published source and was read in October 2026. None is IB Gram's price list. On the VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE we state no position, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and we would rather say so than publish something unsourced.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before IGCSE begins
programmes.description: Number, algebra, geometry and data handling across mathematics, with the sciences and languages building the terminology that later courses assume. The quiet work of these years is fluency, which is built by short frequent practice rather than by teaching.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest effective window in the whole British curriculum and the least used. Abu Dhabi schools form their tier view during Year 9, so a term of work at this point can change which tier a school enters a student for, and the tier sets the grade ceiling for the following two years.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: The content year across all subjects, where the bulk of each syllabus is taught and the tier is confirmed. A student falling behind here compounds, because IGCSE courses assume earlier topics rather than revisiting them.
programmes.countryNote: The internal assessments schools run at the end of Year 10 are the best diagnostic evidence available before the final year, and in most Abu Dhabi schools they are marked by the subject teacher against the real scheme. They are therefore worth reading rather than filing, and reading them is free.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11
programmes.description: Syllabus completion, mocks, the final entry and the papers. Spending in this year reliably buys examination technique: command-term discipline, rounding accuracy, timing and question selection. It does not rebuild underlying fluency, because the week no longer contains the practice volume.
programmes.countryNote: The school's final entry deadline sits months before the papers and fixes the tier at that point. An Al Muroor parent should ask for that date early in Year 11 and treat it rather than the examination as the real deadline for any tiering conversation.

programmes.name: AS, A Level and Diploma routes afterwards
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE tier decision lands. Both the A Level and IB Diploma routes generally assume Extended or Higher content behind them, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, so a Core or Foundation entry narrows post-16 options without any single conversation saying so.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.subjectsIntro: These notes are about value per hour rather than content: where the money goes furthest in each subject, which is what a household rationing a budget needs to know.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Best value where the fault is procedural: frequency density, scale factors, rounding discipline, command terms. Each is a short named repair worth real marks. Poorest value in Year 11 where the fault is fluency, because the hours required no longer exist in the week.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Good value when the hour produces marked written answers rather than explanation. Marks sit in multi-step calculation chains and in explanations that name the particles responsible rather than describing an observation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Good value with one caveat that saves money: a physics difficulty is often an algebra difficulty. A tutor who establishes that before teaching physics can save a family a whole term of paying for the wrong subject.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Value depends entirely on method rather than on the tutor. The subject responds to answers written and marked against the scheme and barely at all to explanation, so an articulate tutor who does not mark is poor value here.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: High value where the hour is spent on feedback on the student's own writing, low value where it is spent on technique in the abstract. Marks go to unsupported assertion in reading answers and to flat sentence structure in composition.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with its own listening and speaking components. A student placed in the wrong one loses marks for reasons unrelated to their English, and checking which applies costs nothing.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Good value because the faults are structural and correctable: definitions offered where analysis was asked for, diagrams drawn imprecisely, evaluation missing. Few sessions, visible change in marked work.

subjects.name: The science practical component
subjects.description: Strong value and almost never bought, because families do not realise practical skills are examined in writing. Method descriptions, graph scales and error questions are writing skills applied to science, and four marked attempts changes them.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Rarely available as a group class anywhere in the emirate because the cohort is too small, so one-to-one is the only format in which it can be bought. The difficulty is algebraic stamina rather than the new calculus content.

subjects.name: A subject already at the top of its range
subjects.description: No value, and we will say so. A provider who accepts every subject a parent offers is not helping them ration a budget; they are billing it. The question worth asking is which subject a provider would refuse.

sections.heading: The price ladder, and what disappears at each step down
paragraphs: Working upwards from the cheapest option is the honest way to present this market, because that is how families actually shop and because the interesting information is what each step adds. The figures are published rates read in October 2026, attributed in the table, and none of them is our price list.

At the bottom, budget online tutoring and university-student tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour. What that buys is an hour of company and supervision while a student works through material they have already been set. For a student who is coping and lacks routine, that is a reasonable purchase and genuinely useful. What is absent is any marking of written work against a published scheme, and any diagnosis, because neither is possible at that price point.

The middle band, AED 150 to 300 an hour on published agency rate pages, adds the two things the bottom lacks: a tutor who teaches the specification rather than following the homework, and written work marked between sessions. That marking is the mechanism by which a grade moves, which is why this band rather than the one below it is the sensible default for a student who is losing marks rather than merely struggling with routine.

Above that, IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and more, and the premium buys judgement rather than hours: which tier to push for, which topics to abandon, which papers to sit, what the mark scheme rewards and where this particular script is leaking marks. A premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour. The table sets out each rung with what is present and what is absent, which is the comparison families are never shown.

sections.heading: What a budget tutor genuinely cannot do
paragraphs: This needs saying precisely rather than dismissively, because budget tutoring is not a scam and for some students it is the right purchase. What it cannot do is structural rather than a matter of effort, and knowing the boundary prevents a family from buying a year of the wrong thing.

It cannot mark written work against a published mark scheme, because that takes time outside the lesson and nobody at AED 45 to 150 an hour is being paid for time outside the lesson. This is the single most consequential absence, since marking is the mechanism by which lost marks become visible and then stop recurring. A student whose work is never marked against a real scheme will continue to lose the same marks in the same way, politely and indefinitely.

It cannot diagnose at specification level, because that requires having taught the exact code and read its mark schemes. A budget tutor can see that a student is struggling with trigonometry. They are unlikely to see that the student is losing marks because three-dimensional questions are being attempted without redrawing the triangle, or that answers are being given as decimals where exact form was demanded. Those are the observations that change a grade and they come from familiarity with the instrument.

And it cannot advise on tier, because that requires knowing the grade ranges, the Extended-only content and what the school is likely to be seeing in its internal data. Tier is the highest-stakes decision in IGCSE and it is fixed at an entry deadline months before the papers. A family paying at the bottom of the market and expecting tier advice is expecting something that is not in the product, and will usually not be told so.

sections.heading: How many subjects can a budget actually support?
paragraphs: This is the decision that determines whether money produces anything, and the arithmetic is more rigid than families expect. Tuition does not work through the lesson. It works through the marked written practice done between lessons, and that practice has to fit into a student's existing week alongside school homework in eight or nine subjects and the mandatory UAE subjects.

Run the numbers. A student has perhaps five or six usable weekday evenings' worth of study capacity, most of which is already committed to school work. One tuition subject adds perhaps two hours of practice a week, which fits. Two subjects add four, which is tight and workable in an examination year. Three add six, at which point either the school's own homework suffers or the tuition practice does, and in practice it is the tuition practice because nobody checks it. By four subjects the lessons continue and the practice has stopped entirely.

What that produces is an expensive illusion. The lessons happen, the tutors are competent, the student attends, and nothing consolidates, because consolidation happens in the practice rather than in the hour. The family then concludes that tutoring does not work, which is a reasonable conclusion from their evidence and the wrong general one. The failure was the allocation, not the teaching.

The table lays the arithmetic out, including the two rows that matter most: one subject plus a free intervention class, which is often the best value configuration available, and the row where the honest answer is to spend nothing and use the free options. A provider willing to put those rows in a table is giving you something you can act on; a provider recommending four subjects on a first phone call has told you how they make decisions about somebody else's money.

sections.heading: Group class economics: why it is cheap and when it works
paragraphs: A group class at a tuition centre is the cheapest paid option per student, and the reason is simple division: one teacher's hour across a room of students. That is a genuine efficiency rather than a trick, and it means a group class can deliver teaching at a fraction of the one-to-one price. What division cannot produce is individual attention, and the question is whether your child's fault needs it.

The faults a group class can genuinely repair are the ones that are purely about content being unknown. If nobody has shown a student how frequency density works, a competent teacher showing a room how frequency density works fixes it for everyone present, including your child. Several of the highest-yield IGCSE repairs fall into this category, which is why a group class is not automatically poor value.

The faults it cannot repair are those requiring individually marked practice. Weak algebraic fluency needs dozens of short exercises with errors identified one at a time, and a teacher with fifteen students cannot provide that. Nor can a group class diagnose: a room is taught a scheme of work pitched at a typical candidate, and your child's particular pattern of lost marks is invisible within it. And a student who will not ask a question in front of peers gets an hour of watching others learn, which is the worst value in this entire market regardless of price.

The table sets out the cost drivers side by side. The practical sequence for an Al Muroor family is to ask the centre which syllabus code the class is pitched at, because a generic IGCSE class usually targets the most common specification and not necessarily your child's, and to ask whether written work is marked individually. If the answers are vague on both, you are buying content delivery rather than tuition, which is fine as long as content delivery is what you need.

sections.heading: The Year 9 discount nobody advertises
paragraphs: There is a genuine discount available in this market and it is not a price promotion. It is timing. The same money spent in Year 9 or early Year 10 buys substantially more than it does in the final term of Year 11, and the reason is mechanical rather than motivational.

Algebraic fluency, terminology volume and written-answer habits are all built by short frequent practice over months. In Year 9 a student has the weekly capacity for that practice, because they are not simultaneously revising eight subjects for a terminal series. A term of weekly work at that point can change the tier a school enters a student for, and the tier sets the grade ceiling for two years. No amount of spending in Year 11 recovers a capped entry, because the entry is an administrative fact submitted months before the papers.

Set against that, spending in the final term buys examination technique: command-term discipline, rounding accuracy, timing, question selection, and the specific requirements of each paper. Those are real marks and frequently a double-digit swing on a paper where the content is known. They are also, in cost terms, a smaller and better-defined purchase: a bounded block rather than a term. So both ends of the course have a sensible spend attached; it is the middle, buying a vague weekly arrangement in Year 11 term one for a problem nobody has diagnosed, that wastes the most.

The practical instruction for an Al Muroor parent with a Year 9 child is to ask the school two questions now: which tier the department currently expects to enter your child for, and when the final entry is submitted. Those two answers define what is still changeable and for how long. They cost nothing and no tutoring page can substitute for them.

sections.heading: Sharing a tutor: pairs, siblings and what breaks
paragraphs: Families often ask whether two students can share a tutor to halve the cost, and the honest answer is that it works in narrow conditions and fails outside them. It is worth setting out both, because a provider that sells pairs indiscriminately is selling a saving that will not materialise.

It works when two students are on the same syllabus code at the same tier, at broadly similar standing, with similar faults, and when both are comfortable working in front of each other. Two Extended 0580 students losing marks to the same procedural errors can be taught together efficiently, with written work still set and marked individually, which is the condition that keeps it real tuition rather than a small class.

It fails in several predictable ways. Different codes or tiers make the teaching diverge immediately, and one student receives content their paper will not test. A significant gap in standing means the pace suits one and loses the other, which is the group-class problem reproduced at a higher price per student. And a reticent student paired with a confident one often says less than they would in a class of fifteen, because the exposure is sharper.

Siblings are a specific case and usually the worst one. Two children at different stages have different needs by definition, and the family dynamic in a shared lesson tends to be unhelpful in ways neither parent nor tutor can easily manage. Where a household has two children needing support, the arrangement that works is consecutive individual slots on the same evening with a different specialist each, which concentrates the disruption without diluting either match. It costs more, and we would rather say so than sell a pair that quietly serves neither child.

sections.heading: Al Muroor: a central district and a smaller loading
paragraphs: Most cost pages for this market treat geography as irrelevant. It is not, and from Al Muroor the effect runs in the family's favour relative to the outer communities, which is worth stating since the rest of this page is about spending less.

The journey component in a visiting tutor's rate depends on the round trip and the traffic risk. From a central island district those are both smaller than from Al Shamkha, Baniyas or Hydra Village, so a visiting arrangement here sits lower in the published AED 180 to 500 band than it would further out. The island's internal afternoon traffic is still real, and the Airport Road corridor in particular is slow, so the risk component does not vanish.

What does not change with geography is the choice effect. Requiring a tutor to be physically present in Al Muroor at five in the afternoon narrows the available set to those willing to make that trip at that hour, and for a scarcer specification — Cambridge 0607, Additional Mathematics 0606, a Pearson science code — the narrowed set is frequently empty. A family facing an empty set substitutes a generalist, and a generalist at specialist prices is the worst transaction in this market.

So the honest summary for a central island household is this: the cost argument for online delivery is weaker here than it is from the mainland, and the specification argument is exactly as strong. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere in the UAE because home visiting is a service we run only in India, and from this district the case rests on matching the code rather than on saving the journey.

sections.heading: The permit, our status and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Because this page is about money, the permit position is worth stating precisely: the permit is free, so no part of a rate should be attributed to it. The UAE private tuition work permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's own service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published and press reporting states that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a specific dirham figure quoted as the penalty is invention — and a useful test of whether the rest of a provider's claims are sourced. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school.

An operation with premises needs a different permit from the emirate regulator; in Dubai that is an educational services permit for a training institute issued by KHDA. IB Gram holds none because it has no premises: it is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. Describing a tutoring service as approved by one of those bodies without a document to show is the most dangerous sentence available in this market.

On claims: we publish no star rating, review count or satisfaction statistic, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method alongside it. Every AED figure on this page is attributed and dated October 2026 and none is our price list. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind, to supply answers for live assessed tasks, or to reproduce board material, which belongs to Cambridge and Pearson and is published on their own sites. No tutor can promise a grade or a grade improvement, and any provider offering one should be treated with real scepticism.

whyPoints.title: We describe the cheap option fairly
whyPoints.description: Budget tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour buys company and routine, which some students genuinely need. What it cannot do is mark against a scheme or diagnose at specification level, and we say which rather than dismissing it.

whyPoints.title: The subject arithmetic is published

whyPoints.title: The timing discount explained
whyPoints.description: The same money buys more in Year 9 than in the final term of Year 11, because fluency needs months of practice capacity that an examination year does not contain. That is the only real discount in this market.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest IGCSE tuition available in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Budget online tutoring and university-student tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour on published rate cards read in October 2026, and a tuition centre group class costs less again per student because one teacher's hour is divided across a room. Cheaper still, and genuinely effective for some faults, is the school's own intervention class, which is usually free and taught by somebody who knows the specification and has seen your child's work.

faqs.question: What does a budget tutor not do for an Al Muroor student?
faqs.answer: Two things, both structural rather than a matter of effort. They cannot mark written work against a published mark scheme, because nobody at that price is paid for time outside the lesson, and marking is the mechanism by which lost marks become visible and stop recurring. And they cannot diagnose at specification level, because that requires having taught the exact code and read its mark schemes. They also cannot advise on tier, which is the highest-stakes IGCSE decision.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we fund for one child?
faqs.answer: One, then review. A student has perhaps two hours a week of spare practice capacity once school homework and the mandatory UAE subjects are accounted for. One tuition subject fits that. Two is tight and defensible in an examination year if both are genuinely at risk. By three the practice thins in all of them, and by four the lessons continue while the practice has stopped entirely, which is four times the cost for less than one subject's effect.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class worth the money?
faqs.answer: For some faults, genuinely yes. A group class delivers teaching, so if nobody has shown your child how a particular rule works, a competent teacher showing the room fixes it. Several of the highest-yield IGCSE repairs are exactly that. It cannot repair weak algebraic fluency, which needs individually marked practice, and it cannot diagnose. Ask which syllabus code the class is pitched at, because a generic class targets the most common specification.

faqs.question: Can two students share an IGCSE tutor to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: It works in narrow conditions: the same syllabus code at the same tier, broadly similar standing, similar faults, and both students comfortable working in front of each other, with written work still set and marked individually. It fails when the codes or tiers differ, when there is a real gap in standing, or when one student is reticent. Siblings at different stages are the case that fails most often, and consecutive individual slots work better.

faqs.question: Why is Year 9 tuition better value than Year 11 tuition?
faqs.answer: Because fluency is built by short frequent practice over months, and a Year 9 student has the weekly capacity for it while a Year 11 student revising eight subjects does not. A term of work in Year 9 can change which tier a school enters a student for, and the tier sets the grade ceiling for two years. Spending in the final term buys examination technique, which is real and valuable and cannot recover a capped entry.

faqs.question: How much of a home tutor's rate is the journey from Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: Less than from the mainland communities, which is a genuine advantage of a central island address. Published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor. From here the round trip is shorter, so a visiting arrangement sits lower in that band, though Airport Road traffic keeps the risk component real.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes in Al Muroor?
faqs.answer: No. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and do not offer home visits in Al Muroor or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. From a central island district the cost argument for video is weaker than it is from the mainland. The specification argument is just as strong: requiring a tutor in a scarcer code such as 0607 or 0606 to also drive here at five in the afternoon often leaves nobody.

faqs.question: What is the best value thing to buy for an IGCSE science student?
faqs.answer: The practical component, which almost nobody buys because families do not realise practical skills are examined in writing. The component tests whether another person could repeat the method, whether variables and controls are identified, graph scale choice, and whether a named source of error is matched by an improvement that addresses it. Those are writing skills applied to science, and four marked attempts changes them permanently.

faqs.question: Should we pay more for a premium named tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if the fault requires it. A premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour, and that level of experience buys diagnostic judgement at the top of the grade range. If your child's problem is that frequency density was never taught, or that answers are rounded partway through, a specialist at AED 200 to 450 will fix it just as effectively. Match the rung to the fault, which is what reading the marked script tells you.

faqs.question: Does the price include VAT on tuition in the UAE?
faqs.answer: On the general tax treatment of tuition fees we state no position, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and we would rather say so than publish something unsourced. What a family should do is ask any provider directly whether a quoted figure includes VAT and get the answer in writing before committing. A provider who cannot answer clearly about their own pricing has told you something about their administration.

faqs.question: Do tutors charge more because of the UAE permit?
faqs.answer: They should not, because the permit is free. The private tuition work permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's own service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time. A tutor who tells you the permit is costly is mistaken, and anyone quoting you a specific fine for tutoring without one is inventing it.

faqs.question: What should I ask before paying anything at all?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which syllabus code and tier my child is entered for, which the school can confirm. Who marks written work between sessions and against what. What is included beyond the hour — a written diagnosis, an error log, a review date with a measure. And which subject you would refuse to take. The last answer is the most informative, because a provider who refuses nothing is not helping you ration a budget.

faqs.question: Is spending nothing ever the right answer?
faqs.answer: For a meaningful share of students, yes, at least initially. Twenty minutes a day of retrieval practice — writing an answer on an old topic without notes, then marking it against the published scheme — costs nothing and outperforms the rereading most students do. The school's own support class is free. Reading three published mark schemes with your child is free. All three should be exhausted before a household commits several thousand dirhams a year.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.closingHeading: Match the rung to the fault, and start with one subject
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-muroor.closingBody: Read the last marked script and work out which rung of the ladder your child's problem actually needs. Company and routine sits at the bottom; teaching with marked work in the middle; tier and paper judgement at the top. Then fund one subject rather than four, because a student has roughly two hours a week of spare practice capacity and the practice is where the learning happens. Try the school's free support class first. Lessons here run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, and the trial is one lesson with no card and no commitment.

intro.heading: Nine subjects, one budget
paragraphs: An IGCSE candidate in Al Mushrif typically sits between six and ten subjects, and almost nobody can fund weekly support in all of them. The useful question is therefore not what a tutor costs per hour but which subjects repay the spend, which the school will handle adequately on its own, and which can wait until a mock result tells you more. Tutoring pages rarely frame it this way because the framing leads to a smaller sale.

The market figures first, so the choosing has numbers behind it. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist tutors reach AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits across the emirate are quoted at AED 180 to 500, including travel. Monthly, Bestimate estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. Advertised packages run at around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Put the two together and the shape of a sensible Al Mushrif budget emerges. One or two subjects funded properly, at the mid-market band, for a defined block, beats four subjects funded thinly at the budget band. Thin support across many subjects is the commonest spending pattern we see and the least effective, because each subject gets too little attention to change anything while the total invoice looks substantial.

Which subjects to fund has an evidence-based answer rather than an intuitive one. Sit a past paper in each candidate subject, mark it against the published scheme, and fund where the gap is largest and most tractable. The subject a student complains about most is frequently not the one losing the most marks, because complaint tracks discomfort. Mathematics and chemistry tend to repay support disproportionately, for structural reasons set out below. Subjects that are mostly content recall often do not, because the fix is a revision method rather than a teacher.

On delivery we are explicit. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. In an inland villa district that removes a cross-island drive from the price and from the cancellation risk, and it widens the pool from whoever will travel to Al Mushrif to everyone who prepares your child's actual syllabus code.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.programmesIntro: An Al Mushrif student arrives at the IGCSE years from one of several routes, and the route changes what is worth funding first. A child who came up through Cambridge Lower Secondary needs less early repair than one who transferred in Year 9 from a different system.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The feeder stage, with optional Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Checkpoint is diagnostic, not certificating. Support here costs the least of anything in the whole school career and prevents the most, because the algebra and scientific method introduced now are assumed without re-teaching once the IGCSE course starts.
programmes.countryNote: A weak Year 9 Checkpoint result is the cheapest warning an Al Mushrif family will receive. A term of light support then costs a fraction of a Year 11 intensive, and it preserves the Extended tier option that a weak Year 10 assessment can close.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, with Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, and typically six to ten subjects taken. The Core tier caps the achievable grade. Candidates sit a defined set of papers within one series, which makes the examination-term intensive a genuinely time-limited purchase rather than an open commitment.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher in mathematics and the sciences, graded 9 to 1. Mathematics A, code 4MA1, runs two papers of two hours weighted equally, so revision has to cover the specification evenly rather than building towards a single dominant paper.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel International GCSE series run in May/June and November. The tail is long: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The usual continuation for an Al Mushrif IGCSE student not moving into the Diploma. Subject options at this stage are constrained by IGCSE tier and grade, which is the financial reason the Year 10 tier decision deserves attention two years before it appears to matter.
programmes.countryNote: For MoE equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.subjectsIntro: The grid below is written as a funding guide rather than a syllabus list: what each subject demands, and what it costs a family to leave it unsupported when it genuinely needs help.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject that most reliably repays support, because its losses are process rather than knowledge: premature rounding, method not shown, histograms with unequal class widths. All are fixable in weeks, and all are invisible to a student working alone from a textbook.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Second on the funding priority list. Moles calculations and ionic equations carry mark weight out of proportion to their teaching time, so a gap there costs more than it appears to. Qualitative analysis questions need observation and inference stated separately.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Electricity and waves concentrate the losses, usually through confusion between series and parallel reasoning. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards knowing how apparatus is arranged, which a student cannot acquire from theory notes and which a tutor can supply quickly.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Large content volume, which makes it look like the obvious subject to fund and often means the opposite. The real gap is usually command-term discipline and graph interpretation, which a few targeted sessions address better than a standing weekly arrangement.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Repays support when the problem is structure rather than vocabulary, which it usually is. A student who narrates a text instead of analysing how it produces an effect can be a strong writer and still sit mid-range for two years. That habit takes weeks to undo.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, directed writing and, in 0511, speaking. Summary tasks lose marks for lifting sentences rather than condensing, and writing tasks lose marks for ignoring the stated audience. Both are technique, which makes a short block effective and a long arrangement unnecessary.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Application-heavy case-study subjects where a defined term earns one mark and applying it earns the rest. Evaluation questions separate the grades. Worth funding late rather than early, because the technique is learnable in a short window close to the series.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: 0478 requires pseudocode and trace tables in a prescribed notation, so students who can code still lose marks for ignoring the convention. 0417 is assessed on documents produced to a specification, where accuracy against the brief matters more than flair.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger Year 11 candidates preparing for A Level or the Diploma. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive earlier than expected, and the gap between an Extended grade 8 and comfort here is genuine, which makes a short bridging block good value.

subjects.name: History and Geography (Cambridge 0470 / 0460)
subjects.description: Source-handling and structured extended writing rather than recall. Rarely the first subject to fund, because the fix is usually an essay plan taught once and practised independently, which is a short intervention rather than a term of weekly sessions.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE year of support actually costs, by scenario
paragraphs: Hourly rates do not help a family decide. Scenarios do. Take four realistic Al Mushrif patterns and cost each against the published market bands, and the choice between them becomes a decision rather than a guess.

The first scenario is one subject, one weekly session, mid-market, through an academic year. On Bestimate's monthly estimates that sits around AED 600 to 1,200 a month. The second is two subjects weekly, which roughly doubles it. The third is four subjects at the budget band, which looks cheaper per hour and frequently costs as much as two subjects done properly while achieving less, because budget-band support is generally homework help rather than mark-scheme teaching. The fourth is nothing until January, then a single-subject intensive at two or three sessions a week for eight weeks at the specialist band.

Scenario four is the one most families actually buy, and it is worth seeing plainly. It costs more per week than any other option, it arrives after tier decisions are made, and it cannot close content gaps that span two years. It works when the problem is genuinely technique, which it sometimes is. It fails when the problem is content, which parents usually discover in week three of the intensive.

The pattern that gives most Al Mushrif families the best outcome per dirham is unglamorous: one subject, mid-market band, starting in the autumn of Year 10 or early Year 11, reviewed at eight sessions, stopped when the gap closes, and then a short pre-series intensive in the one subject that still needs it. It spreads the cost, catches the tier decision while it is still open, and ends.

sections.heading: Which of nine subjects to actually fund
paragraphs: The instinct is to fund the subject the student complains about, and the instinct is usually wrong. Complaint tracks discomfort rather than lost marks, and the two diverge more often than not. A student who finds history tedious may be scoring solidly in it, while quietly dropping a grade in chemistry because moles calculations were never consolidated and nobody noticed.

The structural guide, before any diagnosis, is to prioritise subjects where marks are lost to process and convention rather than to knowledge, because those are the fastest and cheapest to repair. Mathematics tops that list: rounding discipline, method marks, histogram technique and bearing conventions are all mechanical and all worth multiple grades in aggregate. Chemistry is second, because moles and ionic equations carry disproportionate mark weight. Physics follows, because the alternative-to-practical paper assumes apparatus familiarity that theory revision cannot supply.

Subjects that are mostly content recall sit lower on the funding list, not because they matter less but because the fix is a revision method rather than a teacher. A student who rereads notes will plateau in biology or geography no matter who is sitting opposite them, and the intervention that works is retrieval practice under timed conditions, which can be taught once in a single session and then applied independently.

Then run the actual diagnosis. Sit a past paper in the two or three candidate subjects, mark each against the published mark scheme, and sort the lost marks by cause rather than topic. In most cases the result reorders the family's priority list immediately, and in several it shows that one subject needs a term of support while another needs a single session on examination technique.

sections.heading: Cost per useful minute: one-to-one, group class and tuition centre
paragraphs: Hourly rate is the wrong unit for comparing formats, because the formats deliver different amounts of relevant teaching inside the hour. Cost per useful minute is the honest measure, and it reverses several intuitions about what is expensive.

In a one-to-one session every minute is aimed at your child's specific gaps, so the useful fraction approaches the whole hour. In a group of eight working through a general revision programme, the fraction spent on your child's particular weakness might be a small part of the session, which is why a group class at a third of the price can cost more per useful minute than one-to-one for a student with a narrow, diagnosed gap. For broad revision across a whole cohort shortly before a series, the arithmetic flips entirely and the group is excellent value.

A tuition centre adds a journey at both ends and a fixed timetable, and in return offers a working environment away from home, which for some students is the deciding factor. Note that a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued for a training institute, with initial approval first and a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps. That is a specific licence attached to a physical centre, and no online service holds or should imply it. IB Gram does not.

The in-home visit is the most expensive per useful minute, because the published premium over an online qualified tutor funds travel rather than teaching and because soft session edges, late starts and traffic cancellations reduce the delivered hours. In an inland district like Al Mushrif, where a tutor is crossing the island at the worst hour, that reduction is not hypothetical.

sections.heading: Official material: what it costs, and what we will not supply
paragraphs: A surprising share of an IGCSE budget goes on paper. Revision guides, workbooks, question banks, app subscriptions and printed past papers accumulate quickly, and a meaningful proportion of it is bought for the wrong syllabus. Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are three different examinations, and a workbook written for one contains question styles that do not appear in another. Checking the code on the entry confirmation before buying anything is the cheapest saving on this page.

The syllabus document itself is free and published by the board, and it is the single most useful thing a parent can read. It lists exactly what is examined, in what paper, with what weighting. Most families never open it, and most of the anxiety in a Year 11 household is reducible by ten minutes with the right one. Past papers and mark schemes are also published through the boards' own channels and through schools' examinations officers.

What we will not do is reproduce or supply that material. We do not publish or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as downloads. We reference them and link to the official source. Reproducing them is copyright infringement, and for unreleased material it is a malpractice exposure that would land on the student rather than on us. Any tutoring service offering a library of papers it has no right to distribute is telling you something about how it treats other rules.

The practical consequence is that a tutor's value is not access to material, since the material is largely free. It is knowing which questions to set, how to mark them against the scheme, and what the resulting pattern of lost marks means. That is the thing worth paying for, and it is the thing a question bank cannot provide.

sections.heading: The tier decision, priced
paragraphs: Core or Extended at Cambridge, Foundation or Higher at Edexcel, is the single most consequential decision in an IGCSE year, and it is usually made without any marked evidence. The lower tier caps the achievable grade: a student can answer every question on a Core paper correctly and still not reach the grades an Extended entry makes available. That cap is structural rather than a reflection of performance on the day.

The cost of getting it wrong runs in both directions and is asymmetric. Entering a student for Extended who cannot access the harder material produces a worse result than a secure Core grade, plus a year of unnecessary distress. Entering a capable student for Core closes post-16 options they will want in two years, and reopening them means retaking a subject, which costs a year rather than a term.

What makes the decision cheap to get right is that evidence is available for the price of two or three sessions. Set questions from both tiers, mark them against the published mark scheme, and look at what the scripts show. A student who handles Extended-style algebra but collapses on the longer structured questions has a stamina and technique problem, fixable in a term. A student who cannot access the Extended material at all is correctly placed, and pushing them is unkind rather than ambitious. The entry decision belongs to the school, which holds it; what a family can bring is marked scripts rather than an opinion.

The timing matters financially. Schools generally make tier decisions in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments. A diagnostic bought in Year 10 influences a decision that is still open. The same diagnostic bought in February of Year 11 informs a decision already made, which is the most common way families pay for information too late to use.

sections.heading: Charges with no basis, and the free things families pay for
paragraphs: Three things routinely get charged for in this market that should not be, and knowing them saves money immediately. The first is the tutor's permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. If anyone asks a family to cover their licensing cost, the request has no basis. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, and applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service.

The second is a fine. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published. Figures circulate in parent groups and on websites, and none of them could be verified. Treat any specific amount quoted to you as unsourced, including amounts quoted confidently.

The third is school support that is already included in fees. Most schools in the emirate run after-school clinics, departmental help or targeted intervention at no additional cost, and a parent who asks the head of department about a specific topic rather than a general worry often gets either a useful answer or the problem solved. Exhausting that before buying anything is simply sensible sequencing.

A related caution concerns what cannot be bought at any price. Press reporting indicates ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct with a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it, and do not pursue your child's own class teacher. An independent tutor also gives you an unconflicted second reading of how your child is actually doing.

sections.heading: Five subjects count: the equivalency arithmetic nobody explains
paragraphs: This matters financially because a family can spend two years funding subjects that do not count towards the thing they assume they are working for. The Ministry of Education's equivalency requirements for the British track have been publicly clarified: students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that reorders a budget is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student taking five subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, has three that count towards equivalency. One ranking competitor page states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published clarification. Getting this right is a small thing that beats a ranking page on factual accuracy.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold appears in that source, and no figure should be taken from any tutoring website including this one. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly.

Two cautions that belong on every page touching this subject. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs; it is not something a tutoring service performs, accelerates or guarantees, and we describe it rather than offering it. And tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression. Any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process, which is both a trust failure and, in this market, a commercial representation worth being careful about.
