sections.heading: When to stop paying, and how to tell
paragraphs: Every tutoring arrangement should have an end, and most do not because nobody set one. The weekly session that began in October to fix a specific gap is often still running in May, having solved the problem in January. Four months of sessions after that were a habit, and in an eight-subject household with two subjects funded, that is a significant sum spent on reassurance.

The mechanism that prevents it is a measure agreed at the start. A timed paper in session one, marked against the published mark scheme, with lost marks sorted by cause rather than topic. The same style of paper at session eight. If the causes have gone, the work is done and the sessions should stop. If they have halved, continuing is justified. If nothing has moved, either the plan targeted the wrong gap or the match is wrong, and both are the provider's problem to solve rather than the student's to absorb.

There is a second stopping signal worth naming: when the student starts answering the tutor's diagnostic questions before they are finished. That is the point at which the gap has closed and the session has become supervised practice, which a student can do alone for nothing. A tutor who notices and says so is worth more than one who does not, and families should treat an unprompted recommendation to stop as the strongest possible signal of good faith.

The opposite case deserves honesty too. Some students need support through to the series because the subject is genuinely hard for them and the sessions are the thing holding the week together. That is a legitimate reason to continue, and it should be a stated decision rather than a default. The test is whether a parent can say, in one sentence, what the next eight sessions are for.
bullets: Set the measure before session one: a timed paper marked to the scheme
Review at session eight, counting sessions rather than calendar weeks
Stop when the causes of lost marks have gone, not when the term ends
Treat an unprompted recommendation to stop as a good sign
If you cannot say what the next eight sessions are for, do not buy them

process.title: List the subjects and the actual grades
process.description: All of them, with the most recent assessment result and the board and code for each. The list is what makes the funding conversation possible, because the decision in an Al Mushrif household is never whether to buy support but which two subjects to buy it for.

process.title: Diagnose the two candidates, not all nine
process.description: Sit a past paper in the two subjects that look weakest, mark both against the published scheme, and sort the lost marks by cause. This routinely reorders a family's priority list, and it often shows that one subject needs a term while the other needs a single technique session.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session at no cost and with no card required, built around the diagnostic rather than an introduction. You get the written read; the student judges the explanation. If the match is wrong we rematch, which costs nothing in week one and costs a term in week six.

process.title: Fund one subject properly
process.description: One weekly session at the band the diagnosis actually calls for, with the number of sessions and the skipped weeks agreed in advance. One subject funded properly beats four funded thinly, which is the commonest pattern and the least effective one.

process.title: Review at eight sessions and stop when done
process.description: Repeat the paper, compare the causes, and choose: continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. We will recommend stopping when the gap has closed, because an arrangement that outlives its purpose is the most expensive thing in this market.

whyPoints.title: We help you choose which subjects not to fund
whyPoints.description: A nine-subject load and one budget is a selection problem, and the selection should come from marked papers rather than from which subject your child complains about. Complaint tracks discomfort; marked scripts track lost marks, and the two diverge more often than not.

whyPoints.title: Cost per useful minute, not per hour
whyPoints.description: A group class at a third of the price can cost more per useful minute than one-to-one when the gap is narrow, and considerably less when the need is cohort-wide revision. We will say which situation you are in rather than defaulting to the format that bills most.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online, and in an inland district the gap is a cross-island drive at the worst hour.

whyPoints.title: Official material referenced, never redistributed
whyPoints.description: We link to the boards' own syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes and do not reproduce them. The syllabus is free and is the most useful thing a parent can read, and a service distributing material it has no right to is telling you how it treats other rules.

whyPoints.title: The free things named as free
whyPoints.description: The MoHRE private tuition work permit costs nothing and lasts two years. School clinics are already covered by fees. No fine schedule is published, so no amount quoted to you is sourced. None of that generates revenue for us, which is rather the point of saying it.

whyPoints.title: No claimed status, anywhere
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. A tuition centre with premises in Dubai needs its own KHDA permit; an online service is a different thing and should not imply otherwise.

faqs.question: We cannot fund nine subjects. Which two should we choose?
faqs.answer: Choose by marked paper rather than by instinct. Structurally, mathematics repays support fastest because its losses are process rather than knowledge: rounding, method marks, histogram technique and bearing conventions, all mechanical and all worth grades in aggregate. Chemistry is usually second, because moles calculations and ionic equations carry mark weight out of proportion to teaching time. Then sit a past paper in your two candidates, mark each against the published scheme, and sort lost marks by cause. The list frequently reorders itself.

faqs.question: Is four subjects at the budget rate better than two done properly?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Budget-band support, advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, is generally homework help rather than mark-scheme teaching, and spread across four subjects each one gets too little attention to change anything. Two subjects at the qualified band, AED 150 to 300, frequently costs a similar total and produces a different result. The thin-across-many pattern is the most common spending shape we see in Al Mushrif and the least effective one.

faqs.question: Does a group revision class work out cheaper per useful minute?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the gap is broad or narrow. For cohort-wide revision shortly before a series, a group class is excellent value and the arithmetic favours it heavily. For one diagnosed topic, such as histograms with unequal class widths, a shared pace gives that topic a few minutes of an hour, so the cheaper class can cost more per useful minute than one-to-one. Diagnose first with a marked paper, then choose the format. Buying the cheaper option for the wrong problem is not a saving.

faqs.question: How much should we spend on revision guides and question banks?
faqs.answer: Less than most families do, and never before checking the syllabus code. Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Edexcel 4MA1 are different examinations, and a workbook written for one contains question styles absent from another. The syllabus document itself is free from the board and is the most useful thing a parent can read, because it states exactly what is examined in which paper at what weighting. Past papers and mark schemes come through the board's own channels and your school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: Will you send us a bank of past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. We reference and link to the boards' own published material and do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. Redistributing them is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure that would land on the student. A tutor's value is not access to material that is largely free anyway; it is knowing which questions to set, how to mark them against the scheme, and what the pattern of losses means.

faqs.question: Should we pay towards a tutor's UAE licensing costs?
faqs.answer: No, because there are none to pay. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students, applying through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Any request to cover a licensing cost has no basis. Ask whether the permit is current, then ask the questions that actually test competence.

faqs.question: A tutor quoted us a specific fine for tutoring without a permit. Is that figure real?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unsourced. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule is published anywhere official. Amounts circulate in parent groups and on tutoring websites, and none of them could be verified against a government source. A provider quoting a confident figure is either repeating a rumour or using it as pressure, and neither is a good sign about the rest of their claims.

faqs.question: Our daughter takes five subjects including Arabic and Islamic education. Is that enough?
faqs.answer: Not for the Ministry of Education's equivalency count on the British track. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Five subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, leaves three that count. One ranking competitor page states six subjects are required, which does not match the published clarification. Verify your own case through the official channel rather than any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can a tutoring service sort out our equivalency paperwork?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be cautious of any that offers to. Equivalency is a process the Ministry of Education and the attestation authority run; we can describe the published requirements and point you to the official channel, and that is the limit of a tutoring service's legitimate role. Tutoring is also not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, so any page implying that private lessons are necessary for a regulatory outcome is manufacturing urgency.

faqs.question: When should we diagnose the tier question to make it useful?
faqs.answer: In Year 10, while the decision is still open. Schools generally confirm Core or Extended, or Foundation or Higher, in Year 10 or early Year 11 on the evidence of internal assessments. Two or three sessions of questions from both tiers, marked against the published scheme, gives you scripts to take to the school while it can still act on them. The same diagnostic bought in February of Year 11 informs a decision already made, which is information purchased too late to use.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for a subject?
faqs.answer: When the causes of lost marks identified at the start have gone. That requires setting a measure before session one: a timed paper marked against the published mark scheme, with losses sorted by cause rather than topic, repeated at session eight. If the causes have cleared, the work is done. A second signal is when your child starts answering the tutor's diagnostic questions before they finish asking, which means the session has become supervised practice they could do alone for nothing.

faqs.question: Why count sessions instead of weeks for a block in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Because the calendar removes teaching time from every twelve-week plan. Ramadan changes the usable evening hour, Eid removes days, the winter break removes weeks, and examination season makes new content pointless. A block billed across twelve calendar weeks that delivers eight teaching sessions is the quietest disappointment in this market. Agreeing the number of sessions and which weeks will be skipped keeps the review honest, because both sides then compare the same quantity of teaching.

faqs.question: Does anybody come to Al Mushrif if we pay the in-home premium?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram, at any price. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Sessions run one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. The practical gain in an inland villa district is reliability: an online slot has hard edges, while a visit depends on crossing the island at the worst hour, and the third cancellation is usually where a family loses the week's rhythm.

faqs.question: Can we try the school's own support before spending anything?
faqs.answer: You should, and it costs nothing. Most schools in the emirate run after-school clinics, departmental help or targeted intervention already covered by fees. Ask the head of department about the specific topic rather than the general worry, and ask what the last assessment was marked against and which marks were lost. If the answer is detailed, the school may solve it. A tutor earns its place where the gap needs individual time, where the problem is technique, or where confidence has gone.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.closingHeading: Send the subject list and the last set of grades
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-mushrif.closingBody: An IGCSE home tutor decision in Al Mushrif is a selection problem, so the most useful thing you can send is the whole subject list with the most recent result for each and the board and code alongside. From that we can suggest which two subjects to diagnose, and a marked paper will tell you which one actually repays funding. The first lesson is a free trial with no card required, built around that diagnostic. Lessons run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and every rate quoted on this page names its source.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.tutorsIntro: These tutors prepare Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE candidates in Years 10 and 11. Each profile names the board and subjects covered, so an Al Nahyan family can compare the match against the school's entry paperwork before paying anything.

intro.heading: The comparisons an IGCSE household actually needs
paragraphs: Al Nahyan sits inland on Abu Dhabi island, east of Al Karamah, a mix of villas and low-rise blocks with Airport Road along one side and schools in most directions. Families here looking for IGCSE support face a decision made harder by the fact that the useful comparisons are never set out anywhere. The ones that are set out, provider against unnamed provider, help nobody, and they are deliberately framed so that only one answer survives them.

Start with the one that matters most. A Year 11 candidate typically sits eight or nine subjects, and the grades do not come from them evenly. Mathematics and the sciences concentrate their marks in places where a specific habit decides the outcome: a rounding convention, an ionic equation, a frequency density calculation. The content-heavy subjects concentrate theirs in whether the student revises by retrieval or by rereading. English concentrates its in a single habit, analysing rather than narrating, which takes months to change. One budget across eight subjects should follow that distribution rather than the student's sense of which subject feels worst.

The second comparison is between the boards, and it is almost always discussed only in terms of mathematics. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel differ in the sciences too, in how practical understanding is assessed, and in English, in how the papers are structured. A tutor who prepares Cambridge 0625 Physics is not automatically ready for Edexcel 4PH1, and a workbook bought for one contains question styles absent from the other. The codes are on the entry confirmation and they settle it.

The third is between what a parent sees and what an examiner sees. A parent sees a grade and a comment. An examiner saw a script in which marks were lost to specific, nameable causes, most of which have nothing to do with how much the student knows. That gap is where most tutoring money is wasted, because a family buys against the grade when they should be buying against the script. The practical move is to ask the school for the mock script itself rather than the grade summary. A marked paper read side by side with the mark scheme names the causes in half an hour, and that list is what a tutor should be briefed from.

The fourth comparison is between what is widely believed about UAE examinations and what the sources actually say, and the gap there is wide enough to change decisions. On delivery we are straightforward: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which removes the published AED 180 to 500 in-home band from the conversation in favour of the AED 150 to 300 band for qualified online subject tutors.
bullets: Grades do not come from eight subjects evenly; fund according to the distribution
The boards differ in the sciences and English, not only in mathematics
Buy against the marked script, not against the grade on the front of it
Several widely repeated beliefs about UAE examinations are wrong
Delivery is online one-to-one; no UAE home visits

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.programmesIntro: An Al Nahyan household may be comparing two or three routes at once, either across siblings or in planning what comes after Year 11. The programmes below are the ones genuinely in play in this part of Abu Dhabi.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1 with Core and Extended tiers in many subjects, and typically six to ten subjects taken. Compared with continuous-assessment systems, everything resolves in a single terminal series, which rewards revision technique as much as it rewards knowing the content.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered Foundation and Higher in mathematics and the sciences, graded 9 to 1, with some subjects available modularly. Compared with Cambridge the differences are structural rather than in difficulty: different codes, different paper splits, and practical understanding distributed differently across the papers.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel International GCSE series run in May/June and November. As backward-looking illustrations of the tail: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The feeder stage, with optional Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which are diagnostic rather than certificating. Compared with the IGCSE years nothing here counts towards a certificate, which is precisely why acting on a weak result is so inexpensive.
programmes.countryNote: A Year 9 Checkpoint weakness preserves every option, including the Extended tier. The same weakness surfacing in a Year 11 mock has already influenced a tier entry that caps the achievable grade.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The common continuation for an Al Nahyan student not moving into the IB Diploma. Compared with the IGCSE years, the pace assumes prior content is automatic and does not revisit foundations, which is why a summer bridging block is worth more than a term of catch-up.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.subjectsIntro: The grid below describes each subject by where its grade actually comes from, which is the comparison a family with one budget and eight subjects needs rather than a list of topics.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The grade comes from habits more than knowledge: rounding carried through a chain, method shown where marks are awarded for it, histogram frequency density, bearings to three figures. All diagnosable in one script and changeable in a fortnight, which is why it repays support most.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The grade comes from electricity reasoning, unit discipline and familiarity with how apparatus is arranged. The last of those is built over two years of laboratory work in school, which means late revision alone cannot reach part of the paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The grade comes disproportionately from moles calculations and ionic equations, which carry mark weight well out of proportion to their teaching time, plus qualitative analysis questions needing the observation and the inference stated separately.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The grade comes from command-term precision and graph interpretation rather than from content volume, despite the volume being what students fear. Transport in plants, genetics crosses and enzyme graphs concentrate the available marks.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: The grade comes from one habit: analysing how a writer achieves an effect rather than narrating what happens. A strong writer can sit mid-range for two years on that alone, and changing it takes months rather than weeks.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The grade comes from task compliance: condensing rather than lifting in summary work, and writing to the stated audience and purpose. Both are technique, which makes a short block effective and a long arrangement unnecessary.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: The grade comes from application and evaluation. A defined term earns a mark; applying it to the business in the stem earns the rest; weighing rather than restating earns the top band. Responds well to a short block close to the series.

subjects.name: History and Geography (Cambridge 0470 / 0460)
subjects.description: The grade comes from source handling and essay structure. One session on a workable plan, then independent practice, usually achieves more than a term of weekly sessions, which makes these poor candidates for the main budget.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: The grade comes from following a prescribed notation in 0478, where students who can code lose marks on pseudocode and trace tables, and from accuracy against a specification in 0417, where meeting the brief matters more than flair.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: The grade comes from comfort with calculus and trigonometric identities arriving earlier than expected. The gap between an Extended grade 8 and comfort here is real, which makes a short bridging block before the course good value.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-nahyan.regionsIntro: The districts below are the ones Al Nahyan families compare themselves with, and the comparison that matters is which boards the local schools enter rather than which amenities each district has.

regions.name: Al Mushrif
regions.note: South-west and villa-heavy, with long-established British-curriculum campuses. Families here and in Al Nahyan hit the same tier decisions in Year 10 and the same mock pressure in January.

regions.name: Al Khalidiyah

regions.name: Al Zahiyah

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Over the bridge east, newer and growing. Several Al Nahyan families school there, which puts two bridge crossings into the day before any tutoring is arranged.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: On the mainland, with large-scale Cambridge and Indian-curriculum provision. An Al Nahyan child schooled out here loses a substantial part of the afternoon to the bus in each direction.

regions.name: Khalifa City

sections.heading: Eight subjects compared: where the grade actually comes from
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in Al Nahyan sits eight or nine subjects and no household funds eight weekly sessions, so the useful question is where each subject's grade actually comes from. The answer differs enough between subjects to reorder most families' priority list.

In mathematics and chemistry the grade comes substantially from narrow, mechanical things. Rounding carried correctly through a chain of calculation. Method written down where the mark scheme awards it separately from the answer. Frequency density applied to a histogram with unequal class widths. Moles calculations and ionic equations, which between them carry far more marks than their share of teaching time. Each of those is visible in one marked script and changeable within a fortnight, which is why these subjects repay one-to-one support most reliably.

In the content-heavy subjects the grade comes from revision method. A student who rereads notes generates a strong feeling of familiarity and very little recall, which is why hard-working candidates plateau in biology, history or geography for a year and conclude they are weak at the subject. The intervention that works is retrieval practice under timed conditions, and it can be taught in a single session and then applied alone. Buying a weekly session for those subjects is paying a teacher to supervise work the student could do unsupervised.

English sits on its own. The grade comes from one habit, analysing how a text produces an effect rather than narrating what it says, and that habit takes months to shift. It is therefore worth funding early in Year 10 or not at all, because a six-week intensive in April cannot change a way of writing built over years. Business Studies and Economics are the opposite case: evaluation technique is learnable in a defined window close to the papers, which makes them a sensible late purchase.

sections.heading: The boards compared on the sciences and English, not just mathematics
paragraphs: Every comparison of Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel starts and usually finishes with mathematics, which leaves an Al Nahyan family unprepared for the differences that affect the other six subjects. The sciences are where the practical consequences are largest.

Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical option across its sciences, and the questions there assume a candidate knows how apparatus is actually arranged: which piece of equipment measures what, where a reading is taken from, what a sensible precaution looks like. A student who has studied theory diligently and spent little time in a laboratory is exposed by exactly those questions. Edexcel distributes practical understanding differently across its papers. Neither approach is harder; they require different preparation, and a tutor who prepares one and assumes the other covers the science and misses the assessment.

In English the structures differ too. Cambridge 0500 First Language runs reading comprehension, directed writing and composition, while 0510 and 0511 as Second Language courses have their own task types, with a speaking component in 0511 that the school schedules separately. A tutor's familiarity with the task types matters more than their command of English, because the marks follow task compliance: condensing rather than lifting, writing to the stated audience, meeting the specified purpose.

The practical consequence is a single sentence: ask the school for the syllabus code subject by subject rather than once. Schools in this part of Abu Dhabi sometimes enter candidates with different boards across subjects, and an answer about mathematics tells you nothing about physics. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole researched Abu Dhabi competitor cluster, which is a reasonable measure of how rarely anyone asks.

sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper compared with real laboratory work
paragraphs: This deserves a section of its own because it is the one part of the IGCSE sciences that no amount of online tutoring can fully supply, and an honest page should say so rather than imply otherwise.

Cambridge's alternative-to-practical papers test understanding of experimental method rather than manual dexterity. Questions ask which instrument to use, how to read it, what the sources of error are, how to improve a procedure, how to interpret results from an experiment the candidate did not perform. Those are intellectual skills and they are teachable in discussion. What makes them land, though, is having stood at a bench, set up the apparatus and watched it behave imperfectly. A student who has done the practical programme recognises the question; one who has only read about it reconstructs it from theory and loses marks on the details.

The school owns that programme, and nothing replaces it. A tutor's legitimate role is to make sure the student can describe, explain and evaluate what happened in the laboratory in the language the mark scheme rewards, which is a surprisingly common gap: students who performed an experiment competently frequently cannot write about it in the terms required. That work is well suited to one-to-one teaching, and it is the honest limit of what we can offer on the practical side.

Two practical recommendations follow. First, ask the school whether the practical programme is complete and which experiments remain, because the alternative-to-practical paper draws on the whole range. Second, if your child has missed laboratory sessions through absence, raise it with the department rather than trying to cover it with tutoring, because the gap is experiential rather than informational. We will say that rather than sell sessions against it.

sections.heading: What a parent sees compared with what the examiner saw
paragraphs: This is the comparison that determines whether tutoring money is spent well, and almost nobody makes it explicitly. A parent sees a grade, a percentage and a sentence of comment. An examiner saw a script in which every lost mark had a cause, and most of those causes were not about how much the student knew.

Consider a typical mathematics mock. The parent sees a 5 and a note saying more practice is needed. The examiner saw: two accuracy marks lost to rounding at an intermediate step, three method marks unavailable because no working was shown, a four-mark histogram question scoring nothing because frequency density was skipped, two bearings answers rejected for not being written to three figures, and a final question left blank because the student spent eleven minutes on something worth four marks. Only one of those is a knowledge gap. The rest are process, and they are worth a substantial number of marks in aggregate.

That distinction changes the purchase. Buying against the grade produces a plan that re-teaches content the student largely has. Buying against the script produces a plan that fixes five habits, which is faster, cheaper and more reliable. It also produces a measure: the same causes either appear in the next script or they do not.

The practical step is to ask the school for the marked script, not just the grade. If scripts are not routinely returned, ask anyway. A grade without a script is a number with no instructions attached, and a tutor who begins work without seeing one is guessing at the problem exactly as the parent is. The first session with any new tutor should produce a marked script and a written list of causes rather than a plan for the term.

sections.heading: Delivery compared across a real Year 11 week
paragraphs: Comparing formats in the abstract favours whoever is selling. Comparing them against an actual Al Nahyan week, with the school run, the homework and the mandatory subjects counted in, produces a different answer.

The week has fewer usable hours than parents assume. Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, so the timetable carries more subjects than the examination entry list suggests and the homework follows. Add a sport or a music lesson and most households have one or two genuinely free evening hours, with Thursday effectively lost and Saturday morning the most reliable slot in the week.

Against that, an in-home visit consumes more of the week than its billed hour. The tutor's arrival is traffic-dependent, so the session edges are soft; the household organises itself around a visitor; and if an earlier visit overran, your hour shortens without appearing to. A tuition centre adds a journey in each direction, which from inland Al Nahyan at that time of day is not trivial, in exchange for a working environment away from home that genuinely helps some students.

An online slot consumes exactly its hour and has hard edges. What it requires is a quiet hour and a screen the student can see properly, which in a shared room means headphones and an agreement with siblings, settled once. Over a term the comparison is not close, and the reason is consistency rather than quality: tutoring works through the repetition of a reliable weekly contact, and the format that survives contact with a real week is the one that delivers it.

sections.heading: Market folklore compared with what the sources actually say
paragraphs: A surprising amount of what circulates in Abu Dhabi parent groups about IGCSE and UAE examinations turns out to be wrong when checked against an official source, and several of the errors are the kind a family acts on.

The most consequential concerns Ministry equivalency. It is widely repeated, including by a page currently ranking for these searches, that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published clarification states five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. The detail that reorders a subject plan is that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, so a student taking five subjects of which two are Arabic and Islamic education has three that count.

The second concerns the examination calendar. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only; UAE candidates sit June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. A family planning a spring resit is planning around a sitting that is not available to them. The third concerns the tutoring permit, which is widely assumed to cost money: the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. And no fine schedule for unlicensed tutoring is published, so any specific amount quoted to you is unsourced.

The fourth concerns fees and regulators. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is a Dubai measure announced by the Dubai regulator. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation here, and Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve fees through their own authorities. Reading a Dubai announcement as a UAE-wide fact is one of the commonest budgeting errors in the country.

sections.heading: What IGCSE grades are compared against afterwards
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is not an endpoint. It is an input to several later comparisons, each made by a different audience looking at a different thing, and knowing which audience cares about what changes how a family prioritises subjects.

A sixth form or post-16 provider looks at the subjects relevant to the courses applied for, usually with a specific threshold for mathematics and science routes, and at the tier entered. A Core or Foundation grade constrains options in a way that is invisible when the entry is made. The Ministry of Education's equivalency process looks at five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus the Advanced Level requirement. It does not look at which subjects beyond that count, and it does not look at the tier.

Universities, in most cases, look past IGCSE to the post-16 qualification, using the earlier grades as supporting context and occasionally as evidence of English or mathematics competence. Some competitive courses specify IGCSE grades directly. Employers, for school leavers, look at the overall profile rather than individual subjects. None of these audiences looks at the thing families worry most about, which is the gap between a 7 and an 8.

The practical conclusion is to protect the subjects that function as gateways: mathematics, English and the sciences, plus whatever a target post-16 route specifies. Beyond that, a spread of solid grades serves most purposes as well as an uneven profile with two outstanding results. That argues for funding a weak gateway subject rather than polishing a strong one, which is the opposite of what most revision timetables actually do.

sections.heading: This year's plan compared with the one you would make again
paragraphs: Families who have been through a Year 11 once describe the same set of regrets, and they are consistent enough to be worth setting out in advance for an Al Nahyan family about to start.

The first regret is starting in February. Support bought in Year 10 can still influence the tier entry, which caps the achievable grade in many subjects, and content gaps can still be closed with time to consolidate. Support bought in February works inside decisions already made and can only reach technique. Families almost universally say they would have started a year earlier and spent less in total.

The second is funding by complaint. Most families fund the subject the student finds most unpleasant, and most discover later that the marks were being lost somewhere else. The fix is the marked script: it reorders the priority list immediately, usually surprising everyone, and it takes one session rather than a term to produce.

The third is never setting a stopping point. A weekly session begun in November to fix a particular problem is frequently still running in May, having solved the problem in February. The remedy costs nothing to arrange: a measure at the start, a review at session eight, and stopping named as a legitimate outcome. The fourth and smallest regret is buying revision material before checking the syllabus code, which is a five-minute check against a shelf of unusable workbooks.

A fifth regret appears less often and costs more than any of the others: treating the mock grade as a verdict rather than as a diagnosis. Families who read a January mock as a forecast either panic and buy three subjects at once or relax and buy nothing, and both responses ignore the only useful thing in the envelope, which is the script. Asking which topics the mock covered and which have actually been taught takes one email and reframes the whole spring.

faqs.question: We can fund one subject out of eight. How do we choose?
faqs.answer: From the marked scripts rather than from which subject your child dislikes. Mathematics and chemistry usually come first, because their losses are mechanical: rounding carried wrongly, method not shown, frequency density skipped, moles calculations never consolidated. Those are visible in one script and changeable within a fortnight. Content-heavy subjects generally need a revision method taught once rather than a weekly teacher, and English needs an early start or none at all.

faqs.question: Does a Cambridge physics tutor automatically handle Edexcel physics?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 cover similar physics and assess it differently, particularly on practical understanding: Cambridge's alternative-to-practical option asks about apparatus and method directly, while Edexcel distributes that understanding across its papers. Many experienced tutors prepare both and can explain exactly how they differ. One who treats them as the same examination will teach good physics and leave gaps in examination readiness. Ask for the code, subject by subject.

faqs.question: Can online tutoring cover the practical side of the sciences?
faqs.answer: Partly, and we would rather be clear about the limit. The alternative-to-practical paper tests understanding of method rather than manual skill, and that is teachable in discussion. What makes it land is having stood at a bench and watched apparatus behave imperfectly, which only the school's practical programme provides. A tutor's proper role is ensuring your child can describe, explain and evaluate what happened in the language the mark scheme rewards, which is a common and fixable gap.

faqs.question: Is it five accredited subjects for equivalency, or six as we were told?
faqs.answer: Five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five, so a student taking five of which two are Arabic and Islamic education has three that count. One ranking competitor page states six subjects, which does not match the published clarification.

faqs.question: Why does our school say there is no February resit when another parent says there is?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The belief circulates because the series genuinely exists, just not here. Planning a resit around it means planning around a sitting unavailable to your child, and the entry deadline would pass unnoticed. Confirm against the live official timetable on the board's own website.

faqs.question: Should we be paying anything towards a tutor's UAE permit?
faqs.answer: No. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Any request to cover licensing costs has no basis. Ask whether the permit is current, then ask the questions that test competence, because a permit is a right to work rather than a statement about teaching.

faqs.question: A tutor quoted a specific fine for working without a permit. Is that figure real?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unsourced. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, but no fine schedule has been published by any official source. Amounts circulate in parent groups and on tutoring websites and none could be verified. A provider quoting a confident number is either repeating a rumour or using it as pressure, and both are useful signals about the rest of their claims.

faqs.question: Our school has a strong ADEK outcome and our son's chemistry is poor. How?
faqs.answer: Because an inspection outcome describes a school across its whole cohort rather than one class in one year. A well-regarded school can have a weak department, usually after a mid-year staff change, and chemistry shows it fastest because moles calculations and ionic equations carry mark weight out of proportion to teaching time. Ask the school what the last assessment was marked against, whether the class has had a consistent teacher, and which topics remain to be taught.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school for instead of the grade?
faqs.answer: The marked script. A parent sees a 5 and a note saying more practice is needed; the examiner saw accuracy marks lost to rounding, method marks unavailable because working was not shown, a histogram question scoring nothing on frequency density, bearings rejected for not being written to three figures, and a final question left blank after eleven minutes on a four-mark problem. Only one of those is a knowledge gap. The script tells you where to spend money.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre a reasonable alternative from Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: It can be, for one specific reason: some students work better away from home, and that is worth paying for. The costs are a journey in each direction at a bad hour from an inland district, a fixed timetable, and a class size that may not suit a narrow gap. Note that a tuition centre with premises in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to the physical centre. Ask about class size for your child's actual syllabus code before committing.

faqs.question: Does the Dubai fee announcement affect what we pay in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA regulates Dubai, and its confirmation on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year was a Dubai measure under a Dubai incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation here and handles fee matters separately, while Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve fees through their own authorities. Reading a Dubai announcement as nationwide is a common budgeting error.

faqs.question: Who actually looks at individual IGCSE grades later on?
faqs.answer: Fewer audiences than families assume. A post-16 provider looks at the subjects relevant to the courses applied for and at the tier entered. Ministry equivalency looks at five accredited subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Universities mostly look past IGCSE to the post-16 qualification, with some competitive courses specifying named grades. Protect the gateway subjects: mathematics, English, the sciences and anything a target route names.

faqs.question: Our daughter revises constantly and her biology will not move. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly the method rather than the hours. Rereading notes produces familiarity and very little recall, which is exactly why diligent students plateau in content-heavy subjects for a year and conclude they are weak at them. The alternative is retrieval under conditions: a past-paper question answered from memory, marked against the published scheme, with lost marks logged and re-tested a fortnight later. It can be taught in one session and then applied alone for nothing.

faqs.question: If we could do this year again, what would you tell us to change?
faqs.answer: Start in Year 10, while the tier entry is still open and content gaps can be closed with time to consolidate. Fund from the marked script rather than from which subject feels worst, because the two rarely match. Set a measure and a review point at session eight before the first lesson, with stopping named as a legitimate outcome. And check the syllabus code before buying any revision material, which is a five-minute check against a shelf of unusable workbooks.

intro.heading: Price the whole decision, starting at zero
paragraphs: Al Raha Beach families pay substantial school fees and then, often, add a tutoring line without pricing it against what the fees already cover. That is the first and most expensive habit worth breaking. Two of the support options available to a Year 10 or 11 student cost nothing extra: the school's own departmental catch-up and teacher clinics, and the examination boards' published syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes. For absence and for a single specific misunderstanding, the free options are not merely cheaper, they are better informed.

The second habit worth breaking is treating the hourly rate as the cost. It is not. The cost of a tutoring arrangement is the hourly rate multiplied by the hours, plus the extras nobody mentions at the start, plus the value of a term spent on the wrong thing if the match is poor. That third component does not appear on any pricing page in this market and it is frequently the largest of the three.

The published bands are these, each attributed. Entry-level online tuition runs AED 45-150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150-300, and Unitors publishes International GCSE tuition from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit with travel included runs AED 180-500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180-350 and independent home tutors quoting AED 200-500. Specialist International GCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor.

Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Package pricing in this market includes around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. None of those figures are IB Gram's prices; they are market rates published by the providers and surveys named, and they are here so that you can judge any quote you receive, including ours.

What that spread means in practice is that the same two-year course can cost a family a few thousand dirhams or well into five figures per subject, and the difference is almost entirely about how many hours are bought rather than what is paid per hour. A family that buys a bounded repair block after a diagnosis spends a fraction of what a family buying a continuous weekly arrangement from the start of Year 10 spends, and the evidence rarely favours the second.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which removes the travel component from the rate entirely. The rest of this page costs the alternatives properly, names the extras to ask about, and sets out when to stop paying.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raha-be.programmesIntro: Cost varies by specification because the hour counts do. These are the programmes an Al Raha Beach family will be buying support for, with the spending shape each one implies.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two terminal written papers per subject with no coursework in most cases, split into Core and Extended routes. The spending shape is bimodal: a small amount early on the skills that compound, then a concentrated block of timed-paper work in the final terms. The long middle stretch is where continuous arrangements consume budget without adding much.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a UAE candidate. Cambridge allocates each exam centre to one of six administrative zones, states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Tiered into Foundation and Higher with two written papers at each tier. Longer unsignposted problem-solving items at Higher tier are a practised skill rather than a body of content, which means they need spaced work across months rather than a late block, and that changes the spending profile.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: Single tier, sat alongside 0580, with calculus and identities a year early. The one International GCSE entry where a continuous weekly arrangement is genuinely good value rather than a default, because there is no Year 10 runway and no realistic late block that covers it.
programmes.countryNote: Also the scarcest specialism in this market, which affects price indirectly: a narrow pool means fewer competing quotes. Where a school near Al Raha Beach offers 0606, it is the best available bridge to AS Level or to Analysis and Approaches at higher level.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The next stage for students whose school does not run the Diploma, and worth costing now because sixth-form class sizes are smaller and school support is correspondingly more generous. That makes the free option genuinely strong at AS Level and reduces the case for a paid continuous arrangement.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route asks for one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, on top of five International GCSE passes at no less than E or grade 3. Worth knowing before paying for subjects that will not count.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raha-be.subjectsIntro: Not every subject repays the same spend. These entries say what each one needs and therefore whether a paid hour there is good value or avoidable.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: The subject where paid hours most reliably convert into marks, because the failures are specific procedures breaking and somebody has to watch a student work to find them. Also the subject where early spending outperforms late spending, since fluency builds over months.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Good value in a bounded block on electricity and magnetism plus graph discipline for the practical-skills paper. Poor value as a continuous arrangement, because much of the content is recall the student can handle with the board's own materials.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Split the subject deliberately. Mole calculations and electrolysis half-equations justify paid attention; qualitative analysis tests and organic conditions are recall that a peer group or self-study handles for nothing.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume in the sciences and the weakest case for continuous one-to-one, because most of the work is recall. The high-value paid hour here is command-term discipline, which is a technique block rather than a term of teaching.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Needs individual feedback on the student's own writing, which is the one thing a group cannot provide and the one thing the class teacher provides free as part of marking. Ask the school before paying anyone for this.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: Quotation banks and essay structure are buildable alone with the set texts and the board's published papers. The paid hour that earns its place is feedback on a timed essay the student wrote, which is narrow and cheap.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy can be drilled from published materials for nothing. Evaluation technique needs somebody reading the student's own paragraphs and saying where the judgement is missing, which is a genuinely good use of a few paid hours.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is a technique rather than content, which makes a short block unusually efficient. A term of weekly sessions on this subject is almost always more than it needs.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode and trace tables are mechanical and can be drilled alone against published past papers. Among the weakest cases in the specification for sustained paid support, and among the strongest for a two-session technique fix.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: The exception to everything above. New content in Year 11 with no runway, multi-step questions without scaffolding, and a scarce tutor pool. This is the one entry where continuous weekly support across the year is the right purchase.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case studies with their specific figures are memory work, best spread across months and done largely for free. Skills questions on maps and graphs are a short drillable block, which is where a paid hour belongs.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules covering Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. Content is prescribed and may not be substituted, so support must follow the school's own approved material and the school is the first place to ask.

sections.heading: The full price list, from nothing upwards
paragraphs: Set out from zero, the options separate by what each tranche of money actually buys. The first two tiers cost nothing and solve real problems. The middle tiers buy content coverage at a low price. The upper tiers buy individual diagnosis, which is the only thing money reliably buys in this market that nothing cheaper provides.

At zero sits school provision: departmental catch-up sessions, subject clinics and the class teacher's own marking, all inside fees you have already paid. Also at zero sit the boards' own published materials, which are authoritative and largely unopened. A student who has never read a mark scheme for their own specification has an unused asset of real value, and no fee will produce a better one.

Above that, entry-level online tuition at AED 45-150 an hour buys supervision and content recap, which is useful for a capable but disorganised student and inadequate for a candidate needing technique. A qualified subject tutor at AED 150-300 buys teaching to a named specification. An in-home visit at AED 180-500 buys the same teaching plus a journey. A specialist at AED 200-450 and upwards buys paper-level technique and mark-scheme work. A premium named tutor at AED 500-650 or more buys scarcity and availability.

The table sets these out with what each tier genuinely delivers. Read the column on the right rather than the one with the numbers in it, because the question that matters is not what a tier costs but whether what it buys is what your child's marked paper says they need.

sections.heading: The extras nobody mentions at the start
paragraphs: An hourly rate is the beginning of a quote rather than the whole of it, and the differences between providers sit in the terms rather than the headline. Five questions surface almost all of it, and asking them before the first session costs nothing and occasionally changes the decision entirely.

Is the price per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? A provider quoting per session at ninety minutes and one quoting per hour are not comparable until you convert. Is there a minimum commitment, a block you must buy, or a notice period? Several providers in this market sell monthly packages, including around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and a package is a commitment rather than a discount unless you use all of it.

What is the cancellation and rescheduling policy, and who bears a missed session? This is where in-home and online arrangements differ sharply. If a school day overruns, an online session moves and an in-home session is either taken late with the tutor waiting or lost. Across two years that is a real number of paid hours, and it belongs in the comparison rather than being discovered in March.

Does the quoted price include VAT? Ask, and ask for the answer in writing. We do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition as a fact on this page, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority source and we have not published one; what a parent can reasonably require is a clear statement from any provider about whether the figure they quoted is the figure you pay. And finally: what happens if we stop after one lesson? A free trial with no card details taken answers that question before it arises, which is why ours works that way.

sections.heading: The cost of the wrong tutor, priced out
paragraphs: This is the number that belongs at the top of every tutoring pricing page and appears on none of them. Suppose a family hires a competent tutor who does not know their child's specification: a Cambridge 0580 specialist for a Pearson 4MB1 entry, or a generalist working from a Year 11 scheme rather than the actual syllabus. The teaching is not bad. It is simply aimed slightly wrong.

Price it. A weekly session at the mid-band AED 150-300 across two terms is twenty-odd hours. At the lower end that is a few thousand dirhams; at the upper end considerably more. But the fee is the smaller loss. The larger one is twenty-odd hours of the student's own time spent practising for a slightly different examination, plus the two terms in which the real gaps went undiagnosed and compounded, plus the final-term scramble that follows when the mock reveals it.

The same arithmetic applies to tier. A student capped on Core or Foundation whose tutor never asked about the tier can work hard for a year and be awarded a grade they could not exceed. The tutoring was not wasted in any absolute sense; it was spent on the wrong question. That is a failure of the first ten minutes of the relationship, not of the teaching.

The protection is cheap and specific. Establish the board, the syllabus code and the tier in writing from the school before paying anyone. Send one marked paper and require a diagnosis that names topics. Ask which code the tutor teaches most weeks. Those three steps take an evening, cost nothing, and remove the largest single risk in this market, which no amount of paying a higher rate addresses.

sections.heading: Which subjects deserve the money
paragraphs: A household with a fixed budget and three weak subjects has to choose, and the choice should follow what each subject's failures actually respond to rather than which grade looks worst. Some subjects convert paid hours into marks reliably. Others are mostly recall, where the same money buys very little that free materials and a peer group do not.

Mathematics is the strongest case. The failures are specific procedures breaking in the middle of a method, and finding them requires somebody watching one student work. No group class, mark scheme or revision guide does that. It is also the subject where early spending outperforms late spending, because fluency is built over months, which makes it the one place a Year 10 block is good value.

The sciences are mixed and should be split deliberately. Mole calculations, energetics, electricity and magnetism, and graph discipline on the practical-skills paper justify paid attention. Qualitative analysis tests, organic reaction conditions, and the large recall volume in Biology do not; they are peer-group and self-study territory, and a family paying a specialist rate to hear definitions repeated is overspending substantially.

The essay subjects divide differently again. What they need is individual feedback on the student's own writing, which a group cannot give and which the class teacher gives free as part of normal marking. The right move is to ask the school first and then buy a small number of hours for timed essay feedback if the school's capacity is genuinely exhausted. The table sets out the ranking.

sections.heading: Three spending patterns across two years, compared
paragraphs: The same family, the same child and three different plans produce very different totals and surprisingly similar outcomes, with one exception. Setting them side by side is the most useful thing a cost page can do, because almost nobody does the arithmetic before committing.

The first pattern is continuous weekly from the start of Year 10, in one subject, at the mid-band. Roughly seventy paid hours, most of them during a stretch when the school is teaching the same content at the same time. It is the most expensive pattern and it is also the most common, because it is what happens when a family starts a weekly session and never revisits the decision.

The second is targeted: a diagnostic, a Year 10 fluency block, a tier review if relevant, and a post-mock paper block. Perhaps twenty-five to thirty paid hours in total, concentrated where the school has least capacity and where a paid hour therefore adds most. It costs under half as much and in most cases achieves more, because every hour is aimed at something named.

The third is minimal: free options only, with one diagnostic session to decide whether anything more is needed. Some families genuinely need nothing beyond this, particularly where the child is capable and the problem is organisation. The exception to all of it is Additional Mathematics 0606, where new content arrives in Year 11 with no runway and the continuous pattern is the correct one. The table compares them.

sections.heading: The free tier, costed properly
paragraphs: Calling something free invites scepticism, so it is worth being specific about what the zero-cost options actually contain and where they stop. School provision typically includes departmental catch-up sessions, subject clinics or drop-ins after the taught day, and the class teacher's marking and feedback on classwork and assessments. For an Al Raha Beach student attending a campus a short drive away, attending a clinic adds no journey at all because they are already on site.

The boards' own published material includes the syllabus document, which states exactly what is examinable at each tier, past papers, mark schemes and published timetables. A student who learns to read a mark scheme critically gets more from every paper they attempt afterwards, including the ones they attempt alone, which makes that one skill the highest-leverage free gain available.

We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, and a provider offering a downloadable library of them is offering something that is not theirs to give. They belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels and reach students through their school. Reference them and read them at source.

Where the free tier stops is diagnosis. School provision is capacity-limited and a teacher with a full class has limited time to watch one student work through a method and find the step that fails. Published materials tell a student what the answer was, not why theirs was wrong. That boundary is exactly where a paid hour earns its place, and knowing where it falls is what stops a family paying for the part they already have.
bullets: School clinics require no journey for a student already on campus
The syllabus states exactly what is examinable at each tier

sections.heading: When to stop paying
paragraphs: Every cost page in this market explains how to start and none explains how to stop, which is why the commonest overspend is an arrangement that outlived its purpose. There are three clear stopping points and a family that uses them spends substantially less than one that does not.

The first is when a bounded block ends. A repair block finishes with a timed set on the problem it was bought to fix. If the set is passed, the block is done and the honest next step is nothing, not a continuation at the same rate on a different topic chosen by default. The second is when the ranked topic list is empty. In any paper-based block the output is a list of what is costing the most marks, updated after each marked paper; when it is empty and scores have plateaued near the top of what the papers offer, the work is finished.

The third is the examination. A run-in ends at the series. There is no version of tutoring that helps after the final paper, and a monthly arrangement that rolls past it is simply a billing arrangement. For a November resit the decision to restart should be made deliberately within a fortnight of results rather than by letting a package continue.

The test that catches a drifting arrangement is the same one that justifies starting it: evidence. Is the named topic list shorter than it was? Are timed scores moving? If neither has changed in six weeks, the plan should change rather than continue, and a provider who will not say that out loud is the one you are most likely to keep paying. We would rather tell a family the work is finished, because a block that visibly ended is a better advertisement than a subscription that never did.
bullets: Stop when a bounded block's closing timed set is passed
Stop when the ranked topic list is empty and scores have plateaued

sections.heading: What the schedule costs you, and why online removes part of it
paragraphs: Time is a cost too, and in this corridor it is a visible one. Campuses serving Al Raha Beach finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions later on some days. The community's advantage is that several large campuses are a short drive away, so arrival home is often between 15:40 and 16:15. Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, a workable session start is 17:00 for most households and 16:30 for those closest to their campus.

Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and across two years the slots that survive are 18:00 and 18:30. The relevance to cost is simple: a slot that only works on a quiet week will break within a fortnight, and a broken slot in a paid arrangement is a session you budgeted for and did not receive.

In-home arrangements carry two further time costs that online ones do not. A session taken late because the school run overran is time the tutor spent waiting and you paid for. A session lost to traffic or to a closed road is a session gone. Online, both cases become a reschedule to later the same evening at no cost to either side, which across a two-year arrangement is a meaningful number of delivered hours.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The practical effect on price is that no part of a rate pays for a journey, and the practical effect on delivery is that the hours you agree are the hours that happen. Published market bands for comparison, attributed above, put in-home at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online.

whyPoints.description: School provision and the boards' own published materials come first on this page because they cost nothing and, for absence and single misunderstandings, they are better informed than any external tutor. We lose work by saying so and the page is worth more for it.

The sciences should be split: moles, energetics and electricity justify paid hours, while qualitative tests and the large recall volume in Biology do not. Essay subjects need individual feedback, which the class teacher gives free as part of marking.

intro.heading: The question is which component, not which subject
paragraphs: A report card says Chemistry, grade 6. That is not a diagnosis. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry is examined through three components with different weightings: a multiple-choice paper at thirty per cent, a theory paper at fifty, and either a practical test or the alternative to practical at twenty. A student can be strong on two and weak on one, and the single grade hides which. The remedy for each is different.

That structure is the most useful thing a parent can learn about the British pathway, because it converts a vague worry into a specific question. Which component is costing the marks? For most students, the answer is stable across two years, which means it can be identified in one session with a marked paper and then worked on deliberately rather than guessed at across a term of general revision.

The second useful fact is that mark losses are patterned by subject rather than random. In Mathematics they cluster in reverse percentages, similar shapes, bounds and probability without replacement. In Biology they cluster in terminology precision. In Physics they cluster in unit prefixes and rearranged equations. In English they cluster in answering the wrong task well. Each of those is procedural and each can be removed in weeks rather than months, which is the single most encouraging fact available to a family that has just read a disappointing report.

Al Raha Gardens has a local wrinkle worth naming on a page about IGCSE specifically. The school at the centre of this community runs the IB continuum rather than the British pathway, so families here wanting IGCSE commute out, mostly towards Khalifa City, Al Bateen and Al Mushrif. That means an Al Raha Gardens street can contain Middle Years students and Year 11 IGCSE students who have never shared a classroom, and a neighbour's tutor recommendation is frequently a recommendation for a different assessment system entirely.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Raha Gardens is one-to-one teaching over live video, matched by syllabus code and component, with your child's own school material on screen. In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted in the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and that comparison is addressed later on this page.

What follows is subject-level detail: the mathematics topics that reliably cost marks, the science components and where each loses them, how the two boards handle practical work differently, what English mark schemes actually reward, the command terms that decide answers, and how to use past papers so they teach something rather than simply producing a score. sections.heading: Mathematics: the topics that reliably cost marks
paragraphs: IGCSE mathematics has no coursework with either board, so two timed papers carry the entire grade. That makes the subject unusually diagnosable: everything a student can do and cannot do appears in a marked paper, and the pattern repeats. Across both boards and both upper tiers, a short list of topics accounts for a disproportionate share of dropped marks.

Reverse percentages lead it. A student is given a post-increase figure and multiplies rather than divides, producing a plausible number and losing every mark. Similar shapes follow: length, area and volume scale by different powers of the ratio and the length factor gets used for all three. Upper and lower bounds appears regularly and is typically taught once, in Year 10, and never revisited.

Then there is the habit category, which is larger than the topic category. Multi-stage questions award method marks for visible steps, so a student who computes mentally and writes a single line collects the answer mark and forfeits the rest. On a paper with several such questions, that habit alone can cost a grade boundary, and it is the easiest item on this list to change.

The table below pairs each with the fix and a realistic timescale. The timescales matter: a parent deciding whether eight weeks is enough should be able to see that four of these can be removed inside that window and that shown-working discipline takes longer because it is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge.

sections.heading: The three sciences: components, weightings and where each loses marks
paragraphs: Cambridge examines each separate IGCSE science through three components: a multiple-choice paper at thirty per cent, a theory paper at fifty, and a practical component at twenty, taken as either the practical test or the alternative to practical. Knowing those three numbers changes revision planning immediately, because fifty per cent of the grade sits in extended written answers and most students spend most of their revision on recall.

Each component fails in its own way. The multiple-choice paper punishes imprecision: two options are close, the student knows the topic broadly and picks the plausible one. Elimination technique and precise definitions fix that, and both are drillable. The theory paper punishes command-term misreading, where a competent description answers an explain question and scores little. The practical component punishes never having rehearsed its conventions.

Pearson International GCSE takes a different structural route, examining each science through two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than through a separate practical component. The weightings are published by the board and worth reading on the specification page rather than taking from any third party, including this one. The teaching consequence is similar: method and analysis carry the marks, not laboratory dexterity.

The practical reading of all this is that a science grade should never be worked on as a whole. Identify the component, then work on that component's specific failure mode. A student losing marks on the multiple-choice paper and a student losing them on extended theory answers need different sessions, and a tutor who teaches both the same way is teaching to the subject rather than to the student.
