sections.heading: Practical science assessed two ways, and what that means for online lessons
paragraphs: This is the fair objection to online science tutoring and it deserves a straight answer rather than a dismissal. A tutor on video cannot run a titration alongside your child. What a tutor on video can do is teach what the practical components actually assess, which in both boards is method and analysis rather than manual dexterity.

Cambridge's alternative to practical tests experimental design, reading instruments, recording to appropriate precision, plotting, and identifying sources of error. Every one of those is a paper skill with its own conventions, and those conventions are where marks go: a table without units in the headers, a graph with a line of best fit drawn through every point, an error source given as human error rather than as something specific and systematic.

Pearson assesses practical skills inside its written papers, which produces the same teaching conclusion by a different route. The examinable material is the reasoning about an experiment, not the execution of it. A student who can explain why a repeat was taken and what a systematic error does to a gradient scores where a student with excellent bench technique and imprecise vocabulary does not.

Where school practical work has genuinely been missed, because a student joined late or changed schools mid-course, that gap is real and a tutor should say so rather than paper over it. The honest response is to raise it with the school, which holds the equipment and the responsibility, and to secure the analysis skills that carry the marks in the meantime. Graph work, incidentally, is better on a shared screen than on paper, because the plot can be saved and reread.

sections.heading: What English mark schemes actually reward
paragraphs: English is the subject where able students most often lose marks without understanding why, because the loss is rarely about quality of writing. Cambridge First Language English splits evenly between a reading paper and a directed writing and composition paper. Pearson's English Language A splits between a non-fiction and transactional writing paper and a poetry, prose and imaginative writing paper, with a coursework route available in place of part of it; the board publishes the weightings.

The reliable failure is answering the wrong task well. A directed writing question specifies a form, an audience and a purpose: a letter to a head teacher, a speech to a school council, an article for a local paper. A student who writes a beautiful essay in response to a question asking for a speech has produced good writing that cannot access the top band. Fifteen minutes of taught planning fixes this permanently.

On the reading paper, the losses are different. Students summarise where the question asked for analysis of effect, or they identify a technique without saying what it does to the reader. The move that raises marks most quickly is forcing every point to end with an effect: the writer uses this, which makes the reader feel or understand that. Mechanical, and it works.

In Literature the differentiator is quotation accuracy. Six short, precisely remembered quotations per text, each with a point attached, outperform wide reading with nothing quotable. That is a memorisation task, not an interpretive one, and it is therefore reliable: it responds to spaced practice in a way that insight does not.

sections.heading: Command terms decide the answer in every subject
paragraphs: Command terms are the single largest source of avoidable loss across the IGCSE specifications, and they transfer across subjects, which makes teaching them unusually good value. A student who learns the difference between describe, explain and evaluate once improves in science theory papers, in Economics, in Geography and in History simultaneously.

The defaults are predictable. Students describe, because describing is what they can always do. A six-mark explain question answered descriptively typically collects a third of the available marks, and the student leaves the examination believing they answered it well. The gap between what they wrote and what was asked is invisible to them, which is why it survives two years of revision.

The fix is mechanical. Underline the command term before reading the rest of the question. Write the structure the term demands before writing any content. For explain, that means a statement followed by a because. For evaluate, a claim, evidence for, evidence against and a judgement with a reason. Taught properly it takes three or four sessions and then holds for both examined years.

There is a related skill worth building at the same time: reading the mark allocation. A two-mark question wants two distinct points, not one point written twice. A six-mark question in a science theory paper usually wants six separable statements, and students who write a flowing paragraph of three ideas score three. Counting the marks and then counting your own points is a thirty-second habit that pays in every paper.

sections.heading: Past papers, used so that they teach rather than score
paragraphs: Most families collect past papers and then use them as a thermometer. The student sits a paper, gets a mark, feels better or worse, and learns very little. A past paper only teaches when it is marked against the official scheme by somebody who can explain why a mark was withheld, and when the resulting errors are written down and revisited deliberately.

The method that works is one timed section at a time rather than a whole paper. Mark it with the student present, aloud. For every lost mark, decide which of four categories it belongs to: content not known, command term misread, working not shown, or time ran out. Keep the tally across sessions. After five or six sessions the tally tells you what to teach, and it is almost never what the student guessed.

Timing deserves separate attention because it is the category parents underestimate. A student who consistently leaves the last question blank is losing a boundary to pacing rather than to knowledge. Dividing marks by minutes to get a rate, writing that rate on the paper, and practising the final question first for a fortnight are three cheap interventions that between them usually recover the loss.

On materials, a caution. We reference and link official syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes rather than supplying them, because reproducing board material is copyright infringement and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. Your child's school holds legitimate copies of everything needed. A provider advertising a downloadable archive of mark schemes is distributing something it has no right to distribute.

The school at its centre runs the IB continuum rather than the British pathway, so families here wanting IGCSE travel out, mostly to Khalifa City and sometimes as far as Al Bateen and Al Mushrif. That produces an unusually mixed street: Middle Years students and Year 11 IGCSE candidates living next door and sharing no assessment system at all.

The practical effect on scheduling is mild rather than severe. Khalifa City journeys are short, so a Year 10 student can manage 16:30. Students travelling to the inner-city schools are commonly home between 15:45 and 16:15 and do better at 18:00 or later. Schools across Abu Dhabi release students for parts of mock season, and that fortnight is the most productive tutoring window of the year because the marked script is fresh.

Those tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted.

What this page does not claim: no regulator, examination board or school endorses IB Gram, and nothing here implies one does. We hold no ADEK, MoHRE or examination-board accreditation. There is no Abu Dhabi office. Every dirham figure carries its source and date, there is no self-generated rating, and no provider can guarantee a grade or an improvement, including us. faqs.question: Which component should an IGCSE home tutor in Al Raha Gardens work on first?
faqs.answer: Whichever one the marked paper shows is failing, and the marked paper will show it. Cambridge separate sciences split thirty per cent multiple choice, fifty per cent theory and twenty per cent practical, so a single grade can hide three very different problems. A student losing marks on close multiple-choice options needs precision and elimination work. A student losing them on extended theory answers needs command-term teaching. Those are different sessions, and guessing between them wastes the first month.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to Al Raha Gardens homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Al Raha Gardens families are one to one over live video, matched by syllabus code and component, with your child's own material on screen. For reference, in-home one-to-one visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted in the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online.

faqs.question: How much of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade is the theory paper?
faqs.answer: Fifty per cent, with the multiple-choice paper at thirty and the practical component at twenty. That single split should reshape most revision plans, because fifty per cent of the grade sits in extended written answers and most students spend most of their revision time on recall for the multiple-choice paper. If your child is strong on recall and still losing marks, the theory paper and its command terms are almost certainly where the grade is going.

faqs.question: Can science practicals be taught properly over video with no lab?
faqs.answer: The examinable part can. Cambridge's alternative to practical tests experimental design, instrument reading, recording to appropriate precision, plotting and identifying error sources. Pearson assesses the same reasoning inside its written papers. All of it is paper skill with its own conventions: units in table headers, a line of best fit rather than a line through every point, and specific systematic error sources rather than human error. Graph work is arguably better on a shared screen, because the plot can be saved and reread.

faqs.question: Why does my son know the biology and still get a grade 6?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly terminology precision. IGCSE Biology has the largest specification in the science group and its mark schemes want named processes rather than fluent description. A student who writes three accurate sentences where the scheme wants one named term scores one mark from three. The fix is short timed recall on the specification's own wording, twice a week, with immediate correction and a running list of terms he has repeatedly produced imprecisely. It is unglamorous and it is measurable.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should we target with eight weeks left?
faqs.answer: Reverse percentages, similar shape scale factors, upper and lower bounds, and probability without replacement. Each is procedural rather than conceptual, each appears regularly, and each can usually be removed in one or two weeks of deliberate practice. Alongside those, enforce shown working on every line, which takes longer because it is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge but can be worth a grade boundary on a paper with several multi-stage questions.

faqs.question: My daughter writes beautifully in English and gets a 6, so why?
faqs.answer: She is probably answering the wrong task well. Directed writing questions specify a form, an audience and a purpose, and a polished essay written in response to a question asking for a speech cannot reach the top band however good the prose. Fifteen minutes of taught planning, naming the form, audience and purpose before any content, fixes this permanently. On the reading paper, make every point end with a stated effect on the reader rather than stopping at the named technique.

faqs.question: What is the quickest way to raise an IGCSE Literature grade?
faqs.answer: Memorised quotation. Six short, precisely remembered quotations per text, each with a point attached to it, outperform wide reading with nothing quotable. It is a memorisation task rather than an interpretive one, which makes it reliable: it responds to spaced practice in a way that insight does not. Students who can quote precisely also write tighter essays, because the quotation anchors the paragraph and prevents the plot retelling that costs most of the marks.

faqs.question: How do command terms differ, and does learning them help in more than one subject?
faqs.answer: They transfer across nearly every subject, which is what makes them worth teaching. State wants a line. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants reasons with a because. Suggest wants knowledge applied to an unfamiliar context. Compare wants explicit similarities and differences. Evaluate wants a judgement with evidence both ways. Three or four sessions on question wording improves science theory papers, Economics, Geography and History at the same time, which is the highest-return teaching available in these two years.

faqs.question: Does reading the mark allocation really change the answer?
faqs.answer: Substantially, and it takes thirty seconds to do. A two-mark question wants two distinct points, not one point expressed twice. A six-mark question in a science theory paper usually wants six separable statements, and a student who writes a flowing paragraph containing three ideas scores three. Counting the marks, then counting your own points before moving on, is one of the cheapest habits available. Most students have never been told to do it explicitly.

faqs.question: Should we buy past papers and mark schemes from a tutoring provider?
faqs.answer: No. Examination board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and reproducing them is copyright infringement; for unreleased material it is also a malpractice exposure. Your child's school holds legitimate copies of everything needed, and a tutor can work from those. A provider advertising a downloadable archive of mark schemes is distributing material it has no right to distribute, which is a reason for caution about everything else it says.

faqs.answer: Because the school at the centre of this community runs the IB continuum rather than the British pathway. Families wanting IGCSE commute out, mostly to Khalifa City and sometimes as far as Al Bateen and Al Mushrif. The scheduling consequence is a split within one street: Khalifa City students can usually manage a 16:30 session, while students travelling to the inner-city schools are commonly home between 15:45 and 16:15 and do better at 18:00 or later.

faqs.question: Is mock fortnight a good time to begin, or should we wait?
faqs.answer: It is the best fortnight in the year to begin. The student is already in examination mode, so timed practice feels normal, and the marked script arrives fresh with every lost mark visible. Abu Dhabi schools often release students for parts of mock season, which creates the one daytime window of the year. Four sessions built from a real mock paper routinely achieve more than twelve built from a syllabus checklist earlier in the autumn.

faqs.question: Does an Abu Dhabi tutor need a permit even for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit regardless of format. The MoHRE private tutor work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government teachers, private and public-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, a UAE-based tutor without one has no excuse; ask to see it.

faqs.question: What if you have no specialist for my child's component and hour?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than offering a generalist. Mathematics and the separate sciences at common hours usually match within a few days. A specific component in a less common subject, or a fixed weekday hour in a busy window, can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is free. Hearing that early leaves you time to look elsewhere, which is far more useful than finding out in session three that the tutor has never taught the paper you were worried about.

Matching on the code rather than the subject name is what stops a student revising from the wrong set of past papers.

intro.heading: Start with the code, because the code decides the papers
paragraphs: An IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a family of syllabuses from different boards, each with its own paper structure, its own tiering, its own practical arrangements and its own grade scale. Cambridge IGCSE Physics is 0625. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics is 4PH1. They examine overlapping content through different papers, and a student revising from the wrong board's past papers is practising question styles they will never meet. The first thing worth knowing about your child's IGCSE is therefore not the subject but the code.

In Abu Dhabi schools the common codes are Cambridge 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 and 0990 English First Language, 0510 and 0511 English as a Second Language, 0450 Business Studies, 0455 Economics and 0460 Geography, alongside Pearson 4MA1 Mathematics, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology and 4EA1 English Language. Some schools mix boards across subjects, so one student can be sitting Cambridge science and Pearson maths in the same year. Ask the school for the list in writing, subject by subject, and keep the reply where you can find it in Year 11. It is a short email that saves a term of revising from the wrong papers, and the examinations officer answers that question every week.

The second structural fact is tiering. Cambridge splits several subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grades available. Pearson splits mathematics into Foundation and Higher, with Foundation topping out at grade 5 and Higher running 9 down to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. Tier entry is made by the school and it sets a ceiling the student cannot pass however well the papers go, which is why it deserves a conversation in Year 10 rather than a discovery in Year 11.

The third is practical assessment in the sciences. Cambridge science syllabuses offer an alternative-to-practical paper alongside a practical test option, and schools choose which route they enter. The alternative-to-practical paper is its own skill: reading an apparatus diagram, identifying a variable that was not controlled, criticising a method, completing a results table, plotting and interpreting a graph with sensible scales. Students who know the physics and have never practised that paper lose marks on it reliably, and it is one of the easiest gains available in a short block.

IB Gram delivers all of this as live one-to-one online tuition on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For syllabus-specific work that arrangement is an advantage rather than a concession: past papers are annotated on a shared screen, an apparatus diagram can be marked up while both people look at it, and the session is recorded so a student can replay a method before attempting the next question set.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written papers, tiered into Core and Extended in several subjects, with alternative-to-practical or practical test routes in the sciences. Grades are reported A* to G. Cambridge publishes the current assessment model for each syllabus code, and models are revised, so the paper structure should be read at source for the series your child is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable version for each, and states that it is essential to use the correct version because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's school is the centre, so the school's timetable is the authoritative one for an Al Rawdah family.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Parallel qualifications with codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, reported on the 9 to 1 grade scale and tiered in mathematics into Foundation and Higher. Science practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical test in most routes.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables that are later revised, so plan from the live official timetable.

programmes.name: AS and A-Level, what IGCSE feeds into
programmes.description: The usual continuation for a Cambridge or Pearson student. Entry is typically conditional on minimum IGCSE grades in the relevant subjects, and the step up in algebraic and analytical demand is steep, showing in the first AS mock. Tier entry at IGCSE can therefore close a post-16 door quietly.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme, the other post-16 route
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, with internal assessments carrying substantial weight and a 45-point total. An IGCSE Extended or Higher-tier student arrives with solid algebra and essentially no calculus, which is the predictable first-term gap in Diploma mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run a British route to Year 11 and then offer the Diploma, so an Al Rawdah family may be choosing between staying for A-Levels and moving to a Diploma school. That decision is far easier in Year 10, when tier entry can still be aligned with it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-rawdah.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names the syllabus, the paper shape and the trap that most reliably costs marks in it. This is the level of detail a tutor should be able to discuss before you book them.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580
subjects.description: Number, algebra, coordinate geometry, mensuration, trigonometry, transformations, probability and statistics. Cambridge has revised the assessment model, including the balance of calculator and non-calculator papers, so confirm the structure at source. Traps: reverse percentages, bounds rounded away, and histograms with unequal class widths where frequency density is forgotten.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The same mathematical territory on the 9 to 1 scale, with Foundation capped at grade 5 and Higher running 9 to 4 with a grade 3 safety net. Question phrasing differs from Cambridge enough to matter in timed conditions. Traps: incomplete transformation descriptions and tree diagrams where the second denominator is not changed.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics, with an alternative-to-practical or practical test route. Traps: stating a relationship without the condition attached, treating a graph gradient as a value rather than a rate, and losing every subsequent mark to a unit conversion made once.

subjects.name: Physics, Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Comparable content with practical skills assessed inside the written papers. Six-mark extended answers reward a structured explanation, and students who write a list of facts rather than a causal chain lose marks they knew the physics for. Formula recall is less forgiving than many students expect.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620
subjects.description: Particles, stoichiometry, electrochemistry, energetics, rates, organic chemistry and chemical analysis. Traps: mole calculations where the limiting reagent is not identified, ionic equations written without charges balanced, and qualitative analysis answers that name a result without naming the observation that produced it.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Similar ground with its own paper structure and question conventions. Organic mechanisms and calculations involving concentration and gas volumes generate the most requests from Year 11 students in this catchment. Practical-method criticism appears inside the written papers and is routinely under-practised.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610
subjects.description: Cells, transport, nutrition, respiration, coordination, inheritance and ecology. The volume of content makes this a long-run subject rather than a crammable one, and the biggest single source of lost marks is answering a command term with the wrong shape of answer rather than with wrong biology.

subjects.name: English First Language, Cambridge 0500 and 0990
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, summary writing and directed writing, with coursework in some routes. Marks are lost in summary tasks that quote rather than condense, and in directed writing that ignores the specified audience and form. The examined skill is timed analysis, not quantity of reading.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language, Cambridge 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and, in 0511, a speaking component. A student entered for the second-language syllabus is examined against different criteria from a first-language candidate, which is one of the most consequential things for a family to confirm before buying tuition.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics, Cambridge 0450 and 0455
subjects.description: Case-study based papers where marks sit in application to the given business or economy rather than in recited theory. Economics diagrams carry marks that are forfeited through missing labels, and evaluation questions require a judgement with a reason rather than two balanced paragraphs and no conclusion.

subjects.name: Geography and History, Cambridge 0460 and 0470
subjects.description: Source-based and case-study assessment where structure decides the mark. History candidates lose marks by describing a source rather than using it as evidence; geography candidates lose marks on skills questions involving maps, graphs and data interpretation that are entirely practisable.

subjects.name: Alternative-to-practical papers across the sciences
subjects.levels: Where the school enters this route
subjects.description: A separate examined skill: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying uncontrolled variables, criticising a method, completing results tables, choosing graph scales and drawing valid conclusions. Students who have never worked through one lose marks they would otherwise have earned, and a handful of focused sessions reliably recovers them.

sections.heading: What this search means in practice, and the first question to ask the school
paragraphs: Directly: an IGCSE home tutor in Al Rawdah, through IB Gram, means a subject specialist matched to the syllabus code your child is entered for, teaching one-to-one over live video at a time that fits an Abu Dhabi school day, with a free trial lesson first. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. The search phrase is what parents type, and the honest response is to answer it and then say what is actually delivered.

The first question to put to the school is not about tutoring at all. It is: which syllabus code is each subject entered for, which tier, and for the sciences which practical route. Those three facts determine the papers, the grade ceiling and a whole examined skill, and they are the difference between tuition that lands on the right target and tuition that is broadly about the subject.

Parents are sometimes reluctant to ask, as though it signals distrust. It does not. The examinations officer deals with codes daily and the maths or science department will answer in a sentence. Put the question in an email so you have the reply in writing, because the answer also tells you which past papers to download and which mark schemes to work from.

Once the codes are known, the diagnosis is straightforward. One marked past paper per subject, read against the official scheme, names the recurring failures in about twenty minutes. Nearly always they are a small set of repeatable errors rather than a general absence of understanding, and that is good news: repeatable errors respond to targeted practice far faster than missing knowledge does.

Diagnose from a marked paper, not from a conversation

sections.heading: The sciences: paper structures, practical routes and the marks nobody practises
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology, are tiered into Core and Extended and offer an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test depending on what the centre enters. Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 assess practical skills inside the written papers instead. The consequence is that two students in the same Al Rawdah street can be examined on experimental skills in entirely different formats.

The alternative-to-practical paper is the most consistently underprepared component in this catchment. It asks a student to read an apparatus diagram, spot the variable nobody controlled, criticise a method, complete a results table with consistent significant figures, choose a sensible graph scale, draw a line of best fit and state a conclusion the data supports. Each of those is a trainable skill with its own mark-scheme language, and none of them appears in a textbook chapter.

In the theory papers the failures are specific rather than general. Physics candidates state relationships without the condition attached and treat a gradient as a value rather than a rate. Chemistry candidates lose mole questions by not identifying the limiting reagent and lose ionic equations by not balancing charge. Biology candidates write accurate biology in the wrong shape, answering an evaluate command with a description. Extended-response questions in all three reward a causal chain rather than a list.

Where a student is studying online and worried about practical work, the honest position is that an online tutor cannot run a titration with your child. What an online tutor can do is teach the examined practical skills thoroughly, work through every past alternative-to-practical paper available for that code, and make sure the student understands the apparatus they have used in school well enough to criticise a method on paper. The school supplies the laboratory; the tutor supplies the examination technique.

sections.heading: Command terms: the examiner hiding inside every question
paragraphs: A large share of lost IGCSE marks has nothing to do with knowledge. It comes from answering the wrong question well. State, describe, explain, compare, evaluate, suggest, calculate and justify each ask for a different structure, and the mark scheme is written to reward that structure. A student who explains when asked to describe has written more and scored less.

This is teachable in a few sessions and it transfers across every subject. Describe asks what happens, in order, with no reasons. Explain asks why, with a causal chain. Compare asks for both items in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. Evaluate asks for a judgement supported by the strongest reason, which means a conclusion is required rather than optional. Suggest invites a reasoned possibility, so a sensible answer earns credit even when it is not the model one.

The way to learn it is on the student's own marked work. Take a paper, find every question where marks were lost, and classify each loss: wrong content, wrong structure, or wrong reading of the command. In most Year 11 papers the second and third categories together outnumber the first, which is why command-term work is one of the highest-yield things a tutor can do early.

Mark schemes are published by the boards and should be read on their sites rather than redistributed. We cite and link them rather than supplying copies, because reproducing syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables is a copyright matter. A tutor's job is to teach a student to read the scheme, which is a skill they then keep for every paper they sit.

sections.heading: Using past papers properly, which is not the same as doing lots of them
paragraphs: Every family knows past papers matter. Fewer know that the value sits in the marking rather than the attempting. A student who completes ten papers and checks only the final answers has learnt almost nothing about where their marks went. A student who completes four and marks each one against the official scheme, classifying every lost mark, has built a map of their own weaknesses.

The method is simple enough to run without a tutor, although most students do not run it alone. Attempt a paper under timing. Mark it against the published scheme, awarding marks exactly as written rather than generously. Record each lost mark by topic and by type: content, structure, command reading, arithmetic, units. Count the categories. Then spend the next two sessions on whatever the count names, not on whatever feels hardest.

Two or three cycles in, something useful happens: the log stops looking like the student's intuition. Students almost always believe their problem is the hardest topic on the syllabus. The log usually says the problem is units, or incomplete transformation descriptions, or significant figures, or answering describe questions as explain questions. Those are cheap to fix and worth real marks across every paper.

Timing deserves separate treatment. Many Al Rawdah students lose marks at the end of a paper rather than throughout it, which is a pacing failure rather than a knowledge one. The fix is practising sections against the clock and learning to leave a stuck question and return, which sounds obvious and is almost never trained. A student who collects the final ten accessible marks instead of abandoning them has changed a grade boundary without learning any new content.

sections.heading: What subject tuition costs when a student needs more than one
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the wrong unit for a family in this position. A Year 11 student weak in three subjects does not need one rate; they need to decide how many subjects to pay for, which is the decision that actually sets the bill. Three weekly sessions is three times the cost and, more importantly, removes the evenings in which the student would otherwise practise. That trade-off is usually worse than it looks on paper.

With that framing, the published bands read in October 2026 are these. A qualified subject tutor working online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tuition, often delivered by university students, runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel included, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led tuition reaches AED 500 to 650 and above on BartyED's published rate.

The practical approach for three weak subjects is triage rather than parallel coverage. One marked paper per subject establishes which carries the most recoverable marks. Start with that subject alone, at one session a week. Reassess after four weeks. Often the technique work transfers: command-term discipline learnt in biology shows up in geography, and significant-figure discipline learnt in chemistry shows up in physics. That transfer is why sequential beats simultaneous more often than families expect.

All of these are market figures from named published sources, not IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson, when subject, code and session length are known. And a reminder worth repeating: a premium rate does not improve a wrong diagnosis. Paying examiner-level money to fix a student's handling of unequal-width histograms is an expensive route to a cheap problem.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for a subject that has a laboratory attached
paragraphs: Science is the subject where the in-home question is asked most sharply, because parents reasonably wonder whether a screen can teach something that happens on a bench. The answer depends on which part of science you mean. Apparatus handling happens in the school laboratory under a teacher, and no private tutor in either format substitutes for that. Examination technique for practical papers happens on paper, and a shared screen suits it well.

In-home tuition in this market is advertised at AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price. A tutor in the room reads a student's working as it appears and holds attention better with a younger student. Against that, the pool shrinks to those who will drive to Al Rawdah at the hour you want, the start time is subject to traffic, and nothing from the session can be replayed afterwards.

For code-specific work the online format has a concrete advantage: a past paper and its mark scheme can be open on screen for both people, an apparatus diagram can be annotated live, and the recording lets a student revisit the moment a graph scale was chosen. Marking a paper together is the single most valuable hour in IGCSE tutoring, and it is easier to do well on a shared screen than across a kitchen table.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If you do engage an independent in-home tutor here, ask for their MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since the permit costs nothing there is no innocent reason to lack it.

sections.heading: Entries, series and what happens after the results arrive
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so an Al Rawdah candidate sits June with November as the resit route. Entries are made by the school as the examination centre, which also means the school holds the deadline for any tier change.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are past dates cited so they can be checked. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables that are later revised, any revision plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate a date.

After results, the decision most families face is whether to resit. The useful framing is marks rather than feelings: request the breakdown, see which paper and which question types lost the marks, and ask whether a November entry with targeted work would plausibly move it. A resit that repeats the same preparation usually repeats the same result, and a student who needs a specific grade for a specific post-16 route should make the decision on that requirement rather than on disappointment.

One thing worth planning for: the gap between sitting and receiving results is months, and the resit decision has to be made quickly once they arrive. A family that already knows the November route exists, and what its entry deadline looks like at their school, makes that decision calmly. One meeting it for the first time in late August does not.

sections.heading: Checks, claims and the things no tutoring company can honestly promise
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises their licensing and accreditation and publishes its own inspection ratings. Dubai is regulated by KHDA, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the Ministry of Education. Read ratings and policies on the regulator's own site.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum six months to complete the steps and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. When an agency describes its tutors as regulator-approved, ask which permit and what number.

Nor can any tutor promise a grade. No tutor, however experienced with 0620 past papers, can guarantee an outcome that depends on a student's own work on a specific morning. Statistics without a sample size, a date and a method should be read the same way: a published claim of a satisfaction percentage or an average tutor score means nothing unless the underlying data can be produced.

What can be promised is narrower and more useful. A tutor matched to the code. A diagnosis in the first lesson. Marking against the published scheme rather than generously. An error log that drives the plan. Disclosure when no specialist is free, including where a tutor is based outside the UAE. And a recommendation to reduce or stop when the log says the problem has gone, which is the test of whether a provider is selling teaching or selling hours.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science syllabus my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the examinations officer and the head of science and ask for the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route in writing. Cambridge codes look like 0625, 0620 and 0610; Pearson codes look like 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The practical route matters because Cambridge centres choose between an alternative-to-practical paper and a practical test, and the two examine different skills. Keep the reply, because it tells you exactly which past papers and mark schemes are the right ones to work from.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and why does it cost marks?
faqs.answer: It is a written paper that examines experimental skills without a laboratory: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying variables that were not controlled, criticising a method, completing results tables with consistent significant figures, choosing graph scales, drawing lines of best fit and stating conclusions the data supports. Each of those has its own mark-scheme language and none appears in a textbook chapter, so students who have never worked through one lose marks they would otherwise earn. A few focused sessions reliably recover them.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with science practicals at all?
faqs.answer: Not with handling apparatus, which belongs in the school laboratory with a teacher, and no private tutor in any format substitutes for that. What an online tutor can do is teach the examined practical technique thoroughly: working through every available alternative-to-practical paper for the right code, marking it against the scheme, and making sure the student can criticise a method and justify a graph scale on paper. The school supplies the bench; the tutor supplies the examination skill.

faqs.question: Why do command terms matter more than the topic my child finds hard?
faqs.answer: Because a large share of lost marks comes from answering the wrong question well. Describe wants what happens in sequence with no reasons; explain wants a causal chain; compare wants both items held together in each point; evaluate wants a judgement with the strongest supporting reason. A student who explains when asked to describe writes more and scores less. Classifying lost marks on a real paper usually shows structure and command reading outnumbering missing content, and that is quicker to fix.

faqs.question: Is doing more past papers always better?
faqs.answer: No. The value sits in the marking rather than the attempting. Ten papers with only the final answers checked teaches very little; four papers marked against the official scheme with every lost mark classified by topic and type builds a map of the student's actual weaknesses. Two or three cycles in, the log usually contradicts the student's intuition, naming units, significant figures or command reading rather than the hardest topic on the syllabus. Those are cheap to fix and worth marks across every paper.

faqs.question: My child runs out of time at the end of every paper. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a pacing problem rather than a knowledge one, which makes it one of the faster wins available. The training is practising sections against the clock, learning to leave a stuck question and come back to it, and treating the last ten accessible marks as marks rather than as a lost cause. Students are rarely taught this explicitly. A candidate who collects the final questions instead of abandoning them can cross a grade boundary without learning any new content.

faqs.question: We need help in three subjects. Should we book three tutors?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Three weekly sessions triples the cost and removes the evenings in which your child would otherwise practise any of the three. Start with one marked paper per subject to see which carries the most recoverable marks, work on that subject alone for four to six weeks, then reassess. Technique often transfers: command-term discipline learnt in biology shows up in geography, and significant-figure discipline learnt in chemistry shows up in physics, so sequential work compounds in a way parallel coverage does not.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Abu Dhabi students most often ask for help in?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, physics and chemistry lead, with English First Language close behind where a student is sitting the first-language syllabus rather than the second-language one. In mathematics the requests cluster around histograms with unequal class widths, reverse percentages and transformation descriptions. In the sciences they cluster around mole calculations, graph interpretation and the alternative-to-practical paper. In English they cluster around summary writing, where students quote instead of condensing and lose marks for it.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether my child sits 0500 or 0510 English?
faqs.answer: A great deal. Cambridge 0500 and 0990 are First Language English syllabuses; 0510 and 0511 are English as a Second Language, with 0511 carrying a speaking component. They are examined against different criteria, so a student entered for the second-language syllabus is not being assessed as a first-language candidate and should not be prepared as one. Confirm the code in writing before buying any tuition, because the wrong preparation here is particularly wasteful.

faqs.question: What should we do if the results are a grade below what the sixth form requires?
faqs.answer: Get the component breakdown from the examinations officer, see which paper and which question types lost the marks, and check the actual entry condition for the post-16 route rather than assuming it. Then decide about a November entry on that evidence. Cambridge offers a November series and Pearson runs November as well as May and June. A resit with the same preparation tends to produce the same result, so the plan has to come from the breakdown.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start once we have the codes?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days in term time, and the first session is a free trial lesson used as a diagnosis rather than an introduction. Availability tightens before mock windows and in the weeks before a series, when the same specialists are in demand across every school at once. If nobody is free for a particular code, you are told the expected wait and given the alternatives in writing, including where a tutor is based outside the UAE, which you hear before booking rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We cite and link them rather than supplying copies. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter. Your child's school can also provide them. What a tutor adds is teaching the student to read a mark scheme properly, which is a skill that keeps paying across every paper they sit, rather than handing over a folder of PDFs nobody works through.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper online tutor good enough for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: It depends on the job. Budget online tuition advertised at AED 45 to 150 an hour can genuinely cover homework supervision and confidence in Year 9 or early Year 10. For Year 11 work that needs mark-scheme marking, alternative-to-practical technique and triage across topics, the qualified band at AED 150 to 300 is the right place to be, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Premium rates of AED 500 and above make sense only for a narrow need already precisely identified.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Al Rawdah if we pay more?
faqs.answer: No. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors and agencies in Abu Dhabi do provide it, at published market rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. Our delivery into Al Rawdah is live one-to-one video tuition on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the syllabus code your child is entered for, with the past paper and its mark scheme open on a shared screen.

intro.heading: Knowing the subject and knowing the syllabus are different qualifications
paragraphs: A chemistry graduate knows chemistry. Whether they know Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended is a separate question, and it is the one that determines whether your money buys marks. The syllabus specifies which topics are assessed and to what depth, which papers are sat, what the formula provision is, and what wording a mark scheme credits. None of that is deducible from a degree, and most of it is not deducible from having been a good student of the subject either.

Al Reef makes the distinction unavoidable. The community sits out towards the airport, most secondary students travel out of it for school, and the pool of tutors willing to drive here on a weekday evening is small. Insisting on somebody local therefore selects on geography rather than on the syllabus, and for Extended-tier sciences or an Edexcel-specific code it can select on geography alone. The family is not usually told the pool is thin. They are offered the nearest person who agrees.

The symptoms of a syllabus mismatch are recognisable once you know them. Practice papers come from the wrong board, so the mathematics or science is correct and the question style is unfamiliar. The tutor covers a topic the syllabus does not assess, usually because they are working from the single-science specification when the child sits a double award. Or the tutor's explanation of what earns a mark does not match what the school has said, which a student notices and quietly stops trusting.

This page gives you the tools to check before you pay. It sets out what differs between Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subject by subject, publishes four questions that reliably separate a course teacher from a subject expert, maps where marks are actually lost in each of the sciences, explains the tiering decisions that change what should be taught, and states the exam-zone rule that catches families every series. Apply all of it to us as readily as to anybody else.

On delivery there is nothing to interpret. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service we provide only in India. Lessons for Al Reef households are one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard, with your child's own worksheet or marked script open, timed to Gulf Standard Time so the hour fits around a long bus route rather than around somebody's drive out from the Corniche. One further note before the detail. Nothing on this page requires hiring anybody. A parent who emails the school for the code, the tier and the calculator rules, and then reads the marked script for the pattern of lost marks, has done the work that most tutoring arrangements get wrong in their first month, and can hand a tutor a brief instead of a problem.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-reef.subjectsIntro: The subjects Al Reef families ask about most, with the code attached and a note on what the syllabus actually rewards. A tutor who cannot talk at this level of detail is working from the subject rather than the specification.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Circle theorems, trigonometry requiring a drawn diagram and histograms with unequal class widths return marks fastest. Practice has to come from the entered board, because the two set up multi-step questions differently and the mathematics being right is not sufficient.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism cost more marks than any other topic in this corridor. After that it is uncertainty handling, graph gradients, units and significant figures, all of which are technique rather than physics and all of which are quick to fix.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways decide the grade. The paper credits precise language: naming the increased frequency of successful collisions earns the mark that writing faster reaction does not, which is a vocabulary problem with a short remedy.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Approachable enough to be under-revised. The extended-response questions on transport, homeostasis and inheritance are where structured answers separate from broadly correct ones, and structure is among the fastest things to teach.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences in one double award, with specific sub-topics removed rather than everything simplified. A tutor working from the single-science syllabus spends hours on content this course does not assess, which is the clearest example of why the code matters more than the subject.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended reading response carry the paper. Strong readers still lose marks for ignoring audience, form and purpose, all of which the mark scheme credits explicitly, so the gain is in reading the question rather than in reading more widely.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Assessed across reading, writing and listening, with speaking in 0511. The exercises are formulaic and highly trainable, which makes this the highest-yield English option for a limited number of paid hours.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline decide the grade. An analyse question answered with description earns little however much the student knows, and Gulf-specific examples travel well in the data-response paper.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Entirely case-study driven, so practice must use real inserts rather than definitions. Students who revise terminology collect the knowledge marks and miss the application and evaluation marks, which together outweigh them.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Splits into theory and practical programming, and students are usually competent in one and weak in the other. Establishing which half is failing takes a single session and determines whether paid hours are worth spending at all.

sections.heading: Four questions that expose a subject expert who is not a course teacher
paragraphs: These take ten minutes and they work on anybody. Ask them of three providers in an afternoon and you will have a ranking that no amount of reading profiles would have produced. The point is not to catch anybody out; it is that the answers are instant for somebody who has taught the course to an examination and assembled in front of you by somebody who has not, and that difference is audible.

First: which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and what are the papers? A course teacher will ask you for the code if you have not supplied it, and then describe the paper structure back to you. Second: name one topic in that syllabus that is not assessed at my child's tier. Somebody working from the specification can exclude things; somebody working from a general idea of the subject cannot exclude anything, which is the clearest single signal available.

Third: show them a marked script and ask which lost marks are content, which are method not shown, and which are timing. The three need unrelated remedies and a course teacher separates them in a minute. Fourth: what wording does the mark scheme want for a common question in this subject, and what wording earns nothing? In chemistry, for instance, the difference between describing a reaction as faster and naming the increased frequency of successful collisions is a mark, and a tutor who has marked papers will reach for an example like that immediately.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, subject by subject
paragraphs: Both boards are taught across this corridor, sometimes within the same school and occasionally within the same family. The content overlaps heavily and the examinations do not, which is a combination that produces quiet failures rather than obvious ones. Past papers for both are freely available online, so a diligent student can spend a term practising the right material in the wrong format and only discover it from a mock result nobody can explain.

The differences that matter are concrete. Tier names differ, which causes confusion in conversations with tutors: Core and Extended at Cambridge, Foundation and Higher at Pearson. Question phrasing differs, with Pearson generally terser and more directly algebraic in mathematics. Formula provision differs, which changes what has to be memorised. Paper structures differ, so a student who has practised timing on one board's paper can mismanage the other's.

The practical step is a single email to the school asking for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and whether any paper is sat without a calculator, for each subject. Four pieces of information, one message, and the answer governs every revision decision for the next two years. Give the reply to any tutor before the first paid session, and ask them to confirm it back to you in their own words. A tutor who is vague at that point has told you something useful for free, and it has cost you nothing but the time it took to ask.

sections.heading: Where the marks are actually lost in each science
paragraphs: Science grades in this corridor are rarely lost evenly across a paper. They cluster, and the clusters are predictable enough that a tutor who knows the course can name them before seeing a script. That predictability is useful, because it means a family with a limited number of hours can target the clusters rather than revising the syllabus from the beginning, which is what happens by default.

In physics, electricity and electromagnetism cost more marks than any other topic, and the practical paper adds a second cluster around uncertainty, graph gradients and significant figures. In chemistry the clusters are moles calculations and organic reaction pathways, with a third cluster of marks lost to imprecise language across the whole paper. In biology the content is broadly learnable alone and the cluster is in extended-response structure, where a correct but unordered answer collects a fraction of the available credit.

What makes these worth targeting is that they are compact. Electricity is a defined body of work. Moles calculations are a technique. Extended-response structure is a format that can be taught in two sessions and then practised. Compare that with a plan that works forward through the syllabus from topic one: six weeks in, the student has revised material they already knew and has not reached the cluster that was costing them the grade. sections.heading: Tiers, double awards and the content nobody should be revising
paragraphs: Two decisions made by the school govern what your child should be revising, and families routinely do not know either of them. The first is the tier: Core or Extended at Cambridge, Foundation or Higher at Pearson. The second, in the sciences, is whether the entry is for separate sciences or for a double award. Both decisions remove content as well as adding it, and revising removed content is pure waste that nobody notices because it looks like diligence.

The tier decision usually lands between the autumn and spring mocks of Year 11, on mock evidence, and parents can reasonably ask when it is made and whether it can be revisited. The window before it is made is where tutoring has the clearest effect for a boundary student: targeted work on the specific Extended-only topics is a short, defined job. After the entry is submitted, the work changes to paper technique within the chosen tier, and the number of hours needed usually falls.

The double-award question is more often mishandled, because a double award is not a simplified version of three separate sciences. It cuts specific sub-topics while keeping others at full depth, so a tutor working from the separate-science specification covers material that will not be assessed and may miss emphasis that will be. The remedy is a single syllabus audit session at the start: confirm the code, the tier, the paper pattern, the calculator rules, and then produce a written topic list the student can revise from without supervision.

sections.heading: The exam zone rule that catches families every series
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That is a strong statement from an examination board and it exists because the mistake is common. A timetable found through a general search may be for another zone, with different dates and different clash arrangements.

The practical consequence for an Al Reef family is that the only timetable worth planning from is the one your child's school publishes for its own centre. Ask for it, and build the revision block backwards from the first paper in the weakest subject rather than from a general idea of exam season. Where a tutor produces a timetable, check which zone it is for before anybody schedules anything around it.

The second half of the calendar question is the series itself. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two: the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with documented lead times that show why planning happens early. The November 2026 final Pearson timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A provider offering a February entry to a child in Abu Dhabi has told you something about their accuracy.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to teach your child for money
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE operates under a permit system, and a local search returns names rather than permissions. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source and has been left out deliberately. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. The permit attaches to the individual, so no platform can hold it on a tutor's behalf.

There is a second rule that catches families by surprise in this emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than taken from the policy text, so verify it against the current ADEK document. It is also worth stating plainly that IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from ADEK, KHDA, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and any provider claiming one should be asked to produce it.

sections.heading: Availability, disclosed before the trial
paragraphs: Every provider in this market implies unlimited supply and none of the competitor pages studied for this search discloses a coverage limit. The useful alternative is to say which requests are easy and which are not, because a family that knows can plan around it. From Al Reef, the honest picture divides cleanly between mainstream codes and a short list of harder ones.

Mainstream requests move quickly. Mathematics 0580 or 4MA1, Physics 0625, Biology 0610, English as a Second Language 0510: a match and a trial within a few days, because online delivery means availability is not restricted to tutors willing to drive out past the airport road. Harder requests take longer. Coordinated Sciences 0654 needs somebody who knows which sub-topics the double award cuts. Edexcel-specific science codes need somebody who has taught Pearson rather than Cambridge. Arabic as a first language is treated as a specialism by the regulators themselves.

Where a specialist is based outside the UAE, that is stated before the trial rather than discovered afterwards, and the session is scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so it suits an Al Reef evening. Where nothing suitable is free, the options are a short wait, a narrower piece of work with a second tutor while the specialist frees up, or a referral elsewhere. The one option that reliably costs more is a fast general match, because the diagnostic sessions get repeated when the right person becomes available, and a family ends up paying twice for the same reading of the same script.

sections.heading: Using the free hour properly
paragraphs: A free trial answers in sixty minutes what no profile, review or phone call can answer, provided you decide in advance what you are testing. Used badly it becomes an introductory conversation, and the decision ends up resting on the same impressions you were trying to get past. Used well it is the cheapest piece of due diligence available in this market, and it costs nothing, takes no card details and creates no commitment.

Send the material first: the board, code and tier, the school, and the marked mock script with the teacher's annotations intact. Then watch for three things. Does the tutor work from that script rather than from a generic topic? Can they separate content losses from method losses from timing losses? And can they name a syllabus topic that is not assessed at your child's tier, which is the quickest proof that they are reading a specification rather than remembering a subject.

Afterwards, ask your child one question: did you follow it? That is the judgement nobody else can make, and it matters more than credentials at this level, because a student who will not ask a question in a session is paying for a monologue. Finish with the two closing questions for the provider: what happens if the match is wrong, and what will you refuse to do. Three providers tested the same way inside a week gives a genuine comparison, and it is quicker than arranging for anybody to drive to Al Reef.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor knows my child's IGCSE syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions. Which code and tier is my child entered for, and what are the papers? Name one topic in that syllabus that is not assessed at this tier. From this marked script, which lost marks are content, which are method not shown, and which are timing? And what wording does the mark scheme credit for a common question in this subject? Somebody who has taught the course answers all four immediately. Somebody who knows the subject but not the specification cannot exclude any topic, which is the clearest signal of the four.

faqs.question: Why does the syllabus code matter more than the subject?
faqs.answer: Because the code determines what is assessed, which papers are sat, what formulae are provided and what wording a mark scheme credits. Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are both IGCSE chemistry and they are not the same examination. A tutor matched to chemistry rather than to the code will teach correct chemistry against the wrong question style, and the first visible symptom is a mock result that makes no sense given the hours the student has clearly put in.

faqs.question: Does my child sit separate sciences or a double award?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it changes what should be revised. A double award such as Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 is not a simplified version of three separate sciences: it removes specific sub-topics while keeping others at full depth. A tutor working from the separate-science specification will cover material that is not assessed and may under-weight material that is. One syllabus audit session at the start, confirming code, tier and paper pattern, prevents a term of misdirected revision.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science topics cost the most marks around here?
faqs.answer: In physics, electricity and electromagnetism, followed by uncertainty, graph gradients and significant figures in the practical paper. In chemistry, moles calculations and organic reaction pathways, plus marks lost across the whole paper to imprecise language. In biology, extended-response structure on transport, homeostasis and inheritance, where a correct but unordered answer collects a fraction of the credit. All of those clusters are compact and teachable, which is why targeting them beats working forward through the syllabus from topic one.

faqs.question: Can we use Cambridge past papers if my child sits Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Not for full papers. Question phrasing, paper structure and formula provision differ, so practice from the wrong board teaches the right content in the wrong format and mismanages timing. Individual topic questions from the other board can be useful late in the course for extra drill where the topic is identical and the phrasing is not the point. For anything resembling a timed practice paper, use the entered board only. Confirm which it is in writing before building a revision set.

faqs.question: When does the school decide my child's tier?
faqs.answer: In this corridor the decision usually lands between the autumn and spring mocks of Year 11, based on mock evidence, and it belongs to the school. Parents can reasonably ask when it is confirmed and whether it can be revisited. For a student on the boundary, the window before the decision is where tutoring has the clearest effect, because targeted work on the specific Extended-only or Higher-only topics is a short, defined job. After entry, the work becomes paper technique within the chosen tier.

faqs.question: Which exam timetable should we plan from?
faqs.answer: Only the one your child's own exam centre publishes. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable, which is unusually strong language and exists because the mistake is common. A timetable found through a general search may be for a different zone with different dates. If a tutor produces a timetable, check which zone it covers before scheduling anything around it.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE exams in February in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any revision plan or tutoring package built around a spring sitting is built on another country's calendar, and a provider offering a February entry to a child here has told you something useful about their accuracy. Plan from the June or November series and build the block backwards from the first paper.

faqs.question: Why is the local tutor pool thin in Al Reef specifically?
faqs.answer: Distance and demand together. The community sits out towards the airport, most households travel out of it for school and work, and a tutor driving here on a weekday evening commits most of that evening to one paid hour. So the people willing to do it are few, and they are selected by geography rather than by syllabus knowledge. For an Extended-tier science or an Edexcel-specific code, geography and specialism rarely coincide, and the family is usually offered the nearest person who agrees.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, covering school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no figure appears here. The permit attaches to the individual rather than any platform, so ask the person teaching your child rather than whoever introduced them.

faqs.question: What should the first paid session actually contain?
faqs.answer: Work on the marked script, not an introduction. If the first session is spent getting to know your child and discussing how the subject is going, you have paid for something the trial hour should have covered. A properly prepared first session opens the script, identifies two or three clusters of lost marks, works on the highest-value one, and ends with a short question set to attempt alone. You should receive a written note naming the topic covered and the next target.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for past-paper marking?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and you should check whether it is inside the rate. A full Extended paper marked properly against the published scheme takes thirty to forty-five minutes, and the written feedback naming which mark was lost and why is where most visible improvement comes from. Some tutors include it, some charge separately, and some go through answers verbally in the session, which leaves no record by the following week. A higher rate that includes written marking is often the cheaper arrangement.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we buy help with at once?
faqs.answer: One or two, chosen from the marked mocks rather than from which teacher sent the most worrying email. Rank the subjects by how close the mark is to a grade boundary, whether the losses cluster in a few topics or spread evenly, and whether the subject rewards technique. Subjects with evenly spread losses need content recovery rather than tutoring. Subjects already comfortably above target need nothing. Three or four parallel arrangements exhaust the budget before the term that decides the grades.

faqs.question: What happens if the right specialist is not available?
faqs.answer: You are told, which no competitor page studied for this market does at all. The options are a short wait for the right person, a narrower piece of work with a second tutor meanwhile such as paper technique or a syllabus audit, or a referral elsewhere if the wait is unreasonable. Where the specialist is based outside the UAE, that is stated before the trial and the session is timed to Gulf Standard Time. A fast general match is the option that costs most, because the diagnosis gets paid for twice.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to the house in Al Reef?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from IB Gram; visiting tutors are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Al Reef households run one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard with your child's own worksheet or marked script open, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that both the late-afternoon and the post-20:00 window are available at the same rate, and that the tutor is chosen for knowing the syllabus rather than for living within driving distance.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-reef.closingHeading: Get the code, ask the four questions, test one hour
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-reef.closingBody: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Reef is only useful if they know the syllabus your child is entered for, and that is checkable in ten minutes. Email the school for the board, code, tier and calculator rules. Send the marked script. Ask the four questions on this page of every provider, including us. Then take the free trial hour over live video, with no card details and no commitment, and ask your child afterwards whether they followed it. That answer is worth more than any credential.
