intro.heading: Al Reem Island against the next community over
paragraphs: Run the experiment. Search for an International GCSE tutor for Al Reem Island, then for Saadiyat Island, then for Khalifa City, then for Al Raha Beach. The results are substantially the same people, the same agencies and the same published rates, because the Abu Dhabi tutoring market is one market with four search terms attached to it. What changes between those searches is the travel component of an in-home quote. What does not change is the exam.

That asymmetry is worth stating early, because the whole industry around these searches implies the opposite. A page that promises local expertise in Al Reem Island and a different page promising local expertise in Al Raha Gardens are usually the same page with a place name swapped, and the reason they can be is that there is nothing genuinely local about Cambridge 0580. The syllabus is identical. The papers are identical. The grade boundaries are set across the whole candidate entry. A student in a Shams Abu Dhabi tower and a student in a Khalifa City villa sit the same examination, marked the same way, on the same day.

So what does differ by area? Three things, all of them operational. The school a child attends and therefore when their day ends. The journey an in-home tutor would make and therefore what they charge. And the density of the local teaching population, which determines how deep the in-home pool is in the first place. Al Reem Island sits at an unusual point on all three: it is dense and vertical, it has growing but still limited secondary provision, and it is reached by causeway rather than being on the mainland.

It is worth being blunt about why the industry prefers the other framing. A page claiming local expertise can be duplicated across forty neighbourhoods at almost no cost, and each copy ranks for its own search term. A page that admits the academic content is identical everywhere has to earn attention on the quality of what it says about the examination instead, which is harder and considerably rarer. The useful test for any neighbourhood tutoring page, including this one, is whether its claims would still be true if the place name were swapped.

The honest conclusion is that the area-level detail should shape your timetable and not your choice of tutor. Pick the slot around your school's finish time. Pick the person around the syllabus code your child is entered for. Those two decisions are separable, and in this market they are usually conflated, which is how a family ends up with a conveniently located tutor who has never taught Pearson 4MB1.

IB Gram makes that separation structural. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, which means the area question collapses to a scheduling question and the tutor question becomes purely about specification knowledge. The rest of this page works through the comparison in detail, with the published market rates attributed to the sources that produced them.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-reem-is.programmesIntro: Whichever Abu Dhabi community a family lives in, the International GCSE entry is one of a small number of specifications. These are the ones a tutor in this market is actually asked for.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with named syllabus codes and, in many subjects, a split into Core and Extended routes that sets the grade ceiling. The codes are the working vocabulary: 0580 Mathematics, 0606 Additional Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English Language, 0455 Economics, 0478 Computer Science.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The zone is a property of the centre, not of the neighbourhood.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other mainstream route in Abu Dhabi, with its own codes and its own question style: 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4MB1 Mathematics B, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. Tiering into Foundation and Higher where it applies. Longer unsignposted problem-solving items are a defining feature at Higher tier.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so read the live version.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before the International GCSE course, with Checkpoint tests providing the only external read on a student beforehand. A weak Checkpoint strand is a precise, early signal, and acting on it is far cheaper than acting on a Year 11 mock. Cambridge runs Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Al Reem Island families with children at a nearby campus often start here rather than in Year 11, which is the better economics. The gap that produces a grade 5 in Year 11 mathematics is usually a Year 8 algebra gap that nobody had the timetable space to close.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The sixth-form route for International GCSE students at schools without the Diploma. The jump in reading load and mathematical fluency from Extended tier to AS is the steepest in the British track, and the students who manage it are the ones whose Year 11 foundations were secure rather than crammed in the final term.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency route asks for one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, on top of five International GCSE passes. Worth knowing in Year 10, when the subject list is still being decided.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-reem-is.subjectsIntro: These subjects are requested in identical proportions across Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas and the Khalifa City corridor, which is itself the point. Each entry says what the subject assesses and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most requested subject in every Abu Dhabi community without exception. Two terminal papers, no coursework, and a tier that caps the grade. Algebraic fractions, reverse percentages and bounds in division are where Extended candidates lose most, and none of that is area-specific.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism cost the most marks, followed by the practical-skills paper where graph axes, best-fit lines and significant figures erode a grade quietly. Definitions must be given in the syllabus's own wording; a paraphrase that is conceptually right scores nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions are the three heaviest losses at Extended tier. The qualitative analysis tests on the multiple-choice paper are pure recall, which makes them the fastest marks in the specification to recover.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume in the sciences and the subject most sensitive to command terms. Describe and explain carry different marks for identical knowledge. Genetics crosses and transport in plants reward structured diagram answers rather than prose.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response hold the marks, and both are taught skills. Students in international schools often read widely and still lose marks for not addressing the brief: audience, form and purpose are explicitly assessed rather than implied.

subjects.name: English Literature (0475)
subjects.description: Passage-based questions reward close reference to the writer's language over plot summary. The common failure across every Abu Dhabi cohort is an essay that narrates the text accurately and never quotes it. Building a usable quotation bank is most of the work.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks: axes labelled, the right curve shifted in the right direction, equilibrium marked. Data-response questions require evaluation, and a list of advantages and disadvantages with no judgement caps the candidate mid-band.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Case-study driven, so marks follow application to the specific business in the paper. A candidate who memorises definitions and ignores the case text scores in the middle band regardless of how much theory they can recite accurately.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory covers data representation, networks and security; the second paper asks for pseudocode and trace tables. The trace table is the most reliable mark-gainer on the paper and the piece of revision most often skipped because it looks mechanical.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for AS Level or an IB higher level maths route. Introduces calculus, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities a year early, with multi-step questions and no scaffolding. The scarcest specialism in this market in every area.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall carried with its specific figures, plus skills: map interpretation, cross-sections and climate graphs. Naming a case study without the numbers that made it worth naming is the recurring loss across all Abu Dhabi cohorts.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum under federal rules covering Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. The first-language and additional-language routes are different courses, and placement in the wrong one is both common and correctable.

sections.heading: What actually differs between Abu Dhabi communities, and what never does
paragraphs: This is the comparison that matters, and it is short. Three things genuinely vary between Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island, Yas Island and the Khalifa City corridor. The first is school access: which campuses are reachable, and therefore what time a child's day ends and when they are home. The second is the travel component of an in-home rate, which is a function of distance and of the afternoon road conditions between a tutor's home and yours. The third is the depth of the resident teaching population, which determines whether a local pool exists at all for a given specification.

Everything academic is constant. The Cambridge 0580 syllabus is the same document in every community. The Pearson 4MA1 papers are the same papers. Grade boundaries are set across the whole entry rather than by emirate or district. The command terms are identical. The topics where Extended candidates lose marks are identical, which is why a tutor who has taught the specification anywhere can diagnose a student from Al Reem Island, Saadiyat or Khalifa City with equal accuracy.

The regulator is constant too. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the emirate, and it does not operate differently by district. If a school on Al Reem Island and a school in Khalifa City both hold an ADEK licence, that licence means the same thing in both places, and an inspection rating published for one is comparable with a rating published for the other.

Put the two lists side by side and the practical instruction follows. Use the area-level facts to set your timetable, because they are real and they determine whether a session happens. Use the specification facts to choose the tutor, because they are the only facts that determine whether the session is any good. Conflating the two is the standard error in this market, and it is the error that a page promising local expertise in one neighbourhood is designed to encourage.

sections.heading: Three communities, one quote: how the travel component moves
paragraphs: Published market bands put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, at AED 180-500. Bestimate's 2026 rate table quotes AED 180-350 for in-home work; independent home tutors quote AED 200-500. Entry-level online rates run lower, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Specialist International GCSE and A Level tutors run AED 200-450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270.

Within the in-home band, the variable that moves a quote for the same tutor and the same subject is the journey. A tutor living in Al Khalidiyah quoting for an Al Reem Island visit has a short causeway run. The same tutor quoting for Yas Island has a longer inland loop. The same tutor quoting for Saadiyat has a bridge crossing. Three different numbers, one tutor, identical teaching. That is the whole of the area-level price variation in this market.

The comparison across communities therefore produces a counter-intuitive result. The communities where in-home tutoring is most expensive and the pool shallowest are the islands, which are also the communities whose families are most likely to search for a local tutor. The community where in-home is cheapest and the pool deepest is Khalifa City, which is where most of the tutors live. A family on Al Reem Island paying the island premium is subsidising a journey from a neighbourhood that could have taught them over video for less.

IB Gram does not sell the in-home option anywhere in the UAE, so there is no premium to compare. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time, and the rate does not change between Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas or the mainland because nothing about the delivery changes. The figures above are published market rates attributed to the sources that produced them, included so that a quote can be judged rather than accepted.

sections.heading: The school day across the four communities
paragraphs: Scheduling is the one place where neighbourhood detail genuinely changes the answer, and it changes it by an hour or more. Campuses serving these communities finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions running to roughly 16:15 on the days a student has them. The variable is not the finish time. It is the journey after it.

A student at a campus on Al Reem Island itself can be home before 15:45, which makes a 16:30 start workable. A student commuting from the island to the Khalifa City corridor is typically not home before 16:15, and later on an activity day, which pushes the honest earliest start to 17:30. The reverse case is identical: a Khalifa City resident at a central Abu Dhabi school faces the same arithmetic in mirror image.

Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and across all four communities the slots that survive an exam term are the ones at 18:00 and 18:30. The reason is not preference but resilience: a slot that only works on an untroubled week will break within a fortnight, and a term of cancelled sessions is a term of unused tuition that was still budgeted for.

One structural advantage of video delivery is worth naming here, because it is the thing that differs most from an in-home arrangement. When a school day overruns, an online session moves to later the same evening. An in-home session is either taken late with the tutor waiting, which is charged, or cancelled, which is lost. Across a two-year course that difference compounds into a meaningful number of delivered hours.

sections.heading: Where International GCSE marks are lost, in every postcode
paragraphs: The loss pattern is the strongest evidence that the academic problem is not local. Ask a specialist where Extended and Higher candidates lose marks and the list that comes back is the same whether the student lives on Al Reem Island, in Khalifa City or in another emirate entirely, because it is a property of the specification rather than of the cohort.

Algebraic fractions come first in mathematics: cancelling across a sum instead of a factor, and changing the subject of a formula where the subject appears twice. Reverse percentages come next, and they are worth isolating because dividing by the wrong base loses the entire question rather than part of it. In the sciences, electricity and magnetism cost the most in Physics, moles and electrolysis half-equations in Chemistry, and command-term misreading in Biology, where describe and explain carry different marks for identical knowledge.

In the essay subjects the pattern is equally consistent. English Language candidates lose marks for not addressing the brief: audience, form and purpose are explicitly assessed. English Literature candidates narrate the text instead of quoting it. Economics candidates produce accurate diagrams and then list advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement, which caps them mid-band. Business Studies candidates recite theory without reference to the case in front of them.

Each of those is a bounded piece of work. A student with four such problems has perhaps six hours of targeted repair ahead, not a year of general tutoring, and the repair is identical in every neighbourhood. That is why the honest version of a local tutoring page tells a parent that the local part is the timetable and the rest is specification work available from anyone who knows the code.

sections.heading: The series, the centre and the zone
paragraphs: One genuinely non-local fact deserves a section, because families often assume it is local. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June series and the November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting it at an Abu Dhabi parent is quoting the wrong country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

What is centre-specific rather than area-specific is the administrative zone. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong timetable. The zone belongs to the centre your child's school uses, which means two students living in the same Al Reem Island tower but attending different schools can sit the same paper at different times of day.

Counting backwards from a June sitting: results reach centres in August, final entries close months earlier, mocks fall in the spring term, and the last realistic point for a tier change sits earlier still. For a November sitting, the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026.

The planning consequence for tutoring is the same across every community. Eight weeks of timed-paper work has to be scheduled during the spring term for a June sitting rather than organised after the mocks come back, because by then the calendar has closed in. A November resit decision opens the day August results arrive and closes well before the exam. Read the live timetable on the board's own site and confirm the zone with the school's exams officer.

Pearson International GCSE runs May/June and November

sections.heading: The two checks that are identical in every community
paragraphs: Whatever neighbourhood a family lives in, two pieces of due diligence are the same and both are cheap. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Because the permit costs nothing and takes two working days, an independent tutor without one has no cost excuse, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is unverified and should be treated as such. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal category and requires an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant authority.

The second check concerns claims. Regulator approval is a specific licence with a number, not an adjective. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre. We name those bodies on this page to explain what each one governs. Any provider claiming otherwise about itself is making a checkable statement.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point that applies across all four communities equally. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as exact policy wording, and we do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school.

No fine schedule is published, so treat any penalty figure quoted to you as unverified

sections.heading: The honest version of a neighbourhood tutoring page
paragraphs: If a page about International GCSE tutoring in one Abu Dhabi community is going to be worth reading, it has to say which of its claims would survive being moved to the next community over. On this page, the claims that survive are all the specification ones: the codes, the tiers, the loss patterns, the series, the permit, the authorship boundary. The claims that do not survive are the timetable ones, and those are stated as arithmetic rather than as local colour.

What that leaves out is the usual material of these pages: descriptions of the neighbourhood's character, lists of amenities, assertions that local tutors understand local families. None of it changes a grade. A tutor who understands Cambridge 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier will serve a student in a Shams Abu Dhabi tower exactly as well as one in a Khalifa City villa, and a tutor who does not will fail both equally while living closer to one of them.

The one place where local knowledge is genuinely useful is in reading a school's own pattern. Which campuses enter which board, which offer Additional Mathematics 0606 as an extra, when a given school's internal deadlines fall, and how long the afternoon run from that campus actually takes. That is real and it is operational, and it belongs in a conversation with the school rather than being inferred from a page.

So the recommendation at the end of a comparison page is deliberately anticlimactic. Get the syllabus code and tier in writing from the school. Work out when your child is genuinely home from their specific campus. Then pick the person who teaches that code every week, from wherever they happen to be, and fix the session in the window the arithmetic gives you. The answer comes out the same in Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas and Khalifa City, which is the finding this page exists to report.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE tutoring in Al Reem Island different from tutoring in the next community over?
faqs.answer: Operationally yes, academically no. What differs between Abu Dhabi communities is school access and therefore when a child is home, the travel component of an in-home quote, and how deep the resident teaching pool is. What does not differ is the syllabus, the papers, the grade boundaries or the topics where marks are lost, because those are properties of the specification rather than of the postcode. Use the area facts to set your slot and the specification facts to choose the tutor.

faqs.question: Why does the same tutor quote a different rate for Al Reem Island and Yas Island?
faqs.answer: Because the journey differs and nothing else does. Published in-home bands run AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online, and the gap inside the in-home band is travel. A tutor based centrally faces a short causeway run to Al Reem, a longer inland loop to Yas and a bridge crossing to Saadiyat. Three numbers, one tutor, identical teaching. That is the whole of the area-level price variation in this market.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi community has the deepest pool of in-home IGCSE tutors?
faqs.answer: Khalifa City, comfortably, because it holds the largest resident population of secondary teaching staff in the emirate. The islands have the thinnest pools and attract the highest in-home quotes, which produces an awkward result: the families most likely to search for a local tutor are the ones least likely to find a suitable one nearby. An Al Reem Island family paying the island premium is usually subsidising a journey from a neighbourhood that could teach over video for less.

faqs.question: Does ADEK treat schools on Al Reem Island differently from mainland schools?
faqs.answer: No. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools across the whole emirate, and a licence means the same thing on the island as on the mainland. An inspection rating published for an Al Reem Island campus is comparable with one published for a Khalifa City campus. That consistency is useful: it means a parent comparing two schools in two communities is comparing like with like, which is not true of everything in this market.

faqs.question: Are the IGCSE papers the same wherever in the UAE my child sits them?
faqs.answer: The papers and the grade boundaries are the same, because boundaries are set across the whole candidate entry rather than by region. What can differ is the time of day, because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and the correct timetable version depends on the zone. Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone's timetable. The zone belongs to your child's centre, so ask the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: My family is moving from Al Reem Island to Khalifa City. Does the tutoring change?
faqs.answer: Only the slot, unless the school changes too. If your child stays at the same campus, the commute changes and the session time may need to move, which is a five-minute conversation. If the campus changes, the real question is whether the board or tier changes with it, because a board change needs an immediate switch of the past-paper diet and an audit of the handful of topics present in one specification and absent from the other. That is a short, specific job and it is almost never done.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if we live on Al Reem Island?
faqs.answer: It depends on the campus rather than the island. A student at a school on Al Reem Island or in central Abu Dhabi is often home between 15:30 and 15:50, which makes 16:30 workable. A student commuting to the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor is usually not home before 16:00 to 16:30, so 17:30 is the honest earliest. Our range runs 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the slots that survive an exam term across every community are 18:00 and 18:30.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit apartments in Shams Abu Dhabi or the Gate District?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and that includes every district of Al Reem Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video. On a comparison page this is the cleanest consequence of the argument: with no journey to price, the service and the rate are identical in Al Reem Island, Saadiyat, Yas and on the mainland.

faqs.question: Do local tutors understand local schools better than online ones?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth separating what that knowledge is. Useful local knowledge is about schools: which campus enters which board, which offers Additional Mathematics 0606 as an extra, when a given school's internal deadlines fall, and how long the afternoon run takes. None of that requires living nearby, and all of it is available by asking the school. What local knowledge does not provide is specification expertise, which is the thing that actually moves a grade.

faqs.question: Which topics cost Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidates marks regardless of where they live?
faqs.answer: In mathematics: algebraic fractions, changing the subject of a formula where the subject appears twice, reverse percentages, bounds in division and frequency density. In Physics: electricity and magnetism, plus graph discipline on the practical-skills paper. In Chemistry: moles, electrolysis half-equations and organic conditions. In Biology: command terms, where describe and explain carry different marks for identical knowledge. In the essay subjects: not addressing the brief, and evaluation without a judgement. The list is specification-level, not local.

faqs.question: Should I choose a tutor who lives nearby if the rate is the same?
faqs.answer: Only if they also teach your child's syllabus code every week, which on an island is unlikely. Proximity is a tiebreaker rather than a criterion. If two tutors both teach Cambridge 0580 Extended regularly and one is nearer, the difference is immaterial in an online arrangement anyway. If the nearer one teaches a different specification, proximity is buying you a term at the wrong depth for the same money, which is the most expensive form of convenience available.

faqs.question: How much do IGCSE tutors charge across Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published bands are AED 45-150 an hour at entry level, with EdFlik from AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52; AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, with Unitors listing International GCSE from AED 150; AED 180-500 in-home with travel included, per Bestimate's AED 180-350 and independent quotes of AED 200-500; and AED 200-450 or more for specialists, with TutorChase at AED 270. The community a family lives in moves the in-home figure and nothing else.

faqs.question: Is a group class in central Abu Dhabi a reasonable alternative for an island family?
faqs.answer: It is cheaper per hour and it costs an island household a second evening journey at the time your child should be eating. A group also cannot be matched to one student's syllabus code, because the room contains several entries. For content coverage in Year 10 it can work. For Year 11 paper technique, where the value is in marking one student's own paper with them, it does not, and for a family on Al Reem Island the travel makes the trade-off worse rather than better.

faqs.question: What do I need to check about a tutor that is the same in every community?
faqs.answer: Two things. Permit status under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023: the private tuition work permit is free, valid for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, so an independent tutor without one has no cost excuse. And any claim of regulator approval, which is a numbered permit rather than an adjective. IB Gram holds no such approval from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson, and says so.

faqs.question: When should the timed-paper work start for a June sitting?
faqs.answer: During the spring term, not after the mocks are returned. Eight weeks of paper work has to be scheduled while the calendar still has room, and each full paper costs one session to sit and one to mark properly, so the hours add up faster than families expect. For a November sitting the pattern shifts: the decision window opens when August results arrive and closes well before the exam. This timing is identical in every Abu Dhabi community, because the series is.

Only the timetable and the travel change. So set the session time from your own school run, choose the tutor from the syllabus code, and stop paying for proximity. IB Gram teaches Abu Dhabi students one-to-one over live video at the same arrangement in every community, with a free trial lesson first and no card details taken.

intro.heading: A long day before Year 11, and a completely different day once study leave starts
paragraphs: Al Samha lies in the north of the emirate off the Dubai road, past Al Shahama and Al Rahba. There is no large cluster of British-curriculum schools immediately here, so students travel, usually by bus, towards Khalifa City, Al Raha, Yas Island or the island itself. The journey is long at both ends, which means a Year 10 or Year 11 student in this corridor is working inside a shorter evening than a student living near their school, with exactly the same examinations at the end of it.

That makes the tutoring question a scheduling question first. A session that starts the moment a tired student walks through the door achieves little. A session that takes the one genuinely productive hour of the evening leaves nothing for the homework their own teachers set. And an in-home arrangement adds a tutor's forty-minute drive at each end, so the lesson starts later and the evening ends later still. Published in-home rates in this market are AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and from this corridor that travel is a real component.

There is a second, less obvious fact that matters more than any of this for a Year 11 family. The school year does not end with the same shape it started. Once study leave begins and the series is underway, the long bus run largely disappears, exam mornings replace school days, and a student suddenly has whole afternoons of unstructured time. Almost nobody plans for that, and it is the single largest block of usable time a Year 11 student in this corridor will ever get.

The third fact is cheap and frequently ignored: a good deal of the help a family needs is already paid for. School departments run clinics, revision sessions and drop-in help, often unadvertised, and the teacher who marks your child's work knows the gap better than any external tutor. In a corridor where travel eats the week, an after-school club that happens before the bus leaves costs no evening time at all, which makes it the most efficient help available anywhere in this corridor.

IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched to the syllabus code the school entered. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Out here the format matters practically rather than philosophically: the session starts at the booked minute whatever the road is doing, it can be moved to an afternoon during study leave without anybody rearranging a drive, and the tutor is chosen from people who have taught that board rather than from the few who would travel this far for a single lesson on a weekday evening.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal written papers with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, A* to G grading, and science assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test depending on what the centre enters. programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate here sits June with November as the resit route. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, so work from the school's version.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 on the 9 to 1 grade scale, with mathematics tiered into Foundation, capped at grade 5, and Higher, running 9 down to 4 with grade 3 available. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers in most routes.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs May and June and again November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. programmes.name: Post-16: A-Levels or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: The two routes an IGCSE student moves into. A-Levels narrow to three or four subjects examined terminally; the Diploma takes six subjects with internal assessments spread across two years. The second is considerably harder to carry alongside a long daily commute.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-samha.subjectsIntro: Each subject below carries a note on how it behaves in a short evening, because that is the practical question in this corridor rather than which topics exist.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: Cumulative and procedural, so it tolerates short sessions well and rewards frequency over length. Non-calculator fluency in particular is best built in fifteen-minute timed blocks rather than in one long weekly stretch.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1
subjects.levels: Core, Extended, single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Calculation work suits short sessions; the alternative-to-practical paper and extended six-mark explanations need a continuous stretch. Split those two kinds of work across different days rather than mixing them at the end of a long one.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1
subjects.levels: Core, Extended, single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Organic pathways and qualitative analysis reward frequent short exposure, because recall decays quickly between weekly sessions. Mole calculations need a clear head, so they belong early in the evening rather than late.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1
subjects.levels: Core, Extended, single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The most forgiving subject to study late in a long day, because the work is recall and answer structure. Command-term discipline, describe against explain against evaluate, is worth more marks here than additional content.

subjects.name: English First Language, Cambridge 0500 or 0990
subjects.description: Timed analysis is the examined skill and needs an uninterrupted hour, which makes it a poor fit for a short weekday slot and a good fit for a weekend block or a study-leave afternoon.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language, Cambridge 0510 or 0511
subjects.description: A different syllabus from First Language English, with 0511 carrying a speaking component. Confirm which your child is entered for before buying anything, because the assessment criteria differ and so does the preparation.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study papers rewarding application to the given context. Diagram practice works in twenty-minute blocks; full case-study answers need a continuous stretch and are better placed at a weekend.

subjects.name: Geography, Cambridge 0460
subjects.description: Skills questions on maps, graphs and data are highly practisable and routinely under-practised. They suit short sessions; case-study detail needs memorising work the student does alone.

subjects.name: History, Cambridge 0470 or 0977
subjects.description: Source-based assessment where structure decides the mark. Essay planning can be taught in short sessions; full timed answers need an hour and belong in a weekend or study-leave slot.

subjects.name: Alternative-to-practical technique
subjects.levels: Where the centre enters this route
subjects.description: Apparatus diagrams, uncontrolled variables, method criticism, results tables and graph scales. A separate examined skill with its own mark-scheme language, reliably untrained, and one of the clearest recoverable gains before a series.

subjects.name: Past-paper marking and error logging
subjects.description: Marking a paper strictly against the published scheme and classifying every lost mark. The highest-value activity available and one a student can do alone once shown how, which matters when evening time is scarce.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies
subjects.description: Required in private schools regardless of the international curriculum, with separate class organisation for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. They occupy timetable space all year and belong in the weekly plan.

sections.heading: The direct answer, and the two parts of the year that need different plans
paragraphs: To the search itself: an IGCSE home tutor in Al Samha, through IB Gram, means a subject specialist matched to your child's syllabus code and tier, teaching one-to-one over live video at a time that fits the bus, with a free trial lesson used as a diagnosis. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and the market rate for in-home tuition in this emirate is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included.

The year splits into two periods that need different arrangements, and most tutoring plans ignore the second. From September to the start of study leave, time is the scarce resource: a long bus run, a compressed evening, and a homework load set by teachers who may live ten minutes from the school. Plans here should be modest, short and frequent, and should protect the student's own working time rather than competing with it.

From the start of study leave to the last paper, time stops being scarce and becomes abundant and unstructured, which is its own problem. A student with four free afternoons a week and six papers left can waste the lot or can convert it into the largest single gain of their school career. The decision is made in about the third week of that period, by which point the habit has formed either way.

Tutoring should change shape across that boundary. Before study leave, keep it light and aimed at recurring errors. During study leave, move it into afternoons, target the next paper on the timetable rather than the syllabus, and keep sessions short because the student is sitting examinations in the mornings. A provider that runs the same weekly slot through both periods has not noticed that the year changed.
bullets: Term time: time is scarce, so sessions stay short and protect homework
Study leave: time is abundant and unstructured, which needs a plan
Target the next paper during the series, not the whole syllabus
Expect the arrangement to change shape, not just continue

sections.heading: Where students from this corridor sit their IGCSEs, and what that does to the week
paragraphs: Every family here has already chosen a school elsewhere, which means the tutoring plan follows the bus rather than the address. A student at a Khalifa City school with an earlier finish has a usable slot from about half past four. A student bussed to the island is often not home until five or later, and on a bad afternoon considerably later than that.

Those two students need different arrangements, and a provider offering one standard evening slot is serving one of them poorly. The information that resolves it is simple and specific: which school, what time the bus actually arrives, and what else already occupies the evening. Families rarely volunteer it because nobody asks, and it matters more out here than the choice between two equally qualified tutors.

The board mix across these schools is also worth checking rather than assuming. Both Cambridge and Pearson appear in this corridor's schools, sometimes within the same school across different subjects, which means a parent needs the syllabus code and the tier in writing before any revision materials are bought or any tutor is booked. A student revising from the wrong board's papers loses weeks without anybody noticing.

The table below sets out the pattern by destination. It is about time rather than school quality, which is ADEK's domain: read inspection ratings on ADEK's own site and use this to plan the week around whatever school you have chosen. The destination, not the address, is what sets the shape of a workable evening here.

sections.heading: Study leave: the largest block of usable time a Year 11 student gets
paragraphs: Once study leave begins, a Year 11 student in this corridor gains back two hours a day of travel plus most of a school timetable. Over several weeks that is a substantial number of hours, and how they are used decides a meaningful part of the result. The common failure is not laziness; it is the absence of structure. A student used to a bell-driven day is handed four unstructured afternoons and no plan.

The structure that works is built from the exam timetable backwards, paper by paper. Each day has one obvious target: the next paper, or the one after it. Mornings during the series are for sitting examinations; the afternoon belongs to the next paper on the list, in short blocks with breaks, and the evening should be short because the next morning is another examination.

Tutoring in this period is specific and small. A forty-minute session targeting the exact paper coming next, working the question types that have historically lost marks, is worth more than a ninety-minute general revision session. Sessions should be bookable at short notice, because a student who has just sat a paper knows precisely what went wrong and that information expires quickly.

There is one more thing a northern family should plan deliberately: the journey to the examination centre. The centre is the school, which means the long run returns on exam mornings, usually with a fixed and unforgiving start time. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable version for each and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, so the timetable the school issues is the only one worth planning from.

sections.heading: The help you are already paying for, and why it costs no evening
paragraphs: In a corridor where travel consumes the week, help that happens before the bus leaves is worth more per hour than help that happens after it. Most school departments run some combination of clinics, revision sessions, drop-in help and lunchtime support, and a substantial number of families never ask about them because they are not advertised in a newsletter.

The teacher running those sessions also has an advantage no external tutor can match: they mark your child's work, they set the mock, and they know the specific gap. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student the sequence that makes sense is to exhaust that first, then look outside for what the school cannot cover. It costs nothing and it costs no evening, which in this corridor is the scarcer currency.

The second free resource is a classmate on the same syllabus code and tier. Explaining a method to another student is among the most efficient revision techniques available, and two students who travel the same bus route can work on the journey itself, which converts dead time into study time. The condition is the same code and tier; otherwise the practice misleads.

The third is the student's own past-paper work, marked strictly against the published scheme with every lost mark classified by topic and type. This is the highest-value revision activity available in any subject, it needs no tutor once the student has been shown how, and it is the thing that tells a family whether paid help is actually needed and for what. We cite and link board materials rather than redistributing them, since reproducing papers and schemes is a copyright matter.

sections.heading: Cost per usable hour, which is not the same as cost per hour
paragraphs: In this corridor the right unit is cost per usable hour. An hour bought at six in the evening from a student who has travelled two hours and eaten nothing is not the same hour as one bought at ten on a Saturday morning. Both appear identically on an invoice. Only one of them produces marks, and the second one costs the same.

With that in mind, the published bands read in October 2026: budget online tuition at AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500; IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, TutorChase publishing AED 270; premium examiner-led tuition at AED 500 to 650 and above, BartyED publishing AED 650. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The qualified band covers nearly every genuine IGCSE need: board-correct past-paper marking, tier judgement, alternative-to-practical technique and the extended-answer work that separates grade bands. Where a family in this corridor should spend differently is on timing rather than on tier. Two weekend hours at the qualified rate will usually outperform three tired weekday hours at the specialist rate, which is an unusual thing for a tutoring page to say and is nonetheless true.

All of these are market rates from named published sources rather than IB Gram prices; ours is quoted after the free trial lesson once the code, tier and session length are known. And the structural point: an in-home rate out here includes a journey of forty minutes or more each way, which is time nobody is taught in.

sections.heading: Entries, zones and the resit route for a candidate in the north
paragraphs: Entries are made by the school as the examination centre, which also controls tier deadlines and issues the timetable. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version per zone, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a family who will be driving to the centre on exam mornings, that timetable is also a travel document.

Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only, so a candidate in this corridor sits June with November as the resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

The resit decision should be made from the component breakdown rather than from how the results felt. Ask the examinations officer which paper and which question types lost the marks, check the actual grade requirement for the post-16 route, and then decide whether a November entry with targeted work is likely to move it. Preparing a resit the same way as the first attempt tends to reproduce the result.

One practical note specific to this corridor: a November resit sits in a term when the student has also started a post-16 course, with the same long bus run restored. That makes the time budget tighter than it was in the summer, so a resit plan should be deliberately narrow, aimed at the two or three question types the breakdown names rather than at the subject as a whole.

sections.heading: Checks before anyone teaches your child, in either format
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted at you is unverified. Since the permit is free, there is no cost reason for a working tutor to lack one, and asking to see it takes seconds. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff are also reported to bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so avoid that arrangement however convenient it looks.

Two further claims deserve suspicion. No individual tutor is approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, because those bodies regulate schools rather than approving tutors; a tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal. And no tutor should be presented as a Cambridge or Pearson examiner without evidence of current status.

For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of those bodies and no UAE office, publishes no satisfaction statistics, and does not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are published by the boards and should be reached there or through the school.

sections.heading: What we do when the slot you need is gone
paragraphs: The early-evening window is the most contested time of the week across the whole emirate, and this corridor needs it later than most because the bus arrives later. Combine that with a board specialism and a peak week before mocks or the June series, and sometimes there is nothing available at the time you want.

When that happens you are told, and given the options in writing rather than having one chosen for you: a different qualified tutor on the same syllabus code at a workable time; a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same board, disclosed before booking and scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, which for a late-evening slot sometimes improves availability rather than worsening it; a weekend block instead of a weekday session; shorter sessions at higher frequency; or a named wait with a date.

For this corridor the weekend option is usually the best answer rather than the consolation. The time genuinely exists, the student is rested, and the work that needs continuous attention can only happen there. Families protect weekends instinctively and treat weekday evenings as flexible, when out here the reverse is closer to the truth.

The free trial lesson is where the pattern gets tested rather than assumed. One full lesson with the matched tutor, no card required, run at the slot under consideration so the fatigue question is answered honestly. It should produce a named list of recurring errors, a view on whether the tier is right, and a recommended pattern for the student's actual week, including the case where the honest recommendation is the school's own clinic and three sessions rather than a term.

process.title: Send the code, the tier and the arrival time
process.description: The syllabus code and tier from the school in writing, the school your child travels to, and when the bus actually gets in. Those three decide both who can teach your child and when, and out here the second part is the harder constraint.

process.title: Try the free help first
process.description: We will ask whether you have spoken to the head of department about clinics and revision sessions, because help that happens before the bus leaves costs no evening. If that covers the gap, it is the better answer and we will say so.

process.title: Free trial lesson at the real slot
process.description: One full lesson, no card required, run at the time being considered rather than at a convenient one, so the question of whether your child can work at that hour is answered honestly and not theoretically.

process.title: A pattern for term time and a different one for study leave
process.description: Short and frequent during term, protecting the homework window. Afternoon and paper-targeted once study leave begins. The plan says explicitly what changes at that boundary rather than running the same slot through both.

process.title: Re-test, then reduce
process.description: After six to eight weeks a fresh paper is marked against the correct board's scheme and the new error log compared with the first. If the logged failures have gone, the recommendation is fewer sessions or none rather than an automatic renewal.

whyPoints.title: The bus time asked for first
whyPoints.description: Two neighbours in Al Samha can have school days ending forty minutes apart depending on where they travel. Asking for the arrival time before anything else is what makes a slot workable rather than theoretically available.

whyPoints.title: Study leave treated as a planned period
whyPoints.description: Once the series starts, a Year 11 student gains back the commute and most of a timetable. Structuring those afternoons paper by paper is the largest single gain available in this corridor, and almost nobody plans for it.

whyPoints.title: Free school help named before paid help
whyPoints.description: Department clinics, the teacher who marks the work, a classmate on the same code and self-marked past papers cost nothing and cost no travel. Recommending them first loses us bookings and is the correct order.

whyPoints.title: Cost measured per usable hour
whyPoints.description: Three tired weekday hours and two rested weekend hours look identical on an invoice and are not the same purchase. For this corridor the timing decision matters more than the tier of tutor chosen.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Both Cambridge and Pearson appear across this corridor's schools, sometimes within one school. Matching on the code prevents weeks of revision from the wrong board's papers, which is invisible to a parent until it is costly.

whyPoints.title: The UAE-correct exam rules
whyPoints.description: Cambridge February and March is India-only; here it is June and November, and the timetable to plan from is the school's own version for its administrative zone. On exam mornings that timetable is also a travel document.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student in this corridor use study leave?
faqs.answer: Paper by paper, built backwards from the school's exam timetable. Mornings are for sitting examinations; the main afternoon block belongs to the next paper on the list, worked in short stretches with breaks; evenings stay short because another paper follows. The common failure is unstructured general revision across four free afternoons. A student who spends fifteen minutes after each paper noting what went wrong, then targets the next one, converts the period into the biggest gain of their school career.

faqs.question: Does the long bus run disappear once exams start?
faqs.answer: Mostly, and it is replaced by something less forgiving: exam mornings with a fixed start time and the same journey to the centre, which is the school. That makes the timetable a travel document as well as an academic one. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable version, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, so plan from the version your school issues, with margin.

faqs.question: What free help should we exhaust before paying anyone?
faqs.answer: Three things, in this order. The department's clinic or revision session, which often is not advertised and happens before the bus leaves, so it costs no evening at all. The teacher who marks your child's work, asked by email for two priorities rather than a general comment. And a classmate on the same syllabus code and tier, since explaining a method is efficient revision and two students on the same bus route can use the journey itself. Then look outside.

faqs.question: Is it better to book two short sessions or one long one during term?
faqs.answer: Two short ones, for most students in this corridor. Forty minutes twice a week fits a compressed evening, keeps contact with the subject twice rather than once, and matches realistic concentration after a long bus run. The exception is work that needs continuous time: whole past papers, alternative-to-practical papers and full timed essays. Those belong at the weekend, when the student is rested and the hour is genuinely available.

faqs.question: Why do you measure cost per usable hour rather than per hour?
faqs.answer: Because an hour bought at six in the evening from a student who has travelled two hours is not the same as an hour bought on a Saturday morning, and both look identical on an invoice. For a family in this corridor, two rested weekend hours at the qualified rate of AED 150 to 300 will usually outperform three tired weekday hours at a specialist rate. The timing decision therefore matters more than the choice between two equally qualified tutors.

faqs.question: Which school day in this corridor gives the best session slot?
faqs.answer: Generally a Khalifa City destination, where several schools finish earlier and a bussed student can be home in time for a workable half past four start. Al Raha and Yas destinations typically push the first realistic slot to five, and an island school combined with a northern bus route often means 5.30pm or later. The information that settles it is not the school's reputation but its finish time plus the route, which is why we ask for both.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of a session. That paper examines written experimental skills: reading apparatus diagrams, identifying uncontrolled variables, criticising a method, completing results tables with consistent significant figures and choosing graph scales. All of it can be worked on a shared screen with the paper and mark scheme open for both people. What cannot be done remotely is handling apparatus, which belongs in the school laboratory with a teacher.

faqs.question: Our child is revising from past papers that turned out to be the wrong board. What now?
faqs.answer: Put them away and download the correct board's recent papers and schemes. The content overlap is large so nothing false has been learnt, but the question conventions differ and in the sciences the experimental component may be assessed in a completely different way. Two or three sessions on the correct board's conventions usually closes the gap. The underlying fix is to get the syllabus code and tier from the school in writing and keep the reply.

faqs.question: Should we book tutoring during the exam series itself?
faqs.answer: Short, targeted sessions, yes; long general ones, no. A forty-minute session aimed at the exact paper coming next, working the question types that have previously lost marks, is worth more than ninety minutes of broad revision when the student is sitting papers in the mornings. Sessions should also be bookable at short notice, because a student who has just sat a paper knows precisely what went wrong and that information fades within a day.

faqs.question: Would an in-home tutor come out to Al Samha, and what would it cost?
faqs.answer: Some would, many decline, and those who come price the journey into the rate. Published in-home bands are AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. From this corridor that journey can be forty minutes or more each way into evening traffic, so the session starts late and the usable hour shrinks. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service runs only in India.

faqs.question: How tight is availability for the slot we actually need?
faqs.answer: Tight, because the early-evening window is the most contested across the emirate and this corridor needs it later than most. Add a specific syllabus code and a peak week before mocks or the June series and the right tutor may be unavailable at your time. You should be given the options in writing: another qualified tutor on the same code, a weekend block, a tutor based outside the UAE with the location disclosed, shorter sessions meanwhile, or a named wait.

faqs.question: Does a November resit make sense for a student in this corridor?
faqs.answer: It can, with a narrow plan. The complication is that a November entry sits in a term when the student has also started a post-16 course and the long bus run has returned, so the time budget is tighter than it was over the summer. Decide from the component breakdown: which paper and which question types lost the marks, and whether two or three specific fixes would plausibly move the grade. A resit prepared like the first attempt usually reproduces it.

faqs.question: Our Year 10 student is coping. Is it too early to do anything?
faqs.answer: Not too early to do the free things, and probably too early to pay. Ask the department about clinics, establish the syllabus code and tier in writing, and have your child mark one past paper strictly against the published scheme to see what the error pattern looks like. That costs nothing and tells you whether paid help is needed and for what. Year 10 is also the right time to raise tier entry, because the ceiling it sets is harder to change later.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to propose something sensible?
faqs.answer: Four things: the syllabus codes and tiers from the school, the school your child travels to, the time they actually get home, and a photograph of a recent marked paper. With those we can propose a pattern rather than a slot, say whether the free school options should come first, and name an honest number of sessions. An enquiry that gives only the subject produces a standard weekly slot that may not survive the week it has to fit into.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-shamkha.tutorsIntro: IGCSE tutors matched to Al Shamkha families work to a named syllabus code, tier and paper pattern. The first hour is spent on your child's own script, naming what the mark scheme did not award and why.

intro.heading: The syllabus is the brief, not the tutor's reputation
paragraphs: Al Shamkha is a large mainland residential district on the outer edge of Abu Dhabi city, substantially family housing with newer villa developments extending south, with Baniyas alongside and Mohammed Bin Zayed City between it and the centre. Most children here attend a school on the near mainland or in the Khalifa City corridor, and most of those schools enter either Cambridge IGCSE or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE.

Families comparing tutors here usually compare people: who has taught longest, who other families recommend, who lives closest. Those are weak signals. A much better one is whether the person can look at a marked script and say which command term was misread, which method mark was not awarded and why, and which topic the student has actually not secured. That is a syllabus conversation, and a parent can learn enough of it in twenty minutes to run it themselves.

So this page is written from the papers. What the mark scheme pays for. What each command term demands, since the difference between describe and explain is the difference between partial and full credit. The specific topics in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English where marks disappear every series. And how to use a past paper so that it teaches something instead of just producing a score.

The first thing to establish costs nothing: the syllabus code. Cambridge codes are four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 English First Language. Pearson Edexcel codes look like 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1. Ask the school for the code and the tier rather than the subject name, because the boards examine the same content with different papers, different tier vocabulary and different mark schemes, and a plan built for the wrong one is wasted.

The second thing to establish is which series your child sits. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only — it is not available to a candidate sitting in Abu Dhabi. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with November 2026's final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What the mark scheme actually pays for
paragraphs: An IGCSE mark is not awarded for being right. It is awarded for producing the specific thing the question asked for, in a form the scheme recognises, and the two are not the same. A student who knows the physics and writes an answer to a different question than the one in front of them scores nothing, and will tell you afterwards that they knew it.

The command term is the control. State and name want a short factual answer and nothing more; extra prose wins no marks and costs time. Describe wants the features or the pattern — what happens. Explain wants the mechanism or the reason — why it happens. Compare wants both things referenced in the same sentence, not two separate paragraphs. Evaluate wants a judgement with reasons on both sides. Suggest wants an applied answer to an unfamiliar context. Calculate wants the figure with working; determine often wants a method shown even where the answer is read from a graph.

The second control is the mark allocation, which tells a student how many distinct points the scheme contains. A four-mark explain question wants four creditable statements, not one statement expressed at length. Students who write a paragraph of good prose containing two ideas against a four-mark question lose half the marks while feeling fluent, and this is one of the commonest patterns on a marked script.

The third control is showing working. A right answer with no method collects a fraction of the available credit in mathematics and in the quantitative parts of the sciences. This is pure habit, it takes about three weeks of insistence to change, and it is free marks. The table sets the command terms out with what each demands.

sections.heading: Mathematics: where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: In Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1 alike, the losses cluster rather than spread. Algebraic manipulation is first by a distance, because almost every multi-step question at the higher tiers routes through a rearrangement or a factorisation, and an error there propagates into everything after it. One slip costs a question rather than a mark, which is why fluency here is worth more than any individual topic.

After that come four reliable offenders. Bearings, lost almost entirely to not drawing and labelling a diagram before calculating. Compound-shape surface area and volume, where several method marks exist and are forfeited because the working is not laid out in identifiable steps. Histograms with unequal class widths, which appear every series and are consistently under-practised because they feel like a minor topic. And graph questions where values are read off without the construction lines the scheme expects to see.

Then the calculator, which is examined rather than merely permitted. Angle modes left unset for a whole paper, fraction entry producing decimals, statistical functions used without recording the inputs, and correct displayed answers written down with nothing to support them. One session on calculator discipline regularly returns more marks than a topic block, and nobody offers it because it does not sound like teaching.

Where a non-calculator component is sat, add arithmetic fluency: fractions, percentages, ratio, standard form, bounds and estimation without a machine. A student who has only ever revised with the calculator on the desk will underperform their topic knowledge on that paper, and the fix is a few weeks of practice with the machine deliberately removed.

sections.heading: Physics: circuits, units and the practical paper
paragraphs: Physics losses in Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are unusually predictable. Series and parallel circuits are the first thing to go, and the reason is conceptual rather than mathematical: students learn the formulas before they are secure on which quantity is shared and which divides. Once a student can say, without hesitating, that current is the same everywhere in series and potential difference divides, most circuit questions become arithmetic.

Units and prefixes are the second. Milli, micro, kilo and mega mishandled in a calculation produce an answer wrong by a factor of a thousand, and the scheme awards nothing for a correct method with a wrong magnitude in many cases. Standard form handled carelessly does the same. This is a five-minute teaching point and a three-week habit.

Third, the diagram. Moments, equilibrium, forces on an inclined plane and ray optics are all routinely attempted without drawing or annotating anything, and all are routinely lost for exactly that reason. A labelled diagram with forces and distances marked converts most of these into a one-line calculation.

Fourth, the practical component, which rewards something students rarely revise: precise description of a method, identification of control variables, sources of error and how to reduce them, and sensible treatment of anomalous results. A student who can recite the content can still score badly here, because the paper is testing experimental reasoning rather than recall. Practising past practical questions specifically, rather than folding them into general revision, is the single most efficient physics purchase available.

The right magnitude, not just the method

sections.heading: Chemistry: moles, electrolysis and the observations you must learn
paragraphs: Chemistry in Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 has a clear hierarchy of marks. Mole calculations sit at the top: concentration, mass, volume of gas, limiting reagent and percentage yield, all of which depend on a reliable method rather than on cleverness. A student who sets every mole question out the same way — write the equation, find the moles of the known, use the ratio, convert — stops losing them.

Ionic equations are second and are usually lost to the same two errors: not cancelling spectator ions and not balancing charges as well as atoms. Both are mechanical and respond to drilling rather than explanation.

Electrolysis is third and is lost to vagueness about what happens where. Students know that something is reduced at the cathode and something oxidised at the anode, and then cannot predict the product for a molten compound versus an aqueous solution, or say what happens when the electrodes are inert rather than reactive. Learning the few rules that govern this, properly, converts a feared topic into a dependable one.

Fourth is qualitative analysis, which is unusual in the syllabus because it rewards learned observations rather than reasoning. The colour of a precipitate, whether it redissolves in excess, the gas test results — these must be memorised, and students who try to reason them out lose the marks. It is a flashcard topic sitting inside a reasoning subject, which is exactly why it gets neglected. Organic chemistry is fifth, lost mostly to reaction conditions stated loosely where the scheme wants the reagent, the catalyst and the temperature.

table.caption: CHEMISTRY: TOPIC, TRAP AND FIX

sections.heading: Biology and the command-term problem
paragraphs: Biology in Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1 has the largest content volume in the science group and the smallest proportion of losses attributable to content. The scripts show something else: students who know the material and answer a slightly different question from the one asked.

The pattern is consistent. A question says explain and the answer describes. A question asks for the function of a structure and the answer names its parts. A question gives a graph and asks for the biological reason behind a trend, and the answer reports the trend. Each of those is a complete answer to a question that was not set, and the scheme has nothing to award. The student's own account afterwards is almost always "but I knew that", which is true and irrelevant.

The data-based paper concentrates this. It rewards reading a figure accurately, describing a pattern precisely when asked, and explaining a mechanism when asked, and distinguishing those two instructions is worth more than another week of content revision. A useful drill is to take ten past questions, cover the answer space, and have the student say only what the command term is demanding before writing anything.

Content does matter in two places, and they are worth naming. Genetics and inheritance, where the losses are in setting out a cross properly with gametes shown rather than in understanding it. And transport in plants and humans, where process questions want the sequence in order and students give the components. Both reward structured practice rather than re-reading.
