sections.heading: English: the structures that recover marks fastest
paragraphs: English is the subject where families most often buy the wrong thing. The instinct is more reading, which is a long-term good and a poor exam intervention. The marks sit in structure and in following the task, and both are teachable in a few sessions.

For directed writing, the task names an audience, a form and a purpose, and the register has to match all three. A letter to a head teacher written in the voice of a magazine article loses marks that had nothing to do with the quality of the writing. The fix is a checklist the student applies before writing a word: who is this to, what form is it, what is it for, and what three points must it contain.

For summary questions, the loss is reproducing the passage. The scheme pays for identified points expressed concisely in the student's own words, and a fluent paraphrase of two points scores less than a plain list of six. The drill is to find and number the points before writing any prose, which converts the task from composition to extraction.

For composition, a repeatable structure beats inspiration under timing. A planned opening that establishes situation, a controlled middle with a small number of developed ideas, and an ending that does not simply stop — agreed in advance and practised, so that the student is not inventing a shape at the same time as inventing content. For second-language candidates, add accuracy drilling on the specific error patterns their own scripts show, and timed listening practice at speed rather than general exposure.

sections.heading: How to use a past paper so it teaches something
paragraphs: Most families use past papers as a thermometer: sit one, see the score, feel better or worse. Used properly a paper is the most powerful teaching material available, and it is free through your school's exams officer. The difference is entirely in what happens after the paper.

Step one: sit it under exam timing, in one sitting, without notes. A paper done across two evenings with the textbook open measures nothing. Step two: mark it against the real mark scheme, strictly, awarding only what the scheme awards. Generous marking is the commonest way a family destroys the value of the exercise, because it hides exactly the method and command-term losses that needed finding.

Step three, the important one: sort every lost mark into one of four categories. Knowledge, where the method was absent or wrong. Method presentation, where the answer was right and the working too compressed to credit. Misreading, where a different question was answered. Timing, where later marks were never reached. Step four: count the categories. The proportions are the plan, and they usually surprise the family — a student described as weak at a subject often loses more to presentation and misreading than to content.

Step five: act on the largest category first, not on the hardest topic. If timing dominates, practise paper order and pace rather than teaching anything. If misreading dominates, do command-term work across all subjects at once. If method presentation dominates, three weeks of insisting on visible steps. Only if knowledge dominates is a topic block the right purchase, and then the topics are named by the script rather than chosen by instinct.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the content that separates them
paragraphs: The tier decision is a syllabus question before it is anything else, and it is worth understanding in content terms rather than as a label. The higher tier does not simply ask harder versions of the same questions; it adds material. Knowing which material changes the conversation with the department from a general plea to a specific one.

In mathematics the separators are algebraic depth — quadratics, simultaneous equations, algebraic fractions, function notation — along with non-right-angled trigonometry, vectors, and multi-step questions with no signposting. In the sciences the higher tier adds content strands and more demanding quantitative work, and in several subjects a different set of papers entirely. The specifics depend on the syllabus and the exam year, which is why the current syllabus document obtained through your school is the only reliable source.

The cost of the decision lands later. A lower-tier entry caps the achievable grade, and A Level Mathematics and IB Higher Level maths normally require an Extended or Higher tier grade at a reasonable level. From Al Shamkha the sixth-form choice frequently involves a commute as well, so a closed door can mean both a resit series and a different school.

The useful action is free. Ask the department which tier your child is provisionally entered for, and what specifically would have to improve for the other tier to be viable. The second answer is a precise content brief, and four to six sessions in Year 10 aimed at exactly that content is the cheapest high-value tutoring purchase in the IGCSE.

sections.heading: Papers, mark schemes and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Since this page is about working from papers, two boundaries need stating. The first is copyright. Board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson. We reference them and link the official source rather than redistributing them, and papers come to a family through the school's exams officer or the board directly. A provider handing over a folder of scans is distributing somebody else's copyrighted material, which is also a useful signal about how they treat rules generally.

The second is assessed work. A tutor may teach the content, explain what the mark scheme rewards, question a method until the student finds its weakness, read work the student wrote and name which part undersells it, and teach honest description of a method. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or complete assessed work, produce a model answer to the live task for adaptation, or supply data the student did not collect. There is an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a published price; that is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller.

On delivery, restated because this page targets a home-tutor search: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to an Al Shamkha address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, which suits syllabus work well — the exact past-paper question goes onto a shared whiteboard beside the student's own attempt, and the marking happens where both can see it.

One regulatory note parents ask about. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with eligibility covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so distrust any quoted figure. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no UAE office.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe and explain on an IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: It is the difference between partial and full credit, and it accounts for a great many lost marks. Describe wants the features or the pattern — what happens, reported accurately and in order. Explain wants the mechanism or the reason — why it happens, usually signalled by the word because and by naming a cause. A student who describes a graph when the question said explain has written a complete answer to a question that was not set, and the mark scheme has nothing to award for it.

faqs.question: Why does the mark allocation on a question matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it tells the student how many distinct creditable points the scheme contains. A four-mark explain question wants four separate statements, not one idea expressed at length. Students routinely write a fluent paragraph containing two ideas against a four-mark question and lose half the marks while feeling that they answered well. The habit to build is to count the marks, then count the points in the answer before moving on, which takes seconds and is worth several grades across a paper.

faqs.question: Which maths topics should an Al Shamkha family prioritise?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, because almost every multi-step question at the higher tiers routes through it and one early error costs a whole question rather than a mark. Then four reliable offenders: bearings, lost to not drawing a diagram; compound-shape mensuration, lost to working written on one line; histograms with unequal class widths, which appear every series; and graph reading without construction lines. Then calculator discipline, which often returns more marks than any topic block and is almost never offered.

faqs.question: Why do capable physics students lose marks on circuits?
faqs.answer: Because they learn the formulas before they are secure on which quantity is shared and which divides. A student who can say without hesitating that current is the same everywhere in series while potential difference divides, and the reverse in parallel, converts most circuit questions into arithmetic. Add two other predictable losses: unit prefixes mishandled so the answer is wrong by a factor of a thousand, and moments or force questions attempted without drawing and annotating a diagram first.

faqs.question: How should we revise for the physics practical component?
faqs.answer: Separately, and on past practical questions rather than by folding them into general revision. The paper rewards something students rarely practise: precise description of a method another person could repeat, identification of control variables, recognition of sources of error and how to reduce them, and sensible treatment of anomalous results. A student who can recite the content will still score badly if they have never written a method out for marks. It is the most efficient physics purchase available.

faqs.question: What is the most reliable way to stop losing mole calculation marks?
faqs.answer: A fixed layout used for every mole question, without exception: write the balanced equation, find the moles of the known quantity, apply the ratio from the equation, then convert to what the question asked for. Students lose these marks by approaching each question freshly and skipping steps mentally. The method is more valuable than the understanding here, because the scheme awards identifiable steps. The same discipline fixes concentration, gas volume, limiting reagent and percentage yield questions at once.

faqs.question: Why is qualitative analysis in chemistry so often neglected?
faqs.answer: Because it is a memorisation topic sitting inside a reasoning subject, which makes it feel out of place. Precipitate colours, whether a precipitate redissolves in excess, and the results of gas tests have to be learned — a student trying to reason them out in the exam will lose the marks. It is genuinely a flashcard topic, it appears reliably, and it is quick to secure. Treating it as recall rather than as chemistry is the whole of the fix, and it costs almost nothing.

faqs.question: Our child knows biology but the grades do not reflect it. Why?
faqs.answer: Biology has the largest content volume in the science group and the smallest proportion of losses caused by content. Marked scripts show a different pattern: the question says explain and the answer describes; the question asks for a structure's function and the answer names its parts; the data question asks for the biological reason behind a trend and the answer reports the trend. Each is a complete answer to a question that was not set. A useful drill is to state what the command term demands before writing anything.

faqs.question: What actually improves an IGCSE English grade quickly?
faqs.answer: Structure and task compliance, not more reading. For directed writing, a checklist applied before writing: who is this addressed to, what form is it, what is its purpose, which three points must it contain. For summary questions, find and number the points before writing any prose, because a fluent paraphrase of two points scores less than a plain list of six. For composition, a rehearsed structure so the student is not inventing a shape and content simultaneously under timing.

faqs.question: How do we use a past paper so it teaches rather than just scores?
faqs.answer: Five steps. Sit it in one sitting under exam timing with no notes. Mark it strictly against the real scheme, because generous marking hides exactly the losses worth finding. Sort every lost mark into knowledge, method presentation, misreading or timing. Count the categories, since the proportions are the plan and usually surprise the family. Then act on the largest category first rather than on the hardest topic, and re-test with another full paper four to six weeks later to verify it.

faqs.question: What if most of the lost marks turn out to be timing?
faqs.answer: Then teaching content is the wrong purchase. Timing losses need paper-order strategy and pace practice: deciding in advance which sections to attempt first, setting a minute-per-mark budget, and practising leaving a stuck question rather than defending it. Several timed papers under strict conditions fix it, and a tutor's role is mostly to enforce the conditions and review the decisions afterwards. Families who buy topic teaching for a timing problem spend a term and see very little change on the next script.

faqs.question: How do we find out which tier our child is entered for, and can we change it?
faqs.answer: Ask the department which tier your child is provisionally entered for and what specifically would have to improve for the other tier to be viable. Both answers are free and the second is a precise content brief. The higher tier adds material rather than just difficulty — in maths, quadratics, simultaneous equations, algebraic fractions, non-right-angled trigonometry and unsignposted multi-topic questions. Four to six Year 10 sessions aimed at exactly that content is the cheapest high-value purchase in the IGCSE.

faqs.question: Which series will our child sit, and does the board change the revision?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with the February and March series offered to India only, so it is not available in Abu Dhabi. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The board changes the revision considerably: different papers, tier vocabulary, command-term phrasing, calculator policy and mark schemes, with modular unit entry available in several Pearson subjects. Get the syllabus code from the school and practise on that board's papers only.

faqs.question: Will someone come to our home in Al Shamkha for the lessons?
faqs.answer: Not from IB Gram. We run no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. For syllabus work the format suits the task: the exact past-paper question is pasted onto a shared whiteboard next to the student's own attempt and marked where both can see it, and the whiteboard persists so last week's worked answer can be reopened rather than reconstructed from a notebook.

faqs.question: Do you hand over past papers and mark schemes with the sessions?
faqs.answer: No — we cite and link them. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyrighted material belonging to Cambridge and Pearson, and a folder of scans is redistribution of somebody else's property rather than value added for you. Papers come through your school's exams officer or the board directly. What a tutor adds is the strict marking of your child's attempt against the real scheme and the naming of every loss by category, which no download can do.

The dominant category is your brief, and it is often the cheapest thing to fix. We teach live one-to-one over video in Gulf Standard Time, board-correct from session one, with no UAE home visits.

That is what makes a mock paper useful: the same person who reads it can say which marks were technique and which were content.

intro.heading: The mock has already told you what to buy
paragraphs: Al Wahda is central Abu Dhabi: dense apartment blocks around Al Wahda Mall and Hazza Bin Zayed Street, walkable, close to the Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan school belt, with a mix of British, Indian and American curriculum schools inside a short drive. Families here tend to search for a tutor at a specific moment in the year, which is the fortnight after the mock papers come back. That timing is useful, because a marked mock is the best diagnostic instrument a parent will ever be handed free of charge.

Most families use it wrongly. The mock gets read as a verdict — a number, a disappointment, a reason to act — rather than as data. Read as data it says something much more specific: which questions were left blank, which were attempted and abandoned, which earned partial credit, and where in the paper the timing collapsed. Those four patterns point at four different interventions, and only one of them is more revision.

The second fixed point is study leave. Whatever date your child's school has set, teaching effectively ends there and the structure that was holding a revision habit together disappears with it. Which means a block of tutoring should be planned to finish before study leave starts, with the leave itself planned separately and in advance. Families who discover this in the first week of study leave lose the most valuable fortnight of the year to improvisation.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a family in a central Abu Dhabi apartment that removes a real practical irritation — a stranger arriving at a specific hour, parking, the household rearranging itself around a visit — and replaces it with a fixed slot that starts on the minute agreed, with the same screen in front of both people.

This page is built around the stretch between those two dates. How to read a mock paper properly, with a table that maps symptoms to causes. How to plan study leave week by week instead of day by day. How to use the November series deliberately rather than as a failure option. What the Ramadan weeks genuinely do to revision capacity. And what central Abu Dhabi families are actually paying, with every figure attributed to whoever published it.

One framing note. Nothing here promises a grade, because nobody can. What a focused block between the mock and study leave reliably does is recover marks the student is already capable of earning and has been losing to technique. In a subject assessed entirely by written papers that is a substantial amount, and it is measurable, which is why every plan on this page ends with a second marked paper rather than an opinion.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.subjectsIntro: The subject mix from central Abu Dhabi leans towards mathematics and the sciences, with English Language and Business behind them. Each entry below names the component where the marks are actually decided.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers, no coursework. Lost marks concentrate in non-calculator arithmetic, unwritten method lines and the combined-topic final parts of long questions. Tier sets the ceiling, so the tier on the entry is worth confirming in writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical-skills paper decide most grades. Writing a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat it is a writing skill, and it is trainable in a small number of sessions with marked examples.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic pathways separate the upper grades. The recurring loss is a correct calculation presented without units or significant figures, costing two marks a question while the chemistry was understood.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Highest content volume and the subject where command terms matter most: a question asking for an explanation and receiving a description scores nothing. Transport, enzymes and inheritance recur as loss points year after year.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition carry the paper. Strong readers still lose marks for not planning, so the response drifts from the audience and purpose the question specified. Timed writing with criteria annotation moves this fastest.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A separate qualification from First Language English with different recognition. Worth checking which is on the entry, because the difference affects sixth-form and university conversations later.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the case study in the insert is most of the paper. Students who revise definitions plateau and stay there; students who practise applying three concepts to an unfamiliar business move several grades.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus evaluation. Marks are lost on unlabelled axes and on answers that explain without ever weighing one effect against another, which is what the top band asks for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and a content-heavy theory paper. Writing code by hand on paper is the skill nobody practises voluntarily and the one the paper actually tests.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Required alongside the international curriculum under the federal position, taught in separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students, and excluded from the five subjects the Ministry counts for British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Al Wahda can change after the mock
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Al Wahda, in the ordinary sense of the phrase, is a subject specialist working one-to-one with one child on the specification that child is entered for. IB Gram provides that over live video to families in central Abu Dhabi. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we offer only in India. For a household in an apartment block the online format also removes the logistics of a visitor arriving at a fixed hour, which several families here mention before we do.

The question that matters more is what the remaining weeks can achieve. After a mock and before study leave, content teaching is largely finished. What remains is the gap between what the student knows and what they scored, and in a subject assessed entirely by written papers that gap is usually substantial. It is made of unwritten method lines, command terms answered loosely, units omitted, questions attempted in printed order, and two or three topics quietly avoided for a year.

All of those are diagnosable from a marked paper and fixable in a known number of sessions. None of them are fixable by revising harder, which is the advice a disappointing mock usually produces. That distinction is the single most useful thing on this page: more hours of the same activity will not change a mark that is being lost to technique, and more hours is what most families instinctively buy.

What a block in this window cannot do is teach a specification that was never covered. Where the mock shows a third of the syllabus missing, the honest options are a longer plan, a conversation with the school about tier, or a deliberate use of the November series. We will say which of those applies after reading the paper rather than selling a block that cannot work.

sections.heading: Reading a mock paper properly: symptoms and causes
paragraphs: A mock mark on its own is almost useless. The same mark can be produced by four completely different students: one who ran out of time, one who avoided a topic, one who understood everything and wrote too little, and one who genuinely does not know the content. Each needs a different intervention, and buying the wrong one wastes the weeks that remain.

The way to tell them apart is to go through the paper question by question with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, and completed but wrong. The distribution of those labels is the diagnosis. Blanks clustered at the end of the paper mean timing. Blanks scattered through it mean topic avoidance. Partial credit everywhere means method and communication. Completed but wrong means a genuine content gap, and it is the only one of the four that needs teaching rather than training.

The table below is the version of this we use in a first session. It is worth doing even if you never hire anybody, because it converts an upsetting number into a short list of actions. Most parents in central Abu Dhabi who do this find two of the four patterns dominate, and neither of them is the one they assumed.

One practical caution: do this with the paper and the mark scheme, not with the grade sheet. Schools in this emirate vary in how much detail they return, and a grade without the script tells you nothing about where the marks went. It is reasonable to ask the subject teacher to see the marked script.

sections.heading: Planning study leave week by week rather than day by day
paragraphs: Study leave removes the one thing that was keeping a fragile revision habit alive: a timetable someone else wrote. Students who do well during it are rarely the most able; they are the ones whose week had a shape before it started. Students who struggle usually describe the same experience, which is a plan made each morning and abandoned by lunchtime.

The shape that works is weekly rather than daily, and it is built around the examination order rather than around subject preference. Each week gets a primary subject and a secondary one, mornings go to the harder subject because that is when concentration exists, and afternoons go to paper practice rather than to reading. One full timed paper a week, properly marked, is worth more than six hours of notes.

Two things need protecting deliberately. The first is sleep, which collapses first and takes everything else with it. The second is the afternoon of the day before a paper, which should be light: a confident student goes into a paper having rehearsed, not having crammed. Families in central Abu Dhabi with a short commute have an advantage here, because the morning is genuinely usable rather than spent in a car.

sections.heading: Using the November series deliberately
paragraphs: Both main boards run a November session, and UAE candidates can use it. In practice most families only hear about it after a disappointing summer result, which turns a planning option into a consolation prize. Treated deliberately, it is a genuinely useful route and sometimes the better one.

Three situations make it worth raising early with the school. A student on a tier that caps the grade below what they need, where sitting June as a baseline and targeting a focused November entry produces a better final outcome than a frantic spring. A student who has missed substantial teaching through illness or a mid-year school move, where compressing a year's content into one term is not realistic. And a student taking a large number of subjects, where spreading the load across two sittings protects the grades that matter most.

There are real costs to weigh. Entry fees for a private or additional candidate, a summer and autumn term spent still working on a subject the cohort has finished, and the sixth-form application timetable, which may want results before November grades exist. Those are conversations for the examinations officer rather than for a tutor, and they should happen before the June entry rather than after the result.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, the November window has historically run from late October into November, with the November 2026 final timetable finishing on 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge candidates sit June and November; Cambridge's February and March sitting is offered to India only, which is why a page quoting those dates to a UAE family is quoting the wrong country.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the shortened school day and revision capacity
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the local calendar beside it falls apart quickly, and in this country the Ramadan weeks are the part most often planned badly. The school day shortens, which reads on paper as extra study time. In practice children come home earlier with less energy, and the hours that appear are not hours of usable concentration.

What works is deciding in advance that the period is a maintenance phase rather than a push. Shorter sessions, placed either in the early evening or after Iftar, agreed as a fixed arrangement rather than negotiated each week. Light retrieval practice rather than new content. And an explicit acknowledgement to the student that the fortnight is deliberately lighter, which removes the guilt that otherwise makes the whole plan feel like a failure.

The weeks either side then carry the heavier work, and they should be planned to do so from the start. A family that maps six real teaching weeks and two maintenance weeks gets more done than one that optimistically maps eight and loses three to a holiday, a school event and a flat fortnight. It also costs less, because maintenance weeks can be shorter and less frequent.

The broader principle applies to the whole Abu Dhabi school year. Mark the mock window, the winter break, the Ramadan weeks and the study-leave date on one page before buying any block of tutoring. Almost every complaint we hear about a block not working traces back to it being bought for weeks that did not really exist.

sections.heading: What central Abu Dhabi families pay, and for what
paragraphs: Published market rates, read in October 2026, make the decision clearer than the brochures do. At the entry level EdFlik advertises online sessions from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit higher, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IGCSE and IB tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350.

The question is not which number is lowest but which product matches the problem. At entry-level rates a family is usually buying supervision and company, which genuinely helps a disorganised student and does almost nothing for one losing method marks on long questions. At qualified rates you are buying somebody who knows the specification. At specialist rates you are buying somebody who knows the paper, the mark scheme and what a mock paper means. A mock showing partial credit everywhere needs the third category, and buying the first instead is the most common false economy in this market.

Monthly framing helps families here more than hourly framing, because central Abu Dhabi households are budgeting against school fees that are already substantial. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Advertised monthly packages in this market have included AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

IB Gram publishes no tariff on these pages. The rate depends on subject scarcity, level and session length, and it is quoted after a free trial lesson so both sides know what is being bought. Every figure above belongs to the provider or survey named next to it, with the month it was read.

sections.heading: Permits, materials and claims nobody should make
paragraphs: Private tutoring in this country is regulated, and a parent is entitled to ask about it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so a page quoting an amount is not citing anything.

Abu Dhabi adds a rule that matters in a district as school-dense as this one. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. In a neighbourhood where several families use the same school, the apparently convenient arrangement is also the one to avoid.

On materials, the position is simple. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or International Baccalaureate syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. They belong to the boards and are published on the boards' own sites; the correct thing to do is cite and link them. A provider advertising a library of copied mark schemes is advertising a copyright problem.

Finally the claims. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership, and claims none. We name no school as a client or partner. We publish no rating or satisfaction statistic, because we cannot produce the number, date and method behind one. And we do not guarantee grades. Each of those four things is done by pages currently competing for this search, and each is a liability for the family as much as for the provider.

process.title: Send the marked mock, not the grade
process.description: The script with the marks on it is worth more than any description of the problem. Add the syllabus code, the tier and your school's study-leave date. From those four things we can say what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve before anybody is matched.

process.title: Free trial lesson built on that paper
process.description: The trial runs on questions from your child's own mock, so you watch the diagnosis rather than hear a summary of it. Afterwards you should have three named error types written down. If the tutor is not right, we match again rather than asking you to continue.

process.title: A block scoped to the study-leave date
process.description: The plan states the number of sessions, the order of the error types, and the week it finishes — before study leave, not during it. It also states what the block will not attempt, so nothing is discovered in week six.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked work between
process.description: Fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time over live video. Short homework aimed at the named error type, marked at the start of the next session. One timed section a week, annotated against the published mark scheme.

process.title: A second paper, then an honest recommendation
process.description: At the midpoint a second timed paper is marked the same way and compared with the mock by topic. The review says continue, change or stop, and stopping is a recommendation we make when the evidence supports it.

whyPoints.title: The mock is treated as evidence
whyPoints.description: Planning starts from a marked script and a mark scheme rather than from a conversation about confidence. That is the difference between a block that targets the actual losses and a term of general support that leaves the paper unchanged.

whyPoints.title: Blocks end before study leave
whyPoints.description: A plan scoped against your school's own study-leave date finishes while it can still be used. Study leave is then planned separately, as a structure problem, which is what it actually is.

whyPoints.title: The November route raised early
whyPoints.description: Where a tier or a missed term makes June unrealistic, we say so and set out the November option with its real costs. It is a planning route in this country, not a consolation prize, and raising it in the autumn is worth far more than hearing about it in August.

whyPoints.title: Short options offered first
whyPoints.description: Where the mock points at one topic, two or three sessions get recommended rather than a term. A provider who only sells terms has an incentive to find term-sized problems in every paper.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed
whyPoints.description: The dirham bands here carry the name of whoever published them and the month they were read. Three of the strongest pages for this search publish no price at all, and two quote United States dollars to families who pay in dirhams.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling for a dense central district
whyPoints.description: Short commutes make early slots possible and crowded apartments make a visiting tutor awkward. Online delivery fits the way this neighbourhood actually lives, including two siblings taught consecutively on one evening.

faqs.question: My child's mock mark was far below the predicted grade. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the marked script rather than the grade sheet, and go through it with four labels: blank, attempted and abandoned, partially credited, and completed but wrong. The distribution tells you which of four completely different problems you have. Blanks at the end mean timing; scattered blanks mean avoided topics; partial credit everywhere means method and command terms; completed but wrong means a genuine content gap. Only the last one needs teaching. The other three need training, which is faster and cheaper.

faqs.question: How many weeks are there really between the mock and study leave at an Al Wahda school?
faqs.answer: Ask for the study-leave date in writing, then count school weeks and subtract the holidays, any school event and the Ramadan fortnight if it falls inside the window. Families in central Abu Dhabi commonly find an apparent ten weeks becomes six or seven usable ones. That number decides whether a block can teach content or only recover technique, and it should be established before any sessions are bought rather than discovered in the middle of them.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an apartment in Al Wahda?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through paper questions. For an apartment household that removes the logistics of a visitor arriving at a set hour, and in exchange your child is taught by a specialist in their exact syllabus rather than by whoever is available within a short drive.

faqs.question: Is study leave better spent with a tutor or alone?
faqs.answer: Usually a mix, weighted differently from what families expect. Study leave is a structure problem rather than a knowledge problem, so the useful support is short and frequent rather than long and instructional: three or four brief sessions a week that open by marking what was set and close by setting the next piece. Nothing is taught. What that buys is a week with a shape, which is the single biggest predictor of how a student performs during leave, more than ability.

faqs.question: Should we plan for the November series before the June papers are sat?
faqs.answer: If either of two things is true, yes. Your child is on a tier that caps the grade below what they need, or substantial teaching has been missed through illness or a mid-year move. In both cases sitting June as a baseline and targeting a focused November entry often produces a better final result than a frantic spring. Raise it with the examinations officer early, because entry costs, whether the school enters November at all, and the sixth-form application timetable all need checking first.

faqs.question: Which exam series do candidates at central Abu Dhabi schools sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates sit the June series, with November available as the resit route. Cambridge offers its February and March sitting to India only, so any page quoting those dates to a UAE family has the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one, so confirm the zone with your school.

faqs.question: Can a tutor persuade the school to move my child to the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should offer to. The tier decision belongs to the school and is submitted to a board deadline months before the papers. What a tutor can produce is evidence: two timed sections and a diagnostic session marked against the published scheme, showing whether your child can access the harder paper. A conversation backed by that is different from one backed by a parental impression. After the entry deadline the question is closed and the honest plan is to use the available ceiling fully.

faqs.question: How should revision work during the Ramadan weeks in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Treat the period as deliberate maintenance rather than as a push. Shorter sessions, fixed in advance for the early evening or after Iftar rather than renegotiated each week, with light retrieval practice instead of new content. Shortened school days produce earlier arrivals and lower energy, not extra usable hours. Tell your child explicitly that the fortnight is lighter by design, because the guilt of an abandoned plan does more damage than the lost hours, and plan the weeks either side to carry the heavier work.

faqs.question: What does a block of IGCSE tutoring cost for a family in central Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Working from published market figures as at October 2026: qualified online subject tutors advertise from around AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, while entry-level online sessions run from roughly AED 33 to 65 and in-home visits including travel from about AED 180 to 500. One weekly hour across eight weeks therefore spans a wide range. Those are other providers' published rates. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, because the right figure depends on scarcity and level.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor a false economy if the mock showed partial credit everywhere?
faqs.answer: In that specific case, usually yes. Partial credit spread across long questions is a mark-scheme problem: the student understands the material and is not writing what earns the marks. Diagnosing and fixing that needs somebody who knows the published scheme for that specification, which is not what entry-level rates buy. Where the mock shows disorganisation or unfinished homework rather than lost method marks, a cheaper supervisory arrangement can be perfectly sensible. Match the level of purchase to what the script actually shows.

faqs.question: Will a tutor help my child with coursework in subjects that have it?
faqs.answer: Within a firm boundary. A tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains the published criteria and what their command words mean, questions the student about their own reasoning, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the work, does not rewrite sentences and does not supply material for submission. We state that before coursework support starts, because the consequence of crossing the line falls on the student rather than on the tutor or the family.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a student in Al Wahda need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one exposes the individual to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any page quoting a figure with suspicion.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved by ADEK or by the Ministry of Education?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not imply otherwise. IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry of Education, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licence or partnership. You may see that claim on competing pages; it is the most dangerous sentence available in this market. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. What we do hold is subject specialists, and what you can check is whether they know your child's syllabus.

faqs.question: What should the first session produce for a Year 11 student in central Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: A short written list of named error types drawn from the marked mock, and a clear statement of what the remaining weeks can and cannot achieve. Not reassurance, and not a plan to work through the textbook from the current chapter. You should recognise your child in the list, and your child should be able to say what their weakest area is without being prompted. If none of that appears in the first hour, the arrangement is supervision rather than teaching.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.closingHeading: Send the marked paper and the study-leave date
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-wahda.closingBody: Those two documents are enough for us to be useful. From the script we can name the error types that are costing marks; from the study-leave date we can scope a block that finishes while it can still be used. We will match an IGCSE specialist in that subject and specification, run a free trial lesson on your child's own questions, and recommend the smallest block the evidence supports — including the November route where that is genuinely the better plan. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time for families across Al Wahda and central Abu Dhabi.

intro.heading: The question underneath the search
paragraphs: Al Zahiyah is the district most residents still call the Tourist Club Area: the dense north-eastern corner of Abu Dhabi island, towers and mid-rise blocks packed between Al Salam Street and the Corniche, close to Al Mina and Abu Dhabi Mall. It is one of the most tightly populated parts of the emirate, which means the answer to 'is there a tutor near me' is almost certainly yes. That is not the question parents are really asking.

The real question is whether anybody nearby knows the specification. IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge publishes a numbered syllabus for every subject and revises it periodically. Pearson Edexcel publishes its own, with different codes, different paper structures and a different grading scale. Mathematics alone runs as Cambridge 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 across Abu Dhabi schools, and the sciences split again between Cambridge 0620, 0625 and 0610 and the Pearson 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 equivalents. A tutor who knows the subject but not the specification will teach confidently and miss the things the paper actually rewards.

That gap is invisible from outside, and it is the reason a family can pay for a term of lessons and see no movement in a mock result. The tutor was not bad. The tutor was teaching a different course. Most of this page is therefore about verification: the questions that identify a genuine specialist within ten minutes, the permit position that a parent in Abu Dhabi is entitled to check, and the honest limits of availability for scarcer subjects.

On delivery, the plain statement: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah, in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE — home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. Independent tutors in the emirate do visit, and the market prices that convenience in a band we set out further down with its sources. What matters for a tower household in Al Zahiyah is that the visiting option is also the one that narrows your choice of tutor to whoever can reach Al Salam Street by five o'clock.

What follows is written to be used rather than admired. There is a table of questions to put to any prospective tutor with the answers a specialist gives and the answers that should worry you. There is a table of who legally needs a tutoring permit in the UAE and how to verify it. There is a coverage table that states which subjects run thin and what we do when nobody is free, because no competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit at all. The final sections deal with the things a tower household in this district actually has to solve: where a quiet forty-five minutes comes from, what the market charges from the cheapest option upwards, and the boundary a legitimate tutor works inside.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahiyah.programmesIntro: Al Zahiyah's schools and the schools its children travel to cover a wide curriculum spread, and students arrive at IGCSE from several directions. The route in determines which gaps a tutor should expect to find.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which the tier decision is quietly made. Schools build an internal picture of a student's algebraic fluency and written accuracy during Year 9 and use it to recommend Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. Content at this stage looks undemanding beside IGCSE, which disguises how load-bearing it is.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Zahiyah family, Year 9 is the cheapest year in which to buy tuition and the one most often skipped. A term of weekly work on fluency at that point can change which tier a school offers, and the tier sets the grade ceiling for the following two years. No amount of spending in Year 11 recovers a capped entry.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Numbered syllabuses examined by terminal written papers, tiered Core and Extended in several subjects. Practical skills in the sciences are examined on paper, through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre. Grades run A* to G, with Core capped below the top grades.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after consulting the wrong version. An Al Zahiyah parent should get the timetable from the school's exams officer, not from a tutoring website.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A parallel family of specifications with its own codes, tiered Foundation and Higher, graded on the nine to one numerical scale. Several subjects supply a formula sheet in the examination. Papers are usually fewer and longer than the Cambridge equivalents, which changes how timing practice should be structured.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson results arrive on their own schedule and the dates are published. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. For a family planning a resit or an application deadline, those are the dates to work from.

programmes.name: AS, A Level and IB Diploma routes after Year 11
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE tier decision lands. A Levels and the IB Diploma both generally assume the Extended or Higher content behind them, particularly in mathematics and the sciences. Students entered at Core or Foundation find their post-16 options narrowed without any single conversation having told them so.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Verify the current rules through the official channel.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahiyah.subjectsIntro: The specifications below are the ones Abu Dhabi families most often ask about by name, with the syllabus code where it exists. Ask any prospective tutor which of these they have taught and marked; the answer tells you more than a biography does.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers, one of them without a calculator. Extended adds functions, vectors, harder trigonometry and more demanding algebra. The reliable mark losses are scale factors in similar solids, frequency density, and rounding an intermediate value too early.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Maths A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two two-hour papers of equal weight, calculator permitted throughout, formula sheet supplied. The skill tested is fast and correct formula selection rather than recall, which is a genuinely different revision diet from the Cambridge equivalent.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations, electrolysis and organic chemistry. Extended candidates lose most marks on calculation chains and on explanations that describe an observation without naming the particle-level reason for it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, waves, mechanics and thermal physics, with the alternative-to-practical paper as the quiet mark sink. Students who have done the experiments still lose marks describing a method precisely enough for somebody else to repeat it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: High terminology load and long structured answers. The highest-yield work is writing answers against mark schemes rather than reading notes, because the marks sit in specific named terms the student either uses or does not.

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response. Marks are lost to unsupported assertion in the reading paper and to unvaried sentence structure in the composition, both of which respond quickly to targeted feedback on the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Cambridge English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: A different specification from First Language English, with its own listening and speaking components. Students placed in the wrong one of the two lose marks for a reason that has nothing to do with their English.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics and Business Studies
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and applied evaluation decide the top grades. The common fault is answering with a definition where the command term asked for an analysis of a specific case.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences
subjects.description: The 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 specifications, examined through their own paper structures. A tutor who has only taught the Cambridge equivalents will teach broadly the right content against the wrong assessment shape.

subjects.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Optional, sat alongside Extended 0580 by students heading for A Level or Diploma mathematics. Introduces calculus and logarithms early. Students who struggle here are almost always short of algebraic stamina rather than ability.

sections.heading: Is there anybody in Al Zahiyah who actually knows this syllabus?
paragraphs: The honest answer has two parts. Yes, there are many capable tutors living within a short drive of Al Zahiyah, and in a district this dense you will find one easily. No, you cannot tell from proximity, a price or a profile photograph whether any of them has taught and marked the specification your child is entered for, and that is the variable that decides whether the money does anything.

The reason this matters more in IGCSE than in most qualifications is the sheer number of parallel specifications in circulation. A single Abu Dhabi year group can contain students sitting Cambridge 0580, Cambridge 0607 and Pearson 4MA1 mathematics, with the Cambridge cohort split again between Core and Extended. Each has different papers, different calculator rules and a different grading scale. A tutor teaching generic IGCSE mathematics is teaching the union of three courses, which means a meaningful share of every lesson is spent on material the student's own paper will not test.

What a specialist does differently is narrow. They ask for the syllabus code before the first lesson. They read the most recent marked script before teaching anything. They know which topics are Extended-only and will not waste a Core candidate's time on them. They mark written work against the published scheme for a real series rather than giving it a tick. And they can tell you, early and specifically, which three faults are costing the most marks.

The tables in the next two sections exist so that you can test all of this yourself, before paying anybody. Neither requires any subject knowledge on your part. The first is a set of questions with the answers a specialist gives; the second is the permit position, which in the UAE is a matter of regulation rather than preference and which almost no tutoring website in this market explains.

sections.heading: Ten minutes of questions that identify a genuine IGCSE specialist
paragraphs: You do not need to understand the syllabus to audit a tutor. You need questions with factual answers, because a specialist answers them instantly and anybody else deflects into reassurance. Reassurance is the warning sign. A tutor who responds to a specification question with a statement about how much students enjoy their lessons has told you they do not know the answer.

Run the conversation in this order. Establish the code first, because everything else depends on it. Then the tier, then the paper structure, then the calculator rule, then whether a formula sheet is supplied. Those five facts take ninety seconds for someone who teaches the course and are impossible to improvise. If all five come back correctly, move on to the diagnostic questions: what the student's last marked paper showed, and what the tutor would do in the first three lessons.

The table below sets out the exchange. The middle column is roughly what a specialist says; the third is the kind of answer that should end the conversation. None of this is adversarial and a good tutor will not take it that way — most are relieved to talk to a parent who has asked something specific, because the alternative is being judged on charm.

One further question is worth asking at the end, and the answer matters more than any of the above: what will you tell me if this is not working. A tutor who has an answer to that has thought about accountability. A tutor who says it will definitely work has told you they will not raise it with you when it does not.

table.caption: QUESTIONS TO PUT TO ANY PROSPECTIVE IGCSE TUTOR
rows: Which syllabus code does my child sit?

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is a regulated activity and the rules are published, which makes it one of the few things about hiring a tutor that a parent can check rather than guess. Private tutoring in the Emirates requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 concerning private tuition work permits.

The headline facts are worth knowing precisely. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a tutor who tells you it is expensive to obtain is mistaken. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged between fifteen and eighteen. The ministry's own service page for it is listed as private tutor licensing, with no fee and a two working day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of fine amounts has been published — press reporting states explicitly that the ministry did not specify the amounts or detail the penalties — so any figure quoted to you as the penalty is somebody's guess. In Abu Dhabi there is a further layer: press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates that private and charter school staff may not provide paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify that against the current ADEK document before relying on the wording.

A tuition centre with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs its own permit from the emirate's regulator, which in Dubai is an educational services permit for a training institute issued by KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit and makes no such claim: we are an independent online matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, and no accreditation from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

sections.heading: Coverage, match times, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit, which is strange, because every platform has one. Demand for IGCSE specialists in the Emirates is not spread evenly across subjects, and the thin places are predictable: the less common languages, the combined-science and double-award variants, Computer Science at Extended tier, and anything where a family needs a specific board rather than a broad subject.

Timing compounds it. Nearly every Abu Dhabi household wants the same slot, somewhere between four and seven in the afternoon on Gulf Standard Time, because that is when a child is home and still awake. A specialist with a full book is therefore unavailable in exactly the window you want, even though they have capacity at ten in the morning. The honest response to this is not to quietly substitute a generalist. It is to say so, and to offer the alternatives: a different weekday, a weekend session, or a short wait for a named person.

The table states the position by subject band as it stands. Match times are typical rather than promised, and they lengthen in the weeks before a series as the specialist pool fills. The fallback column is the part worth reading, because it is where other platforms are silent: where no UAE-based specialist covers a combination, we say so and explain what the alternative actually involves before anybody commits.

There is one more disclosure that belongs here. Our tutors are not described as current examiners for Cambridge, Pearson or any other board, because that status cannot be evidenced for individuals in a way a parent could check, and examiner experience should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased papers. If a provider leans on examiner language, ask them which board, which subject, which series, and what they are claiming it gives them.

sections.heading: Al Zahiyah logistics: towers, lift time and the real cost of a visit
paragraphs: Density changes the economics of a visiting tutor in a way the hourly rate conceals. Al Zahiyah is apartment living, much of it in towers with basement parking, single-bank lifts and visitor registration at the desk. A tutor arriving for a five o'clock session leaves earlier, parks, waits, signs in and rides up. None of that is teaching and all of it is paid for, either in the rate or in the lesson.

The second constraint is the room. A one-to-one lesson needs a surface, a quiet forty-five minutes and nobody walking through. In a three-bedroom apartment with two other children home from school, that is harder to produce than it sounds, and it is the most common reason a visiting arrangement quietly stops working after a month. A live video lesson has the same problem in miniature but solves it more cheaply: headphones, a closed door, and no second adult in the apartment.

The third is traffic, which in Al Zahiyah is specific rather than general. Al Salam Street and the approaches to Al Mina move slowly in the late afternoon, and anyone driving in from the mainland side of the bridges adds an unpredictable half hour. A tutor who is late twice loses the slot; a tutor who builds the risk into their rate charges for it. Market rates for in-home visiting in the emirate reflect exactly this: survey data puts them at AED 180 to 350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted between AED 200 and 500.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is an India-only service for us, and the honest version of that argument is the one above. The time a visiting tutor spends in a lift is time you have paid for, and the pool of tutors willing to make that trip to this district is much smaller than the pool who teach the specification.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start in practice. Budget online tutoring in the UAE is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, drawn from published platform rate cards read in October 2026. At that level the hour typically goes on checking homework the student has already attempted. It is genuinely useful for confidence and for keeping a student working, and it will not reliably move a grade, because nobody at that price is marking written work against a published scheme between sessions.

The next band up, around AED 150 to 300 an hour on published agency rate pages, is where a qualified subject tutor teaches the specification and marks work between lessons. That is the point at which measurable change becomes plausible, and for most Al Zahiyah families it is the sensible default. Above it, IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and more in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and the premium buys judgement rather than hours: which tier, which topics to abandon, which papers to sit. At the top, a premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour.

In-home visiting sits across these bands with its own loading. The Bestimate survey puts it at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors are quoted from AED 200 to 500. Monthly figures are often more useful than hourly ones for budgeting: that same survey estimates AED 240 to 600 a month for a weekly one-hour session at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages advertised in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

All of those figures belong to the market and were read in October 2026. None of them is IB Gram's price list. Our own arrangement begins with a free trial lesson and a consultation in which the specification, the tier and the diagnosis get established before any schedule is discussed; the condition on the trial is simply that it is one lesson and you decide afterwards. Whether tuition fees carry VAT in the UAE is a question for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page, and we do not state a position on it here.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed IGCSE work
paragraphs: IGCSE has less coursework exposure than the Diploma, but the boundary still exists and it is worth stating to a student in plain terms. A tutor may teach content, model methods, explain what a command term requires, mark a student's own attempt against the published scheme and show them where credit was available and unclaimed. That is the whole legitimate range, and it is enough to move a grade.

A tutor may not supply answers to live assessed work, sit with a student during an assessment, produce coursework for submission, or edit a piece into something the student could not have written. We decline those requests. The reason is not squeamishness: the entry belongs to the student, and work they did not produce puts that entry at risk under the board's regulations. At least one provider competing in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a four-figure dirham price. That is not a shortcut, and the consequences land on the child rather than the seller.

A second boundary concerns board material. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own sites. We do not reproduce or distribute them, and a tutor works through them with a student from the official source. Any website offering a downloadable library of current board material is doing something you should not want your child's name attached to.

The third is about what gets promised. No tutor can promise a grade or a grade improvement, and any claim of a guaranteed outcome should be treated with real scepticism. What honest tuition offers is a correct diagnosis, teaching aimed at it, written work marked against the real criteria, and a straight answer about how much of the gap the remaining time can close. A provider who will not say what their plan cannot achieve has told you something important about the plan.

sections.heading: Starting from a marked paper rather than from a subject
paragraphs: The most useful document in the house is the last marked script, and most families never send it anywhere. A mock paper marked by the class teacher against the official scheme is a diagnostic record: it shows not just the total, but the exact questions where marks stopped arriving and the pattern behind them. Read properly, three or four recurring faults usually account for most of the lost marks, and at least two of them are technique rather than content.

A worked example makes the point. A student scores fifty-eight on an Extended mathematics paper. Reading the script, nine marks went on questions that said 'show that' and were answered by substituting the printed value back in; six went to answers rounded at an intermediate step; five went to a histogram question where frequency density was never calculated; four went to an unattempted final question the student never reached. That is twenty-four marks, and none of it is a gap in mathematical understanding. The plan writes itself: two lessons on command terms, one on rounding discipline, one on histograms, and timed practice to fix the pacing.

A tutor who starts from the subject instead will begin at the top of the syllabus and work down, which is reassuring, slow and unlikely to find any of the above. This is the difference the verification questions earlier on this page are designed to detect, and it is why the first thing we ask an Al Zahiyah family for is the script rather than a description of the problem.

What follows from that is simply an ordinary weekly arrangement: a specialist matched to the code and tier, a free trial lesson in which the diagnosis is already in hand, a cadence the household can sustain, and a review date at which we look at the marked work rather than at how the lessons felt. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Al Zahiyah school run, and timings move during Ramadan to post-Iftar slots where a family prefers it.
