faqs.question: Will an IGCSE tutor come to our apartment in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one IGCSE tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah, elsewhere in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors in the emirate do visit, and the market prices that at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on the source. In a tower district the premium largely buys parking, lift time and traffic risk rather than teaching.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether a tutor really knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask five factual questions in this order: which syllabus code, which tier, how many papers, whether a calculator is permitted on all of them, and whether a formula sheet is supplied. A specialist answers all five in about ninety seconds. Anyone who deflects into general reassurance about enjoyment or confidence has answered the question a different way. Then ask what your child's last marked paper showed; the right response is a request to read it before offering any diagnosis.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE specifications are actually used in Abu Dhabi schools?
faqs.answer: Several in parallel, which is the root of most confusion. Mathematics appears as Cambridge 0580, Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1. Sciences split between the Cambridge 0620, 0625 and 0610 family and the Pearson 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1 family. English divides between First Language 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510, which are different qualifications. Your school's exams officer can confirm the exact codes in one email, and that email is worth more than any tutoring brochure.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Al Zahiyah need a licence?
faqs.answer: A permit, yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the ministry's service page lists no fee and a two working day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: How much is the fine for tutoring in the UAE without a permit?
faqs.answer: No amount has been published, so nobody can tell you honestly. The official position is that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from the ministry are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. Press reporting states explicitly that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, and a figure circulating online could not be verified against any official source. Any website quoting you a specific dirham penalty is guessing, which is a reason to distrust the rest of its claims.

faqs.question: Can my child's class teacher tutor them privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Treat that as closed. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff indicates teachers are prohibited from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that staff tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. Verify the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording, but the practical advice is simple: use an independent specialist instead.

faqs.question: What does the cheapest tuition in Abu Dhabi actually get you?
faqs.answer: Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour on published platform rate cards read in October 2026. At that level the hour usually goes on reviewing homework the student has already attempted, which supports confidence and routine. What it does not include is written work marked against a published mark scheme between sessions, and that marking is the mechanism by which a grade actually moves. It is a reasonable purchase for a student who is coping and needs company, not for one who is losing marks.

faqs.question: Which exam series can an Al Zahiyah IGCSE candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong version. Get the timetable from your school, not from a website.

faqs.question: When do Pearson International GCSE results actually arrive?
faqs.answer: On a published schedule that differs from Cambridge's. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those dates matter for anyone planning a resit or an application deadline. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so the live official PDF is the only source worth relying on.

faqs.question: What if no specialist covers my child's subject in our preferred slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting someone close enough. Almost every Abu Dhabi family wants the same late-afternoon window on Gulf Standard Time, so a specialist with a full book may have capacity in the morning and none when you need it. The options are usually a different weekday, a weekend session, or a short wait for a named tutor. Where no UAE-based specialist covers the combination at all, we say so plainly and explain what the realistic alternative involves before you commit.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE tuition in Year 9 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the least popular advice on this page. Year 9 is when a school forms its view of whether Core or Extended is right, and a term of work on algebraic fluency at that stage can change the tier offered. The tier sets the grade ceiling for two years. The same money spent in the final term before the papers buys exam technique, which is worth having and genuinely effective, but it cannot recover a capped entry once the school has submitted it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary we state to the student at the first session. A tutor teaches content, models methods, explains what a command term requires and marks the student's own attempts against the published scheme. A tutor does not supply answers for live assessed work, sit alongside a student during an assessment, or produce coursework for submission. We decline that because the entry belongs to your child and work they did not produce puts it at risk under the board's regulations.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes for us to download?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of anyone who does. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables are published by Cambridge and Pearson on their own websites, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter. A tutor works through them with your child from the official source, which is also the only way to be sure the version in use is current. Boards revise specifications, and a downloaded copy from an unofficial library may be two syllabuses out of date.

faqs.question: How quickly should we see something change after starting in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: That depends on the diagnosis, and a provider who answers with a number before reading the script is guessing. Procedural faults such as early rounding, frequency density or mishandled command terms often return marks within three or four lessons because each is a single rule plus practice. Conceptual gaps take several weeks of teaching. Underlying fluency problems take a term or more. No tutor can promise a grade, and the review date exists precisely so that an honest answer gets given at a fixed point rather than avoided.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahiyah.closingHeading: Audit the tutor before you pay for the term
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-zahiyah.closingBody: Take the question table on this page to whoever you are considering, including us. Five factual questions about the specification separate a specialist from a competent graduate in about ninety seconds, and the sixth — what will you tell me if this is not working — separates the accountable from the optimistic. Then send the last marked script and let a specialist read it before the trial lesson. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Al Zahiyah school run, and we do not offer home visits in the UAE because that is an India-only service. The trial is one lesson, and you decide afterwards.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-baniyas.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE subjects to Abu Dhabi students at both tiers. Each is matched to a named syllabus code rather than to a subject label, because the code determines the papers, the practical arrangements and what the mark scheme rewards.

intro.heading: Start from the code, not the subject name
paragraphs: There is no such thing as an IGCSE Physics tutor in the abstract. There is a Cambridge 0625 tutor and a Pearson 4PH1 tutor, and while the physics in both is the same physics, the papers are not the same papers, the practical arrangements differ and the mark schemes reward different things. The same applies in every subject. A tutor who cannot say which code they are teaching is going to teach the union of two specifications, and the student will meet the consequences in a mock rather than in a lesson.

Baniyas is a large mainland district on the south-eastern side of Abu Dhabi, laid out across eastern and western sides with numbered sectors and Mussafah close by. Students from here attend schools across the mainland corridor and the island, and between those schools you will find both board families in use, sometimes within one year group. That is the practical reason the code matters here: two children in neighbouring houses studying what looks like the same subject may be sitting different papers.

This page is written from the syllabus rather than from the market. It lists the codes in regular use in Abu Dhabi, explains how the sciences examine practical skills on paper, distinguishes First Language English from English as a Second Language — which are different qualifications routinely confused — and sets Cambridge against Pearson subject by subject. Then it goes to where written marks are actually lost, which in most subjects is terminology and command words rather than knowledge.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Baniyas or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a page about syllabus specificity the argument is direct — a tutor who has taught your child's exact code is a scarcer thing than a tutor who will drive out to the mainland, and the first of those is what changes a grade.

Two factual boundaries apply throughout. Specifications, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own websites; we reference and link them rather than reproducing them, and a site offering a downloadable library of current board material is doing something you should not want your child's name near. And the codes below should be confirmed with your school's exams officer rather than assumed from this page, because boards revise specifications and a school can change board between cohorts.

On the calendar, which affects every subject here: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to UAE candidates; the February and March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam through using the wrong version.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-baniyas.programmesIntro: The three stages below are where IGCSE subject outcomes are actually determined, and the subject-specific work differs at each. Knowing the stage tells a tutor what kind of intervention is possible.

programmes.name: Subject choices and tiering, Year 9
programmes.description: The year options are chosen and tiers are first discussed. Subject choice has consequences beyond interest: triple science versus a double award changes what post-16 routes remain open, and the English pathway chosen determines which qualification a student ends up holding.
programmes.countryNote: For a Baniyas family this is the cheapest point at which to intervene in any subject, and the one most often skipped. A term of work in Year 9 can change a tier recommendation; the same money in Year 11 buys examination technique, which is worth having and cannot change an entry already submitted.

programmes.name: Content delivery, Year 10
programmes.description: Most of the syllabus content is taught this year across every subject, and the sciences in particular front-load terminology that later topics assume. A student falling behind in Year 10 compounds, because IGCSE courses do not revisit topics; they build on them.
programmes.countryNote: The internal assessments schools run at the end of Year 10 are the best diagnostic evidence available before the final year. They are marked by the subject teacher against the real scheme in most Abu Dhabi schools, which makes the scripts worth reading question by question rather than filing.

programmes.name: Completion, mocks and the series, Year 11
programmes.description: Syllabus completion, mock examinations, the final entry and the papers. Subject-specific work in this year is about converting known content into marks: terminology precision, command words, method shown, timing, and the specific requirements of each paper in each subject.
programmes.countryNote: Across eight or nine subjects, a Baniyas household cannot support all of them. The honest approach is to pick the one or two where the last marked script shows a correctable, specific fault, and to leave the rest to the school and the student's own revision.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-baniyas.subjectsIntro: Below are the subjects Abu Dhabi families most often ask about by name, with the specific content area where marks go. Ask any prospective tutor which of these codes they have taught and marked; the answer is more informative than a biography.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, waves, mechanics and thermal physics, plus a practical component examined on paper. Marks go to method descriptions that are not repeatable, to graph work with poorly chosen scales, and to explanations that state an observation without naming the cause.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: The same physics in a different assessment shape, with its own paper structure and formula provision. A tutor whose experience is entirely Cambridge will teach broadly correct content against the wrong paper, which shows up as timing problems rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, ionic equations, electrolysis, rates and organic chemistry. The reliable mark losses are multi-step calculation chains abandoned halfway and explanations that describe a colour change without reference to the particles responsible for it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Equivalent content, different papers. Students moving between schools mid-course sometimes find they have changed board without anyone flagging it, which is worth checking with the exams officer rather than assuming continuity.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: The heaviest terminology load of the three sciences and the subject where revision method matters most. Students who read notes plateau; students who write structured answers against mark schemes improve, because the marks sit in specific named terms.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: A double-award route covering all three sciences in two awards' worth of content. Students entered for it and tutored as though they were sitting the separate sciences waste time on material their papers will not reach.

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing, composition and reading response for students whose English is first-language standard. Marks are lost to unsupported assertion in the reading paper and to monotonous sentence structure in the composition, both of which respond quickly to feedback on the student's own writing.

subjects.name: Cambridge English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: A different qualification with its own listening and speaking components, for students for whom English is an additional language. A student placed in the wrong one of these two loses marks for a reason unrelated to their actual English.

subjects.name: Cambridge Literature in English 0475
subjects.description: Set texts, unseen passages and essay response. The common fault is retelling the plot where the question asks about method and effect, which is a habit rather than a gap and changes within three or four pieces of marked writing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and applied evaluation carry the top grades. Students answer with definitions where the command term asked for analysis of a specific case, which is the single most common structural fault in both subjects.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Two written papers, one without a calculator, with a defined list of formulae to recall. Extended adds functions, vectors and harder trigonometry. Procedural faults rather than conceptual ones account for most lost marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478 and ICT 0417
subjects.description: Two distinct qualifications frequently confused by families. Computer Science involves algorithms and programming logic; ICT is applications and data handling. Specialist availability for both is thinner than for the sciences, which we disclose rather than conceal.

sections.heading: The codes in regular use across Abu Dhabi schools
paragraphs: The table below lists the specifications a tutor in this emirate is actually likely to meet, with both board families side by side. It is not exhaustive, and the right use of it is as a prompt for one email to your school's exams officer asking which codes your child is entered for.

Two things are visible once the codes are written out. First, how many parallel qualifications exist under the same subject names: a conversation about IGCSE Chemistry could be about 0620 or 4CH1, and a conversation about IGCSE English could be about three different qualifications. Second, how much of the difference is structural rather than content-based — paper counts, formula provision, tiering vocabulary and practical arrangements vary, while the underlying subject does not.

The last column names where marks reliably go in each. Those are patterns across marked scripts rather than rules, and they are useful mainly because they are specific enough to act on. A student losing marks to method descriptions that cannot be repeated does not need more physics; they need four pieces of method writing marked against the scheme's wording. A student losing marks to plot retelling in Literature does not need to reread the text.

A note on what this page will not do. We do not reproduce or distribute specifications, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own sites. A tutor works through them with a student from the official source. That also means the codes here should be checked against the current published specification, because boards revise them and a tutoring page is not an authority on what is live.

sections.heading: The sciences: how practical skills are examined on paper
paragraphs: Parents often assume a science practical means their child performs an experiment in front of an examiner. In most Abu Dhabi centres it does not. Practical skills in IGCSE science are assessed in writing, either through a practical test sat under examination conditions or through a written alternative paper, and which applies is a decision made by the centre. That is the first thing to establish, because the two require different preparation.

The written alternative is the one families underestimate, and it is where able students lose marks they should not. It asks a candidate to describe a method precisely enough that another person could follow it, to identify variables and controls, to read and plot data, to choose sensible graph scales, to draw a line of best fit with judgement, and to identify sources of error and suggest improvements. Every one of those is a writing skill applied to science, and a student who has performed the experiment perfectly in class may still not be able to produce the words.

The method question is the clearest example. A mark scheme for describing an experiment awards credit for naming the measuring instrument, stating what is varied and what is kept constant, specifying repeats, and saying how the result is calculated. A student who writes a vivid paragraph about what they did in the lab, without those elements, scores a fraction of the available marks. Four pieces of method writing marked against the scheme's own wording changes this permanently, and almost nobody does them.

The error and improvement questions are the second reliable loss, and the reason is that they are rarely practised. A student asked to identify a source of error will name human reaction time in an experiment where it is irrelevant, or suggest an improvement that does not address the error named. The remedy is mechanical: a handful of marked attempts in which the error and the improvement must be linked explicitly to each other. The table sets out what each element of the component asks for and what the tutoring focus should be.

sections.heading: English: three qualifications, one subject name
paragraphs: This is the clearest case on the page of a code mattering more than a subject name, and it is the one that causes the most confusion in Abu Dhabi households. Cambridge offers First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510, and they are not two tiers of one qualification; they are different courses with different assessments for different students. Literature in English 0475 is a third, separate thing.

First Language English assumes English at first-language standard and examines directed writing, composition and reading response. The marks sit in the quality of argument and the control of language: a reading answer that asserts an effect without quoting the words producing it loses credit, and a composition in which every sentence has the same shape loses credit for style regardless of correctness. English as a Second Language has its own structure, including listening and speaking components, and examines a different set of competences.

Placement in the wrong one of these is more common than it should be, particularly where a student has transferred school mid-course or arrived in the UAE partway through. The consequence is a grade that reflects the mismatch rather than the student. If you are unsure which your child is entered for, that is a one-line question to the exams officer and it is worth asking this week rather than after a mock.

For tuition, each has a different highest-yield intervention. First Language English responds almost entirely to feedback on the student's own writing, marked against the published criteria, rather than to teaching about technique in the abstract. Literature responds to breaking the habit of retelling the plot, which takes three or four marked essays. English as a Second Language responds to structured practice in its specific task types, including the speaking component, which students almost never rehearse under conditions despite its weight.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the same subject, two assessment shapes
paragraphs: Families sometimes ask which board is easier. It is the wrong question and the honest answer is that they are differently shaped rather than differently difficult, and that your child's school has already chosen, so the useful question is what the chosen shape demands.

The differences that matter in practice are these. Paper counts and lengths differ, which changes timing practice. Formula provision differs: Pearson supplies a formula sheet in several subjects where Cambridge expects recall of a defined list, which changes whether memorisation or fast selection is the skill to train. Tiering vocabulary differs, Core and Extended against Foundation and Higher, with different grade ranges attached. And grading scales differ, letters against numbers, which matters when a household tries to compare two children.

A less obvious difference is the resit and modular structure further up the system, which is one reason some Abu Dhabi schools have moved board. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student this is mostly irrelevant; for a family thinking about the route beyond Year 11 it is worth asking the school about directly. And where a school changes board between cohorts, siblings two years apart can be on different specifications in the same subject at the same school, which catches parents out routinely.

The practical instruction is short. Get the codes. Check whether a formula sheet is supplied in each subject. Check the paper count and length so timing practice is set correctly. Check which practical arrangement applies in the sciences. Those four facts per subject take one email and they determine whether a tutor's work is aimed at the right target. A tutor who has not asked for them is not working from the specification, whatever they say about experience.

sections.heading: Where written marks are lost: terminology and command words
paragraphs: Across subjects and across both boards, two faults account for an extraordinary share of lost marks in Abu Dhabi scripts, and neither is a gap in knowledge. The first is missing terminology. The second is a misread command word. Both are cheap to fix and almost never taught explicitly.

Terminology first. Mark schemes in the sciences and humanities award credit for specific named terms. A student who describes a process correctly in ordinary language, without using the term the scheme requires, scores less than a student with a weaker understanding who uses the word. That feels unjust and it is simply how the instrument works, and a student who learns it adjusts within a few marked answers. The practice that fixes it is writing answers and then checking them against the scheme's own wording, marking each required term present or absent.

Command words next. Boards publish their command term definitions, and students who have never read them write answers that are accurate and unrewarded. 'State' wants a bare answer and gives no credit for working. 'Explain' requires a cause linked to an effect in a complete sentence. 'Describe' wants what happens rather than why. 'Show that' demands a derivation arriving at the printed result, and substituting the printed value back in scores nothing. 'Evaluate' requires a judgement with evidence and an acknowledged limitation.

The exercise that exposes this takes twenty minutes and no subject knowledge. Take a marked script, underline the command word in every question that lost marks, and check each against the published definition. In most scripts two or three terms account for the bulk of the damage, and the same two or three recur across subjects. That is a targeting problem rather than a teaching problem, and it is the single most efficient thing a parent can do with an evening.

sections.heading: Revision that works in content-heavy subjects
paragraphs: Biology, Geography, History and the humanities share a problem: the volume of material invites revision by reading, and revision by reading does not work. Students report feeling prepared and then cannot produce the content under examination conditions, which is demoralising in a way that looks like inability and is actually a method failure.

The mechanism is retrieval. Reading a page produces recognition — the sense that the material is familiar — which the brain mistakes for the ability to recall it unprompted. Writing an answer without notes produces retrieval, which is what the examination actually requires. The difference in outcome between the two methods, for the same total hours, is large. Students who switch method usually notice within three weeks.

A workable routine in a content-heavy subject is short and dull. Pick a topic covered three or more weeks ago. Write for fifteen minutes on a past-paper question from it without opening anything. Then open the notes and the mark scheme, mark the attempt, and list the specific terms or points that were missing. Repeat with a different old topic the next day. Twenty minutes a day of that beats two hours of rereading on a Saturday, and in a Baniyas household where the afternoon is consumed by travel it is also the only pattern that fits.

The tutor's role in this is narrower than families expect and more useful. It is to set the right questions, to mark the attempts against the published scheme rather than generously, and to maintain the list of recurring omissions so the student can see which terms keep escaping. That list is the artefact worth paying for in a content-heavy subject. Explanation of content the student has already read is the least valuable thing a tutor can spend an hour on and the thing most hours get spent on.

sections.heading: What to ask the subject teacher at parents' evening
paragraphs: Parents' evening is four minutes per subject and most of it gets spent on generalities. A family with four prepared questions per subject leaves with information that changes a tuition decision, and the questions are the same in every subject.

First: which syllabus code and tier is my child entered for, and when is the final entry submitted? That single question settles the specification and tells you the real deadline for any conversation about tiering. Second: what does the last marked assessment show as the main reason for lost marks — content, method, terminology or timing? A subject teacher usually knows this immediately and it is the diagnosis a tutor would otherwise spend a paid hour producing.

Third: is there a school intervention or support class in this subject, and is my child in it? It is free, it is taught by somebody who knows the specification and has seen the work, and for a procedural or terminology gap it is frequently the best option available at any price. Families spend money on tuition every term without having asked this question, and no tutoring provider has an incentive to raise it.

Fourth: what should my child be doing between now and the next assessment, specifically? Not 'revise more' but which topics, which paper, which skill. A teacher's answer to that is worth more than a brochure, and if a tutor is engaged it gives them a target aligned with the school rather than a parallel programme. Take the answers home in writing. Over eight subjects that is one page, and it is the most useful page a Baniyas household will have all year.

sections.heading: Sources, the permit and what we decline
paragraphs: Everything factual on this page is either attributable or marked as something to confirm. Board material — specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides — belongs to Cambridge and Pearson and is published on their own websites. We reference and link it rather than reproducing it, and a tutor works through it with a student from the official source. Any site offering a downloadable library of current board material is doing something a parent should decline.

The syllabus codes listed here should be confirmed with your school's exams officer. Boards revise specifications, schools change board between cohorts, and a tutoring page is not an authority on what is currently live. On examination dates: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered in India only, and Pearson runs May/June and November. No specific future-dated examination window appears on this page, because a page naming a year goes stale without anybody touching it.

On tutors and permits: any paid private tutor in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with the ministry's own service page listing no fee and a two working day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so a figure quoted as the penalty is invention. In Abu Dhabi, press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules indicates school staff may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school.

On status and claims: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and holds no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. It is not a registered examination centre. We decline to produce assessed work of any kind, to supply answers for live assessed tasks, or to describe tutors as current examiners for any board. No tutor can promise a grade, and we publish no rating or satisfaction statistic, because stating one honestly requires the sample size, the date and the method alongside it.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE syllabus codes is my child in Baniyas actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Only the school can tell you, and it is one email to the exams officer. Across Abu Dhabi you will find Cambridge 0580, 0607, 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654, 0500, 0510, 0475, 0455, 0450, 0478 and 0417, alongside Pearson 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1, 4EA1 and others. The codes determine paper counts, formula provision, tiering vocabulary and practical arrangements, so a tutor who has not asked for them is working from a generic syllabus rather than your child's.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in Baniyas for IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors in the emirate do, and IB Gram does not. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Baniyas or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. For subject specificity the trade clearly favours video: a tutor who has taught your child's exact specification is scarcer than one willing to drive out to the mainland, and it is the first of those that moves a grade.

faqs.question: How is the IGCSE science practical actually assessed?
faqs.answer: In writing, either through a practical test sat under examination conditions or through a written alternative paper, and which applies is a decision made by your centre. So the first question is which one your child faces. Both examine the same underlying skills: describing a method precisely enough to be repeated, identifying variables and controls, recording and plotting data, choosing graph scales, and identifying sources of error with improvements that address them.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their science answer is correct?
faqs.answer: Almost always missing terminology. Mark schemes award credit for specific named terms, so an answer that describes a process accurately in ordinary language can score less than a weaker answer that uses the required word. This feels unjust and it is simply how the instrument works. The fix is mechanical: write answers, then check them against the scheme's own wording, marking each required term as present or absent. Students adjust within a few marked attempts.

faqs.question: What is the difference between English 0500 and English 0510?
faqs.answer: They are different qualifications rather than two tiers of one. Cambridge First Language English 0500 assumes English at first-language standard and examines directed writing, composition and reading response. English as a Second Language 0510 has its own structure, including listening and speaking components, for students for whom English is an additional language. Literature in English 0475 is a third, separate subject. Placement in the wrong one produces a grade that reflects the mismatch rather than the student.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge or Pearson easier for IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Neither, and your school has already chosen, so the useful question is what the chosen shape demands. The differences are structural: paper counts and lengths, whether a formula sheet is supplied, tiering vocabulary, grading scale, and the practical arrangement. A tutor whose experience is entirely one board will teach broadly correct content against the wrong paper, which shows up as timing problems rather than wrong answers. Get the code and the paper structure before anything else.

faqs.question: Why does reading notes not work for IGCSE Biology?
faqs.answer: Because reading produces recognition rather than recall. A familiar page feels like knowledge and the examination requires retrieval without prompts, which is a different skill. A workable routine is dull and effective: pick a topic covered three or more weeks ago, write for fifteen minutes on a past-paper question without opening anything, then mark the attempt against the scheme and list the terms that were missing. Twenty minutes daily beats two hours of rereading.

faqs.question: What should I ask at parents' evening in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: Four questions per subject. Which syllabus code and tier, and when the final entry is submitted. What the last marked assessment shows as the main reason for lost marks — content, method, terminology or timing. Whether a school intervention class exists and whether your child is in it. And what specifically your child should do before the next assessment. Take the answers home in writing; over eight subjects that is one page and the most useful page of the year.

faqs.question: Do you provide past papers and mark schemes to download?
faqs.answer: No, and be cautious of anyone who does. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, subject guides and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are published on their own websites, which is also the only place you can be sure the version is current. A tutor works through them with your child from the official source. Boards revise specifications, and a downloaded copy from an unofficial library can be two syllabuses out of date without saying so.

faqs.question: Which command words cost the most marks in Abu Dhabi scripts?
faqs.answer: Consistently 'show that', which demands a derivation arriving at the printed result and gives nothing for substituting that result back in; 'explain', which needs a cause linked to an effect in a complete sentence rather than a description; and 'evaluate', which requires a judgement with evidence and an acknowledged limitation. Boards publish their command term definitions. Underlining the command word in every question that lost marks on a marked script takes twenty minutes and usually identifies two or three repeat offenders.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 the same as the separate sciences?
faqs.answer: No. It is a double-award route covering all three sciences across two awards' worth of content, so parts of the separate-science specifications are not reached. A student entered for it and tutored as though they were sitting 0610, 0620 and 0625 will spend real time on material their papers never ask about. This is one of the clearest cases where confirming the code with the exams officer saves money rather than just adding precision.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two sciences for a Baniyas student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor who teaches Cambridge Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 can genuinely do both, and there is real value in one person noticing that a physics problem is actually an algebra problem. What does not work is stretching a single tutor across four unrelated subjects for scheduling convenience. Where a second specialist is needed we say so, and where no specialist covers a combination we say that too.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we fund across eight or nine?
faqs.answer: One or two, chosen by evidence rather than by complaint. Tuition works through the marked written practice between lessons, and a student's free evenings do not multiply when you add subjects. Pick the subject where the last marked script shows a correctable, specific fault — missing terminology, a command word misread, a method description that cannot be repeated — and leave the rest to the school and the student's own retrieval practice.

faqs.question: Should we use the November series if a subject goes badly in June?
faqs.answer: It is the available route for a Cambridge candidate in the UAE, and Pearson offers November alongside May/June. What binds is the centre rather than the board: entries are made through a centre, internal deadlines fall earlier than the board's, and not every centre takes late or private entries. So the first call after a disappointing result is to the exams officer. Note also that Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only, not here.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-corniche.tutorsIntro: Corniche families usually arrive having collected two or three quotes that cannot be compared because they describe different things. We start by making them comparable, then match on syllabus code and component rather than on price alone.

intro.heading: Most tutoring comparisons compare the wrong things
paragraphs: A parent on the Corniche collecting quotes typically ends up with three numbers that look comparable and are not. One is an agency rate that includes a replacement policy and travel. One is a freelance rate that includes neither. One is a platform rate for a university student rather than a qualified teacher. Comparing those three on price alone is comparing a taxi fare with a bus ticket and a bicycle.

The same problem applies to the geographical comparison families run first. The Corniche, Al Khalidiyah, Al Bateen and Al Mushrif sit minutes apart on the city's western side. Their children attend, in large part, the same schools. Those schools enter candidates for the same two examination boards. The topic errors that cost marks are identical across all four districts. There is no educational difference between them to find, however long a parent spends looking for one.

What does differ between the four is logistics, and on the Corniche specifically the logistics are towers. Visitor parking, reception procedures and lift waits consume minutes that belong to a paid hour, and no quote in this market itemises them. A tutor held at a building entrance for ten minutes has still charged the full hour, and across a term that is several sessions of waiting paid at a teaching rate.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video, matched by syllabus code and component. In-home one-to-one visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted across the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, and that comparison is set out properly later on this page.

The comparisons worth your attention are three. Which provider model suits the problem you have: agency, marketplace, budget platform, freelance tutor or tuition centre. Which board and tier your child is actually entered for, since Cambridge and Pearson are different courses with different calculator rules and different grading scales. And which format suits the child, because a younger or less self-directed student genuinely benefits from somebody in the room.

What follows works through each of those with figures attributed to the provider or rate table they came from and the month they were read. Nothing here is an IB Gram price list. The point is to make the quotes you have been given comparable, including ours, so that the decision is made on something other than confidence. Three of the six best-ranked pages for Abu Dhabi tutoring queries publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Corniche family transacts in.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-corniche.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, what you are buying expertise in and where a cheaper model stops being adequate.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Two timed papers, no coursework. A budget tutor can supervise practice; only somebody who knows the specification can tell you that Cambridge separates a non-calculator paper while Pearson allows a calculator on both, which changes how arithmetic is practised.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Cambridge splits thirty per cent multiple choice, fifty theory and twenty practical. The practical component has conventions a generalist will not know: units in table headers, a line of best fit rather than a line through every point, specific error sources rather than human error.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic written with units is a discipline a budget tutor can enforce. The qualitative analysis tables and ionic equation conventions are specification knowledge, and that is where the cheaper models stop being adequate in Year 11.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest specification in the sciences, where terminology precision decides marks. Timed recall with immediate correction is the work and it does not require an examiner, which makes Biology unusually good value at the middle band rather than the top one.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Directed writing rewards correct form, audience and purpose, and students lose marks writing well while answering the wrong task. Teaching the fifteen-minute planning habit is a qualified-teacher skill rather than a specialist one.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Six short memorised quotations per text, each with a point attached, outperform wide reading with nothing quotable. That is a memorisation and structure job, which means the middle band is usually sufficient and often better than the top one.

subjects.name: Economics and Business
subjects.description: A labelled diagram earns credit before prose is read, which is the cheapest available mark in both subjects and fixable in a fortnight at any band. Definition precision is slower and needs spacing across months rather than a late push.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed, where the loss is unseen topics rather than misunderstood ones. Working through the specification checklist systematically is the approach, and it requires somebody holding the right checklist for the right code.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Trace tables and pseudocode conventions are examinable skills distinct from writing working code, which is why a professional developer is often a poor choice as a tutor here. The practical component also carries an internal deadline that drives the autumn.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with separate provision for Arab and non-Arab students. Short regular oral and written practice is the realistic intervention, which the budget band delivers perfectly well across a whole year.

sections.heading: The Corniche against Al Khalidiyah, Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
paragraphs: Here is the district comparison done properly, because families run it first and deserve a real answer. The four sit minutes apart. Their children attend the same schools, which enter the same two examination boards, which produce the same topic errors in the same order. There is no educational variable between them, and anybody claiming otherwise is selling a postcode.

The differences that do exist are about access and housing stock. The Corniche and Al Markaziyah are apartment-dominated, with the parking and lift problem described above. Al Khalidiyah is similar. Al Bateen is mixed, so in-home access varies street by street. Al Mushrif is largely villa housing, which makes in-home tutoring operationally simplest and is reflected in slightly keener quotes from tutors who prefer villa calls.

The second difference is the afternoon return, and it is small here by Abu Dhabi standards. Students attending schools in Al Bateen or Al Khalidiyah are home earliest. Students travelling to Al Mushrif are commonly fifteen to thirty minutes later. Students crossing a bridge to an island school or running out to Khalifa City are latest and almost always fix an evening slot for the year.

Read the table below as logistics rather than as a ranking. Then spend your attention on the three comparisons that follow it, which are the ones that change a grade: provider model, board and tier, and what a quote actually includes. Those three take about an hour between them and are worth considerably more than a week of asking neighbours who they use.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, with sources rather than claims
paragraphs: Every provider in this market compares itself favourably against an unnamed set of other platforms, which is not a comparison. The table below compares models rather than companies, and where a figure appears it belongs to that provider's own published page with the month it was read. That is the standard the ranking pages in this cluster generally do not meet.

Three recurring problems are worth naming because you will meet them. Some providers publish a price in structured data that contradicts the price on the visible page. At least one publishes a star rating it generated itself, which is against structured-data policy and tells you nothing about teaching quality. And several route UAE enquiries to tutors who are not in the country while implying local delivery.

The second thing to check in any model is the replacement policy. A tutor who stops being available mid-term is a normal event, and what matters is what happens next. An agency usually substitutes somebody; a freelance arrangement simply ends; a marketplace returns you to a search. Ask the question before you book rather than after, because the answer differs enormously between models and almost nobody volunteers it.

On availability, the honest position across every model is that nobody covers every subject at every hour. For IGCSE, common tiers at common hours usually match within a few days. A narrow combination at one fixed weekday hour can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is free. A provider that never says so is not more capable; it is less candid.

sections.heading: What you are actually comparing when you compare tutors
paragraphs: Most quotes in this market are not comparable because they describe different products. Before choosing between them, normalise them against the same questions. The table below is the list we use, and it is worth running whether you end up with us or with somebody else, because it exposes the differences that price alone conceals.

Two of the items matter more than the rest. The first is whether the tutor teaches your child's exact syllabus code and tier every week, because a tutor who knows the subject but not the specification will teach the wrong difficulty and the wrong conventions. The second is what happens when a session is missed, by either side, since that determines what you are actually paying for across a term.

A third item is quietly important and almost never asked: what the first session will produce. A provider that cannot answer that is selling hours rather than a plan. The right answer is a diagnosis you can check against marked work, naming whether the losses are content, question wording, unshown working or pacing, each of which needs a different remedy.

Run the list and the decision usually makes itself. Where two providers come out equivalent, choose on the thing that actually varies for a Corniche household, which is whether the full hour reaches your child or whether some of it is spent in a lift lobby. That is a small consideration per session and a real one across a term.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: the comparison nobody makes and everybody should
paragraphs: Before comparing tutors, find out which course your child is actually on. The code is printed on the front of every past paper: a four-digit number beginning with zero is Cambridge International, and a code of the form 4MA1 or 4PH1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. The schools around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif sometimes use different boards for different subjects in the same building.

The differences change what any tutor should be doing. In mathematics, Cambridge separates its papers so a candidate sits one without a calculator and one with, while Pearson permits a calculator on both; that single fact changes how arithmetic is practised for two years. In the sciences, Cambridge assesses practical skills through a practical test or the alternative to practical, while Pearson assesses the same reasoning inside its written papers.

Grading scales differ too, which confuses households with two children on different boards. Cambridge reports A* to G with Core capped at C; Pearson reports 9 to 1 with Foundation capped at 5 and Higher running from 9 down to 4, with a 3 available. A grade 6 and a grade B are not directly comparable, and a report mixing boards across subjects makes the comparison harder still.

The tier question travels with the board question and is the more consequential of the two. Ask the school in writing for the tier in each examined subject, the maximum grade that tier allows, and the last date a change can be submitted. A Cambridge Core entry caps at C and a Pearson Foundation entry at 5, and those ceilings can close science and mathematics routes at sixteen.

sections.heading: Group class, one-to-one, or a centre
paragraphs: The format comparison is usually framed as a budget question and is better framed as a diagnosis question. A group class works for a student near target who needs structure, pace and the company of others doing the same work. It costs less per hour and it provides something one-to-one does not: the reassurance of not being the only person finding a topic difficult.

What a group class cannot do is address one student's specific error pattern, because the group moves at group pace. If your child's problem is that they do not show working in multi-stage questions, or that they consistently misread evaluate as describe, those errors are invisible in a group of twelve and will survive a whole term of classes. That is not a criticism of the format; it is a statement of what it is for.

A tuition centre adds premises and a timetable, which some families value highly because it removes the scheduling problem entirely. The thing to verify is the permit: a tutoring operation with premises and staff needs an educational services permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence, and it is a reasonable thing to ask to see.

The combination that works most often is a group class for structure plus occasional one-to-one on the identified weakness, rather than either replacing the other. For a Corniche household the one-to-one half of that is simplest online, because the group class has already consumed the travel budget for the week.

sections.heading: Why the answer comes out the same across all four districts
paragraphs: If the Corniche, Al Khalidiyah, Al Bateen and Al Mushrif share schools, boards and topic errors, then whatever separates a good outcome from a poor one must sit elsewhere. It does. It sits in whether the tutor teaches your child's exact code and tier weekly, whether the diagnosis happened before the hours were bought, and whether the full hour reaches the child.

A district-based search optimises for none of those. It returns people who can reach your building, which constrains both the hours they can offer and the specifications they happen to know. On the Corniche it additionally returns people willing to deal with visitor parking and a lift lobby, which is a smaller group again and not selected for teaching quality.

The honest counterweight is that for a younger child none of this applies, because what that child needs is an adult in the room and the specification barely matters yet. Key Stage 3 fluency work is well served by a nearby tutor at a budget rate, and we would recommend that over anything we sell if it is what the situation calls for.

For Year 10 and Year 11, where the grade is decided by specification knowledge and paper technique, the district is noise. Spend the attention you were going to spend on location on the three comparisons in this page instead: provider model, board and tier, and what a quote actually includes. Each of those can be settled with an email or a phone call, and together they do more than any amount of local searching.

sections.heading: Permits, verification and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, which is both a legal fact and a useful screening tool. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18.

Because it costs nothing, a UAE-based tutor without one has no financial excuse. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

Abu Dhabi adds a layer. Press reporting indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that as press-reported rather than ADEK's exact wording and verify against the current policy if it matters to your situation.

What we will not claim: no regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram. We hold no ADEK, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval of any kind, and a KHDA educational services permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises, which we do not imply. There is no Abu Dhabi office. No provider can guarantee a grade or an improvement, including us. Every dirham figure here carries its source and the month it was read.

faqs.question: Why do two tutoring quotes for the same subject differ so much?
faqs.answer: Usually because they describe different products. One may be an agency rate including travel and a replacement policy; one a freelance rate including neither; one a platform rate for a university student rather than a qualified teacher. Published Abu Dhabi bands run from about AED 33 to 65 for student tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, and AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel. Normalise before comparing.

faqs.question: What should I ask before accepting any tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Seven things. Does the tutor teach my child's exact code and tier every week. Is travel inside the rate. What happens if a session is missed, by either side. What happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term. What will the first session produce. Is the tutor UAE-based and permitted. And can you tell me the component weightings for this subject. The last one is a published fact, so hesitation is itself the answer.

faqs.question: Do parking and lift waits really matter for an in-home session?
faqs.answer: On the Corniche, yes, and nobody quotes for it. Visitor parking in a waterfront tower is often full at the hour tutors arrive, reception procedures take minutes, and lifts at five in the afternoon are slow. A tutor who reaches the door ten minutes late has charged the full hour. Across a twelve-week term that is roughly two sessions of waiting paid at a teaching rate, which is a cost that never appears in any comparison table in this market.

faqs.question: Which provider model suits a Year 11 student with a weak paper?
faqs.answer: A specialist who teaches that exact paper, which in practice means the upper middle or specialist band, published at roughly AED 150 to 300 and AED 200 to 450 respectively. A budget platform cannot address paper technique, and a generalist agency often cannot either. The thing to verify is not the brand but whether the individual tutor teaches your child's code and tier weekly, which is a question any provider should be able to answer directly.

faqs.question: Is a group class a reasonable alternative for IGCSE revision?
faqs.answer: For a student near target who needs structure, pace and company, yes, and it costs less per hour. What a group cannot do is see one student's error pattern: if your child does not show working in multi-stage questions, or misreads evaluate as describe, those errors are invisible in a class of twelve and will survive a term. The combination that works is a group class for structure plus occasional one-to-one on the identified weakness.

faqs.question: How do I check which examination board my child sits?
faqs.answer: Look at the top of any past paper. A four-digit code beginning with zero is Cambridge International, so 0580, 0625, 0620, 0610 or 0500. A code of the form 4MA1 or 4PH1 is Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Schools around Al Bateen and Al Mushrif sometimes use different boards for different subjects in the same building, so check each examined subject rather than assuming one answer covers them all.

faqs.question: What practical difference does the board make to revision?
faqs.answer: A substantial one. In mathematics, Cambridge separates its papers so a candidate sits one without a calculator and one with, while Pearson permits a calculator on both; that changes how arithmetic is practised for two years. In the sciences, Cambridge assesses practical skills through a practical test or the alternative to practical, while Pearson assesses the same reasoning inside its written papers. Revision material bought for the wrong code teaches the wrong conventions.

faqs.question: Should I ask about a replacement policy before booking?
faqs.answer: Yes, and almost nobody does. A tutor becoming unavailable mid-term is a normal event rather than an exceptional one, and what happens next differs enormously by model. An agency usually substitutes somebody. A freelance arrangement simply ends. A marketplace returns you to a search. Ask the question before booking, because afterwards you are negotiating from a weaker position in the middle of a term you needed the sessions for.

faqs.question: How do I verify a Corniche tutor is legally permitted to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tutor work permit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government teachers, private and public-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a UAE-based tutor without one has no excuse, and those tutoring without it face penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can a tuition centre in Abu Dhabi operate without a specific licence?
faqs.answer: A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and requires an educational services permit for a training institute. That is a specific licence rather than a general trade licence, and it is a reasonable thing to ask a centre to show you. Note also that no provider, including us, should describe itself as approved by a regulator; IB Gram holds no accreditation from ADEK, MoHRE or any examination board.

faqs.question: When is a cheaper tutor genuinely the right choice?
faqs.answer: In Key Stage 3 and for supervision work, where the need is fluency and habit rather than specification knowledge. Published budget rates run from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, and for algebraic manipulation practice, vocabulary drilling or keeping a Year 8 student on top of homework that is good value. It stops being the right choice in Year 10, when habits start forming against a specific specification and installing them wrongly costs more than it saved.

faqs.question: What should the first paid session produce on the Corniche?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis you can check against marked work, naming whether the losses are content not known, question wording misread, working not shown, or time running out. Those four need different remedies and different numbers of hours. A provider who cannot tell you in advance what the first session will produce is selling hours rather than a plan, and that is the clearest signal available before any money moves.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff the subject and hour we need?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the slot with a generalist. Common IGCSE subjects at common hours usually match within a few days. A specific tier at one fixed weekday hour can take a week or more, and occasionally nobody suitable is free at all. Corniche households compete with Al Reem, Al Bateen and Saadiyat families for the same early-evening window. Hearing that early leaves you time to try another provider while it still matters.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-corniche.closingHeading: Bring your quotes, we will make them comparable
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-corniche.closingBody: Send the quotes you already have, the syllabus code from a past paper, the tier if you know it, and the most recent marked script. We will normalise the quotes against the same questions, classify where the marks are going, and tell you which provider model fits the problem, including when a cheaper one does. The resulting sheet is yours whoever you use. If it is us, your child meets a specialist in that specification on a free trial lesson first, live online, one to one.

intro.heading: Start from the date on the entry form, not from the subject
paragraphs: Almost every parent who types "IGCSE home tutor in Eastern Mangroves" into Google is doing it in the same week of the year: the week a report comes home, or the week a mock paper gets handed back with a grade nobody expected. The instinct is to find a person. The more useful first step is to find the date. Your child is entered for a specific series, with a specific set of papers, and everything a tutor can usefully do is bounded by how many teaching weeks sit between today and that first paper.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Those are the two windows a candidate in the UAE works to. Counted in school weeks rather than calendar weeks, a family starting in the first half of the autumn term has roughly two full terms of teaching available before a June paper; a family starting after the mock results has closer to one. The same tutor, the same subject and the same child produce very different outcomes across those two windows, and the honest version of this page says so.

Eastern Mangroves sits on the eastern edge of Abu Dhabi island, built around the marina and the mangrove channel, with Salam Street and the Sheikh Zayed Bridge both minutes away. That geography matters for one practical reason: children living here are bussed or driven in several directions — into the Al Bateen and Al Mushrif school belt, across to Al Reem Island, over the bridge to Saadiyat, or out along the highway to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. A tutor who happens to live nearby does not solve the problem, because the problem is the hour between the school gate and dinner, not the distance between two addresses.

That is why IB Gram delivers one-to-one teaching for UAE families over live video rather than in the home. Home visits are a service we run only in India. In the UAE the delivery model is online, and it buys something a local search cannot: the tutor is chosen for the syllabus and the paper, not for the postcode. A family here needing Cambridge Physics 0625 Paper 6 practice, or Edexcel Maths 4MA1 Higher tier, gets the person who teaches that paper every week — not whoever is free within a twenty-minute drive of the promenade.

What follows is the page we would want if we were the ones with eight weeks left. The exam year counted backwards with the deadlines that are set by other people. An eight-week plan with the evidence that each week worked. What the Abu Dhabi market charges, in dirhams, attributed to who publishes it. What the Ramadan weeks and the mock window do to a revision timetable. And a clear line on what a tutor may and may not touch when coursework is involved.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-eastern-ma.programmesIntro: Eastern Mangroves children sit in three different parts of the same British-curriculum pipeline, and each part has a different relationship with time. Lower Secondary has years of slack; Year 11 has weeks. The entries below describe what a tutor is actually working on at each stage in an Abu Dhabi school year.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary (Years 7-9)
programmes.description: The years before the syllabus codes appear. Schools use Cambridge Lower Secondary or their own scheme of work, and the Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October windows. Nothing here is examined by a board for a final grade, which makes it the cheapest place in the whole pipeline to fix an algebra gap or a written-answer habit. A single term of fortnightly support in Year 8 removes work that otherwise costs a full term in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi this is also the stage where a family's curriculum choice is still reversible. Children moving in from a CBSE, American or IB Middle Years setting usually arrive here, and the mismatch shows up in two specific places: algebraic manipulation and the structure of an extended written answer. ADEK inspection reports on the Al Bateen and Al Mushrif schools frequently comment on writing stamina rather than content knowledge.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 10
programmes.description: Content delivery year. Most of the specification gets taught here, and most of it gets taught once. The usual pattern in Abu Dhabi schools is that Year 10 ends with an internal examination that doubles as the tier and set decision for Year 11. A tutor in Year 10 is doing consolidation rather than rescue: closing the topics that were taught during a term the child was unwell, travelling or new to the school.
programmes.countryNote: Year 10 is also when the board becomes visible. An Eastern Mangroves family with children at two different schools can easily have one child on Cambridge 0580 and one on Edexcel 4MA1, with different paper structures, different calculator rules and different tiering. Knowing which code is on the entry is the single most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first session.

programmes.name: IGCSE Year 11
programmes.description: Examination year, and the one every search for a tutor is really about. Teaching time runs out around the end of the spring term, when study leave starts. Everything after that is practice under timed conditions against mark schemes. The work that moves a grade here is narrow and diagnosable: command-term discipline, working shown for method marks, and the two or three topics that recur in every past paper the student gets wrong.
programmes.countryNote: Year 11 in Abu Dhabi has two fixed obstacles that a tutor has to plan around rather than ignore: the mock window, usually in the weeks either side of the winter break, and the Ramadan weeks with their shortened school day. Both change what a session can achieve, and both are visible on the school calendar months in advance.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level, IBDP or the equivalency file
programmes.description: The IGCSE grades are not the end of the paperwork. They feed a sixth-form entry decision and, for families staying in the UAE, the Ministry of Education equivalency file that sits behind a local university application. The grade profile that matters is not the average but the specific subjects: the ones a sixth form uses as a prerequisite and the five the Ministry counts.
programmes.countryNote: For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects at IGCSE or GCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. Verify the current wording with the Ministry before acting on it; IB Gram describes the process and does not perform it.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-eastern-ma.subjectsIntro: Requests from this part of Abu Dhabi island cluster tightly around maths and the three sciences, with English Language second and Business and Economics behind that. The descriptions below name where the marks actually go, because that is what decides whether eight weeks is enough.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two written papers on both boards, no coursework. Marks are lost in three repeatable places: non-calculator arithmetic under time pressure, multi-step algebra where the method mark is never claimed because working is skipped, and the final-part question that needs two topics joined together. A tier error costs more than any of them, because the Core and Foundation ceiling caps the grade.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken by students heading for A Level Maths or an IB Higher Level maths course. The content overlaps with the first term of a sixth-form course, which makes it the single best bridge for a strong Year 11. Marks go on proof layout, calculus notation and the discipline of writing a full solution rather than an answer.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical paper decide most grades. Cambridge candidates sitting Paper 6 need to describe a method precisely enough for somebody else to repeat it, identify the controlled variable and read a graph gradient with units. None of that is taught by watching; it is taught by writing method answers and having them marked against the published scheme.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic reaction pathways are the three topics that separate a 6 from an 8. The pattern in marked papers is consistent: the chemistry is understood, the calculation is set out without units or significant figures, and two marks disappear per question.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The highest-content science and the one where command terms matter most. A question that says 'explain' and receives a description earns nothing. Transport in plants, enzymes and inheritance are the recurring loss points, and the fix is answer structure rather than more revision reading.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the composition carry the paper. Students who read widely still lose marks because they do not plan, so the response drifts away from the audience and purpose named in the question. Timed writing with annotation against the assessment criteria moves this faster than any other intervention.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with a different mark scheme and different university recognition. Worth checking which one is on the entry, because families sometimes discover the answer only when results arrive.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole game. Definitions are worth little; applying a concept to the specific business in the insert is worth most of the paper. Students who revise by memorising terms plateau around a 5 and stay there until they practise application.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the theory paper. The theory half is heavily content-based and rewards systematic coverage; the programming half rewards writing code by hand on paper, which almost no student practises until a tutor insists on it.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the international curriculum under federal rules, taught in separate streams for Arab and non-Arab students. These subjects sit outside the five the Ministry of Education counts for British-track equivalency, which surprises most families the first time they read the requirement.

regions.note: Over the Sheikh Zayed Bridge, and the longest regular run from this pocket. A child leaving a Saadiyat school at 3.30pm is rarely settled before 4.45pm, so early-evening sessions work and immediate-after-school ones do not.

regions.note: The far northern end of the emirate, relevant here because siblings sometimes split between an island school and one closer to the Dubai border. Two children, two commutes, two different session times.

This is the format for Years 9 and 10, and for a Year 11 student who starts early enough that teaching is still possible rather than only revision. Progress is measured against school assessments, not against the tutor's own tests.
