sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor in Eastern Mangroves can still change this term
paragraphs: An IGCSE home tutor in Eastern Mangroves, in the sense parents mean when they search for one, is a subject specialist working one-to-one with a single child on a named syllabus. IB Gram provides exactly that, delivered over live video to families on this part of Abu Dhabi island. We do not send tutors to UAE addresses; in-home visiting is something we run only in India. The teaching, the marking and the planning are identical. The travel is the only thing missing, and the travel was never the part that moved the grade.

The useful question is what a term can still do. With two terms left before a June paper, a tutor can teach content, rebuild a topic from scratch and change a student's working habits. With one term left, content teaching is mostly over and the work shifts to recovering marks the student is already capable of earning: method lines, command terms, units, significant figures, and the discipline of reading the question twice. With four weeks left, the honest answer is paper technique and nothing else, and a tutor who promises more than that is selling comfort.

That distinction decides what you should buy. Families in this neighbourhood frequently arrive having already bought the wrong thing — a long weekly commitment when three focused sessions on one topic would have done, or three sessions in May when a term in January was the real need. The first conversation should therefore be about the calendar, the entry and a marked paper, in that order. Everything else follows from those three facts, and all three are free to establish.

One practical note specific to this pocket of the island. Because children here travel in four different directions for school, families with more than one child almost never get a single convenient hour. Online delivery is what makes two different slots on the same evening possible at all, and it is the reason a sibling pair at an island school and a Khalifa City school can both be taught properly in the same week.
bullets: Two terms left: content teaching is genuinely possible
One term left: recover marks the student can already earn

sections.heading: The IGCSE year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what parents are actually acting on. The dates below are the ones set by other people — the board, the school and the examinations officer — and they close in an order that surprises families who assume the exam date is the only deadline that matters.

The sequence runs roughly like this. Final entries are submitted by the school's examinations officer months before the papers, and that submission fixes the board, the tier and the subject list. Mock examinations follow, usually either side of the winter break, and the mock result is what most schools use to confirm or change a predicted grade. Study leave removes teaching time entirely. Then the papers themselves, then results, then the narrow window for a review of marking, and finally the resit entry for the November series if one is needed.

Cambridge adds one more complication worth knowing about. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A parent planning a family trip around what looks like the published date should confirm the zone version with the school, not with a search result.

The table below is a planning skeleton rather than a list of dates, which is deliberate. Dates get revised, and a page that restates them goes stale without anyone touching it. Link the official timetable from Cambridge or Pearson and check it each series.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, written as a plan rather than a promise
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block families in Abu Dhabi most often buy, usually because that is what sits between a disappointing mock and the start of study leave. It is enough to move a grade when the gap is technique and not knowledge, and it is not enough to teach a specification that was never covered. Being clear about which situation you are in is the whole of the planning problem.

A block that works has a shape. The first session is a marked paper, because nothing else tells you where the marks went. The next three take the two or three error types that paper revealed and attack them one at a time, with homework that produces evidence between sessions. The midpoint is a second timed paper on the same specification, which either shows movement or shows that the diagnosis was wrong. The last three sessions are timing, command terms and the specific question styles the student still avoids.

What a block should not contain is new content in weeks seven and eight. Material introduced that late tends to collapse under examination pressure, and it displaces the practice that would have earned marks reliably. If the diagnosis in week one shows that a third of the specification is missing, the honest recommendation is a longer plan, a tier conversation with the school, or a November resit route — not a faster version of the same eight weeks.

The plan below is the one we would put in front of a Year 11 family at the promenade with a June paper ahead of them. The third column is the part most revision plans leave out: the evidence that the week actually worked, stated in advance so it cannot be rationalised afterwards.

sections.heading: Why the tier decision closes long before the paper
paragraphs: The entry form carries more weight than any revision plan, and most families never see it. On Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 a candidate is entered for either the Core or the Extended tier; on Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 it is Foundation or Higher. The tier fixes the ceiling. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available, regardless of how well the papers are answered, and that cap is invisible until results day.

Schools make the decision on evidence — set placement, Year 10 examinations, the mock — and they make it to a board deadline that sits months before the papers. Which means the window to argue for a different tier is the window before the entry is submitted, not the term before the exam. A parent who wants to make that case needs marked evidence that the student can handle the harder paper, not an opinion. That evidence is exactly what a diagnostic session plus two timed sections produces.

There is a mirror-image error that costs just as much. A student entered on the higher tier who cannot access the back half of the paper loses marks they would have banked comfortably on the lower one, and the resulting grade can be worse than a confident Core entry. Neither direction is automatically right. The decision belongs to the school, informed by evidence, and a tutor's job is to produce the evidence rather than to lobby.

The same logic applies to the subject list itself. Dropping a subject, moving a science from triple to a combined award, or adding Additional Mathematics all have deadlines attached, and all of them are easier in the autumn term than in the spring. Families who raise these questions in February are usually told, accurately, that it is too late.
bullets: Ask the school which code and tier each child is entered for, in writing
Collect marked evidence before arguing for a tier change, not after
Check whether a science is entered as separate subjects or a combined award
Know that the ceiling on a lower tier applies however well the paper is answered

sections.heading: Online or in-home for a family on the mangrove channel
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real market in Abu Dhabi with real prices, and a page that pretends otherwise is not much use to a parent weighing options. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one visits, travel included, somewhere between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour; Bestimate's 2026 rate table for the Emirates puts the common band at AED 180 to 350, with specialist IB and IGCSE tutors quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above. Monthly in-home packages advertised in this market have run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits.

Online rates sit lower because the travel is not being paid for. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200; EdFlik advertises budget online sessions from AED 45 to 65; Tutopiya quotes from roughly AED 33 to 52 at the entry level, and an AED 799 monthly plan for eight sessions has been advertised in this market. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for a specialist. Those are their published figures, not ours, and they are the numbers a family in Eastern Mangroves is choosing between.

The money is only half the comparison, though. For a family at the promenade the other half is the hour between 3.15pm and 4.45pm, which is when the bus arrives, the uniform comes off and the attention disappears. An in-home visit consumes a slice of that hour in arrival and settling; a video session starts at the minute agreed. Over a term of weekly sessions the difference is measured in several hours of actual teaching, which is worth more than the per-hour saving in either direction.

The comparison below is about formats, not brands. IB Gram's own position in it is straightforward: one-to-one online, a free trial lesson first, and no visits to UAE addresses. If an in-home visit is what a family wants, the honest answer is that it is available in this market from other providers at the rates above, and that we do not provide it here.

sections.heading: What the Abu Dhabi school year does to a revision timetable
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the local calendar in front of it falls apart in week three. The Abu Dhabi school year has a shape, and a family planning eight weeks of tutoring needs to know where the holes are before they buy the block rather than after.

Three features matter most. The winter break lands in the middle of the mock season for most schools, which means a student either revises through it or arrives at the mock cold. The Ramadan weeks bring a shortened school day, which sounds like extra study time and usually is not: children come home earlier but with less energy, and the most productive sessions during that period are short, early-evening or post-Iftar, and agreed in advance rather than improvised week by week. And study leave, which looks like a gift, removes the structure that was holding a weak revision habit together.

The practical response is to decide, at the start of a block, which weeks are real teaching weeks and which are maintenance. A family that plans six teaching weeks and two maintenance weeks gets more done than one that plans eight and loses three to a holiday, a school trip and a bad fortnight. It also costs less, because maintenance weeks can be shorter sessions.

There is a quieter benefit to planning this way. A student who knows in advance that the Ramadan fortnight is a lighter period, and that the two weeks after it are heavy, does not experience the heavy weeks as a punishment. Revision collapses far more often from a student giving up on a plan than from the plan being wrong.
bullets: Mark the mock window, the winter break and the Ramadan weeks before buying a block
Expect shortened school days to lower energy rather than raise available hours
Plan post-Iftar or early-evening sessions in advance, not week by week
Treat study leave as a structure problem, not a time problem

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what the rating means
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi private schools, including every school an Eastern Mangroves family is likely to use, sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. It is worth knowing that ADEK is named by effectively none of the tutoring pages competing for this search, which tells you something about how locally grounded most of them are.

The wider map matters for families who move within the country, which in this neighbourhood is common. Dubai private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, and Ras Al Khaimah's by its Department of Knowledge; both of those authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

An inspection rating is a judgement about a school, not about your child's subject. A school rated highly overall can still have a weak department, and a school rated lower can have an outstanding one. The useful reading is the subject-level commentary inside the report, which is where a parent finds out whether the issue they are seeing at home is visible to the inspectors too. That is a far better basis for deciding whether to buy tutoring than the headline band.

One thing a parent should never see claimed is regulator approval for a tutoring provider. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval, accreditation or licence, and does not claim any. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and any tutoring page implying it holds one without the permit number is misrepresenting itself.

sections.heading: Where a tutor's help stops: coursework, papers and permits
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry work a student submits rather than sits, and the boundary around that work is not negotiable. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain the assessment criteria, question a student about their own reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write the coursework, does not rewrite paragraphs into their own words, and does not supply content for a student to submit as their own. That line protects the student, because the consequence of crossing it falls on them.

The same restraint applies to materials. We do not reproduce or supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to the boards, they are published on the boards' own sites, and the right thing to do is cite and link them. A provider offering a library of copied mark schemes is offering a copyright problem, and in the case of unreleased material, a malpractice problem.

Permits are the third boundary, and the one most parents do not know to ask about. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so any page quoting an amount is guessing.

One further rule applies in this emirate specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct carries a similar restriction. So the apparently convenient option — your child's own subject teacher, privately, in the evening — is the one to avoid. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it, as the detail is press-reported.

whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0625 Paper 6 specialist and an Edexcel 4PH1 specialist are not interchangeable, and neither is likely to live within a short drive of the mangrove channel. Choosing online means choosing from the people who teach that exact paper every week.

faqs.question: How many teaching weeks are left before my child's IGCSE papers?
faqs.answer: Count school weeks, not calendar weeks, and stop counting at the start of study leave rather than at the first paper. Then subtract the winter break, the Ramadan fortnight if it falls inside your window, any school trip and the mock weeks themselves. Families on this stretch of the island are usually surprised by how much the figure shrinks: an apparently comfortable twelve weeks becomes seven or eight real teaching weeks. That number is what determines whether a tutor can teach content or only recover marks the student can already earn, so it is the first thing worth establishing.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to an apartment at Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching for families here is one-to-one over live video, at a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for working through paper questions. The practical trade is straightforward: you give up having somebody physically in the room, and in exchange your child is taught by a specialist in the exact syllabus and paper they are entered for rather than by whoever happens to live nearby.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series will a candidate in Abu Dhabi actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and those are the two your child's centre will use. Cambridge offers an additional February/March series to India only, so a page quoting those dates at a UAE family is quoting the wrong country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November window is also the normal resit route after a summer result. Confirm the exact paper dates against the official timetable for your school's administrative zone.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge administrative zone and why does it change the timetable?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. For a family planning travel around what looks like the published date, that is a real risk. Ask your school's examinations officer which zone the centre sits in and work from that timetable, not from a date found in a search result.

faqs.question: Can we still change my child's tier before the entry is submitted?
faqs.answer: Only before the school submits final entries, which happens months ahead of the papers. On Cambridge Mathematics 0580 the choice is Core or Extended; on Edexcel 4MA1 it is Foundation or Higher, and the lower tier caps the grade available however well the papers are answered. If you want to argue for a change, bring marked evidence that your child can access the harder paper — two timed sections and a diagnostic session usually produce it. The decision belongs to the school, and after the deadline it is simply closed.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week block of IGCSE tutoring cost in this part of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Take the market bands rather than a single number. Qualified online subject tutors are published in this market from around AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IGCSE and IB specialists quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above; in-home visits including travel are advertised from roughly AED 180 to 500. One weekly hour across eight weeks therefore runs from about AED 1,200 at the lower qualified rate to AED 3,600 at specialist rates. Those are other providers' published figures as at October 2026. IB Gram quotes after a free trial rather than publishing a tariff.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting tutoring four weeks before the first paper?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, provided everyone is honest about what four weeks buys. It is enough for paper technique: timing, question order, command-term discipline, claiming method marks, units and significant figures. It is not enough to teach a topic that was never covered, and a plan that tries to do both usually delivers neither. For a student who understands the material but keeps scoring below their ability, four focused weeks can genuinely move a grade. For a student with a third of the specification missing, the better conversation is about the November series.

faqs.question: How do we find out which board and code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer rather than the subject teacher, and ask in writing for the syllabus code and tier on each entry. You should get something like Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher. It matters more than parents expect: the two boards structure papers differently, apply different calculator rules and tier differently, so past papers from the wrong board waste revision time while feeling productive. Families here with children at two different schools often find each child is on a different board entirely.

faqs.question: Will the Ramadan weeks help or hurt my child's revision?
faqs.answer: Shortened school days look like extra study time and rarely behave that way. Children come home earlier with less energy, so the hours exist but the concentration does not. What works is deciding in advance that the fortnight is a lighter maintenance period — shorter sessions, early evening or after Iftar, agreed in advance rather than improvised — and that the weeks either side carry the heavy work. A revision plan that quietly assumes normal capacity through that period is the kind that collapses in its third week.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework my child has to submit?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the skill the coursework assesses, explain the published criteria, ask questions that make a student examine their own reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the work, does not rewrite paragraphs and does not supply material to be submitted as the student's own. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the child, not on the tutor, which is why we state the boundary before any coursework subject starts rather than when a deadline is close.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor working with my child in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any page quoting an exact amount with suspicion.

faqs.question: Is it acceptable to pay my child's own school teacher for evening lessons in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is the arrangement to avoid in this emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. Beyond the rules, the arrangement is poor practice: the person marking the work should not also be paid to prepare it. A specialist with no connection to the school gives you an independent read on where the marks are going.

faqs.question: What will my child's IGCSE grades need to show for Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or grade 3, together with one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking competitor publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Confirm the current requirement with the Ministry or the attestation authority directly; IB Gram describes the process and does not carry it out or guarantee an outcome.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject we need this term?
faqs.answer: We tell you at the first conversation instead of placing a generalist and hoping it works out. Scarce combinations — a particular science paper at a particular hour, or a minority language — sometimes have no match in the slot a family wants. Where that happens you get the choice plainly: a different time with the right specialist, a wait with a date attached, or a tutor based outside the UAE with their location stated before the trial lesson rather than after it. Nobody is placed into a subject they do not teach.

faqs.question: How will we know after a month whether the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: By comparing two marked papers rather than two opinions. The first session produces a timed paper with the error types written down; the midpoint produces a second one on the same specification, marked the same way. Movement should be visible by topic, not just in the total. You should also hear a change in how your child describes the subject: naming a specific weakness is progress, while vague reassurance usually is not. If neither has happened in four weeks, the plan or the tutor is wrong and should change.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-eastern-ma.closingHeading: Start with the date, then the paper, then the tutor
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-eastern-ma.closingBody: If your child is in Year 11 with a June paper ahead of them, the useful next step takes ten minutes: find the syllabus code and tier on the entry, count the real teaching weeks left, and send a marked mock paper. We will tell you honestly what that window can achieve, arrange a free trial lesson with an IGCSE specialist in that exact subject, and scope a block with an end date before study leave. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, for families across Eastern Mangroves and the wider island.

intro.heading: Start with the invoice, not the brochure
paragraphs: A family on Hudayriyat Island who types "IGCSE home tutor" into Google is rarely short of options. What they are short of is a number. Three of the six agency pages ranking for UAE tutoring queries in October 2026 published no price at all, and the two that did quoted US dollars, which is not the currency anybody here pays school fees in. GetYourTutors, the strongest single page in that set at roughly 2,294 words, even asks the price question in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it. So the first thing this page does is publish the market bands in AED and say where each one came from.

The honest answer has a wide range, because the UAE tutoring market is wide. At the bottom, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which in practice buys a university student working from the textbook. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, is quoted between AED 180 and 500, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table putting the middle of that at AED 180 to 350. A named IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier reaches AED 650. Those are market figures from other people's published pages, read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list.

Converted to a monthly budget, which is how most families on this island actually plan, the same bands look different. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packaged offers in this market include an online plan at AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Read those two side by side and the structure of the decision becomes clear: the in-home plan costs roughly twice as much for half as many contact points.

Hudayriyat Island sharpens that arithmetic more than most Abu Dhabi addresses. The island is reached by bridge from Al Bateen, residential handovers here are recent, and there is no established cluster of Cambridge-experienced teachers living a few minutes away. A tutor driving to a villa on Hudayriyat is driving from the mainland or from Abu Dhabi island, and that drive is inside the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not. The pool of people willing to make it twice a week, in the right subject, at the right paper tier, is small. Narrow pool plus travel cost is the worst combination a parent can buy into, because it quietly decides the tutor for you.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Hudayriyat Island families are one-to-one over live video, scheduled around the school run and the evening, with a shared whiteboard and a recording the student can replay. That removes the travel premium from the price and removes the radius from the choice. A Year 11 student working towards Extended tier Cambridge Mathematics gets a tutor who has taught that tier and marked that paper, rather than the best available person inside a twenty-minute drive of a bridge.

The rest of this page is built the same way: what the market charges, what each band buys, where families waste money, and what you can verify before you pay anybody. Every AED figure carries its source. Every exam date is named by its series rather than a year, so it stays true. Where something could not be verified — and IB session dates are the main case — this page says so instead of guessing.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education, examined subject by subject with a separate grade for each. Many subjects are tiered: Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, the sciences into Core and Extended papers, and the tier a school enters a child for caps the grade available. Written papers dominate the mark, with practical and coursework components varying by subject.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi centres are allocated to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A family on Hudayriyat Island should take the zone timetable from their own school's exams officer rather than from a generic online calendar.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international GCSE, graded 9 to 1, sat by a large share of British-curriculum students in Abu Dhabi. Mathematics Specification A, code 4MA1, runs Foundation and Higher tiers across two papers. Pearson's structure differs from Cambridge in assessment routes and in how some subjects handle practical skills, which matters when a child moves school mid-course.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com, because provisional versions are revised.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The stage immediately before IGCSE, assessed through Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests. Checkpoint results are the earliest honest signal of whether a child is on a Core or an Extended trajectory in Mathematics and the sciences, and they arrive early enough for the gap to be closed without buying exam-year rates.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. For a family on Hudayriyat Island, that calendar is the cheapest intervention point available: a Year 8 Checkpoint result acted on costs a fraction of Year 11 crisis tuition at specialist rates.

programmes.name: AS and A Level progression
programmes.description: Where most Abu Dhabi British-curriculum students go after IGCSE. The step up is steepest in Mathematics and the sciences, because A Level assumes the Extended tier content as a floor rather than a ceiling. A child entered for Core tier at IGCSE has a measurable gap to close before AS Mathematics is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. That requirement shapes A Level subject choice well before results day.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Abu Dhabi island families ask for most, with the part of each one where marks actually go missing. Hours are not interchangeable across subjects: a Mathematics tier problem and a Biology recall problem need different work, and paying specialist rates for the wrong one is the most common waste in this market.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision dominates everything. Core tier caps the grade, and a child sitting Core while targeting an A Level in a numerate subject has a structural problem, not a revision problem. Marks are lost on method presentation, non-calculator arithmetic, and the multi-step questions at the back of the paper where working is worth more than the answer.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics and Further Pure
subjects.description: Taken alongside standard IGCSE Mathematics by students heading for A Level Mathematics or engineering. Calculus and trigonometric identities arrive here first, and the jump in abstraction is where confident Extended students suddenly stall. Worth real hours in Year 11 if the A Level route is already decided.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are the reliable failure point. Students who can recite the equations lose marks on circuit reasoning, on graph interpretation, and on the extended-response questions that ask why rather than what. Practical skills are assessed through an alternative-to-practical paper at most centres.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways carry disproportionate marks and disproportionate panic. The recoverable marks sit in ionic equations, titration arithmetic and precise state symbols — all of which respond quickly to marked past-paper work rather than to re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students lose marks by writing general answers to specific command terms: describe, explain and suggest each have a mark-scheme meaning. Genetics, transport in plants and homeostasis are the topics most often half-learned.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A large share of Abu Dhabi candidates sit ESL rather than First Language English. Reading comprehension technique and the summary question are where the marks are, and both are trainable in a handful of sessions. Note that ESL and First Language English are counted differently by some university admissions offices.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature (0500 / 0475)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended-response essay reward structure over vocabulary. Students arrive able to identify a technique but unable to explain its effect on a reader, which is where the band descriptors separate a 6 from an 8. Timed essay practice with marking is the only reliable fix.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation language decide the top band. A correctly labelled supply and demand shift is worth more than a paragraph of description, and the evaluation sentence at the end of a long-answer question is the one most candidates skip entirely.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode logic and the theory paper pull in opposite directions. Students comfortable writing code lose marks on binary arithmetic, data representation and network theory, which are pure recall. The algorithm trace questions are the highest-yield practice available.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the licensed international curriculum as a Ministry requirement in UAE private schools, and it is examined separately from the IGCSE suite. First-language and additional-language streams are taught apart because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

subjects.name: Geography and History (0460 / 0470)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity is the whole game. A named example with a date and a figure scores where a generic description does not, and the source-based questions in History need a method rather than knowledge. Both subjects reward a revision timetable built around command terms.

subjects.name: ICT (0417)
subjects.description: Two practical papers plus a theory paper, and students usually underestimate the practical marking criteria. Document and spreadsheet tasks are marked against precise specifications, so a near-miss on a formatting instruction loses the mark outright.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat.regionsIntro: Hudayriyat Island sits inside a wider Abu Dhabi school catchment, and families here routinely drive to campuses in several of these districts. Online delivery means the tutor list does not change when the address does, which is why these neighbouring areas share the same coverage.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: The mainland side of the Hudayriyat bridge and the district most Hudayriyat families cross into first. Al Bateen Academy's IB Diploma provision sits here, and the morning bridge traffic is the single biggest factor in what time an evening session can realistically start.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A separate island with its own school cluster and its own bridge. A tutor who covers both Saadiyat and Hudayriyat in one evening is driving the length of Abu Dhabi island between them, which is exactly the cost online delivery removes.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High-density towers with a large British-curriculum population and The British International School Abu Dhabi nearby. Reem families and Hudayriyat families compete for the same small pool of Extended-tier science tutors.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: East of the city with its own campuses and a long commute to the western islands. Yas and Hudayriyat sit at opposite ends of the same tutor market, which is why in-home rates in both carry a travel component.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The Al Raha corridor runs along the Abu Dhabi–Dubai road and holds a concentrated British-curriculum enrolment. Sessions here are usually booked after 5pm because the school run plus the corridor traffic eats the late afternoon.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Villa communities with a heavy IGCSE and IB intake and a well-known 4pm bottleneck. Families in Khalifa City ask the same cost questions as Hudayriyat families and face the same travel loading on in-home rates.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Reef
regions.note: Mainland communities further from the island campuses, where the drive is long enough that an in-home tutor's travel is often non-negotiable. Online removes the constraint entirely and widens the subject-specialist pool.

regions.name: The Corniche and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established central districts with older school campuses and a mixture of British, IB and Ministry curriculum provision. Many Hudayriyat children were enrolled here before moving to the island, so their school and their address no longer match.

schoolClusters.note: The campuses Hudayriyat Island families reach first, crossing the bridge into Al Bateen and continuing along the island. Several run Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE alongside other provision, and the mix of boards within a single district is why asking which board your child's school uses is the first question on this page.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor costs on Hudayriyat Island, in AED and by the month
paragraphs: A qualified IGCSE tutor working online in this market charges roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour; the same quality of tutor coming to a villa is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is inside the rate. Those are published market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. Converted to a monthly commitment at one session a week, the gap is roughly AED 120 to 800 a month for identical teaching.

Monthly framing is more useful than hourly framing because it is how school fees, transport and activities are already budgeted in Abu Dhabi. Bestimate's rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a mid-market qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Against that, the packaged offers in this market are revealing: AED 799 a month buys eight online sessions, while AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month buys four in-home visits of two hours each. Same eight hours in one case, twice the price in the other, with the difference going to a car.

Hudayriyat Island has no established local tutor population, because residential handovers here are recent and the island was developed as a leisure and lifestyle destination before it was a school catchment. Every in-home tutor is arriving over the bridge from Al Bateen or further. That is a real cost to them and it is priced in, openly or otherwise. It also quietly reduces your choice: the tutor who will do the drive on a Tuesday at 5pm may not be the tutor who has marked Extended tier 0580 for five years.

The table below sets the market bands against a monthly figure and a per-hour figure so the two are comparable. Every band is attributed. IB Gram's own position sits deliberately outside the table: the first lesson is a free trial, and pricing is quoted after a consultation once the subject, tier and number of sessions are known, because quoting a flat hourly rate across every subject and tier is how competitor pages end up contradicting themselves.

sections.heading: The travel premium, priced honestly
paragraphs: The difference between an online rate and an in-home rate is not a quality difference. It is a logistics charge, and on an island reached by a single bridge it is a large one. A tutor who spends fifty minutes in a car to deliver sixty minutes of teaching has an effective hourly cost close to double the stated rate, and either the price reflects that or the tutor stops accepting the booking. Both outcomes are bad for a family on Hudayriyat Island.

There are things the premium genuinely buys. A younger child who cannot yet work independently at a screen benefits from somebody physically present. A household with unreliable connectivity has a practical problem online cannot solve. A student with specific access needs may work better face to face. Those cases are real and this page is not going to pretend otherwise. What the premium does not buy is better subject knowledge, and in Years 10 and 11 subject knowledge is almost always the binding constraint.

Against that, the premium costs things that are easy to miss on the first invoice. Cancellations become expensive because the tutor's travel slot cannot be refilled. Rescheduling around a school event or a family trip is hard. The session has to happen at the time the drive allows, which in Abu Dhabi usually means after the worst of the traffic rather than when the child is freshest. And the subject pool shrinks to whoever is both qualified and willing to cross the bridge, which on a specialist paper tier can be nobody at all.

The comparison below is the one families actually need. It is not a list of advantages; it sets out what each format costs, what it constrains, and where it genuinely wins. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE, so the in-home column describes the market rather than an option we offer.

sections.heading: Where families on this island waste money
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A parent sees a disappointing Year 10 report, books two sessions a week for a term, and discovers in March that the problem was tier placement rather than effort. Six months of weekly tuition at mid-market rates is somewhere around AED 3,000 to 6,000; one diagnostic hour against a marked past paper would have found it. The sequence matters more than the spend.

The second is paying specialist rates for general help. An AED 450 an hour subject specialist earns that rate on paper technique, tier strategy and exam-season triage. Paying it to supervise homework or re-teach Year 9 content is a poor allocation of the same budget, and the tutor will usually say so if asked directly. Conversely, paying AED 50 an hour for help with Extended tier organic chemistry in the final term is false economy of a different kind.

The third is the unexamined package. Monthly plans look tidy and they hide two things: the per-hour rate once travel and admin are inside it, and what happens when the family wants to stop. Ask for the hourly equivalent, ask what a cancellation costs, and ask what happens to unused sessions. A provider who cannot answer those three questions in writing is not a provider to commit a term to.

The fourth is paying for a credential that has not been evidenced. Examiner status is the clearest example: several pages in this market describe tutors as examiners for boards without showing anything verifiable, and the premium attached to the word is substantial. If examiner experience is part of the price, ask which board, which component and which years, and ask it before the first invoice rather than after the third.

sections.heading: Hudayriyat Island: a new address with an off-island school run
paragraphs: Hudayriyat Island was developed as a leisure and lifestyle destination before it became a residential address, and the school-age population here is newer than the housing. There is no long-established campus cluster on the island itself, so the school run crosses the bridge into Al Bateen and then continues along Abu Dhabi island or out to the Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor. That single fact explains most of what is distinctive about arranging tuition here.

The practical consequence is a late and compressed evening. A child leaving a campus in the central districts at around 3pm is home across the bridge later than a child who lives five minutes from the gate, and the window between arriving home and being too tired to learn anything is short. Families here tend to book either immediately after the commute or after dinner, and the second option works considerably better for Mathematics and the sciences than the first.

It also means your child's school and your address no longer tell the same story. Many Hudayriyat families were enrolled elsewhere in Abu Dhabi before moving to the island, so the board, the paper tier and the assessment calendar all belong to a campus some distance away. A tutor needs the school's scheme of work and its mock timetable, not a generic one, and an in-home tutor selected for proximity to the house has no particular connection to the campus that sets the deadlines.

Online delivery turns the geography into a non-issue. The session happens wherever the child is sitting, which on this island is a useful property in itself: families here travel, and a student who is on Saadiyat for the weekend or out of the country during a school break does not lose the slot. The tutor is chosen for having taught the exact paper tier, and the bridge stops being part of the decision.

sections.heading: Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1 — the question that decides the price of help
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum schools do not all use the same board, and families frequently do not know which one their own school enters for. This matters more than almost anything else on this page, because a tutor working from the wrong board's past papers is wasting every hour you pay for. Cambridge and Pearson cover similar ground and assess it differently: different papers, different tier names, different formula provision, different command-term conventions.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended. Pearson's Mathematics Specification A, 4MA1, splits into Foundation and Higher. The grade ceilings differ, the paper structures differ, and the amount of calculator work differs. A student moving between an Extended Cambridge class and a Higher Pearson class mid-course has a specific, identifiable gap, and naming it is a twenty-minute job for a tutor who knows both specifications.

The same applies across the sciences. Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are not interchangeable, and the treatment of practical assessment in particular is different. This is where a generic tutor and a board-specific tutor diverge sharply in value: the generic tutor teaches the physics, which the student can mostly get from school, while the board-specific tutor teaches the physics against the paper the student is actually going to sit.

So the first question to ask any prospective tutor is not what they charge. It is which board, which specification code, and which papers they have taught and marked. A tutor who answers that question precisely is worth a higher rate than one who answers it vaguely, and the difference is visible in the first session.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards from the exam
paragraphs: Most families start thinking about tuition when a report lands, which is usually the wrong end of the calendar. Counted backwards from the exam, the useful decision points sit months earlier, and a family on Hudayriyat Island who understands that sequence buys fewer hours at lower rates for better results. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series. Pearson runs May/June and November. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to candidates in India only and is not a route open to UAE students.

The entry deadline is the milestone nobody thinks about and the one that cannot be moved. Final entries sit months before the papers, and they are made by the school's exams officer, not by the family. If a tier change is needed — Core to Extended, Foundation to Higher — the conversation has to happen before that deadline, which means the diagnostic work has to happen before that. By the time mocks are marked, the tier is usually fixed.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. Take the dates from your own school. For Pearson, the live official timetable on qualifications.pearson.com is the only version worth planning from, because provisional timetables are revised.

The table below is the sequence as a parent should hold it, with the month-level timing that stays true from year to year rather than dates that go stale. Specific published milestones are given where they are backward-looking and therefore checkable: the November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: ADEK, the tutoring permit, and what you can verify before paying
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection ratings. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A family on Hudayriyat Island is inside the Abu Dhabi system, so the inspection report and the school's licensing both come from ADEK.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and by permit. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two consequences follow for a parent. First, anyone offering private lessons without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit costs them nothing to obtain, so there is no good reason for its absence. Second, Abu Dhabi has an additional rule: ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar. The marketing line about hiring your child's own teacher privately is not a line to act on in this emirate.

IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no board accreditation, and nothing on this page should be read as implying otherwise. A tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; that is a specific licence issued to specific entities and it is not something an online matching platform can borrow. What a parent can reasonably ask us for is the tutor's permit position, their board experience, and a free trial lesson before any money moves.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with coursework
paragraphs: This market contains providers who sell completed assessed work. One of them lists finished Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750. Buying that is not an expensive shortcut; it is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. Any page in this market that is not explicit about the boundary is leaving a family to discover it at the worst possible moment.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may explain what an assessment criterion is asking for, in the board's own words. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses — experimental design, data handling, structuring an argument, referencing. A tutor may read what the student has written and say precisely where it falls short of the criterion. A tutor may ask questions that make the student notice a problem themselves. All of that is teaching and all of it is legitimate.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, redraft a paragraph into better English, supply a structure for the student to fill in, or edit a draft to completion. The line is authorship: every word submitted has to be the student's own, and a tutor who blurs that is creating a malpractice exposure that sits on the candidate's record. IB Gram tutors state this boundary to the student in the first session on any coursework-bearing subject, and they do not move it under deadline pressure.

The same restraint applies to board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. We reference them and link to the official source; we do not reproduce or distribute them. A provider handing over a bundle of copied board documents is telling you something about how it treats rules in general.

sections.heading: MoE equivalency: the five-subject rule that decides which grades count
paragraphs: Families in Abu Dhabi planning a UAE university route need their child's certificate recognised by the Ministry of Education, and the British-track requirement is specific enough to plan around. Students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that catches families out is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A child with five passes where two of them are Arabic and Islamic education does not have five countable subjects, and that is a planning problem rather than a results-day problem. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong; the sourced figure is five.

For the American track the requirements are different again: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics through at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB route, no points threshold is published here, because none has been verified on the Ministry's own pages — a family on an IB path should confirm the current requirement with the Ministry or the school's IB coordinator rather than with a tutoring website.

Two cautions worth stating plainly. Equivalency is a process the family completes with the authority, not something a tutoring platform performs or guarantees on anybody's behalf, and IB Gram does not present it as such. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression; anybody implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a regulatory process.
