sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: A detail almost entirely absent from competing pages: UAE private schools teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies regardless of which international curriculum they are licensed for. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. For a Year 10 student on Hudayriyat Island, that means the IGCSE timetable is not the whole week.

The organisational rules are precise. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, with the school's licensed-curriculum language used for non-Arabs.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and the published advice is that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic are required to hold the appropriate regulator approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete credential a parent can ask a school about directly.

For tutoring, two things follow. These subjects carry real timetable weight and real marks on a school report, so a family budgeting only for Mathematics and the sciences may be missing where the grade pressure actually is. And the use of any different or additional content for the mandatory subjects, without prior Ministry permission, is prohibited — so support in these subjects means working with the school's own material and the school's own expectations, not importing an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: Getting started from Hudayriyat Island, including when we cannot help
paragraphs: The sequence is deliberately short. You tell us the school, the board, the subject and the paper tier, plus what the last school assessment said. We match a tutor who has taught that specification, and the first lesson is a free trial with no card required. After the trial you decide whether to continue, and pricing is quoted against the actual plan — subject, tier, number of sessions — rather than as a single hourly figure applied to everything.

What happens next is the part most pages skip. Sometimes no specialist is free at the time a family needs. A narrow combination — Extended tier Further Pure Mathematics at 5pm Gulf Standard Time on a Tuesday, for instance — can genuinely have nobody available that week. When that happens we say so and give a realistic date rather than putting a generalist in the slot and hoping. A family that has been told the truth can plan; a family that has been fobbed off loses a month.

Where a UAE-based tutor is unavailable for a niche subject, the alternative is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification over the same video platform, with the session timed to Gulf Standard Time. That is disclosed before anything is booked, because a parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number.

Lead forms on this site collect personal information about a minor, so it is worth being plain about that too. We collect the child's year group, school, board and subject because a match cannot be made without them, we do not ask for grades, photographs or documents at enquiry stage, and the privacy policy linked on every page explains how to have the record deleted. That is a UAE data-protection obligation under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, and it is also the minimum a parent should expect.

process.title: Tell us the board and the tier
process.description: Name the school, the board, the specification code if you have it, and the paper tier your child is entered for. That last detail decides more than any other: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, need different work and different past papers. If you do not know the tier, the school's exams officer does.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session, no card required, with a tutor who has taught that specification. Treat it as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration: ask for a past-paper question to be worked through and marked live, and ask the tutor at the end what they think the real problem is. You will learn more from that than from any profile.

process.title: Agree the plan and the price
process.description: Pricing is quoted after the trial against the actual plan — subject, tier, number of sessions a week, and how long the block runs. Ask for the hourly equivalent, the cancellation terms and what happens to unused sessions, in writing. Any provider who will not put those three answers in writing is not worth a term's commitment.

process.title: Fix the slot around the bridge and the school run
process.description: Sessions are scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, and for Hudayriyat Island families that usually means after the commute or after dinner rather than straight off the bus. A session the child is alert for is worth more than an earlier one they sleep through. Timing is reviewed once the first fortnight shows what actually works.

process.title: Work against the school's own calendar
process.description: The tutor plans from your school's scheme of work, its mock timetable and its internal coursework deadlines, not a generic syllabus order. That is why we ask which campus your child attends even though the lesson is online: the deadlines that matter are the ones that school sets.

process.title: Review after six sessions and change what is not working
process.description: At six sessions there is enough evidence to judge. If the marked work is not moving, the honest options are a different tutor, a different session shape, or a conversation with the school about tier. We would rather change the match than carry a term of sessions that are not earning their cost.

whyPoints.title: The price conversation happens first
whyPoints.description: Market AED bands are published on this page with the source and the month they were read, because a family cannot plan against a refusal to answer. Three of six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all. Our own pricing comes after a free trial and a conversation about subject and tier, which is the only honest way to quote it.

whyPoints.title: Subject expertise instead of a radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the tutor is chosen for having taught the exact specification and paper tier, not for living near the Hudayriyat bridge. On a narrow combination — Extended tier Additional Mathematics, say — the difference between a board-specific tutor and the nearest available one is the entire value of the hour.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no board accreditation, and says so. There is no self-asserted star rating, no student-outcome percentage without the underlying data, and no examiner claim without the board, component and years behind it. Competitors in this market publish contradictory ratings on a single page.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not write, redraft or complete any part of a coursework task, and that is stated to the student in the first session. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; the risk of that sits on the candidate, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed before you book
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is available for the subject, tier and slot you need, we say so and give a date. If the tutor who fits is based outside the UAE, we say that too, before anything is booked, with sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: Dates and rules taken from the source
whyPoints.description: Exam series are named by month so the page stays true, published milestones are quoted with their date so they can be checked, and regulator rules are taken from ADEK, MoHRE and the Ministry rather than paraphrased. Where something could not be verified — IB session dates in particular — the page says so rather than guessing.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE home tutor in Hudayriyat Island actually cost?
faqs.answer: In-home one-to-one tuition in this market is quoted between AED 180 and 500 an hour with travel inside the rate, with Bestimate's Dubai table putting the middle at AED 180 to 350. Published monthly in-home packages run AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. A qualified tutor working online sits lower, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with an online package seen at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram prices. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE and quotes its own pricing after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home tutor on Hudayriyat Island cost more than an online one?
faqs.answer: Because the drive is inside the rate. Hudayriyat Island is reached by bridge from Al Bateen and has no established local tutor population, so a tutor coming to a villa here travels from Abu Dhabi island or the mainland. Fifty minutes of driving for sixty minutes of teaching roughly doubles their effective cost, and the price reflects it. The premium buys logistics, not better subject knowledge. It also narrows your choice to whoever is both qualified in the right specification and willing to make the crossing twice a week, which on a specialist paper tier can be a very short list.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa on Hudayriyat Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons for Hudayriyat Island families are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a session recording. We target the home-tutor search because that is the phrase parents type, and then answer it honestly: the teaching is the same, the tutor pool is wider, and the travel premium is not on the invoice. If having somebody physically present is genuinely necessary, an in-home provider is the right choice and this page gives you the market rate to judge one by.

faqs.question: What should a Hudayriyat Island family buy first — a diagnosis or a term of lessons?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, almost always. One hour against a marked past paper, with a written list of what is wrong, costs a single session and frequently changes the whole plan. The most expensive error in this market is booking two sessions a week for a term and discovering in the spring that the real problem was tier placement rather than effort. Six months of mid-market weekly tuition is somewhere around AED 3,000 to 6,000; the diagnostic hour that would have found the tier problem is a fraction of that. Buy the information before you buy the hours.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child's school uses Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer, and ask for the specification code rather than the board name. Abu Dhabi's British-curriculum schools use both boards, sometimes different ones for different subjects, and the codes are what a tutor needs: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1, Cambridge Physics is 0625 and Pearson is 4PH1. This is worth five minutes of your time before you pay anybody, because a tutor working from the wrong board's past papers is wasting every hour. It is also the first question to put to a prospective tutor, ahead of their rate.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE exam series in February or March that my child could sit?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to candidates in India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. This matters because generic online calendars sometimes show the India dates, and a family planning around them would prepare for a window their child cannot enter. Take the dates from your own school's exams officer: Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE results arrive, and how does a resit fit the university timeline?
faqs.answer: Results follow the series by a matter of weeks. For Pearson, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the day after, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. That January timing is the detail that matters for a resit: a November entry taken after disappointing June grades produces results in the middle of the university application cycle, not before it. If a resit is in play, the conversation with the school and with the universities concerned needs to happen immediately after results rather than in the new year.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and does it cost them anything?
faqs.answer: Yes to the permit and no to the cost. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone offering private lessons without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Since it costs nothing, there is no reasonable explanation for a tutor not holding one.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at their Abu Dhabi school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Not if the child is enrolled at that teacher's school. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar bar on serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours also need the MoHRE permit. This is press-reported and worth confirming against the current ADEK policy document, but it is enough reason not to pursue the arrangement. A tutor from outside the school avoids the conflict entirely.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram hold ADEK or KHDA approval for tutoring in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider telling you otherwise should be asked for a permit number. IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no accreditation from Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi; it does not accredit online tutoring platforms. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and it is not something a matching platform can claim. What you can reasonably ask us for is the tutor's permit position, their board and paper experience, and a free trial before paying.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IGCSE coursework without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear enough to hold. A tutor may explain what a criterion asks for in the board's own words, teach the skills the task assesses, read the student's own draft and say exactly where it falls short, and ask questions that make the student find the problem. A tutor may not write any part of it, redraft a paragraph, supply a structure to fill in, or edit a draft to completion. The test is authorship: every submitted word must be the student's. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at around AED 3,750, and the consequence of buying that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects do Hudayriyat Island families ask for most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, by a wide margin, then Physics and Chemistry, then English. The pattern is consistent across Abu Dhabi island: Mathematics because the tier decision has consequences for A Level and university routes, the sciences because electricity in Physics and moles in Chemistry are reliable stumbling points, and English because directed writing and extended response reward a structure students are rarely taught explicitly. Arabic sits alongside all of it as a Ministry requirement in UAE private schools, examined separately, and families budgeting only for maths and science sometimes miss where the report-card pressure actually is.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Year 11 student usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week per subject through the course, rising to two in the final term or during an exam-season block, is the shape most families settle on. More than that is rarely useful mid-course, because the limiting factor is how much marked practice a student completes between sessions rather than contact hours. The honest answer depends on the gap: a tier problem needs more hours earlier, a technique problem can move substantially in six sessions. Review at six sessions against marked work, and if it is not moving, change the tutor or the shape rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: What happens if no IGCSE specialist is free for our Hudayriyat Island slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we give a realistic date. A narrow combination such as Extended tier Further Pure Mathematics at a specific weekday time can genuinely have nobody available that week, and putting a generalist in the slot would waste your money and the student's term. Where a UAE-based tutor is not available for a niche subject, the alternative is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same specification over the same platform with sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before anything is booked. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count among the five IGCSE subjects the Ministry wants?
faqs.answer: No. For the British track, the Ministry of Education requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A student with exactly five passes, two of which are Arabic and Islamic education, does not have five countable subjects. The track also needs one accredited Advanced Level subject at grade E or better, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One competitor in this market publishes a six-subject requirement; the sourced figure is five. Confirm current detail with the Ministry.

faqs.question: Can a Hudayriyat Island family move sessions during Ramadan or the summer break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families change the timing rather than pausing. Online sessions can shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan without a tutor's travel schedule deciding the hour, which is one of the practical advantages of the format in this market. School holidays work the same way: families who travel keep the slot because the session follows the student rather than the address. If a genuine pause is wanted — during mock weeks or the heaviest coursework fortnight — say so in advance and the block restarts rather than running down unused.

abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat.closingHeading: Get the number before you get the tutor
abu-dhabi/igcse-home-tutor-in-hudayriyat.closingBody: If you are weighing an IGCSE home tutor in Hudayriyat Island, you now have the AED bands, the source behind each one, and the arithmetic on what the travel premium adds without adding teaching. The next useful step costs nothing: tell us the school, the board, the specification code and the paper tier, take the free trial lesson, and ask the tutor at the end what they think the real problem is. If the answer is a tier conversation with the school rather than a term of sessions, we will say that. Pricing comes after the trial, quoted against the actual plan, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.
